Iron Pickaxe.name: Iron Pickaxe
Iron Pickaxe.tooltip: The Iron Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe. It can mine blocks weaker than Meteorite. In Journey Mode, the Iron Pickaxe replaces the Copper Pickaxe for newly created characters. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Lead Pickaxe. The Iron Pickaxe has slightly less pickaxe power, damage, and mining speed. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Dirt Block.name: Dirt Block
Dirt Block.tooltip: The Dirt Block is one of the most common blocks in Terraria, occurring naturally almost everywhere throughout the world. All caves above the elevation of 0 ft are made of Dirt. Below 0 ft, in the underground layer, the caves are made of roughly 50% Dirt. Small patches of Dirt can be found in the cavern layer, though it is mostly made of Stone. Dirt Blocks may be covered by different types of grass: regular, Corrupt, Crimson, Hallowed, mowed, or mowed Hallowed. Grass spreads onto adjacent Dirt Blocks, and it can be grown manually using seeds or the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth. In all cases, the grass applies to the block as a whole, and will appear on all exposed surfaces. If a grass block is covered by blocks on its four sides, the grass will remain and show as markings on the block. However, if the block is completely surrounded with eight blocks, the grass is lost and the block will revert to regular Dirt.

Stone Block.name: Stone Block
Stone Block.tooltip: The Stone Block is a type of block that is generated naturally in very large parts of the world. The majority of the Underground and Cavern layers is comprised of Stone Blocks. As a crafting ingredient, they are vital early in the game to craft the Furnace and Wooden Arrows. After Hardmode is activated in a world, nearby Corrupt, Crimson, and Hallowed blocks can spread through Stone Blocks, changing them into Ebonstone, Crimstone, or Pearlstone, respectively. Ebonstone and Crimstone Blocks can be returned to normal with Purification Powder, whereas Pearlstone Blocks require Vile or Vicious Powders. All three types can also be transformed back into regular Stone Blocks with the Green Solution. Stone Blocks can be found with moss growing on them, and it can be placed on them manually. Gemcorns can only be planted on Stone Blocks. Rock Golems and gem trees drop Stone Blocks, making them a renewable source of Stone Blocks.

Iron Broadsword.name: Iron Broadsword
Iron Broadsword.tooltip: The Iron Broadsword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. It is the counterpart to the Iron Shortsword. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Lead Broadsword. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Mushroom.name: Mushroom
Mushroom.tooltip: The Mushroom is a pre-Hardmode crafting material and recovery potion that spawns randomly on grass or Hallowed grass on the surface layer. It can be harvested with any tool or weapon. When used, the Mushroom restores 15 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for 30 seconds. This duration can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths. In The Constant worlds, eating a Mushroom also resets Hunger to 5 minutes of Peckish, if the player is hungry.

Iron Shortsword.name: Iron Shortsword
Iron Shortsword.tooltip: The Iron Shortsword is a pre-Hardmode shortsword. It is the counterpart to the Iron Broadsword. In Journey Mode, the Iron Shortsword replaces the Copper Shortsword for newly created characters. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Lead Shortsword. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Iron Hammer.name: Iron Hammer
Iron Hammer.tooltip: The Iron Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer. Newly created characters spawn with an Iron Hammer in Journey Mode. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Lead Hammer. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Torch.name: Torch
Torch.tooltip: Torches are furniture items that function as light sources when placed, held, or dropped (via the Throw button). Regular Torches can be found randomly in Chests and Pots, as a bonus drop from slimes, Torch Zombies, or purchased from the Merchant or Skeleton Merchant for 50 Copper each. Placing at least 101 Torches in close proximity below the surface layer in any biome will start the Torch God mini-event. Completing the event will grant the Torch God's Favor, which allows the player to automatically convert ordinary Torches to one of the biome types.

Wood.name: Wood
Wood.tooltip: Wood is a type of block that is generally obtained by cutting down trees using an axe or a chainsaw. Regular Wood can be harvested from Forest trees, vanity trees, Living Trees, and Underground Cabins in underground or cavern layers, as well as by using the Faecorn. Forest trees can be cultivated by placing Acorns on top of regular grass or Mowed grass above surface, and vanity trees can be cultivated by placing Sakura Sapling or Yellow Willow Sapling on top of any grass (but yields Ebonwood or Shadewood instead if placed on Corrupt or Crimson grass variants). Apart from regular Wood, there are 11 other types of wood. Crafting recipes that include Any Wood as an ingredient can use any type except Dynasty Wood, Feywood, and Pine Wood.

Iron Axe.name: Iron Axe
Iron Axe.tooltip: The Iron Axe is a pre-Hardmode axe. In Journey Mode(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), the Iron Axe replaces the Copper Axe for newly created characters. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Lead Axe. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Iron Ore.name: Iron Ore
Iron Ore.tooltip: Iron Ore is a pre-Hardmode ore. It spawns in the Underground and Cavern layers, and occasionally on the surface. Iron Ore also has a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes. It can be obtained from all types of crates. Its alternate ore counterpart is  Lead Ore.
Iron Ore.drops_summary: Azure Crate (0.89%), Baby Slime (0.16%), Black Slime (0.16%), +30 more

Copper Ore.name: Copper Ore
Copper Ore.tooltip: Copper Ore is a pre-Hardmode ore. It spawns in the Underground and Cavern layers, and occasionally on the surface.
Copper Ore.drops_summary: Azure Crate (0.89%), Baby Slime (0.16%), Black Slime (0.16%), +30 more

Gold Ore.name: Gold Ore
Gold Ore.tooltip: Gold Ore is a pre-Hardmode ore. It spawns in the Underground and Cavern layers, and occasionally on Floating Islands. Gold Ore also has a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes. Its alternate ore counterpart is  Platinum Ore.
Gold Ore.drops_summary: Azure Crate (0.89%), Baby Slime (0.16%), Black Slime (0.16%), +28 more

Silver Ore.name: Silver Ore
Silver Ore.tooltip: Silver Ore is a pre-Hardmode ore. It spawns in the Underground and Cavern layers, and occasionally on Floating Islands. Silver Ore also has a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes. Its alternate ore counterpart is  Tungsten Ore.
Silver Ore.drops_summary: Azure Crate (0.89%), Baby Slime (0.16%), Black Slime (0.16%), +30 more

Copper Watch.name: Copper Watch
Copper Watch.tooltip: Watches are informational accessories that show the current in-game time in the top-right corner of the screen. The display of time can be toggled by  clicking the watch icon underneath the minimap while the inventory is open or   selecting the watch icon in the equipment menu.

Silver Watch.name: Silver Watch
Silver Watch.tooltip: Watches are informational accessories that show the current in-game time in the top-right corner of the screen. The display of time can be toggled by  clicking the watch icon underneath the minimap while the inventory is open or   selecting the watch icon in the equipment menu.

Gold Watch.name: Gold Watch
Gold Watch.tooltip: Watches are informational accessories that show the current in-game time in the top-right corner of the screen. The display of time can be toggled by  clicking the watch icon underneath the minimap while the inventory is open or   selecting the watch icon in the equipment menu.

Depth Meter.name: Depth Meter
Depth Meter.tooltip: The Depth Meter is an informational accessory that enables an on-screen display of the player's vertical position, or depth. Depth is relative to the boundary between the Surface and Underground layers, which has a depth of 0 and is displayed as "Level". Depth is shown in the number of feet (1 foot = 1/2 tile) to this boundary, and is measured from the player's feet. The display also shows the name of the current layer. The Depth Meter has a 1/100 (1%) chance of being dropped by Cave Bats, Jungle Bats, Ice Bats, Giant Bats, and Spore Bats. Furthermore, it has a 1/80 (1.25%) chance of being dropped from Crawdads(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Giant Shellies(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Salamanders(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Depth Meter.drops_summary: Most bats (1%), Crawdad (1.25%), Giant Shelly (1.25%), +1 more

Gold Bar.name: Gold Bar
Gold Bar.tooltip: The Gold Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Platinum Bar.
Gold Bar.drops_summary: Azure Crate (1.39%), Boreal Crate (1.39%), Bramble Crate (1.39%), +21 more

Copper Bar.name: Copper Bar
Copper Bar.tooltip: The Copper Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Tin Bar. Newly created characters outside of Journey Mode will always spawn with the Copper Shortsword, Copper Pickaxe, and Copper Axe, regardless of whether the world generated with Copper or Tin.
Copper Bar.drops_summary: Chest (25%), Iron Crate (3.47%), Mythril Crate (1.16%), +2 more

Silver Bar.name: Silver Bar
Silver Bar.tooltip: The Silver Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar.
Silver Bar.drops_summary: Azure Crate (1.39%), Boreal Crate (1.39%), Bramble Crate (1.39%), +22 more

Iron Bar.name: Iron Bar
Iron Bar.tooltip: The Iron Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Lead Bar. Newly created characters in Journey Mode will always spawn with the Iron Shortsword, Iron Pickaxe, and Iron Axe, regardless of whether the world generated with Iron or Lead.
Iron Bar.drops_summary: Azure Crate (1.39%), Boreal Crate (1.39%), Bramble Crate (1.39%), +23 more

Gel.name: Gel
Gel.tooltip: Gel is a common crafting material dropped by most slimes and Slimed Zombies. Gel is vital due to it being an ingredient in Torches, and is used regularly from the beginning stages all the way through to endgame scenarios. It is also used as ammunition for the Flamethrower and the Elf Melter, and can therefore be stored in the player's ammo slots.

Wooden Sword.name: Wooden Sword
Wooden Sword.tooltip: The Wooden Sword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Wooden Door.name: Wooden Door
Wooden Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Stone Wall.name: Stone Wall
Stone Wall.tooltip: Stone Wall is a background wall made from Stone Blocks. Like other walls, it stops enemies from spawning when it is placed and can be used for houses.

Acorn.name: Acorn
Acorn.tooltip: The Acorn is a type of seed used to plant trees. Acorns can be planted on regular green grass, Hallowed grass, Corrupt grass, Crimson grass, Jungle grass, Sand, or Snow, where they will create saplings that will grow into trees, under the right conditions. Acorns are randomly dropped when cutting down or shaking trees and can also be purchased from the Dryad for 10 Copper each. Acorns cannot be retrieved after being placed. Destroying the sapling will not yield any items. Trees grown from Acorns will be much shorter than ones naturally generated at world creation. This can be circumvented by Infused Fertilizer. Acorns can be used as ammunition for the Acorn Slingshot.

Lesser Healing Potion.name: Lesser Healing Potion
Lesser Healing Potion.tooltip: The  Lesser Healing Potion is a pre-Hardmode recovery potion that restores 50 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for 60 seconds when used. This duration can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths. It is the first tier of healing potion, preceding the Healing Potion, Greater Healing Potion, Jungle Juice and Super Healing Potion. In addition to being crafted, Lesser Healing Potions can also be found naturally in pots (only in pre-Hardmode), generated chests, Wooden and Pearlwood Crates, or dropped from most early pre-Hardmode bosses. They can also be purchased for 3 Silver from the Merchant, or from the Skeleton Merchant during moon phases 2, 4, 6, and 8:    . Naturally-placed Lesser Healing Potions appear frequently on platforms in the Dungeon (along with Lesser Mana Potions). When encountered in placed form, they function as Placed Bottle crafting stations. They also show the "bottle" tooltip on the map. They can be freed with a pickaxe or ⚷ Open / Activate and retrieved, and can be placed by the player by crafting them into Decorative Healing Potions.
Lesser Healing Potion.drops_summary: Brain of Cthulhu (100%), Chest (50%), Eater of Worlds (100%), +5 more

Life Crystal.name: Life Crystal
Life Crystal.tooltip: The Life Crystal is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the player's health capacity by 20, adding a red heart to the player's health bar, while also restoring 20 health.  Life Crystals can be found naturally placed in any area in the Underground layer and below, though they are fairly uncommon. They cannot be found in the Underworld or the Dungeon. Life Crystals also have a 1/8 (12.5%) chance to drop from a Golden Crate, or 19/160 (11.88%) chance from a Titanium Crate. Up to 15 Life Crystals can be used per player, increasing health capacity by 300 health (15 hearts). Added to the 100 health (5 hearts) new players begin with, a total of 400 health (20 hearts) can be achieved. Additional Life Crystals can no longer be used at that point, and attempting to do so will not consume the item. After a world converts to Hardmode, and after the 400 health maximum is reached from consuming Life Crystals, Life Fruits can then be used to increase health capacity further, to a maximum of 500 health (20 Life Fruits).

Dirt Wall.name: Dirt Wall
Dirt Wall.tooltip: The Dirt Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in most caves and under overhangs on the surface, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player. The Natural Dirt Wall is an item that places an unsafe Dirt Wall. It is visually identical and is obtained by throwing a Dirt Wall into Shimmer.

Bottle.name: Bottle
Bottle.tooltip: A Bottle is a crafting material required to craft most potions. Like the Pink Vase, Mug, and different Cups, placing it (on most "flat-surface items" or a platform) allows it to act as a Placed Bottle where the player can craft potions. Bottles can also be "filled" when standing near water or honey, turning them into Bottled Water or Bottled Honey, respectively. Bottles can be crafted from Glass and found in chests.

Wooden Table.name: Wooden Table
Wooden Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Furnace.name: Furnace
Furnace.tooltip: The Furnace is a crafting station used mainly to smelt ores into bars and create various pieces of furniture. It is also a light source, but it is not valid for housing. The Furnace smelts all pre-Hardmode ores besides Hellstone, which must be smelted in a Hellforge. The Glass Kiln, Hellforge, and Hardmode Forges are upgraded versions of the Furnace, each with additional crafting recipes. The Furnace can also be purchased from the Merchant when he is in the Jungle biome for 3 Silver.

Wooden Chair.name: Wooden Chair
Wooden Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Iron Anvil.name: Iron Anvil
Iron Anvil.tooltip: The Iron Anvil and Lead Anvil are pre-Hardmode crafting stations used mainly to craft weapons and armor. Both anvils can craft the same items. Most of their recipes require metal bars, although they are also used to make other items, such as the Jungle tier of equipment. An anvil is a vital crafting station for most of the game, as it is used to make items from every tier up to Cobalt and Palladium, after which it must be replaced by a Mythril or Orichalcum Anvil. Both anvils are craftable, but can sometimes also be found in Underground Cabins. The Iron Anvil can furthermore be purchased from the Merchant.

Work Bench.name: Work Bench
Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Goggles.name: Goggles
Goggles.tooltip: Goggles are a piece of armor placed in the helmet slot. Unlike most helmets, Goggles do not cover the player's hair. Due to their low defense, they are often used as vanity items.

Lens.name: Lens
Lens.tooltip: A Lens is a common crafting material that has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to drop from Demon Eyes and Wandering Eyes.

Wooden Bow.name: Wooden Bow
Wooden Bow.tooltip: The Wooden Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow. Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.

Wooden Arrow.name: Wooden Arrow
Wooden Arrow.tooltip: The Wooden Arrow is a pre-Hardmode arrow. It has no special properties and is used for crafting a variety of more advanced ammunition. When fired with certain bows, Wooden Arrows will be converted into a special projectile (e.g. the Molten Fury converting them into Flaming Arrows). Some other bows, such as the Pulse Bow, can convert any type of arrow. Wooden Arrows can be crafted, found in Pots and Chests, dropped by Pincushion Zombies, and purchased from the Merchant for 5 Copper each. They can also be purchased from the Skeleton Merchant during moon phases 2, 3, 6, and 7.

Flaming Arrow.name: Flaming Arrow
Flaming Arrow.tooltip: The Flaming Arrow is a pre-Hardmode arrow. It has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to inflict the On Fire! debuff for 3 seconds on enemies.

Shuriken.name: Shuriken
Shuriken.tooltip: The Shuriken is a consumable ranged weapon. It can hit up to 4 targets.

Suspicious Looking Eye.name: Suspicious Looking Eye
Suspicious Looking Eye.tooltip: The Suspicious Looking Eye is a boss-summoning item that summons the Eye of Cthulhu when used. It can be used in any biome, but only at night. In addition to being crafted, Suspicious Looking Eyes also have a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Ivy Chests and Gold Chests found in the Cavern layer, including locked ones found inside the Dungeon.

Demon Bow.name: Demon Bow
Demon Bow.tooltip: The Demon Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow. It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Tendon Bow. Its best modifier is Unreal.

War Axe of the Night.name: War Axe of the Night
War Axe of the Night.tooltip: The War Axe of the Night is a pre-Hardmode axe. Its Crimson counterpart is the Blood Lust Cluster. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Light's Bane.name: Light's Bane
Light's Bane.tooltip: The Light's Bane is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. When swung, it creates a dark slash near the tip of the sword. The slashes deal 50% of the weapon's damage (8 base damage) and its full knockback, have 5 armor penetration, pierce once, and will automatically target enemies within a radius of 3.125 tiles. The weapon also has a chance to create a big slash that is twice as large and deals 100% of the weapon's damage. The chance of big slashes occurring is equal to the player's melee critical strike chance. It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Blood Butcherer. The Light's Bane is faster than the Blood Butcherer, but has a lower size and base damage. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Unholy Arrow.name: Unholy Arrow
Unholy Arrow.tooltip: The Unholy Arrow is a pre-Hardmode arrow. It can pierce 4 enemies, and its damage decreases by 5% per enemy pierced. In addition to being crafted, Unholy Arrows are dropped by the Eye of Cthulhu. Furthermore, they can be purchased from the Arms Dealer at night for 40 Copper each once the Eater of Worlds or Brain of Cthulhu has been defeated. In Hardmode, these restrictions are lifted and Unholy Arrows are available at any time.
Unholy Arrow.drops_summary: Eye of Cthulhu (100%), Treasure Bag (Eye of Cthulhu) (100%)

Chest.name: Chest
Chest.tooltip: Chests are a type of furniture functioning as storage items. They are accessed using ⚷ Open / Activate and can store up to 40 item stacks in rows of  10×4 /   8×5. In addition to many being craftable, a number of Chests are placed in random locations during world generation. The loot contained in these Chests is determined during world generation, and will not change if the world enters Hardmode. Chests cannot be broken with items inside (the blocks a filled Chest is placed on would also have this trait). However, the Block Swap feature allows the player to change the type of a Chest without having to destroy it. Some types of Chests can be locked by the player using a Chest Lock. When doing so, they will require a key to open again. There are 23 varieties of naturally-occurring Chests (12 of which cannot be crafted), 53 that can only be crafted, and 1 purchasable Chest, for a total of 77 Chest types.

Band of Regeneration.name: Band of Regeneration
Band of Regeneration.tooltip: The Band of Regeneration is an accessory that can be found in Gold Chests in the Underground and Cavern layers and in Living Mahogany Trees in the Underground Jungle. When equipped, it regenerates 1 health every second. This effect stacks with the player's natural health regeneration, but unlike the natural regeneration, does not slow or stop when the player is moving or being attacked.

Magic Mirror.name: Magic Mirror
Magic Mirror.tooltip: The Magic Mirror is a pre-Hardmode tool. When used, it plays an animation before teleporting the player to their spawn point. Compared to the Recall Potion, the Magic Mirror has unlimited uses, but a delay of 0.75 seconds (45 ticks), which is longer than the Recall Potion's 0.167 seconds (10 ticks) before teleporting. The Ice Mirror(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is a functionally identical alternative to the Magic Mirror. Magic Mirrors can be found in Chests generated in the Underground and Cavern layers. Ice Mirrors can be found in Frozen Chests generated in the Ice biome. Newly created characters in Journey Mode(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) spawn with a Magic Mirror.

Jester's Arrow.name: Jester's Arrow
Jester's Arrow.tooltip: The Jester's Arrow is a pre-Hardmode arrow. It is unaffected by gravity and can pierce an infinite number of enemies, and its damage decreases by 10% per each enemy pierced. In addition to being crafted, Jester's Arrows can be found in Gold Chests in the Cavern layer.

Angel Statue.name: Angel Statue
Angel Statue.tooltip: Statues are furniture items. While some are purely decorative, others have a functional effect when activated via Wire—depending on the statue, it may spawn enemies, drop items, or teleport an NPC to the statue's location. Most statues can be found already placed in any area underground (most frequently in the Dungeon, Underground Cabins, and Cavern level), though Angel Statues also appear in Chests. Like all furniture, a pickaxe, a drill, or explosives are used to collect them. There are a total of 117 different statues: 25 decoration statues, 36 text and numerical statues, and 56 functional mechanisms.

Cloud in a Bottle.name: Cloud in a Bottle
Cloud in a Bottle.tooltip: The Cloud in a Bottle is an accessory that can be found in Gold Chests in the Underground and Cavern layers. When equipped, it allows the player an extra jump. The extra jump has a 75% jump duration compared to a normal jump, increasing the maximum height the player can reach without other accessories by 5 tiles, for a total of 11 tiles.

Hermes Boots.name: Hermes Boots
Hermes Boots.tooltip: The Hermes Boots are a pre-Hardmode accessory that can be found in Chests in the Underground and Cavern layers. While equipped, they grant the ability to sprint, allowing the player to reach maximum running speed faster, and they increase the player's maximum movement speed to 31 mph (22.73 tiles/second). The player will leave behind a visual trail of dust clouds as they sprint. The Hermes Boots, Flurry Boots, and Sailfish Boots(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) have the same functionality, and their effects do not stack with each other.

Enchanted Boomerang.name: Enchanted Boomerang
Enchanted Boomerang.tooltip: The Enchanted Boomerang is a pre-Hardmode boomerang. It is a direct upgrade to the Wooden Boomerang. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Demonite Ore.name: Demonite Ore
Demonite Ore.tooltip: Demonite Ore is a pre-Hardmode ore. It is primarily dropped from the Eater of Worlds, as well as the Eye of Cthulhu in Corruption worlds. Demonite Ore can also be found rarely in small veins underground. When below 0 ft in elevation, a Gold Pickaxe or better is needed to mine it, otherwise any pickaxe can be used. It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Crimtane Ore.

Demonite Bar.name: Demonite Bar
Demonite Bar.tooltip: The Demonite Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar. It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Crimtane Bar.

Heart.name: Heart
Heart.tooltip: Hearts (or Candy Apples during Halloween and Candy Canes during Christmas) are common power-ups which can be dropped by slain enemies, broken pots, or as a bonus drop from slimes. Enemies and pots will only drop Hearts when the closest player does not have full health. They are not inventory items, but are instead instantly consumed and restore 20 health. They emit a faint red light. The drop rate of Hearts from enemies is linked to that of Stars. If the closest player is below full health but has full mana, then the chance to drop a Heart is 1/12 (8.33%). If they are below full health and full mana, however, then Stars take priority and the chance to drop a Heart is reduced to 1/24 (4.17%). For the drop rate of Hearts from pots, see Pot § Upon breaking. It is also possible to spawn Hearts (and their seasonal counterparts) with a Heart Statue. Hearts can be collected within a range of 2.625 tiles, which can be increased with a Heartreach Potion to 18.25 tiles.

Corrupt Seeds.name: Corrupt Seeds
Corrupt Seeds.tooltip: Corrupt Seeds are seeds used to plant Corrupt grass on Dirt Blocks, which will then spread The Corruption in all directions. They drop from the Eye of Cthulhu and can be purchased from the Dryad for 5 Silver each during a Blood Moon in a world with Corruption. In a world with Crimson, Corrupt Seeds can be purchased from the Dryad if she is spoken to in a Hardmode Graveyard. Corrupt Seeds can also be planted on Mud Blocks to create Corrupt Jungle grass.
Corrupt Seeds.drops_summary: Eye of Cthulhu (100%), Treasure Bag (Eye of Cthulhu) (100%)

Vile Mushroom.name: Vile Mushroom
Vile Mushroom.tooltip: The Vile Mushroom is a type of mushroom growing on Corrupt grass or Corrupt Jungle grass, where they can be cut and collected with a single swing from any weapon or tool. Vile Mushroom can only grow when there are proper walls behind the soil block, or no walls at all. Vile Mushrooms cannot be eaten or brewed into any potions; they are used solely to craft Vile Powder.

Ebonstone Block.name: Ebonstone Block
Ebonstone Block.tooltip: Ebonstone is a block type found in The Corruption. Before Hardmode, it is most prominent in the lining of Chasms. It requires at least a Nightmare Pickaxe or explosives to mine (this can be bypassed by using Purification Powder to turn Ebonstone to normal Stone, which is mineable with any pickaxe). Deathweed can grow on it. Ebonstone is the Corruption version of Stone (similar to Crimstone in The Crimson, or Pearlstone in The Hallow). As with Crimstone, Ebonstone can be converted into ordinary Stone via Purification Powder or Green Solution used by the Clentaminator. In Hardmode, the spread of Corruption converts ordinary Stone blocks into Ebonstone. Ebonstone itself also spreads Corruption to susceptible blocks nearby.
quality_issues: MISSING_TOOLTIP

Grass Seeds.name: Grass Seeds
Grass Seeds.tooltip: Grass Seeds are seeds used to plant regular grass on Dirt Blocks. They are purchased from the Dryad for 20 Copper each, while a Blood Moon is not occurring. They can also be obtained from putting Poo into an Extractinator, with a 0.67% chance per item.

Sunflower.name: Sunflower
Sunflower.tooltip: The Sunflower is a large, tall plant which can be found growing naturally on grass, and can be broken with a pickaxe or drill, or by coming into contact with water. It cannot be grown from seeds like most other plants, but is instead placed fully-grown, either naturally upon world generation or by the player. It can also be purchased from the Dryad for 50 Silver each, while a Blood Moon is not occurring. Sunflowers can only be placed on regular, Hallowed, Jungle, or Ash grass, at any height. They cannot be placed on Corrupt grass, Crimson grass, Mushroom grass, bare Dirt Blocks, nor in Clay Pots or Planter Boxes. Sunflowers grant the Happy! buff to players in their vicinity, increasing their movement speed and reducing enemy spawns. Furthermore, they serve as a small barrier against the spread of the Corruption/Crimson and Hallow, negate some of the effects of the evil biomes, and help preventing Graveyard biomes from forming.

Vilethorn.name: Vilethorn
Vilethorn.tooltip: The Vilethorn is a pre-Hardmode wand. It has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being obtained from destroying Shadow Orbs found in The Corruption or a 1/5 (20%) chance from Corrupt Crates(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Defiled Crates(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). When used, it extends a thorn from the player's position, which passes through blocks, pierces infinite enemies, and deals 0.17 s global invincibility. The thorn has 7 segments, and each has a length of 2 tiles. The thorn extends segmentally every 0.1 s, with each individual segment lasting 0.95 s. Its Crimson counterpart is the Crimson Rod. Its best modifier is Ruthless on  Desktop and Mythical elsewhere. This is due to differences in how damage is rounded between versions, with Mythical Vilethorn dealing 11 damage on vanilla desktop versions and 12 elsewhere.
Vilethorn.drops_summary: Corrupt Crate (20%), Defiled Crate (20%), Shadow Orb (20%)
quality_issues: NO_ITEM_NAME: 'Summons a vile thorn'

Starfury.name: Starfury
Starfury.tooltip: The Starfury is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being found inside Skyware Chests on Floating Islands, as well as a 1/4 (25%) chance of being obtained from Sky Crates and Azure Crates. When swung, it occasionally summons a star projectile that falls from the sky to the cursor. The star deals 150% of the weapon's damage (37 base damage) and pierces once before dissipating on the second hit, but inflicts no knockback. The star will pass through all blocks until it reaches the lowest empty space at or above the cursor, after which it will break on the next block it hits. Its best modifier is Legendary.
Starfury.drops_summary: Azure Crate (25%), Sky Crate (25%), Skyware Chest (25%)

Purification Powder.name: Purification Powder
Purification Powder.tooltip: Thrown Powders are consumable items that can be used to convert blocks and walls between their pure, Crimson, or Corrupt forms. When thrown, they release a cloud of sparkling powder with a very short range, comparable to that of a broadsword, and produce a fair amount of light. Thrown Powder comes in three variants: Purification Powder is able to revert any Corrupted, Crimson, or Hallowed blocks and walls back into their pure form, such as reverting Ebonstone into Stone, Crimsand into Sand, or Pink Ice into Ice. It is purchased solely from the Dryad for 75 Copper each, while a Blood Moon is not active. Purification Powder can also be used on a Tortured Soul in order to transform him into the Tax Collector NPC, as well as on a Mystic Frog to transform it into the Mystic Slime town pet. Vile Powder is able to convert blocks and walls, including the Crimson and the Hallowed ones, into their Corrupted form, such as converting Pearlstone into Ebonstone. If thrown at a Bunny, Penguin, or Goldfish, it will turn into its Corrupted variants: the Corrupt Bunny, Corrupt Penguin, and Corrupt Goldfish, respectively. It can be crafted from Vile Mushrooms or purchased from the Dryad for 1 Silver each during a Blood Moon in a Corrupt world. Vile Powder can be used to spread the Corruption onto convertible tiles. Vicious Powder is functionally identical to its counterpart, Vile Powder, to where it can convert blocks and walls, including the Corrupted and the Hallowed ones, into their Crimson form. If thrown at a Bunny, Penguin, or Goldfish, it will turn into its Crimson variants: the Vicious Bunny, Vicious Penguin, and Vicious Goldfish, respectively. It can be crafted from Vicious Mushrooms or purchased from the Dryad for 1 Silver each during a Blood Moon in a Crimson world. Vicious Powder can be used to spread the Crimson onto convertible tiles.

Rotten Chunk.name: Rotten Chunk
Rotten Chunk.tooltip: The Rotten Chunk is a crafting material that has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped from Eaters of Souls, Devourers, Corruptors, and on the Nintendo 3DS version, the Eater of Worlds.

Worm Tooth.name: Worm Tooth
Worm Tooth.tooltip: Worm Tooth is a crafting material dropped by Devourers in The Corruption. Unlike most Corruption items, it does not have a Crimson equivalent.

Worm Food.name: Worm Food
Worm Food.tooltip: Worm Food is a boss-summoning item that summons the Eater of Worlds when used. It can only be used in The Corruption or Underground Corruption, at any time.

Copper Coin.name: Copper Coin
Copper Coin.tooltip: Coins are the main unit of currency in Terraria, primarily used for transactions with NPCs. They are obtained by killing enemies, selling items to or interacting with NPCs, or finding them in multiple forms of loot. The currency comprises four different denominations of coins: Copper Coins, Silver Coins, Gold Coins, and Platinum Coins. The denominations are, ranked from lowest to highest value: 100 Copper Coins for 1 Silver Coin. 100 Silver Coins for 1 Gold Coin. 100 Gold Coins for 1 Platinum Coin. Despite coins appearing as the materials copper, silver, gold, or platinum, they are not related to their respective ores and cannot be crafted from them. The coin value an enemy drops upon death is calculated from fixed base values with some random variation. See NPC drops § Coin drops for further information. As a secondary function, coins are used as ammunition for the Coin Gun. They can also be placed to form Coin Piles.

Fallen Star.name: Fallen Star
Fallen Star.tooltip: The Fallen Star is an item that randomly falls from the sky at night and disappears at dawn (4:30 AM). They can be used to craft Mana Crystals, which permanently increase a player's mana capacity by 20 points each. They are also used in a variety of crafting recipes, and as ammunition for the Star Cannon and Super Star Shooter. Hence, Fallen Stars can be stored in ammo slots. Fallen Stars will spawn randomly throughout the entire nighttime, and their spawn rate is determined by two factors: the world size and a multiplier randomly set at nightfall. See Notes for details. Fallen Stars emit light while on the ground, making them easy to spot at night. They cannot be placed by the player as permanent light sources, but can be combined with a Bottle to craft the Star in a Bottle. They will disappear during the day, regardless of whether they are dropped by a player, but can remain in a player's inventory or a storage item (such as a Chest) indefinitely. In the uncommon event that a Fallen Star hits an enemy or critter, it will deal 1,000 base damage to the struck entity. Fallen Stars cannot damage players, unless playing in a Remix or Zenith world. In these worlds, Fallen Stars that fall from the sky do not drop as an item on impact, and can only be obtained from pots or slimes as their bonus drop.

Copper Greaves.name: Copper Greaves
Copper Greaves.tooltip: Copper armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Copper Helmet, Copper Chainmail, and Copper Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 48 Copper Bars (144 Copper Ore). The full set grants 6 defense while equipped. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Tin armor.

Iron Greaves.name: Iron Greaves
Iron Greaves.tooltip: Iron armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Iron Helmet, Iron Chainmail, and Iron Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 60 Iron Bars (180 Iron Ore). The full set grants 9 defense while equipped. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Lead armor. The Ancient Iron Helmet is functionally identical to and interchangeable with the Iron Helmet. The Ancient Iron Helmet has a 1/100 (1%) chance of being dropped by Skeletons and Spore Skeletons, and can also be obtained by dropping an Iron Helmet into Shimmer. Its appearance is based on the sprite of the Iron Helmet prior to 1.0.3.

Silver Greaves.name: Silver Greaves
Silver Greaves.tooltip: Silver armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Silver Helmet, Silver Chainmail, and Silver Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 60 Silver Bars (240 Silver Ore). The full set grants 13 defense while equipped. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Tungsten armor.

Gold Greaves.name: Gold Greaves
Gold Greaves.tooltip: Gold armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Gold Helmet, Gold Chainmail, and Gold Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Gold Bars (300 Gold Ore). The full set grants 16 defense while equipped. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Platinum armor. The Ancient Gold Helmet is functionally identical to and interchangeable with the Gold Helmet. Grappling Hook.name: Grappling Hook
Grappling Hook.tooltip: Hooks are a class of tools which aid the player in traversing terrain. When used, hooks fire a chain that latches to a surface or platform and pulls the player towards it. A hook is an essential tool which offers significant freedom from terrain height restrictions as well as being a fast movement option, and will often be the first major mobility tool a player acquires. A variety of hooks are available at all stages of the game (see table below). The Grapple hotkey activates the equipped hook in the player's equipment slot, or the first hook from the inventory (from left to right, top to bottom) without requiring it to be in the player's hotbar.Verify Several higher-tier hooks, such as the Ivy Whip, allow the player to grapple multiple surfaces simultaneously. If the character grapples one surface, then fires the hook a second time, another chain extends from the player without dislodging the first. Upon grappling a second surface, the player will be suspended in midair at a point midway between the two surfaces. This allows players more freedom during construction, or for navigating hazardous areas, such as above lava or Meteorite. All Journey Mode characters will spawn with the basic Grappling Hook already in their inventory.

Chain.name: Chain
Chain.tooltip: Chains are used both for climbing and as components for various crafting recipes.

Shadow Scale.name: Shadow Scale
Shadow Scale.tooltip: The Shadow Scale is a pre-Hardmode crafting material dropped from the Eater of Worlds (and its Treasure Bag in Expert Mode). It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Tissue Sample.
Shadow Scale.drops_summary: Eater of Worlds (100%), Eater of Worlds (50%), Treasure Bag (Eater of Worlds) (100%)

Piggy Bank.name: Piggy Bank
Piggy Bank.tooltip: The Piggy Bank is a portable storage item which can be purchased from the Merchant for 1 Gold. It requires a flat-surface item for placement. It has 40 slots like other storage items. The Piggy Bank inventory can also be accessed via the Money Trough(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Eye Bone(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Unlike normal Chests, the Piggy bank (along with the Safe, Defender's Forge, and Void Vault) is considered "personal storage". Items contained in a Piggy Bank are attached to the character rather than to a container in the world: The bank can be picked up and moved regardless of the items within. Coins and items stored within it are safe from other players, and will not be dropped on death. They will even travel with a character who goes to a different world. However, if a Hardcore character dies, all items in their personal storage will be deleted with the character and permanently lost.

Mining Helmet.name: Mining Helmet
Mining Helmet.tooltip: Mining armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Mining Helmet, Mining Shirt, and Mining Pants. The Mining Helmet can be purchased from the Merchant for 4 Gold and can also be dropped by Undead Miners with a 1/20 (5%) chance. The Mining Shirt and Mining Pants are dropped from Undead Miners with a 3/25 (12%) chance. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +4 defense +30% mining speed The player emits a small amount of light. All Mining armor pieces are interchangeable with pieces from the Prospector armor and the Ultrabright Helmet, still providing the set bonus. The only difference is the defense.

Wood Wall.name: Wood Wall
Wood Wall.tooltip: Wood Walls are a background wall made from Wood. Like other walls, it stops enemies from spawning when it is placed and can be used for houses.

Wood Platform.name: Wood Platform
Wood Platform.tooltip: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Flintlock Pistol.name: Flintlock Pistol
Flintlock Pistol.tooltip: The Flintlock Pistol is a pre-Hardmode gun that can be bought from the Arms Dealer for 5 Gold. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Musket.name: Musket
Musket.tooltip: The Musket is a pre-Hardmode gun. It will always drop from the first Shadow Orb destroyed in a Corruption world (along with 100 Musket Balls) and has a 1/5 (20%) chance of dropping from destroyed Shadow Orbs afterward. It also has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being obtained from Corrupt(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Defiled Crates(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) fished in the Corruption. The Musket has a base 12% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. Its Crimson counterpart is The Undertaker. The Musket deals a much higher damage per shot at a slower fire rate. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Musket Ball.name: Musket Ball
Musket Ball.tooltip: The Musket Ball is a pre-Hardmode bullet. It has no special properties and is used for crafting a variety of more advanced ammunition. When either Musket Balls or Tungsten Bullets are fired with certain guns, they will be converted into a special projectile (e.g. the Uzi converting them into High Velocity Bullets). Some other guns, such as the Pew-matic Horn, can convert any type of bullet. Musket Balls can be bought from the Arms Dealer for 7 Copper each, or 70 Silver for 1000 rounds. They can also be obtained from Shadow Orbs and Crimson Hearts (along with a Musket or The Undertaker), or from a Present (along with a Red Ryder) during Christmas. The Endless Musket Pouch serves as an infinite amount of Musket Balls.

Minishark.name: Minishark
Minishark.tooltip: The Minishark is a pre-Hardmode gun that can be purchased from the Arms Dealer for 35 Gold. When used, it rapidly fires bullets at a slight spread, with each shot having a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of not consuming any ammunition.  Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.

Iron Bow.name: Iron Bow
Iron Bow.tooltip: The Iron Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Lead Bow. Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.

Shadow Greaves.name: Shadow Greaves
Shadow Greaves.tooltip: Shadow armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Shadow Helmet, Shadow Scalemail, and Shadow Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 60 Demonite Bars (180 Demonite Ore) and 45 Shadow Scales. It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Crimson armor. Shadow armor pieces are interchangeable with Ancient Shadow armor pieces, still providing the set bonus but not the afterimage effect. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +19 defense +15% critical strike chance +75% acceleration and deceleration speed and ×1.15 maximum movement speed The player also emits visual afterimages and shadow particles while moving, and equipped Rocket Boots will emit purple flames.

Nightmare Pickaxe.name: Nightmare Pickaxe
Nightmare Pickaxe.tooltip: The Nightmare Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe. It can mine blocks up to Hellstone, Crimstone Blocks, and Ebonstone Blocks. Its Crimson counterpart is the Deathbringer Pickaxe. The Nightmare Pickaxe has slightly less pickaxe power and mining speed. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

The Breaker.name: The Breaker
The Breaker.tooltip: The Breaker is a pre-Hardmode hammer. Its Crimson counterpart is the Flesh Grinder. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Candle.name: Candle
Candle.tooltip: Candles are a type of furniture and light source. Candles can only be placed on flat-surface items. Candles will produce light underwater if placed and can be toggled on and off with ⚷ Open / Activate and by mechanisms. Certain types of candles provide buffs or debuffs. The Water Candle is a special type of candle found in Dungeons which increases enemy spawn rates by 33% and the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50% when placed or held. The Peace Candle reduces spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%, in contrast to the Water Candle. The Shadow Candle(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns in the area. For Water Candles and Peace Candles, multiple candles cannot stack, even if one is placed and the other is held.

Copper Chandelier.name: Copper Chandelier
Copper Chandelier.tooltip: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers come in many varieties which differ only in appearance and sell value. All chandeliers can be picked up using a pickaxe, drill, or explosives. Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.

Silver Chandelier.name: Silver Chandelier
Silver Chandelier.tooltip: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers come in many varieties which differ only in appearance and sell value. All chandeliers can be picked up using a pickaxe, drill, or explosives. Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.

Gold Chandelier.name: Gold Chandelier
Gold Chandelier.tooltip: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers come in many varieties which differ only in appearance and sell value. All chandeliers can be picked up using a pickaxe, drill, or explosives. Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.

Mana Crystal.name: Mana Crystal
Mana Crystal.tooltip: The Mana Crystal is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the player's maximum mana by 20, up to a maximum of 200 total. It takes 9 Mana Crystals to reach this maximum. It also restores 20 mana when used, but only as long as the character's maximum mana is below 200. Mana Crystals are created by combining 5 Fallen Stars. It takes 45 Fallen Stars to maximize the player's mana.

Lesser Mana Potion.name: Lesser Mana Potion
Lesser Mana Potion.tooltip: The Lesser Mana Potion is a recovery potion that restores 50 mana when used and inflicts the Mana Sickness debuff upon use. It can be purchased from the Merchant for 1 Silver each, and can also be found in Wooden and Pearlwood Crates obtained from fishing. Naturally-placed Lesser Mana Potions appear frequently on platforms in the Dungeon (along with Lesser Healing Potions). When encountered in placed form, they function as Placed Bottle crafting stations. They also show the "bottle" tooltip on the map. They can be freed with a pickaxe or ⚷ Open / Activate and retrieved, and can be placed by the player by crafting them into Decorative Mana Potions. It is the first tier of mana potion, preceding the Mana Potion, Greater Mana Potion, and Super Mana Potion.

Band of Starpower.name: Band of Starpower
Band of Starpower.tooltip: The Band of Starpower is an accessory that increases the player's maximum mana by 40. The Band of Starpower has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being obtained from destroying Shadow Orbs found in The Corruption or a 1/5 (20%) chance from Corrupt Crates and Defiled Crates, which are fished in the Corruption. It can furthermore be crafted.
Band of Starpower.drops_summary: Corrupt Crate (20%), Defiled Crate (20%), Shadow Orb (20%)

Flower of Fire.name: Flower of Fire
Flower of Fire.tooltip: The Flower of Fire is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron wand that fires a slow, non-piercing fireball that can bounce off blocks up to five times. The fireball dissipates upon contact with an enemy, with a 1/2 (50%) chance to inflict the On Fire! debuff for a duration of 5 seconds. The Flower of Fire has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being obtained from Shadow Chests in The Underworld, and has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Obsidian Lock Boxes obtained from Obsidian and Hellstone Crates. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Magic Missile.name: Magic Missile
Magic Missile.tooltip: The Magic Missile is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron wand. When used, it fires a magic missile that follows the cursor when ⚒ Use / Attack key is held. If the ⚒ Use / Attack key is released mid-drag, the missile will be fired in that direction. If the cursor is stationary on release, it is fired directly away from the player. Once it is released, the missile homes in on nearby enemies, creating a small explosion upon contact with an enemy or block. The Magic Missile has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from the Locked Gold Chests found in the Dungeon, as well as a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from Golden Lock Boxes. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Dirt Rod.name: Dirt Rod
Dirt Rod.tooltip: The Dirt Rod is a unique tool that is used solely to move Dirt Blocks around, and is unlike the use of ordinary mining tools and block placement. When used while the cursor is over a Dirt Block, the block becomes a Dirt Ball projectile that sticks to the cursor as long as the ⚒ Use / Attack key is held down. The Dirt Ball can be carried through blocks and relocated anywhere on the screen. When released, the Dirt Ball is affected by gravity and also continues to carry the speed it was being moved at previously, allowing it to be "thrown". Upon impact with any blocks, a released Dirt Ball turns back into a solid Dirt Block. The Dirt Rod is purchased from the Dryad for (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 5 Gold / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 20 Gold.

Shadow Orb.name: Shadow Orb
Shadow Orb.tooltip: The Shadow Orb is a background object found deep in the chasms of The Corruption. A world generated with the Corruption features several Shadow Orbs, and destroying at least three of them (in a single world) is usually a crucial step in game advancement. This can be done using any hammer or explosives. Shadow Orbs emit purple, flickering light, similar to Demon Altars. They are the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Crimson Hearts. Shadow Orbs are usually located in the chasms of the Corruption inside the horizontal tunnels or at the bottom of the vertical pits surrounded by Ebonstone Blocks. In order to reach them, the player may use a Nightmare Pickaxe or better pickaxe, explosives, or Purification Powder.

Meteorite.name: Meteorite
Meteorite.tooltip: Meteorite is a pre-Hardmode ore typically mined from Meteorite crash sites. It also spawns in high numbers during a Meteor Shower and rarely drops from Meteor Heads. A Meteorite crash site is a mini-biome guaranteed to spawn after the Eater of Worlds or Brain of Cthulhu is defeated for the first time. If the boss is defeated between midnight and dawn (12:00 AM – 4:30 AM), then the meteor crashes immediately. Otherwise, it will crash at the next midnight (12:00 AM). Meteorite can be mined using a Tungsten Pickaxe or better (its counterpart, the Silver Pickaxe, does not have enough pickaxe power). Contact with Meteorite blocks causes the player to be inflicted with the Burning debuff, unless the player has the Obsidian Skull accessory (or its upgrades) equipped, or is using an Obsidian Skin Potion.

Meteorite Bar.name: Meteorite Bar
Meteorite Bar.tooltip: The Meteorite Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar. In addition to being crafted, Meteorite Bars can also be found as common items in Shadow Chests, or more rarely in Gold Chests in the Cavern layer that generate close to the Underworld.

Hook.name: Hook
Hook.tooltip: The Hook is a crafting material used solely to craft the Grappling Hook. It has a 1/25 (4%) chance to drop from Skeletons, Undead Miners, Hoplites, and Undead Vikings in the Marble Caves, Ice biome, and Cavern layer. It also has a 1/30 (3.33%) chance to drop from Piranhas in the Jungle, Underground Jungle, Cavern, and Underground layer.

Flamarang.name: Flamarang
Flamarang.tooltip: The Flamarang is a pre-Hardmode boomerang and an upgrade to the Enchanted Boomerang. It has a 1/2 (50%) chance of inflicting the On Fire! debuff to enemies for 3 seconds on hit. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Molten Fury.name: Molten Fury
Molten Fury.tooltip: The Molten Fury is a pre-Hardmode bow. When used, it converts Wooden Arrows into Flaming Arrows, causing them to inflict the On Fire! debuff on hit. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Volcano.name: Volcano
Volcano.tooltip: The Volcano is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. When swung, it creates an explosion upon enemy hits, dealing 75% of the weapon's damage (30 base damage) to the enemy and 2 other targets in an area around the enemy. The Volcano has a 1/2 (50%) chance to inflict the On Fire! debuff for 3 seconds, while its explosion is guaranteed to inflict it for the same duration. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Molten Pickaxe.name: Molten Pickaxe
Molten Pickaxe.tooltip: The Molten Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe. It can mine blocks up to Dungeon Bricks, Cobalt Ore, and Palladium Ore. The Molten Pickaxe occasionally inflicts the On Fire! debuff on hit enemies. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Meteor Helmet.name: Meteor Helmet
Meteor Helmet.tooltip: Meteor armor is a pre-Hardmode mage armor set consisting of the Meteor Helmet, Meteor Suit, and Meteor Leggings. Crafting a full set requires a total of 45 Meteorite Bars (135 Meteorite). The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +16 defense +27% magic damage Reduces the mana cost of the Space Gun, Laser Rifle, Gray Zapinator, and Orange Zapinator to 0 Immunity to meteorite projectiles during the Meteor Shower event The player also leaves behind a visual trail of flames.

Meteor Suit.name: Meteor Suit
Meteor Suit.tooltip: Meteor armor is a pre-Hardmode mage armor set consisting of the Meteor Helmet, Meteor Suit, and Meteor Leggings. Crafting a full set requires a total of 45 Meteorite Bars (135 Meteorite). The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +16 defense +27% magic damage Reduces the mana cost of the Space Gun, Laser Rifle, Gray Zapinator, and Orange Zapinator to 0 Immunity to meteorite projectiles during the Meteor Shower event The player also leaves behind a visual trail of flames.

Meteor Leggings.name: Meteor Leggings
Meteor Leggings.tooltip: Meteor armor is a pre-Hardmode mage armor set consisting of the Meteor Helmet, Meteor Suit, and Meteor Leggings. Crafting a full set requires a total of 45 Meteorite Bars (135 Meteorite). The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +16 defense +27% magic damage Reduces the mana cost of the Space Gun, Laser Rifle, Gray Zapinator, and Orange Zapinator to 0 Immunity to meteorite projectiles during the Meteor Shower event The player also leaves behind a visual trail of flames.

Bottled Water.name: Bottled Water
Bottled Water.tooltip: Bottled Water is a pre-Hardmode crafting material and recovery potion. It can be crafted at a sink or a body of water. Bottled Water mainly serves as the basis of almost every craftable potion in the game, and is also required for crafting flasks. When used, it restores 30 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for 45 seconds. This duration can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths.

Space Gun.name: Space Gun
Space Gun.tooltip: The Space Gun is a pre-Hardmode magic gun. When used, it fires fast green lasers that can hit up to three enemies. The lasers will increase in damage, pierce, knockback and size (only visually) as they travel. While a full set of Meteor armor is equipped, the Space Gun costs no mana to use. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Rocket Boots.name: Rocket Boots
Rocket Boots.tooltip: Rocket Boots are a pre-Hardmode accessory that can be purchased from the Goblin Tinkerer for 5 Gold. While equipped, they allow the player to hold ↷ Jump in midair to fly for a total of 1.17 seconds. While flying, the boots emit visual flame particles that give off a large amount of light. The flight time of the Rocket Boots is divided into 7 "charges" that each last 0.17 seconds, and releasing ↷ Jump during flight immediately consumes all remaining flight time in a charge. All charges are reset immediately when the player lands on any solid object, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or latches onto a tile with a hook.

Gray Brick.name: Gray Brick
Gray Brick.tooltip: The Gray Brick is a pre-Hardmode brick.

Gray Brick Wall.name: Gray Brick Wall
Gray Brick Wall.tooltip: Gray Brick Wall is a background wall crafted from Gray Bricks. They can only be painted white, black or brown.

Red Brick.name: Red Brick
Red Brick.tooltip: Red Bricks are bricks crafted from Clay Block.

Red Brick Wall.name: Red Brick Wall
Red Brick Wall.tooltip: Red Brick Wall is a background wall crafted from Red Bricks. It stops enemies from spawning where it is placed and, if covering an entire room, can be used to make NPC houses. These can be painted with any available paint color, except Red which will yield no change in the sprite.

Clay Block.name: Clay Block
quality_issues: MISSING_TOOLTIP

Blue Brick.name: Blue Brick
Blue Brick.tooltip: Dungeon Bricks are a type of brick from which the Dungeon is constructed. On world generation, one of three colors of Dungeon Brick is chosen to create the entirety of the Dungeon. Dungeon Brick is one of very few block types that is impervious to explosions. 100% pickaxe power (a Molten Pickaxe or better) is required to mine Dungeon Bricks in the Underground-level Dungeon, although any pickaxe can mine Dungeon Bricks at or above the Surface layer, and any Dungeon Bricks placed within the center third of the world. They can also be obtained from Dungeon Crates or Stockade Crates.

Blue Brick Wall.name: Blue Brick Wall
Blue Brick Wall.tooltip: Dungeon Brick Walls are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Dungeon, considered unsafe. They drop as items when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting on  Desktop,  Console, and  Mobile. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player. There are a total of nine different variants (three variants in three colors), but each Dungeon can include only the three wall types matching that Dungeon's color. A single Dungeon will usually contain all three types in different areas; in each area, the faction flags found will correspond to the wall variant. Cursed Dungeon Brick Walls(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are items that place unsafe Dungeon Brick Walls. They are visually identical to their counterparts and are obtained via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

Chain Lantern.name: Chain Lantern
Chain Lantern.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Green Brick.name: Green Brick
Green Brick.tooltip: Dungeon Bricks are a type of brick from which the Dungeon is constructed. On world generation, one of three colors of Dungeon Brick is chosen to create the entirety of the Dungeon. Dungeon Brick is one of very few block types that is impervious to explosions. 100% pickaxe power (a Molten Pickaxe or better) is required to mine Dungeon Bricks in the Underground-level Dungeon, although any pickaxe can mine Dungeon Bricks at or above the Surface layer, and any Dungeon Bricks placed within the center third of the world. They can also be obtained from Dungeon Crates or Stockade Crates.

Green Brick Wall.tooltip: Dungeon Brick Walls are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Dungeon, considered unsafe. Cursed Dungeon Brick Walls(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are items that place unsafe Dungeon Brick Walls. They can also be obtained from Dungeon Crates or Stockade Crates.

Cursed Dungeon Brick Walls(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are items that place unsafe Dungeon Brick Walls.
