Gold Brick.name: Gold Brick
Gold Brick.tooltip: Gold Bricks are a type of brick crafted from Gold Ore. In some worlds, they are found as part of Jungle Shrines in the Underground Jungle. Like the ore they are made of, placed Gold Bricks will sparkle.

Gold Brick Wall.name: Gold Brick Wall
Gold Brick Wall.tooltip: The Gold Brick Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Jungle Shrines in some worlds. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is always considered a safe wall.

Silver Brick.name: Silver Brick
Silver Brick.tooltip: Silver Brick is a type of Brick and an aesthetic building material. Like the ore it is made of, placed Silver Bricks will sparkle. It is not recommended that it be used for building unless the player has silver ore to spare. It can be crafted into Silver Brick Walls.

Silver Brick Wall.name: Silver Brick Wall
Silver Brick Wall.tooltip: Silver Brick Walls are a type of background wall crafted from Silver Bricks. Enemies will not spawn where they are placed, and they can be used for NPC houses.

Copper Brick.name: Copper Brick
Copper Brick.tooltip: Copper Brick is a type of Brick and an aesthetic building material. Like the ore used to make it, placed Copper Bricks will sparkle. As copper becomes fairly useless quite early in the game, this is an inexpensive ore brick to build with. Despite being made of Copper, it has no sell value, as with most other bricks. Copper Plating is also available as a decorative block, with the same ingredients and color but a different texture.

Copper Brick Wall.name: Copper Brick Wall
Copper Brick Wall.tooltip: Copper Brick Walls are a type of background wall crafted from Copper Bricks. Like most walls, they will stop enemy spawning, and can be used for NPC houses.

Spike.name: Spike
Spike.tooltip: The Spike is a trap that can be found in the Dungeon. Upon contact, it deals 60 damage to the player, on all difficulties, and inflicts the Bleeding debuff for 10 / 20 / 25 seconds. It can be broken with a pickaxe, drill, or explosives. Spikes cannot be destroyed by explosives when the For the Worthy seed is active.

Water Candle.name: Water Candle
Water Candle.tooltip: The Water Candle is a furniture item that emits a low amount of light, and can be placed only on flat-surface items. While placed nearby or while held, it grants the Water Candle debuff to the player. The Water Candle debuff increases all enemy and critter spawn rates by 33%, and increases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50%. The debuff is applied to any players holding or standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on a Water Candle. In order to be considered "holding" the candle, it must be in the player's hotbar and currently selected; merely being in a player's inventory will not suffice. Multiple candles will not stack with each other, even if one is placed and the other held. Several Water Candles are found commonly on the shelves of the Dungeon. They can also be crafted at a Crystal Ball. Placed Water Candles can be shut off by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them, and will toggle when activated via wiring. Water Candles that are turned off will not activate the Water Candle debuff. The Water Candle's effect is the opposite of the Peace Candle, which decreases enemy spawn rates. If a Peace Candle and a Water Candle are active at the same time, neither have any effect on spawn rates. Conversely, the Water Candle's effect stacks with that of the Battle Potion.

Book.name: Book
Book.tooltip: The Book is a crafting material used only to craft Bookcases, Pianos, and Librarian Blocks. It can also be placed as decoration on Flat-surface items. Books are found placed on the Dungeon's many shelves, where they can be freed with a pickaxe or drill. They can also be renewably obtained from Dungeon or Stockade Crates, and can be bought from the Wizard for 15 Silver each.

Cobweb.name: Cobweb
Cobweb.tooltip: Cobwebs are crafting materials used to craft Silk and other items. Cobwebs can also be placed. Placed Cobwebs catch players who fall into them and reset fall damage. They break after a short time when a player is stuck in them, and they can also be harvested instantly with any weapon or swung tool. Cobwebs are commonly found in underground areas in clusters of 5 or more alongside the edges of walls or ceilings, and are guaranteed to drop a Cobweb item when broken. They are also found in large quantities in Spider Nests, where they regrow over time; however, Cobwebs found there only have a 1/4 (25%) chance to drop when broken. In Expert Mode worlds with the Remix seed enabled, web spit attack from Black Recluses and Jungle Creepers can randomly place Cobwebs in a 13×13 rectangular area centered on the location where Web Spit projectiles disappear.

Necro Helmet.name: Necro Helmet
Necro Helmet.tooltip: Necro armor is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron ranged armor set consisting of the Necro Helmet, Necro Breastplate, and Necro Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 135 Cobwebs and 150 Bones. The Ancient Necro Helmet is dropped from Angry Bones, Dark Casters, and Librarian Skeletons in the Dungeon, at a 1/450 (0.22%) chance. It is functionally identical to and interchangeable with the Necro Helmet. Its appearance is based on the sprite of the Necro Helmet prior to 1.0.3. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +19 defense +15% ranged damage +10% ranged critical strike chance The player also emits a visual afterimage while moving, and their hurt sound will be set to that of a Skeleton.

Necro Breastplate.name: Necro Breastplate
Necro Breastplate.tooltip: Necro armor is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron ranged armor set consisting of the Necro Helmet, Necro Breastplate, and Necro Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 135 Cobwebs and 150 Bones. The Ancient Necro Helmet is dropped from Angry Bones, Dark Casters, and Librarian Skeletons in the Dungeon, at a 1/450 (0.22%) chance. It is functionally identical to and interchangeable with the Necro Helmet. Its appearance is based on the sprite of the Necro Helmet prior to 1.0.3. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +19 defense +15% ranged damage +10% ranged critical strike chance The player also emits a visual afterimage while moving, and their hurt sound will be set to that of a Skeleton.

Necro Greaves.name: Necro Greaves
Necro Greaves.tooltip: Necro armor is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron ranged armor set consisting of the Necro Helmet, Necro Breastplate, and Necro Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 135 Cobwebs and 150 Bones. The Ancient Necro Helmet is dropped from Angry Bones, Dark Casters, and Librarian Skeletons in the Dungeon, at a 1/450 (0.22%) chance. It is functionally identical to and interchangeable with the Necro Helmet. Its appearance is based on the sprite of the Necro Helmet prior to 1.0.3. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +19 defense +15% ranged damage +10% ranged critical strike chance The player also emits a visual afterimage while moving, and their hurt sound will be set to that of a Skeleton.

Bone.name: Bone
Bone.tooltip: Bones are crafting materials and consumable ranged weapons. They are dropped by Angry Bones, Dark Casters, Cursed Skulls, and Librarian Skeletons which spawn in the Dungeon. Bones are greatly affected by gravity, and arc similarly to Throwing Knives and Shurikens. Of these three consumable ranged weapons, Bones have the least range (Throwing Knives having the greatest). Furthermore, Bones can be placed as blocks using the Bone Wand, upon which they become Bone Blocks.

Muramasa.name: Muramasa
Muramasa.tooltip: The Muramasa is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron broadsword that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from the Locked Gold Chests found in the Dungeon, as well as a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from Golden Lock Boxes. When swung, it creates a blue slash upon enemy hits. The slashes deal 50% of the weapon's damage (12 base damage), inflict no knockback, do not pierce, and have 5 armor penetration. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Cobalt Shield.name: Cobalt Shield
Cobalt Shield.tooltip: The Cobalt Shield is a pre-Hardmode shield accessory that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from Locked Gold Chests found in the Dungeon, as well as a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from Golden Lock Boxes(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). While equipped, it grants 1 defense and immunity to knockback.

Aqua Scepter.name: Aqua Scepter
Aqua Scepter.tooltip: The Aqua Scepter is a pre-Hardmode wand that fires arcing streams of water in quick succession, with each stream being able to hit up to 5 targets. The water streams bounce upwards upon colliding with lava. They pierce infinitely after a bounce, move slower, are less affected by gravity and can last for a significantly longer time. The Aqua Scepter has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from the Locked Gold Chests found in the Dungeon, as well as a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from Golden Lock Boxes(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Its best modifier is Mythical.

Lucky Horseshoe.name: Lucky Horseshoe
Lucky Horseshoe.tooltip: The Lucky Horseshoe is an accessory that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being found inside Skyware Chests on Floating Islands, as well as a 1/4 (25%) chance of being obtained from Sky Crates and Azure Crates. While equipped, it negates fall damage and grants +0.05 luck. This bonus does not stack with any of its upgrades.
Lucky Horseshoe.drops_summary: Azure Crate (25%), Sky Crate (25%), Skyware Chest (25%)

Shiny Red Balloon.name: Shiny Red Balloon
Shiny Red Balloon.tooltip: The Shiny Red Balloon is an accessory that increases the player's jump duration by 33% and jump speed by 30%, increasing the height that the player can jump from 6 tiles to ~10½ tiles, effectively a ~75% boost. However, it reduces jump height when underwater, from 8 tiles to ~7 tiles. The Shiny Red Balloon has a 1/4 (25%) of being found inside Skyware Chests on Floating Islands, as well as a 1/4 (25%) chance of being obtained from Sky Crates and Azure Crates.
Shiny Red Balloon.drops_summary: Azure Crate (25%), Sky Crate (25%), Skyware Chest (25%)

Harpoon.name: Harpoon
Harpoon.tooltip: The Harpoon is a unique pre-Hardmode ranged weapon that auto-fires an arcing spear projectile connected to the player via a chain that pierces through enemies and inflicts the Bleeding debuff for 8–12 seconds on hit. It retracts if it hits a third enemy, collides with solid blocks, has traveled for more than 62.5 tiles away from the player, or if the player lets go of the ⚒ Use / Attack button. Its physics are similar to launched flails, though it is highly affected by gravity. The Harpoon has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of being dropped by most enemies during a Goblin Army. The Harpoon only has an attack cooldown of 0.08 seconds after its spear is fully retracted; meaning its fire rate is mostly dependent only on how long it takes for it to retract. The projectile also pierces infinitely and goes through blocks on its return trip, similar to a flail or boomerang, making it effective for crowd control. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Spiky Ball.name: Spiky Ball
Spiky Ball.tooltip: The Spiky Ball is a consumable ranged weapon that is primarily used as a passive trap by tossing them to the ground, where enemies who pass over them will take damage up to 7 times (after which the Spiky Balls vanish). If not destroyed, they will automatically vanish after 1 minute and 20 seconds. They can also be directly thrown at enemies, but they have a very short arc and quickly fall to the ground. Spiky Balls have a 199/400 (49.75%) chance of being dropped by all goblins during the Goblin Army event (except for the Goblin Warlock), and can be purchased from the Goblin Tinkerer for 80 Copper each. The Goblin Tinkerer uses Spiky Balls to defend himself against nearby enemies.

Ball O' Hurt.name: Ball O' Hurt
Ball O' Hurt.tooltip: The Ball O' Hurt is a pre-Hardmode flail that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being obtained from destroying Shadow Orbs found in The Corruption or a 1/5 (20%) chance from Corrupt Crates and Defiled Crates, which are fished in the Corruption. Its Crimson flail counterpart is The Meatball. Its Crimson Heart melee weapon counterpart is The Rotted Fork. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Ball O' Hurt.drops_summary: Corrupt Crate (20%), Defiled Crate (20%), Shadow Orb (20%)

Blue Moon.name: Blue Moon
Blue Moon.tooltip: The Blue Moon is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron flail that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from the Locked Gold Chests found in the Dungeon, as well as a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from Golden Lock Boxes. If the Sunfury is also in the player's inventory, then the Sunfury will be thrown out at the same time as the Blue Moon, but in the mirrored direction. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Handgun.name: Handgun
Handgun.tooltip: The Handgun is a pre-Hardmode gun that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from Locked Gold Chests in the Dungeon, and from Golden Lock Boxes found in Dungeon Crates or Stockade Crates. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Water Bolt.name: Water Bolt
Water Bolt.tooltip: The Water Bolt is a pre-Hardmode spell book that can be found hidden within the shelves of the Dungeon, along with having a 1/40 (2.5%) chance to be dropped by Water Bolt Mimics. When used, it fires a slow-moving piercing water ball projectile that can bounce off blocks. The water ball dissipates after hitting blocks up to five times, after hitting ten enemies, or after lasting for 30 seconds. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Bomb.name: Bomb
Bomb.tooltip: The Bomb is an explosive that explodes 3 seconds after being thrown. The explosion breaks nearly all blocks, background walls, and furniture within a 4-tile radius, except explosion-proof objects. The explosion also deals 100 damage to all enemies, critters, and players in the radius, but not NPCs. The Bomb works in liquids. A lit Bomb can be defused by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it, canceling the explosion and safely dropping the Bomb as an item for the player to pick it back up. The Bomb can be purchased from the Demolitionist and Skeleton Merchant for 3 Silver each or obtained from Pots, Chests, by powering Bomb Statues, or as a drop from Undead Miners with a 18/25 (72%) chance. It also has a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes. The Hardmode variant of the Bomb is the Power Bomb. Power Bombs have a greater radius and can explode early Hardmode ores, unlike the Bomb.
Bomb.drops_summary: Most slimes (0.31%), Gold Chest (33.33%), Undead Miner (72%)

Dynamite.name: Dynamite
Dynamite.tooltip: Dynamite is an explosive that explodes 5 seconds after being thrown. The explosion breaks nearly all blocks, background walls, and furniture within a radius of 7 tiles, except explosion-proof objects. The explosion also deals 250 damage to all enemies, critters, and players (but not NPCs) within 7.8 tiles  horizontally and vertically of the Dynamite. Dynamite works in liquids. Lit Dynamite can be defused by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it, canceling the explosion and safely dropping the Dynamite as an item for the player to pick it back up. Dynamite can be found in Chests or purchased from the Demolitionist for 20 Silver each.

Grenade.name: Grenade
Grenade.tooltip: The Grenade is an explosive consumable ranged weapon which can be purchased from the Demolitionist for 75 Copper each, or found rarely in natural Chests and, once Hardmode is activated, in Pots (replacing Shurikens). A thrown Grenade will bounce slightly and roll until it either hits a valid target or 3 seconds have elapsed, after which it will explode.

Sand Block.name: Sand Block
Sand Block.tooltip: Sand Blocks are soil blocks found in vast quantities in Desert biomes, at shore and bottom of Ocean biomes, and can be found as microbiomes in patches in the Underground layer. They are also shot as projectiles by Antlions. Sand can spread and be converted by the evil biomes and The Hallow (see below). Sand is subject to gravity, a unique quality only shared by Slush, Silt, Shell Piles, Cracked Dungeon Bricks, and Ash on For the Worthy and Zenith worlds. Sand Blocks will deal damage to any player or enemy they fall on. If the amount of Sand falling on the player is significant, the Suffocation debuff will be inflicted until the player manages to escape. Sand is used to craft a small number of building blocks and other items directly, but it is also the raw material for Glass, which is used for a full furniture set and a variety of other items. All forms of Sand are also ammunition for the Sandgun, but they cannot be stored in the ammo slots of the inventory. Similar to the Sand Ball projectiles shot by Antlions, shot Sand Blocks will be placed on the ground as blocks if there are space available.

Glass.name: Glass
Glass.tooltip: Glass is crafted from different types of sand at a Furnace. Glass can be placed as a block and is an ingredient in producing various items.

Sign.name: Sign
Sign.tooltip: The Sign is a decorative furniture item that can store a player-written message. A Sign must be placed and then the ⚷ Open / Activate button must be pressed on it to edit or display its message. A Sign can be placed on top of blocks, beside them, or hanging from their underside, or be placed on walls. A Sign's message can be up to 10 lines long, at 48 characters max per line, for a total of 480 characters maximum per sign. Signs can be used for decoration, labeling areas, adventure text, etc. There is a maximum limit of 32,000 placed Signs that can be written on in each world. If more than 32,000 are put down, only the first 32,000 Signs that are interacted with can be edited; the rest do not open a menu upon pressing ⚷ Open / Activate (until one of the first 32,000 Signs is removed).

Ash Block.name: Ash Block
Ash Block.tooltip: The Ash Block is a block that covers the upper and lower sections of The Underworld, and can occasionally encase Hellstone. It can be used for building and for growing Fireblossom. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) In the Ash forests on the outer edges of the Underworld, Ash grass naturally generates on Ash Blocks, with Ash trees growing on them. Ash Grass Seeds can be planted on Ash Blocks.

Obsidian.name: Obsidian
Obsidian.tooltip: Obsidian is a pre-Hardmode ore that is created when water and lava collide. Mining Obsidian requires a Gold/Platinum Pickaxe or better. Explosives can also destroy Obsidian. Uniquely, Obsidian has no bar form of its own. It is used to craft Hellstone Bars instead. Obsidian can be converted into Sand Blocks when used on an Extractinator.

Hellstone.name: Hellstone
Hellstone.tooltip: Hellstone is a pre-Hardmode ore that can be found in The Underworld. Mining it requires at least a Nightmare/Deathbringer Pickaxe, and it cannot be mined with explosives in pre-Hardmode. Hellstone releases a half-tile of lava when mined in The Underworld. Hellstone inflicts the Burning debuff on players who touch it, which can be negated through items such as the Obsidian Skull and Obsidian Skin Potion.

Hellstone Bar.name: Hellstone Bar
Hellstone Bar.tooltip: The Hellstone Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar. It is used to craft some of the most powerful equipment available pre-Hardmode, and remains useful, if not necessary, in dealing with the shift in difficulty upon entering Hardmode. Notably, the Molten Pickaxe is the only pre-Hardmode pickaxe capable of mining the first tier of Hardmode ores, Cobalt and Palladium.

Mud Block.name: Mud Block
Mud Block.tooltip: Mud Blocks are a very common block type that comprises the majority of the Jungle, Underground Jungle, and Glowing Mushroom biome. It also generates in irregular patches in the Cavern layer. Mud Blocks may be covered by Jungle grass, Mushroom grass, Corrupt grass, or Crimson grass on any side, which can be planted with Jungle Grass Seeds, Mushroom Grass Seeds, Corrupt Seeds, and Crimson Seeds. Only Jungle grass and Mushroom grass are incapable of growing on Dirt Blocks.

Sapphire.name: Sapphire
Sapphire.tooltip: Sapphire is a gem found within the Underground and Cavern layers of a world. It can craft the its corresponding set of standard gem items, and has no exclusive recipes. It can be obtained in the following ways: Mining the naturally generated placed form, Gemstone Blocks form with noticeable blue gemstones embedded in it, or Gem stash background object form. Extracting from Silt, Slush, or Desert Fossil by putting them in an Extractinator. Harvesting Sapphire gem trees. Dropping from Geodes with a 2/7 (28.57%) chance. Rarely, Sapphire can be found in bulk in its own Gemstone Cave micro-biome, or in one that contains other gems as well. Like all other gems, Sapphire can be placed on blocks, and can be crafted back into its Gemstone Block form at a Heavy Assembler in a Graveyard biome.

Ruby.name: Ruby
Ruby.tooltip: Ruby is a gem found within the Underground and Cavern layers of a world. It can craft the its corresponding set of standard gem items, and it also has two exclusive recipes: the Gold Crown and the Platinum Crown. It can be obtained in the following ways: Mining the naturally generated placed form, Gemstone Blocks form with noticeable red gemstones embedded in it, or Gem stash background object form. Extracting from Silt, Slush, or Desert Fossil by putting them in an Extractinator. Harvesting Ruby gem trees. Dropping from Geodes with a 2/7 (28.57%) chance. Rarely, Ruby can be found in bulk in its own Gemstone Cave micro-biome, or in one that contains other gems as well. Like all other gems, Ruby can be placed on blocks, and can be crafted back into its Gemstone Block form at a Heavy Assembler in a Graveyard biome.

Emerald.name: Emerald
Emerald.tooltip: Emerald is a gem found within the Underground and Cavern layers of a world. It can craft the its corresponding set of standard gem items, and has no exclusive recipes. It can be obtained in the following ways: Mining the naturally generated placed form, Gemstone Blocks form with noticeable green gemstones embedded in it, or Gem stash background object form. Extracting from Silt, Slush, or Desert Fossil by putting them in an Extractinator. Harvesting Emerald gem trees. Dropping from Geodes with a 2/7 (28.57%) chance. Rarely, Emerald can be found in bulk in its own Gemstone Cave micro-biome, or in one that contains other gems as well. Like all other gems, Emerald can be placed on blocks, and can be crafted back into its Gemstone Block form at a Heavy Assembler in a Graveyard biome.

Topaz.name: Topaz
Topaz.tooltip: Topaz is a gem found within the Underground and Cavern layers of a world. It is the second-least valuable gem available, being able to craft the its corresponding set of standard gem items, and it also has two exclusive recipes: the Sandgun and the Magiluminescence. They can be obtained in the following ways: Mining the naturally generated placed form, Gemstone Blocks form with noticeable yellow gemstones embedded in it, or Gem stash background object form. Extracting from Silt, Slush, or Desert Fossil by putting them in an Extractinator. Harvesting Topaz gem trees. Dropping from Geodes with a 2/7 (28.57%) chance. Rarely, Topaz can be found in bulk in its own Gemstone Cave micro-biome, or in one that contains other gems as well. Like all other gems, Topaz can be placed on blocks, and can be crafted back into its Gemstone Block form at a Heavy Assembler in a Graveyard biome.

Amethyst.name: Amethyst
Amethyst.tooltip: Amethyst is a gem found within the Underground and Cavern layers of a world. Out of all available gems, Amethyst is the least valuable gem, being able to craft the its corresponding set of standard gem items, and has no exclusive recipes. It can be obtained in the following ways: Mining the naturally generated placed form, Gemstone Blocks form with noticeable purple gemstones embedded in it, or Gem stash background object form. Extracting from Silt, Slush, or Desert Fossil by putting them in an Extractinator. Harvesting Amethyst gem trees. Dropping from Geodes with a 2/7 (28.57%) chance. Rarely, Amethyst can be found in bulk in its own Gemstone Cave micro-biome, or in one that contains other gems as well. Like all other gems, Amethyst can be placed on blocks, and can be crafted back into its Gemstone Block form at a Heavy Assembler in a Graveyard biome.

Diamond.name: Diamond
Diamond.tooltip: Diamond is a gem found within the Underground and Cavern layers of a world. Out of all available gems, Diamond is the most valuable gem, being able to craft its corresponding set of standard gem items, and it also has two exclusive recipes: the Magic Mirror and the Diamond Toilet. It can be obtained in the following ways: Mining the naturally generated placed form, Gemstone Blocks form with noticeable white gemstones embedded in it, or Gem stash background object form. Extracting from Silt, Slush, or Desert Fossil by putting them in an Extractinator. Harvesting Diamond gem trees. Dropping from Geodes with a 2/7 (28.57%) chance. Rarely, Diamond can be found in bulk in its own Gemstone Cave micro-biome, or in one that contains other gems as well. Like all other gems, Diamond can be placed on blocks, and can be crafted back into its Gemstone Block form at a Heavy Assembler in a Graveyard biome.

Glowing Mushroom.name: Glowing Mushroom
Glowing Mushroom.tooltip: The Glowing Mushroom is a plant, crafting material, and block that can be found on Mushroom grass in the Glowing Mushroom biome. Glowing Mushroom plants emit blue light. Instead of being placed as a plant, Glowing Mushroom items are placed as solid blocks. Glowing Mushroom items can be obtained by destroying Glowing Mushroom plants, cutting down Giant Glowing Mushrooms, and destroying Mushroom vines and cattails. Doing so will also yield Mushroom Grass Seeds.

Star.name: Star
Star.tooltip: Stars (or Soul Cakes during Halloween and Sugar Plums during Christmas) are common power-ups which can be dropped by any enemy with a chance of 13/24 (54.17%), as long as the closest player does not have full mana. They are not inventory items, but are instead instantly consumed, restoring 100 mana and providing the Mana Surge buff, which increases magic damage by up to 20% for a brief duration. It is also possible to spawn Stars (and their seasonal counterparts) with a Star Statue. Stars can be collected within a range of 2.625 tiles, which can be increased with a Celestial Magnet (and its upgrades) to 21.375 tiles.

Ivy Whip.name: Ivy Whip
Ivy Whip.tooltip: Hooks are a class of tools which aid the player in traversing terrain. When used, hooks fire a chain that latches to a surface or platform and pulls the player towards it. A hook is an essential tool which offers significant freedom from terrain height restrictions as well as being a fast movement option, and will often be the first major mobility tool a player acquires. A variety of hooks are available at all stages of the game (see table below). The Grapple hotkey activates the equipped hook in the player's equipment slot, or the first hook from the inventory (from left to right, top to bottom) without requiring it to be in the player's hotbar.Verify Several higher-tier hooks, such as the Ivy Whip, allow the player to grapple multiple surfaces simultaneously. If the character grapples one surface, then fires the hook a second time, another chain extends from the player without dislodging the first. Upon grappling a second surface, the player will be suspended in midair at a point midway between the two surfaces. This allows players more freedom during construction, or for navigating hazardous areas, such as above lava or Meteorite. All Journey Mode characters will spawn with the basic Grappling Hook already in their inventory.

Breathing Reed.name: Breathing Reed
Breathing Reed.tooltip: The Breathing Reed is a tool that aids in underwater breathing, and also functions as a broadsword. It has a 9/40 (22.5%) chance of being found in Water Chests, Ocean Crates, and Seaside Crates. When selected, the Breathing Reed is held above the player. This slows down the rate at which their breath meter depletes, and halves the rate at which they lose health while drowning. The reed's tip does not need to be above the surface of the water for this to take effect. The player's breath meter refills as soon as the tip of the reed is outside of water, but not within a block. Its best modifier is Legendary.
Breathing Reed.drops_summary: Ocean Crate (22.5%), Seaside Crate (22.5%), Water Chest (22.5%)

Flipper.name: Flipper
Flipper.tooltip: The Flipper is an accessory that allows a player to swim in liquids. When equipped, the player can swim upwards in any liquid by holding or pressing ↷ Jump repeatedly – essentially allowing unlimited multi-jumps while within liquid. It can be found in Water Chests and Ocean/Seaside Crates.
Flipper.drops_summary: Ocean Crate (22.5%), Seaside Crate (22.5%), Water Chest (22.5%)

Healing Potion.name: Healing Potion
Healing Potion.tooltip: The Healing Potion is a pre-Hardmode recovery potion that restores 100 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for 60 seconds when used. This duration can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths. It is the second tier of healing potion, succeeding the Lesser Healing Potion and preceding the Greater Healing Potion, Jungle Juice and Super Healing Potion. In addition to being crafted, Healing Potions can be found naturally in pots during Hardmode and pots in the Underworld in pre-Hardmode. Healing Potions are also dropped by Deerclops, Skeletron, and the Wall of Flesh, and are sold by the Merchant and the Skeleton Merchant in Hardmode for 10 Silver.
Healing Potion.drops_summary: Most crates (25%), Deerclops (100%), Gold Chest (50%), +2 more

Mana Potion.name: Mana Potion
Mana Potion.tooltip: The Mana Potion is a recovery potion that restores 100 mana and inflicts the Mana Sickness debuff upon use. It can be crafted or occasionally obtained from any Crates except for Wooden and Pearlwood Crates. They are also sold by the Merchant in Hardmode for 2 Silver 50 Copper. It is the second tier of mana potion, succeeding the Lesser Mana Potion, and preceding the Greater Mana Potion and Super Mana Potion.

Blade of Grass.name: Blade of Grass
Blade of Grass.tooltip: The Blade of Grass is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. When swung, it fires a Leaf Blade projectile that travels upwards in a circle and homes in on enemies. The Leaf Blade projectile can pass through blocks, deals 25% of the weapon's damage (4 base damage), has 20 armor penetration, and can pierce two enemies. The sword and its projectiles both have a 1/4 (25%) chance of inflicting the Poisoned debuff for 7 seconds upon hit. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Thorn Chakram.name: Thorn Chakram
Thorn Chakram.tooltip: The Thorn Chakram is a pre-Hardmode boomerang. Unlike most boomerangs, it does not necessarily return immediately upon contact with objects, but instead can bounce off blocks before returning. The Thorn Chakram has a 1/2 (50%) chance to inflict the Poisoned debuff. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Obsidian Brick.name: Obsidian Brick
Obsidian Brick.tooltip: The Obsidian Brick is a brick-block mainly used for building. It can be crafted at a Furnace or mined by any tier of pickaxe. It is commonly found in the Underworld's Ruined Houses.

Obsidian Skull.name: Obsidian Skull
Obsidian Skull.tooltip: The Obsidian Skull is a pre-Hardmode immunity accessory that grants +1 defense and immunity to the Burning debuff inflicted upon contact with Meteorite, Hellstone, Hellstone Bricks, or Ancient Hellstone Bricks. It does not grant immunity to lava or fire-based attacks. In For the Worthy(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Zenith(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) worlds, the Obsidian Skull also protects against the Burning debuff inflicted by contact with Crispy Honey Blocks.

Mushroom Grass Seeds.name: Mushroom Grass Seeds
Mushroom Grass Seeds.tooltip: Mushroom Grass Seeds are seeds that have a 1/40 (2.5%) chance to drop from harvesting Glowing Mushrooms. The seeds can also be purchased from the Dryad for 1 Silver 50 Copper each if she is spoken to in a Glowing Mushroom biome. Shaking a Giant Glowing Mushroom occasionally yields Mushroom Grass Seeds as well. They can also be obtained by using Poo on an Extractinator. Mushroom Grass Seeds must be planted on Mud Blocks and can be grown both above and under ground. Once planted, Mushroom grass will begin to spread to adjacent Mud Blocks and grow Glowing Mushrooms, as well as Giant Glowing Mushrooms when enough space is available. Mushroom grass spreads much slower than ordinary or Corrupt grass, at a speed comparable to Jungle grass – 3–5 tiles per day for each continuous section of Mud Blocks. Mushroom grass, as well as the mushrooms that grow on it, emit moderate light.

Jungle Grass Seeds.name: Jungle Grass Seeds
Jungle Grass Seeds.tooltip: Jungle Grass Seeds are seeds used to plant Jungle grass in Mud Blocks, which can potentially create an artificial Jungle or Underground Jungle (depending on depth) if enough Jungle grass and plants are created. Jungle Grass Seeds can be found by cutting down plants growing on Jungle grass using virtually any tool or weapon. They can also be obtained from putting Poo into an Extractinator, with an 0.67% chance per item.

Wooden Hammer.name: Wooden Hammer
Wooden Hammer.tooltip: The Wooden Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and either Agile or Forceful/Strong for combat purposes, due to its unusually low base damage.

Star Cannon.name: Star Cannon
Star Cannon.tooltip: The Star Cannon is a pre-Hardmode ranged weapon that consumes and fires Fallen Stars. The projectiles are not affected by gravity, pierce an infinite amount of enemies, and dissipate after 1 minute or upon impact with a block. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Blue Phaseblade.name: Blue Phaseblade
Blue Phaseblade.tooltip: Phaseblades are a group of pre-Hardmode broadswords. There are nine different color variations with identical statistics. Letting go of ⚒ Use / Attack while swinging will throw the weapons, causing them to sharply drop down after traveling for 0.5 seconds or upon contact with blocks, then embed themselves in the ground and continuously damage any enemy that touches them. They can be recalled by pressing ⚒ Use / Attack again, which will damage enemies along the way. They can also be recalled mid-throw. All phaseblades emit a small amount of light corresponding to their color when swung, thrown, or embedded in the ground. Phasesabers are the Hardmode upgrades of the phaseblades. Their best modifier is Legendary.

Meteor Hamaxe.name: Meteor Hamaxe
Meteor Hamaxe.tooltip: The Meteor Hamaxe is a pre-Hardmode hamaxe. It combines the functionality of a hammer and an axe. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Empty Bucket.name: Empty Bucket
Empty Bucket.tooltip: Buckets are tools used to carry water, lava, or honey, allowing them to be removed or placed. With an Empty Bucket, pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button on any sufficient body of liquid collects it, which replaces the Empty Bucket with the respective Water Bucket, Lava Bucket, or Honey Bucket. Pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button again will deposit the liquid at the location of the cursor, wherein the filled bucket is again replaced with an Empty Bucket. Each bucket holds one tile of liquid. Shimmer cannot be collected with standard buckets. When an Empty Bucket is dropped as an item into the world (with the Throw button) while it is raining, and there are no background walls behind the dropped item, it will turn into a Water Bucket after some time has passed. Empty Buckets will not fill under Rain Clouds or Magic Droppers. The Bottomless Water Bucket, Bottomless Lava Bucket and Bottomless Honey Bucket act as infinite water, lava, and honey placing buckets, whereas the Super Absorbant Sponge, Lava Absorbant Sponge, and Honey Absorbant Sponge are essentially infinite Empty Buckets that accept only water, lava or honey, respectively. They also add and remove liquids at a slightly faster speed than their normal bucket counterparts (especially when moving the cursor around while filling/draining).

Water Bucket.tooltip: Buckets are tools used to carry water, lava, or honey, allowing them to be removed or placed.
