Jungle Rose.name: Jungle Rose
Jungle Rose.tooltip: The Jungle Rose is a vanity accessory which can be harvested from the floor of the Jungle and Underground Jungle. Certain small red flowers growing on Jungle grass have a 1/20 (5%) chance to drop the item when cut. The Jungle Rose cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Stinger.name: Stinger
Stinger.tooltip: The Stinger is a crafting material used in various Jungle-themed crafting recipes. It is obtained from Spiked Jungle Slimes, Hornets, and Moss Hornets found in the Underground Jungle biome. Excluding the consumable items, crafting all items requires 58 Stingers.
Stinger.drops_summary: Hornet (66%), Moss Hornet (16.67%), Spiked Jungle Slime (50%)

Vine.name: Vine
Vine.tooltip: Vines are crafting materials dropped by Man Eaters in the Underground Jungle biome with a 1/2 (50%) / 100% drop chance.

Feral Claws.name: Feral Claws
Feral Claws.tooltip: Feral Claws are a pre-Hardmode accessory that can be found in Jungle Crates, Bramble Crates, and Ivy Chests located in Jungle Shrines and at the base of a Living Mahogany Tree in the Underground Jungle. While equipped, it grants the following effects: Enables autoswing for all melee weapons and whips +12% melee speed
Feral Claws.drops_summary: Bramble Crate (19%), Ivy Chest (21.72%), Jungle Crate (19%)

Anklet of the Wind.name: Anklet of the Wind
Anklet of the Wind.tooltip: The Anklet of the Wind is an accessory that gives a 10% bonus to movement speed. The effect also stacks with the movement speed bonus of the Aglet. It can be found in Jungle and Bramble Crates with a 19% chance, and also in Ivy Chests located in Jungle Shrines and at the base of a Living Mahogany Tree in the Underground Jungle with a 21.72% chance.
Anklet of the Wind.drops_summary: Bramble Crate (19%), Ivy Chest (21.72%), Jungle Crate (19%)

Staff of Regrowth.name: Staff of Regrowth
Staff of Regrowth.tooltip: The Staff of Regrowth is a multi-function tool that can be found in Ivy Chests, Jungle Crates, and Bramble Crates. It has the following functions: It grows Grass on Dirt Blocks, without consuming Grass Seeds. When swung, it breaks directly-targeted vegetation only. It only harvests blooming herbs, and Smart Cursor only targets blooming herbs. Even when they are directly targeted, it will not break immature herbs, nor harvest non-blooming mature herbs. It increases the yield of harvested herbs and seeds. It automatically replants herbs harvested from Planter Boxes and Clay Pots, without consuming seeds. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.
Staff of Regrowth.drops_summary: Bramble Crate (19%), Ivy Chest (21.72%), Jungle Crate (19%)

Hellstone Brick.name: Hellstone Brick
Hellstone Brick.tooltip: Hellstone Bricks are placeable blocks that occur naturally in unique Ruined Houses, though they can also be crafted. Like plain Hellstone, players without an Obsidian Skull or one of its upgrades in their accessory slot will receive the Burning debuff from making contact with the brick. Mining the block or carrying it in one's inventory incurs no negative effect, however. As with most damaging blocks, NPCs and enemies are immune to this damage. Unlike Hellstone itself, Hellstone Bricks are always vulnerable to explosions.

Whoopie Cushion.name: Whoopie Cushion
Whoopie Cushion.tooltip: The Whoopie Cushion is a voice accessory that makes a farting sound when the player takes damage while it is equipped. It can also be used with the ⚒ Use / Attack key to play the sound at any time. The Whoopie Cushion has a 1/50 (2%) / 99/2500 (3.96%) chance of being dropped by Giant Worms and Diggers in the Underground and Cavern layers. It can also be obtained by throwing a Zombie Arm into Shimmer. The Whoopie Cushion cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Shackle.name: Shackle
Shackle.tooltip: The Shackle is an accessory that grants 1 point of defense. It is dropped by most kinds of Zombies with a 1/50 (2%) chance. Shackles may be useful early in the game when only few accessories are available. Typically, they should be replaced with more valuable accessories once out of free slots.

Molten Hamaxe.name: Molten Hamaxe
Molten Hamaxe.tooltip: The Molten Hamaxe is a pre-Hardmode hamaxe. It has a chance to inflict the On Fire! debuff on enemy hits. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Flamelash.name: Flamelash
Flamelash.tooltip: The Flamelash is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron wand. When used, it fires a fireball that follows the cursor when ⚒ Use / Attack key is held. If the ⚒ Use / Attack key is released mid-drag, the fireball will be fired in that direction. If the cursor is stationary on release, it is fired directly away from the player. Once it is released, the fireball homes in on nearby enemies and can pierce once, creating a small explosion upon contact with a block or second enemy. It also has a 1/2 (50%) chance of inflicting the On Fire! debuff for 4–8 seconds. The Flamelash has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Shadow Chests in the Underworld, as well as a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Obsidian Lock Boxs obtained from Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Phoenix Blaster.name: Phoenix Blaster
Phoenix Blaster.tooltip: The Phoenix Blaster is a pre-Hardmode gun and the direct upgrade to the Handgun, with increased damage and velocity but slightly less knockback. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Sunfury.name: Sunfury
Sunfury.tooltip: The Sunfury is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron flail that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Shadow Chests in the Underworld, as well as a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Obsidian Lock Boxes obtained from Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates. It has a 1/4 (25%) chance to inflict the On Fire! debuff for 3 seconds on hit. The Sunfury also has a base 11% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. If the Blue Moon is also in the player's inventory, then the Blue Moon will be thrown out at the same time as the Sunfury, but in the mirrored direction. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Hellforge.name: Hellforge
Hellforge.tooltip: The Hellforge is a crafting station that functions as a regular Furnace, with the additional ability of smelting Hellstone into Hellstone Bars. It is also used to craft the essential Adamantite/Titanium Forge in Hardmode. Like its predecessor, it emits light when placed and is not a valid light source for housing. The Hellforge cannot be crafted, and is instead found in Ruined Houses in the Underworld or obtained from Obsidian Crates or Hellstone Crates. It can only be collected from the Underworld with tools with at least 65% pickaxe power, i.e. a Deathbringer/Nightmare Pickaxe or better is required. It cannot be broken by explosives during pre-Hardmode.

Clay Pot.name: Clay Pot
Clay Pot.tooltip: The Clay Pot is a furniture item in which a herb or flower seed can be planted. If left empty, wild grass plants will randomly grow out of it, provided the pot is placed on the surface or in Space. The plant in a Clay Pot cannot be cut in the regular manner, e.g. via nearby swinging tools. Instead, it needs to be removed with a pickaxe, a drill, the Staff of Regrowth, or the Axe of Regrowth(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

Nature's Gift.name: Nature's Gift
Nature's Gift.tooltip: Nature's Gift is an accessory that reduces the mana cost of using magic weapons and other mana-consuming items by 6%. It is acquired by harvesting a rare flower that grows on Jungle grass in the Underground Jungle, using any weapon or tool. The flower appears as a blue version of the Jungle Rose.

Bed.name: Bed
Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration. Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 craftable Beds and 5 that can be acquired from the environment. All Beds are functionally identical and differ only in appearance.

Silk.name: Silk
Silk.tooltip: Silk is an item used to craft the Bed, as well as several placeable decorative items and vanity clothing items.

Lesser Restoration Potion.name: Lesser Restoration Potion
Lesser Restoration Potion.tooltip: The Lesser Restoration Potion is a recovery potion that combines the effects of the Lesser Healing Potion and Lesser Mana Potion. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Lesser Restoration Potions were removed after updating to any version equal to 1.4.0.1. Any Lesser Restoration Potions existing in world are replaced with Restoration Potions.

Restoration Potion.name: Restoration Potion
Restoration Potion.tooltip: The Restoration Potion is a recovery potion that can be found in Shadow Chests in the Underworld. When used, it restores 90 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for only 45 seconds (rather than the usual 60 of health-restoring potions). The duration of Potion Sickness can be reduced to 33.75 seconds via the Philosopher's Stone, Charm of Myths or Catalyst Band. Despite its appearance, the Restoration Potion is not created by upgrading a Lesser Restoration Potion.

Jungle Hat.name: Jungle Hat
Jungle Hat.tooltip: Jungle armor is a pre-Hardmode mage armor set consisting of the Jungle Shirt, Jungle Hat, and Jungle Pants. Crafting a full set requires a total of 32 Jungle Spores, 2 Vines, and 10 Stingers. Jungle armor pieces are interchangeable with Ancient Cobalt armor pieces, still providing the set bonus but not the grass particle effect. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +17 defense +6% magic damage +12% magic critical strike chance +80 maximum mana +16% mana cost reduction The player also emits visual grass particles while moving.

Jungle Shirt.name: Jungle Shirt
Jungle Shirt.tooltip: Jungle armor is a pre-Hardmode mage armor set consisting of the Jungle Shirt, Jungle Hat, and Jungle Pants. Crafting a full set requires a total of 32 Jungle Spores, 2 Vines, and 10 Stingers. Jungle armor pieces are interchangeable with Ancient Cobalt armor pieces, still providing the set bonus but not the grass particle effect. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +17 defense +6% magic damage +12% magic critical strike chance +80 maximum mana +16% mana cost reduction The player also emits visual grass particles while moving.

Jungle Pants.name: Jungle Pants
Jungle Pants.tooltip: Jungle armor is a pre-Hardmode mage armor set consisting of the Jungle Shirt, Jungle Hat, and Jungle Pants. Crafting a full set requires a total of 32 Jungle Spores, 2 Vines, and 10 Stingers. Jungle armor pieces are interchangeable with Ancient Cobalt armor pieces, still providing the set bonus but not the grass particle effect. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +17 defense +6% magic damage +12% magic critical strike chance +80 maximum mana +16% mana cost reduction The player also emits visual grass particles while moving.

Molten Helmet.name: Molten Helmet
Molten Helmet.tooltip: Molten armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Molten Helmet, Molten Breastplate, and Molten Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 45 Hellstone Bars (135 Hellstone and 45 Obsidian). The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +25 defense +17% melee damage +7% melee critical strike chance +7% melee speed Immunity to the On Fire! and Burning debuffs The player also leaves behind a visual trail of flames.

Molten Breastplate.name: Molten Breastplate
Molten Breastplate.tooltip: Molten armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Molten Helmet, Molten Breastplate, and Molten Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 45 Hellstone Bars (135 Hellstone and 45 Obsidian). The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +25 defense +17% melee damage +7% melee critical strike chance +7% melee speed Immunity to the On Fire! and Burning debuffs The player also leaves behind a visual trail of flames.

Molten Greaves.name: Molten Greaves
Molten Greaves.tooltip: Molten armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Molten Helmet, Molten Breastplate, and Molten Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 45 Hellstone Bars (135 Hellstone and 45 Obsidian). The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +25 defense +17% melee damage +7% melee critical strike chance +7% melee speed Immunity to the On Fire! and Burning debuffs The player also leaves behind a visual trail of flames.

Meteor Shot.name: Meteor Shot
Meteor Shot.tooltip: The Meteor Shot is a pre-Hardmode bullet. When fired, it can either bounce from a solid block once or pierce through one enemy, but not both.

Sticky Bomb.name: Sticky Bomb
Sticky Bomb.tooltip: The Sticky Bomb is an explosive that functions like the Bomb, but sticks onto any block on contact. If the block it sticks to is removed by some means, it will fall until it hits another.

Black Lens.name: Black Lens
Black Lens.tooltip: The Black Lens is a crafting material dropped by Demon Eyes and Wandering Eyes at a 1/100 (1%) chance.

Sunglasses.name: Sunglasses
Sunglasses.tooltip: The Sunglasses are a vanity item equipped in the social helmet slot. While equipped, the sun in the background will change to its pre-1.2 variant wearing sunglasses as well. Cattiva will also appear wearing sunglasses when equipped.

Wizard Hat.name: Wizard Hat
Wizard Hat.tooltip: The Wizard Hat is a pre-Hardmode armor piece that can be equipped in the helmet slot. While equipped, it grants +4 defense and increases the player's magic damage by 5%. It is always dropped by Tim. The Wizard Hat is part of the Wizard set, which further consists of a Mystic Robe or any gem-augmented Robe. The Wizard set provides a Set Bonus of +10% magic critical strike chance with the Wizard Hat equipped. The Wizard Hat's alternative is the Magic Hat.

Top Hat.name: Top Hat
Top Hat.tooltip: The Tuxedo set is a vanity set consisting of the Top Hat, Tuxedo Shirt and Tuxedo Pants. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. While the other two pieces are crafted, the Top Hat is instead dropped by The Groom.

Tuxedo Shirt.name: Tuxedo Shirt
Tuxedo Shirt.tooltip: The Tuxedo set is a vanity set consisting of the Top Hat, Tuxedo Shirt and Tuxedo Pants. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. While the other two pieces are crafted, the Top Hat is instead dropped by The Groom.

Tuxedo Pants.name: Tuxedo Pants
Tuxedo Pants.tooltip: The Tuxedo set is a vanity set consisting of the Top Hat, Tuxedo Shirt and Tuxedo Pants. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. While the other two pieces are crafted, the Top Hat is instead dropped by The Groom.

Summer Hat.name: Summer Hat
Summer Hat.tooltip: The Summer Hat is a vanity item equipped in the Social Helmet Slot. It is purchased from the Clothier for 1 Gold, when he is spoken to during the day outside of a Graveyard.

Bunny Hood.name: Bunny Hood
Bunny Hood.tooltip: The Bunny Hood is a vanity headgear item. It has a 1/75 (1.33%) chance of being dropped by Corrupt Bunnies and Vicious Bunnies(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). On the Nintendo 3DS version, it can also be dropped by Diseaster Bunnies or Lepus.

Plumber's Hat.name: Plumber's Hat
Plumber's Hat.tooltip: The Plumber's set is a vanity set made up of the Plumber's Hat, the Plumber's Shirt, and the Plumber's Pants. The hat has a 1/250 (0.4%) chance to be dropped by Fire Imps, while the shirt and pants are purchased from the Clothier for 25 Gold each, during a full moon. These items are purely vanity items and provide no increase in defense or other bonuses.

Plumber's Shirt.name: Plumber's Shirt
Plumber's Shirt.tooltip: The Plumber's set is a vanity set made up of the Plumber's Hat, the Plumber's Shirt, and the Plumber's Pants. The hat has a 1/250 (0.4%) chance to be dropped by Fire Imps, while the shirt and pants are purchased from the Clothier for 25 Gold each, during a full moon. These items are purely vanity items and provide no increase in defense or other bonuses.

Plumber's Pants.name: Plumber's Pants
Plumber's Pants.tooltip: The Plumber's set is a vanity set made up of the Plumber's Hat, the Plumber's Shirt, and the Plumber's Pants. The hat has a 1/250 (0.4%) chance to be dropped by Fire Imps, while the shirt and pants are purchased from the Clothier for 25 Gold each, during a full moon. These items are purely vanity items and provide no increase in defense or other bonuses.

Hero's Hat.name: Hero's Hat
Hero's Hat.tooltip: The Hero's set is a vanity set composed of the Hero's Hat, the Hero's Shirt, and the Hero's Pants. Crafting the entire set requires 420 Cobwebs and 27 Jungle Grass Seeds as base ingredients. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Hero's Shirt.name: Hero's Shirt
Hero's Shirt.tooltip: The Hero's set is a vanity set composed of the Hero's Hat, the Hero's Shirt, and the Hero's Pants. Crafting the entire set requires 420 Cobwebs and 27 Jungle Grass Seeds as base ingredients. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Hero's Pants.name: Hero's Pants
Hero's Pants.tooltip: The Hero's set is a vanity set composed of the Hero's Hat, the Hero's Shirt, and the Hero's Pants. Crafting the entire set requires 420 Cobwebs and 27 Jungle Grass Seeds as base ingredients. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Fish Bowl.name: Fish Bowl
Fish Bowl.tooltip: The Fish Bowl, Gold Fish Bowl (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Pupfish Bowl (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Lava Serpent Bowl (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are decorative furniture items. The Fish Bowl and Gold Fish Bowl also double as wearable items that can be equipped in the player's helmet slot. Fish Bowls cause only visual effects when placed in the helmet vanity slot. When instead placed in the functional head armor slot, the breath meter appears as if the player were underwater, and if worn long enough the player will drown and die. Breathing aids like the Breathing Reed or Gills Potion will allow for normal breathing when wearing the bowl. The Fish, Gold Fish and Pupfish Bowls are crafted, while the Lava Serpent Bowl has a 39/200 (19.5%) chance of being found inside Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates. Crafted Fish Bowls can be converted back into their ingredients by throwing them into Shimmer, gaining back the fish as an item.

Archaeologist's Hat.name: Archaeologist's Hat
Archaeologist's Hat.tooltip: The Archaeologist's set is a vanity set composed of the Archaeologist's Hat, the Archaeologist's Jacket and the Archaeologist's Pants. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. While two of the pieces are crafted, the Archaeologist's Hat is not, but rather has a guaranteed chance to drop from Doctor Bones. It is possible to craft these items in a world that has The Crimson instead of The Corruption by creating an artificial Corruption, by bringing Leather over from a world with the Corruption, or by using a Corrupt Statue to spawn Eaters of Souls.

Archaeologist's Jacket.name: Archaeologist's Jacket
Archaeologist's Jacket.tooltip: The Archaeologist's set is a vanity set composed of the Archaeologist's Hat, the Archaeologist's Jacket and the Archaeologist's Pants. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. While two of the pieces are crafted, the Archaeologist's Hat is not, but rather has a guaranteed chance to drop from Doctor Bones. It is possible to craft these items in a world that has The Crimson instead of The Corruption by creating an artificial Corruption, by bringing Leather over from a world with the Corruption, or by using a Corrupt Statue to spawn Eaters of Souls.

Archaeologist's Pants.name: Archaeologist's Pants
Archaeologist's Pants.tooltip: The Archaeologist's set is a vanity set composed of the Archaeologist's Hat, the Archaeologist's Jacket and the Archaeologist's Pants. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. While two of the pieces are crafted, the Archaeologist's Hat is not, but rather has a guaranteed chance to drop from Doctor Bones. It is possible to craft these items in a world that has The Crimson instead of The Corruption by creating an artificial Corruption, by bringing Leather over from a world with the Corruption, or by using a Corrupt Statue to spawn Eaters of Souls.

Black Thread.name: Black Thread
Black Thread.tooltip: Threads are crafting materials used primarily in vanity items. Black Thread and Pink Thread can be purchased from the Clothier, while Green Thread can be crafted.

Green Thread.name: Green Thread
Green Thread.tooltip: Threads are crafting materials used primarily in vanity items. Black Thread and Pink Thread can be purchased from the Clothier, while Green Thread can be crafted.

Ninja Hood.name: Ninja Hood
Ninja Hood.tooltip: Ninja armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Ninja Hood, Ninja Shirt and Ninja Pants. King Slime drops each piece separately (1 per kill with a 1/3 (33.33%) chance each), or two pieces from the Treasure Bag it drops in Expert Mode. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +9 defense +9% critical strike chance +20% movement speed A visual afterimage while moving.

Ninja Shirt.name: Ninja Shirt
Ninja Shirt.tooltip: Ninja armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Ninja Hood, Ninja Shirt and Ninja Pants. King Slime drops each piece separately (1 per kill with a 1/3 (33.33%) chance each), or two pieces from the Treasure Bag it drops in Expert Mode. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +9 defense +9% critical strike chance +20% movement speed A visual afterimage while moving.

Ninja Pants.name: Ninja Pants
Ninja Pants.tooltip: Ninja armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Ninja Hood, Ninja Shirt and Ninja Pants. King Slime drops each piece separately (1 per kill with a 1/3 (33.33%) chance each), or two pieces from the Treasure Bag it drops in Expert Mode. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +9 defense +9% critical strike chance +20% movement speed A visual afterimage while moving.

Leather.name: Leather
Leather.tooltip: Leather is a crafting material that is used to create the Archaeologist's Jacket and the Archaeologist's Pants. It is made using Rotten Chunks, a material only obtainable in Corruption worlds. It cannot be obtained in a Crimson world unless the player makes an artificial Corruption biome (e.g. using Corrupt Seeds, purchased from the Dryad in a Graveyard(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)) or uses a Corrupt Statue.

Red Hat.name: Red Hat
Red Hat.tooltip: The Clothier's set is a vanity set consisting of the Red Hat, Clothier's Jacket(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Clothier's Pants(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. The Red Hat will always drop from the Clothier NPC. The other parts of the set are sold by the Clothier for 3 Gold each, during Halloween.

Goldfish.name: Goldfish
Goldfish.tooltip: The Goldfish is a critter that swims in water and walks on land during rain. It flops in place when out of water and rain; it does not take damage while doing so. The Goldfish has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Goldfish can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Fish Bowl). Once crafted, the Goldfish cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The Goldfish can be spawned by the Fish Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Goldfish to spawn in place of an ordinary one. During a Blood Moon, or when hit with Vile Powder/Vicious Powder(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Goldfish will turn into Corrupt Goldfish or Vicious Goldfish(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

Robe.name: Robe
Robe.tooltip: Robes are equipable items, most of which provide magic damage bonuses and are a part of the Wizard set. All gem robes are adapted from the Robe, a vanity item equipped in the shirt slot. They resemble the robes worn by Dark Casters and Tim. Gem staves and Gem robes have a unique mechanic called Gem enchantment, which modifies the projectile fired from gem staves by the ability of the corresponding gem type.

Robot Hat.name: Robot Hat
Robot Hat.tooltip: The Robot Hat is a vanity item equipped in the Social Helmet Slot. It has a 1/250 (0.4%) chance to drop from Piranhas and Angler Fish.

Gold Crown.name: Gold Crown
Gold Crown.tooltip: The Gold Crown is a craftable vanity item that can be worn in the Social Helmet inventory slot. It is also one of the crafting materials for the Slime Crown, which is used to spawn King Slime.  Its alternate ore counterpart is the Platinum Crown.

Hellfire Arrow.name: Hellfire Arrow
Hellfire Arrow.tooltip: The Hellfire Arrow is a pre-Hardmode arrow that explodes upon impact, damaging all enemies in a small area. Hellfire Arrows can be found in Shadow Chests and Pots in The Underworld, crafted at an anvil, or purchased from the Demolitionist for 1 Silver each in Hardmode.

Sandgun.name: Sandgun
Sandgun.tooltip: The Sandgun is a pre-Hardmode ranged weapon that fires sand ball projectiles that are affected by gravity. Upon contact with an enemy or block, the sand ball turns into its respective form of block (if the space is not occupied). Its sand balls have varying effects depending on which sand block is used for ammunition: Its best modifier is Unreal.

Guide Voodoo Doll.name: Guide Voodoo Doll
Guide Voodoo Doll.tooltip: The Guide Voodoo Doll is a boss-summoning item used to summon the Wall of Flesh. It is a guaranteed drop from Voodoo Demons, a fairly rare enemy in the Underworld. If the item is dropped and destroyed by lava in the Underworld, the Guide will instantly die and the Wall of Flesh will be summoned. The Guide must be alive for this process to occur. If the item is destroyed by lava elsewhere, the Guide will die as normal but the boss will not be summoned; if the item is destroyed by lava when the Guide is not alive, the item will be wasted without summoning the boss. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, if more than one Guide Voodoo Doll is in a stack upon being destroyed by lava, other NPCs will be killed alongside the Guide depending on the amount within the stack. However, the Wall of Flesh will only be summoned once. When the Guide Voodoo Doll is equipped as an accessory, it becomes possible for the player and other NPCs to kill the Guide with direct attacks from weapons (which normally would not damage him).  The Guide Voodoo Doll cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Diving Helmet.name: Diving Helmet
Diving Helmet.tooltip: The Diving Helmet is an armor piece for the helmet slot. It has a 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped by Sharks and Orcas. When equipped, it causes the breath meter to deplete much slower and slows the rate at which drowning damage is taken.

Familiar Shirt.name: Familiar Shirt
Familiar Shirt.tooltip: The Familiar set is a vanity set that displays the player's default clothes. It consists of the Familiar Wig, the Familiar Shirt, and the Familiar Pants, and can be purchased from the Clothier for 3 Gold (set). When a piece of the Familiar set is equipped in the vanity armor slot, it will disable the graphics of any item worn in the corresponding armor slot. As such, the Familiar Wig will show the character's hairstyle whereas the Familiar Shirt and Familiar Pants will show the character's default shirt and pants, respectively. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Familiar Pants.name: Familiar Pants
Familiar Pants.tooltip: The Familiar set is a vanity set that displays the player's default clothes. It consists of the Familiar Wig, the Familiar Shirt, and the Familiar Pants, and can be purchased from the Clothier for 3 Gold (set). When a piece of the Familiar set is equipped in the vanity armor slot, it will disable the graphics of any item worn in the corresponding armor slot. As such, the Familiar Wig will show the character's hairstyle whereas the Familiar Shirt and Familiar Pants will show the character's default shirt and pants, respectively. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Familiar Wig.name: Familiar Wig
Familiar Wig.tooltip: The Familiar set is a vanity set that displays the player's default clothes. It consists of the Familiar Wig, the Familiar Shirt, and the Familiar Pants, and can be purchased from the Clothier for 3 Gold (set). When a piece of the Familiar set is equipped in the vanity armor slot, it will disable the graphics of any item worn in the corresponding armor slot. As such, the Familiar Wig will show the character's hairstyle whereas the Familiar Shirt and Familiar Pants will show the character's default shirt and pants, respectively. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Demon Scythe.name: Demon Scythe
Demon Scythe.tooltip: The Demon Scythe is a pre-Hardmode spell book that has a 1/35 (2.86%) chance of being dropped by Demons and Voodoo Demons. When used, it fires a sickle projectile that is initially static before gradually accelerating. The sickles can hit up to five times before dissipating, and they cannot pass through blocks. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Night's Edge.name: Night's Edge
Night's Edge.tooltip: The Night's Edge is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron broadsword. When swung, a circular purple aura follows the swing, reaching slightly farther than the sword itself. Another aura swings towards the cursor, further increasing range. The auras can hit up to two enemies each, but the same enemy cannot be hit by both auras. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Dark Lance.name: Dark Lance
Dark Lance.tooltip: The Dark Lance is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron spear that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Shadow Chests in the Underworld, as well as a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Obsidian Lock Boxes obtained from Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates. The Dark Lance inflicts the Shadowflame debuff for 4–5 seconds and creates a small shockwave at its tip. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Coral.name: Coral
Coral.tooltip: Corals are crafting materials which can be found in the Ocean biomes at the ends of the world. They grow naturally on Sand Blocks underwater, within 380 tiles of the left or right edges of the world, and above the depth of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) −20 feet / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 0 feet, as long as no more than 5 Corals ((Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or Seashells) are within 7 tiles horizontally and vertically. Corals can be harvested either with a pickaxe/drill/explosives, by mining out the sand underneath them, or by placing a block above them. Afterwards, they can be placed on any type of block and will take on a random appearance out of six possible varieties. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Corals will spawn slower on sand under less than 5 tiles of water. Spawn rates scale with rain, wind, and empty space up to 14 tiles above the Sand Block. (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Corals will only spawn on sand under at least 5 tiles of water. Rain and wind do not affect spawn rates.

Cactus.name: Cactus
Cactus.tooltip: Cactus is a crafting material obtained by harvesting Cactus plants, using an axe or chainsaw just like with trees. In addition to crafting, Cactus can be used as a building material.

Trident.name: Trident
Trident.tooltip: The Trident is a pre-Hardmode spear that has a 9/40 (22.5%) chance of being found in Water Chests, Ocean Crates, and Seaside Crates. When held while submerged in water or lava, the player is granted increased movement speed and jump height. The player can decrease fall speed by holding ▲ Up. These effects do not work in honey or Shimmer. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Trident.drops_summary: Ocean Crate (22.5%), Seaside Crate (22.5%), Water Chest (22.5%)

Silver Bullet.name: Silver Bullet
Silver Bullet.tooltip: The Silver Bullet is a pre-Hardmode bullet. It deals 2 more damage and is slightly faster than Musket Balls. It also deals 300% damage to Werewolves. Silver Bullets can be bought from the Arms Dealer in worlds with Silver for 15 Copper each, or 1 Gold 50 Silver for 1000 rounds. During pre-Hardmode, they are only sold during Blood Moons. Once Hardmode begins, they are always available. Silver Bullets can also be found replacing Wooden Arrows in Pots during Hardmode, obtained from Shadow Chests, or crafted. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Tungsten Bullet.

Throwing Knife.name: Throwing Knife
Throwing Knife.tooltip: The Throwing Knife is a consumable ranged weapon. It can hit up to 2 targets. It can be purchased from the Merchant during a Blood Moon for 50 Copper each and may also be found in Chests. The Throwing Knife is greatly affected by gravity and arcs similarly to Shurikens and Bones. It has the greatest range out of these consumable ranged weapons (with Bones having the least). The Merchant will use Throwing Knives to defend himself against nearby enemies.

Spear.name: Spear
Spear.tooltip: The Spear is a pre-Hardmode spear that has a 1/11 (9.09%) chance of being found in Wooden Chests that are located on the surface as well as in the underground layer. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Blowpipe.name: Blowpipe
Blowpipe.tooltip: The Blowpipe is a pre-Hardmode ranged weapon that has a 1/11 (9.09%) chance of being obtained from wooden Chests on the Surface or in the Underground layer. When used, it fires Seeds and darts as ammunition. While a Blowpipe is in a player's inventory, there is a chance that any vegetation growing on normal grass, in Clay Pots, and in Planter Boxes will drop Seeds. Flowers typically drop 4 Seeds at a time, while tall grass typically drops 1–2 Seeds. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Glowstick.name: Glowstick
Glowstick.tooltip: The Glowstick is a consumable light source that can be held or tossed a fair distance.
Glowstick.drops_summary: Chest (16.67%), Flying Fish (100%), Gold Chest (25%), +3 more

Seed.name: Seed
Seed.tooltip: The Seed is a pre-Hardmode dart. While a Blowpipe or Blowgun is in a player's inventory, there is a chance that any vegetation growing on normal grass, in Clay Pots, and in Planter Boxes will drop Seeds. Flowers typically drop 4 Seeds at a time, while tall grass typically drops 1–2 Seeds.

Wooden Boomerang.name: Wooden Boomerang
Wooden Boomerang.tooltip: The Wooden Boomerang is a pre-Hardmode boomerang that has a 1/11 (9.09%) chance of being obtained from wooden Chests on the Surface or in the Underground layer. It can also be purchased from the Skeleton Merchant for 1 Gold during a full moon. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Aglet.name: Aglet
Aglet.tooltip: The Aglet is a pre-Hardmode movement accessory that increases the player's movement speed by 5%. The Aglet has a 1/11 (9.09%) chance of being found inside surface Chests, or a 1/120 (0.83%) chance in Wooden Crates and Pearlwood Crates obtained from fishing. It is also sold by the Skeleton Merchant for 2 Gold 50 Silver during a New Moon.

Sticky Glowstick.name: Sticky Glowstick
Sticky Glowstick.tooltip: The Sticky Glowstick is a consumable light source that behaves identically to the standard Glowstick, but sticks to any surface on contact, rather than ricocheting or rolling. After being thrown, a Sticky Glowstick will emit light for 5 minutes and expire afterward. Sticky Glowsticks can be crafted, and are sometimes dropped by Pots in the Underground Snow biome.

Poisoned Knife.name: Poisoned Knife
Poisoned Knife.tooltip: The Poisoned Knife is a consumable ranged weapon that has a 1/2 (50%) chance to inflict the Poisoned debuff. It otherwise behaves exactly like the Throwing Knife, except for having slightly better stats overall and auto-use. It can hit up to 2 targets.

Obsidian Skin Potion.name: Obsidian Skin Potion
Obsidian Skin Potion.tooltip: The Obsidian Skin Potion is a buff potion which grants the Obsidian Skin buff when consumed. The buff makes the player immune to lava and the On Fire! debuff. It also grants immunity to the Burning debuff from touching Meteorite, Hellstone, Hellstone Bricks, and Ancient Hellstone Bricks for its duration. This lasts for 6 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Obsidian Skin Potions can be found in pots and Shadow Chests in the Underworld, as well as in crates.
Obsidian Skin Potion.drops_summary: Most crates (4.17%), Golden Crate (6.67%), Iron Crate (3.13%), +5 more

Regeneration Potion.name: Regeneration Potion
Regeneration Potion.tooltip: The Regeneration Potion is a buff potion which grants the Regeneration buff when consumed. The buff provides health regeneration by restoring an additional 2 health per second, for a total of 960 health. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Regeneration Potions can be found in Pots and Chests.

Swiftness Potion.name: Swiftness Potion
Swiftness Potion.tooltip: The Swiftness Potion is a buff potion which grants the Swiftness buff when consumed. The buff increases the player's maximum movement speed by 25%, but does not stack with sprinting accessories (such as Hermes Boots), nor does it affect the speed of mounts. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Swiftness Potions can be found in pots, chests, and crates, and have a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes.
Swiftness Potion.drops_summary: Most slimes (0.18%), Chest (11.11%), Gold Chest (9.52%), +2 more

Gills Potion.name: Gills Potion
Gills Potion.tooltip: The Gills Potion is a buff potion which grants the Gills buff when consumed. The buff prevents the player's breath meter from depleting and thus prevents drowning. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Gills Potions can be found in Pots, Chests, and crates.
Gills Potion.drops_summary: Gold Chest (9.52%), Pearlwood Crate (1.43%), Wooden Crate (1.43%)

Ironskin Potion.name: Ironskin Potion
Ironskin Potion.tooltip: The Ironskin Potion is a buff potion that grants the Ironskin buff when consumed. The buff increases the player's defense by 8, thus reducing damage by 4 / 6 / 8. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Ironskin Potions can be found in Pots, Chests, and crates, and have a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes.
Ironskin Potion.drops_summary: Most slimes (0.18%), Chest (11.11%), Pearlwood Crate (1.43%), +1 more

Mana Regeneration Potion.name: Mana Regeneration Potion
Mana Regeneration Potion.tooltip: The Mana Regeneration Potion is a buff potion which grants the Mana Regeneration buff when consumed. The buff increases the rate at which the player's mana regenerates. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Mana Regeneration Potions can be found in Pots and Shadow Chests in The Underworld.

Magic Power Potion.name: Magic Power Potion
Magic Power Potion.tooltip: The Magic Power Potion is a buff potion which grants the Magic Power buff when consumed. The buff increases magic damage by 20%. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().  In addition to being crafted, Magic Power Potions can be found in Pots and Shadow Chests in The Underworld.

Featherfall Potion.name: Featherfall Potion
Featherfall Potion.tooltip: The Featherfall Potion is a buff potion which grants the Featherfall buff when consumed. The buff negates fall damage, and reduces the player's fall speed and gravity to 1/3 (33.33%) of normal, allowing them to jump higher and fall slower. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). While the buff is active, the player can also control their falling speed more precisely depending on the Hover Controls option in gameplay settings. The three available speeds are normal gravity, the default of 1/3rd normal gravity, and 10% of normal gravity. With the default hold control scheme, the player will experience normal gravity while the ▼ Down key is held, 10% gravity while the ▲ Up key is held, and 1/3rd gravity otherwise. With the click control scheme, their gravity will be set to 1/3rd upon touching and leaving the ground, and can be increased by one stage by pressing ▼ Down or decreased by one stage by pressing ▲ Up. The Featherfall buff also works with mounts and minecarts (except for the Bee Mount), and works during reversed gravity. Fall damage will be negated even if the player is falling at normal speed or is under the effects of the Stoned debuff. In addition to being crafted, Featherfall Potions can be found in pots and chests.

Spelunker Potion.name: Spelunker Potion
Spelunker Potion.tooltip: The Spelunker Potion is a buff potion which grants the Spelunker buff when consumed. The buff illuminates valuable nearby objects and highlights them with a yellow tint. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Spelunker buff highlights the following: Ores Gems Pots Herbs Dye plants Chests Life Crystals Life Fruit Statues Paintings Digtoise Huge Dragon Egg In addition to being crafted, Spelunker Potions can be found in Pots, Chests, and crates, and have a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes.
Spelunker Potion.drops_summary: Azure Crate (4.17%), Baby Slime (0.18%), Black Slime (0.18%), +32 more

Invisibility Potion.name: Invisibility Potion
Invisibility Potion.tooltip: The Invisibility Potion is a buff potion that grants the Invisibility buff when consumed. This lasts for 3 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The buff is furthermore immediately canceled if the player takes damage of any kind. The buff provides the following effects: The player becomes invisible, including their armor, vanity items, and mount. −17% enemy spawn rates and −20% maximum enemy spawn count. −750 aggro, meaning enemies will prefer to target other players, and many kinds of enemies will not chase after the player while they are not using items (see Aggro § Target chasing for details). This does not prevent enemies from firing projectiles at the player. Attacking or using any item will cause the player to reappear temporarily and reduce the aggro reduction bonus to –250. In addition to being crafted, Invisibility Potions can be found in Pots and Chests.

Shine Potion.name: Shine Potion
Shine Potion.tooltip: The Shine Potion is a buff potion which grants the Shine buff when consumed. The buff makes the player glow brightly, which is useful for exploring caves or while exploring underwater. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Shine Potions can be found in Pots, Chests, and Crates.
Shine Potion.drops_summary: Chest (11.11%), Gold Chest (9.52%), Pearlwood Crate (1.43%), +1 more

Night Owl Potion.name: Night Owl Potion
Night Owl Potion.tooltip: The Night Owl Potion is a buff potion that grants the Night Owl buff when consumed. The buff improves the player's night vision, and sharply increases the radius of any available light source. The buff itself has no effect in total darkness. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Night Owl Potions can be found in Pots, Chests, and Crates.
Night Owl Potion.drops_summary: Chest (11.11%), Gold Chest (9.52%), Pearlwood Crate (1.43%), +1 more

Battle Potion.name: Battle Potion
Battle Potion.tooltip: The Battle Potion is a buff potion which grants the Battle buff when consumed. The buff increases the spawn rate and maximum number of enemies and critters that can be on-screen at once by 100%, effectively doubling these rates. This lasts for 7 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().

Thorns Potion.name: Thorns Potion
Thorns Potion.tooltip: The Thorns Potion is a buff potion which grants the Thorns buff when consumed. The buff inflicts a knockback of 10 (Extremely strong) on enemies that come into contact with the player, and deals 100% of their damage to them. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Thorns Potions can be found in Pots and Chests.

Water Walking Potion.name: Water Walking Potion
Water Walking Potion.tooltip: The Water Walking Potion is a buff potion which grants the Water Walking buff when consumed. The buff allows the player to walk on the surface of all liquids (water, lava, honey, and Shimmer), and prevents fall damage when falling onto liquid surfaces. The player can sink into liquids by pressing ▼ Down. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Water Walking Potions can be found in pots and chests.

Archery Potion.name: Archery Potion
Archery Potion.tooltip: The Archery Potion is a buff potion which grants the Archery buff when consumed. The buff increases the damage of arrow-firing weapons by 10%, as well as the velocity of arrows by 20%. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Archery Potions can be found in Pots and Chests.

Hunter Potion.name: Hunter Potion
Hunter Potion.tooltip: The Hunter Potion is a buff potion which grants the Hunter buff when consumed. The buff shows the location of enemies, critters, and NPCs on the screen by highlighting them in red (enemies) or green (critters and NPCs). Although these affected entities glow, they do not emit any light to the surrounding area. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Hunter Potions can be found in Pots, Chests, and Crates.
Hunter Potion.drops_summary: Most crates (4.17%), Gold Chest (9.52%), Iron Crate (3.13%), +4 more

Gravitation Potion.name: Gravitation Potion
Gravitation Potion.tooltip: The Gravitation Potion is a buff potion which grants the Gravitation buff when consumed. The buff allows the player to invert gravity with ▲ Up, making the screen appear upside-down and causing the player to fall upwards and walk on top of ceilings. The effect can be toggled while in midair. This lasts for 3 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Gravitation Potions can be found in Pots, Chests, and crates.
Gravitation Potion.drops_summary: Most crates (4.17%), Gold Chest (11.11%), Golden Crate (6.67%), +4 more

Gold Chest.name: Gold Chest
Gold Chest.tooltip: The Gold Chest is a naturally-generated chest, with various loot as its contents. Each chest includes one special item, as well as some coins and other more common items. Gold Chests are found in Underground Cabins or randomly in the Underground and Cavern layers, as well as in the Pyramids. Apart from the initial items, Gold Chests function identically to other chests. Removing all items from a Gold Chest will allow it to be freed or broken with a pickaxe or drill. It can then be picked up, placed, and used just like any other chest, with 40 slots of storage space. There are only three minor differences to other chests: Gold Chests cannot be crafted and are only generated on world creation at the random locations; they can also be sold to an NPC at 10 Silver, which is more than the standard chest, which only sells for 1 Silver. Gold Chests have a sparkle effect when exposed to a light source, similar to coins.

Daybloom Seeds.name: Daybloom Seeds
Daybloom Seeds.tooltip: Daybloom Seeds are a type of seed that can be obtained from harvesting Dayblooms while they are blooming or using the Staff of Regrowth on naturally grown Dayblooms while they are fully grown. Daybloom will only bloom during daytime, showing off a sunflower-like head. Each plant will drop 1–3 Daybloom Seeds when harvested while blooming. Daybloom Seeds can be placed on pure and Hallowed grass (including Mowed grass and Mowed Hallowed grass), empty Clay Pots, or any types of Planter Boxes, and will grow into harvestable Dayblooms. They will grow anywhere, not just in direct sunlight on the Surface, but will only yield seeds when blooming.

Moonglow Seeds.name: Moonglow Seeds
Moonglow Seeds.tooltip: Moonglow Seeds are a type of seed that can be obtained from harvesting Moonglows while they are blooming or using the Staff of Regrowth on naturally grown Moonglows while they are fully grown. Moonglow will only bloom at night, and will glow and give off blue orbs of light. Each plant drops 1–3 Moonglow Seeds when harvested while blooming. Moonglow Seeds can be placed on Jungle grass, empty Clay Pots, or any types of Planter Boxes, and will grow into harvestable Moonglows. They will grow anywhere, not just in the Jungle, but will only yield seeds when blooming.

Blinkroot Seeds.name: Blinkroot Seeds
Blinkroot Seeds.tooltip: Blinkroot Seeds are a type of seed that can be obtained from harvesting Blinkroots while they are blooming or using the Staff of Regrowth on naturally grown Blinkroots while they are fully grown. A Blinkroot plant switches between its blooming and non-blooming state at random. Its blooming state can be identified by the yellow dots on the ends of its fronds and the blinking light it emits. Each plant will drop 1–3 Blinkroot Seeds when harvested while blooming. Blinkroot Seeds can be placed on Dirt and Mud Blocks, empty Clay Pots, or any types of Planter Boxes, and will grow into harvestable Blinkroots. They will grow anywhere, not just in the Underground, but will only yield seeds when blooming.

Deathweed Seeds.name: Deathweed Seeds
Deathweed Seeds.tooltip: Deathweed Seeds are a type of seed that can be obtained from harvesting Deathweeds while they are blooming or using the Staff of Regrowth on naturally grown Deathweeds while they are fully grown. A Deathweed plant only blooms during Blood Moons and Full Moons. Its blooming state can be identified by the sickly red pods on its leaves. Each plant will drop 1–3 Deathweed Seeds when harvested while blooming. Deathweed Seeds can be placed on Corrupt and Crimson grass, Ebonstone and Crimstone Blocks, empty Clay Pots, or any types of Planter Boxes, and will grow into harvestable Deathweeds. They will grow anywhere, not just in the evil biomes, but will only yield seeds when blooming.

Waterleaf Seeds.name: Waterleaf Seeds
Waterleaf Seeds.tooltip: Waterleaf Seeds are a type of seed that can be obtained from harvesting Waterleaves while they are blooming or using the Staff of Regrowth on naturally grown Waterleaves while they are fully grown. A Waterleaf plant only blooms during Rain. Each plant drops 1–3 Waterleaf Seeds when harvested while blooming. Waterleaf Seeds can be placed on Sand and Pearlsand Blocks, empty Clay Pots, or any types of Planter Boxes, even inside water or honey, and will grow into harvestable Waterleaves. They will grow anywhere, not just in the Desert, but will only yield seeds when blooming.

Fireblossom Seeds.name: Fireblossom Seeds
Fireblossom Seeds.tooltip: Fireblossom Seeds are a type of seed that can be obtained from harvesting Fireblossoms while they are blooming or using the Staff of Regrowth on naturally grown Fireblossoms while they are fully grown. А Fireblossom will bloom when the sun is setting if it is not raining, from 3:45 PM to 7:30 PM. Each plant will drop 1–3 Fireblossom Seeds when harvested while blooming. Fireblossom Seeds can be placed on Ash Blocks, empty Clay Pots, or any types of Planter Boxes, even inside lava, and will grow into harvestable Fireblossoms. They will grow anywhere, not just in the Underworld, but will only yield seeds when blooming. Like the Fireblossom, this item is not destroyed when coming into contact with lava, despite having a rarity of .

Daybloom.name: Daybloom
Daybloom.tooltip: Daybloom is a type of herb that appears as a small yellow flower with a straight green stem. It grows naturally on regular grass and Hallowed grass. Daybloom can be harvested with virtually any weapon or tool, and can be planted manually using Daybloom Seeds in Clay Pots and Planter Boxes, or on suitable soil tiles. Daybloom blooms during daytime (4:30 AM to 7:29 PM). Its blooming is indicated by the yellow sunflower-like head. Harvesting mature Daybloom yields 1 Daybloom item. Harvesting blooming Daybloom yields 1 Daybloom item and 1–3 Daybloom Seeds. Harvesting blooming Daybloom with the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth yields 1–2 Dayblooms and 1–5 Daybloom Seeds instead. Both Daybloom and Daybloom Seeds have a chance to be obtained from the Herb Bag. Daybloom can also be dropped by Angry Dandelions.

Moonglow.name: Moonglow
Moonglow.tooltip: Moonglow is a type of herb which appears as a bent stalk with a drooping blue-white flower. It grows naturally on regular Jungle grass. Moonglow can be harvested with virtually any weapon or tool, and can be planted manually using Moonglow Seeds in Clay Pots and Planter Boxes, or on suitable soil tiles. Moonglow blooms during nighttime (7:30 PM to 4:29 AM). Its blooming is indicated by the blue flower and blue-white light particles emitted. Harvesting mature Moonglow yields 1 Moonglow item. Harvesting blooming Moonglow yields 1 Moonglow item and 1–3 Moonglow Seeds. Harvesting blooming Moonglow with the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth yields 1–2 Moonglows and 1–5 Moonglow Seeds instead. Both Moonglow and Moonglow Seeds have a chance to be obtained from the Herb Bag.

Blinkroot.name: Blinkroot
Blinkroot.tooltip: <div class="drop infobox modesbox c-normal mw-collapsible  " style="min-width:25em; ; clear:right"> Blinkroot is a type of herb that appears as stems with glowing dots. It grows naturally on Dirt or Mud Blocks, regardless of lighting or elevation, as long as the blocks bear no grass of any kind. Blinkroot can be harvested with virtually any weapon or tool, and can be planted manually using Blinkroot Seeds in Clay Pots and Planter Boxes, or on suitable soil tiles. Blinkroot enters and exits its bloom state randomly. Its blooming is indicated by the yellow dots and pulsating yellow light emitted. Harvesting mature Blinkroot yields 1 Blinkroot item. Harvesting blooming Blinkroot yields 1 Blinkroot item and 1–3 Blinkroot Seeds. Harvesting blooming Blinkroot with the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth yields 1–2 Blinkroots and 1–5 Blinkroot Seeds instead. Both Blinkroot and Blinkroot Seeds have a chance to be obtained from the Herb Bag.

Deathweed.name: Deathweed
Deathweed.tooltip: Deathweed is a type of herb which appears as a short, withered purple stalk. It grows naturally on Ebonstone, Crimstone, Corrupt grass, Crimson grass, Corrupt Jungle grass, and Crimson Jungle grass. Deathweed can be harvested with virtually any weapon or tool, and can be planted manually using Deathweed Seeds in Clay Pots and Planter Boxes, or on suitable soil tiles. Deathweed blooms during a Blood Moon or a full moon at nighttime (7:30 PM to 4:29 AM). Its blooming is indicated by purple glowing particles. Harvesting mature Deathweed yields 1 Deathweed item. Harvesting blooming Deathweed yields 1 Deathweed item and 1–3 Deathweed Seeds. Harvesting blooming Deathweed with the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth yields 1–2 Deathweeds and 1–5 Deathweed Seeds instead. Both Deathweed and Deathweed Seeds have a chance to be obtained from the Herb Bag.

Waterleaf.name: Waterleaf
Waterleaf.tooltip: Waterleaf is a type of herb which appears as a small, turquoise-colored sprout. It grows naturally on Sand and Pearlsand Blocks, but will never spawn in the Ocean biome. Waterleaf can be harvested with virtually any weapon or tool, and can be planted manually using Waterleaf Seeds in Clay Pots and Planter Boxes, or on suitable soil tiles. Waterleaf blooms when it is raining. Its blooming is indicated by turquoise leaves and little water particles emitted. Harvesting mature Waterleaf yields 1 Waterleaf item. Harvesting blooming Waterleaf yields 1 Waterleaf item and 1–3 Waterleaf Seeds. Harvesting blooming Waterleaf with the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth yields 1–2 Waterleafs and 1–5 Waterleaf Seeds instead. Both Waterleaf and Waterleaf Seeds have a chance to be obtained from the Herb Bag.

Fireblossom.name: Fireblossom
Fireblossom.tooltip: Fireblossom is a type of herb which appears as a small, magma-colored flower. It grows naturally on Ash Blocks and Ash grass. Fireblossom can be harvested with virtually any weapon or tool, and can be planted manually using Fireblossom Seeds in Clay Pots and Planter Boxes, or on suitable soil tiles. Fireblossom blooms at sunset, from 3:45 PM to 7:30 PM, unless it is raining. Its blooming is indicated by the fiery flower and fire particles emitted. Harvesting mature Fireblossom yields 1 Fireblossom item. Harvesting blooming Fireblossom yields 1 Fireblossom item and 1–3 Fireblossom Seeds. Harvesting blooming Fireblossom with the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth yields 1–2 Fireblossoms and 1–5 Fireblossom Seeds instead. Both Fireblossom and Fireblossom Seeds have a chance to be obtained from the Herb Bag.

Shark Fin.name: Shark Fin
Shark Fin.tooltip: The Shark Fin is a crafting material that has a 19/20 (95%) chance of being dropped by Sharks and Orcas found in the Ocean biome, and a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Sand Sharks during a Sandstorm.

Feather.name: Feather
Feather.tooltip: The Feather is a common crafting material dropped frequently by Harpies. It is used in crafting the Featherfall and Gravitation Potions and once again becomes important in Hardmode for crafting the first tier of wings – Angel and Demon Wings.

Tombstone.name: Tombstone
Tombstone.tooltip: A Tombstone is a furniture item that drops when a player dies. It can then be retrieved and used much like a sign or as a form of decoration. By default, it contains the death message generated based on how the player died along with the real-life date of the death. Upon death, a Tombstone will bounce around until it lands on a suitable 2-tile wide surface, where it will place itself. If a Tombstone cannot find a place to land (due to lack of suitable space), it cannot be retrieved and will eventually despawn. Two Tombstones cannot land on each other. Variants are chosen randomly upon death. Golden Tombstones drop when the player had more than 10 Gold in their inventory. Having 4–8 Tombstones placed in close proximity will gradually darken and desaturate the environment. Five or more Tombstones placed in close proximity will generate a Graveyard mini-biome. Breaking a Tombstone has 12.5% / 25% / 50% chance to spawn a Ghost off-screen. In Hardcore, Tombstones cannot be easily obtained because death is permanent. Instead, NPCs in worlds with Hardcore characters will drop Tombstones when they are killed. Variants are still chosen randomly; all NPCs drop a normal Tombstone except the Merchant and Tax Collector who drop a golden variant. In For the Worthy (including Zenith) worlds, the Tombstone projectiles dropped by players (but not those dropped by NPCs in Hardcore) deal 210 / 280 / 420 damage to players and 70 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters. Because Tombstones create Graveyards, and mark a place where a player had died, they are highlighted by Dangersense Potions. Abigail's Flower can be uncommonly found as a plant growing on grass near a placed Tombstone, regardless of world progression. Its spawn chance is increased in a The Constant world.

Mime Mask.name: Mime Mask
Mime Mask.tooltip: The Mime Mask is a vanity item equipped in the Social Helmet slot. It is purchased from the Clothier during a Blood Moon for 2 Gold. (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) The game does not display the Mime Mask as a vanity item.

Antlion Mandible.name: Antlion Mandible
Antlion Mandible.tooltip: The Antlion Mandible is a crafting material dropped by Antlions, Antlion Larvae, Antlion Chargers, and Antlion Swarmers found in the Desert and Underground Desert biomes.

Illegal Gun Parts.name: Illegal Gun Parts
Illegal Gun Parts.tooltip: Illegal Gun Parts are a crafting material used to craft the Sandgun, the Megashark, and the Flamethrower. They are sold by the Arms Dealer for 20 Gold at night.

The Doctor's Shirt.name: The Doctor's Shirt
The Doctor's Shirt.tooltip: The Doctor's set is a vanity set which consists of The Doctor's Shirt and The Doctor's Pants. They are purchased from the Clothier for 40 Gold (set) in total, during Waning Gibbous. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

The Doctor's Pants.name: The Doctor's Pants
The Doctor's Pants.tooltip: The Doctor's set is a vanity set which consists of The Doctor's Shirt and The Doctor's Pants. They are purchased from the Clothier for 40 Gold (set) in total, during Waning Gibbous. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Golden Key.name: Golden Key
Golden Key.tooltip: Golden Keys are required to unlock the Locked Gold Chests found in the Dungeon and Golden Lock Boxes(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) obtained by fishing in the Dungeon, as well as to free the Elder Slime(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) from an Old Shaking Chest(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). A Golden Key is consumed upon use, so each unlock will require an additional key. Golden Keys can be acquired by: Finding one in an unlocked normal Chest in the Dungeon. Killing a Dungeon Slime (100% chance). Killing any other Dungeon enemy, excluding post-Plantera enemies (1.52% chance). Breaking a Pot in the Dungeon (1/35 (2.86%) chance ((Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)) / 1/40 (2.5%) chance ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions)).

Shadow Chest.name: Shadow Chest
Shadow Chest.tooltip: The Shadow Chest is a storage item which is found only in The Underworld, generally on top of or within Ruined Houses, and contains rare items. All Shadow Chests are initially locked, requiring a Shadow Key to open. The key is not consumed when used. Each Shadow Chest contains one high-tier item of  rarity, along with other standard Underground loot. Like all other naturally-occurring Chests, Shadow Chests can be freed with a pickaxe or drill after being emptied, and picked up by the player for placement and use elsewhere.

Shadow Key.name: Shadow Key
Shadow Key.tooltip: The Shadow Key is an item used solely to open Shadow Chests found scattered in the Underworld and Obsidian Lock Boxes found from Obsidian and Hellstone Crates. It is not consumed upon use; one Shadow Key can be used to open unlimited Shadow Chests. It can be found as secondary loot in Locked Gold Chests and Water Chests within the Dungeon, or from Golden Lock Boxes found in Dungeon and Stockade Crates.

Obsidian Brick Wall.name: Obsidian Brick Wall
Obsidian Brick Wall.tooltip: The Obsidian Brick Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Ruined Houses in the Underworld, considered unsafe. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.

Jungle Spores.name: Jungle Spores
Jungle Spores.tooltip: Jungle Spores are crafting materials acquired by destroying green glowing orbs that grow randomly on Jungle grass in the Underground Jungle, in or below the Cavern layer. Each orb drops 2–3 Jungle Spores. Harvested Jungle Spores cannot be replanted. Crafting all items requires a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 122 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 62 Jungle Spores.

Loom.name: Loom
Loom.tooltip: The Loom is a crafting station used to craft Silk, as well as some items that require Silk as an ingredient. It can sometimes be found in Underground Cabins.

Piano.name: Piano
Piano.tooltip: Pianos are a type of furniture which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 15 /  10 craftable Pianos, and 5 non-craftable Pianos that can be found in the Dungeon, Ruined Houses, and Pirate Invasion event. Some Pianos can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin that they are found in.

Dresser.name: Dresser
Dresser.tooltip: Dressers are a type of flat-surface furniture (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and storage item. They also fulfill house's table requirement. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 19 / (3DS version) 5 craftable versions, and (Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) 5 noncraftable versions which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Bench.name: Bench
Bench.tooltip: Benches are furniture items that fulfill a house's chair requirement. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Bench will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5.

Bathtub.name: Bathtub
Bathtub.tooltip: Bathtubs are furniture items which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 65 / (Old-gen console version) 16 / (3DS version) 11 Bathtub types, all being functionally identical but presenting different appearances.

Red Banner.name: Red Banner
Red Banner.tooltip: Banners are decorative furniture items that can be placed on the underside of blocks. Many are found naturally-placed in various biomes. There are also (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) four / (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) six crafted banners (Red, Green, Blue, Yellow, (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Pink, White) using Silk. Banners can be hung off of blocks and off of platforms which are in (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) any position / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) their bottom position (after being struck three times with a hammer). Faction flags are banners found in the Dungeon. In post-Plantera worlds, the faction flags found hanging in a particular Dungeon area correspond to the background wall type (brick, slab, or tile), both of which signify the types of enemies that will spawn there. See Hardmode Dungeon for more info. There are a total of 25 decorative banners: 6 crafted, 6 faction flags, 3 Floating Island, 6 Underworld, 3 Pyramid, and 1 dropped from the Dark Mage during the Old One's Army event.
