Lamp Post.name: Lamp Post
Lamp Post.tooltip: The Lamp Post is a piece of furniture that emits light. It can be placed underwater and can be toggled with wires. It counts as a light source for housing.

Tiki Torch.name: Tiki Torch
Tiki Torch.tooltip: The Tiki Torch is a stationary light source that must be placed in order to provide light. Like Torches, it can be placed on platforms, and will be put out, broken and subsequently dropped when coming into contact with water. However, the Tiki Torch cannot be collected by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it.

Barrel.name: Barrel
Barrel.tooltip: The Barrel is a storage item with 40 storage slots. It is functionally identical to Chests.

Chinese Lantern.name: Chinese Lantern
Chinese Lantern.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Cooking Pot.name: Cooking Pot
Cooking Pot.tooltip: The Cooking Pot is a crafting station that is solely used to turn various items into food, consumables that induce the Well Fed, Plenty Satisfied and Exquisitely Stuffed buffs. Such food material include the Bowl of Soup, Cooked Fish, Cooked Shrimp, and Grub Soup. The Cauldron is the Halloween-themed variant of the Cooking Pot that is functionally identical in every way, except for its animated sprite and the small amount of light it emits. Unlike the Cooking Pot, the Cauldron cannot be crafted, and can only be purchased from the Witch Doctor for 1 Gold 50 Silver during Halloween.

Safe.name: Safe
Safe.tooltip: The Safe is a portable storage item with 40 slots to store other items. The Safe, Piggy Bank, Defender's Forge(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Void Vault(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) have the unique ability to be carried while they contain items. The Safe can be purchased from the Merchant for 20 Gold after Skeletron has been defeated. The Safe functions identically to the Piggy Bank. However, it can also be placed on blocks in addition to platforms or on other flat furniture pieces. Additionally, the Safe and Piggy Bank do not share storage space.

Skull Lantern.name: Skull Lantern
Skull Lantern.tooltip: The Skull Lantern is a decorative piece of furniture that provides light. They always face left, and cannot be turned off via Wire.

Trash Can.name: Trash Can
Trash Can.tooltip: The Trash Can is a storage item with 40 storage slots. It is functionally identical to Chests; it does not delete items like the Trash Slot in the player's inventory.

Candelabra.name: Candelabra
Candelabra.tooltip: Candelabras are a type of furniture and light source that emits light when placed on a flat surface such as blocks, platforms, and flat furniture items. It is not destroyed by water. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 23 /  12 craftable and 5 looted variations of the Candelabra.

Pink Vase.name: Pink Vase
Pink Vase.tooltip: The Pink Vase is a decorative furniture item. A placed Pink Vase also serves as a Placed Bottle for potion crafting.

Mug.name: Mug
Mug.tooltip: The Mug is a cup made of Glass. It can be used to craft Ale. It can be placed on a flat furniture item, where it functions as a Placed Bottle crafting station.

Keg.name: Keg
Keg.tooltip: The Keg is a crafting station used solely to brew Ale. In addition to being crafted, it can sometimes be found in Underground Cabins.

Ale.name: Ale
Ale.tooltip: Ale is a potion that grants the Tipsy debuff for 2 minutes when consumed. Ale can be crafted at a Keg or purchased from the Tavernkeep(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) for 1 Silver each. The Tipsy debuff provides the following effects: This content is transcluded from Tipsy. -4 defense +10% melee damage +2% melee critical strike chance +10% melee speed +5 Fishing Power Reduces the time to produce Poo by 66.67% Ale is also used as ammunition for the Ale Tosser(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and can therefore be stored in the player's inventory ammo slots.
quality_issues: NO_ITEM_NAME: 'I've got the cure for what ails ya! Get it?'

Bookcase.name: Bookcase
Bookcase.tooltip: Bookcases are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station used for the crafting of three Hardmode magic weapons (the Crystal Storm, Cursed Flames, and Golden Shower) as well as the Librarian furniture out of Librarian Blocks. Bookcases also fulfill a house's table requirement. There is a total of 65 types of Bookcases: 60 craftable Bookcases, and 5 looted from the environment: one from the Underworld, three from the Dungeon, and one from the Pirate Invasion. Some bookcases can also be found in Underground Cabins; their style follows the theme of the cabin where they are found.

Throne.name: Throne
Throne.tooltip: The Throne is a decorative furniture item. It fulfills a house's chair requirement. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on the Throne will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5.

Bowl.name: Bowl
Bowl.tooltip: Bowls are a type of decorative furniture that can be placed on flat-surface items. Unlike plates, food cannot be placed in bowls. Only the regular Bowl can be used in crafting. The regular Bowl can also occasionally be found in the Dungeon on top of Tables and Work Benches.

Bowl of Soup.name: Bowl of Soup
Bowl of Soup.tooltip: The Bowl of Soup is a food item crafted at the Cooking Pot. When consumed, it grants the Plenty Satisfied buff. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().

Toilet.name: Toilet
Toilet.tooltip: Toilets are furniture items which can be placed on the ground. They are functionally similar to chairs, and fulfill a house's chair requirement. Similarly to chairs, Toilets can be sat on by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Having any tier of Well Fed active while sitting on a Toilet allows the production of Poo. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Toilet will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Toilets act as mechanisms that can be activated via wire, which makes them appear to explosively eject sewage. This effect is purely a novelty visual. Ejected sewage on the ground fades after a few seconds. There are 67 Toilets.

Grandfather Clock.name: Grandfather Clock
Grandfather Clock.tooltip: Grandfather Clocks are furniture items which provide information about the in-game time. If a player is nearby a Grandfather Clock (about 80 tiles horizontally and 50 tiles vertically), the time is displayed on the right side of the screen, underneath the minimap. The time is rounded to the last hour, similar to Tin and Copper Watches, but pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it will show precise time in minutes as a status message on the bottom left corner. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 21 /  5 craftable versions and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 5 / (Old-gen console version) 2 noncraftable (but still lootable) versions. The regular Grandfather Clock can rarely be found in Underground Cabins. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Armor Statue.name: Armor Statue
Armor Statue.tooltip: Statues are furniture items. While some are purely decorative, others have a functional effect when activated via Wire—depending on the statue, it may spawn enemies, drop items, or teleport an NPC to the statue's location. Most statues can be found already placed in any area underground (most frequently in the Dungeon, Underground Cabins, and Cavern level), though Angel Statues also appear in Chests. Like all furniture, a pickaxe, a drill, or explosives are used to collect them. There are a total of 117 different statues: 25 decoration statues, 36 text and numerical statues, and 56 functional mechanisms.

Goblin Battle Standard.name: Goblin Battle Standard
Goblin Battle Standard.tooltip: The Goblin Battle Standard is an event-summoning item that initiates the Goblin Army event when used. The Goblin Battle Standard is consumed when used, so one must be crafted for each invasion the player wishes to summon. In order for it to be used, at least one player in the current world must also have 200 health or more. The Tattered Cloth required for crafting the Goblin Battle Standard is obtained by killing Goblin Scouts, which spawn occasionally in the East and West sixths of the world.

Tattered Cloth.name: Tattered Cloth
Tattered Cloth.tooltip: The Tattered Cloth is a crafting material that is always dropped by Goblin Scouts.

Sawmill.name: Sawmill
Sawmill.tooltip: The Sawmill is a crafting station for advanced Wood and Furniture crafting. It is 3 blocks wide, 3 blocks high, and must be placed on top of solid blocks or platforms.

Cobalt Ore.name: Cobalt Ore
Cobalt Ore.tooltip: Cobalt Ore belongs to the first tier of the early Hardmode ores. Upon the first altar broken, either it or Palladium Ore can spawn in the underground and cavern layers. Mining Cobalt Ore requires a Molten Pickaxe or better. As with all early Hardmode ores, decreasing quantities of the ore spawn with every third altar broken afterwards, it is immune to explosives (apart from the Power Bomb and Sticky Power Bomb), and it can be obtained from Hardmode crates.
Cobalt Ore.drops_summary: Most crates (1.19%), Mythril Crate (2.08%), Pearlwood Crate (3.57%)

Mythril Ore.name: Mythril Ore
Mythril Ore.tooltip: Mythril Ore belongs to the second tier of the early Hardmode ores. Upon the second altar broken, either it or Orichalcum Ore can spawn in the cavern layer. Mining Mythril Ore requires a Cobalt/Palladium Pickaxe or better. As with all early Hardmode ores, decreasing quantities of the ore spawn with every third altar broken afterwards, it is immune to explosives (apart from the Power Bomb and Sticky Power Bomb), and it can be obtained from Hardmode crates.
Mythril Ore.drops_summary: Most crates (1.19%), Mythril Crate (2.08%), Titanium Crate (2.5%)

Adamantite Ore.name: Adamantite Ore
Adamantite Ore.tooltip: Adamantite Ore belongs to the third tier of the early Hardmode ores.

Pwnhammer.name: Pwnhammer
Pwnhammer.tooltip: The Pwnhammer is a Hardmode hammer that is always dropped by the Wall of Flesh. It is able to destroy Demon Altars and Crimson Altars, causing one type of Hardmode ore to appear in the world. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.
Pwnhammer.drops_summary: Treasure Bag (Wall of Flesh) (100%), Wall of Flesh (100%)

Excalibur.name: Excalibur
Excalibur.tooltip: The Excalibur is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss broadsword. When swung, a large yellow aura follows the swing, reaching about twice the distance of the sword itself. The aura can hit up to three enemies. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Hallowed Seeds.name: Hallowed Seeds
Hallowed Seeds.tooltip: Hallowed Seeds are Hardmode seeds used to plant Hallowed grass on Dirt Blocks, which will then spread The Hallow. Hallowed Seeds are purchased from the Dryad in Hardmode for 20 Silver each.

Ebonsand Block.name: Ebonsand Block
Ebonsand Block.tooltip: Sand Blocks are soil blocks found in vast quantities in Desert biomes, at shore and bottom of Ocean biomes, and can be found as microbiomes in patches in the Underground layer. They are also shot as projectiles by Antlions. Sand can spread and be converted by the evil biomes and The Hallow (see below). Sand is subject to gravity, a unique quality only shared by Slush, Silt, Shell Piles, Cracked Dungeon Bricks, and Ash on For the Worthy and Zenith worlds. Sand Blocks will deal damage to any player or enemy they fall on. If the amount of Sand falling on the player is significant, the Suffocation debuff will be inflicted until the player manages to escape. Sand is used to craft a small number of building blocks and other items directly, but it is also the raw material for Glass, which is used for a full furniture set and a variety of other items. All forms of Sand are also ammunition for the Sandgun, but they cannot be stored in the ammo slots of the inventory. Similar to the Sand Ball projectiles shot by Antlions, shot Sand Blocks will be placed on the ground as blocks if there are space available.

Cobalt Hat.name: Cobalt Hat
Cobalt Hat.tooltip: Cobalt armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Cobalt Breastplate and Cobalt Leggings, as well as three different headpieces: the Cobalt Helmet, Cobalt Mask, and Cobalt Hat, providing bonuses for the melee, ranged, and magic damage type respectively. Crafting a full set with one headpiece requires a total of 45 Cobalt Bars (135 Cobalt Ore). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 65 Cobalt Bars (195 Cobalt Ore). Its alternate ore counterpart is the Palladium armor. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: The player also emits visual afterimages while moving.

Cobalt Bar.name: Cobalt Bar
Cobalt Bar.tooltip: The Cobalt Bar is a Hardmode bar. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Palladium Bar.
Cobalt Bar.drops_summary: Most crates (2.78%), Mythril Crate (3.47%), Pearlwood Crate (2.68%), +1 more

Mythril Bar.name: Mythril Bar
Mythril Bar.tooltip: The Mythril Bar is a Hardmode bar. It is one of the two ores able to create a Hardmode Anvil, which is used to craft most Hardmode equipment. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Orichalcum Bar.
Mythril Bar.drops_summary: Most crates (2.78%), Mythril Crate (3.47%), Shadow Hammer (33.3%), +1 more

Cobalt Chainsaw.name: Cobalt Chainsaw
Cobalt Chainsaw.tooltip: The Cobalt Chainsaw is a Hardmode chainsaw and the alternative to the Cobalt Waraxe. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Palladium Chainsaw. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Mythril Chainsaw.name: Mythril Chainsaw
Mythril Chainsaw.tooltip: The Mythril Chainsaw is a Hardmode chainsaw and the alternative to the Mythril Waraxe. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Orichalcum Chainsaw. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Cobalt Drill.name: Cobalt Drill
Cobalt Drill.tooltip: The Cobalt Drill is a Hardmode drill. It is the alternative to the Cobalt Pickaxe, having a higher base mining speed but shorter range and lacking the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Mythril and Orichalcum Ore. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Palladium Drill. The Cobalt Drill has slightly less pickaxe power and damage. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Mythril Drill.name: Mythril Drill
Mythril Drill.tooltip: The Mythril Drill is a Hardmode drill. It is the alternative to the Mythril Pickaxe, having a higher base mining speed but shorter range and lacking the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Adamantite and Titanium Ore. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Orichalcum Drill. The Mythril Drill has slightly less pickaxe power, damage, and mining speed. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Adamantite Chainsaw.name: Adamantite Chainsaw
Adamantite Chainsaw.tooltip: The Adamantite Chainsaw is a Hardmode chainsaw and the alternative to the Adamantite Waraxe. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Titanium Chainsaw. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Adamantite Drill.name: Adamantite Drill
Adamantite Drill.tooltip: The Adamantite Drill is a Hardmode drill. It is the alternative to the Adamantite Pickaxe, having a higher base mining speed but shorter range and lacking the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Adamantite and Titanium Ore. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Titanium Drill. The Adamantite Drill has slightly less pickaxe power and damage. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount. (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it, and furthermore cannot get modifiers that affect its speed, either.

Dao of Pow.name: Dao of Pow
Dao of Pow.tooltip: The Dao of Pow is a Hardmode flail. It has a 4/5 (80%) chance of inflicting the Confused debuff for 2–4 seconds upon striking an enemy.

Mythril Halberd.name: Mythril Halberd
Mythril Halberd.tooltip: The Mythril Halberd is a Hardmode spear. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Orichalcum Halberd. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Adamantite Bar.name: Adamantite Bar
Adamantite Bar.tooltip: The Adamantite Bar is a Hardmode bar. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Titanium Bar.
Adamantite Bar.drops_summary: Most crates (2.78%), Shadow Hammer (33.3%), Titanium Crate (4.44%)

Glass Wall.name: Glass Wall
Glass Wall.tooltip: Glass Walls are transparent walls that can be used to make windows that let in natural light, while preventing monster spawns. They are crafted from Glass and also spawn naturally in houses on Floating Islands. They can be crafted into Stained Glass.

Compass.name: Compass
Compass.tooltip: The Compass is an informational accessory that enables an on-screen display of the player's horizontal position. Position is shown in the number of feet (1 foot = 1/2 tile) to the east or west of the center of the map. The centerpoint of the map is usually very close to the initial spawn point. The Compass has a 79/6400 (1.23%) chance of being dropped by Crawdads, Giant Shellies, and Salamanders, a 1/75 (1.33%) chance to be dropped by Piranhas, and a 1/50 (2%) chance to be dropped by Mother Slimes, Snow Flinx, Undead Vikings, and Armored Vikings.
Compass.drops_summary: Armored Viking (2%), Crawdad (1.23%), Giant Shelly (1.23%), +5 more

Diving Gear.name: Diving Gear
Diving Gear.tooltip: The Diving Gear is an accessory that combines the functionality of the Flipper and Diving Helmet: The player can swim upwards in any liquid by holding or pressing ↷ Jump repeatedly. The player's breath meter will deplete much slower, and the rate at which drowning damage is taken is slowed.

GPS.name: GPS
GPS.tooltip: The GPS is an informational accessory that enables an on-screen display of the in-game time, the player's horizontal position, and their depth.

Obsidian Horseshoe.name: Obsidian Horseshoe
Obsidian Horseshoe.tooltip: The Obsidian Horseshoe is a pre-Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the following effects while equipped: Immunity to the Burning debuff inflicted by Meteorite, Hellstone, and Hellstone Bricks Immunity to fall damage +0.05 luck(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)

Obsidian Shield.name: Obsidian Shield
Obsidian Shield.tooltip: The Obsidian Shield is a pre-Hardmode shield and immunity accessory that grants +2 defense, immunity to knockback, and immunity to the Burning debuff.

Tinkerer's Workshop.name: Tinkerer's Workshop
Tinkerer's Workshop.tooltip: The Tinkerer's Workshop is a flat-surface item and crafting station that is used primarily to combine multiple accessories into single items that usually provide the abilities of their components. For instance, it can combine the Rocket Boots and Hermes Boots into a single item (the Spectre Boots) that provides the same rocket-jumping and accelerated movement as the individual items do, without occupying two accessory slots. The Tinkerer's Workshop can be purchased from the Goblin Tinkerer for 10 Gold. (Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) When combining items, the Tinkerer's Workshop will assign a new random modifier to the crafted item. The modifiers the individual items had beforehand do not influence the modifier of the new combined item. (3DS version) Items crafted at the Tinkerer's Workshop will be assigned no modifier. The Tinkerer's Workshop is also used to craft most of the unrecordable Music Boxes, the Shellphone(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Weighted Pressure Plates, The Grand Design(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Multicolor Wrench(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), the Ultrabright Helmet(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Boulders on the  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version.

Cloud in a Balloon.name: Cloud in a Balloon
Cloud in a Balloon.tooltip: The Cloud in a Balloon is an accessory that combines the functionality of the Cloud in a Bottle and the Shiny Red Balloon. It boosts jump duration by 33% and jump speed by 30%, increasing the player's first jump's height to 10.5 tiles (~75% increase), and provides a double jump that can reach a height of 9 tiles, for a total height of 19.5 tiles. The total jump height of the Cloud in a Balloon is reduced when underwater, reducing the player's total underwater jump height from 15 tiles (8 + 7 from Cloud jump) to 13 tiles (7 + 6 from Cloud jump).

Adamantite Headgear.name: Adamantite Headgear
Adamantite Headgear.tooltip: Adamantite armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Adamantite Breastplate and Adamantite Leggings, as well as three different headpieces: the Adamantite Helmet, Adamantite Mask, and Adamantite Headgear, providing bonuses for the melee, ranged, and magic damage type respectively. Crafting a full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Adamantite Bars (216 Adamantite Ore). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 78 Adamantite Bars (312 Adamantite Ore). Its alternate ore counterpart is the Titanium armor. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: The player also emits a faint pulsating aura.

Spectre Boots.name: Spectre Boots
Spectre Boots.tooltip: The Spectre Boots are a pre-Hardmode accessory crafted from Rocket Boots and either Hermes Boots, Flurry Boots, Sailfish Boots(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), or Dunerider Boots(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and combines their functionality (except the faster speed on sand from Dunerider Boots). They grant the following effects while equipped: The ability to sprint, allowing the player to reach maximum running speed faster. The player will leave behind a visual trail of dust clouds as they sprint. Increased maximum movement speed to 31 mph (22.73 tiles/second). The ability to hold ↷ Jump in midair to fly for a total of 1.17 seconds. While flying, the boots emit a visual cloud trail.

Adamantite Glaive.name: Adamantite Glaive
Adamantite Glaive.tooltip: The Adamantite Glaive is a Hardmode spear. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Titanium Trident. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Toolbelt.name: Toolbelt
Toolbelt.tooltip: The Toolbelt is a construction accessory that can be purchased from the Goblin Tinkerer for 10 Gold. While equipped, it grants +1 placement range, but not tool range.

Pearlsand Block.name: Pearlsand Block
Pearlsand Block.tooltip: Sand Blocks are soil blocks found in vast quantities in Desert biomes, at shore and bottom of Ocean biomes, and can be found as microbiomes in patches in the Underground layer. They are also shot as projectiles by Antlions. Sand can spread and be converted by the evil biomes and The Hallow (see below). Sand is subject to gravity, a unique quality only shared by Slush, Silt, Shell Piles, Cracked Dungeon Bricks, and Ash on For the Worthy and Zenith worlds. Sand Blocks will deal damage to any player or enemy they fall on. If the amount of Sand falling on the player is significant, the Suffocation debuff will be inflicted until the player manages to escape. Sand is used to craft a small number of building blocks and other items directly, but it is also the raw material for Glass, which is used for a full furniture set and a variety of other items. All forms of Sand are also ammunition for the Sandgun, but they cannot be stored in the ammo slots of the inventory. Similar to the Sand Ball projectiles shot by Antlions, shot Sand Blocks will be placed on the ground as blocks if there are space available.

Pearlstone Block.name: Pearlstone Block
Pearlstone Block.tooltip: The Pearlstone Block is a Hardmode block type found in The Hallow. It requires at least a Nightmare Pickaxe, Deathbringer Pickaxe, or explosives to mine. Pearlstone is the Hallow version of Stone (similar to Ebonstone in The Corruption, or Crimstone in The Crimson). In a way similar to Ebonstone and Crimstone, Pearlstone can be converted into ordinary Stone via Vile Powder, Vicious Powder, or the Clentaminator with the Green Solution. During the initial creation of the Hallow biome upon the defeat of the Wall of Flesh, Stone blocks in the conversion path become Pearlstone blocks (see Hardmode). Pearlstone itself also continues to spread Hallow to all Stone, Sand, Ice, and Grass covered dirt within a three tile radius. Over time, it will grow Crystal Shards if it is in the Cavern layer or below.

Mining Shirt.name: Mining Shirt
Mining Shirt.tooltip: Mining armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Mining Helmet, Mining Shirt, and Mining Pants. The Mining Helmet can be purchased from the Merchant for 4 Gold and can also be dropped by Undead Miners with a 1/20 (5%) chance. The Mining Shirt and Mining Pants are dropped from Undead Miners with a 3/25 (12%) chance. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +4 defense +30% mining speed The player emits a small amount of light. All Mining armor pieces are interchangeable with pieces from the Prospector armor and the Ultrabright Helmet, still providing the set bonus. The only difference is the defense.

Mining Pants.name: Mining Pants
Mining Pants.tooltip: Mining armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Mining Helmet, Mining Shirt, and Mining Pants. The Mining Helmet can be purchased from the Merchant for 4 Gold and can also be dropped by Undead Miners with a 1/20 (5%) chance. The Mining Shirt and Mining Pants are dropped from Undead Miners with a 3/25 (12%) chance. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +4 defense +30% mining speed The player emits a small amount of light. Pearlstone Brick.name: Pearlstone Brick
Pearlstone Brick.tooltip: Pearlstone Brick is a brick made from Pearlstone. It does not spread The Hallow when placed, therefore making it a safer construction material than its raw ingredients.

Iridescent Brick.name: Iridescent Brick
Iridescent Brick.tooltip: Iridescent Brick is a cheap brick. It can be mined with any pickaxe or drill. It and its walls can either be crafted, or collected from Jungle Shrines in the Underground Jungle.

Mudstone Brick.name: Mudstone Brick
Mudstone Brick.tooltip: The Mudstone Brick is a type of brick made from Stone Blocks and Mud Blocks. It can also be obtained from Jungle Shrines. It is brown in color with a Stone-like texture.

Cobalt Brick.name: Cobalt Brick
Cobalt Brick.tooltip: Cobalt Brick is a сobalt tier brick.

Mythril Brick.name: Mythril Brick
Mythril Brick.tooltip: Mythril Brick is a mythril tier brick.

Pearlstone Brick Wall.name: Pearlstone Brick Wall
Pearlstone Brick Wall.tooltip: Pearlstone Brick Walls are a type of wall crafted from Pearlstone Bricks. Like most walls, they will stop enemy spawning, and can be used for NPC houses.

Iridescent Brick Wall.name: Iridescent Brick Wall
Iridescent Brick Wall.tooltip: The Iridescent Brick Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Jungle Shrines in some worlds. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is always considered a safe wall. Iridescent Brick Walls reflect the color of the light that they are lit with.

Mudstone Brick Wall.name: Mudstone Brick Wall
Mudstone Brick Wall.tooltip: The Mudstone Brick Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Jungle Shrines in some worlds. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is always considered a safe wall.

Cobalt Brick Wall.name: Cobalt Brick Wall
Cobalt Brick Wall.tooltip: Cobalt Brick Wall is a background wall crafted from Cobalt Bricks.

Mythril Brick Wall.name: Mythril Brick Wall
Mythril Brick Wall.tooltip: Mythril Brick Wall is a background wall crafted from Mythril Bricks.

Holy Water.name: Holy Water
Holy Water.tooltip: Thrown Water refers to a set of three consumable weapons that each convert a small area into a biome ( Hallow , Corruption , or Crimson for Holy Water , Unholy Water , and Blood Water respectively) when thrown. This conversion affects a roughly circular area with a radius of four tiles from the center. Enemies within this radius are also damaged slightly; this damage is not classified as any of the four damage types and therefore cannot be modified by any buffs or equipment.

Unholy Water.name: Unholy Water
Unholy Water.tooltip: Thrown Water refers to a set of three consumable weapons that each convert a small area into a biome ( Hallow , Corruption , or Crimson for Holy Water , Unholy Water , and Blood Water respectively) when thrown. This conversion affects a roughly circular area with a radius of four tiles from the center. Enemies within this radius are also damaged slightly; this damage is not classified as any of the four damage types and therefore cannot be modified by any buffs or equipment.

Silt Block.name: Silt Block
Silt Block.tooltip: Silt Blocks are a type of soil blocks that generates in the Underground and Cavern layers, appearing more frequently at lower depths. Silt is affected by gravity and will deal damage to any player or enemy it falls on. Unlike Sand Blocks, silt can stop The Hallow, The Crimson, and The Corruption from spreading. Silt looks similar to Ash Blocks, but is a lighter color. Silt can be placed in an Extractinator or Chlorophyte Extractinator to be converted into various valuable materials, including gems, coins, ores, and very rarely, the Amber Mosquito pet summoning item.

Fairy Bell.name: Fairy Bell
Fairy Bell.tooltip: The Fairy Bell is a Hardmode light pet-summoning item that spawns a Fairy, a glowing creature resembling a Pixie, which follows the player and produces light for an unlimited duration. The summoned Fairy will be either pink, green, or blue, the color of which changes randomly each time the Fairy is summoned. The Fairy is faster and brighter than the Shadow Orb and Crimson Heart, but not as fast or bright as the Wisp in a Bottle.

Breaker Blade.name: Breaker Blade
Breaker Blade.tooltip: The Breaker Blade is a Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Wall of Flesh. It has a larger size than most other swords. It deals 250% damage (175 base damage) to enemies at 90% health or higher. Its best modifier is Legendary.
Breaker Blade.drops_summary: Treasure Bag (Wall of Flesh) (25%), Wall of Flesh (25%)

Blue Torch.name: Blue Torch
Blue Torch.tooltip: Torches are furniture items that function as light sources when placed, held, or dropped (via the Throw button). Regular Torches can be found randomly in Chests and Pots, as a bonus drop from slimes, Torch Zombies, or purchased from the Merchant or Skeleton Merchant for 50 Copper each. Placing at least 101 Torches in close proximity below the surface layer in any biome will start the Torch God mini-event. Completing the event will grant the Torch God's Favor, which allows the player to automatically convert ordinary Torches to one of the biome types.

Clockwork Assault Rifle.name: Clockwork Assault Rifle
Clockwork Assault Rifle.tooltip: The Clockwork Assault Rifle is a Hardmode gun that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Wall of Flesh. When used, it fires in three-shot bursts, with each burst consuming one piece of ammunition. Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.
Clockwork Assault Rifle.drops_summary: Treasure Bag (Wall of Flesh) (25%), Wall of Flesh (25%)

Cobalt Repeater.name: Cobalt Repeater
Cobalt Repeater.tooltip: The Cobalt Repeater is a Hardmode repeater. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Palladium Repeater. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Mythril Repeater.name: Mythril Repeater
Mythril Repeater.tooltip: The Mythril Repeater is a Hardmode repeater.  Its alternate ore counterpart is the Orichalcum Repeater. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Dual Hook.name: Dual Hook
Dual Hook.tooltip: The Dual Hook is a Hardmode grappling hook that reaches 27.5 tiles and has two hooks which can be launched simultaneously; however, only one hook can be attached to a block at any time. Launching a second hook will not release the player from the first hook unless the new hook successfully attaches to a block. The Dual Hook has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being dropped by Mimics.

Star Statue.name: Star Statue
Star Statue.tooltip: Statues are furniture items. While some are purely decorative, others have a functional effect when activated via Wire—depending on the statue, it may spawn enemies, drop items, or teleport an NPC to the statue's location. Most statues can be found already placed in any area underground (most frequently in the Dungeon, Underground Cabins, and Cavern level), though Angel Statues also appear in Chests. Like all furniture, a pickaxe, a drill, or explosives are used to collect them. There are a total of 117 different statues: 25 decoration statues, 36 text and numerical statues, and 56 functional mechanisms.

Planked Wall.name: Planked Wall
Planked Wall.tooltip: Planked Wall is a background wall that naturally spawns in Underground Cabins. It can also be crafted.

Wooden Beam.name: Wooden Beam
Wooden Beam.tooltip: Beams or columns are background furniture items that provide support for Torches and can be used as decoration. They form continuous vertical pillars when stacked. They are found naturally in Underground Cabins, and can be crafted. Beams and columns can be stacked from the ground, and exist in the background, providing support for suspended Torches that will not inhibit character movement. In this way, beams and columns provide a function similar to trees (which also exist in the background and allow the player to suspend high Torches), but which the player can construct where they like. Where background walls exist, beams and columns can also be placed in "midair", without support from below. Despite their appearance as background walls, beams and columns instead share a layer with other furniture items (like tables, Torches, statues, Switches, timers, etc.), thus the two cannot share the same tile space. They can also prevent a door from opening.

Adamantite Repeater.name: Adamantite Repeater
Adamantite Repeater.tooltip: The Adamantite Repeater is a Hardmode repeater. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Titanium Repeater. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Adamantite Sword.name: Adamantite Sword
Adamantite Sword.tooltip: The Adamantite Sword is a Hardmode broadsword. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Titanium Sword. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Cobalt Sword.name: Cobalt Sword
Cobalt Sword.tooltip: The Cobalt Sword is a Hardmode broadsword. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Palladium Sword. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Mythril Sword.name: Mythril Sword
Mythril Sword.tooltip: The Mythril Sword is a Hardmode broadsword. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Orichalcum Sword. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Moon Charm.name: Moon Charm
Moon Charm.tooltip: The Moon Charm is a Hardmode accessory that, when equipped during nighttime, transforms the player into a werewolf and applies the Werewolf buff, which provides several stat bonuses. Additionally, the Moon Charm replaces the sound the player makes when damaged with the hurt sound that regular Werewolf enemies also have. The Werewolf buff does not pacify Werewolf enemies or make the player immune to damage from them. Although the regular Werewolf enemy is colored blue, the player Werewolf will be colored brown. The Moon Charm has a 1/60 (1.67%) chance of being dropped by Werewolves.  The Werewolf buff provides the player with these bonuses: +2% melee critical strike chance +5.1% melee damage +5.1% melee speed +5% movement speed +3 defense Slightly increased jump height and jump speed +0.5 health regeneration per second (similar to the Band of Regeneration, but with half the speed)

Ruler.name: Ruler
Ruler.tooltip: The Ruler is a pre-Hardmode shortsword purchased from the Goblin Tinkerer for 10 Silver. It swings four times in quick succession per use, with slightly varying angles with each stab.  Its best modifier is Legendary.

Crystal Ball.name: Crystal Ball
Crystal Ball.tooltip: The Crystal Ball is a Hardmode furniture item which functions as a crafting station. It is purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on a placed Crystal Ball grants the Clairvoyance buff and opens its crafting menu. The Clairvoyance buff boosts the following magic-related stats: +20 maximum mana +5% magic damage +2% magic critical strike chance −2% mana cost The Clairvoyance buff lasts until the player dies or leaves the world. The buff can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). Unlike equipment buff items, the Crystal Ball must be placed in order to activate the buff. It can be mined with a pickaxe or drill and picked up again, even while the buff is active, which will not cancel the buff. Placement is only dependent on an adequate space of 2×2 tiles being available.

Disco Ball.name: Disco Ball
Disco Ball.tooltip: The Disco Ball is a novelty Hardmode light source that can be placed on the underside of blocks, generating short pulses of colored light that cycle through the spectrum (In the Nintendo 3DS version, the Disco Ball will cycle through red, green, and blue only). The light can be toggled with wires. It is purchased from the Merchant in Hardmode for 1 Gold each.

Sorcerer Emblem.name: Sorcerer Emblem
Sorcerer Emblem.tooltip: The Sorcerer Emblem is a Hardmode accessory that increases magic damage by 15%. It has a 1/4 (25%) chance to drop from the Wall of Flesh.
Sorcerer Emblem.drops_summary: Treasure Bag (Wall of Flesh) (25%), Wall of Flesh (25%)

Warrior Emblem.name: Warrior Emblem
Warrior Emblem.tooltip: The Warrior Emblem is a Hardmode accessory that increases melee damage by 15%. It has a 1/4 (25%) chance to drop from the Wall of Flesh.
Warrior Emblem.drops_summary: Treasure Bag (Wall of Flesh) (25%), Wall of Flesh (25%)

Ranger Emblem.name: Ranger Emblem
Ranger Emblem.tooltip: The Ranger Emblem is a Hardmode accessory that increases ranged damage by 15%. It has a 1/4 (25%) chance to drop from the Wall of Flesh.
Ranger Emblem.drops_summary: Treasure Bag (Wall of Flesh) (25%), Wall of Flesh (25%)

Demon Wings.name: Demon Wings
Demon Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Angel Wings.name: Angel Wings
Angel Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Magical Harp.name: Magical Harp
Magical Harp.tooltip: The Magical Harp is a Hardmode magic weapon that autofires ricocheting, piercing projectiles that graphically resemble purple musical notes. Each projectile lasts for 3 seconds before dissipating and will both ricochet infinitely and pierce enemies up to 5 times. The Magical Harp's musical notes gain a 5% damage penalty for each enemy hit. Notes produce a reasonable amount of purple light and are not affected by gravity. Notes are initially at a high speed until they go a variable distance, equivalent to the distance between the player and the cursor, where they slow down. Additionally, initial note velocity is set so the amount of time until the note reaches the cursor is constant. The Magical Harp also plays sound while firing that resembles plucked strings, with a pitch that correlates to the distance of the cursor. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Rainbow Rod.name: Rainbow Rod
Rainbow Rod.tooltip: The Rainbow Rod is a Hardmode, post-The Twins wand. When used, it fires a rainbow missile that follows the cursor when ⚒ Use / Attack key is held. If the ⚒ Use / Attack key is released mid-drag, the missile will be fired in that direction. If the cursor is stationary on release, it is fired directly away from the player. Once it is released, the missile homes in on nearby enemies and can pierce twice, creating a small explosion upon contact with a block or third enemy. The missile does not dissipate when touching a block while being controlled, and is not affected by liquids (unlike the Flamelash). Its best modifier is Mythical.

Ice Rod.name: Ice Rod
Ice Rod.tooltip: The Ice Rod is a Hardmode magic weapon that autofires blocks of ice, which have the unique ability of placing solid, temporary  Ice Blocks at the location of the cursor and which last for 15 seconds before shattering. These Ice Blocks are translucent, cast a dim, flickering blue light, and are slippery like normal Ice Blocks. The Ice Rod can be purchased from the Wizard for 50 Gold. The location of the cursor must be unoccupied in order to form an Ice Block. If the tile is occupied either by blocks or background objects, the fired Ice Block acts as an ordinary projectile, flying in a straight line and unaffected by gravity, and shatters when it hits an enemy or other foreground objects. If the cursor is on an existing Ice Block from a previous casting, it will cause the next projectile to pass through the existing Ice Block. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Neptune's Shell.name: Neptune's Shell
Neptune's Shell.tooltip: Neptune's Shell is a Hardmode accessory that aids maneuverability in water, honey, and Shimmer by granting indefinite breathing time while submerged, swimming via the ↷ Jump key, and eliminating the slow movement speed usually caused by submerging underwater. Entering applicable liquids with this accessory equipped transforms the player into a merperson and grants the Merfolk buff. While in this form, the breath meter will refill as if the player is in open air, therefore effectively preventing drowning. Neptune's Shell has a 1/50 (2%) / 99/2500 (3.96%) chance of being dropped by Creatures from the Deep. Neptune's Shell can be considered an upgrade from the Diving Gear in most respects, but it lacks the extra mobility on Ice Blocks from the Arctic Diving Gear and the extra lighting underwater of the Jellyfish Necklace.

Mannequin.name: Mannequin
Mannequin.tooltip: The Mannequin is a furniture item that can be used to display armor, weapons, and vanity items, as well as accessories and dyes. Items can be placed on a Mannequin by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it, which opens a small set of inventory-like slots beneath the player's main inventory. There are three slots for helmet, shirt, and pants, five slots for accessories, and one slot for weapons. In addition, each slot besides the weapons slot has an associated dye slot underneath it. Placing items in these slots immediately displays them on the Mannequin. Mannequins can only be removed if no items are placed on them. The Mannequin always displays armor and clothing in their male sprite forms. The Womannequin can be used to display them in their female counterparts. The pose of a Mannequin can be changed by pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button on it whilst holding any hammer. This changes its appearance, as well as the position of the weapon that it is holding.

Greater Healing Potion.name: Greater Healing Potion
Greater Healing Potion.tooltip: The Greater Healing Potion is a Hardmode recovery potion that restores 150 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for 60 seconds when used. This duration can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths. Greater Healing Potions can be crafted using materials found in The Hallow or obtained from most Hardmode bosses as well as from Biome Mimics and Martian Saucers. It is the third tier of healing potion, succeeding the Lesser Healing Potion and Healing Potion, and preceding the Jungle Juice and Super Healing Potion.

Greater Mana Potion.name: Greater Mana Potion
Greater Mana Potion.tooltip: The Greater Mana Potion is a Hardmode recovery potion that restores 200 mana and inflicts the Mana Sickness debuff upon use. Unlike most potions, Greater Mana Potions cannot be crafted, and are instead purchased from the Wizard for 5 Silver, or dropped from all Biome Mimics except the Jungle Mimic. It is the third tier of mana potion, succeeding the Lesser Mana Potion and Mana Potion, and preceding the Super Mana Potion.

Pixie Dust.name: Pixie Dust
Pixie Dust.tooltip: Pixie Dust is a common Hardmode crafting material that always drops from Pixies.

Crystal Shard.name: Crystal Shard
Crystal Shard.tooltip: Crystal Shards are a common Hardmode crafting material found in the Underground Hallow. They can naturally grow on the left, right, and bottom sides of Pearlstone, Pink Ice, Pearlsand, Hardened Pearlsand, and Pearlsandstone Blocks. Due to their constant regrowth, they can be farmed (see Guide:Farming resources § Crystal Shards for details). Crystal Shards emit a small glow, similar to Demonite Ore and Crimtane Ore. They do not spread the Hallow. When a Crystal Shard is to be grown, it has a 1/50 (2%) chance to be replaced by a Gelatin Crystal(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) instead. Crystal Shards furthermore have a 1/2 (50%) chance to be obtained from Divine Crates(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), in stacks of 4–10. Crystal Shards are also placeable in nearly any position (on walls, floors, and ceilings), though they are often not luminous enough to replace other light sources, and placement has no other functional effect. Although natural Crystal Shards can only grow on blocks related with The Hallow, they can be placed anywhere once harvested. Crafting all items, including only one color of Phasesaber and excluding consumables and furniture, requires a total of 90 Crystal Shards. The amount required to craft every weapon and every color of Phasesaber is 290 Crystal Shards.

Clown Hat.name: Clown Hat
Clown Hat.tooltip: The Clown set is a vanity set which consists of the Clown Hat, the Clown Shirt, and the Clown Pants. It is purchased from the Clothier for 4 Gold (set), once a Clown has been defeated. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Clown Shirt.name: Clown Shirt
Clown Shirt.tooltip: The Clown set is a vanity set which consists of the Clown Hat, the Clown Shirt, and the Clown Pants. It is purchased from the Clothier for 4 Gold (set), once a Clown has been defeated. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Clown Pants.name: Clown Pants
Clown Pants.tooltip: The Clown set is a vanity set which consists of the Clown Hat, the Clown Shirt, and the Clown Pants. It is purchased from the Clothier for 4 Gold (set), once a Clown has been defeated. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Flamethrower.name: Flamethrower
Flamethrower.tooltip: The Flamethrower is a Hardmode, post-Skeletron Prime ranged weapon that uses Gel for ammunition. When used, it consumes one Gel and releases five bursts of fire in quick succession. The fire expands as it travels, creating a cone-like area of effect, before dissipating shortly after. The fire has 15 armor penetration, inflicts the Hellfire debuff for 20 seconds, and can pierce through three enemies. The fire's damage decreases by 15% per enemy pierced. Its best modifier is Unreal. A modifier granting +10% speed will increase the number of flame streams per use from five to six while still consuming 1 Gel. A modifier with added velocity will increase the range of each stream, i.e. by about 5 tiles for +15% and about 3 tiles for +10%.

Bell.name: Bell
Bell.tooltip: The Bell is a Hardmode crafting material purchased from the Wizard for 1 Gold. It is used to the craft the Fairy Bell, a light pet-summoning item. When used, the Bell creates a sound that changes in pitch depending on the distance between the player and the point clicked.

Harp.name: Harp
Harp.tooltip: The Harp is a Hardmode crafting material, used only to craft the Magical Harp. While the Harp can be used itself, it has no functional use, and only makes sounds. It is sold by the Wizard for 1 Gold each. When used, the Harp generates harp sounds. The sound's pitch is determined by the distance between the center of the character and the point clicked. Clicking the center of the character plays middle C, while clicking at a distance of at least that of the top or bottom of the screen plays C6 (two octaves above middle C). The smallest interval between notes the harp can play is a whole tone, or two semitones. A difference of 1/24 of the screen height equals an interval of a whole tone.

Red Wrench.name: Red Wrench
Red Wrench.tooltip: Wrenches are tools for placing Wires, which are used to connect mechanisms together, such as a trap with a Pressure Plate. There are four different wrenches: the Red Wrench, Green Wrench, Blue Wrench, and Yellow Wrench(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), each placing its respective color of Wire. All wrenches are purchased from the Mechanic for 2 Gold each. All Wrenches use the same ordinary Wire item as ammunition, but the color of wrench used will determine the color of Wire when placed. The colors all function identically but can be placed so as to overlap or intersect each other without interfering with each other. Junction Boxes(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can further be used to keep intersecting Wire paths of the same color from interfering with each other. All four wrenches can be combined to make a Multicolor Wrench(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), a single tool that can place Wire of any color. Ordinary wrenches cannot be used to remove placed Wires. Instead, a Wire Cutter or one of its derivatives is required. All Wire colors become the same ordinary Wire item again when freed.

Wire Cutter.name: Wire Cutter
Wire Cutter.tooltip: The Wire Cutter is a tool that allows players to free and harvest Wires and Actuators. It is sold by the Mechanic NPC who is initially found in the Dungeon. The Wire Cutter has a large range bonus, making it easier to remove wires at a distance.

Active Stone Block.name: Active Stone Block
Active Stone Block.tooltip: The Active Stone Block and Inactive Stone Block are blocks that act as mechanisms. A given pair behave as a single block whose presence can be switched "on" or "off" using wire and a trigger. When triggered, an Active Stone Block becomes an Inactive Stone Block, and vice versa. Wires must pass through all Active/Inactive Stone Blocks that are to be triggered. An Active Stone Block is a foreground object. This means it looks and behaves as an ordinary Stone Block, inhibits movement, allows entities to stand or walk on it, blocks light, and can stop liquids. An Inactive Stone Block is a background object. While still visible, it looks like darker Stone Block, and behaves like furniture. It is essentially empty space, allowing the passage of players, items, liquids, light, etc. Inactive Stone Blocks cannot be placed next to each other without the support of other adjacent foreground blocks. Active blocks do not have this shortcoming, and switching them to Inactive afterwards using wires will still have the same outcome.

Inactive Stone Block.name: Inactive Stone Block
Inactive Stone Block.tooltip: The Active Stone Block and Inactive Stone Block are blocks that act as mechanisms. A given pair behave as a single block whose presence can be switched "on" or "off" using wire and a trigger. When triggered, an Active Stone Block becomes an Inactive Stone Block, and vice versa. Wires must pass through all Active/Inactive Stone Blocks that are to be triggered. An Active Stone Block is a foreground object. This means it looks and behaves as an ordinary Stone Block, inhibits movement, allows entities to stand or walk on it, blocks light, and can stop liquids. An Inactive Stone Block is a background object. While still visible, it looks like darker Stone Block, and behaves like furniture. It is essentially empty space, allowing the passage of players, items, liquids, light, etc. Inactive Stone Blocks cannot be placed next to each other without the support of other adjacent foreground blocks. Active blocks do not have this shortcoming, and switching them to Inactive afterwards using wires will still have the same outcome.

Lever.name: Lever
Lever.tooltip: The Lever is a 2×2 activation mechanism purchased from the Mechanic for 30 Silver. It can activate Statues, lights, etc. via ⚷ Open / Activate. The Lever can be placed on any flat surface, the same as furniture, including on platforms. It can also be placed on background walls. Despite its depiction as a switch with two positions, the Lever does not need to act as an on/off mechanism. When wired to Dart Traps, for example, activating the Lever will always cause the trap to shoot, the same as a Pressure Plate would, no matter which position the Lever happens to be in.

Laser Rifle.name: Laser Rifle
Laser Rifle.tooltip: The Laser Rifle is a Hardmode magic gun that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Wall of Flesh. When used, it fires fast-moving purple lasers that can hit up to three enemies. The lasers will increase in damage, pierce, knockback, and size (only visually) as they travel. While a full set of Meteor armor is equipped, the Laser Rifle costs no mana to use. Its best modifier is Mythical.
Laser Rifle.drops_summary: Treasure Bag (Wall of Flesh) (25%), Wall of Flesh (25%)

Crystal Bullet.name: Crystal Bullet
Crystal Bullet.tooltip: The Crystal Bullet is a Hardmode bullet. It shatters upon impact with enemies or solid blocks, splitting into two small shards. The shards have a short range, can pass through blocks, and each deal 50% of the gun and bullet's combined damage.

Holy Arrow.name: Holy Arrow
Holy Arrow.tooltip: The Holy Arrow is a Hardmode arrow. Upon contact with enemies or blocks, two Hallow Star projectiles will fall from the sky to the impact location. The stars deal 1/3 (33.33%) of the combined damage of the arrow and weapon, and do not pierce.

Magic Dagger.name: Magic Dagger
Magic Dagger.tooltip: The Magic Dagger is a Hardmode magic weapon that has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being dropped by Mimics. When used, it rapidly fires Magic Dagger projectiles that travel in a straight line in the direction of the cursor for 24 tiles, then suddenly become affected by gravity. The projectiles can hit up to 3 enemies and cannot pass through blocks. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Crystal Storm.name: Crystal Storm
Crystal Storm.tooltip: The Crystal Storm is a Hardmode spell book that rapidly fires a slight spread of small crystal shards. The shards last for 2.5 seconds each and slow down as they travel. They can bounce off blocks an unlimited amount of times for their duration, and do not pierce. The Crystal Storm is the Hallow counterpart to the Corruption's Cursed Flames and the Crimson's Golden Shower, all of which require a Spell Tome and ingredients exclusive to their underground biome counterparts. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Cursed Flames.name: Cursed Flames
Cursed Flames.tooltip: The Cursed Flames are a Hardmode spell book that fire gravity-affected bouncing green fireballs. The fireballs can bounce off blocks four times and pierce enemies once, and they inflict the Cursed Inferno debuff for 7 seconds on hit, dealing 24 damage per second. The Cursed Flames are the Corruption counterpart to the Crimson's Golden Shower and the Hallow's Crystal Storm, all of which require a Spell Tome and ingredients exclusive to their underground biome counterparts. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Soul of Light.name: Soul of Light
Soul of Light.tooltip: Soul of Light is a Hardmode crafting material dropped by most enemies killed in the Underground Hallow (in the Cavern layer) with a 1/5 (20%) chance. This also includes enemies not native to the biome, such as Granite Elementals. See Notes for details.

Soul of Night.name: Soul of Night
Soul of Night.tooltip: Soul of Night is a Hardmode crafting material dropped by most enemies killed in the Underground Corruption or Underground Crimson (in the Cavern layer), with a 1/5 (20%) chance. This also includes enemies not native to the biome, such as normal cavern enemies, Underworld enemies, but not enemies spawned from statues. See Notes for details.

Cursed Flame.name: Cursed Flame
Cursed Flame.tooltip: Cursed Flame is a Hardmode crafting material, whose Crimson counterpart is Ichor. It is dropped by World Feeders, Vile Ghouls and Clingers, all of which can be found in The Corruption. It can also be found in Defiled Crates.

Cursed Torch.name: Cursed Torch
Cursed Torch.tooltip: Torches are furniture items that function as light sources when placed, held, or dropped (via the Throw button). Regular Torches can be found randomly in Chests and Pots, as a bonus drop from slimes, Torch Zombies, or purchased from the Merchant or Skeleton Merchant for 50 Copper each. Placing at least 101 Torches in close proximity below the surface layer in any biome will start the Torch God mini-event. Completing the event will grant the Torch God's Favor, which allows the player to automatically convert ordinary Torches to one of the biome types.

Adamantite Forge.name: Adamantite Forge
Adamantite Forge.tooltip: The Adamantite Forge and Titanium Forge are Hardmode crafting stations that incorporate the same functions as a regular Furnace and Hellforge, with the additional bonus of being able to smelt Adamantite, Titanium and Chlorophyte ores into their respective bars. They emit light and give off fire particles when placed, like the Furnace and Hellforge. The Adamantite Forge and Titanium Forge are functionally identical.

Mythril Anvil.name: Mythril Anvil
Mythril Anvil.tooltip: The Mythril Anvil and Orichalcum Anvil are Hardmode crafting stations that serve and extend the function of a pre-Hardmode Anvil. These are very crucial to game advancement, as they account for making nearly every Hardmode recipe before the Ancient Manipulator. In addition to acting as a direct replacement to Lead and Iron Anvils and inheriting all of their crafting recipes, they further serve the similar function of crafting bars forged of Hardmode ores into weapons, armor and tools, as well as several other items, such as wings.

Unicorn Horn.name: Unicorn Horn
Unicorn Horn.tooltip: The Unicorn Horn is a Hardmode crafting material that is always dropped by Unicorns in The Hallow.

Dark Shard.name: Dark Shard
Dark Shard.tooltip: The Dark Shard is a Hardmode crafting material used in the crafting of the Dao of Pow, Onyx Blaster and Ruinous Staff. It has a 1/10 (10%) chance of being dropped by Dark Mummies and Shadow Mummies(Old-gen console and 3DS versions) in Corrupt Deserts, and Blood Mummies(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) in Crimson Deserts. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, the Dark Shard also has a 1/15 (6.67%) chance to drop from Tainted/Vile Ghouls which respectively spawn within the Crimson/Corrupted Underground Desert, and a 1/25 (4%) chance of dropping from Bone Biters and Flesh Reavers. The Hallow counterpart is the Light Shard.

Light Shard.name: Light Shard
Light Shard.tooltip: The Light Shard is a Hardmode crafting material used in the crafting of the Dao of Pow, Sky Fracture and Ruinous Staff. It has a 1/10 (10%) chance to drop from Light Mummies and Spectral Mummies (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) which spawn in Hallowed deserts. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, the Light Shard also has a 1/15 (6.67%) chance to drop from Dreamer Ghouls in The Hallowed Underground Desert, and a 1/25 (4%) chance of dropping from Crystal Threshers. Its Corruption/Crimson counterpart is the Dark Shard.

Red Pressure Plate.name: Red Pressure Plate
Red Pressure Plate.tooltip: Pressure Plates are activation mechanisms that trigger wired mechanisms when stepped on. A pressure plate's color determines which characters can trigger it. Red, Brown, Gray, Orange, and Lihzahrd Pressure Plates are randomly generated on the map during world creation as the trigger for traps. They only take up a very small space on top of blocks, so they may be difficult to spot. The color of naturally spawned pressure plates is dependent on the color of the block they are generated on top of. Except for Lihzahrd Pressure Plates, they can also be purchased from the Mechanic. Weighted Pressure Plates activate once on being depressed, and again on being released. All Weighted Pressure Plates of the same color share a single state. As long as one Weighted Pressure Plate of a given color is already pressed down within a circuit, stepping on another identical plate will not send a new signal. They can be crafted from regular pressure plates. The Teal Pressure Pad is a special kind of pressure plate that responds to projectiles impacting it, which includes pets that touch it. Unlike regular pressure plates, the Teal Pressure Pad can be placed on all four sides of a block, e.g. on the ceiling or sidewall. It can be purchased from the Mechanic.

Wire.name: Wire
Wire.tooltip: Wire is a unique item generally used to connect mechanisms to triggers, like a Pressure Plate, Timer, Switch, or Lever. Wires are placed using Wrenches (or their upgrades), and are retrieved using the Wire Cutter (or its upgrades), both of which can only be obtained from the Mechanic. Wire placed by differently colored Wrenches will be of different colors, which allows independent wire paths to overlap without interfering with each other. While Wire is available for purchase from the Mechanic for 5 Silver each, it can also be obtained from naturally-occurring mechanisms, which exist sparsely in the Caverns and more frequently in the Dungeon and Jungle Temple, such as in traps and Chain Lantern/Switch arrangements. Wires occupy their own dedicated placement layer, and so can occupy the same tile space as blocks, walls, furniture, plants, and liquids. Wires can be placed in midair, without the need for support. Explosions have no effect on placed Wires. By default, placed Wires are invisible unless the player holds a mechanism-related item as the tool in hand, (e.g., a Pressure Plate, Wrench, or even a stack of Wire itself). However, if the player is carrying a Mechanical Lens (or its upgrade, The Grand Design) they can not only see Wires at will, but can control the visibility of individual Wire colors. With Wrenches and Wire Cutters, the player's Wire placing and cutting reach is roughly 25 tiles horizontally and vertically. With The Grand Design, the player can place or cut Wire anywhere on the screen. Wires are considered "connected" to triggers and mechanisms when they are placed in the same tile space as those items. Usually, this is indicated by the Wire and the item visually "touching", though not all items fully occupy their tile space (e.g. certain statues). Wire is considered "ammunition" for Wrenches, and can therefore be placed in the ammo slots of a player's inventory.

Spell Tome.name: Spell Tome
Spell Tome.tooltip: The Spell Tome is a Hardmode crafting material that is purchased from the Wizard for 5 Gold.

Star Cloak.name: Star Cloak
Star Cloak.tooltip: The Star Cloak is a Hardmode accessory that causes three stars to fall around the player whenever the player takes damage. It consumes no mana. The stars pass through blocks until reaching the player's altitude, at which point they continue falling until hitting blocks. They can pierce once, dissipating on the second hit. The stars deal 75 / 150 / 225 damage which is not classified as any of the four damage types and therefore cannot be modified by any buffs or equipment. Furthermore, the stars have 25 armor penetration.

Megashark.name: Megashark
Megashark.tooltip: The Megashark is a Hardmode, post-The Destroyer gun and the direct upgrade to the Minishark. When used, it fires bullets very rapidly in a small spread. It also has a 50% chance not to consume ammunition. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Shotgun.name: Shotgun
Shotgun.tooltip: The Shotgun is a Hardmode gun that can be purchased from the Arms Dealer for 25 Gold. When used, it fires a spread of 4–5 bullets, consuming one piece of ammunition. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Philosopher's Stone.name: Philosopher's Stone
Philosopher's Stone.tooltip: The Philosopher's Stone is a Hardmode accessory which decreases the Potion Sickness debuff duration by 25%. This debuff normally imposes a 60-second cooldown after consuming a recovery potion; the Philosopher's Stone reduces it to 45 seconds. It has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance to be dropped by Mimics.

Titan Glove.name: Titan Glove
Titan Glove.tooltip: The Titan Glove is a Hardmode accessory that has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being dropped by Mimics. While equipped, it grants the following effects: ×2 knockback for melee weapons +10% size for melee weapons

Cobalt Naginata.name: Cobalt Naginata
Cobalt Naginata.tooltip: The Cobalt Naginata is a Hardmode spear. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Palladium Pike. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Switch.name: Switch
Switch.tooltip: The Switch is an activation mechanism purchased from the Mechanic for 20 Silver. It can also be found in the Dungeon connected to Chain Lanterns, where it can be harvested with a Pickaxe or Drill. The Switch can be placed on top or on the sides of blocks, or on the sides of Wooden Beams or trees. Switches can also be placed on background walls. It is activated by right-clicking on it. Despite its name, the Switch does not need to act as an on/off mechanism. When wired to Dart Traps, for example, right-clicking the Switch will always cause the Trap to shoot, the same as a Pressure Plate would, no matter which position the switch happens to be in.

Dart Trap.name: Dart Trap
Dart Trap.tooltip: The Dart Trap is a trap that can be found naturally placed in Cavern layer and Dungeon. It fires a dart when triggered via wire which does not consume any ammunition. It has a cooldown of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 3 1/3 seconds / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 3 seconds between firing. The darts deal 40 / 80 / 120 damage and inflict Poisoned for 10 / 20 / 25 seconds to players (20 damage and 10 seconds of Poisoned to NPCs, enemies, and critters). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Dart Traps can be rotated 90° with a hammer.

Boulder.name: Boulder
Boulder.tooltip: The Boulder is a unique placeable foreground object that is stationary when placed. When unsupported, it falls and begins to roll away, picking up speed and damaging players, enemies, critters, and NPCs along its path. Boulders will also begin to roll if hit with a pickaxe or drill, meaning that they cannot be picked up again once placed. Boulders will roll across flat surfaces and down slopes, but will break and disappear on contact with an obstacle. They deal 70 / 140 / 280 / 420 damage to players (70 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters), inflict a knockback of 10 (Extremely strong) on contact, and can pierce through an unlimited number of entities. Boulders accelerate to a top speed of 27 tiles per second (36 mph) over the course of 2.17 seconds or 32 tiles. Boulder traps occur naturally in the Underground and Cavern layers, and consist of a single Boulder in the ceiling, supported by six (2×3) Active Stone Blocks wired to an Orange Pressure Plate. Once a player walks onto the Pressure Plate, the Boulder falls down and begins rolling. In For the Worthy (including Zenith) worlds, Boulders will release 2–4 miniature Boulders when they break. These function identical to the Boulder projectile, but are smaller and deal 75% damage (157 / 210 / 315). During world generation, a small number of Boulders are designated to drop a Friendly Boulder when they break. Depending on world size, 2 (small worlds), 4 (medium worlds), or 6 (large worlds) Boulders out of all the Boulders in the world are selected for this. This number is doubled in No Traps.

Mechanical Eye.name: Mechanical Eye
Mechanical Eye.tooltip: The Mechanical Eye is a Hardmode boss-summoning item that summons The Twins when used. It can be used in any biome, but only at night. If the Twins have not been defeated yet in a Hardmode world, all enemies that can drop at least 1 Copper have a 1/2500 (0.04%) chance of dropping a Mechanical Eye.

Cursed Arrow.name: Cursed Arrow
Cursed Arrow.tooltip: The Cursed Arrow is a Hardmode arrow. It inflicts the Cursed Inferno debuff for 7 seconds upon contact with enemies. Its Crimson counterpart is the Ichor Arrow.

Cursed Bullet.name: Cursed Bullet
Cursed Bullet.tooltip: The Cursed Bullet is a Hardmode bullet. It inflicts the Cursed Inferno debuff for 7 seconds on hit, causing damage over time that cannot be extinguished by water (unlike the On Fire! debuff). Its Crimson counterpart is the Ichor Bullet.

Soul of Fright.name: Soul of Fright
Soul of Fright.tooltip: The Soul of Fright is one of the six souls. It is a crafting material dropped by Skeletron Prime.

Soul of Might.name: Soul of Might
Soul of Might.tooltip: The Soul of Might is one of the six souls. It is a crafting material dropped by The Destroyer.

Soul of Sight.name: Soul of Sight
Soul of Sight.tooltip: The Soul of Sight is one of the six souls that can be obtained in Hardmode. It is a crafting material dropped by The Twins.

Gungnir.name: Gungnir
Gungnir.tooltip: The Gungnir is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss spear. When thrust, it creates a small shockwave at its tip. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Hallowed Plate Mail.name: Hallowed Plate Mail
Hallowed Plate Mail.tooltip: Hallowed armor is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss armor set consisting of the Hallowed Plate Mail and Hallowed Greaves, as well as four different headpieces: the Hallowed Mask, Hallowed Helmet, Hallowed Headgear, and Hallowed Hood, providing bonuses for melee, ranged, magic, and summon damage type respectively. Crafting a full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Hallowed Bars. Crafting all six pieces requires a total of 90 Hallowed Bars. Hallowed armor pieces are interchangeable with Ancient Hallowed armor pieces, still providing the set bonus. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: Upon enemy hits, the player receives the Holy Protection buff, which grants the ability to dodge the next attack dealt by an enemy or other damage source. It has a 30-second cooldown after the dodge has been activated. The player also emits visual pulses and afterimages while moving.

Hallowed Greaves.name: Hallowed Greaves
Hallowed Greaves.tooltip: Hallowed armor is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss armor set consisting of the Hallowed Plate Mail and Hallowed Greaves, as well as four different headpieces: the Hallowed Mask, Hallowed Helmet, Hallowed Headgear, and Hallowed Hood, providing bonuses for melee, ranged, magic, and summon damage type respectively. Crafting a full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Hallowed Bars. Crafting all six pieces requires a total of 90 Hallowed Bars. It has a 30-second cooldown after the dodge has been activated. The player also emits visual pulses and afterimages while moving.

Cross Necklace.name: Cross Necklace
Cross Necklace.tooltip: The Cross Necklace is a Hardmode accessory that increases the duration of the invincibility frames a player is afforded after taking damage. The Cross Necklace has a (Desktop, Console, Mobile and 3DS versions) 1/6 (16.67%) / (Old-gen console version) 1/7 (14.29%) chance to be dropped by Mimics.

Mana Flower.name: Mana Flower
Mana Flower.tooltip: The Mana Flower is a pre-Hardmode accessory that reduces mana cost by 8%, and automatically consumes mana potions in the player's inventory or opened Void Bag when mana is depleted.

Mechanical Worm.name: Mechanical Worm
Mechanical Worm.tooltip: The Mechanical Worm is a Hardmode boss-summoning item that summons The Destroyer when used. It can be used in any biome, but only at night. If the Destroyer has not been defeated yet in a Hardmode world, all enemies that can drop at least 1 Copper have a 1/2500 (0.04%) chance of dropping a Mechanical Worm.

Mechanical Skull.name: Mechanical Skull
Mechanical Skull.tooltip: The Mechanical Skull is a Hardmode boss-summoning item that summons Skeletron Prime when used. It can be used in any biome, but only at night. If Skeletron Prime has not been defeated yet in a Hardmode world, all enemies that can drop at least 1 Copper have a 1/2500 (0.04%) chance of dropping a Mechanical Skull.

Hallowed Headgear.tooltip: Hallowed armor is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss armor set consisting of the Hallowed Plate Mail and Hallowed Greaves, as well as four different headpieces: the Hallowed Mask, Hallowed Helmet, Hallowed Headgear, and Hallowed Hood, providing bonuses for melee, ranged, magic, and summon damage type respectively. Slime Crown.name: Slime Crown
Slime Crown.tooltip: The Slime Crown is a boss-summoning item that summons King Slime when used. It can be used in any biome at any time. When thrown into Shimmer, the Slime Crown is consumed and the Slime Rain event begins immediately. If the event is already in progress, then the item merely sinks to the bottom of the Shimmer like all other non-decraftable items.

Light Disc.name: Light Disc
Light Disc.tooltip: The Light Disc is a Hardmode, post-The Destroyer boomerang. It does not necessarily return immediately upon contact with objects, but instead can bounce off blocks before returning. Unlike most boomerangs, it does not have to return to the player before being fired, with a maximum of six Light Discs that can be thrown out at one time. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Music Box (Overworld Day).name: Music Box (Overworld Day)
Music Box (Overworld Day).tooltip: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End), which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 Gold after defeating the Moon Lord. A recorded Music Box can be played back in one of two ways: Equipping it as an accessory. Placing it as furniture and activating it, either by the ⚷ Open / Activate button or with wires. Recorded Music Boxes can be reverted into blank ones through Shimmer transmutation. There are 101 different Music Boxes available.

Soul of Flight.name: Soul of Flight
Soul of Flight.tooltip: The Soul of Flight is a Hardmode crafting material used to craft several different types of wings and the Soul of Flight in a Bottle(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Souls of Flight are dropped by Wyverns and are the most common soul aside from the Souls of Light and Night. Souls of Flight are dropped at the position of the Wyvern's head upon death, and like all other souls, float in midair at the drop point, rather than falling to the ground. This can make Souls of Flight more difficult to spot, e.g. if the Wyvern's head was off-screen or within blocks at the time of death.
