Demonite Brick.name: Demonite Brick
Demonite Brick.tooltip: Demonite Brick is a brick crafted from Demonite Ore and Ebonstone. A box of it also appears after the Wall of Flesh has been defeated on a Corruption world ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions) in any type of world). It is not resistant to explosions, and gives off a faint glow when placed.

Hallowed Repeater.name: Hallowed Repeater
Hallowed Repeater.tooltip: The Hallowed Repeater is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss repeater. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Drax.name: Drax
Drax.tooltip: The Drax is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses drill and axe. It is the alternative to the Pickaxe Axe, having a higher base mining speed but shorter range and lacking the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Chlorophyte Ore. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Explosives.name: Explosives
Explosives.tooltip: Explosives are a placeable, consumable mechanism that can be triggered using wiring. Pressing ▲ Up and ▼ Down keys when placing Explosives rotates the placed visual. Triggering Explosives cause a large explosion. The explosion destroys most placed blocks and items (except for explosion-proof items) within a radius of 10 tiles, and deals damage within a 16.25×16.25-tile area. The explosion deals 500 damage and inflicts a knockback of 10 (Extremely strong) to all entities. Explosives can spawn naturally as traps wired to Pressure Plates, or wired to Detonators(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) next to a vein of ores can be found in the Underground and Cavern layer.

Inlet Pump.name: Inlet Pump
Inlet Pump.tooltip: Inlet and Outlet Pumps are mechanisms used to transport liquids (water, lava, honey, and Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)), without having to construct pathways through blocks or rely on gravity. Instead, an Inlet and Outlet Pump need only be connected to each other with Wires and activated, which transfers fluid from the Inlet Pump to the Outlet Pump. Each activation transfers up to four tiles of liquid. For continuous automated pumping, a timer can be used. Despite its appearance as a pipe that takes in liquid from beside it, an Inlet Pump must be submerged in liquid, as it removes liquid that lies directly over its graphic, and does so equally from all of its 2×2 tile space. Similarly, an Outlet Pump spawns liquid directly over its graphic, and does so equally over all of its 2×2 tile space.

Outlet Pump.name: Outlet Pump
Outlet Pump.tooltip: Inlet and Outlet Pumps are mechanisms used to transport liquids (water, lava, honey, and Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)), without having to construct pathways through blocks or rely on gravity. Instead, an Inlet and Outlet Pump need only be connected to each other with Wires and activated, which transfers fluid from the Inlet Pump to the Outlet Pump. 1 Second Timer.name: 1 Second Timer
1 Second Timer.tooltip: Timers are triggering mechanisms that periodically send an activation signal to other mechanisms. There are five different types of timers, which differ in the interval at which the signal is sent: 5 Second Timer, 3 Second Timer, 1 Second Timer, 1/2 Second Timer, and 1/4 Second Timer. Timers need to be placed in order to function; they can be placed freely in the air, allowing platforms and walls to be built off of them. They are toggled on and off by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Timers can also be activated and deactivated using other mechanism activation items. For example, a Switch on the same path of Wire will toggle a timer on and off. Multiple timers on the same circuit will also repeatedly toggle each other on and off. All timers can be purchased from the Mechanic, while some can also be crafted.

Candy Cane Block.name: Candy Cane Block
Candy Cane Block.tooltip: Candy Cane Blocks are blocks that are dropped in stacks of 20–49 from Presents obtained during the Christmas event, with a chance of 16.803% in pre-Hardmode and 15.683% in Hardmode. They have no value other than as building material, and in crafting Candy Cane Wall. Despite them both being Candy Cane Blocks, they do not "merge" when placed next to each other.

Candy Cane Wall.name: Candy Cane Wall
Candy Cane Wall.tooltip: Candy Cane Walls are background walls crafted from Candy Cane Blocks. They can only be obtained during Christmas, but will remain in the world after Christmas passes.

Santa Hat.name: Santa Hat
Santa Hat.tooltip: The Santa set is a vanity set which consists of the Santa Hat, the Santa Shirt, and the Santa Pants. It is purchased from Santa Claus for 45 Gold (set) after the Frost Legion has been defeated. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Snow Block.name: Snow Block
Snow Block.tooltip: Snow Blocks are blocks found naturally-placed in the Snow biome. Snow Blocks placed in the Surface layer, either naturally or by a player, will cause a snowfall effect. This is purely visual, and has no functional effects. Snow Blocks cannot be infected by The Hallow or evil biomes. Snow in any form cannot be melted into water, nor produced from water or Ice Blocks. Snow blocks are also dropped by the Hardmode Frost Legion enemies, and its Snow Balla throws Snowballs that create further Snow blocks when impacting.
Snow Block.drops_summary: Mister Stabby (100%), Snow Balla (100%), Snowman Gangsta (100%)

Snow Brick.name: Snow Brick
Snow Brick.tooltip: Snow Bricks are bricks crafted from Snow Blocks. Placing snow bricks will cause snow to fall in the background and they count toward the qualifications for a Snow biome.

Snow Brick Wall.name: Snow Brick Wall
Snow Brick Wall.tooltip: The Snow Brick Wall is a pre-Hardmode background wall.

Blue Light.name: Blue Light
Blue Light.tooltip: Christmas lights are decorative furniture items and light sources that resemble Christmas string lights and emit very dim light. They can be placed on all four sides of blocks and can be toggled with wires. Christmas lights are purchased from Santa Claus for 5 Silver each. Christmas lights are available in three colors that are each sold separately.

Blue Present.name: Blue Present
Blue Present.tooltip: The Present is a grab bag item available during the Christmas seasonal event which contains a random Christmas-themed reward. It can be opened by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it in the player's inventory, similar to all other grab bags. Presents can be opened anytime, even outside the Christmas season. Presents are dropped with a 1/13 (7.69%) chance by any enemy that has more than 1 maximum health, deals more than 0 damage, and drops coins, during Christmas only. Therefore, enemies spawned by statues, enemies from the Old One's Army and Lunar Events, etc. can never drop Presents (see Coin drops for the full list). Moreover, Meteor Heads cannot drop Presents either. Presents can be placed down as furniture, and one of eight possible appearances can be cycled through  by pressing ▲ Up and ▼ Down.

Snow Globe.name: Snow Globe
Snow Globe.tooltip: The Snow Globe is a Hardmode event-summoning item used to summon the Frost Legion event. The player also must have at least 200 maximum health to initiate the event, but can then be used in any world at any time afterward. The Snow Globe has a 1/15 (6.67%) chance of being obtained from Presents (dropped during the Christmas event) opened specifically in Hardmode worlds.

Carrot.name: Carrot
Carrot.tooltip: The Carrot is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Pet Bunny that follows the player. If the player gets too far away from the bunny, it will fly at a fast speed while emitting a trail of smoke to catch up to the player. The color of the bunny's fur is defined by the shirt color chosen for the character, meaning the color can be changed using a Dresser. The Carrot is only available to players in the Terraria Collector's Edition and Terraria 15th Anniversary Collector's Edition, and will automatically appear in the inventory of any newly generated characters.

Adamantite Beam.name: Adamantite Beam
Adamantite Beam.tooltip: The Adamantite Beam is a Hardmode brick. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Titanstone Block.

Adamantite Beam Wall.name: Adamantite Beam Wall
Adamantite Beam Wall.tooltip: Adamantite Beam Wall is a type of wall crafted from Adamantite Beam.

Demonite Brick Wall.name: Demonite Brick Wall
Demonite Brick Wall.tooltip: Demonite Brick Wall is a wall crafted from a Demonite Brick. It emits a faint blue glow when placed.  Like most walls, they will stop enemy spawning, and can be used for NPC houses.

Sandstone Brick.name: Sandstone Brick
Sandstone Brick.tooltip: Sandstone Bricks are brick-type blocks that spawn naturally in Pyramids and can also be crafted manually.

Sandstone Brick Wall.name: Sandstone Brick Wall
Sandstone Brick Wall.tooltip: The Sandstone Brick Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Pyramids. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is always considered a safe wall.

Ebonstone Brick.name: Ebonstone Brick
Ebonstone Brick.tooltip: Ebonstone Brick is a type of brick. Unlike its raw block counterpart, the Ebonstone Block, it does not spread The Corruption, nor does it turn the area into a Corruption biome, thus making it a safe construction material for NPC houses and other structures. Its Crimson counterpart is Crimstone Brick.

Ebonstone Brick Wall.name: Ebonstone Brick Wall
Ebonstone Brick Wall.tooltip: Ebonstone Brick Wall is a wall crafted from Ebonstone Brick. Like the brick, Ebonstone Brick Walls do not spread The Corruption.

Red Stucco.name: Red Stucco
Red Stucco.tooltip: Stucco blocks are decorative building materials that are available in four different colors.

Yellow Stucco.name: Yellow Stucco
Yellow Stucco.tooltip: Stucco blocks are decorative building materials that are available in four different colors.

Green Stucco.tooltip: Stucco blocks are decorative building materials that are available in four different colors.

Ebonwood.name: Ebonwood
Ebonwood.tooltip: Ebonwood is a type of wood harvested from Ebonwood trees and Ebonwood Palm trees found naturally growing in Corruption biomes. Ebonwood trees can be cultivated by placing Acorns on top of Corrupt grass or Corrupt Jungle grass above surface, and Ebonwood Palm trees can be cultivated by placing Acorns on top of Ebonsand Blocks above surface.

Rich Mahogany.name: Rich Mahogany
Rich Mahogany.tooltip: Rich Mahogany is a type of wood harvested from Mahogany trees found naturally growing in the Jungle and Underground Jungle, or from Living Mahogany Trees, Underground Cabins in the Underground Jungle, and Jungle Shrines. Mahogany trees can naturally grow from Jungle grass above surface, or they can also be cultivated by placing Acorns on top of Jungle grass above surface.

Pearlwood.name: Pearlwood
Pearlwood.tooltip: Pearlwood is a Hardmode-exclusive type of wood harvested from Pearlwood trees and Pearlwood Palm trees found naturally growing in Hallow biomes. Pearlwood trees can be cultivated by placing Acorns on top of Hallowed grass or Mowed Hallowed grass above surface, and Pearlwood Palm trees can be cultivated by placing Acorns on top of Pearlsand Blocks above surface.

Ebonwood Wall.name: Ebonwood Wall

Rich Mahogany Wall.name: Rich Mahogany Wall
Rich Mahogany Wall.tooltip: The Rich Mahogany Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Underground Cabins in the Underground Jungle, as well as in Jungle Shrines in some worlds. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is always considered a safe wall.

Pearlwood Wall.name: Pearlwood Wall
Pearlwood Wall.tooltip: Pearlwood Wall is a type of wall made from Pearlwood.

Ebonwood Chest.name: Ebonwood Chest
Ebonwood Chest.tooltip: Chests are a type of furniture functioning as storage items. They are accessed using ⚷ Open / Activate and can store up to 40 item stacks in rows of  10×4 /   8×5. In addition to many being craftable, a number of Chests are placed in random locations during world generation. The loot contained in these Chests is determined during world generation, and will not change if the world enters Hardmode. Chests cannot be broken with items inside (the blocks a filled Chest is placed on would also have this trait). However, the Block Swap feature allows the player to change the type of a Chest without having to destroy it. Some types of Chests can be locked by the player using a Chest Lock. When doing so, they will require a key to open again. There are 23 varieties of naturally-occurring Chests (12 of which cannot be crafted), 53 that can only be crafted, and 1 purchasable Chest, for a total of 77 Chest types.

Rich Mahogany Chest.name: Rich Mahogany Chest
Rich Mahogany Chest.tooltip: The Rich Mahogany Chest is a chest found only in Underground Cabins within the Jungle and Underground Jungle biomes. Like Granite Chests and Marble Chests, Rich Mahogany Chests have exactly the same loot as Gold Chests.

Ebonwood Chair.name: Ebonwood Chair
Ebonwood Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Ebonwood Platform.name: Ebonwood Platform
Ebonwood Platform.tooltip: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Ebonwood Bed.name: Ebonwood Bed
Ebonwood Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration. Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 craftable Beds and 5 that can be acquired from the environment. All Beds are functionally identical and differ only in appearance.

Ebonwood Door.name: Ebonwood Door
Ebonwood Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Ebonwood Sword.name: Ebonwood Sword
Ebonwood Sword.tooltip: The Ebonwood Sword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. Its Crimson counterpart is the Shadewood Sword. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Ebonwood Hammer.name: Ebonwood Hammer
Ebonwood Hammer.tooltip: The Ebonwood Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer. Its Crimson counterpart is the Shadewood Hammer. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Ebonwood Bow.name: Ebonwood Bow
Ebonwood Bow.tooltip: The Ebonwood Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow and a variation of the Wooden Bow. It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Shadewood Bow. Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.

Rich Mahogany Sword.name: Rich Mahogany Sword
Rich Mahogany Sword.tooltip: The Rich Mahogany Sword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword and a variation of the Wooden Sword. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Rich Mahogany Hammer.name: Rich Mahogany Hammer
Rich Mahogany Hammer.tooltip: The Rich Mahogany Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Rich Mahogany Bow.name: Rich Mahogany Bow
Rich Mahogany Bow.tooltip: The Rich Mahogany Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow and a variation of the Wooden Bow. Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.

Pearlwood Sword.name: Pearlwood Sword
Pearlwood Sword.tooltip: The Pearlwood Sword is a Hardmode broadsword and a variation of the Wooden Sword. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Pearlwood Hammer.name: Pearlwood Hammer
Pearlwood Hammer.tooltip: The Pearlwood Hammer is a Hardmode hammer. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Pearlwood Bow.name: Pearlwood Bow
Pearlwood Bow.tooltip: The Pearlwood Bow is a Hardmode bow and a variation of the Wooden Bow. Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.

Rainbow Brick.name: Rainbow Brick
Rainbow Brick.tooltip: Rainbow Brick is a Hardmode brick that can be obtained as a drop from the Rainbow Slime. It glows in the dark when placed, and cycles through the colors of the rainbow. The cycling colors of Rainbow Bricks, Rainbow Brick Walls, Helium Moss, Helium Moss Brick, Helium Moss Brick Walls, Rainbow Torches, the Disco Ball, and Rainbow Hair Dye are synchronized with each other. If a waterfall passes through a Rainbow Brick, it will also cycle through the colors. Rainbow Bricks will not change the color of lavafalls, honeyfalls, or Shimmerfalls(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

Rainbow Brick Wall.name: Rainbow Brick Wall
Rainbow Brick Wall.tooltip: Rainbow Brick Walls are Hardmode background walls crafted from Rainbow Bricks. Like Rainbow Bricks, they glow when placed and continuously change color.

Ice Block.name: Ice Block
Ice Block.tooltip: Ice Blocks are a common block type found alongside Snow Blocks in the Snow and Ice biomes. They can be mined with a pickaxe or drill. Ice Blocks have low friction, causing a player walking over them to slide when stopping or changing directions. This effect can be mitigated by equipping Ice Skates or other accessories crafted from them. Ice Blocks can be converted into three other variants via the spread of biomes: Corruption spreads onto Ice to create Purple Ice Blocks Crimson spreads onto Ice to create Red Ice Blocks Hallow spreads onto Ice to create Pink Ice Blocks These will also spread their respective biomes.

Red's Wings.name: Red's Wings
Red's Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Red's Helmet.name: Red's Helmet
Red's Helmet.tooltip: Red's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is the vanity set made for Redigit, lead developer of Terraria. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. Redigit's equipment also includes these non-vanity items, which will drop in addition to his clothing set: Red's Wings Red's Throw

Fish.name: Fish
Fish.tooltip: Fish may refer to: Fishing catches, items caught while fishing Quest fish, part of the Angler's fishing quests Potion fish, crafting ingredients for potions Fish (item), an item used to summon a Penguin pet Zephyr Fish, an item used to summon the Zephyr Fish pet Flying Fish, a flying enemy that spawns when it rains Angler Fish, an enemy found in the Cavern layer and the Jungle

Ice Boomerang.name: Ice Boomerang
Ice Boomerang.tooltip: The Ice Boomerang is a pre-Hardmode boomerang that has a 15.52% chance of being found inside Frozen Chests in the Ice biome, as well as a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being obtained from Frozen and Boreal Crates.
Ice Boomerang.drops_summary: Boreal Crate (16.67%), Frozen Chest (15.52%), Frozen Crate (16.67%)

Keybrand.name: Keybrand
Keybrand.tooltip: The Keybrand is a Hardmode, post-Plantera broadsword that has a 1/200 (0.5%) / 399/40,000 (0.9975%) chance of being dropped by Blue Armored Bones, Hell Armored Bones, and Rusty Armored Bones in the Hardmode Dungeon. It deals increased damage against enemies depending on their missing health, up to a maximum of 200% damage against enemies that have less than 10% health remaining. The Keybrand also has a 20% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. Letting go of ⚒ Use / Attack while swinging will throw the weapon, causing it to sharply drop down after traveling for 0.5 seconds, or touching any solid block, then embed itself in the ground and continuously damage any enemy that touches it. It can be recalled by pressing ⚒ Use / Attack again, which will damage enemies along the way. It can also be recalled mid-throw. Its best modifier is Legendary.
Keybrand.drops_summary: Blue Armored Bones (0.5%), Hell Armored Bones (0.5%), Rusty Armored Bones (0.5%)

Cutlass.name: Cutlass
Cutlass.tooltip: The Cutlass is a Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of being dropped by regular Pirate Invasion enemies (excluding the Parrot), a 1/50 (2%) chance from Pirate Captains, and a 1/10 (10%) chance from the Flying Dutchman. Striking enemies with the weapon increases its damage by 12% per hit, up to a maximum of 50%. This damage bonus decays at a rate of 0.5% per tick or 30% per second. Its best modifier is Legendary.
Cutlass.drops_summary: Most pirates (0.5%), Flying Dutchman (10%), Pirate Captain (2%)

Boreal Wood Work Bench.name: Boreal Wood Work Bench
Boreal Wood Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

True Excalibur.name: True Excalibur
True Excalibur.tooltip: The True Excalibur is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses broadsword and the direct upgrade to the Excalibur. When swung, a large yellow aura with a pink edge follows the swing, reaching about twice the distance of the sword itself. The aura can hit up to six enemies. Its best modifier is Legendary.

True Night's Edge.name: True Night's Edge
True Night's Edge.tooltip: The True Night's Edge is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses broadsword and the direct upgrade to the Night's Edge. When swung, a circular purple aura follows the swing, reaching farther than the sword itself. The aura can hit up to two enemies. The sword will also fire a spinning green blade that deals 50% of the weapon's damage (35 base damage) and can strike up to 3 times. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Frostbrand.name: Frostbrand
Frostbrand.tooltip: The Frostbrand is a Hardmode broadsword that has a 19/80 (23.75%) chance of being dropped by Ice Mimics. When swung, it fires a Frost Bolt projectile that pierces two enemies before dissipating on the third hit, cannot pass through blocks, and inflicts the Frostbite debuff for 4 seconds on hit. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Boreal Wood Table.name: Boreal Wood Table
Boreal Wood Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Red Potion.name: Red Potion
Red Potion.tooltip: The Red Potion is a potion which can be found in chests within worlds generated with the Drunk seed enabled (1/30 (3.33%) chance), or the For the Worthy seed enabled (1/10 (10%) chance), or both Drunk and For the Worthy enabled (13/100 (13%) chance). It can also be dropped by Jungle Mimics, which spawn in Underground Jungle during Hardmode when Celebration Mk 10 is enabled. It inflicts a very large number of debuffs for 1 hour / 2 hours / 2.5 hours on players who consume it. If For the worthy is enabled, it instead grants up to three random buffs for 30 minutes.

Tactical Shotgun.name: Tactical Shotgun
Tactical Shotgun.tooltip: The Tactical Shotgun is a Hardmode, post-Plantera gun that has a 1/12 (8.33%) / 23/144 (15.97%) chance of being dropped by Tactical Skeletons in the Hardmode Dungeon. When used, it fires six bullets in a spread, consuming one piece of ammunition. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Ivy Chest.name: Ivy Chest
Ivy Chest.tooltip: The Ivy Chest is a chest storage item found only in Jungle Shrines and Living Mahogany Trees in the Underground Jungle.

Frozen Chest.name: Frozen Chest
Frozen Chest.tooltip: The Frozen Chest is a Chest storage item found only in the Ice biome, spawning as frequently as Chests do in other biomes.

Marrow.name: Marrow
Marrow.tooltip: The Marrow is a Hardmode bow that has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance to be dropped by Skeleton Archers. When used, it converts any type of arrow into high-velocity Bone Arrows that shatter into 2 bone shards upon hitting enemies or blocks, each of which deals 25% of the weapon's damage (11 base damage when using Wooden Arrows) but does not inflict knockback. The bone shards do not pierce and are launched away from the struck enemy or block, in addition to being heavily affected by gravity. The Marrow has a base 9% critical strike chance, as opposed to the usual 4%. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Unholy Trident.name: Unholy Trident
Unholy Trident.tooltip: The Unholy Trident is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss wand that fires high-velocity purple tridents which lose speed as they travel and have 25 armor penetration, and inflict the Shadowflame debuff for 5–10 seconds on hit. Upon contact with blocks, the tridents briefly become stuck and will deal damage to enemies that touch them. The Unholy Trident has a 1/30 (3.33%) chance of being dropped by Red Devils. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Frost Helmet.name: Frost Helmet
Frost Helmet.tooltip: Frost armor is a Hardmode melee/ranged armor set consisting of the Frost Helmet, Frost Breastplate, and Frost Leggings. Crafting the full set requires a total of 3 Frost Cores and 46 Adamantite or Titanium Bars (184 ore). The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +43 defense +26% melee and ranged damage +11% melee and ranged critical strike chance +10% melee speed +8% movement speed Melee and ranged weapons give off blue light and particles, and inflict the Frostbite debuff for 5–14 seconds upon enemy hits. The player also leaves behind a visual snow trail while walking, and their hurt sound will be set to that of Thin Ice shattering.

Frost Breastplate.name: Frost Breastplate

The player also leaves behind a visual snow trail while walking, and their hurt sound will be set to that of Thin Ice shattering.

Tin Ore.name: Tin Ore
Tin Ore.tooltip: Tin Ore is a pre-Hardmode ore. It spawns in the Underground and Cavern layers, and occasionally on the surface. Tin Ore also has a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes. Its alternate ore counterpart is  Copper Ore.
Tin Ore.drops_summary: Azure Crate (0.89%), Baby Slime (0.16%), Black Slime (0.16%), +30 more

Lead Ore.name: Lead Ore

Tin Bar.name: Tin Bar
Tin Bar.tooltip: The Tin Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Copper Bar. Newly created characters outside of Journey Mode will always spawn with the Copper Shortsword, Copper Pickaxe, and Copper Axe, regardless of whether the world generated with Copper or Tin.

Lead Bar.name: Lead Bar
Lead Bar.tooltip: The Lead Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Iron Bar. Newly created characters in Journey Mode will always spawn with the Iron Shortsword, Iron Pickaxe, and Iron Axe, regardless of whether the world generated with Iron or Lead.
Lead Bar.drops_summary: Azure Crate (1.39%), Boreal Crate (1.39%), Bramble Crate (1.39%), +23 more

Tungsten Bar.name: Tungsten Bar
Tungsten Bar.tooltip: The Tungsten Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Silver Bar.
Tungsten Bar.drops_summary: Azure Crate (1.39%), Boreal Crate (1.39%), Bramble Crate (1.39%), +22 more

Platinum Bar.name: Platinum Bar
Platinum Bar.tooltip: The Platinum Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Gold Bar.
Platinum Bar.drops_summary: Azure Crate (1.39%), Boreal Crate (1.39%), Bramble Crate (1.39%), +21 more

Tin Watch.name: Tin Watch
Tin Watch.tooltip: Watches are informational accessories that show the current in-game time in the top-right corner of the screen. The display of time can be toggled by  clicking the watch icon underneath the minimap while the inventory is open or   selecting the watch icon in the equipment menu.

Tungsten Watch.name: Tungsten Watch
Tungsten Watch.tooltip: Watches are informational accessories that show the current in-game time in the top-right corner of the screen. The display of time can be toggled by  clicking the watch icon underneath the minimap while the inventory is open or   selecting the watch icon in the equipment menu.

Platinum Watch.name: Platinum Watch
Platinum Watch.tooltip: Watches are informational accessories that show the current in-game time in the top-right corner of the screen. The display of time can be toggled by  clicking the watch icon underneath the minimap while the inventory is open or   selecting the watch icon in the equipment menu.

Tin Chandelier.name: Tin Chandelier
Tin Chandelier.tooltip: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers come in many varieties which differ only in appearance and sell value. All chandeliers can be picked up using a pickaxe, drill, or explosives. Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.

Tungsten Chandelier.name: Tungsten Chandelier
Tungsten Chandelier.tooltip: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers come in many varieties which differ only in appearance and sell value. All chandeliers can be picked up using a pickaxe, drill, or explosives. Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.

Platinum Chandelier.name: Platinum Chandelier
Platinum Chandelier.tooltip: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers come in many varieties which differ only in appearance and sell value. All chandeliers can be picked up using a pickaxe, drill, or explosives. Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.

Platinum Candle.name: Platinum Candle
Platinum Candle.tooltip: Candles are a type of furniture and light source. Candles can only be placed on flat-surface items. Candles will produce light underwater if placed and can be toggled on and off with ⚷ Open / Activate and by mechanisms. Certain types of candles provide buffs or debuffs. The Water Candle is a special type of candle found in Dungeons which increases enemy spawn rates by 33% and the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50% when placed or held. The Peace Candle reduces spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%, in contrast to the Water Candle. The Shadow Candle(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns in the area. For Water Candles and Peace Candles, multiple candles cannot stack, even if one is placed and the other is held.

Platinum Candelabra.name: Platinum Candelabra
Platinum Candelabra.tooltip: Candelabras are a type of furniture and light source that emits light when placed on a flat surface such as blocks, platforms, and flat furniture items. It is not destroyed by water. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 23 /  12 craftable and 5 looted variations of the Candelabra.

Platinum Crown.name: Platinum Crown
Platinum Crown.tooltip: The Platinum Crown is a craftable vanity item that can be worn in the Social Helmet inventory slot. It is also one of the crafting materials for the Slime Crown, which is used to spawn the King Slime. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Gold Crown.

Lead Anvil.name: Lead Anvil
Lead Anvil.tooltip: The Iron Anvil and Lead Anvil are pre-Hardmode crafting stations used mainly to craft weapons and armor. Both anvils can craft the same items. Most of their recipes require metal bars, although they are also used to make other items, such as the Jungle tier of equipment. An anvil is a vital crafting station for most of the game, as it is used to make items from every tier up to Cobalt and Palladium, after which it must be replaced by a Mythril or Orichalcum Anvil. Both anvils are craftable, but can sometimes also be found in Underground Cabins. The Iron Anvil can furthermore be purchased from the Merchant.

Tin Brick.name: Tin Brick
Tin Brick.tooltip: Tin Brick is a type of Brick and an aesthetic building material made from Tin Ore. In some worlds it can also be harvested from Jungle Shrines. Like the ore it is made of, placed Tin Bricks will sparkle. As tin becomes fairly useless early in the game, this is an inexpensive ore brick to build with. Despite being made of Tin, it has no sell value, as with most other blocks. Tin Plating is also available as a decorative block, with the same ingredients and color but a different texture.

Tungsten Brick.name: Tungsten Brick
Tungsten Brick.tooltip: Tungsten Brick is a type of Brick and an aesthetic building material. Like the ore it is made of, placed Tungsten Bricks will sparkle. It is not recommended that it be used for building unless the player has tungsten to spare. Despite being made of Tungsten, it has no sell value. It can be crafted into Tungsten Brick Walls.

Platinum Brick.name: Platinum Brick
Platinum Brick.tooltip: Platinum Brick is a type of Brick and an aesthetic building material. Like the ore it's made of, placed Platinum Bricks will sparkle. Despite being made of Platinum, it has no sell value. It can be crafted into Platinum Brick Walls.

Tin Brick Wall.name: Tin Brick Wall
Tin Brick Wall.tooltip: The Tin Brick Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Jungle Shrines in some worlds. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is always considered a safe wall.

Tungsten Brick Wall.name: Tungsten Brick Wall
Tungsten Brick Wall.tooltip: Tungsten Brick Wall is a background wall crafted from Tungsten Bricks. Like most walls, they will stop enemy spawning, and can be used for NPC houses.

Platinum Brick Wall.name: Platinum Brick Wall
Platinum Brick Wall.tooltip: Platinum Brick Wall is a background wall crafted from Platinum Bricks. Like most walls, they will stop enemy spawning, and can be used for NPC houses.

Beam Sword.name: Beam Sword
Beam Sword.tooltip: The Beam Sword is a Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/150 (0.67%) chance of being dropped by Armored Skeletons. When swung, it fires a yellow Sword Beam projectile that can pierce one enemy and bounce off blocks three times before dissipating. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Ice Blade.name: Ice Blade
Ice Blade.tooltip: The Ice Blade is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that is found in Frozen Chests in the Ice biome, Frozen Crates, and Boreal Crates. When swung, it occasionally fires an Ice Bolt projectile that deals the weapon's damage and does not pass through blocks or pierce enemies. The Ice Blade also has a base 6% critical strike chance, as opposed to the usual 4%.  Its best modifier is Legendary.
Ice Blade.drops_summary: Boreal Crate (16.67%), Frozen Chest (15.52%), Frozen Crate (16.67%)

Ice Bow.name: Ice Bow
Ice Bow.tooltip: The Ice Bow is a Hardmode bow that has a 19/80 (23.75%) chance of being dropped by Ice Mimics. When used, it converts any type of arrow into high-velocity Frost Arrows. Unlike the Frostburn Arrow item, they do not inflict the Frostburn debuff. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Frost Staff.name: Frost Staff
Frost Staff.tooltip: The Frost Staff is a Hardmode wand that has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by Icy Mermen and Ice Elementals. When used, it fires a frost bolt that pierces one enemy and does not pass through blocks. The Frost Staff also inflicts the Frostbite debuff for 7 seconds on hit. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Wood Helmet.name: Wood Helmet
Wood Helmet.tooltip: Wood armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Wood Helmet, Wood Breastplate, and Wood Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Wood. The full set grants 3 defense while equipped.

Wood Breastplate.name: Wood Breastplate
Wood Breastplate.tooltip: Wood armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Wood Helmet, Wood Breastplate, and Wood Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Wood. The full set grants 3 defense while equipped.

Wood Greaves.name: Wood Greaves
Wood Greaves.tooltip: Wood armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Wood Helmet, Wood Breastplate, and Wood Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Wood. The full set grants 3 defense while equipped.

Ebonwood Helmet.name: Ebonwood Helmet
Ebonwood Helmet.tooltip: Ebonwood armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Ebonwood Helmet, Ebonwood Breastplate, and Ebonwood Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Ebonwood. The full set grants 5 defense while equipped. Its Crimson counterpart is Shadewood armor, which has identical stats.

Ebonwood Breastplate.name: Ebonwood Breastplate
Ebonwood Breastplate.tooltip: Ebonwood armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Ebonwood Helmet, Ebonwood Breastplate, and Ebonwood Greaves. Rich Mahogany Helmet.name: Rich Mahogany Helmet
Rich Mahogany Helmet.tooltip: Rich Mahogany armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Rich Mahogany Helmet, Rich Mahogany Breastplate, and Rich Mahogany Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Rich Mahogany. The full set grants 4 defense while equipped.

Rich Mahogany Breastplate.name: Rich Mahogany Breastplate
Rich Mahogany Breastplate.tooltip: Rich Mahogany armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Rich Mahogany Helmet, Rich Mahogany Breastplate, and Rich Mahogany Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Rich Mahogany. The full set grants 4 defense while equipped.

Rich Mahogany Greaves.name: Rich Mahogany Greaves
Rich Mahogany Greaves.tooltip: Rich Mahogany armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Rich Mahogany Helmet, Rich Mahogany Breastplate, and Rich Mahogany Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Rich Mahogany. The full set grants 4 defense while equipped.

Pearlwood Helmet.name: Pearlwood Helmet
Pearlwood Helmet.tooltip: Pearlwood armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Pearlwood Helmet, Pearlwood Breastplate, and Pearlwood Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Pearlwood. The full set grants 8 defense while equipped.

Pearlwood Breastplate.name: Pearlwood Breastplate
Pearlwood Breastplate.tooltip: Pearlwood armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Pearlwood Helmet, Pearlwood Breastplate, and Pearlwood Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Pearlwood. The full set grants 8 defense while equipped.

Pearlwood Greaves.name: Pearlwood Greaves
Pearlwood Greaves.tooltip: Pearlwood armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Pearlwood Helmet, Pearlwood Breastplate, and Pearlwood Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Pearlwood. The full set grants 8 defense while equipped.

Amethyst Staff.name: Amethyst Staff
Amethyst Staff.tooltip: The Amethyst Staff is a pre-Hardmode wand and type of gem staff that fires a purple bolt which does not pierce and homes onto the closest enemy within a 31.25-tile radius. While wearing a Gem robe, the fired bolt will be enchanted by ability of the corresponding gem type, granting it additional effects (see Notes for details). Its best modifier is Mythical.

Topaz Staff.name: Topaz Staff
Topaz Staff.tooltip: The Topaz Staff is a pre-Hardmode wand and type of gem staff that fires a yellow bolt which does not pierce and explodes upon dissipating, dealing 35% of the weapon's damage (5 base damage) and knockback (base knockback of 1.225 (Extremely weak)) to other nearby enemies within an area, but not to the target hit directly by the bolt. While wearing a Gem robe, the fired bolt will be enchanted by ability of the corresponding gem type, granting it additional effects (see Notes for details). Its best modifier is Mythical.

Sapphire Staff.name: Sapphire Staff
Sapphire Staff.tooltip: The Sapphire Staff is a pre-Hardmode wand that fires a blue bolt that does not pierce.

Emerald Staff.name: Emerald Staff
Emerald Staff.tooltip: The Emerald Staff is a pre-Hardmode wand and type of gem staff that fires a high-velocity green bolt which gradually slows down and then lingers in place. The green bolt can pierce once, and can stick to blocks and deal damage to enemies that walk into it. While moving, the green bolt also has a damaging trail that follows it, extending its hitbox. While wearing a Gem robe, the fired bolt will be enchanted by ability of the corresponding gem type, granting it additional effects (see Notes for details). Its best modifier is Mythical.

Ruby Staff.name: Ruby Staff
Ruby Staff.tooltip: The Ruby Staff is a pre-Hardmode wand and type of gem staff that quickly fires a red bolt, which deals 50% of the weapon's damage (9 base damage) and 100% of its knockback, and has 4 armor penetration, but does not pierce. While wearing a Gem robe, the fired bolt will be enchanted by ability of the corresponding gem type, granting it additional effects (see Notes for details). Its best modifier is Mythical.

Diamond Staff.name: Diamond Staff
Diamond Staff.tooltip: The Diamond Staff is a pre-Hardmode wand and type of gem staff that fires a bright white bolt which can pierce once and has a large hitbox, indicated by the faint, extra shine. While wearing a gem robe, the fired bolt will be enchanted by ability of the corresponding gem type, granting it additional effects (see Notes for details). Its best modifier is Mythical.

Grass Wall.name: Grass Wall
Grass Wall.tooltip: The Grass Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in above-ground tunnels and grottoes on the surface, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained by purchasing it from the Dryad for 10 Copper each, while a Blood Moon is not occurring. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.

Jungle Wall.name: Jungle Wall
Jungle Wall.tooltip: The Jungle Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in the Underground Jungle, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained by purchasing it from the Dryad for 10 Copper each, in Hardmode. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.

Flower Wall.name: Flower Wall
Flower Wall.tooltip: The Flower Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in the Forest and in Enchanted Sword Shrines, considered unsafe. It does drop as an item when destroyed. It can also be obtained by purchasing it from the Dryad for 10 Copper each. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.

Jetpack.name: Jetpack
Jetpack.tooltip: The Jetpack is a Hardmode wing-type accessory obtainable after defeating any mechanical boss. Like all wings, it grants the player the ability to fly and glide when equipped, as well as not take fall damage. At top speed, it allows traveling at 33 mph horizontally and 38 mph vertically. It has a flight time of 2.5 seconds and a vertical speed multiplier of 150%. Additionally, the Jetpack have a unique ability to upwards boost by holding the ▲ Up key when flying, increasing the top vertical speed to 77 mph. However, the flight time is consumed at double the normal rate when the boost is activated. The Jetpack can be purchased from the Steampunker for 40 Gold during the following moon phases:

Butterfly Wings.name: Butterfly Wings
Butterfly Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Cactus Wall.name: Cactus Wall
Cactus Wall.tooltip: Cactus Wall is a background wall made from Cactus.

Cloud.name: Cloud
Cloud.tooltip: Cloud is a type of block found beneath Floating Islands, along with Rain Cloud blocks; on the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, they can be found in stacks in Skyware Chests, Sky Crates and Azure Crates as well. Cloud blocks display as solid blocks, but light passes through them as if they were empty space. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, landing on them will not inflict fall damage.
Cloud.drops_summary: Azure Crate (50%), Sky Crate (50%), Skyware Chest (100%)

Cloud Wall.name: Cloud Wall
Cloud Wall.tooltip: The Cloud Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated on Floating Islands. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is always considered a safe wall.

Seaweed.name: Seaweed
Seaweed.tooltip: Seaweed is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Turtle to follow the player around. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Turtle will fly with a propeller to catch up to the player. Seaweed has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being found in Ivy Chests, located in the Underground Jungle's Jungle Shrines or Living Mahogany Trees. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, it also has a 1/20 (5%) chance of being obtained from Jungle Crates and Bramble Crates.
Seaweed.drops_summary: Bramble Crate (5%), Ivy Chest (2%), Jungle Crate (5%)

Rune Hat.name: Rune Hat
Rune Hat.tooltip: The Rune set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Rune Hat and Rune Robe. Both pieces are always dropped by the Rune Wizard, a rare Underground enemy. Wearing the full set causes the player to emit a pulse effect, as well as a bright orange and green particle effect from their feet when walking. The particles are visible in darkness but do not emit light onto other objects. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Rune Robe.name: Rune Robe
Rune Robe.tooltip: The Rune set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Rune Hat and Rune Robe. Both pieces are always dropped by the Rune Wizard, a rare Underground enemy. Wearing the full set causes the player to emit a pulse effect, as well as a bright orange and green particle effect from their feet when walking. The particles are visible in darkness but do not emit light onto other objects. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Mushroom Spear.name: Mushroom Spear
Mushroom Spear.tooltip: The Mushroom Spear is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss spear that can be purchased from the Truffle for 70 Gold. When thrust, it summons seven spinning mushrooms that linger in midair and deal 33.33% of the weapon's damage (20 base damage) but do not inflict knockback. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Terra Blade.name: Terra Blade
Terra Blade.tooltip: The Terra Blade is a Hardmode, post-Plantera broadsword. When swung, a green aura follows the swing, reaching farther than the sword itself. The aura can hit up to three enemies. The sword will also fire a green slash projectile that pierces infinitely, dealing the weapon's damage but reducing its damage by 25% of its current damage for each target it pierces. The projectile will dissipate after 1.5 seconds, upon contact with blocks, or when its damage falls to 0 after piercing. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Grenade Launcher.name: Grenade Launcher
Grenade Launcher.tooltip: The Grenade Launcher is a Hardmode, post-Plantera launcher. When used, it consumes rockets and launches grenades that explode after three seconds have passed or upon contact with enemies. The grenades are strongly affected by gravity and can damage the player for a flat 60 damage. The Grenade Launcher has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance to be dropped from Plantera, and it is guaranteed to drop the first time Plantera is defeated (unless in Expert Mode, where she drops her Treasure Bag instead). In addition, 50–149 Rocket Is will be dropped alongside the Grenade Launcher. Its best modifier is Unreal for combat purposes and Rapid for mining and usage of liquid rockets.

Rocket Launcher.name: Rocket Launcher
Rocket Launcher.tooltip: The Rocket Launcher is a Hardmode, post-Plantera launcher that has a 1/18 (5.56%) / 35/324 (10.8%) chance of being dropped by Skeleton Commandos in the Hardmode Dungeon. When used, it fires rockets as ammunition, which can damage the player for a flat 60 damage. Enemies that are directly hit by rockets take double damage (110 base damage). Its best modifier is Unreal for combat purposes and Rapid for mining and usage of liquid rockets.

Proximity Mine Launcher.name: Proximity Mine Launcher
Proximity Mine Launcher.tooltip: The Proximity Mine Launcher is a Hardmode, post-Plantera launcher that can be purchased from the Cyborg for 35 Gold. When used, it consumes a rocket and fires a mine that travels in a short arc before becoming stationary and semi-transparent until an enemy approaches or until a minute passes, at which point it explodes. The player will not activate the mine, but will be damaged by an exploding mine. Stationary mines deal 300% of the weapon's damage (240 base damage) to enemies, but not to players, who only take a flat 60 damage instead. Its best modifier is Unreal for combat purposes and Rapid for mining and usage of liquid rockets.

Fairy Wings.name: Fairy Wings
Fairy Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Slime Block.name: Slime Block
Slime Block.tooltip: The Slime Block is a type of block crafted using the Solidifier. Walking or landing on Slime Blocks produces droplet particles.

Flesh Block.name: Flesh Block
Flesh Block.tooltip: The Flesh Block is a Hardmode block. They are used to craft Flesh furniture and Flesh Block Walls. When placed, eyeballs and intestines can be seen bulging out of the block. Flesh Blocks will not spread The Crimson.

Mushroom Wall.name: Mushroom Wall
Mushroom Wall.tooltip: The Mushroom Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Underground Cabins in the Glowing Mushroom biome, considered safe. It is also considered a safe wall when placed by the player. Spraying Mud Walls or Jungle Walls with Dark Blue Solution creates unsafe Mushroom Walls. These do not drop as an item when destroyed.

Rain Cloud.name: Rain Cloud
Rain Cloud.tooltip: Rain Cloud is a type of block found beneath Floating Islands, along with Cloud blocks. Rain Cloud blocks cause purely decorative raindrops to appear beneath them that fall for about 18 tiles before fading away for 5 more. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, landing on Rain Clouds will not inflict fall damage.

Bone Block.name: Bone Block
Bone Block.tooltip: Bone Blocks are blocks that are placed by the Bone Wand at the cost of 1 Bone per block. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, mining them will drop Bones. There is no way to obtain the block as an item in these versions. On the  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version, mining them will drop the Bone Block as an item. There is no way to convert them back into regular Bones. The block item cannot be used to craft Bone Block Walls or Bone furniture, which are instead made from raw Bones themselves, at a Bone Welder.

Frozen Slime Block.name: Frozen Slime Block
Frozen Slime Block.tooltip: Frozen Slime Blocks are blocks without any friction, making them more slippery than their constituent block, the Ice Block. When a character moves atop Frozen Slime Blocks, their movement speed is maintained when direction keys are released, sliding at full speed until the Frozen Slime Blocks end or an obstacle is reached. Speed is maintained even when auto-stepping up single-block steps.

Bone Block Wall.name: Bone Block Wall
Bone Block Wall.tooltip: The Bone Block Wall is a type of wall which is crafted from Bones. Despite the naming similarity to Bone Blocks, it has never been able to craft them, nor been used to craft them.

Slime Block Wall.name: Slime Block Wall
Slime Block Wall.tooltip: The Slime Block Wall is a type of Wall made from a Slime Block.

Flesh Block Wall.name: Flesh Block Wall
Flesh Block Wall.tooltip: The Flesh Block Wall is a type of background wall. As with most placed walls, it is compatible with NPC housing and will stop enemies from spawning.

Rocket I.name: Rocket I
Rocket I.tooltip: Rockets are a Hardmode, post-Plantera type of ammunition which are mainly sold by the Cyborg. The Rocket I variant is also dropped by Plantera when it drops the Grenade Launcher. Most launchers use Rockets as ammunition. All rocket types have two significant defining traits: area of effect, and the ability to destroy tiles. Rockets I and II have a small area of effect, closest to that of a Bomb or Grenade, while Rockets III and IV have an area similar to the blast radius of Dynamite. Rockets I and III will leave tiles unaffected, while II and IV will break blocks and furniture in their blast radius (except for explosion-proof objects). In most cases, a rocket's splash damage will harm the player who fired it if they are caught in the blast radius, dealing a flat 60 damage. These explosions will not affect other players unless they have PvP enabled, however.

Rocket II.tooltip: Rockets are a Hardmode, post-Plantera type of ammunition which are mainly sold by the Cyborg. The Rocket I variant is also dropped by Plantera when it drops the Grenade Launcher. Asphalt Block.name: Asphalt Block
Asphalt Block.tooltip: The Asphalt Block is a unique Hardmode block that multiplies the top speed of players running along it by 3.5×, and doubles the rate of deceleration when slowing down. It only increases the player's normal movement speed, stacking multiplicatively with buffs such as Swiftness and Well Fed, and does not directly increase acceleration. It only affects players running directly on it; the speed of enemies, NPCs, and critters will remain unaffected. Immediately after jumping or falling off of Asphalt Block, the speed will return to normal. With no other boosts, running on Asphalt gives the player a maximum running speed of 53 mph, with about 3 seconds of acceleration, while the normal maximum running speed is 15 mph.

Cobalt Pickaxe.name: Cobalt Pickaxe
Cobalt Pickaxe.tooltip: The Cobalt Pickaxe is a Hardmode pickaxe. It is the alternative to the Cobalt Drill, having a lower base mining speed but longer range and the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Mythril and Orichalcum Ore. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Palladium Pickaxe. The Cobalt Pickaxe has slightly less pickaxe power, damage, and mining speed. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Mythril Pickaxe.name: Mythril Pickaxe
Mythril Pickaxe.tooltip: The Mythril Pickaxe is a Hardmode pickaxe. It is the alternative to the Mythril Drill, having a lower base mining speed but longer range and the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Adamantite and Titanium Ore. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Orichalcum Pickaxe. The Mythril Pickaxe has slightly less pickaxe power, damage, and mining speed. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Adamantite Pickaxe.name: Adamantite Pickaxe
Adamantite Pickaxe.tooltip: The Adamantite Pickaxe is a Hardmode pickaxe. It is the alternative to the Adamantite Drill, having a lower base mining speed but longer range and the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Adamantite and Titanium Ore. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Titanium Pickaxe. The Adamantite Pickaxe has slightly less pickaxe power, damage, and mining speed. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Clentaminator.name: Clentaminator
Clentaminator.tooltip: The Clentaminator is a Hardmode tool which can be used to create or destroy biomes. It uses Solutions as ammunition, with each Solution spreading a different biome. It has a similar firing pattern to the Flamethrower, but has a much longer range, fires through blocks and works in water. The Clentaminator is generally the fastest means of spreading or removing Hallow, Corruption and Crimson. It can also rapidly convert Jungle to Glowing Mushroom biome and vice versa. It can be purchased from the Steampunker for 2 Platinum. After the Moon Lord is defeated, the Clentaminator can be upgraded into the Terraformer by throwing it into Shimmer. The Clentaminator cannot be purchased in Remix and Zenith worlds. The Clentaminator cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Green Solution.name: Green Solution
Green Solution.tooltip: Solutions are a type of ammunition used solely by the Clentaminator and Terraformer. Each solution will convert certain blocks and walls to other blocks and walls, creating and/or destroying different biomes in the process. There are 8 different solutions. 7 of them are sold by the Steampunker, who sells different solutions based on certain conditions, and one is sold by the Truffle, who always sells it. Solutions cannot be purchased in worlds with the Remix special world seed active.

Hammush.name: Hammush
Hammush.tooltip: The Hammush is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss hammer that is purchased from the Truffle for 40 Gold. When used, the Hammush releases 5 lingering Mushroom projectiles from its tip and along its swing arc. The Mushroom projectiles deal 50% of the Hammush's damage (13 base damage), but do not inflict knockback and cannot pierce. Like the Pwnhammer, it can destroy altars. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Nettle Burst.name: Nettle Burst
Nettle Burst.tooltip: The Nettle Burst is a Hardmode wand that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Plantera. When used, it extends a snaking vine from the player's position, which passes through blocks, pierces infinite enemies, and deals 0.17 s global invincibility. The snaking vine has 11–12 segments, and each has a length of 2 tiles. The vine extends segmentally every 0.07 s, with each individual segment lasting 1.48 s. The projectiles of Nettle Burst have 10 armor penetration, which stacks with the former segment.Hence the actual armor penetration increases with segments, from the root's 10 to the end's 110 or 120. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Ankh Banner.name: Ankh Banner
Ankh Banner.tooltip: Banners are decorative furniture items that can be placed on the underside of blocks. Many are found naturally-placed in various biomes. There are also (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) four / (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) six crafted banners (Red, Green, Blue, Yellow, (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Pink, White) using Silk. Banners can be hung off of blocks and off of platforms which are in (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) any position / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) their bottom position (after being struck three times with a hammer). Faction flags are banners found in the Dungeon. In post-Plantera worlds, the faction flags found hanging in a particular Dungeon area correspond to the background wall type (brick, slab, or tile), both of which signify the types of enemies that will spawn there. See Hardmode Dungeon for more info. There are a total of 25 decorative banners: 6 crafted, 6 faction flags, 3 Floating Island, 6 Underworld, 3 Pyramid, and 1 dropped from the Dark Mage during the Old One's Army event.

Crimson Helmet.name: Crimson Helmet
Crimson Helmet.tooltip: Crimson armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Crimson Helmet , Crimson Scalemail , and Crimson Greaves . Crafting a full set requires a total of 60 Crimtane Bars (180 Crimtane Ore ) and 45 Tissue Samples .

Crimson Scalemail.name: Crimson Scalemail
Crimson Scalemail.tooltip: Crimson armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Crimson Helmet , Crimson Scalemail , and Crimson Greaves . Crafting a full set requires a total of 60 Crimtane Bars (180 Crimtane Ore ) and 45 Tissue Samples .

Crimson Greaves.name: Crimson Greaves
Crimson Greaves.tooltip: Crimson armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Crimson Helmet , Crimson Scalemail , and Crimson Greaves . Crafting a full set requires a total of 60 Crimtane Bars (180 Crimtane Ore ) and 45 Tissue Samples .

Blood Butcherer.name: Blood Butcherer
Blood Butcherer.tooltip: The Blood Butcherer is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. When swung, it inflicts the Blood Butchered debuff upon enemy hits for 9 seconds and causing enemies to visibly bleed, dealing 4 damage per second (4 damage displayed every 1 second). Repeated attacks will cause the debuff to stack up to 5 times, for a total of 20 damage per second (20 damage displayed every 1 second). It is the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Light's Bane. The Blood Butcherer has a greater size and base damage than the Light's Bane, but has a slower speed. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Tendon Bow.name: Tendon Bow
Tendon Bow.tooltip: The Tendon Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow. It is the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Demon Bow. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Flesh Grinder.name: Flesh Grinder
Flesh Grinder.tooltip: The Flesh Grinder is a pre-Hardmode hammer. Its Corruption counterpart is The Breaker. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Deathbringer Pickaxe.name: Deathbringer Pickaxe
Deathbringer Pickaxe.tooltip: The Deathbringer Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe. It can mine blocks up to Hellstone, Crimstone Blocks, and Ebonstone Blocks. Its Corruption counterpart is the Nightmare Pickaxe. The Deathbringer Pickaxe has slightly more pickaxe power and mining speed. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Blood Lust Cluster.name: Blood Lust Cluster
Blood Lust Cluster.tooltip: The Blood Lust Cluster is a pre-Hardmode axe. Its Corruption counterpart is the War Axe of the Night. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

The Undertaker.name: The Undertaker
The Undertaker.tooltip: The Undertaker is a pre-Hardmode gun. It will always drop from the first Crimson Heart destroyed in a Crimson world (along with 100 Musket Balls) and has a 1/5 (20%) chance of dropping from destroyed Crimson Hearts afterward. It also has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being obtained from Crimson and Hematic Crates fished in the Crimson. Its Corruption counterpart is the Musket. The Undertaker has a lower damage per shot but fires much faster. Its best modifier is Unreal.

The Meatball.name: The Meatball
The Meatball.tooltip: The Meatball is a pre-Hardmode flail. Its Corruption counterpart is the Ball O' Hurt. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

The Rotted Fork.name: The Rotted Fork
The Rotted Fork.tooltip: The Rotted Fork is a pre-Hardmode spear that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being obtained from destroying Crimson Hearts found in The Crimson or a 1/5 (20%) chance from Crimson Crates and Hematic Crates. When thrust, it creates a small shockwave at its tip. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
The Rotted Fork.drops_summary: Crimson Crate (20%), Crimson Heart (20%), Hematic Crate (20%)

Snow Hood.name: Snow Hood
Snow Hood.tooltip: Snow armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Snow Hood, Snow Coat, and Snow Pants. Each piece has a 1/30 (3.33%) chance to be dropped by Frozen Zombies. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +9 defense Immunity to the Chilled and Frozen debuffs Snow armor pieces are interchangeable with pieces from Pink Snow armor, still providing the set bonus.

Living Wood Chair.name: Living Wood Chair
Living Wood Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Bone Work Bench.name: Bone Work Bench
Bone Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Mushroom Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Cactus Door.name: Cactus Door
Cactus Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Flame Wings.name: Flame Wings
Flame Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Disc Wall.name: Disc Wall
Disc Wall.tooltip: The Disc Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated on Floating Islands. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is always considered a safe wall.

Skyware Chair.name: Skyware Chair
Skyware Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Bone Table.name: Bone Table
Bone Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Living Wood Wand.name: Living Wood Wand
Living Wood Wand.tooltip: Block-placing wands are special tools that allow the player to place blocks they would normally not be able to place. They do not consume any mana. Each wand consumes a specific material from the player's inventory (details listed below). There are 6 different block-placing wands.

Purple Ice Block.name: Purple Ice Block
Purple Ice Block.tooltip: Ice Blocks are a common block type found alongside Snow Blocks in the Snow and Ice biomes. They can be mined with a pickaxe or drill. Ice Blocks have low friction, causing a player walking over them to slide when stopping or changing directions. This effect can be mitigated by equipping Ice Skates or other accessories crafted from them. Ice Blocks can be converted into three other variants via the spread of biomes: Corruption spreads onto Ice to create Purple Ice Blocks Crimson spreads onto Ice to create Red Ice Blocks Hallow spreads onto Ice to create Pink Ice Blocks These will also spread their respective biomes.

Crimstone Block.name: Crimstone Block
Crimstone Block.tooltip: Crimstone is a block type found in The Crimson. Before Hardmode, it is most prominent in the lining of Chasms. It requires at least 65% pickaxe power (Nightmare Pickaxe / Deathbringer Pickaxe, or better) or explosives to mine. Crimstone is the Crimson version of Stone. As with its Corruption counterpart, the Ebonstone, Crimstone can be converted into ordinary Stone via Purification Powder. In Hardmode, the spread of Crimson converts ordinary Stone blocks into Crimstone. Crimstone itself also spreads Crimson to susceptible blocks nearby.

Pharaoh's Mask.name: Pharaoh's Mask
Pharaoh's Mask.tooltip: The Pharaoh's set is a vanity set consisting of the Pharaoh's Mask and the Pharaoh's Robe. A full set can be found in a Gold Chest within a Pyramid, at a 1/9 (11.11%) chance. On Celebration Mk 10 worlds, this chance is guaranteed. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, it can also be obtained by throwing a Sandstorm in a Bottle and a Flying Carpet into Shimmer to get each respective vanity piece. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Actuator.name: Actuator
Actuator.tooltip: The Actuator is a mechanism item purchased from the Mechanic for 10 Silver each, or harvested from sand traps, lava traps, boulder traps, or Dead Man's Chest traps. It has to be placed on a tile and connected with wiring to function. When activated, the tile it is on toggles between active and inactive state, effectively allowing any block to be toggled like Active or Inactive Stone Blocks. Like Wire, Actuators are normally invisible and only become visible when a mechanism item is held. The following items interact with Actuators: They can be placed with The Grand Design (though they can also be placed by hand). They can be removed with the Wire Cutter or The Grand Design. The Presserator automatically places Actuators on objects when placing them, if the player has any. The Actuation Rod can toggle any Actuator within a limited range without requiring Wire.

Blue Wrench.name: Blue Wrench
Blue Wrench.tooltip: Wrenches are tools for placing Wires, which are used to connect mechanisms together, such as a trap with a Pressure Plate. There are four different wrenches: the Red Wrench, Green Wrench, Blue Wrench, and Yellow Wrench(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), each placing its respective color of Wire. All wrenches are purchased from the Mechanic for 2 Gold each. All Wrenches use the same ordinary Wire item as ammunition, but the color of wrench used will determine the color of Wire when placed. The colors all function identically but can be placed so as to overlap or intersect each other without interfering with each other. Junction Boxes(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can further be used to keep intersecting Wire paths of the same color from interfering with each other. All four wrenches can be combined to make a Multicolor Wrench(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), a single tool that can place Wire of any color. Ordinary wrenches cannot be used to remove placed Wires. Instead, a Wire Cutter or one of its derivatives is required. All Wire colors become the same ordinary Wire item again when freed.

Green Wrench.tooltip: Wrenches are tools for placing Wires, which are used to connect mechanisms together, such as a trap with a Pressure Plate.
