Blue Pressure Plate.name: Blue Pressure Plate
Blue Pressure Plate.tooltip: Pressure Plates are activation mechanisms that trigger wired mechanisms when stepped on. A pressure plate's color determines which characters can trigger it. Red, Brown, Gray, Orange, and Lihzahrd Pressure Plates are randomly generated on the map during world creation as the trigger for traps. They only take up a very small space on top of blocks, so they may be difficult to spot. The color of naturally spawned pressure plates is dependent on the color of the block they are generated on top of. Except for Lihzahrd Pressure Plates, they can also be purchased from the Mechanic. Weighted Pressure Plates activate once on being depressed, and again on being released. All Weighted Pressure Plates of the same color share a single state. As long as one Weighted Pressure Plate of a given color is already pressed down within a circuit, stepping on another identical plate will not send a new signal. They can be crafted from regular pressure plates. The Teal Pressure Pad is a special kind of pressure plate that responds to projectiles impacting it, which includes pets that touch it. Unlike regular pressure plates, the Teal Pressure Pad can be placed on all four sides of a block, e.g. on the ceiling or sidewall. It can be purchased from the Mechanic.

Discount Card.name: Discount Card
Discount Card.tooltip: The Discount Card is a Hardmode accessory. When equipped, it reduces NPC shop buy prices, Nurse healing, and reforging prices by 1/5 (20%). The card must be equipped before talking to an NPC to enable discounts. The Discount Card has a 1/1000 (0.1%) chance to be dropped by pirates (except Parrots) during Pirate Invasions, with a 1/250 (0.4%) chance from the Pirate Captain. It also has a 1/15 (6.67%) chance to be dropped by the Flying Dutchman. The Discount Card does not affect the following: Sell prices (when selling items to NPCs). Items repurchased after selling them (e.g. selling a Titan Glove for 2 Gold will still cost 2 Gold to take back). Items sold by the Tavernkeep for Defender Medals, such as his sentry summon weapons.
Discount Card.drops_summary: Most pirates (0.1%), Flying Dutchman (6.67%), Pirate Captain (0.4%)

Lucky Coin.name: Lucky Coin
Lucky Coin.tooltip: The Lucky Coin is a Hardmode accessory. While equipped, it causes enemies to drop extra coins when damaged and grants the player +0.05 luck. It has a 1/2000 (0.05%) chance to be dropped by pirates (except Parrots) during Pirate Invasions, with a 1/500 (0.2%) chance from the Pirate Captain. It also has a 1/15 (6.67%) chance to be dropped by the Flying Dutchman. With the Lucky Coin equipped, there is a 1/5 (20%) chance that 1 to 10 extra coins of the same type will drop each time the player damages an enemy. Each time extra coins drop, the following probabilities determine the coin type: 89.1% chance for Copper Coins 9.9% chance for Silver Coins 1% chance for Gold Coins
Lucky Coin.drops_summary: Most pirates (0.05%), Flying Dutchman (6.67%), Pirate Captain (0.2%)

Unicorn on a Stick.name: Unicorn on a Stick
Unicorn on a Stick.tooltip: The Unicorn on a Stick is a Hardmode novelty item which, when selected, is held stationary in front of the player to provide the illusion that they are riding a unicorn. It has no real function, unlike the Unicorn Mount. The Unicorn on a Stick has a 1/100 (1%) chance of being dropped by Unicorns.

Sandstorm in a Bottle.name: Sandstorm in a Bottle
Sandstorm in a Bottle.tooltip: The Sandstorm in a Bottle is an accessory found inside Gold Chests within Pyramids.
Sandstorm in a Bottle.drops_summary: Gold Chest (44.44%), Mirage Crate (2.86%), Oasis Crate (2.86%)

Boreal Wood Sofa.name: Boreal Wood Sofa
Boreal Wood Sofa.tooltip: Sofas are furniture items which fulfill a house's chair requirement. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Players can sit in sofas by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Players can choose to sit on the left, middle, or right positions, and thus up to 3 players can sit on a sofa at a time. Sitting on sofas gives a boost to health regeneration, similar to chairs and beds. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Sofa will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 21 craftable sofas and 5 noncraftable sofas. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Beach Ball.name: Beach Ball
Beach Ball.tooltip: The Beach Ball is a novelty item that can be purchased from the Party Girl for 20 CC.

Charm of Myths.name: Charm of Myths
Charm of Myths.tooltip: The Charm of Myths is a Hardmode accessory which combines the effects of the Band of Regeneration and the Philosopher's Stone.

Moon Shell.name: Moon Shell
Moon Shell.tooltip: The Moon Shell is a Hardmode accessory that can be crafted at the Tinkerer's Workshop. It combines the effects of the Moon Charm and the Neptune's Shell: Equipping it will turn the player into a Merfolk when entering water or honey (at any time), or into a Werewolf at night. The Merfolk form replaces the Werewolf form if entering water at night. The buffs from the Moon Charm: +2% melee critical strike chance +5.1% melee damage +5.1% melee speed +5% movement speed +3 defense Slightly increased jump height and jump speed +0.5 health regeneration per second (similar to the Band of Regeneration, but with half the speed) The buff from the Neptune's Shell: Entering applicable liquids with this accessory equipped transforms the player into a merperson and grants the Merfolk buff. While in this form, the breath meter will refill as if the player is in open air, therefore effectively preventing drowning. The player will be able to move freely in water.

Star Veil.name: Star Veil
Star Veil.tooltip: The Star Veil is a Hardmode accessory that combines the functions of the Star Cloak and the Cross Necklace, spawning falling star projectiles and increasing the length of the invincibility frames granted when the player is hurt.

Water Walking Boots.name: Water Walking Boots
Water Walking Boots.tooltip: Water Walking Boots are a pre-Hardmode accessory that grants the ability to walk on water, honey, and Shimmer. They do not allow walking on lava. While on said liquids, pressing ▼ Down will cause the player to fall through the liquid, similarly to platforms. Water Walking Boots have a 1/10 (10%) chance of being obtained from Water Chests, Ocean Crates, and Seaside Crates.
Water Walking Boots.drops_summary: Ocean Crate (10%), Seaside Crate (10%), Water Chest (10%)

Tiara.name: Tiara
Tiara.tooltip: The Princess set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Tiara and the Princess Dress. It is purchased from the Clothier for 35 Gold (set), during a New Moon. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Princess Dress.name: Princess Dress
Princess Dress.tooltip: The Princess set is a vanity set that can be obtained from Goodie Bags with a 2/57 (3.51%) chance. It consists of a Princess Hat and Princess Dress. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Pharaoh's Robe.name: Pharaoh's Robe
Pharaoh's Robe.tooltip: The Pharaoh's set is a vanity set consisting of the Pharaoh's Mask and the Pharaoh's Robe. A full set can be found in a Gold Chest within a Pyramid, at a 1/9 (11.11%) chance. On Celebration Mk 10 worlds, this chance is guaranteed. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, it can also be obtained by throwing a Sandstorm in a Bottle and a Flying Carpet into Shimmer to get each respective vanity piece. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Green Cap.name: Green Cap
Green Cap.tooltip: The Green Cap is a piece of armor. It will always drop from the Guide, but only when his name is Andrew.

Mushroom Cap.name: Mushroom Cap
Mushroom Cap.tooltip: The Mushroom Cap is a vanity hat purchased from the Truffle for 2 Gold. It greatly resembles a Glowing Mushroom without the stalk.

Tam O' Shanter.name: Tam O' Shanter
Tam O' Shanter.tooltip: The Tam O' Shanter is a Hardmode vanity item purchased from the Clothier for 2 Gold 50 Silver, during the third quarter moon phase.

Mummy Mask.name: Mummy Mask
Mummy Mask.tooltip: The Mummy set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Mummy Mask, the Mummy Shirt, and the Mummy Pants. Each piece is dropped by Mummies with a 1/75 (1.33%) chance. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Mummy Shirt.name: Mummy Shirt
Mummy Shirt.tooltip: The Mummy set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Mummy Mask, the Mummy Shirt, and the Mummy Pants. Each piece is dropped by Mummies with a 1/75 (1.33%) chance. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Mummy Pants.name: Mummy Pants
Mummy Pants.tooltip: The Mummy set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Mummy Mask, the Mummy Shirt, and the Mummy Pants. Each piece is dropped by Mummies with a 1/75 (1.33%) chance. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Cowboy Hat.name: Cowboy Hat
Cowboy Hat.tooltip: The Cowboy set is a Hardmode vanity set that includes the Cowboy Hat, Cowboy Jacket, and Cowboy Pants. It is purchased from the Clothier for 15 Gold (set), during the first-quarter moon phase. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Cowboy Jacket.name: Cowboy Jacket
Cowboy Jacket.tooltip: The Cowboy set is a Hardmode vanity set that includes the Cowboy Hat, Cowboy Jacket, and Cowboy Pants. It is purchased from the Clothier for 15 Gold (set), during the first-quarter moon phase. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Cowboy Pants.name: Cowboy Pants
Cowboy Pants.tooltip: The Cowboy set is a Hardmode vanity set that includes the Cowboy Hat, Cowboy Jacket, and Cowboy Pants. It is purchased from the Clothier for 15 Gold (set), during the first-quarter moon phase. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Pirate Hat.name: Pirate Hat
Pirate Hat.tooltip: The Pirate set is a vanity set which consists of the Pirate Hat, Pirate Shirt and Pirate Pants. They are purchased from the Pirate for 15 Gold (set). These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Pirate Shirt.name: Pirate Shirt
Pirate Shirt.tooltip: The Pirate set is a vanity set which consists of the Pirate Hat, Pirate Shirt and Pirate Pants. They are purchased from the Pirate for 15 Gold (set). These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Pirate Pants.name: Pirate Pants
Pirate Pants.tooltip: The Pirate set is a vanity set which consists of the Pirate Hat, Pirate Shirt and Pirate Pants. They are purchased from the Pirate for 15 Gold (set). These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Viking Helmet.name: Viking Helmet
Viking Helmet.tooltip: The Viking Helmet is an armor piece for the helmet slot. It has a 1/50 (2%) chance to be dropped by Undead Vikings in the Ice biome. It provides a sizeable amount of defense (as much as a Gold Helmet or Tungsten Helmet), but it does not have an associated set or set bonus, hindering its utility.

Crimtane Ore.name: Crimtane Ore
Crimtane Ore.tooltip: Crimtane Ore is a pre-Hardmode ore. It is primarily dropped from the Brain of Cthulhu, as well as the Eye of Cthulhu in Crimson worlds. Crimtane Ore can also be found rarely in small veins underground. When below 0 ft in elevation, a Gold Pickaxe or better is needed to mine it, otherwise any pickaxe can be used. It is the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Demonite Ore.

Cactus Sword.name: Cactus Sword
Cactus Sword.tooltip: The Cactus Sword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Cactus Pickaxe.name: Cactus Pickaxe
Cactus Pickaxe.tooltip: The Cactus Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe. It can mine blocks weaker than Meteorite. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Ice Brick.name: Ice Brick
Ice Brick.tooltip: The Ice Brick is a brick type made from Ice Blocks. It does not have the sliding properties of ice, nor does it cause snow to fall like Snow Bricks.

Ice Brick Wall.name: Ice Brick Wall
Ice Brick Wall.tooltip: Ice Brick Wall is a type of Wall that is made using Ice Bricks.

Adhesive Bandage.name: Adhesive Bandage
Adhesive Bandage.tooltip: The Adhesive Bandage is an immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Bleeding debuff. It has a 1/100 (1%) / 199/10000 (1.99%) chance to drop from Rusty Armored Bones, Werewolves, and Angler Fish. While the Adhesive Bandage is exclusive to Hardmode on the  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version, it can be obtained in pre-Hardmode on the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version by throwing a Bezoar into Shimmer.
Adhesive Bandage.drops_summary: Angler Fish (1%), Rusty Armored Bones (1%), Werewolf (1%)

Armor Polish.name: Armor Polish
Armor Polish.tooltip: The Armor Polish is a Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Broken Armor debuff. It has a 1/100 (1%) / 199/10000 (1.99%) chance to drop from Armored Skeletons and Blue Armored Bones.

Bezoar.name: Bezoar
Bezoar.tooltip: The Bezoar is a pre-Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Poisoned debuff. It has a 1/100 (1%) / 199/10000 (1.99%) chance to drop from Hornets, Moss Hornets, and Toxic Sludges.

Blindfold.name: Blindfold
Blindfold.tooltip: The Blindfold is a Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Darkness debuff. It has a 1/100 (1%) / 199/10000 (1.99%) chance to drop from Corrupt Slimes, Slimelings, Crimslimes, Dark Mummies, and Blood Mummies.

Fast Clock.name: Fast Clock
Fast Clock.tooltip: The Fast Clock is a Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Slow debuff. It has a 1/100 (1%) / 199/10000 (1.99%) chance to drop from Pixies, regular Mummies, and Wraiths.

Megaphone.name: Megaphone
Megaphone.tooltip: The Megaphone is an immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Silenced debuff. It has a 1/100 (1%) / 199/10000 (1.99%) chance to drop from Pixies, Green Jellyfish, Dark Mummies, and Blood Mummies.

Nazar.name: Nazar
Nazar.tooltip: The Nazar is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Cursed debuff. It has a 1/100 (1%) / 199/10000 (1.99%) chance to drop from Cursed Skulls, Giant Cursed Skulls, Cursed Hammers, Crimson Axes, and Enchanted Swords.

Vitamins.name: Vitamins
Vitamins.tooltip: Vitamins are a Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Weak debuff. It has a 1/100 (1%) / 199/10000 (1.99%) chance to drop from Corruptors and Floaty Grosses.

Trifold Map.name: Trifold Map
Trifold Map.tooltip: The Trifold Map is a Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Confused debuff. It has a 1/100 (1%) / 199/10000 (1.99%) chance to drop from Clowns, Giant Bats, and Light Mummies.

Cactus Helmet.name: Cactus Helmet
Cactus Helmet.tooltip: Cactus armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Cactus Helmet, Cactus Breastplate, and Cactus Leggings. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Cactus. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +3 defense A Thorns effect, which causes the player to deal 15 / 30 / 45 damage and inflict a knockback of 10 (Extremely strong) on enemies upon contact.

Cactus Breastplate.name: Cactus Breastplate
Cactus Breastplate.tooltip: Cactus armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Cactus Helmet, Cactus Breastplate, and Cactus Leggings. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Cactus. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +3 defense A Thorns effect, which causes the player to deal 15 / 30 / 45 damage and inflict a knockback of 10 (Extremely strong) on enemies upon contact.

Cactus Leggings.name: Cactus Leggings
Cactus Leggings.tooltip: Cactus armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Cactus Helmet, Cactus Breastplate, and Cactus Leggings. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Cactus. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +3 defense A Thorns effect, which causes the player to deal 15 / 30 / 45 damage and inflict a knockback of 10 (Extremely strong) on enemies upon contact.

Power Glove.name: Power Glove
Power Glove.tooltip: The Power Glove is a Hardmode accessory. While equipped, it grants the following effects: Enables autoswing for all melee weapons and whips +12% melee speed ×2 knockback for melee weapons +10% size for melee weapons

Lightning Boots.name: Lightning Boots
Lightning Boots.tooltip: The Lightning Boots are a pre-Hardmode accessory and the direct upgrade to the Spectre Boots. They grant the following effects while equipped: The ability to sprint, allowing the player to reach maximum running speed faster. The player will leave behind a visual trail of dust clouds as they sprint. Increased maximum movement speed to 35 mph (25.67 tiles/second). The ability to hold ↷ Jump in midair to fly for a total of 1.17 seconds. While flying, the boots emit a visual cloud trail. When paired with wings, this flight is disabled to give the wings an additional 0.7 seconds of flight time.

Sun Stone.name: Sun Stone
Sun Stone.tooltip: The Sun Stone is a Hardmode, post-Golem accessory which has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Golem. It grants the same stat bonuses as the Moon Stone; however, these bonuses only activate during the day. The stat bonuses are: +10% melee speed +10% damage (all types) +2% critical strike chance +1 HP/s health regeneration +4 defense +15% mining speed +0.5 summon knockback

Moon Stone.name: Moon Stone
Moon Stone.tooltip: The Moon Stone is a Hardmode accessory which has a 1/35 (2.86%) / 69/1225 (5.63%) chance to drop from Vampires during the Solar Eclipse event. It grants the same stat bonuses as the Sun Stone, but these bonuses will only activate during the night or during a Solar Eclipse. The stat bonuses are: +10% melee speed +10% damage (all types) +2% critical strike chance +1 HP/s health regeneration +4 defense +15% mining speed +0.5 summon knockback

Armor Bracing.name: Armor Bracing
Armor Bracing.tooltip: Armor Bracing is a Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Weak and Broken Armor debuffs.

Medicated Bandage.name: Medicated Bandage
Medicated Bandage.tooltip: The Medicated Bandage is an immunity accessory that combines the functions of the Adhesive Bandage and the Bezoar. This item grants immunity to any Bleeding and Poison debuffs. It is one of the ingredients required to make the Ankh Charm, which is further required to make the Ankh Shield. While the Medicated Bandage is exclusive to Hardmode on the  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version, it can be obtained in pre-Hardmode on the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, as it is possible to obtain the Adhesive Bandage by throwing the Bezoar into Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

The Plan.name: The Plan
The Plan.tooltip: The Plan is a Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Slow and Confused debuffs.

Countercurse Mantra.name: Countercurse Mantra
Countercurse Mantra.tooltip: The Countercurse Mantra is an immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Silenced and Cursed debuffs. It can be obtained in pre-Hardmode, as the Megaphone can be obtained by throwing the Nazar into Shimmer.

Coin Gun.name: Coin Gun
Coin Gun.tooltip: The Coin Gun is a Hardmode ranged weapon that uses coins as ammunition, which affects its damage and velocity depending on the type of coin fired. The weapon itself has 0 base damage, with the entirety of its damage value stemming from the coins used to fire it. Coin projectiles dissipate upon hitting an enemy or solid block and cannot be retrieved once fired. The Coin Gun is dropped very rarely (1/4000 (0.025%) chance) by regular Pirate Invasion enemies, excluding the Parrot. The Coin Gun's drop chance from Pirate Captains is quadrupled (1/1000 (0.1%) chance) and increased again from the Flying Dutchman (1/50 (2%) chance). Its best modifier is Agile, as it can only receive modifiers affecting its speed, velocity, critical strike chance, and knockback. Rapid and Hasty modifiers are recognized in-game as its "best" modifier due to them increasing the item's value by the most.
Coin Gun.drops_summary: Most pirates (0.025%), Flying Dutchman (2%), Pirate Captain (0.1%)

Lava Charm.name: Lava Charm
Lava Charm.tooltip: The Lava Charm is an accessory that grants immunity to lava for 7 seconds. It is found in Chests located in the cavern layer as well as obtained from Hellstone Crates and Obsidian Crates with a 1/20 (5%) chance. It can only be found in Chests in the lower portion of the Caverns where lava pools can naturally spawn, as opposed to Chests throughout the entirety of the Caverns. When the Lava Charm is equipped and the player comes into contact with lava, a 7-second countdown begins, signified by a lava meter that displays over the player's head. It operates similarly to the breath meter, but displays flame icons instead of bubbles. Lava immunity time is recharged gradually by exiting lava, the same way breathing time is recharged by exiting water (albeit much more slowly).
Lava Charm.drops_summary: Gold Chest (5%), Hellstone Crate (5%), Obsidian Crate (5%)

Obsidian Water Walking Boots.name: Obsidian Water Walking Boots
Obsidian Water Walking Boots.tooltip: Obsidian Water Walking Boots are a pre-Hardmode immunity accessory that grant the ability to walk on water, honey, and Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), while also giving immunity to the Burning debuff. They do not allow walking on lava.

Lava Waders.name: Lava Waders
Lava Waders.tooltip: The Lava Waders are a pre-Hardmode immunity accessory. They grant the following effects while equipped: The ability to stand and walk on the surface of all liquids. When walking on liquid, press the ▼ Down key allows submerging into the liquid. Prevents fall damage when landing on the surface of any liquid. Immunity to the Burning debuff. Immunity to lava for 7 seconds. Decreases the damage taken from lava from 80 to 35, and reduces the duration of On Fire! debuff inflicted by lava from 7 / 14 / 17.5 seconds to 3.5 / 7 / 8.75 seconds. Equipping the Ash Wood armor at the same time provides immunity to lava damage and debuff.

Pure Water Fountain.name: Pure Water Fountain
Pure Water Fountain.tooltip: Water fountains are mechanisms and crafting stations that change the color of all nearby water. They can be activated via ⚷ Open / Activate or wire. Like Sinks, they can be used to craft items that require water as a crafting station. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) The range of a fountain's effects is a radius 60 tiles horizontally and 53 tiles vertically, measured from the edges of its sprite. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 10 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 8 different obtainable fountains, all of which are purchased from the Witch Doctor for 4 Gold each at any time.  Additionally, some special world seeds contain naturally generated Water Fountains on their Floating Islands: Drunk worlds have Icy and Desert Water Fountains. Celebration Mk 10 worlds have Hallowed Water Fountains. Remix worlds have Corrupt or Crimson Water Fountains depending on the world evil. On the  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS versions, they can be purchased for free, but are only available after Plantera has been defeated.

Desert Water Fountain.name: Desert Water Fountain
Desert Water Fountain.tooltip: Water fountains are mechanisms and crafting stations that change the color of all nearby water. They can be activated via ⚷ Open / Activate or wire. Like Sinks, they can be used to craft items that require water as a crafting station. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) The range of a fountain's effects is a radius 60 tiles horizontally and 53 tiles vertically, measured from the edges of its sprite. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 10 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 8 different obtainable fountains, all of which are purchased from the Witch Doctor for 4 Gold each at any time.  Additionally, some special world seeds contain naturally generated Water Fountains on their Floating Islands: Drunk worlds have Icy and Desert Water Fountains. Celebration Mk 10 worlds have Hallowed Water Fountains. Remix worlds have Corrupt or Crimson Water Fountains depending on the world evil. On the  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS versions, they can be purchased for free, but are only available after Plantera has been defeated.

Shadewood.name: Shadewood
Shadewood.tooltip: Shadewood is a type of wood harvested from Shadewood trees and Shadewood Palm trees found naturally growing in Crimson biomes. Shadewood trees can be cultivated by placing Acorns on top of Crimson grass or Crimson Jungle grass above surface, and Shadewood Palm trees can be cultivated by placing Acorns on top of Crimsand Blocks above surface.

Shadewood Door.name: Shadewood Door
Shadewood Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Shadewood Platform.name: Shadewood Platform
Shadewood Platform.tooltip: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Shadewood Chest.name: Shadewood Chest
Shadewood Chest.tooltip: Chests are a type of furniture functioning as storage items. They are accessed using ⚷ Open / Activate and can store up to 40 item stacks in rows of  10×4 /   8×5. In addition to many being craftable, a number of Chests are placed in random locations during world generation. The loot contained in these Chests is determined during world generation, and will not change if the world enters Hardmode. Chests cannot be broken with items inside (the blocks a filled Chest is placed on would also have this trait). However, the Block Swap feature allows the player to change the type of a Chest without having to destroy it. Some types of Chests can be locked by the player using a Chest Lock. When doing so, they will require a key to open again. There are 23 varieties of naturally-occurring Chests (12 of which cannot be crafted), 53 that can only be crafted, and 1 purchasable Chest, for a total of 77 Chest types.

Shadewood Chair.name: Shadewood Chair
Shadewood Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Shadewood Work Bench.name: Shadewood Work Bench
Shadewood Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Shadewood Table.name: Shadewood Table
Shadewood Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Shadewood Dresser.name: Shadewood Dresser
Shadewood Dresser.tooltip: Dressers are a type of flat-surface furniture (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and storage item. They also fulfill house's table requirement. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 19 / (3DS version) 5 craftable versions, and (Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) 5 noncraftable versions which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Shadewood Piano.name: Shadewood Piano
Shadewood Piano.tooltip: Pianos are a type of furniture which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 15 /  10 craftable Pianos, and 5 non-craftable Pianos that can be found in the Dungeon, Ruined Houses, and Pirate Invasion event. Some Pianos can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin that they are found in.

Shadewood Bed.name: Shadewood Bed
Shadewood Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration. Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 craftable Beds and 5 that can be acquired from the environment. All Beds are functionally identical and differ only in appearance.

Shadewood Sword.name: Shadewood Sword
Shadewood Sword.tooltip: The Shadewood Sword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword and a variation of the Wooden Sword. Its Corruption counterpart is the Ebonwood Sword. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Shadewood Hammer.name: Shadewood Hammer
Shadewood Hammer.tooltip: The Shadewood Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer. Its Corruption counterpart is the Ebonwood Hammer. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Shadewood Bow.name: Shadewood Bow
Shadewood Bow.tooltip: The Shadewood Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow and a variation of the Wooden Bow. It is the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Ebonwood Bow. Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.

Shadewood Helmet.name: Shadewood Helmet
Shadewood Helmet.tooltip: Shadewood armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Shadewood Helmet, Shadewood Breastplate, and Shadewood Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Shadewood. The full set grants 5 defense while equipped. Its Corruption counterpart is Ebonwood armor, which has identical stats.

Shadewood Breastplate.name: Shadewood Breastplate
Shadewood Breastplate.tooltip: Shadewood armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Shadewood Helmet, Shadewood Breastplate, and Shadewood Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Shadewood. The full set grants 5 defense while equipped. Its Corruption counterpart is Ebonwood armor, which has identical stats.

Shadewood Greaves.name: Shadewood Greaves
Shadewood Greaves.tooltip: Shadewood armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Shadewood Helmet, Shadewood Breastplate, and Shadewood Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Shadewood. The full set grants 5 defense while equipped. Its Corruption counterpart is Ebonwood armor, which has identical stats.

Shadewood Wall.name: Shadewood Wall
Shadewood Wall.tooltip: Shadewood Walls are a type of Wall made from Shadewood.

Cannon.name: Cannon
Cannon.tooltip: The Cannon is a Hardmode placeable furniture/weapon, purchased from the Pirate for 25 Gold. Once placed, it can be fired by pressing ⚒ Use / Attack key on it with any Torch (which is not consumed). The Cannon fires an arcing Cannonball that explodes upon contact with a block. The Cannonball can also pierce through three enemies, exploding upon the fourth hit. The Cannonball and its explosion deal 300 classless damage and knockback of 8 (Very strong), and do not destroy blocks. The Cannon has a cooldown of 0.33 seconds before it can be fired again by using Torches, which is shared between all Cannons in the world. The angle of a placed Cannon can be adjusted by pressing ⚷ Open / Activate key on either side of the Cannon to rotate it in that direction,  or tapping the side of the Cannon. There are 9 possible orientations and it cannot fire downward, though the arcing trajectory of the Cannonballs can be used to hit targets below the emplacement. Each rotation tilts the Cannon by one step (22.5°). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) The Cannon can also be triggered by Wire. Depending on where the Wire is connected, it will either shoot a Cannonball or rotate toward the side the Wire is on. When a Cannon is fired with this method, there is a cooldown of 10 seconds before that specific Cannon can be fired again by wiring signal, and a cooldown of 2 seconds before any other Cannon in the world can be fired by wiring signal. Torches can be still used to fire Cannons during this cooldown.

Cannonball.name: Cannonball
Cannonball.tooltip: The Cannonball is a type of decorative block sold by the Pirate for 2 Silver each.

Flare Gun.name: Flare Gun
Flare Gun.tooltip: The Flare Gun is a weapon that is found randomly in Gold Chests underground. When used, it fires Flares, which provide light and stick to the blocks they hit. The Flare Gun cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Flare.name: Flare
Flare.tooltip: Flares are a type of ammunition used solely by the Flare Gun. When fired, they travel in a slight arc and stick to blocks, similar to Sticky Glowsticks, but have greater velocity and range. They emit low-level tinted light that lasts for 10 minutes. Flares work in liquids, although they bounce off Shimmer. Flares cannot be recovered once they burn out. All types of Flares (except the Cursed Flare) inflict the On Fire! debuff. There is a 2/3 (66.67%) chance that the debuff will last 5 seconds, and a 1/3 (33.33%) chance that it will last 10 seconds.

Bone Wand.name: Bone Wand
Bone Wand.tooltip: Block-placing wands are special tools that allow the player to place blocks they would normally not be able to place. They do not consume any mana. Each wand consumes a specific material from the player's inventory (details listed below). There are 6 different block-placing wands.
Bone Wand.drops_summary: Angry Bones (0.4%), Cursed Skull (0.4%), Dark Caster (0.4%)

Leaf Wand.name: Leaf Wand
Leaf Wand.tooltip: Block-placing wands are special tools that allow the player to place blocks they would normally not be able to place. They do not consume any mana. Each wand consumes a specific material from the player's inventory (details listed below). There are 6 different block-placing wands.
Leaf Wand.drops_summary: Angry Bones (0.4%), Cursed Skull (0.4%), Dark Caster (0.4%)

Flying Carpet.name: Flying Carpet
Flying Carpet.tooltip: The Flying Carpet is a flight accessory that allows the player to float for 5 seconds, similar to the Hoverboard. It can be found inside Chests located within Pyramids in the Desert. It can also be obtained by throwing a Pharaoh's Robe into Shimmer. The Flying Carpet is activated by holding ↷ Jump in mid-air, after all jumps from extra jump accessories are used. Once it is activated, the player is put on an imaginary horizontal rail. Releasing the key deactivates the carpet, but it may be reactivated at a lower height if there is still flight time left.

Avenger Emblem.name: Avenger Emblem
Avenger Emblem.tooltip: The Avenger Emblem is a Hardmode accessory that grants 12% increased damage to all weapons.

Mechanical Glove.name: Mechanical Glove
Mechanical Glove.tooltip: The Mechanical Glove is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses accessory. While equipped, it grants the following effects: Enables autoswing for all melee weapons and whips +12% melee damage +12% melee speed ×2 knockback for melee weapons +10% size for melee weapons

Land Mine.name: Land Mine
Land Mine.tooltip: The Land Mine is a unique Hardmode, post-Plantera placeable item.

Paladin's Shield.name: Paladin's Shield
Paladin's Shield.tooltip: The Paladin's Shield is a Hardmode, post-Plantera shield that has a 1/10 (10%) / 19/100 (19%) chance of being dropped by Paladins in the Hardmode Dungeon. While equipped, it grants the following effects: +6 defense Immunity to knockback While the wearer's health is above 25%, it grants all nearby players on their team (excluding themselves) the Paladin's Shield buff, which provides 25% damage reduction and redirects that damage to the wearer.

Web Slinger.name: Web Slinger
Web Slinger.tooltip: Hooks are a class of tools which aid the player in traversing terrain. When used, hooks fire a chain that latches to a surface or platform and pulls the player towards it. A hook is an essential tool which offers significant freedom from terrain height restrictions as well as being a fast movement option, and will often be the first major mobility tool a player acquires. A variety of hooks are available at all stages of the game (see table below). The Grapple hotkey activates the equipped hook in the player's equipment slot, or the first hook from the inventory (from left to right, top to bottom) without requiring it to be in the player's hotbar.Verify Several higher-tier hooks, such as the Ivy Whip, allow the player to grapple multiple surfaces simultaneously. If the character grapples one surface, then fires the hook a second time, another chain extends from the player without dislodging the first. Upon grappling a second surface, the player will be suspended in midair at a point midway between the two surfaces. This allows players more freedom during construction, or for navigating hazardous areas, such as above lava or Meteorite. All Journey Mode characters will spawn with the basic Grappling Hook already in their inventory.

Jungle Water Fountain.name: Jungle Water Fountain
Jungle Water Fountain.tooltip: Water fountains are mechanisms and crafting stations that change the color of all nearby water. They can be activated via ⚷ Open / Activate or wire. Like Sinks, they can be used to craft items that require water as a crafting station. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) The range of a fountain's effects is a radius 60 tiles horizontally and 53 tiles vertically, measured from the edges of its sprite. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 10 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 8 different obtainable fountains, all of which are purchased from the Witch Doctor for 4 Gold each at any time.  Additionally, some special world seeds contain naturally generated Water Fountains on their Floating Islands: Drunk worlds have Icy and Desert Water Fountains. Celebration Mk 10 worlds have Hallowed Water Fountains. Remix worlds have Corrupt or Crimson Water Fountains depending on the world evil. On the  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS versions, they can be purchased for free, but are only available after Plantera has been defeated.

Umbrella.name: Umbrella
Umbrella.tooltip: The Umbrella is a pre-Hardmode melee weapon. It has a 1/11 (9.09%) chance of being obtained from wooden Chests on the Surface or in the Underground layer, and can also be purchased for 1 Gold from the Skeleton Merchant during a Waning Gibbous. When held, the Umbrella appears above the character, allowing the player to fall at a slower rate and preventing fall damage. The player can hold ▼ Down to increase the fall speed. If the player is in a world using the Vampirism secret world seed, the Umbrella can be held to prevent burning in the sunlight. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Chlorophyte Ore.name: Chlorophyte Ore
Chlorophyte Ore.tooltip: Chlorophyte Ore is a Hardmode ore. When Hardmode starts, a portion of Mud Blocks located near Jungle grass blocks (naturally in the Underground Jungle) will be converted into Chlorophyte Ore.

Steampunk Wings.name: Steampunk Wings
Steampunk Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Snowball.name: Snowball
Snowball.tooltip: The Snowball is a consumable ranged weapon that can be crafted from Snow Blocks. Snowballs can also be used as ammunition for the Snowball Cannon.

Ice Skates.name: Ice Skates
Ice Skates.tooltip: Ice Skates are a pre-Hardmode accessory that improves a player's movement control on Thin Ice, all Ice Blocks, Ice Rod blocks, Frozen Slime Blocks and Aetherium Blocks. The player accelerates faster, slides shorter distances, and will no longer cause Thin Ice to break when landing from falls or jumps. Ice Skates have a 15.52% chance of being found inside Frozen Chests in the Ice biome, as well as a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being obtained from Frozen(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Boreal Crates(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
Ice Skates.drops_summary: Boreal Crate (16.67%), Frozen Chest (15.52%), Frozen Crate (16.67%)

Snowball Launcher.name: Snowball Launcher
Snowball Launcher.tooltip: The Snowball Launcher is a pre-Hardmode furniture item and placeable weapon that has a 1/25 (4%) chance of being dropped by Snow Flinx. Once placed, interacting with it using the ⚒ Use / Attack button causes it to fire a Snowball that damages enemies, and holding the button will cause it to release a rapid fire of Snowballs with a spread of roughly 30°. The Snowball Launcher has a firing cooldown of 0.12 seconds, giving it a maximum fire rate of 8.57 Snowballs per second. Snowballs have a base damage of 35 and knockback of 3.5 (Weak). This is not affected by the default base damage (−1) or knockback (0) of the Snowball Launcher item. The Snowball Launcher can also be triggered by wire. Depending on the lateral position of the connected wire within the sprite of the Snowball Launcher, it will either shoot a Snowball (with a cooldown of 0.17 seconds) or turn to the side the wire is on.

Web Covered Chest.name: Web Covered Chest
Web Covered Chest.tooltip: Web Covered Chests can be found in Spider Nests, though they are rare. They always contain a Web Slinger, in addition to common or uncommon items (also found in Gold Chests) depending on the height they were found: Underground or Caverns.

Climbing Claws.name: Climbing Claws
Climbing Claws.tooltip: The Climbing Claws are an accessory that lets players partially "stick" to the sides of blocks, slowly sliding down them when moving against them in midair. Jumps can also be performed off the sides of blocks. By repeatedly sticking and jumping, vertical blocks can be scaled. When sliding down, the slide speed can be accelerated using the ▼ Down key. Climbing Claws have a 1/11 (9.09%) chance of being found inside surface Chests, or a 1/120 (0.83%) chance in Wooden Crates and Pearlwood Crates obtained from fishing. They can also be purchased for 2 Gold 50 Silver from the Skeleton Merchant during a Waxing Crescent. Their availability very early in the game makes them a useful accessory for mobility, as they allow the player to slowly but surely climb up some walls without needing ropes. Climbing Claws function identically to the Shoe Spikes, but are found in different locations. When both Climbing Claws and Shoe Spikes are equipped, the wearer remains completely "stuck" at a fixed point when moving against the sides of blocks, and may slide down with the ▼ Down key. This effect can also be achieved using a single accessory if the Climbing Claws and Shoe Spikes are combined into the Tiger Climbing Gear at a Tinkerer's Workshop.

Ancient Iron Helmet.name: Ancient Iron Helmet
Ancient Iron Helmet.tooltip: Iron armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Iron Helmet, Iron Chainmail, and Iron Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 60 Iron Bars (180 Iron Ore). The full set grants 9 defense while equipped. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Lead armor. The Ancient Iron Helmet is functionally identical to and interchangeable with the Iron Helmet. The Ancient Iron Helmet has a 1/100 (1%) chance of being dropped by Skeletons and Spore Skeletons, and can also be obtained by dropping an Iron Helmet into Shimmer. Its appearance is based on the sprite of the Iron Helmet prior to 1.0.3.

Ancient Gold Helmet.name: Ancient Gold Helmet
Ancient Gold Helmet.tooltip: Gold armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Gold Helmet, Gold Chainmail, and Gold Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Gold Bars (300 Gold Ore). The full set grants 16 defense while equipped. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Platinum armor. The Ancient Gold Helmet is functionally identical to and interchangeable with the Gold Helmet. The Ancient Gold Helmet has a 1/100 (1%) chance of being dropped by Skeletons and Spore Skeletons, and can also be obtained by dropping a Gold Helmet into Shimmer. Its appearance is based on the sprite of the Gold Helmet prior to 1.0.3.

Ancient Shadow Helmet.name: Ancient Shadow Helmet
Ancient Shadow Helmet.tooltip: Ancient Shadow armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set obtained from Eater of Souls. Each piece is dropped individually with a 1/525 (0.19%) chance. It shares identical stats with Shadow armor, but it reproduces the pre-1.0.3 Shadow armor's sprites. Ancient Shadow armor pieces are interchangeable with Shadow armor pieces, still providing the set bonus. The player will also emit purple bubbles, and create a semi-transparent after-image effect behind themselves when moving. This effect appears to be clones of the player. These clones do not appear to have bodies inside of the armor, as there is no face visible.

Ancient Shadow Scalemail.name: Ancient Shadow Scalemail
Ancient Shadow Scalemail.tooltip: Ancient Shadow armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set obtained from Eater of Souls. Each piece is dropped individually with a 1/525 (0.19%) chance. It shares identical stats with Shadow armor, but it reproduces the pre-1.0.3 Shadow armor's sprites. Ancient Shadow armor pieces are interchangeable with Shadow armor pieces, still providing the set bonus. The player will also emit purple bubbles, and create a semi-transparent after-image effect behind themselves when moving. This effect appears to be clones of the player. These clones do not appear to have bodies inside of the armor, as there is no face visible.

Ancient Shadow Greaves.name: Ancient Shadow Greaves

These clones do not appear to have bodies inside of the armor, as there is no face visible.

Ancient Necro Helmet.name: Ancient Necro Helmet
Ancient Necro Helmet.tooltip: Necro armor is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron ranged armor set consisting of the Necro Helmet, Necro Breastplate, and Necro Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 135 Cobwebs and 150 Bones. The Ancient Necro Helmet is dropped from Angry Bones, Dark Casters, and Librarian Skeletons in the Dungeon, at a 1/450 (0.22%) chance. It is functionally identical to and interchangeable with the Necro Helmet. Its appearance is based on the sprite of the Necro Helmet prior to 1.0.3. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +19 defense +15% ranged damage +10% ranged critical strike chance The player also emits a visual afterimage while moving, and their hurt sound will be set to that of a Skeleton.

Ancient Cobalt Helmet.name: Ancient Cobalt Helmet
Ancient Cobalt Helmet.tooltip: Ancient Cobalt armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Ancient Cobalt Helmet, Ancient Cobalt Breastplate, and Ancient Cobalt Leggings. Each piece has a 1/300 (0.33%) chance of being dropped by Hornets and Man Eaters. It shares identical stats with Jungle armor, but differs in appearance. Ancient Cobalt armor pieces are interchangeable with Jungle armor pieces, still providing the set bonus. The player also emits a visual afterimage while moving instead of grass particles.

Ancient Cobalt Breastplate.name: Ancient Cobalt Breastplate
Ancient Cobalt Breastplate.tooltip: Ancient Cobalt armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Ancient Cobalt Helmet, Ancient Cobalt Breastplate, and Ancient Cobalt Leggings. Each piece has a 1/300 (0.33%) chance of being dropped by Hornets and Man Eaters. It shares identical stats with Jungle armor, but differs in appearance. Ancient Cobalt armor pieces are interchangeable with Jungle armor pieces, still providing the set bonus. The player also emits a visual afterimage while moving instead of grass particles.

Ancient Cobalt Leggings.name: Ancient Cobalt Leggings
Ancient Cobalt Leggings.tooltip: Ancient Cobalt armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Ancient Cobalt Helmet, Ancient Cobalt Breastplate, and Ancient Cobalt Leggings. Each piece has a 1/300 (0.33%) chance of being dropped by Hornets and Man Eaters. It shares identical stats with Jungle armor, but differs in appearance. Ancient Cobalt armor pieces are interchangeable with Jungle armor pieces, still providing the set bonus. The player also emits a visual afterimage while moving instead of grass particles.

Black Belt.name: Black Belt
Black Belt.tooltip: The Black Belt is a Hardmode, post-Plantera accessory that grants a 1/10 (10%) chance to dodge an attack, including instances of damage taken from hazards such as traps and lava. A cloud of smoke surrounds the player when performing a dodge. The Black Belt has a 1/12 (8.33%) / 23/144 (15.97%) chance of being dropped by Bone Lees in the post-Plantera Dungeon.

Boomstick.name: Boomstick
Boomstick.tooltip: The Boomstick is a pre-Hardmode gun. It can be found in Ivy Chests (21.72% chance) in the Underground Jungle, and also in Jungle Crates (19/100 (19%) chance). When used, it fires a spread of 3–4 bullets, consuming one piece of ammunition. Its best modifier is Unreal.
Boomstick.drops_summary: Bramble Crate (19%), Ivy Chest (21.72%), Jungle Crate (19%)

Rope.name: Rope
Rope.tooltip: Ropes are placeable items that primarily provide quick vertical mobility. They can be placed adjacent to blocks in any direction, or in midair where background walls are present. Ropes can also be placed atop any existing placed Rope, which extends the total length of the Rope downward without the player having to be at the bottom of the Rope column. Once placed, Ropes are used by pressing ▲ Up or ▼ Down while moving over them. There are four different types of Rope, which are acquired in different ways: Rope can be found randomly in Chests and Pots, as a bonus drop from slimes, or purchased from the Merchant and Skeleton Merchant for 10 Copper each. Vine Rope is acquired by destroying vines while the Guide to Plant Fiber Cordage is equipped. Silk Rope is crafted from Silk at a Loom. Web Rope is crafted By Hand from Cobwebs. All Rope variants operate identically, but Silk and Web Ropes are immune to falling lava, as opposed to normal and Vine Ropes, which will be dislodged similarly to Torches. All types can be crafted into their respective Rope Coils, consumable items useful for placing Ropes in inaccessible locations. Vertical movement speed on a Rope equals that of a free fall, though moving down via the Rope and hitting the ground does not cause fall damage. Horizontal movement is also possible by placing adjacent Rope horizontally, but is much slower. Visually, the player appears to move along a Rope using a mechanical tool with wheels, as though they were riding a rail. This tool appears automatically when using Rope, does not exist as a separate item, and is available from the beginning of the game.

Campfire.name: Campfire
Campfire.tooltip: Campfires are a type of furniture and crafting station that emit light and grant the Cozy Fire buff to players in their vicinity, which provides 10% increased innate health regeneration and additionally grants 0.5 HP/s constant regeneration. The buff is applied to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the campfire, similar to Heart Lanterns and Sunflowers. Campfires are also minor crafting stations, and uniquely, campfires are used to cook Marshmallow on a Stick (see their page for details). Campfires can be toggled off and on with ⚷ Open / Activate, which extinguishes the flame, light, and disables the Cozy Fire buff. They can also be extinguished and lit with the Water Gun and Slime Gun respectively, and as mechanisms, they can be toggled with wire. Campfires are extinguished by rain in The Constant special world seed.

Marshmallow.name: Marshmallow
Marshmallow.tooltip: The Marshmallow is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 1 minute, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). Marshmallows can be purchased from the Merchant for 1 Silver each when he is spoken to in a Snow biome. The Marshmallow is also a crafting material used to craft the Marshmallow on a Stick, which can be turned into a Cooked Marshmallow at a Campfire, greatly extending its buff duration.

Marshmallow on a Stick.name: Marshmallow on a Stick
Marshmallow on a Stick.tooltip: The Marshmallow on a Stick is an item that is used to create a Cooked Marshmallow by holding it over any lit Campfire, i.e. the Marshmallow must overlap with the 2×3-tile rectangle of the Campfire. It must be held for up to 15 seconds. The Marshmallow on a Stick must be held by the player, either by attaching it to the cursor in the inventory or selecting it in the hotbar, for the entire duration over the Campfire in order for it to be cooked. Selecting a different item in the hotbar, moving/turning away from the Campfire, or turning the Campfire off resets the timer. The exact cooking duration is randomized and can last between 7.5 seconds and 15 seconds. The average cooking duration is 12.5 seconds.

Cooked Marshmallow.name: Cooked Marshmallow
Cooked Marshmallow.tooltip: The Cooked Marshmallow is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().  The Cooked Marshmallow is created by holding a Marshmallow on a Stick over a Campfire for up to 15 seconds. The Marshmallow on a Stick must be held by the player, either by attaching it to the cursor in the inventory or selecting it in the hotbar, for the entire duration over the Campfire in order for it to be cooked. Selecting a different item in the hotbar, moving/turning away from the Campfire, or turning the Campfire off resets the timer.

Red Rocket.name: Red Rocket

Ice Torch.name: Ice Torch
Ice Torch.tooltip: Torches are furniture items that function as light sources when placed, held, or dropped (via the Throw button). Regular Torches can be found randomly in Chests and Pots, as a bonus drop from slimes, Torch Zombies, or purchased from the Merchant or Skeleton Merchant for 50 Copper each. Placing at least 101 Torches in close proximity below the surface layer in any biome will start the Torch God mini-event. Completing the event will grant the Torch God's Favor, which allows the player to automatically convert ordinary Torches to one of the biome types.

Shoe Spikes.name: Shoe Spikes
Shoe Spikes.tooltip: The Shoe Spikes are an accessory that lets players partially "stick" to the sides of blocks, slowly sliding down them when moving against them in midair. Jumps can also be performed off the sides of blocks. By repeatedly sticking and jumping, vertical blocks can be scaled. When sliding down, the slide speed can be accelerated using the ▼ Down key. Shoe Spikes can be found in Gold Chests found in Underground and Cavern layers, and in Rich Mahogany Chests found in the Underground Jungle. Shoe Spikes function identically to the Climbing Claws, but are found in different locations, Climbing Claws only appearing in surface chests. When both Shoe Spikes and Climbing Claws are equipped simultaneously, the wearer remains completely "stuck" at a fixed point when moving against the sides of blocks, and may slide down with the ▼ Down key. This effect can be achieved using a single accessory if the Shoe Spikes and Climbing Claws are combined into the Tiger Climbing Gear at a Tinkerer's Workshop.

Tiger Climbing Gear.name: Tiger Climbing Gear
Tiger Climbing Gear.tooltip: Tiger Climbing Gear is an accessory that allows for sliding down or completely stopping while touching walls. Holding the ▼ Down key while clinging to a wall allows the player to slide down walls a little faster than if they only had one of the ingredient accessories. While either clinging or sliding, the player can jump off of the wall, allowing them to scale vertical surfaces with ease. This accessory is useful if paired with wings, as the player's flight time is reset when latching onto a wall.

Tabi.name: Tabi
Tabi.tooltip: The Tabi is a Hardmode, post-Plantera accessory which allows the player to perform a dash by double-tapping either the ◀ Left or ▶ Right key, or the Dash button once. The dash ability has a one-second cooldown between uses. The Tabi has a 1/12 (8.33%) / 23/144 (15.97%) chance to drop from Bone Lees in the post-Plantera Dungeon.

Pink Snow Hood.name: Pink Snow Hood
Pink Snow Hood.tooltip: Pink Snow armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Pink Snow Hood, Pink Snow Coat, and Pink Snow Pants. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +9 defense Immunity to the Chilled and Frozen debuffs Pink Snow armor pieces are interchangeable with pieces from Snow armor, still providing the set bonus.

Pink Snow Coat.name: Pink Snow Coat
Pink Snow Coat.tooltip: Pink Snow armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Pink Snow Hood, Pink Snow Coat, and Pink Snow Pants. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +9 defense Immunity to the Chilled and Frozen debuffs Pink Snow armor pieces are interchangeable with pieces from Snow armor, still providing the set bonus.

Pink Snow Pants.name: Pink Snow Pants
Pink Snow Pants.tooltip: Pink Snow armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Pink Snow Hood, Pink Snow Coat, and Pink Snow Pants. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +9 defense Immunity to the Chilled and Frozen debuffs Pink Snow armor pieces are interchangeable with pieces from Snow armor, still providing the set bonus.

Pink Thread.name: Pink Thread
Pink Thread.tooltip: Threads are crafting materials used primarily in vanity items. Black Thread and Pink Thread can be purchased from the Clothier, while Green Thread can be crafted.

Mana Regeneration Band.name: Mana Regeneration Band
Mana Regeneration Band.tooltip: The Mana Regeneration Band is an accessory item made by combining a Band of Starpower and a Band of Regeneration at a Tinkerer's Workshop. It grants the following effects while equipped: +1 HP/second health regeneration +40 maximum mana +30 mana/second mana regeneration

Sandstorm in a Balloon.name: Sandstorm in a Balloon
Sandstorm in a Balloon.tooltip: The Sandstorm in a Balloon is an accessory that combines the functions of the Sandstorm in a Bottle and the Shiny Red Balloon. It boosts jump duration by 33% and jump speed by 30%, increasing the player's first jump's height to 10.5 tiles, and provides a double jump that can reach a height of 26.5 tiles, for a total height of 37 tiles. The total jump height of the Sandstorm in a Balloon is reduced when underwater, reducing the total underwater jump height from 27 tiles to 22 tiles. Unlike most other double-jump balloons, the Sandstorm in a Balloon's full jump is high enough for the player to take minor fall damage, unless the player has fall damage immunity accessories like the Lucky Horseshoe.

Master Ninja Gear.name: Master Ninja Gear
Master Ninja Gear.tooltip: The Master Ninja Gear is a Hardmode, post-Plantera accessory that combines the abilities of the Black Belt, the Tabi, and the Tiger Climbing Gear. It allows the player to cling to and slide down vertical walls, quickly dash short distances by double-tapping either the ◀ Left or ▶ Right key, or the Dash button once, and offers a 1/10 (10%) chance to automatically dodge enemy attacks. There is a one-second cooldown period between dashes.

Rope Coil.name: Rope Coil
Rope Coil.tooltip: Rope Coils are consumable mobility items that, when thrown by the player, travel in an arc affected by gravity until striking a block. On making contact, a vertical string of ten pieces of the respective Rope type will be placed, starting from the point of contact and descending until the Rope runs out or makes contact with another block below. Once in place, the Ropes created by a Rope Coil are ordinary Rope items that can be climbed, expanded with other placed Ropes, and collected with a pickaxe or drill. If a thrown Rope Coil strikes the top of an already placed Rope, it will automatically extend the existing Rope. If the coil cannot extend lower than ten tiles because of an obstacle, the excess Rope pieces will drop as items. If the coil cannot extend at all, the excess Rope will drop as the coil item. There are no rope coil analogues for chains nor streamers.

Blowgun.name: Blowgun
Blowgun.tooltip: The Blowgun is a pre-Hardmode ranged weapon that can be purchased from the Witch Doctor for 5 Gold. It is an indirect upgrade to the Blowpipe. When used, it fires Seeds and darts as ammunition. While a Blowgun is in a player's inventory, there is a chance that any vegetation growing on normal grass, in Clay Pots, and in Planter Boxes will drop Seeds. Flowers typically drop 4 Seeds at a time, while tall grass typically drops 1–2 Seeds. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Blizzard in a Bottle.name: Blizzard in a Bottle
Blizzard in a Bottle.tooltip: The Blizzard in a Bottle is a pre-Hardmode accessory which works similarly to the Cloud in a Bottle, allowing the player to double-jump. Instead of a cloud being produced when the player jumps, a trail of snow is produced at the player's feet. The Blizzard jump goes 8 tiles into the air, totaling 14 tiles when put together with the first jump. The Blizzard in a Bottle has a 15.52% chance of being found inside Frozen Chests in the Ice biome, as well as a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being obtained from Frozen(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Boreal Crates(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, it can also be crafted at a Crystal Ball.
Blizzard in a Bottle.drops_summary: Boreal Crate (16.67%), Frozen Chest (15.52%), Frozen Crate (16.67%)

Frostburn Arrow.name: Frostburn Arrow
Frostburn Arrow.tooltip: The Frostburn Arrow is a pre-Hardmode arrow. It has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to inflict the Frostburn debuff for 3 seconds on enemies.

Enchanted Sword.name: Enchanted Sword
Enchanted Sword.tooltip: The Enchanted Sword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. When swung, it occasionally fires an Enchanted Beam projectile that cannot pierce enemies or pass through blocks. Both the sword and its projectile produce lingering particles that emit large amounts of light. The Enchanted Sword can be obtained by destroying an "enchanted sword in stone" background object, which can be found in random locations underground and in Enchanted Sword Shrines. Destroying this background object has a 29/30 (96.67%) chance to drop an Enchanted Sword, with the other 1/30 (3.33%) times instead dropping a Terragrim. The Enchanted Sword also has a 1/30 (3.33%) and 1/15 (6.67%) chance to be found in Golden and Titanium Crates respectively. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Pickaxe Axe.name: Pickaxe Axe
Pickaxe Axe.tooltip: The Pickaxe Axe is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses pickaxe and axe. It is the alternative to the Drax, having a lower base mining speed but longer range and the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Chlorophyte Ore. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Cobalt Waraxe.name: Cobalt Waraxe
Cobalt Waraxe.tooltip: The Cobalt Waraxe is a Hardmode axe and the alternative to the Cobalt Chainsaw. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Palladium Waraxe. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Mythril Waraxe.name: Mythril Waraxe
Mythril Waraxe.tooltip: The Mythril Waraxe is a Hardmode axe and the alternative to the Mythril Chainsaw. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Orichalcum Waraxe. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Adamantite Waraxe.name: Adamantite Waraxe
Adamantite Waraxe.tooltip: The Adamantite Waraxe is a Hardmode axe and the alternative to the Adamantite Chainsaw. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Titanium Waraxe. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Eater's Bone.name: Eater's Bone
Eater's Bone.tooltip: The Eater's Bone is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Eater that follows the player. The Baby Eater will not teleport to the player when it is far away, unlike most other pets. The Eater's Bone has a 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped by the Eater of Worlds.
Eater's Bone.drops_summary: Eater of Worlds (5%), Treasure Bag (Eater of Worlds) (5%)

Blend-O-Matic.name: Blend-O-Matic
Blend-O-Matic.tooltip: The Blend-O-Matic is a crafting station that is purchased from the Steampunker for 10 Gold. On the  Old-gen console and 3DS, it can only be purchased at night. Its sole purpose is to craft Asphalt Blocks which are used to run faster when walked on.

Meat Grinder.name: Meat Grinder
Meat Grinder.tooltip: The Meat Grinder is a Hardmode crafting station used to craft Flesh Blocks and Lesion Blocks. It has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of being dropped by several Crimson and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Corruption enemies. Flesh and Lesion Blocks can be used as building materials, and crafted into flesh-/lesion-themed walls and furniture via the Decay Chamber/Flesh Cloning Vat. As a result, the Meat Grinder is of little use without them.

Extractinator.name: Extractinator
Extractinator.tooltip: The Extractinator (or Silt Extractinator) is a special crafting station that converts Silt, Slush, and Desert Fossils into various resources such as ores, coins, and gems. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, it can also convert Glowing Mosses into any other regular moss, fishing trash into low level bait, and other miscellaneous materials. After being placed, suitable blocks must be consumed using the ⚷ Open / Activate key directly on the Extractinator, and the converted items will be dropped. Extractable blocks are selected automatically from the player's inventory while Auto Select is activated. When an Extractinator receives a Wire signal, it will attempt to process an extractable block from a Chest placed directly next to the Extractinator. It can perform this up to once per second. It can be obtained from multiple sources, with a 4.9% chance of spawning in Frozen Chests, a 5% to 6.67% chance of spawning in Gold Chests in the Underground and Cavern layers, and a 1.86% chance of being dropped by opening Wooden Crates. Underground Cabins in the Underground Desert(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) also have a chance to contain an Extractinator as part of the random decor. Feeding blocks to the Extractinator is the only way to obtain Amber Mosquitoes, and, along with opening crates, the only reliable way to obtain a world's alternative pre-Hardmode ores.
Extractinator.drops_summary: Frozen Chest (4.9%), Gold Chest (5%), Wooden Crate (1.86%)

Solidifier.name: Solidifier
Solidifier.tooltip: The Solidifier is a crafting station used to craft Slime furniture, some miscellaneous blocks, and two weapons: the Slime Spear and Slime Whip. The Solidifier is always dropped by King Slime, and is also always placed on the starting island of a newly generated Skyblock world.

Amber.name: Amber
Amber.tooltip: Amber is a gem found within the Underground Desert of a world. It can craft the its corresponding set of standard gem items, and it also has three exclusive recipes: the Crate Potion, the Harpy Charm, and the Slasher's Mysterious Skull. It can only be obtained in the following ways, which differ from the other gems: Mining the naturally generated placed form found in the Underground Desert. Extracting from Silt, Slush, or Desert Fossil by putting them in an Extractinator. Harvesting Amber gem trees. Dropping from Geodes with a 2/7 (28.57%) chance. Like all other gems, Amber can be placed on blocks, and can be crafted back into its Gemstone Block form at a Heavy Assembler in a Graveyard biome.

Confetti Gun.name: Confetti Gun
Confetti Gun.tooltip: The Confetti Gun is a consumable novelty weapon that fires a cloud of colorful confetti. This effect is purely visual and causes no damage or functional effect. Confetti Guns are consumed upon use; they can only be used once each. They are purchased from the Party Girl for 1 Silver each.

Chlorophyte Mask.name: Chlorophyte Mask
Chlorophyte Mask.tooltip: Chlorophyte armor is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses armor set consisting of the Chlorophyte Plate Mail and Chlorophyte Greaves, as well as four different headpieces: the Chlorophyte Mask, Chlorophyte Helmet, Chlorophyte Headgear, and Chlorophyte Visor, providing bonuses for the melee, ranged, magic and summon damage type respectively. Crafting a full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Chlorophyte Bars (270 Chlorophyte Ore). Crafting all six pieces requires a total of 90 Chlorophyte Bars (450 Chlorophyte Ore). The full set grants the following effects while equipped: Summons a Leaf Crystal minion above the player. It periodically fires green, laser-like bolts of energy that instantly hit the target and deals 100 base damage and 10 (Extremely strong) knockback.

Chlorophyte Bar.name: Chlorophyte Bar
Chlorophyte Bar.tooltip: The Chlorophyte Bar is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses bar.

Red Dye.name: Red Dye
Red Dye.tooltip: Dyes are items that can be placed in the "dye slots" of a player's inventory to alter the colors and/or textures of equipped armor, vanity items, and accessories. The Dye Trader NPC sells two dyes (Silver Dye and Brown Dye) as well as the Dye Vat (5 Gold). The other dyes must be crafted using the Dye Vat or obtained through trading in Strange Plants to the Dye Trader. Primary crafted dyes can be further combined to craft Bright, Gradient, and Compound dyes. There are 119 different dyes in the game (118 on single-player worlds, as Team Dye is not available in single-player worlds). Some dyes will make sprites visible in complete darkness, most of which are Strange Dyes. If the Critter Shampoo is dyed (by placing a dye in the respective accessory dye slot), the dye will be applied to all of the player's minions.

Paintbrush.name: Paintbrush
Paintbrush.tooltip: The Paintbrush is a tool which is used to apply paint to tiles. It is purchased from the Painter for 1 Gold. Its upgrade, the Spectre Paintbrush, grants a bonus to range. The Paintbrush cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Paint Roller.name: Paint Roller
Paint Roller.tooltip: The Paint Roller is a tool which is used to paint walls. It is purchased from the Painter for 1 Gold. Its upgrade, the Spectre Paint Roller, grants a bonus to range. Using a roller requires paint to be in the player's inventory. The Paint Roller cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Red Paint.name: Red Paint
Red Paint.tooltip: Paint is used to modify the color of objects. Nearly anything can be painted, including blocks, background walls, and furniture, along with non-collectable environment objects like trees, tall grass, flowers, and other ambient growth. Basic paint is purchased from the Painter NPC. Two of the same color can be combined at a Dye Vat to create "deep" color versions, which apply their color more vividly and are required in order to paint certain objects. Coating(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is used to apply a special effect over a block and can be applied in tandem with paint and other coatings. It is purchased from the Painter NPC. Paint and coatings are applied to blocks and furniture with the Paintbrush, and to walls with the Paint Roller, with each tile consuming one item of paint/coating. The Paint Sprayer will automatically paint items when placing them. Paint and coatings can be removed with the Paint Scraper, although they will never be retrieved upon doing so. Destroying a painted block will not drop the paint item either. Paint can be placed in ammo slots. If more than one type of paint or coating is present in the player's inventory, the paint or coating in the earliest inventory slot is used first (starting from the top-left slot).

Paint and coatings are applied to blocks and furniture with the Paintbrush, and to walls with the Paint Roller, with each tile consuming one item of paint/coating. The Paint Sprayer will automatically paint items when placing them. Paint and coatings can be removed with the Paint Scraper, although they will never be retrieved upon doing so. Destroying a painted block will not drop the paint item either. Paint can be placed in ammo slots. If more than one type of paint or coating is present in the player's inventory, the paint or coating in the earliest inventory slot is used first (starting from the top-left slot).
