Paint Scraper.name: Paint Scraper
Paint Scraper.tooltip: The Paint Scraper is a tool which is used to remove paint off tiles and walls, eliminating the need of breaking and re-placing a tile to remove its paint. The Paint Scraper is purchased for 1 Gold from the Painter. Its upgrade, the Spectre Paint Scraper, grants a bonus to range. Paint removed by a scraper can never be recovered. The Paint Scraper can be used to obtain moss by removing it from tiles. The Paint Scraper cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Lihzahrd Brick.name: Lihzahrd Brick
Lihzahrd Brick.tooltip: Lihzahrd Bricks are blocks that make up the structure of the Jungle Temple. They are the toughest block in the game, being impervious to explosives and only breakable using the Picksaw or a better pickaxe or drill. They also cannot be made inactive using Actuators until Plantera has been defeated, unless they are above the surface layer. Like Jungle grass, placing 140 (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) / 80 (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Lihzahrd Bricks in one area creates a Jungle biome.

Lihzahrd Brick Wall.name: Lihzahrd Brick Wall
Lihzahrd Brick Wall.tooltip: The Lihzahrd Brick Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in the Jungle Temple, considered unsafe. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player. The Forbidden Lihzahrd Brick Wall is an item that places an unsafe Lihzahrd Brick Wall. It is visually identical and is obtained by throwing a Lihzahrd Brick Wall into Shimmer after Golem has been defeated.

Slush Block.name: Slush Block
Slush Block.tooltip: Slush Blocks are blocks that appear naturally in Ice biomes. They are subject to gravity and will fall if the blocks supporting them are removed, dealing damage to any player or enemy they fall on (similar to Sand and Silt). Slush can be placed in an Extractinator or Chlorophyte Extractinator to be converted into various valuable materials, including gems, coins, ores, and very rarely, the Amber Mosquito pet summoning item.

Palladium Ore.name: Palladium Ore
Palladium Ore.tooltip: Palladium Ore belongs to the first tier of the early Hardmode ores. Upon the first altar broken, either it or Cobalt Ore will spawn in the underground and cavern layers. Mining Palladium Ore requires a Molten Pickaxe or better. As with all early Hardmode ores, decreasing quantities of the ore spawn with every third altar broken afterwards, it is immune to explosives (apart from the Power Bomb and Sticky Power Bomb), and it can be obtained from Hardmode crates.
Palladium Ore.drops_summary: Most crates (1.19%), Mythril Crate (2.08%), Pearlwood Crate (3.57%)

Orichalcum Ore.name: Orichalcum Ore
Orichalcum Ore.tooltip: Orichalcum Ore belongs to the second tier of the early Hardmode ores. Upon the second altar broken, either it or Mythril Ore can spawn in the cavern layer. Mining Orichalcum Ore requires a Cobalt/Palladium Pickaxe or better. As with all early Hardmode ores, decreasing quantities of the ore spawn with every third altar broken afterwards, it is immune to explosives (apart from the Power Bomb and Sticky Power Bomb), and it can be obtained from Hardmode crates.
Orichalcum Ore.drops_summary: Most crates (1.19%), Mythril Crate (2.08%), Titanium Crate (2.5%)

Titanium Ore.name: Titanium Ore
Titanium Ore.tooltip: Titanium Ore belongs to the third tier of the early Hardmode ores. Upon the third altar broken, either it or Adamantite Ore can spawn in the cavern layer, roughly at lava depth. Mining Titanium Ore requires a Mythril/Orichalcum Pickaxe or better. As with all early Hardmode ores, decreasing quantities of the ore spawn with every third altar broken afterwards, it is immune to explosives (apart from the Power Bomb and Sticky Power Bomb), and it can be obtained from Hardmode crates. It is one of the two ores able to create Hardmode Forges, which are used for smelting all ores obtained in future progression, as well as itself.

Teal Mushroom.name: Teal Mushroom
Teal Mushroom.tooltip: The Teal Mushroom is a type of mushroom. It grows on Dirt, Stone, Mud, or regular Jungle grass in the Underground and Cavern layers. Unlike many plants, instead of broken by any attack, it has to be harvested with a pickaxe. Its sole purpose is to make Teal Dye.

Green Mushroom.name: Green Mushroom
Green Mushroom.tooltip: The Green Mushroom is a type of mushroom. It grows on Dirt, Stone, Mud, or regular Jungle grass in the Underground and Cavern layers. Unlike many plants, instead of broken by any attack, it has to be harvested with a pickaxe. Its sole purpose is to make Green Dye.

Sky Blue Flower.name: Sky Blue Flower
Sky Blue Flower.tooltip: The Sky Blue Flower is a type of plant. It grows on Jungle grass in any layer except the Underworld, or on regular Sand Blocks submerged in at least 2 tiles of any liquid above surface. Unlike many plants, instead of broken by any attack, it has to be harvested with a pickaxe. Its sole purpose is to make Sky Blue Dye.

Yellow Marigold.name: Yellow Marigold
Yellow Marigold.tooltip: The Yellow Marigold is a type of plant. It grows on regular grass and Hallowed grass above surface. Unlike many plants, instead of broken by any attack, it has to be harvested with a pickaxe. Its sole purpose is to make Yellow Dye.

Blue Berries.name: Blue Berries
Blue Berries.tooltip: Blue Berries are a dye material and type of plant. Placed Blue Berries have the appearance of a blueberry bush. They can grow on regular grass or Jungle grass above surface. Unlike many plants, instead of broken by any attack, it has to be harvested with a pickaxe. Its sole purpose is to make Blue Dye.

Lime Kelp.name: Lime Kelp
Lime Kelp.tooltip: The Lime Kelp is a dye material and type of plant. It grows on any tiles submerged in at least 2 tiles of any liquid in the Underground and Cavern layers. Unlike many plants, instead of broken by any attack, it has to be harvested with a pickaxe. Its sole purpose is to make Lime Dye.

Pink Prickly Pear.name: Pink Prickly Pear
Pink Prickly Pear.tooltip: The Pink Prickly Pear is a dye material. It grows on top of regular or Hallowed Cacti above surface, but can also be seen on top of Corrupt or Crimson Cacti (see Notes for details). Unlike many plants, instead of being broken by any attack, it has to be harvested with a pickaxe. Its sole purpose is to craft Pink Dye.

Orange Bloodroot.name: Orange Bloodroot
Orange Bloodroot.tooltip: The Orange Bloodroot is a type of plant. It can grow below Dirt Blocks in the Underground and Cavern layers. Unlike many plants, instead of broken by any attack, it has to be harvested with a pickaxe. Its sole purpose is to make Orange Dye.

Red Husk.name: Red Husk
Red Husk.tooltip: The Red Husk is a dye material that is dropped by Cochineal Beetles. Its sole purpose is to make Red Dye.

Cyan Husk.name: Cyan Husk
Cyan Husk.tooltip: The Cyan Husk is a dye material that is dropped by Cyan Beetles, which only spawn in the Underground Snow biome. Its sole purpose is to make Cyan Dye.

Violet Husk.name: Violet Husk
Violet Husk.tooltip: The Violet Husk is a dye material that is dropped by Lac Beetles, which only spawn in the Underground Jungle. Its sole purpose is to make Violet Dye.

Purple Mucus.name: Purple Mucus
Purple Mucus.tooltip: The Purple Mucus is a dye material that is dropped by Sea Snails, which only spawn in the Ocean biome. Its sole purpose is to make Purple Dye.

Black Ink.name: Black Ink
Black Ink.tooltip: Black Ink is a dye material that is dropped by Squids, which only spawn in the Ocean biome. Its sole purpose is to make Black Dye.

Dye Vat.name: Dye Vat
Dye Vat.tooltip: The Dye Vat is a crafting station used to craft dyes, paints, and colored string and Golf Balls. It is purchased from the Dye Trader for 5 Gold.

Bee Gun.name: Bee Gun
Bee Gun.tooltip: The Bee Gun is a pre-Hardmode magic gun that has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by the Queen Bee. When used, it fires a burst of Bee projectiles that home in on enemies, can pierce enemies twice or bounce on blocks three times, and have a 1/2 (50%) chance to deal 1 extra damage. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Possessed Hatchet.name: Possessed Hatchet
Possessed Hatchet.tooltip: The Possessed Hatchet is a Hardmode, post-Golem boomerang that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped from Golem. When thrown, it homes in on enemies within 50 tiles and inflicts the Hemorrhage debuff on hit. Unlike most boomerangs, it does not have to return to the player before being fired, with no limit to the number that can be thrown out at one time. With no enemies nearby, it returns to the player after traveling 25 tiles. The Possessed Hatchet can hit up to 10 targets. This is different from most boomerangs, which can hit infinite enemies while returning. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Bee Keeper.name: Bee Keeper
Bee Keeper.tooltip: The Bee Keeper is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by the Queen Bee. When swung, it will inflict the Confused debuff on hit for 2 seconds. It also summons a burst of 1–3 Bee projectiles on hit, which home in on enemies, deal 1/3 (33.33%) of the weapon's damage (10 base damage), can pierce enemies twice and bounce on blocks three times, and have a 1/2 (50%) to deal 1 extra damage. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Hive.name: Hive
Hive.tooltip: Hive is a block type that Bee Hives are made from. Upon mining it may either turn into liquid honey, spawn in a Bee, or simply drop like a regular item. Hive blocks can also be acquired by dropping Honey Blocks or Crispy Honey Blocks into Shimmer. Hive blocks can only be placed using a Hive Wand, consuming Hive blocks from the player's inventory. While using the Hive block directly, there is a 1/30 (3.33%) chance per tick (average of once every 0.5 seconds) to release a bee projectile that chases enemies, without consuming the item. The bee projectile deals 5 base damage and is considered a melee projectile, meaning it can critically strike using the player's melee critical strike chance, and benefit from melee effects such as Flasks, Magma Stone, Frost armor's set bonus, and Sharpening Station, but does not have its damage boosted by the player's melee damage bonuses. Hive blocks can be converted into Honey Blocks when used on an Extractinator.

Honey Block.name: Honey Block
Honey Block.tooltip: Honey Blocks are blocks formed when water comes into contact with honey. When placed, they slow the movement of any player walking on them. Vertically, a player can slowly slide down them (even without having the Climbing Claws or Shoe Spikes equipped). They also greatly reduce jump height to one tile, or 3 tiles with the Shiny Red Balloon equipped. NPCs, critters, and enemies are not affected.

Hive Wall.name: Hive Wall
Hive Wall.tooltip: The Hive Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Bee Hives, considered unsafe. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player. Unlike Hive blocks, it does not need a Hive Wand to be placed.

Crispy Honey Block.name: Crispy Honey Block
Crispy Honey Block.tooltip: The Crispy Honey Block is a block formed when honey comes into contact with lava. It can also be crafted. Crispy Honey Blocks are not destroyed when dropped into lava, despite having a rarity of .

Honey Bucket.name: Honey Bucket
Honey Bucket.tooltip: Buckets are tools used to carry water, lava, or honey, allowing them to be removed or placed. With an Empty Bucket, pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button on any sufficient body of liquid collects it, which replaces the Empty Bucket with the respective Water Bucket, Lava Bucket, or Honey Bucket. Pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button again will deposit the liquid at the location of the cursor, wherein the filled bucket is again replaced with an Empty Bucket. Each bucket holds one tile of liquid. Shimmer cannot be collected with standard buckets. When an Empty Bucket is dropped as an item into the world (with the Throw button) while it is raining, and there are no background walls behind the dropped item, it will turn into a Water Bucket after some time has passed. Empty Buckets will not fill under Rain Clouds or Magic Droppers. The Bottomless Water Bucket, Bottomless Lava Bucket and Bottomless Honey Bucket act as infinite water, lava, and honey placing buckets, whereas the Super Absorbant Sponge, Lava Absorbant Sponge, and Honey Absorbant Sponge are essentially infinite Empty Buckets that accept only water, lava or honey, respectively. They also add and remove liquids at a slightly faster speed than their normal bucket counterparts (especially when moving the cursor around while filling/draining).

Hive Wand.name: Hive Wand
Hive Wand.tooltip: Block-placing wands are special tools that allow the player to place blocks they would normally not be able to place. They do not consume any mana. Each wand consumes a specific material from the player's inventory (details listed below). There are 6 different block-placing wands.
Hive Wand.drops_summary: Angry Bones (0.4%), Cursed Skull (0.4%), Dark Caster (0.4%)

Beenade.name: Beenade
Beenade.tooltip: The Beenade is a consumable ranged weapon that acts similarly to a regular Grenade when thrown but releases 15–24 friendly bee projectiles upon detonating after 3 seconds. These bee projectiles deal 100% of the Beenade's damage (12 base damage) per hit and have a 1/2 (50%) chance to deal 1 extra damage, but cannot inflict critical hits. The bee projectiles will home in on nearby enemies before dissipating after a 10-second duration, upon piercing enemies or ricocheting off solid blocks a total of 3 times, or immediately upon contact with water or lava. Beenades have a 3/4 (75%) / 100% chance of being dropped by the Queen Bee in stacks of 10–30 (10–29), and can also be crafted from Grenades and Bee Wax.

Gravity Globe.name: Gravity Globe
Gravity Globe.tooltip: The Gravity Globe is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord accessory that allows the holder to flip gravity, so that the player falls up instead of down, and toggle gravity back to normal afterward. Once equipped, pressing the ▲ Up key toggles the gravity direction. This only affects the player with the item equipped. The Gravity Globe is always dropped from the Moon Lord's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.

Honey Comb.name: Honey Comb
Honey Comb.tooltip: The Honey Comb is a pre-Hardmode accessory which has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to be dropped by the Queen Bee. When equipped, it spawns 1–4 Bee projectiles which attack nearby enemies each time the player takes damage, and grants the Honey buff for 5 seconds after being damaged.

Abeemination.name: Abeemination
Abeemination.tooltip: The Abeemination is a boss-summoning item that summons the Queen Bee when used. It can only be used in the Jungle or Underground Jungle, at any time.

Bottled Honey.name: Bottled Honey
Bottled Honey.tooltip: Bottled Honey is a pre-Hardmode crafting material and recovery potion. When used, it restores 80 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for 60 seconds. This duration can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths. It also grants the player the Honey buff for 15 seconds. In addition to being crafted, Bottled Honey is also dropped by the Queen Bee, found in Bee Hives in the Underground Jungle.

Rain Hat.name: Rain Hat
Rain Hat.tooltip: Rain armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Rain Hat and Rain Coat. Each piece has a 1/40 (2.5%) chance to be dropped by Raincoat Zombies. The full set grants 3 defense while equipped.

Rain Coat.name: Rain Coat
Rain Coat.tooltip: Rain armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Rain Hat and Rain Coat. Each piece has a 1/40 (2.5%) chance to be dropped by Raincoat Zombies. The full set grants 3 defense while equipped.

Lihzahrd Door.name: Lihzahrd Door
Lihzahrd Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Temple Key.name: Temple Key
Temple Key.tooltip: The Temple Key is dropped by Plantera and is used to unlock the Lihzahrd Door, the door to the Jungle Temple. It is consumed upon use, like Golden Keys.

Lihzahrd Chest.name: Lihzahrd Chest
Lihzahrd Chest.tooltip: Lihzahrd Chests are chests found in the Jungle Temple. Each contains one Lihzahrd Power Cell, and may contain a Lihzahrd Furnace, some Solar Tablet Fragments, and sometimes, a Solar Tablet. They also contain other typical Gold Chest loot.

Lihzahrd Chair.name: Lihzahrd Chair
Lihzahrd Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Lihzahrd Table.name: Lihzahrd Table
Lihzahrd Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Lihzahrd Work Bench.name: Lihzahrd Work Bench
Lihzahrd Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Super Dart Trap.name: Super Dart Trap
Super Dart Trap.tooltip: The Super Dart Trap is a trap found inside the Jungle Temple and, rarely, outside the Temple's door. It fires a dart when activated via Wire, which costs no ammunition, but has a cooldown period of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 3.33 seconds / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 3 seconds between firings. The darts deal 80 / 160 / 240 damage and inflict Poisoned for 15 / 30 / 37.5 seconds to players (40 damage and 15 seconds of Poisoned to NPCs, enemies, and critters). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Super Dart Traps can be rotated 90° with a hammer. (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Unlike Lihzahrd Bricks, breaking Super Dart Traps does not require the Picksaw.

Flame Trap.name: Flame Trap
Flame Trap.tooltip: The Flame Trap is a trap found naturally in the Jungle Temple. When activated, it fires a jet of fire, which has a maximum range of 20 ( 47) tiles, and can pierce an infinite number of targets. It has a cooldown of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 3.33 seconds / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 3 seconds between firings. The fire deals 80 / 160 / 240 damage to players (40 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters), and inflicts the Hellfire debuff for 20 / 40 / 50 seconds on players (20 seconds on NPCs, enemies, and critters). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Flame Traps can be rotated 90° with a hammer.

Spiky Ball Trap.name: Spiky Ball Trap
Spiky Ball Trap.tooltip: The Spiky Ball Trap is a type of trap that can be found naturally in the Jungle Temple and, rarely, outside the Temple's door. When activated, it dispenses orange spiky balls that bounce several times. It has a cooldown of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 5 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 4 seconds between activations. The spiky balls deal 80 / 160 / 240 damage to players (40 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Spiky Ball Traps can be rotated 90° with a hammer. The total number of spiky balls spawned at once is limited. See below for details. (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Unlike Lihzahrd Bricks, breaking Spiky Ball Traps does not require the Picksaw.

Spear Trap.name: Spear Trap
Spear Trap.tooltip: The Spear Trap is a trap found naturally in the Jungle Temple and, rarely, outside the Temple's door. When activated, it launches a spear in a straight line that can pierce an infinite number of targets and retracts upon hitting a solid block or reaching its maximum range of 19.5 tiles. It has a cooldown of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 1.5 seconds / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 2 seconds between firings. The spear deals 120 / 240 / 360 damage to players (60 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Spear Traps can be rotated 90° with a hammer. (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Unlike Lihzahrd Bricks, breaking Spear Traps does not require the Picksaw.

Wooden Spike.name: Wooden Spike
Wooden Spike.tooltip: The Wooden Spike is a type of trap block that damages players who come in contact with it. The Wooden Spike deals 80 damage on contact and inflicts the Bleeding debuff for 10 / 20 / 25 seconds. Wooden Spikes are exclusively obtainable in limited quantities from the Jungle Temple, and can be broken with any drill, pickaxe, or explosive, unlike the Lihzahrd Bricks found around them, which require a Picksaw or stronger mining tool to break.

Lihzahrd Pressure Plate.name: Lihzahrd Pressure Plate
Lihzahrd Pressure Plate.tooltip: Pressure Plates are activation mechanisms that trigger wired mechanisms when stepped on. A pressure plate's color determines which characters can trigger it. Red, Brown, Gray, Orange, and Lihzahrd Pressure Plates are randomly generated on the map during world creation as the trigger for traps. They only take up a very small space on top of blocks, so they may be difficult to spot. The color of naturally spawned pressure plates is dependent on the color of the block they are generated on top of. Except for Lihzahrd Pressure Plates, they can also be purchased from the Mechanic. Weighted Pressure Plates activate once on being depressed, and again on being released. All Weighted Pressure Plates of the same color share a single state. As long as one Weighted Pressure Plate of a given color is already pressed down within a circuit, stepping on another identical plate will not send a new signal. They can be crafted from regular pressure plates. The Teal Pressure Pad is a special kind of pressure plate that responds to projectiles impacting it, which includes pets that touch it. Unlike regular pressure plates, the Teal Pressure Pad can be placed on all four sides of a block, e.g. on the ceiling or sidewall. It can be purchased from the Mechanic.

Lihzahrd Statue.name: Lihzahrd Statue
Lihzahrd Statue.tooltip: Statues are furniture items. While some are purely decorative, others have a functional effect when activated via Wire—depending on the statue, it may spawn enemies, drop items, or teleport an NPC to the statue's location. Most statues can be found already placed in any area underground (most frequently in the Dungeon, Underground Cabins, and Cavern level), though Angel Statues also appear in Chests. Like all furniture, a pickaxe, a drill, or explosives are used to collect them. There are a total of 117 different statues: 25 decoration statues, 36 text and numerical statues, and 56 functional mechanisms.

Lihzahrd Watcher Statue.name: Lihzahrd Watcher Statue
Lihzahrd Watcher Statue.tooltip: Statues are furniture items. While some are purely decorative, others have a functional effect when activated via Wire—depending on the statue, it may spawn enemies, drop items, or teleport an NPC to the statue's location. Most statues can be found already placed in any area underground (most frequently in the Dungeon, Underground Cabins, and Cavern level), though Angel Statues also appear in Chests. Like all furniture, a pickaxe, a drill, or explosives are used to collect them. There are a total of 117 different statues: 25 decoration statues, 36 text and numerical statues, and 56 functional mechanisms.

Lihzahrd Guardian Statue.name: Lihzahrd Guardian Statue
Lihzahrd Guardian Statue.tooltip: Statues are furniture items. Wasp Gun.name: Wasp Gun
Wasp Gun.tooltip: The Wasp Gun is a Hardmode magic gun that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Plantera. When used, it fires 2–4 homing wasp projectiles that ricochet or hit enemies a maximum of three times before dissipating. The wasp projectiles also have 10 armor penetration. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Piranha Gun.name: Piranha Gun
Piranha Gun.tooltip: The Piranha Gun is a Hardmode, post-Plantera ranged weapon that costs no ammunition. It fires a spread of three returning Mechanical Piranha projectiles that inflict the Hemorrhage debuff for 4–6 seconds on hit. The Mechanical Piranha initially moves in a straight path until it collides with an enemy, at which point it latches into the target, follows its movement and deals continuous damage while the ⚒ Use / Attack button is held. If the initial target is killed and the button is still held, the projectiles will home in towards other nearby enemies. The Piranhas return to the gun when the button is released or once no other enemies are in the vicinity, and despawn after one minute of continuous use. Any Piranhas that return to the gun while the ⚒ Use / Attack button is held will be automatically relaunched towards the cursor. Each Piranha can target different enemies, or the same one if there are too few nearby. The Piranha Gun is always found in the Dungeon's Jungle Chest, which can only be unlocked with a Jungle Key after Plantera has been defeated. Its best modifier is Unreal. Because its attack speed is unaffected by modifiers, Godly and Demonic can also be considered the best modifiers for the Piranha Gun.

Pygmy Staff.name: Pygmy Staff
Pygmy Staff.tooltip: The Pygmy Staff is a Hardmode, post-Plantera summon weapon that summons a Pygmy minion. It fires a spear towards nearby enemies that inflicts the Acid Venom debuff for 5–10 seconds, but does not pierce enemies or pass through blocks. The Pygmy Staff has a 1/4 (25%) / 1/2 (50%) chance of being dropped by Plantera. Its best modifier is Fabled.

Pygmy Necklace.name: Pygmy Necklace
Pygmy Necklace.tooltip: The Pygmy Necklace is a pre-Hardmode accessory that provides the player with one additional minion slot. It is purchased from the Witch Doctor for 20 Gold at night.

Tiki Mask.name: Tiki Mask
Tiki Mask.tooltip: Tiki armor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera summoner armor set consisting of the Tiki Mask, Tiki Shirt, and Tiki Pants. The set can be purchased from the Witch Doctor for a total of 1 Platinum 50 Gold (set).  The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +35 defense +30% summon damage +30% whip range +4 minion slots

Tiki Shirt.name: Tiki Shirt
Tiki Shirt.tooltip: Tiki armor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera summoner armor set consisting of the Tiki Mask, Tiki Shirt, and Tiki Pants. The set can be purchased from the Witch Doctor for a total of 1 Platinum 50 Gold (set).  The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +35 defense +30% summon damage +30% whip range +4 minion slots

Tiki Pants.name: Tiki Pants
Tiki Pants.tooltip: Tiki armor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera summoner armor set consisting of the Tiki Mask, Tiki Shirt, and Tiki Pants. The set can be purchased from the Witch Doctor for a total of 1 Platinum 50 Gold (set).  The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +35 defense +30% summon damage +30% whip range +4 minion slots

Leaf Wings.name: Leaf Wings
Leaf Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Blizzard in a Balloon.name: Blizzard in a Balloon
Blizzard in a Balloon.tooltip: The Blizzard in a Balloon is an accessory that combines the effects of the Blizzard in a Bottle and the Shiny Red Balloon. It boosts jump duration by 33% and jump speed by 30%, increasing the player's first jump's height to ~10½ tiles (~75% increase), and provides a double jump that can reach a height of 14½ tiles, for a total height of 25 tiles. The total jump height of the Blizzard in a Balloon is reduced when underwater, reducing the total underwater jump height from 19 tiles (8 + 11 from Blizzard jump) to 16 tiles (7 + 9 from Blizzard jump).

Bundle of Balloons.name: Bundle of Balloons
Bundle of Balloons.tooltip: The Bundle of Balloons is an accessory that allows the wearer to perform a quadruple jump, as well as increasing the player's jump duration by 33% and jump speed by 30%. Each of the jumps has an effect from the different combined items: sandstorm jump, then blizzard jump, then cloud jump. Crafting this item requires three of the variants of Cloud in a Balloon, which in turn requires a total of 3 Shiny Red Balloons. In particular it requires the relatively rare Sandstorm in a Bottle.

Bat Wings.name: Bat Wings
Bat Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. Bone Sword.name: Bone Sword
Bone Sword.tooltip: The Bone Sword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of being dropped by Skeletons and Spore Skeletons. Upon hitting an enemy, it releases a non-piercing lobbed bone projectile that is affected by gravity, and deals 75% of the weapon's damage (14 base damage) and its full knockback. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Hercules Beetle.name: Hercules Beetle
Hercules Beetle.tooltip: The Hercules Beetle is a Hardmode, post-Plantera accessory that increases the damage of summon weapons by 15% and increases their knockback by 2. The Hercules Beetle can be purchased from the Witch Doctor for 40 Gold if he is spoken to in the Jungle after Plantera has been defeated.

Smoke Bomb.name: Smoke Bomb
Smoke Bomb.tooltip: The Smoke Bomb is a throwable, consumable novelty item that, when thrown, emits thick gray smoke for one minute. Upon throwing a Smoke Bomb, it will bounce or roll until it comes to a complete stop and continues to release smoke. Each can only be used once and cannot be picked up again once thrown. Smoke Bombs can be purchased from the Party Girl for 20 Copper each.

Bone Key.name: Bone Key
Bone Key.tooltip: The Bone Key is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Skeletron Head that follows the player. The Baby Skeletron Head floats around the player and sometimes spins its head, similarly to Skeletron's spinning head attack or the Dungeon Guardians in general. This action may also occur if the player is a bit further away from the Skeletron Head. The Bone Key is always dropped by Dungeon Guardians. Because Dungeon Guardians have extremely high stats intended to instantly kill all players, this can be a difficult item to acquire.

Nectar.name: Nectar
Nectar.tooltip: The Nectar is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Hornet that follows the player. This pet will not teleport to the player when it is far away. The Nectar has a 1/15 (6.67%) / 1/9 (11.11%) chance of being dropped by the Queen Bee.

Tiki Totem.name: Tiki Totem
Tiki Totem.tooltip: The Tiki Totem is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Tiki Spirit that floats and spins above the player's head. Unlike most pets, it will not teleport to the player when the player moves too quickly for it to keep up; it will simply float straight towards the player. The Tiki Totem can be purchased from the Witch Doctor for 2 Platinum when he is spoken to in the Jungle biome during Hardmode.

Lizard Egg.name: Lizard Egg
Lizard Egg.tooltip: The Lizard Egg is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Pet Lizard that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Pet Lizard will sprout wings like those of a Flying Snake to catch up with the player. The Lizard Egg has a 1/1000 (0.1%) chance of being dropped by Flying Snakes and Lihzahrds in the Jungle Temple.

Grave Marker.name: Grave Marker
Grave Marker.tooltip: A Tombstone is a furniture item that drops when a player dies. It can then be retrieved and used much like a sign or as a form of decoration. By default, it contains the death message generated based on how the player died along with the real-life date of the death. Upon death, a Tombstone will bounce around until it lands on a suitable 2-tile wide surface, where it will place itself. If a Tombstone cannot find a place to land (due to lack of suitable space), it cannot be retrieved and will eventually despawn. Two Tombstones cannot land on each other. Variants are chosen randomly upon death. Golden Tombstones drop when the player had more than 10 Gold in their inventory. Having 4–8 Tombstones placed in close proximity will gradually darken and desaturate the environment. Five or more Tombstones placed in close proximity will generate a Graveyard mini-biome. Breaking a Tombstone has 12.5% / 25% / 50% chance to spawn a Ghost off-screen. In Hardcore, Tombstones cannot be easily obtained because death is permanent. Instead, NPCs in worlds with Hardcore characters will drop Tombstones when they are killed. Variants are still chosen randomly; all NPCs drop a normal Tombstone except the Merchant and Tax Collector who drop a golden variant. In For the Worthy (including Zenith) worlds, the Tombstone projectiles dropped by players (but not those dropped by NPCs in Hardcore) deal 210 / 280 / 420 damage to players and 70 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters. Because Tombstones create Graveyards, and mark a place where a player had died, they are highlighted by Dangersense Potions. Abigail's Flower can be uncommonly found as a plant growing on grass near a placed Tombstone, regardless of world progression. Its spawn chance is increased in a The Constant world.

Gravestone.name: Gravestone
Gravestone.tooltip: A Tombstone is a furniture item that drops when a player dies. It can then be retrieved and used much like a sign or as a form of decoration. By default, it contains the death message generated based on how the player died along with the real-life date of the death. Upon death, a Tombstone will bounce around until it lands on a suitable 2-tile wide surface, where it will place itself. If a Tombstone cannot find a place to land (due to lack of suitable space), it cannot be retrieved and will eventually despawn. Two Tombstones cannot land on each other. Variants are chosen randomly upon death. Golden Tombstones drop when the player had more than 10 Gold in their inventory. Having 4–8 Tombstones placed in close proximity will gradually darken and desaturate the environment. Five or more Tombstones placed in close proximity will generate a Graveyard mini-biome. Breaking a Tombstone has 12.5% / 25% / 50% chance to spawn a Ghost off-screen. In Hardcore, Tombstones cannot be easily obtained because death is permanent. Instead, NPCs in worlds with Hardcore characters will drop Tombstones when they are killed. Variants are still chosen randomly; all NPCs drop a normal Tombstone except the Merchant and Tax Collector who drop a golden variant. In For the Worthy (including Zenith) worlds, the Tombstone projectiles dropped by players (but not those dropped by NPCs in Hardcore) deal 210 / 280 / 420 damage to players and 70 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters. Because Tombstones create Graveyards, and mark a place where a player had died, they are highlighted by Dangersense Potions. Abigail's Flower can be uncommonly found as a plant growing on grass near a placed Tombstone, regardless of world progression. Its spawn chance is increased in a The Constant world.

Leaf Blower.name: Leaf Blower
Leaf Blower.tooltip: The Leaf Blower is a Hardmode magic gun that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Plantera. When used, it rapidly fires a spread of leaf projectiles that begin swirling after traveling for about 15 tiles, and move in a spiral circle pattern while gradually fading away. The leaves cannot pass through blocks or pierce enemies. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Chlorophyte Bullet.name: Chlorophyte Bullet
Chlorophyte Bullet.tooltip: The Chlorophyte Bullet is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses bullet. It strongly homes in on the nearest enemy.

Parrot Cracker.name: Parrot Cracker
Parrot Cracker.tooltip: The Parrot Cracker is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Pet Parrot that follows the player. If the player stays still for long enough, it will perch on a nearby solid block, staying still until the player moves away from it. The Parrot Cracker can be purchased from the Pirate for 3 Platinum 75 Gold if he is spoken to in an Ocean biome.

Strange Glowing Mushroom.name: Strange Glowing Mushroom
Strange Glowing Mushroom.tooltip: The Strange Glowing Mushroom is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Truffle that follows the player. The Baby Truffle emits a small amount of blue light similar to Glowing Mushrooms. The Strange Glowing Mushroom can be purchased from the Truffle for 45 Gold.

Seedling.name: Seedling
Seedling.tooltip: The Seedling is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pet-summoning item that spawns a Pet Sapling to follow the player around. When the player is far enough away or in midair, it will sprout leaflets from its arms and use them as makeshift wings to fly towards them. The Seedling has a 1/20 (5%) / 1/15 (6.67%) chance of being dropped by Plantera.

Wisp in a Bottle.name: Wisp in a Bottle
Wisp in a Bottle.tooltip: The Wisp in a Bottle is a Hardmode, post-Plantera light pet-summoning item that spawns a light-providing Wisp that follows the player around. While active, it is similar to the Flickerwick. The Wisp emits cyan light and is brighter and keeps better pace with the player than other light pets, except the Suspicious Looking Tentacle and Jewel of Light(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) which have the same light radius. It moves in accordance with the direction keys the player is pressing, although it is oriented above the player's head by default. The Wisp's movement range appears to be about 7 tiles to the left, right, and below the player's hitbox and 7 tiles above the Wisp's normal starting position. The Wisp in a Bottle has a 1/400 (0.25%) / 799/160,000 (0.4994%) chance of being dropped by Blue Armored Bones, Rusty Armored Bones, and Hell Armored Bones.
Wisp in a Bottle.drops_summary: Blue Armored Bones (0.25%), Hell Armored Bones (0.25%), Rusty Armored Bones (0.25%)

Palladium Bar.name: Palladium Bar
Palladium Bar.tooltip: The Palladium Bar is a Hardmode bar. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Cobalt Bar.
Palladium Bar.drops_summary: Most crates (2.78%), Mythril Crate (3.47%), Pearlwood Crate (2.68%)

Palladium Sword.name: Palladium Sword
Palladium Sword.tooltip: The Palladium Sword is a Hardmode broadsword. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Cobalt Sword. The Palladium Sword has slightly higher damage and knockback, but a slower attack speed. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Palladium Pike.name: Palladium Pike
Palladium Pike.tooltip: The Palladium Pike is a Hardmode spear.

Palladium Repeater.name: Palladium Repeater
Palladium Repeater.tooltip: The Palladium Repeater is a Hardmode repeater.  Its alternate ore counterpart is the Cobalt Repeater. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Palladium Pickaxe.name: Palladium Pickaxe
Palladium Pickaxe.tooltip: The Palladium Pickaxe is a Hardmode pickaxe. It is the alternative to the Palladium Drill, having a lower base mining speed but longer range and the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Mythril and Orichalcum Ore. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Cobalt Pickaxe. The Palladium Pickaxe has slightly more pickaxe power, damage, and mining speed. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Palladium Drill.name: Palladium Drill
Palladium Drill.tooltip: The Palladium Drill is a Hardmode drill. It is the alternative to the Palladium Pickaxe, having a higher base mining speed but shorter range and lacking the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Mythril and Orichalcum Ore. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Cobalt Drill. The Palladium Drill has slightly more pickaxe power and damage. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Palladium Chainsaw.name: Palladium Chainsaw
Palladium Chainsaw.tooltip: The Palladium Chainsaw is a Hardmode chainsaw and the alternative to the Palladium Waraxe. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Cobalt Chainsaw. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Orichalcum Bar.name: Orichalcum Bar
Orichalcum Bar.tooltip: The Orichalcum Bar is a Hardmode bar. It is one of the two ores able to create a Hardmode Anvil, which is used to craft most Hardmode equipment. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Mythril Bar.
Orichalcum Bar.drops_summary: Most crates (2.78%), Mythril Crate (3.47%), Titanium Crate (4.44%)

Orichalcum Sword.name: Orichalcum Sword

Palladium Mask.name: Palladium Mask
Palladium Mask.tooltip: Palladium armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Palladium Breastplate and Palladium Leggings, as well as three different headpieces: the Palladium Mask, Palladium Helmet, and Palladium Headgear, providing bonuses for the melee, ranged, and magic damage type respectively. Crafting a full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Palladium Bars (162 Palladium Ore). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 78 Palladium Bars (234 Palladium Ore). Its alternate ore counterpart is the Cobalt armor. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: Hitting an enemy grants the Rapid Healing buff for 5 seconds, providing a flat health regeneration of 2 HP per second. Further hits will refresh the duration. The buff is not canceled when the armor is removed. Being flat health regeneration, it applies separately from the normal type. This also causes this regeneration to bypass the Bleeding debuff. While this buff is applied, the player emits visual orange heart particles.

Orichalcum Mask.tooltip: Orichalcum armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Orichalcum Breastplate and Orichalcum Leggings, as well as three different headpieces: the Orichalcum Mask, Orichalcum Helmet, and Orichalcum Headgear, providing bonuses for the melee, ranged, and magic damage type respectively. There is a cooldown of 0.33 seconds before another flower petal can be summoned, meaning that this set bonus adds roughly 100 DPS.

Titanium Mask.name: Titanium Mask
Titanium Mask.tooltip: Titanium armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Titanium Breastplate and Titanium Leggings, as well as three different headpieces: the Titanium Mask, Titanium Helmet, and Titanium Headgear, providing bonuses for melee, ranged, and magic damage type respectively. Crafting a full set with one headpiece requires a total of 59 Titanium Bars (236 Titanium Ore). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 85 Titanium Bars (340 Titanium Ore). Its alternate ore counterpart is the Adamantite armor. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: Attacking grants the player the Titanium Barrier buff, which spawns Titanium Shards that spin around the player. Each shard dissipates on enemy hits or after 10 seconds has passed.

Orichalcum Anvil.name: Orichalcum Anvil
Orichalcum Anvil.tooltip: The Mythril Anvil and Orichalcum Anvil are Hardmode crafting stations that serve and extend the function of a pre-Hardmode Anvil. These are very crucial to game advancement, as they account for making nearly every Hardmode recipe before the Ancient Manipulator. In addition to acting as a direct replacement to Lead and Iron Anvils and inheriting all of their crafting recipes, they further serve the similar function of crafting bars forged of Hardmode ores into weapons, armor and tools, as well as several other items, such as wings.

Titanium Forge.name: Titanium Forge
Titanium Forge.tooltip: The Adamantite Forge and Titanium Forge are Hardmode crafting stations that incorporate the same functions as a regular Furnace and Hellforge, with the additional bonus of being able to smelt Adamantite, Titanium and Chlorophyte ores into their respective bars. They emit light and give off fire particles when placed, like the Furnace and Hellforge. The Adamantite Forge and Titanium Forge are functionally identical.

Hallowed Bar.name: Hallowed Bar
Hallowed Bar.tooltip: The Hallowed Bar is a Hardmode bar. It is dropped by all three mechanical bosses: The Twins, The Destroyer, and Skeletron Prime.

Chlorophyte Claymore.name: Chlorophyte Claymore
Chlorophyte Claymore.tooltip: The Chlorophyte Claymore is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses broadsword. When swung, a large green aura with a bright edge follows the swing, extending its reach and also covering behind the player. The sword also releases several short-lived spore clouds as it is swung, which are purely visual and deal no damage. On every third use, a sparkling glow appears at tip of the sword and the swing becomes empowered, causing it to deal 150% of the weapon's damage (142 base damage) and 125% of its knockback (base knockback of 7.5 (Very strong)). If the empowered swing collides with solid blocks (including platforms and Planter Boxes), it creates a small explosion at the point of impact which deals same damage as the empowered swing, while also launching several lingering spore clouds upwards that pierce infinitely and deal 112.5% of the weapon's damage (106 base damage), but cannot pass through blocks. The explosion and spore clouds do not inflict any knockback. Its shortsword counterpart is the Chlorophyte Saber. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Chlorophyte Saber.name: Chlorophyte Saber
Chlorophyte Saber.tooltip: The Chlorophyte Saber is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses shortsword. When used, the sword is thrusted in repeated stabbing motions with slightly varying angles for each thrust, akin to Gladius and Starlight. Each thrust deals 70% of the weapon's damage (56 base damage) and inflicts the Spored debuff on enemies and other players in PvP for 5 seconds, causing enemies to lose 90 health per second (60 damage displayed every 0.67 seconds) and players to lose 15 health per second (1 damage displayed every 0.07 seconds). The damage of Spored can be increased by Accelerated Afflictions. Its broadsword counterpart is the Chlorophyte Claymore. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Chlorophyte Partisan.name: Chlorophyte Partisan
Chlorophyte Partisan.tooltip: The Chlorophyte Partisan is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses spear. When thrust, it fires a Spore Cloud projectile that deals the weapon's damage and knockback, lasts for a short time, can pass through blocks, and pierces an infinite number of enemies. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Chlorophyte Shotbow.name: Chlorophyte Shotbow
Chlorophyte Shotbow.tooltip: The Chlorophyte Shotbow is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses repeater. When used, it fires 2–3 arrows per shot, consuming one piece of ammunition. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Chlorophyte Pickaxe.name: Chlorophyte Pickaxe
Chlorophyte Pickaxe.tooltip: The Chlorophyte Pickaxe is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses pickaxe. It is the alternative to the Chlorophyte Drill, having a lower base mining speed but longer range and the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Chlorophyte Ore. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Chlorophyte Drill.name: Chlorophyte Drill
Chlorophyte Drill.tooltip: The Chlorophyte Drill is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses drill. It is the alternative to the Chlorophyte Pickaxe, having a higher base mining speed but shorter range and lacking the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. It can mine blocks up to Chlorophyte Ore. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Chlorophyte Chainsaw.name: Chlorophyte Chainsaw
Chlorophyte Chainsaw.tooltip: The Chlorophyte Chainsaw is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses chainsaw and the alternative to the Chlorophyte Greataxe. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Chlorophyte Greataxe.name: Chlorophyte Greataxe
Chlorophyte Greataxe.tooltip: The Chlorophyte Greataxe is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses axe and the alternative to the Chlorophyte Chainsaw. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Chlorophyte Warhammer.name: Chlorophyte Warhammer
Chlorophyte Warhammer.tooltip: The Chlorophyte Warhammer is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses hammer. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Chlorophyte Arrow.name: Chlorophyte Arrow
Chlorophyte Arrow.tooltip: The Chlorophyte Arrow is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses arrow. It can bounce off blocks up to three times, dissipating upon hitting blocks for the fourth time. It bounces towards the direction of the nearest enemy within a 50-tile radius that has an unobstructed line of sight to the arrow. Its damage is decreased by 34% after bouncing for the first time, but further bounces do not incur a damage penalty.

Amethyst Hook.name: Amethyst Hook
Amethyst Hook.tooltip: Hooks are a class of tools which aid the player in traversing terrain. When used, hooks fire a chain that latches to a surface or platform and pulls the player towards it. A hook is an essential tool which offers significant freedom from terrain height restrictions as well as being a fast movement option, and will often be the first major mobility tool a player acquires. A variety of hooks are available at all stages of the game (see table below). The Grapple hotkey activates the equipped hook in the player's equipment slot, or the first hook from the inventory (from left to right, top to bottom) without requiring it to be in the player's hotbar.Verify Several higher-tier hooks, such as the Ivy Whip, allow the player to grapple multiple surfaces simultaneously. If the character grapples one surface, then fires the hook a second time, another chain extends from the player without dislodging the first. Upon grappling a second surface, the player will be suspended in midair at a point midway between the two surfaces. This allows players more freedom during construction, or for navigating hazardous areas, such as above lava or Meteorite. All Journey Mode characters will spawn with the basic Grappling Hook already in their inventory.

Amber Mosquito.name: Amber Mosquito
Amber Mosquito.tooltip: The Amber Mosquito is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Dinosaur that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, a pterosaur will carry it by the tail to continue following them. The Amber Mosquito can be obtained by putting Silt, Slush, or Desert Fossils(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) into an Extractinator or Chlorophyte Extractinator(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). With Silt or Slush, it only has a 1/10,000 (0.01%) chance to drop, while with Desert Fossils it has a slightly higher chance of 27/100,000 (0.027%).

Umbrella Hat.name: Umbrella Hat
Umbrella Hat.tooltip: The Umbrella Hat is a vanity item that has a 1/45 (2.22%) chance to drop from Umbrella Slimes during the Rain event.

Nimbus Rod.name: Nimbus Rod
Nimbus Rod.tooltip: The Nimbus Rod is a Hardmode magic weapon that creates storm clouds that drop damaging "rain" projectiles directly below themselves. When cast, a cloud projectile is fired from the Nimbus Rod and travels towards the cursor. Upon reaching its destination or colliding with a solid block, the cloud stops and starts sending damaging raindrop particles downward, each dealing the weapon's stated damage. The raindrop can hit up to 5 targets. Each cloud lasts for five minutes and up to two clouds can be spawned at once. Using the Nimbus Rod when there are already two active clouds will cause the oldest cloud to disappear. The Nimbus Rod has a 1/15 (6.67%) chance of being dropped by Angry Nimbuses. Its best modifier is Demonic because it cannot get modifiers that affect knockback.

Orange Torch.name: Orange Torch
Orange Torch.tooltip: Torches are furniture items that function as light sources when placed, held, or dropped (via the Throw button). Regular Torches can be found randomly in Chests and Pots, as a bonus drop from slimes, Torch Zombies, or purchased from the Merchant or Skeleton Merchant for 50 Copper each. Placing at least 101 Torches in close proximity below the surface layer in any biome will start the Torch God mini-event. Completing the event will grant the Torch God's Favor, which allows the player to automatically convert ordinary Torches to one of the biome types.

Crimsand Block.name: Crimsand Block
Crimsand Block.tooltip: Sand Blocks are soil blocks found in vast quantities in Desert biomes, at shore and bottom of Ocean biomes, and can be found as microbiomes in patches in the Underground layer. They are also shot as projectiles by Antlions. Sand can spread and be converted by the evil biomes and The Hallow (see below). Sand is subject to gravity, a unique quality only shared by Slush, Silt, Shell Piles, Cracked Dungeon Bricks, and Ash on For the Worthy and Zenith worlds. Sand Blocks will deal damage to any player or enemy they fall on. If the amount of Sand falling on the player is significant, the Suffocation debuff will be inflicted until the player manages to escape. Sand is used to craft a small number of building blocks and other items directly, but it is also the raw material for Glass, which is used for a full furniture set and a variety of other items. All forms of Sand are also ammunition for the Sandgun, but they cannot be stored in the ammo slots of the inventory. Similar to the Sand Ball projectiles shot by Antlions, shot Sand Blocks will be placed on the ground as blocks if there are space available.

Bee Cloak.name: Bee Cloak
Bee Cloak.tooltip: The Bee Cloak is a Hardmode accessory that combines the effects of the Star Cloak and the Honey Comb. When the player is injured, three stars will fall on the player's current location and bees are released.

Eye of the Golem.name: Eye of the Golem
Eye of the Golem.tooltip: The Eye of the Golem is a Hardmode, post-Golem accessory that grants +10% critical strike chance. It has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Golem.

Honey Balloon.name: Honey Balloon
Honey Balloon.tooltip: The Honey Balloon is an accessory that combines the functions of a Shiny Red Balloon and a Honey Comb. It boosts jump height by 33% and jump speed by 30%, increasing the player's jump height to ~10½ blocks (~75% increase), while oddly reducing it when underwater, from 8 blocks-to 7 blocks, and releases a small swarm of angry bees when the player is hurt, which seek out and deal small amounts of damage to enemies. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, it also grants the Honey buff after being damaged.

Blue Horseshoe Balloon.name: Blue Horseshoe Balloon
Blue Horseshoe Balloon.tooltip: The Blue Horseshoe Balloon is an accessory that grants immunity to fall damage, increases jump height by 75%, grants a double-jump, and grants +0.05 luck(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The height of the first jump is increased from 6 blocks to 10.5 blocks, while the double-jump's height is increased from 5 blocks to 9 blocks, reaching a total of 19.5 blocks with both jumps.

White Horseshoe Balloon.name: White Horseshoe Balloon
White Horseshoe Balloon.tooltip: The White Horseshoe Balloon is an accessory that grants immunity to fall damage, increases jump height by 33% and jump speed by 30%, grants a double-jump, and grants +0.05 luck(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The height of the first jump is increased from 6 blocks to 10.5 blocks (~75% increase), while the double-jump's height is increased from 8 blocks to 14.5 blocks, reaching a total of 25 blocks with both jumps. Jump height is oddly reduced when underwater, reducing total underwater jump height from 19 blocks (8 + 11 from Blizzard jump) to 16 blocks (7 + 9 from Blizzard jump).

Yellow Horseshoe Balloon.name: Yellow Horseshoe Balloon
Yellow Horseshoe Balloon.tooltip: The Yellow Horseshoe Balloon is an accessory that grants immunity to fall damage, increases jump height by 75%, grants a double-jump, and grants +0.05 luck(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The height of the first jump is increased from 6 blocks to 10.5 blocks, while the double-jump's height is increased from 15 blocks to 26.5 blocks, reaching a total of 37 blocks with both jumps. Jump height is instead reduced by 15% when underwater, reducing total underwater jump height from 27 blocks (8 + 19 from Sandstorm jump) to 22 blocks (7 + 15 from Sandstorm jump).

Frozen Turtle Shell.name: Frozen Turtle Shell
Frozen Turtle Shell.tooltip: The Frozen Turtle Shell is a Hardmode accessory that has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by Ice Tortoises. While equipped, it grants the Ice Barrier buff, which provides +25% damage reduction while the player's health is at or below 50%. While the effect is active, it displays as a blue circle spinning around the player.

Sniper Rifle.name: Sniper Rifle
Sniper Rifle.tooltip: The Sniper Rifle is a Hardmode, post-Plantera gun that has a 1/12 (8.33%) / 23/144 (15.97%) chance of being dropped by Skeleton Snipers in the Hardmode Dungeon. When used, it fires bullets at an extremely high damage and velocity, with a slow fire rate. It also converts Musket Balls and Tungsten Bullets into High Velocity Bullets, giving them the special effects but not affecting their damage. The Sniper Rifle has a base 29% critical strike chance, as opposed to the usual 4%. The Sniper Rifle also has a "zoom" ability activated by holding the ⚷ Open / Activate key (identical to that of the Binoculars and the Rifle Scope), allowing the screen to extend in the direction of the cursor. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Venus Magnum.name: Venus Magnum
Venus Magnum.tooltip: The Venus Magnum is a Hardmode gun that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Plantera. When used, it converts Musket Balls and Tungsten Bullets into High Velocity Bullets, giving them the special effects but not affecting their damage. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Crimson Rod.name: Crimson Rod
Crimson Rod.tooltip: The Crimson Rod is a pre-Hardmode magic weapon that launches a reddish rain cloud towards the cursor, where it rains damaging blood droplets downward onto enemies below. One cloud projectile can be placed at a time and it does not pass through terrain, instead stopping if it hits a surface before it reaches its target location. Once placed, the cloud will remain for five minutes, similarly to the Nimbus Rod's cloud. As well, its coverage area is rather narrow, making it difficult to use in open areas or against agile foes. The droplets can pierce one enemy, dissipating upon hitting a second one or a solid block. The Crimson Rod has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being obtained from destroying Crimson Hearts found in The Crimson or a 1/5 (20%) chance from Crimson Crates and Hematic Crates, which are fished in the Crimson. Its Corruption counterpart is the Vilethorn. Its best modifier is Demonic because it cannot get modifiers that affect knockback.
Crimson Rod.drops_summary: Crimson Crate (20%), Crimson Heart (20%), Hematic Crate (20%)

Crimtane Bar.name: Crimtane Bar
Crimtane Bar.tooltip: The Crimtane Bar is a pre-Hardmode bar. It is the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Demonite Bar.

Stynger.name: Stynger
Stynger.tooltip: The Stynger is a Hardmode, post-Golem launcher that consumes Stynger Bolts as ammunition. When used, it fires high-velocity Stynger Bolts that explode upon contact with enemies or blocks. The explosion additionally releases 2–5 shrapnel fragments that spread out in random directions and can also explode, each dealing the weapon's full damage and knockback. The main Stynger Bolt deals double damage (124 base damage), but not its explosion. The Stynger has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Golem. When dropped, the Stynger is always accompanied by 60 to 99 Stynger Bolts. Additional Stynger Bolts can be purchased from the Witch Doctor and Arms Dealer (75 Copper per bolt), if the Stynger is in the player's inventory. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Flower Pow.name: Flower Pow
Flower Pow.tooltip: The Flower Pow is a Hardmode flail that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Plantera. When thrown, it rapidly fires pink flower petals at nearby enemies, which deal 33.33% of the weapon's damage (43 base damage) and inflict 50% of its knockback (base knockback of 3.25 (Weak)).  Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Rainbow Gun.name: Rainbow Gun
Rainbow Gun.tooltip: The Rainbow Gun is a Hardmode, post-Plantera magic gun that fires a curving rainbow which persists for 40 seconds or until another rainbow is fired, and repeatedly deals damage to enemies that touch it. The rainbow can be also forced to dissipate instantly by using ⚷ Open / Activate on it while the player is within 15 tiles of it. The Rainbow Gun is always found in the Dungeon's Hallowed Chest, which can only be unlocked with a Hallowed Key after Plantera has been defeated. Its best modifier is Ruthless. The Mythical modifier provides the widest array of stat bonuses, but the only stats that improve damage output are damage and critical chance. Switching to a different weapon causes existing projectiles to use that weapon's base critical chance instead, meaning that the Rainbow Gun's DPS is optimized with the Ruthless modifier when used in the intended way.

Stynger Bolt.name: Stynger Bolt
Stynger Bolt.tooltip: The Stynger is a Hardmode, post-Golem launcher that consumes Stynger Bolts as ammunition. When used, it fires high-velocity Stynger Bolts that explode upon contact with enemies or blocks. The explosion additionally releases 2–5 shrapnel fragments that spread out in random directions and can also explode, each dealing the weapon's full damage and knockback. The main Stynger Bolt deals double damage (124 base damage), but not its explosion. The Stynger has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Golem. When dropped, the Stynger is always accompanied by 60 to 99 Stynger Bolts. Additional Stynger Bolts can be purchased from the Witch Doctor and Arms Dealer (75 Copper per bolt), if the Stynger is in the player's inventory. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Chlorophyte Jackhammer.name: Chlorophyte Jackhammer
Chlorophyte Jackhammer.tooltip: The Chlorophyte Jackhammer is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses hammer. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount. Mechanical tools can only have universal modifiers, because they cannot have their speed modified.

Teleporter.name: Teleporter
Teleporter.tooltip: The Teleporter is a travel mechanism purchased from the (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Mechanic / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Steampunker for 2 Gold 50 Silver. When two Teleporters are wired together with a triggering mechanism, they can exchange players, NPCs, and most enemies between them. Teleporting is always instantaneous, has no load time or cooldown, no Mana or coin cost, and no limit on distance. Unlike most furniture, Teleporters are foreground objects. They consist of three inseparable blocks which, like all block types, can individually be shaped with a hammer or actuated.

Flower of Frost.name: Flower of Frost
Flower of Frost.tooltip: The Flower of Frost is a Hardmode wand that has a 19/80 (23.75%) chance of being dropped by Ice Mimics. When used, it fires a non-piercing ball of frost that can bounce off blocks up to seven times, dissipating on its eighth impact. The ball of frost inflicts the Frostbite debuff for 8 seconds on hit. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Uzi.name: Uzi
Uzi.tooltip: The Uzi is a Hardmode gun that has a 1/100 (1%) chance of being dropped by Angry Trappers. When used, it rapidly fires bullets at a high velocity. It also converts Musket Balls and Tungsten Bullets(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) into High Velocity Bullets, giving them the special effects but not affecting their damage. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Magnet Sphere.name: Magnet Sphere
Magnet Sphere.tooltip: The Magnet Sphere is a Hardmode, post-Plantera spell book that has a 1/300 (0.33%) / 599/90,000 (0.6656%) chance of being dropped by Blue Armored Bones, Rusty Armored Bones, and Hell Armored Bones in the post-Plantera Dungeon. When used, it fires a slow-moving cyan sphere that rapidly fires instantaneous, non-piercing beams at the closest enemy as it travels. It passes through all enemies and bounces off solid blocks. The sphere dissipates after 15 seconds have passed, it has traveled 52 tiles, or when another sphere is fired. Its best modifier is Ruthless. The Mythical modifier provides the widest array of stat bonuses, but the only stats that improve damage output are damage and critical chance. Switching to a different weapon causes existing projectiles to use that weapon's base critical chance instead, meaning that the Magnet Sphere's DPS is optimized with the Ruthless modifier when used in the intended way.
Magnet Sphere.drops_summary: Blue Armored Bones (0.33%), Hell Armored Bones (0.33%), Rusty Armored Bones (0.33%)

Purple Stained Glass.name: Purple Stained Glass
Purple Stained Glass.tooltip: Stained Glass are a group of walls made from combining gems with Glass Walls. They work like the normal Glass Wall besides changing the color of the sunlight to match that of the stained glass. Multicolored Stained Glass causes sunlight to shift through the color spectrum in a similar manner to Rainbow Brick, although dimmer.

Skull.name: Skull
Skull.tooltip: The Skull is a rare vanity item that has a 1/500 (0.2%) chance of being dropped by Skeletons and Spore Skeletons(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), which are found in the Cavern layer, or a 1/2500 (0.04%) chance by those spawned from a Skeleton Statue or a Bone Skeleton Statue(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).
