Balla Hat.name: Balla Hat
Balla Hat.tooltip: The Balla Hat is a vanity item purchased from the Clothier after the Frost Legion has been defeated. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, it can only be purchased during the day, for 1 Gold. On the  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version, it can be obtained for free at any time.

Gangsta Hat.name: Gangsta Hat
Gangsta Hat.tooltip: The Gangsta Hat is a vanity item purchased from the Clothier after the Frost Legion has been defeated. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, it can only be purchased at night, for 1 Gold. On the  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version, it can be obtained for free at any time.

Sailor Hat.name: Sailor Hat
Sailor Hat.tooltip: The Sailor set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Sailor Hat, Sailor Shirt, and Sailor Pants. Each piece has a 1/500 (0.2%) chance of being dropped by Pirate Deckhands, Pirate Corsairs,  Pirate Deadeyes, and Pirate Crossbowers during the Pirate Invasion event. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Eye Patch.name: Eye Patch
Eye Patch.tooltip: The Eye Patch is a Hardmode vanity item. It has a 1/500 (0.2%) chance of being dropped by Pirate Deckhands, Pirate Corsairs, Pirate Deadeyes, and Pirate Crossbowers during the Pirate Invasion event.

Sailor Shirt.name: Sailor Shirt
Sailor Shirt.tooltip: The Sailor set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Sailor Hat, Sailor Shirt, and Sailor Pants. Each piece has a 1/500 (0.2%) chance of being dropped by Pirate Deckhands, Pirate Corsairs,  Pirate Deadeyes, and Pirate Crossbowers during the Pirate Invasion event. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Sailor Pants.name: Sailor Pants
Sailor Pants.tooltip: The Sailor set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Sailor Hat, Sailor Shirt, and Sailor Pants. Each piece has a 1/500 (0.2%) chance of being dropped by Pirate Deckhands, Pirate Corsairs,  Pirate Deadeyes, and Pirate Crossbowers during the Pirate Invasion event. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Skeletron Mask.name: Skeletron Mask
Skeletron Mask.tooltip: Masks are vanity items dropped by all non-event bosses, as well as those from the Old One's Army(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). They are worn in the social head slot. Each boss has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance to drop its own mask in all difficulties, with the following exceptions: The Skeletron Mask has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to drop from Skeletron's Treasure Bag. The Dark Mage Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 1) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Dark Mage. The Ogre Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 2) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Ogre.

Amethyst Robe.name: Amethyst Robe
Amethyst Robe.tooltip: The Amethyst Robe is an armor item that can be worn in the shirt slot. It is a gem robe and part of the Wizard set. The Amethyst Robe enchants gem staff projectiles to home in towards the nearest enemy. The Amethyst Staff instead receives a flat damage buff of 4.  Wearing the Wizard Hat alongside the Amethyst Robe provides a set bonus of +10% magic critical strike chance, whereas wearing a Magic Hat alongside it provides a set bonus of +60 mana. Any leg-slot equipment can be worn with these set bonuses remaining intact.

Topaz Robe.name: Topaz Robe
Topaz Robe.tooltip: The Topaz Robe is an armor item that can be worn in the shirt slot. It is a gem robe and part of the Wizard set. The Topaz Robe enchants gem staff projectiles to burst in a large area of effect when the projectile expires, doing 35% of the original knockback and damage. The Topaz Staff instead receives a flat damage buff of 4. Wearing the Wizard Hat alongside the Topaz Robe provides a set bonus of +10% magic critical strike chance, whereas wearing a Magic Hat alongside it provides a set bonus of +60 mana. Any leg-slot equipment can be worn with these set bonuses remaining intact.

Sapphire Robe.name: Sapphire Robe
Sapphire Robe.tooltip: The Sapphire Robe is an armor item that can be worn in the shirt slot. It is a gem robe and part of the Wizard set. The Sapphire Robe enchants gem staff projectiles to create two projectiles which move in a double-helix pattern, each dealing 60% damage. The Sapphire Staff instead receives a flat damage buff of 4, applied after the 60% damage multiplier. Wearing the Wizard Hat alongside the Sapphire Robe provides a set bonus of +10% magic critical strike chance, whereas wearing a Magic Hat alongside it provides a set bonus of +60 mana. Any leg-slot equipment can be worn with these set bonuses remaining intact.

Emerald Robe.name: Emerald Robe
Emerald Robe.tooltip: The Emerald Robe is an armor item that can be worn in the shirt slot. It is a gem robe and part of the Wizard set. The Emerald Robe enchants gem staff projectiles to stick to blocks, as well as increasing their pierce by 1. It also causes projectiles to be shot out much faster and then decelerate over time, eventually lingering in mid-air if they have not hit any blocks. The Emerald Staff instead receives a flat damage buff of 4.  Wearing the Wizard Hat alongside the Emerald Robe provides a set bonus of +10% magic critical strike chance, whereas wearing a Magic Hat alongside it provides a set bonus of +60 mana. Any leg-slot equipment can be worn with these set bonuses remaining intact.

Ruby Robe.name: Ruby Robe
Ruby Robe.tooltip: The Ruby Robe is an armor item that can be worn in the shirt slot. It is a gem robe and part of the Wizard set. When worn, the Ruby Robe enchants gem staff projectiles to spawn an additional projectile after a short delay at a cost of 50% less damage, leading to a net-neutral effect on damage per second. It also adds 4 Armor penetration to the attacks. The Ruby Staff instead receives a flat damage buff of 4, applied after the 50% damage multiplier. Wearing the Wizard Hat alongside the Ruby Robe provides a set bonus of +10% magic critical strike chance, whereas wearing a Magic Hat alongside it provides a set bonus of +60 mana. Any leg-slot equipment can be worn with these set bonuses remaining intact.

Diamond Robe.name: Diamond Robe
Diamond Robe.tooltip: The Diamond Robe is an armor item that can be worn in the shirt slot. It is a gem robe and part of the Wizard set. When worn, the Diamond Robe enchants gem staff projectiles to hit in a larger radius and pierce an additional enemy. The Diamond Staff instead receives a flat damage buff of 4. Wearing the Wizard Hat alongside the Diamond Robe provides a set bonus of +10% magic critical strike chance, whereas wearing a Magic Hat alongside it provides a set bonus of +60 mana. Any leg-slot equipment can be worn with these set bonuses remaining intact.

White Tuxedo Shirt.name: White Tuxedo Shirt
White Tuxedo Shirt.tooltip: The White Tuxedo set is a vanity set consisting of the White Tuxedo Shirt and the White Tuxedo Pants. It is purchased from the Clothier for 50 Gold (set), on the night of a Full Moon. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. The set exists on  Old-gen console and 3DS, but is unobtainable on these versions.

White Tuxedo Pants.name: White Tuxedo Pants
White Tuxedo Pants.tooltip: The White Tuxedo set is a vanity set consisting of the White Tuxedo Shirt and the White Tuxedo Pants. It is purchased from the Clothier for 50 Gold (set), on the night of a Full Moon. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. The set exists on  Old-gen console and 3DS, but is unobtainable on these versions.

Panic Necklace.name: Panic Necklace
Panic Necklace.tooltip: The Panic Necklace is an accessory, that, when equipped, grants the player the Panic! buff for 8 seconds when harmed by any source of damage besides fire blocks, increasing movement speed by 100%. The Panic Necklace has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being obtained from destroying Crimson Hearts found in The Crimson or a 1/5 (20%) chance from Crimson Crates and Hematic Crates, which are fished in the Crimson. It can furthermore be crafted.
Panic Necklace.drops_summary: Crimson Crate (20%), Crimson Heart (20%), Hematic Crate (20%)

Life Fruit.name: Life Fruit
Life Fruit.tooltip: The Life Fruit is a Hardmode plant and permanent booster item that grows on Jungle grass in any area within the Underground layer or below, and only after any mechanical boss has been defeated. Life Fruit grow 25% faster on average in Expert Mode. When used, a Life Fruit permanently increases the player's health capacity by 5 and restores the player's health by 5, turning one unit in the player's health bar golden. Life Fruit can only be used once a player has reached the 400 health cap from consuming Life Crystals. A total of 20 Life Fruit is required to reach the maximum 500 health capacity. Once this is reached, the player's health cannot be increased beyond 500, with the exception of the Lifeforce buff.

Lihzahrd Altar.name: Lihzahrd Altar
Lihzahrd Altar.tooltip: The Lihzahrd Altar is a furniture item used for summoning Golem with Lihzahrd Power Cells. Upon pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it, one Lihzahrd Power Cell is consumed from the player's inventory and Golem is instantly summoned. The Lihzahrd Altar is always found naturally placed in the final chamber of the Jungle Temple. Like Lihzahrd Bricks, the Lihzahrd Altar is impervious to explosions and can only be removed with the Picksaw, Laser Drill, or Luminite Pickaxes. Once picked up, it can be placed anywhere and can be used to summon Golem in any area at any time, as long as the world is in Hardmode with Plantera defeated.

Lihzahrd Power Cell.name: Lihzahrd Power Cell
Lihzahrd Power Cell.tooltip: The Lihzahrd Power Cell is a boss-summoning item used to summon Golem. It can only be used at the Lihzahrd Altar (located in the final chamber of the Jungle Temple), at any time, as long as the world is in Hardmode and Plantera has been defeated. Upon pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Lihzahrd Altar, one Lihzahrd Power Cell is consumed from the player's inventory and Golem is summoned. One Lihzahrd Power Cell is guaranteed to be found within each Lihzahrd Chest, and they additionally have a 1/50 (2%) chance of dropping from Lihzahrds and Flying Snakes, both of which spawn exclusively within the Jungle Temple.

Picksaw.name: Picksaw
Picksaw.tooltip: The Picksaw is a Hardmode pickaxe and axe that has a 1/4 (25%) / 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by Golem. It can mine all blocks. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Heat Ray.name: Heat Ray
Heat Ray.tooltip: The Heat Ray is a Hardmode magic gun that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Golem. When used, it fires yellow lasers that instantly travel their maximum distance. The lasers do not pierce enemies. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Staff of Earth.name: Staff of Earth
Staff of Earth.tooltip: The Staff of Earth is a Hardmode wand that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Golem. When used, it fires a Boulder that is affected by gravity, bounces off blocks and rolls on the ground, and can pierce enemies five times, before dissipating on the sixth hit. The Boulder's base damage and knockback depend on its velocity. The Staff of Earth also has a base 24% critical strike chance, as opposed to the usual 4%. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Golem Fist.name: Golem Fist
Golem Fist.tooltip: The Golem Fist is a Hardmode flail that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Golem. When used, it fires a large, high-velocity fist attached to a chain that retracts on impact with enemies or blocks, or after traveling for more than 31.25 tiles away from the player.. Upon hitting enemies or blocks, it creates a shockwave that deals 100% of the weapon's damage and knockback to nearby enemies if extended by more than 9.375 tiles. Both the Golem Fist and its shockwave have a 1/3 (33.33%) to inflict the Confused debuff for 1-2 seconds on hit. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Water Chest.name: Water Chest
Water Chest.tooltip: Water Chests are a type of Chest that can be found in pools of water greater than 250 tiles, most notably in the Ocean, but more rarely in any body of water, including water lakes anywhere in the Underground and Caverns layers, Surface lakes and very occasionally Floating Lakes. In addition to containing common chest loot based on where they are found, there are special items that can only be found in these chests, listed below.

Binoculars.name: Binoculars
Binoculars.tooltip: The Binoculars are a tool that can be held in order to shift the player's view based on the cursor location. They must be placed in the hotbar and selected. While highlighted in the hotbar, the screen view is scrolled a short distance away from the character, following the mouse pointer. The view becomes centered not on the player, but on a point almost halfway between the player and the cursor. The Binoculars have a 1/40 (2.5%) / 1/30 (3.33%) chance of being dropped by the Eye of Cthulhu.
Binoculars.drops_summary: Eye of Cthulhu (2.5%), Treasure Bag (Eye of Cthulhu) (3.33%)

Rifle Scope.name: Rifle Scope
Rifle Scope.tooltip: The Rifle Scope is a Hardmode, post-Plantera accessory. It grants the ability to increase view range while holding a gun by pressing and holding ⚷ Open / Activate and moving the cursor.  The Rifle Scope has a 1/12 (8.33%) / 23/144 (15.97%) chance of being dropped by Skeleton Snipers in the post-Plantera Dungeon.

Destroyer Emblem.name: Destroyer Emblem
Destroyer Emblem.tooltip: The Destroyer Emblem is a Hardmode, post-Golem accessory that gives the player 10% increased damage and 8% increased critical strike chance.

High Velocity Bullet.name: High Velocity Bullet
High Velocity Bullet.tooltip: The High Velocity Bullet is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss bullet. It is the bullet with the highest velocity. The High Velocity Bullet can hit up to 3 targets. The damage of the High Velocity Bullet decreases by 15% each time it hits a target. High Velocity Bullets are crafted with materials that can be purchased from NPCs. The combined cost of the crafting materials for 50 High Velocity Bullets is 9 Silver 50 Copper, which is 19 Copper per bullet. The cost of crafting 10,000 High Velocity Bullets is 19 Gold.

Jellyfish Necklace.name: Jellyfish Necklace
Jellyfish Necklace.tooltip: The Jellyfish Necklace is an accessory which has a 1/100 (1%) chance to drop from Pink, Blue, or Green Jellyfish in the Ocean and Underground or Cavern layer. In the  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version, the Jellyfish Necklace provides a faint pink glow when the player is submerged in water or honey. In the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, this glow is also provided out of liquids and its brightness is significantly increased when submerged.

Zombie Arm.name: Zombie Arm
Zombie Arm.tooltip: The Zombie Arm is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/250 (0.4%) chance of being dropped by Zombies, Frozen Zombies, and Raincoat Zombies. When held, it visually appears on the player. It will also randomly release visual Zombie gore when swung. Its best modifier is Legendary.

The Axe.name: The Axe
The Axe.tooltip: The Axe is a Hardmode hamaxe that has a 1/50 (2%) / 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped by Plantera. When swung, it produces an electric guitar sound that changes in tone depending on the distance from the cursor to the player.  Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Ice Sickle.name: Ice Sickle
Ice Sickle.tooltip: The Ice Sickle is a Hardmode broadsword that can be dropped with a 1/100 (1%) chance by Armored Vikings, Ice Elementals, Ice Tortoises, and Icy Mermen. When swung, it fires a spinning blue sickle projectile that deals 67% of the weapon's damage (33 base damage) and can pierce up to 4 enemies. The sickle gradually slows down after being fired, dissipating after traveling for 3 seconds. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Clothier Voodoo Doll.name: Clothier Voodoo Doll
Clothier Voodoo Doll.tooltip: The Clothier Voodoo Doll is a boss-summoning item used to summon Skeletron after it has been defeated. It has a 1/300 (0.33%) chance to drop from Angry Bones, Dark Casters, and Librarian Skeletons in the Dungeon. When equipped in an accessory slot (but not social slots), the Clothier Voodoo Doll allows the player, Fallen Stars, and other NPCs to harm and kill the Clothier. As long as the Clothier Voodoo Doll is equipped, the Clothier will summon Skeletron upon dying at night (7:30 PM to 4:30 AM). The Clothier can die by any means to summon Skeletron. Unlike the Guide Voodoo Doll, the Clothier Voodoo Doll is not destroyed upon use, and has no effect when dropped into lava. The Clothier Voodoo Doll cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Poison Staff.name: Poison Staff
Poison Staff.tooltip: The Poison Staff is a Hardmode wand that has a 1/40 (2.5%) chance of being dropped by Black Recluses. When used, it fires a burst of 3–4 Poison Fangs in a roughly 30° spread. Each projectile pierces two enemies and inflicts the Poisoned debuff for 30 seconds. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Slime Staff.name: Slime Staff
Slime Staff.tooltip: The Slime Staff is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Baby Slime minion. It bounces towards enemies, dealing contact damage. The Slime Staff's drop rate from most slimes and Slimed Zombies is 1/10000 (0.01%) / 1/7000 (0.0143%). Pinky has a greatly increased drop rate of 1/100 (1%) / 1/70 (1.4286%), and King Slime holds the greatest drop rate of 1/30 (3.3333%). Additionally, Sand Slimes have a drop rate of 1/8000 (0.0125%) / 1/5600 (0.0179%). The slimes which cannot drop the Slime Staff are: Shimmer, Golden, Lava, Dungeon, Umbrella, Hoppin' Jack, Corrupt, Queen Slime, Crimslime, Gastropod and Rainbow. Its best modifier is Fabled.
Slime Staff.drops_summary: Most slimes (0.01%), Pinky (1%), Sand Slime (0.013%), +2 more

Poison Dart.name: Poison Dart
Poison Dart.tooltip: The Poison Dart is a pre-Hardmode dart. It inflicts the Poisoned debuff on hit, which has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to last for 60 seconds, and a 2/3 (66.67%) chance to last for 30 seconds.

Eye Spring.name: Eye Spring
Eye Spring.tooltip: The Eye Spring is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns an Eyeball Spring that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Eyeball Spring spins its tentacles to catch up to the player. The Eye Spring has a 1/15 (6.67%) / 1/10 (10%) chance of being dropped by Eyezors.

Toy Sled.name: Toy Sled
Toy Sled.tooltip: The Toy Sled is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Snowman that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Baby Snowman rides in a toy sled to catch up to them. The Toy Sled has a 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped by Ice Mimics.

Book of Skulls.name: Book of Skulls
Book of Skulls.tooltip: The Book of Skulls is a pre-Hardmode spell book that has a 36/343 (10.5%) / 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by Skeletron. When used, it fires slow-moving skull projectiles which home in on enemies, can pierce twice before dissipating on the third hit, can pass through blocks, and emit a fair amount of light. Its best modifier is Mythical.

KO Cannon.name: KO Cannon
KO Cannon.tooltip: The KO Cannon is a Hardmode flail that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by Clowns. When used, it fires a boxing glove attached to the player via a chain. The glove retracts on contact with blocks or enemies, or after traveling 12 tiles. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Pirate Map.name: Pirate Map
Pirate Map.tooltip: The Pirate Map is a Hardmode event-summoning item used to summon a Pirate Invasion. The Pirate Map has a 1/100 (1%) chance of dropping from most enemies killed in the surface Ocean biome during Hardmode (see Notes for more details). In order for it to be used, at least one player must have 200 health or more.

Turtle Helmet.name: Turtle Helmet
Turtle Helmet.tooltip: Turtle armor is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses melee armor set consisting of the Turtle Helmet, Turtle Scale Mail, and Turtle Leggings. Crafting the full set requires a total of 54 Chlorophyte Bars (270 Chlorophyte Ore) and 3 Turtle Shells. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +65 defense +15% damage reduction +14% melee damage +12% melee critical strike chance +750 aggro Stronger Thorns effect upon taking contact damage, which inflicts 200% of the enemy's contact damage back at them and applies a knockback of 10 (Extremely strong). A visual turtle shell appears on the player's back.

Turtle Scale Mail.name: Turtle Scale Mail
Turtle Scale Mail.tooltip: Turtle armor is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses melee armor set consisting of the Turtle Helmet, Turtle Scale Mail, and Turtle Leggings. Crafting the full set requires a total of 54 Chlorophyte Bars (270 Chlorophyte Ore) and 3 Turtle Shells. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +65 defense +15% damage reduction +14% melee damage +12% melee critical strike chance +750 aggro Stronger Thorns effect upon taking contact damage, which inflicts 200% of the enemy's contact damage back at them and applies a knockback of 10 (Extremely strong). A visual turtle shell appears on the player's back.

Turtle Leggings.name: Turtle Leggings
Turtle Leggings.tooltip: Turtle armor is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses melee armor set consisting of the Turtle Helmet, Turtle Scale Mail, and Turtle Leggings. Crafting the full set requires a total of 54 Chlorophyte Bars (270 Chlorophyte Ore) and 3 Turtle Shells. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +65 defense +15% damage reduction +14% melee damage +12% melee critical strike chance +750 aggro Stronger Thorns effect upon taking contact damage, which inflicts 200% of the enemy's contact damage back at them and applies a knockback of 10 (Extremely strong). A visual turtle shell appears on the player's back.

Snowball Cannon.name: Snowball Cannon
Snowball Cannon.tooltip: The Snowball Cannon is a pre-Hardmode ranged weapon which uses Snowballs as ammunition. The Snowball Cannon has a 15.52% chance of being found inside Frozen Chests in the Ice biome, as well as a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being obtained from Frozen and Boreal Crates. Its best modifier is Unreal.
Snowball Cannon.drops_summary: Boreal Crate (16.67%), Frozen Chest (15.52%), Frozen Crate (16.67%)

Bone Pickaxe.name: Bone Pickaxe
Bone Pickaxe.tooltip: The Bone Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe that has a 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped by Undead Miners. It can mine blocks up to Demonite Ore, Crimtane Ore, and Obsidian. Upon hitting an enemy, it releases a non-piercing lobbed bone projectile that is affected by gravity, and deals 75% of the pickaxe's damage (6 base damage) and its full knockback. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Magic Quiver.name: Magic Quiver
Magic Quiver.tooltip: The Magic Quiver is a Hardmode accessory that boosts arrow- and Stake-firing weapons. It has a 1/40 (2.5%) chance of being dropped from Skeleton Archers. When equipped, it grants the following bonuses to arrows, Stakes, and the weapons that fire them: +10% damage, to both the ammo and the weapon +10% knockback, to the weapon only +120% velocity in total (does not fully affect certain projectiles; see Notes for details) +20% chance not to consume ammo

Magma Stone.name: Magma Stone
Magma Stone.tooltip: The Magma Stone is an accessory that causes the wearer's melee attacks to inflict the Hellfire debuff for up to 6 seconds on enemies. In PvP, only direct hits from melee weapons can inflict the Hellfire debuff, while melee projectiles instead inflict the On Fire! debuff; both debuffs last up to 6 seconds against other players. The Magma Stone also adds orange flame particle effects on the sprites of both the weapon and its projectiles, giving off light. It has a 1/50 (2%) chance to be dropped by Lava Bats and a 1/150 (0.67%) chance to be dropped by Hellbats in The Underworld. The duration of debuffs applied is random and depends on the type of attack as well as the target:

Obsidian Rose.name: Obsidian Rose
Obsidian Rose.tooltip: The Obsidian Rose is an accessory that reduces the base damage taken from lava from 80 to 35 and halves the duration of the On Fire! debuff inflicted by it from 7 / 14 / 17.5 seconds to 3.5 / 7 / 8.75 seconds. Additionally, equipping both Ash Wood armor and the Obsidian Rose (or its upgrades) provides immunity to lava damage and debuff. The Obsidian Rose has a 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped by Fire Imps, an enemy found in The Underworld.

Bananarang.name: Bananarang
Bananarang.tooltip: The Bananarang is a Hardmode boomerang that is dropped by the Clown during Blood Moon with a 1/10 (10%) chance. Unlike most boomerangs, it does not have to return to the player before being fired, with a maximum of ten Bananarangs that can be thrown out at one time. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Chain Knife.name: Chain Knife
Chain Knife.tooltip: The Chain Knife is a pre-Hardmode flail that has a 1/250 (0.4%) chance of being dropped by Cave Bats. When used, it fires a knife attached to a chain that can extend up to 9.4 tiles. On the I am error secret world seed, the Chain Knife has a chance of being obtained from any Chest. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Rod of Discord.name: Rod of Discord
Rod of Discord.tooltip: The Rod of Discord is a Hardmode tool that has a 1/500 (0.2%) / 1/400 (0.25%) chance of being dropped by Chaos Elementals. When used, it instantly teleports the player to the location of the cursor and inflicts the Chaos State debuff on the player for 6 seconds. Using the Rod of Discord while this debuff is active causes the player to lose health equal to 1/7 (14.29%) of their maximum health. It can be upgraded into the Rod of Harmony by throwing it into Shimmer after the Moon Lord has been defeated.

Death Sickle.name: Death Sickle
Death Sickle.tooltip: The Death Sickle is a Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/40 (2.5%) / 79/1600 (4.94%) chance of being dropped by Reapers during the Solar Eclipse event. When swung, it fires a spinning purple sickle that can pass through blocks. The sickles travel slowly for about 12 tiles before stopping in place, can pierce four enemies, or linger for three seconds before dissipating. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Turtle Shell.name: Turtle Shell
Turtle Shell.tooltip: The Turtle Shell is a Hardmode crafting material. It has a 1/12 (8.33%) chance of being dropped by Giant Tortoises, which spawn in the Jungle and Underground Jungle.

Tissue Sample.name: Tissue Sample
Tissue Sample.tooltip: The Tissue Sample is a pre-Hardmode crafting material dropped from Creepers (and the Brain of Cthulhu's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode). It is the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Shadow Scale.

Vertebra.name: Vertebra
Vertebra.tooltip: The Vertebra (Vertebrae (Old-gen console and 3DS versions)) is a crafting material that has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by Crimeras, Blood Crawlers, Face Monsters, Floaty Grosses.

Bloody Spine.name: Bloody Spine
Bloody Spine.tooltip: The Bloody Spine is a boss-summoning item that summons the Brain of Cthulhu when used. It can only be used in The Crimson or Underground Crimson, at any time.

Ichor.name: Ichor
Ichor.tooltip: Ichor is a Hardmode crafting material dropped by Ichor Stickers in the Underground Crimson and the Tainted Ghoul in the Crimson Underground Desert. It is also obtained from Hematic Crates. It is used to craft many Ichor-related items. It is the Crimson counterpart to the Corruption's Cursed Flame.

Ichor Torch.name: Ichor Torch
Ichor Torch.tooltip: Torches are furniture items that function as light sources when placed, held, or dropped (via the Throw button). Regular Torches can be found randomly in Chests and Pots, as a bonus drop from slimes, Torch Zombies, or purchased from the Merchant or Skeleton Merchant for 50 Copper each. Placing at least 101 Torches in close proximity below the surface layer in any biome will start the Torch God mini-event. Completing the event will grant the Torch God's Favor, which allows the player to automatically convert ordinary Torches to one of the biome types.

Ichor Arrow.name: Ichor Arrow
Ichor Arrow.tooltip: The Ichor Arrow is a Hardmode arrow. It inflicts the Ichor debuff for 10 seconds upon contact with enemies. Its Corruption counterpart is the Cursed Arrow.

Ichor Bullet.name: Ichor Bullet
Ichor Bullet.tooltip: The Ichor Bullet is a Hardmode bullet. It inflicts the Ichor debuff on hit for 10 seconds (15 seconds in PvP), decreasing the enemy's defense by 15. Combined with the bullet's base damage, it effectively deals a total of 21 damage. Its Corruption counterpart is the Cursed Bullet.

Golden Shower.name: Golden Shower
Golden Shower.tooltip: The Golden Shower is a Hardmode spell book that fires arcing golden ichor streams in quick succession. Each stream can hit up to 5 targets. The streams inflict the Ichor debuff for 10 seconds (15 seconds in PvP), which adds 15 armor penetration. The Golden Shower is the Crimson counterpart to the Corruption's Cursed Flames and the Hallow's Crystal Storm, all of which require a Spell Tome and ingredients exclusive to their underground biome counterparts. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Bunny Cannon.name: Bunny Cannon
Bunny Cannon.tooltip: The Bunny Cannon is a Hardmode placeable furniture/weapon. It can be purchased from the Pirate for 50 Gold when the Party Girl is present and one of the mechanical bosses has been defeated. Once placed, it can be fired by pressing ⚒ Use / Attack key on it with any Torch (which is not consumed). The Bunny Cannon fires an arcing Explosive Bunny projectile that bounces off blocks and pierces an infinite amount of targets. The projectile loses 50% of its momentum every time it bounces, and once it has lost most of its momentum, it will (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) transform into an Explosive Bunny critter / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) explode after several seconds. If the projectile lasts for 10 seconds without losing enough momentum, it will explode. The projectile and its explosion deal 350 classless damage and knockback of 8 (Very strong), and do not destroy blocks. The Bunny Cannon has a cooldown of 0.33 seconds before it can be fired again by using Torches, which is shared between all Bunny Cannons in the world. The angle of a placed Bunny Cannon can be adjusted by pressing ⚷ Open / Activate key on either side of the Bunny Cannon to rotate it in that direction,  or tapping the side of the Bunny Cannon. There are 9 possible orientations and it cannot fire downward, though the arcing trajectory of the Explosive Bunnies can be used to hit targets below the emplacement. Each rotation tilts the Bunny Cannon by one step (22.5°). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) The Bunny Cannon can also be triggered by Wire. Depending on where the wire is connected, it will either shoot an explosive bunny or rotate toward the side the Wire is on. When a Bunny Cannon is fired with this method, there is a cooldown of 1 minute 8 seconds before that specific Bunny Cannon can be fired again by wiring signal, and a cooldown of 7 seconds before any other Bunny Cannon in the world can be fired by wiring signal. Torches can be still used to fire Bunny Cannons during this cooldown. Explosive Bunny critters spawned by the cannon will disappear in a puff of smoke when attempting to capture it with Bug Net and deal no damage on death.

Explosive Bunny.name: Explosive Bunny
Explosive Bunny.tooltip: The Explosive Bunny is a critter that explodes upon death. Crafting it requires a Bunny, which must be caught with any Bug Net. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Explosive Bunnies can be released as a critter, though it will always be placed at the player's feet instead of at the cursor like with most other critters. Projectiles launched by the Bunny Cannon will also release an Explosive Bunny at the projectiles position after a short period, though they cannot be caught and their explosion deals no damage to enemies or the player. The Explosive Bunny's explosion deals 350 / 700 / 1050 damage to the player (175 damage to friendly NPCs, critters, and enemies) within a 8×8-tile area centered on it, but does not destroy tiles.

Vial of Venom.name: Vial of Venom
Vial of Venom.tooltip: The Vial of Venom is a Hardmode crafting material purchased from the Witch Doctor for 15 Silver each, after Plantera has been defeated.

Flask of Venom.name: Flask of Venom
Flask of Venom.tooltip: The Flask of Venom is a Hardmode, post-Plantera flask that causes melee weapons and whips to inflict the Acid Venom debuff on hit for 5–9 seconds, as well as the Potent Acid debuff for 1 second. Melee weapons that fire projectiles will also inflict the debuffs on enemies hit by the projectiles. The Flask of Venom cannot be used in conjunction with other flasks, and using it will remove any existing flask effects. Like all other flasks, the effect will not be canceled when the player dies.

Venom Arrow.name: Venom Arrow
Venom Arrow.tooltip: The Venom Arrow is a Hardmode, post-Plantera arrow. It has the highest base damage of all arrows and inflicts the Acid Venom debuff on hit for 10 seconds, as well as the Potent Acid debuff for 2 seconds.

Venom Bullet.name: Venom Bullet
Venom Bullet.tooltip: The Venom Bullet is a Hardmode, post-Plantera bullet. It creates a conical splash of venom upon impact that afflicts the target it struck, as well as those within the area, with the Potent Acid debuff for two seconds and Acid Venom for 10. Venom Bullets are crafted with materials that can be purchased from NPCs. The combined cost of the crafting materials for 50 Venom Bullets is 17 Silver 50 Copper, which is 35 Copper per bullet. The cost of crafting 10,000 Venom Bullets is 35 Gold.

Fire Gauntlet.name: Fire Gauntlet
Fire Gauntlet.tooltip: The Fire Gauntlet is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses accessory. While equipped, it grants the following effects: Enables autoswing for all melee weapons and whips +12% melee damage +12% melee speed ×2 knockback for melee weapons +10% size for melee weapons Causes melee weapons to inflict the Hellfire debuff on hit

Cog.name: Cog
Cog.tooltip: Cogs are Hardmode crafting materials and placeable blocks that are purchased from the Steampunker for 7 Silver each. They are used to make High Velocity Bullets, Liquid Sensors, and Steampunk furniture. When Cogs are placed together they will display animated machinery. Corners, lines, and junctions will never be animated, though blocks inside the group of Cogs and the left border will always be animated and other borders are sometimes animated with a 2/3 (66.67%) chance. Crafting all Steampunk furniture will require 159 () / 153 ( ) / 33 () Cogs.

Confetti.name: Confetti
Confetti.tooltip: Confetti is a crafting material used to make several festive items. It is purchased from the Party Girl for 2 Silver each, or dropped by Confetti Slimes.

Nanites.name: Nanites
Nanites.tooltip: Nanites are a Hardmode crafting material used solely for crafting items that inflict the Confused debuff. Nanites are purchased from the Cyborg for 15 Silver each.

Explosive Powder.name: Explosive Powder
Explosive Powder.tooltip: Explosive Powder is a Hardmode crafting material purchased from the Demolitionist for 12 Silver each, once the Wall of Flesh has been defeated. It is solely used to make Exploding Bullets, an ammo type with strong knockback.

Gold Dust.name: Gold Dust
Gold Dust.tooltip: Gold Dust is a Hardmode crafting material that is purchased from the Merchant for 17 Silver each. Its sole purpose is to craft the Flask of Gold and Golden Bullets, which both allow the player to inflict the Midas debuff.

Party Bullet.name: Party Bullet
Party Bullet.tooltip: The Party Bullet is a bullet that releases a visual cloud of confetti upon contact with enemies or blocks. Party Bullets are craftable with a Hardmode ingredient (see Crafting section below). Party Bullets can also be dropped from a Pigronata with a 1/9 (11.11%) chance; this is the only way to obtain Party Bullets pre-Hardmode. Party Bullets are crafted with materials that can be purchased from NPCs. The combined cost of the crafting materials for 50 Party Bullets is 4 Silver 50 Copper, which is 9 Copper per bullet. The cost of crafting 10,000 Party Bullets is 9 Gold.

Nano Bullet.name: Nano Bullet
Nano Bullet.tooltip: The Nano Bullet is a Hardmode, post-Plantera bullet. It inflicts the Confused debuff on hit for 1–3 seconds, reversing enemy movement to make them run away from the player rather than towards them. The fired Nano Bullets receive a 1.25× damage multiplier, which is applied to the total damage of gun and bullet, and after other damage bonuses. Nano Bullets can also bounce off blocks once, disippating upon hitting blocks for the second time. They bounce towards the direction of the nearest enemy within a 50-tile radius that has an unobstructed line of sight of to the bullet, but will only deal 66%  damage after bouncing. Nano Bullets are crafted with materials that can be purchased from NPCs. The combined cost of the crafting materials for 50 Nano Bullets is 17 Silver 50 Copper, which is 35 Copper per bullet. The cost of crafting 10,000 Nano Bullets is 35 Gold.

Exploding Bullet.name: Exploding Bullet
Exploding Bullet.tooltip: The Exploding Bullet is a Hardmode bullet. It explodes on impact with enemies or blocks, dealing damage and knockback to a single other enemy within an area. Exploding Bullets are crafted with materials that can be purchased from NPCs. The combined cost of the crafting materials for 50 Exploding Bullets is 14 Silver 50 Copper, which is 29 Copper per bullet. The cost of crafting 10,000 Exploding Bullets is 29 Gold.

Golden Bullet.name: Golden Bullet
Golden Bullet.tooltip: The Golden Bullet is a Hardmode bullet. It inflicts the Midas debuff on hit for 2 seconds, causing enemies to drop 10%-50% more coins when killed. Golden Bullets are crafted with materials that can be purchased from NPCs. The combined cost of the crafting materials for 50 Golden Bullets is 19 Silver 50 Copper, which is 39 Copper per bullet. The cost of crafting 10,000 Golden Bullets is 39 Gold.

Flask of Cursed Flames.name: Flask of Cursed Flames
Flask of Cursed Flames.tooltip: The Flask of Cursed Flames is a Hardmode flask that causes melee weapons and whips(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) to inflict the Cursed Inferno debuff on hit for 3–6 seconds, which deals 24 damage per second and increases knockback on targets. Melee weapons that fire projectiles will also inflict the debuff on enemies hit by the projectiles. The Flask of Cursed Flames cannot be used in conjunction with other flasks, and using it will remove any existing flask effects. Like all other flasks, the effect will not be canceled when the player dies.

Flask of Fire.name: Flask of Fire
Flask of Fire.tooltip: The Flask of Fire is a flask that causes melee weapons and whips(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) to inflict the On Fire! debuff for 3–6 seconds on enemies hit. Melee weapons that fire projectiles will also inflict the debuff on enemies hit by the projectiles. The Flask of Fire cannot be used in conjunction with other flasks, and using it will remove any existing flask effects. Like all other flasks, the effect will not be canceled when the player dies.

Flask of Gold.name: Flask of Gold
Flask of Gold.tooltip: The Flask of Gold is a Hardmode flask that causes melee weapons and whips(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) to inflict the Midas debuff for 2 seconds on enemies hit. Melee weapons that fire projectiles will also inflict the debuff on enemies hit by the projectiles. The Flask of Gold cannot be used in conjunction with other flasks, and using it will remove any existing flask effects. Like all other flasks, the effect will not be canceled when the player dies.

Flask of Ichor.name: Flask of Ichor
Flask of Ichor.tooltip: The Flask of Ichor is a Hardmode flask that causes melee weapons and whips(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) to inflict the Ichor debuff for 10–19 seconds on enemies hit. Melee weapons that fire projectiles will also inflict the debuff on enemies hit by the projectiles. The Flask of Ichor cannot be used in conjunction with other flasks, and using it will remove any existing flask effects. Like all other flasks, the effect will not be canceled when the player dies.

Flask of Nanites.name: Flask of Nanites
Flask of Nanites.tooltip: The Flask of Nanites is a Hardmode, post-Plantera flask that causes melee weapons and whips(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) to inflict the Confused debuff for 1–3 seconds on enemies hit. Melee weapons that fire projectiles will also inflict the debuff on enemies hit by the projectiles. It also grants a 1.05× damage multiplier to melee and whip attacks, which is applied after other damage bonuses. The Flask of Nanites cannot be used in conjunction with other flasks, and using it will remove any existing flask effects. Like all other flasks, the effect will not be canceled when the player dies.

Flask of Party.name: Flask of Party
Flask of Party.tooltip: The Flask of Party is a flask that causes melee weapons and whips(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) to create bursts of confetti when hitting enemies. The confetti is purely cosmetic and does not provide damage bonuses. Melee weapons that fire projectiles will also create confetti when the projectiles hit enemies. The Flask of Party cannot be used in conjunction with other flasks, and using it will remove any existing flask effects. Like all other flasks, the effect will not be canceled when the player dies.

Flask of Poison.name: Flask of Poison
Flask of Poison.tooltip: The Flask of Poison is a flask that causes melee weapons and whips(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) to inflict the Poisoned debuff for 5–9 seconds on enemies hit. Melee weapons that fire projectiles will also inflict the debuff on enemies hit by the projectiles. The Flask of Poison cannot be used in conjunction with other flasks, and using it will remove any existing flask effects. Like all other flasks, the effect will not be canceled when the player dies.

Eye of Cthulhu Trophy.name: Eye of Cthulhu Trophy
Eye of Cthulhu Trophy.tooltip: Trophies are decorative furniture items which usually have a 1/10 (10%) chance to be dropped from most bosses. While they can be considered the "boss version of banners", they are purely cosmetic and do not provide any bonuses. Some trophies can only be rewarded by the Angler for completing fishing quests. In total, there are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 33 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 24 trophies.

Blood Moon Rising.name: Blood Moon Rising
Blood Moon Rising.tooltip: Paintings are decorative furniture items that can be placed on background walls. Each one is a framed image that depicts a particular scene, usually Terraria-related. Their tooltips generally contain a person's name, intended to credit each painting's artist; although the names appear to be fictional, most of them correspond to known Terraria developers, artists, testing staff, and community members (see Trivia below). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions, the Magic Lantern, Spelunker Glowsticks, and Spelunker Flares. There are a total of 193 paintings, 25 of which are sold by the Painter, 7 by the Princess, 4 by the Golfer, 2 by the Zoologist, 2 by the Clothier, 1 by the Truffle, and 27 are randomly sold by the Traveling Merchant. 35 paintings can be found in Underground Cabins, another 14 in the Underground Desert Cabins, 26 in the Dungeon, 12 in The Underworld, 6 from Floating Islands, 5 obtained by fishing, 1 from the Jungle Temple, 5 randomly acquired from Goodie Bags, 8 dropped by Solar Eclipse enemies, 8 awarded randomly by the Angler for completing fishing quests, 1 from the Living Tree, and 4 dropped by enemies.

Wall Skeleton.name: Wall Skeleton
Wall Skeleton.tooltip: The Wall Skeleton is a Decorative Furniture item that can be placed on walls, similar to Paintings. Wall Skeletons can only be obtained by looting them from the Dungeon, where they only appear in areas backed by Slab Walls.

Hanging Skeleton.name: Hanging Skeleton
Hanging Skeleton.tooltip: The Hanging Skeleton is a decorative furniture item that can be placed on background walls. It can be found in the Dungeon, where they only appear in areas backed by Slab or Tile Walls.

Blue Slab Wall.name: Blue Slab Wall
Blue Slab Wall.tooltip: Dungeon Brick Walls are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Dungeon, considered unsafe. They drop as items when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting on  Desktop,  Console, and  Mobile. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player. There are a total of nine different variants (three variants in three colors), but each Dungeon can include only the three wall types matching that Dungeon's color. A single Dungeon will usually contain all three types in different areas; in each area, the faction flags found will correspond to the wall variant. Cursed Dungeon Brick Walls(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are items that place unsafe Dungeon Brick Walls. They are visually identical to their counterparts and are obtained via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

Blue Brick Platform.name: Blue Brick Platform
Blue Brick Platform.tooltip: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Brass Lantern.name: Brass Lantern
Brass Lantern.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. Blue Dungeon Chair.name: Blue Dungeon Chair
Blue Dungeon Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Blue Dungeon Table.name: Blue Dungeon Table
Blue Dungeon Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Blue Dungeon Work Bench.name: Blue Dungeon Work Bench
Blue Dungeon Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Blue Dungeon Candle.name: Blue Dungeon Candle
Blue Dungeon Candle.tooltip: Candles are a type of furniture and light source. Candles can only be placed on flat-surface items. Candles will produce light underwater if placed and can be toggled on and off with ⚷ Open / Activate and by mechanisms. Certain types of candles provide buffs or debuffs. The Water Candle is a special type of candle found in Dungeons which increases enemy spawn rates by 33% and the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50% when placed or held. The Peace Candle reduces spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%, in contrast to the Water Candle. The Shadow Candle(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns in the area. For Water Candles and Peace Candles, multiple candles cannot stack, even if one is placed and the other is held.

Blue Dungeon Door.name: Blue Dungeon Door
Blue Dungeon Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Blue Dungeon Bookcase.name: Blue Dungeon Bookcase
Blue Dungeon Bookcase.tooltip: Bookcases are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station used for the crafting of three Hardmode magic weapons (the Crystal Storm, Cursed Flames, and Golden Shower) as well as the Librarian furniture out of Librarian Blocks. Bookcases also fulfill a house's table requirement. There is a total of 65 types of Bookcases: 60 craftable Bookcases, and 5 looted from the environment: one from the Underworld, three from the Dungeon, and one from the Pirate Invasion. Some bookcases can also be found in Underground Cabins; their style follows the theme of the cabin where they are found.

Catacomb.name: Catacomb
Catacomb.tooltip: The Catacomb is a decorative item that can be placed on background walls in a manner similar to a painting. It resembles a rectangular pit in the wall with a skeleton resting inside. The Catacomb can appear with one of three different frame styles, and one of three different skeleton positions. Catacombs can be found on the walls deep within a Dungeon with tiled walls.

Dungeon Shelf.name: Dungeon Shelf
Dungeon Shelf.tooltip: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Skellington J Skellingsworth.name: Skellington J Skellingsworth
Skellington J Skellingsworth.tooltip: Paintings are decorative furniture items that can be placed on background walls. Each one is a framed image that depicts a particular scene, usually Terraria-related. Their tooltips generally contain a person's name, intended to credit each painting's artist; although the names appear to be fictional, most of them correspond to known Terraria developers, artists, testing staff, and community members (see Trivia below). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions, the Magic Lantern, Spelunker Glowsticks, and Spelunker Flares. There are a total of 193 paintings, 25 of which are sold by the Painter, 7 by the Princess, 4 by the Golfer, 2 by the Zoologist, 2 by the Clothier, 1 by the Truffle, and 27 are randomly sold by the Traveling Merchant. 35 paintings can be found in Underground Cabins, another 14 in the Underground Desert Cabins, 26 in the Dungeon, 12 in The Underworld, 6 from Floating Islands, 5 obtained by fishing, 1 from the Jungle Temple, 5 randomly acquired from Goodie Bags, 8 dropped by Solar Eclipse enemies, 8 awarded randomly by the Angler for completing fishing quests, 1 from the Living Tree, and 4 dropped by enemies.

Sunflowers.name: Sunflowers
Sunflowers.tooltip: The Sunflower is a large, tall plant which can be found growing naturally on grass, and can be broken with a pickaxe or drill, or by coming into contact with water. It cannot be grown from seeds like most other plants, but is instead placed fully-grown, either naturally upon world generation or by the player. It can also be purchased from the Dryad for 50 Silver each, while a Blood Moon is not occurring. Sunflowers can only be placed on regular, Hallowed, Jungle, or Ash grass, at any height. They cannot be placed on Corrupt grass, Crimson grass, Mushroom grass, bare Dirt Blocks, nor in Clay Pots or Planter Boxes. Sunflowers grant the Happy! buff to players in their vicinity, increasing their movement speed and reducing enemy spawns. Furthermore, they serve as a small barrier against the spread of the Corruption/Crimson and Hallow, negate some of the effects of the evil biomes, and help preventing Graveyard biomes from forming.

Beanie.name: Beanie
Beanie.tooltip: The Beanie is a vanity item purchased from the Clothier for 1 Gold, while living in the Snow biome.

Imbuing Station.name: Imbuing Station
Imbuing Station.tooltip: The Imbuing Station is a crafting station used to craft flasks. It is purchased from the Witch Doctor for 7 Gold.

Star in a Bottle.name: Star in a Bottle
Star in a Bottle.tooltip: The Star in a Bottle is a functional lantern that grants the Star in a Bottle buff, providing mana regeneration of 5 mana per second to all players within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles. Like other lanterns, the Star in a Bottle is a mechanism that can be toggled on or off if wired, though this does not affect the buff.

The Destroyer.name: The Destroyer
The Destroyer.tooltip: The Destroyer is a Hardmode mechanical boss that is essentially a more difficult version of the Eater of Worlds. Its segments share a single health pool, meaning individual segments cannot die. Each of The Destroyer's segments fires lasers at the player, and as they take damage, they launch Probes, independent flying enemies that fire lasers and can be killed individually. While The Destroyer is alive, its exclusive music The Destroyer will play. When Otherworldly music is enabled, the track Boss 2 (Otherworldly) will play instead.

Shadowbeam Staff.name: Shadowbeam Staff
Shadowbeam Staff.tooltip: The Shadowbeam Staff is a Hardmode, post-Plantera wand that has a 1/20 (5%) / 39/400 (9.75%) chance of being dropped by Necromancers in the Hardmode Dungeon. When used, it fires a purple beam that travels almost instantly to its maximum distance (112.5 tiles), bouncing off blocks on impact. The beam can pierce infinite enemies, but for each enemy hit, its damage is reduced by 10%. Each enemy can only be hit once. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Inferno Fork.name: Inferno Fork
Inferno Fork.tooltip: The Inferno Fork is a Hardmode, post-Plantera wand that has a 1/20 (5%) / 39/400 (9.75%) chance of being dropped by Diabolists in the Hardmode Dungeon. When used, it fires a fireball that causes a lingering explosion upon contact with an enemy or a block. The explosion hits repeatedly, dealing 75% of the weapon's damage (52 base damage). The fireball and the explosion also inflict the Hellfire debuff for 8–15 seconds. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Spectre Staff.name: Spectre Staff
Spectre Staff.tooltip: The Spectre Staff is a Hardmode, post-Plantera wand that has a 1/20 (5%) / 39/400 (9.75%) chance of being dropped by Ragged Casters in the Hardmode Dungeon.

Wooden Fence.name: Wooden Fence
Wooden Fence.tooltip: Fences are a type of safe wall that are visually thin with most of them having transparency to allow view of the background. The only fences that have no transparency to them are Palm Fence, Rich Mahogany Fence, and Shadewood Fence. Unlike most other safe walls, they allow for wild plants and trees to grow. The safe Grass Wall, Flower Wall, and Jungle Wall are functionally identical to fences. All fences are obtained by crafting, and the Wrought Iron Fence can also be found on certain designs of the Dungeon.

Lead Fence.name: Lead Fence
Lead Fence.tooltip: Fences are a type of safe wall that are visually thin with most of them having transparency to allow view of the background. The only fences that have no transparency to them are Palm Fence, Rich Mahogany Fence, and Shadewood Fence. Unlike most other safe walls, they allow for wild plants and trees to grow. The safe Grass Wall, Flower Wall, and Jungle Wall are functionally identical to fences. All fences are obtained by crafting, and the Wrought Iron Fence can also be found on certain designs of the Dungeon.

Bubble Machine.name: Bubble Machine
Bubble Machine.tooltip: The Bubble Machine is a novelty furniture mechanism purchased from the Party Girl for 4 Gold (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) during the day / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) at any time. When placed, it continuously produces bubbles. These bubbles are purely visual, have no functional effect, and can be produced infinitely at no cost. Each bubble is of a random size, and a random one of four possible colors: pink, purple, green, or blue. With no obstacles in the way, bubbles last for random durations. They will pop on contact with characters or foreground blocks. It can be activated and deactivated via wire, but is always on by default when first placed.

Bubble Wand.name: Bubble Wand
Bubble Wand.tooltip: The Bubble Wand is an auto-swing novelty item that produces rainbow-colored bubbles. The bubbles are purely visual, have no functional effect, and can be produced infinitely at no cost. The Bubble Wand is purchased from the Party Girl for 5 Gold. Each bubble is of a random size, and a random one of four possible colors: Pink, purple, green, or blue. With no obstacles in the way, bubbles last for random durations. They will pop on contact with characters or foreground blocks.

Marching Bones Banner.name: Marching Bones Banner
Marching Bones Banner.tooltip: Banners are decorative furniture items that can be placed on the underside of blocks. Many are found naturally-placed in various biomes. There are also (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) four / (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) six crafted banners (Red, Green, Blue, Yellow, (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Pink, White) using Silk. Banners can be hung off of blocks and off of platforms which are in (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) any position / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) their bottom position (after being struck three times with a hammer). Faction flags are banners found in the Dungeon. In post-Plantera worlds, the faction flags found hanging in a particular Dungeon area correspond to the background wall type (brick, slab, or tile), both of which signify the types of enemies that will spawn there. See Hardmode Dungeon for more info. There are a total of 25 decorative banners: 6 crafted, 6 faction flags, 3 Floating Island, 6 Underworld, 3 Pyramid, and 1 dropped from the Dark Mage during the Old One's Army event.

Obsidian Platform.name: Obsidian Platform
Obsidian Platform.tooltip: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Obsidian Door.name: Obsidian Door
Obsidian Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Obsidian Chair.name: Obsidian Chair
Obsidian Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Obsidian Table.name: Obsidian Table
Obsidian Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Obsidian Work Bench.name: Obsidian Work Bench
Obsidian Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Obsidian Vase.name: Obsidian Vase
Obsidian Vase.tooltip: Vases are non-craftable furniture items. They can be found either in the Dungeon or the Underworld and can be mined with any pickaxe or drill.

Obsidian Bookcase.name: Obsidian Bookcase
Obsidian Bookcase.tooltip: Bookcases are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station used for the crafting of three Hardmode magic weapons (the Crystal Storm, Cursed Flames, and Golden Shower) as well as the Librarian furniture out of Librarian Blocks. Bookcases also fulfill a house's table requirement. There is a total of 65 types of Bookcases: 60 craftable Bookcases, and 5 looted from the environment: one from the Underworld, three from the Dungeon, and one from the Pirate Invasion. Some bookcases can also be found in Underground Cabins; their style follows the theme of the cabin where they are found.

Blue Dungeon Bed.name: Blue Dungeon Bed
Blue Dungeon Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration. Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 craftable Beds and 5 that can be acquired from the environment. All Beds are functionally identical and differ only in appearance.

Waldo.name: Waldo
Waldo.tooltip: Paintings are decorative furniture items that can be placed on background walls. Each one is a framed image that depicts a particular scene, usually Terraria-related. Their tooltips generally contain a person's name, intended to credit each painting's artist; although the names appear to be fictional, most of them correspond to known Terraria developers, artists, testing staff, and community members (see Trivia below). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions, the Magic Lantern, Spelunker Glowsticks, and Spelunker Flares. There are a total of 193 paintings, 25 of which are sold by the Painter, 7 by the Princess, 4 by the Golfer, 2 by the Zoologist, 2 by the Clothier, 1 by the Truffle, and 27 are randomly sold by the Traveling Merchant. 35 paintings can be found in Underground Cabins, another 14 in the Underground Desert Cabins, 26 in the Dungeon, 12 in The Underworld, 6 from Floating Islands, 5 obtained by fishing, 1 from the Jungle Temple, 5 randomly acquired from Goodie Bags, 8 dropped by Solar Eclipse enemies, 8 awarded randomly by the Angler for completing fishing quests, 1 from the Living Tree, and 4 dropped by enemies.

Darkness.name: Darkness
Darkness.tooltip: Darkness is a debuff that decreases the player's light vision, which functions much like a reverse Night Owl buff, dimming rather than amplifying provided light. Visually, the debuff causes the player to gain a blue tint, (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and their eyes will appear to close for the debuff's duration. The debuff can prevented by equipping the Blindfold or its derivatives.

Their tooltips generally contain a person's name, intended to credit each painting's artist; although the names appear to be fictional, most of them correspond to known Terraria developers, artists, testing staff, and community members (see Trivia below). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions, the Magic Lantern, Spelunker Glowsticks, and Spelunker Flares. There are a total of 193 paintings, 25 of which are sold by the Painter, 7 by the Princess, 4 by the Golfer, 2 by the Zoologist, 2 by the Clothier, 1 by the Truffle, and 27 are randomly sold by the Traveling Merchant. 35 paintings can be found in Underground Cabins, another 14 in the Underground Desert Cabins, 26 in the Dungeon, 12 in The Underworld, 6 from Floating Islands, 5 obtained by fishing, 1 from the Jungle Temple, 5 randomly acquired from Goodie Bags, 8 dropped by Solar Eclipse enemies, 8 awarded randomly by the Angler for completing fishing quests, 1 from the Living Tree, and 4 dropped by enemies.

Spectre Hood.name: Spectre Hood
Spectre Hood.tooltip: Spectre armor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera magic armor set consisting of the Spectre Robe and Spectre Pants, as well as two different headpieces: the Spectre Hood and Spectre Mask, providing offensive and defensive bonuses respectively. Crafting a full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Spectre Bars (27 Ectoplasm and 270 Chlorophyte Ore). Crafting all four pieces requires a total of 66 Spectre Bars (33 Ectoplasm and 330 Chlorophyte Ore). The full set grants the following effects while equipped:

Spectre Robe.name: Spectre Robe
Spectre Robe.tooltip: Spectre armor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera magic armor set consisting of the Spectre Robe and Spectre Pants, as well as two different headpieces: the Spectre Hood and Spectre Mask, providing offensive and defensive bonuses respectively. Spectre Pickaxe.name: Spectre Pickaxe
Spectre Pickaxe.tooltip: The Spectre Pickaxe is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pickaxe. It can mine blocks up to Chlorophyte Ore. It also has a notably high range bonus of 3 blocks. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Spectre Hamaxe.name: Spectre Hamaxe
Spectre Hamaxe.tooltip: The Spectre Hamaxe is a Hardmode, post-Plantera hamaxe. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Ectoplasm.name: Ectoplasm
Ectoplasm.tooltip: Ectoplasm is a Hardmode, post-Plantera crafting material dropped from Dungeon Spirits in the Dungeon. Dungeon Spirits drop 1–2 Ectoplasm upon death.

Gothic Chair.name: Gothic Chair
Gothic Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Gothic Table.name: Gothic Table
Gothic Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Gothic Work Bench.name: Gothic Work Bench
Gothic Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Gothic Bookcase.name: Gothic Bookcase
Gothic Bookcase.tooltip: Bookcases are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station used for the crafting of three Hardmode magic weapons (the Crystal Storm, Cursed Flames, and Golden Shower) as well as the Librarian furniture out of Librarian Blocks. Bookcases also fulfill a house's table requirement. There is a total of 65 types of Bookcases: 60 craftable Bookcases, and 5 looted from the environment: one from the Underworld, three from the Dungeon, and one from the Pirate Invasion. Some bookcases can also be found in Underground Cabins; their style follows the theme of the cabin where they are found.

Paladin's Hammer.name: Paladin's Hammer
Paladin's Hammer.tooltip: The Paladin's Hammer is a Hardmode, post-Plantera broadsword that has a 1/15 (6.67%) / 29/225 (12.89%) chance of being dropped by Paladins in the Hardmode Dungeon. When used, it swings once before being thrown at a high velocity, piercing an infinite number of enemies, and returning to the player after traveling a certain distance or upon hitting solid blocks. Upon colliding with blocks after being thrown, it creates a huge shockwave that inflicts 175% of the weapon's knockback (base knockback of 15.75 (Insane)) to nearby enemies. Both the hammer and its shockwave inflict the Broken Armor debuff for 1.5 seconds to enemies and for 10–20 seconds to other players on PvP, which adds 20 armor penetration against enemies and halves the defense of players. The thrown hammer deals 133.3% of the weapon's damage (133 base damage) on its first hit. Afterwards, it deals 90% of the weapon's damage to the second enemy hit and then loses 10% damage on each subsequent hit, dealing 81% damage to the third enemy, 72.9% damage to the fourth enemy, and so on. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

SWAT Helmet.name: SWAT Helmet
SWAT Helmet.tooltip: The SWAT Helmet is a vanity item that has a 1/12 (8.33%) / 23/144 (15.97%) chance to drop from Tactical Skeletons in the post-Plantera Dungeon.

Bee Wings.name: Bee Wings
Bee Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Giant Harpy Feather.name: Giant Harpy Feather
Giant Harpy Feather.tooltip: The Giant Harpy Feather is a rare crafting material used solely to craft Harpy Wings. It has a 1/150 (0.67%) chance of being dropped by Harpies.

Bone Feather.name: Bone Feather
Bone Feather.tooltip: The Bone Feather is a rare Hardmode, post-Plantera crafting material used solely to craft Bone Wings. It has a 1/300 (0.33%) chance of being dropped by any Armored Bones variant (Blue, Rusty, or Hell Armored Bones) in the Dungeon after Plantera has been defeated.
Bone Feather.drops_summary: Blue Armored Bones (0.33%), Hell Armored Bones (0.33%), Rusty Armored Bones (0.33%)

Fire Feather.name: Fire Feather
Fire Feather.tooltip: The Fire Feather is a Hardmode crafting material used solely to craft the Flame Wings. It has a (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 1/50 (2%) / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 1/75 (1.33%) chance of being dropped by Red Devils in The Underworld after defeating any mechanical boss.

Ice Feather.name: Ice Feather
Ice Feather.tooltip: The Ice Feather is a Hardmode crafting material used solely to craft Frozen Wings. The Ice Feather has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by Ice Golems during a Blizzard in the Snow biome.

Broken Bat Wing.name: Broken Bat Wing
Broken Bat Wing.tooltip: The Broken Bat Wing is a rare Hardmode crafting material used solely to craft Bat Wings. It has a 1/40 (2.5%) chance of being dropped by Vampires during a Solar Eclipse.

Tattered Bee Wing.name: Tattered Bee Wing
Tattered Bee Wing.tooltip: The Tattered Bee Wing is a rare Hardmode crafting material dropped by Moss Hornets with a (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 1/100 (1%) / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 1/150 (0.67%) chance. It is used solely to craft Bee Wings. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, at least one mechanical boss must be defeated before it will drop.

Large Amethyst.name: Large Amethyst
Large Amethyst.tooltip: Large Gems are items designed for the PvP game Capture the Gem, and are dropped when the player dies, even if they are in Classic or Softcore mode. With each different Large Gem that is held or carried in the player's inventory, a hologram of it appears above the player's head. If two or more different Large Gems are carried, their holograms will revolve in a circular pattern above the player's head. They are immediately deleted if placed in a player's trash slot. Large Gems can be placed into a Gem Lock to function as a key. This is primarily used in making adventure maps. Each Large Gem can also be combined with a Minecart at any Anvil to produce a Gem Minecart. The Gem Minecarts are mechanically identical to the regular Minecart, but are aesthetically representative of their Gem type, and sparkle.
