Jungle Chest.name: Jungle Chest
Jungle Chest.tooltip: Biome Chests are Hardmode Chests found within the Dungeon. Each contains one specific rare, powerful weapon, in addition to other miscellaneous items. While Biome Chests are placed during world creation, they are initially locked and can only be opened with an appropriate Biome Key, which will only become available in Hardmode. Only five Biome Chests (one of each type) will spawn in a particular world. Each represents a biome found in the current world. There are six types of Biome Chests in total, though a world will only contain one evil biome chest, a Crimson or Corruption variant, depending on which of those biomes the world contains. In order to open a Biome Chest, the following steps are required to take: Defeat Plantera for the first time to lift the curse from Biome Keys, allowing them to be used. As long as Plantera has not been killed, Biome Keys display the tooltip "It has been cursed by a powerful Jungle creature". Obtain the appropriate Biome Key by killing enemies within their respective biome. Return to the Dungeon and find the appropriate Chest for the key that was obtained.

Jungle Key.name: Jungle Key
Jungle Key.tooltip: Biome Keys are Hardmode items used to open the Biome Chests in the Dungeon. Opening a Chest consumes the key. Though unusable until Plantera is defeated, they can be dropped at any time during Hardmode. Each key has a 1/2500 (0.04%) chance of dropping from an enemy in the key's respective biome. Any enemy in the biome that drops coins, except Meteor Heads, when killed has a chance of dropping a key, not just biome-exclusive enemies. Additionally, enemies in hybrid biomes have a chance to drop any key from their composite biomes. The type of key is determined by which biome the player currently is in, not the enemy killed. Any Biome Key dropped prior to defeating Plantera will display the tooltip “It has been cursed by a powerful Jungle creature” and will be unable to open its respective chest until Plantera is defeated, although they are usable in other worlds that have Plantera defeated already.

Though unusable until Plantera is defeated, they can be dropped at any time during Hardmode. Each key has a 1/2500 (0.04%) chance of dropping from an enemy in the key's respective biome. Any enemy in the biome that drops coins, except Meteor Heads, when killed has a chance of dropping a key, not just biome-exclusive enemies. Additionally, enemies in hybrid biomes have a chance to drop any key from their composite biomes. The type of key is determined by which biome the player currently is in, not the enemy killed. Any Biome Key dropped prior to defeating Plantera will display the tooltip “It has been cursed by a powerful Jungle creature” and will be unable to open its respective chest until Plantera is defeated, although they are usable in other worlds that have Plantera defeated already.

Imp Face.name: Imp Face
Imp Face.tooltip: Paintings are decorative furniture items that can be placed on background walls. Each one is a framed image that depicts a particular scene, usually Terraria-related. Their tooltips generally contain a person's name, intended to credit each painting's artist; although the names appear to be fictional, most of them correspond to known Terraria developers, artists, testing staff, and community members (see Trivia below). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions, the Magic Lantern, Spelunker Glowsticks, and Spelunker Flares. There are a total of 193 paintings, 25 of which are sold by the Painter, 7 by the Princess, 4 by the Golfer, 2 by the Zoologist, 2 by the Clothier, 1 by the Truffle, and 27 are randomly sold by the Traveling Merchant. 35 paintings can be found in Underground Cabins, another 14 in the Underground Desert Cabins, 26 in the Dungeon, 12 in The Underworld, 6 from Floating Islands, 5 obtained by fishing, 1 from the Jungle Temple, 5 randomly acquired from Goodie Bags, 8 dropped by Solar Eclipse enemies, 8 awarded randomly by the Angler for completing fishing quests, 1 from the Living Tree, and 4 dropped by enemies.

Spectre Paintbrush.name: Spectre Paintbrush
Spectre Paintbrush.tooltip: The Spectre Paintbrush is a Hardmode tool which is used to apply paint to tiles, much like the regular Paintbrush sold by the Painter. The advantage over its predecessor is the Spectre Paintbrush's increased range of +3 tiles. The Spectre Paintbrush cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Spectre Paint Roller.name: Spectre Paint Roller
Spectre Paint Roller.tooltip: The Spectre Paint Roller is a Hardmode tool which is used to paint walls, much like the regular Paint Roller sold by the Painter. The advantage over its predecessor is the Spectre Paint Roller's increased range of +3 tiles. The Spectre Paint Roller cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Spectre Paint Scraper.name: Spectre Paint Scraper
Spectre Paint Scraper.tooltip: The Spectre Paint Scraper is a Hardmode tool which is used to remove paint off tiles and walls, much like the regular Paint Scraper sold by the Painter. The advantage over its predecessor is the Spectre Paint Scraper's increased range of +3 tiles. Paint removed by a scraper can never be recovered. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Like the Paint Scraper, the Spectre Paint Scraper can also collect moss. The Spectre Paint Scraper cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Shroomite Headgear.name: Shroomite Headgear
Shroomite Headgear.tooltip: Shroomite armor is a Hardmode , post- Plantera ranged armor set consisting of the Shroomite Breastplate and Shroomite Leggings , as well as three different headpieces: the Shroomite Headgear , Shroomite Mask , and Shroomite Helmet , providing bonuses for ranged weapons using a specific type of ammunition . Crafting the full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Shroomite Bars (810 Glowing Mushrooms and 270 Chlorophyte Ore ). Crafting all five pieces requires a total of 78 Shroomite Bars (1170 Glowing Mushrooms and 390 Chlorophyte Ore).

Autohammer.tooltip: The Autohammer is a Hardmode crafting station used to craft Shroomite Bars as well as Mini Nuke I and II. It can be purchased from the Truffle for 1 Platinum after Plantera has been defeated.

Shroomite Bar.name: Shroomite Bar
Shroomite Bar.tooltip: The Shroomite Bar is a Hardmode, post-Plantera bar.

S.D.M.G..name: S.D.M.G.
S.D.M.G..tooltip: The S.D.M.G. (Space Dolphin Machine Gun) is a Hardmode gun that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord. When used, it very rapidly fires bullets in a small spread. It also has a 66% chance not to consume ammunition. The S.D.M.G. has a base 14% critical strike chance, as opposed to the usual 4%. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Cenx's Tiara.name: Cenx's Tiara
Cenx's Tiara.tooltip: Cenx's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime 's). It is one of two vanity sets made for Cenx , the Creative Director on Terraria . Equipping the full set produces pink glowing particles when the player is near a light source. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Vampire Knives.name: Vampire Knives
Vampire Knives.tooltip: The Vampire Knives are a Hardmode, post-Plantera melee weapon. When used, it rapidly fires a spread of 4–8 red knife projectiles. Upon hitting an enemy, each knife causes a lifesteal effect that heals the player for 7.5% of the damage dealt (rounded down), signified by a red beam connecting to the player. The knives will eventually decrease in damage and fade after traveling a certain distance. The Vampire Knives are always found in the Dungeon's Crimson Chest, which can only be unlocked with a Crimson Key after Plantera has been defeated. Their best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Broken Hero Sword.name: Broken Hero Sword
Broken Hero Sword.tooltip: The Broken Hero Sword is a Hardmode, post-Plantera crafting material that has a 1/4 (25%) / 7/16 (43.75%) chance of being dropped by Mothrons.

Scourge of the Corruptor.name: Scourge of the Corruptor
Scourge of the Corruptor.tooltip: The Scourge of the Corruptor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera melee weapon. When used, it fires an Eater's Bite, a fast javelin-like projectile, that splits into weaker Tiny Eater projectiles upon contact with enemies or blocks. Tiny Eaters home in on enemies and bounce up to five times before dissipating. The Scourge of the Corruptor is always found in the Dungeon's Corruption Chest, which can only be unlocked with a Corruption Key after Plantera has been defeated. Its Crimson counterpart are the Vampire Knives. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Staff of the Frost Hydra.name: Staff of the Frost Hydra
Staff of the Frost Hydra.tooltip: The Staff of the Frost Hydra is a Hardmode, post-Plantera summon weapon that summons the Frost Hydra sentry. It fires Frost Blasts towards enemies, which pierce twice and inflict the Frostbite debuff. The Staff of the Frost Hydra is always found in the Dungeon's Ice Chest, which can only be unlocked with a Frozen Key after Plantera has been defeated. Its best modifier is Fabled. However, if the player's summon damage bonuses reach 164% (including whip bonuses) or 64% (excluding whip bonuses), the best modifier becomes Ruthless.

Sweetheart Necklace.name: Sweetheart Necklace
Sweetheart Necklace.tooltip: The Sweetheart Necklace is an accessory which releases a concentrated burst of bees and grants the player the Panic! and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Honey buffs when damaged, increasing movement speed by 100% for (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 8 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 5 seconds and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) health regeneration for 5 seconds.

Flurry Boots.name: Flurry Boots
Flurry Boots.tooltip: The Flurry Boots are a pre-Hardmode accessory that can be found in Frozen Chests in the Ice biome, as well as in Frozen(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Boreal Crates(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). While equipped, they grant the ability to sprint, allowing the player to reach maximum running speed faster, and they increase the player's maximum movement speed to 31 mph (22.73 tiles/second). The player will leave behind a visual trail of dust clouds as they sprint. The Hermes Boots, Flurry Boots, and Sailfish Boots(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) have the same functionality, and their effects do not stack with each other.
Flurry Boots.drops_summary: Boreal Crate (16.67%), Frozen Chest (15.52%), Frozen Crate (16.67%)

D-Town's Helmet.name: D-Town's Helmet
D-Town's Helmet.tooltip: D-Town's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). D-Town's Wings.name: D-Town's Wings
D-Town's Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Bubblegum Block Wall.name: Bubblegum Block Wall

Titanstone Block Wall.name: Titanstone Block Wall

Magic Cuffs.name: Magic Cuffs
Magic Cuffs.tooltip: The Magic Cuffs are a pre-Hardmode accessory that grant the following effects while equipped: +2 defense +40 maximum mana Restores mana when the player takes damage. Mana restored is equal to the damage of the attack before factoring defense and damage reduction.

Music Box (Snow).name: Music Box (Snow)
Music Box (Snow).tooltip: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End), which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 Gold after defeating the Moon Lord. A recorded Music Box can be played back in one of two ways: Equipping it as an accessory. Placing it as furniture and activating it, either by the ⚷ Open / Activate button or with wires. Recorded Music Boxes can be reverted into blank ones through Shimmer transmutation. There are 101 different Music Boxes available.

Butterfly Dust.name: Butterfly Dust
Butterfly Dust.tooltip: Butterfly Dust is a rare Hardmode crafting material used solely to craft Butterfly Wings. It has a 1/2 (50%) chance of being dropped by Moths in the Underground Jungle. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, at least one mechanical boss must be defeated before it will drop.

Ankh Charm.name: Ankh Charm
Ankh Charm.tooltip: The Ankh Charm is a Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the following debuffs:

Ankh Shield.name: Ankh Shield
Ankh Shield.tooltip: The Ankh Shield is a Hardmode shield and immunity accessory that grants the following effects while equipped: +5 defense Immunity to knockback Immunity to the following debuffs:

Blue Flare.name: Blue Flare
Blue Flare.tooltip: Flares are a type of ammunition used solely by the Flare Gun. When fired, they travel in a slight arc and stick to blocks, similar to Sticky Glowsticks, but have greater velocity and range. They emit low-level tinted light that lasts for 10 minutes. Flares work in liquids, although they bounce off Shimmer. Flares cannot be recovered once they burn out. All types of Flares (except the Cursed Flare) inflict the On Fire! debuff. There is a 2/3 (66.67%) chance that the debuff will last 5 seconds, and a 1/3 (33.33%) chance that it will last 10 seconds.

Angler Fish Banner.name: Angler Fish Banner
Angler Fish Banner.tooltip: Enemy banners are functional furniture items that can be placed on the underside of blocks and platforms. They are obtained by killing most enemies and a few critters. When placed, enemy banners provide a Banner buff to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the banner. The buff grants players +50%/+100% damage inflicted with all damage to the corresponding enemy and −25%/−50% damage taken from attacks by the enemy. The banners of Old One's Army enemies will apply a weaker banner buff to the respective enemy, granting the players +10%/+20% damage inflicted and −8.33% / −16.67% damage taken. Multiple banners of the same type will not grant stacked buffs. Multiple different banner types in the vicinity will, however, all take effect and consolidate into a single buff icon. There are a total of 286 obtainable enemy banners: 115 in pre-Hardmode, 171 in Hardmode. Out of these, 118 belong to event enemies (28 in pre-Hardmode and 90 in Hardmode). In addition, there are 6 unobtainable enemy banners.

Glass Platform.name: Glass Platform
Glass Platform.tooltip: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Glass Chair.name: Glass Chair
Glass Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Golden Chair.name: Golden Chair
Golden Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Golden Toilet.name: Golden Toilet
Golden Toilet.tooltip: Toilets are furniture items which can be placed on the ground. They are functionally similar to chairs, and fulfill a house's chair requirement. Similarly to chairs, Toilets can be sat on by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Having any tier of Well Fed active while sitting on a Toilet allows the production of Poo. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Toilet will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Toilets act as mechanisms that can be activated via wire, which makes them appear to explosively eject sewage. This effect is purely a novelty visual. Ejected sewage on the ground fades after a few seconds. There are 67 Toilets.

Glass Door.name: Glass Door
Glass Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Steampunk Door.name: Steampunk Door
Steampunk Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. Hellstone, Spectre, and Shroomite Bars are exceptions that require a secondary material in addition. Hallowed Bars are not crafted but are instead dropped by the mechanical bosses. Many bars can also be looted from chests and crates. All bars that have a counterpart can be converted to their counterpart using the Chlorophyte Extractinator.

Glass Bed.name: Glass Bed
Glass Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration. Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it. Living Wood Wall.name: Living Wood Wall
Living Wood Wall.tooltip: The Living Wood Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Living Trees, considered unsafe, where it does not drop as an item when destroyed. It can also be found naturally generated in Living Mahogany Trees, considered safe, where it does drop as an item when destroyed. It can also be obtained via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player. Unsafe Living Wood Walls only allow Goldfish, Snails, Mice, Worms, Bunnies, and Gnomes to spawn in front of them. This effect is not applied in Remix and Zenith worlds. The Overgrown Living Wood Wall is an item that places an unsafe Living Wood Wall. It is visually identical and is obtained by throwing a Living Wood Wall into Shimmer.

Fart in a Jar.name: Fart in a Jar
Fart in a Jar.tooltip: The Fart in a Jar is an accessory that allows the player to perform a double jump, accompanied by a farting sound effect. The Fart jump goes 10.5 tiles into the air, totalling 16.5 tiles when put together with the first jump.

Candy Apple.name: Candy Apple
Candy Apple.tooltip: Hearts (or Candy Apples during Halloween and Candy Canes during Christmas) are common power-ups which can be dropped by slain enemies, broken pots, or as a bonus drop from slimes. Enemies and pots will only drop Hearts when the closest player does not have full health. They are not inventory items, but are instead instantly consumed and restore 20 health. They emit a faint red light. The drop rate of Hearts from enemies is linked to that of Stars. If the closest player is below full health but has full mana, then the chance to drop a Heart is 1/12 (8.33%). If they are below full health and full mana, however, then Stars take priority and the chance to drop a Heart is reduced to 1/24 (4.17%). For the drop rate of Hearts from pots, see Pot § Upon breaking. It is also possible to spawn Hearts (and their seasonal counterparts) with a Heart Statue. Hearts can be collected within a range of 2.625 tiles, which can be increased with a Heartreach Potion to 18.25 tiles.

Soul Cake.name: Soul Cake
Soul Cake.tooltip: Stars (or Soul Cakes during Halloween and Sugar Plums during Christmas) are common power-ups which can be dropped by any enemy with a chance of 13/24 (54.17%), as long as the closest player does not have full mana. They are not inventory items, but are instead instantly consumed, restoring 100 mana and providing the Mana Surge buff, which increases magic damage by up to 20% for a brief duration. It is also possible to spawn Stars (and their seasonal counterparts) with a Star Statue. Stars can be collected within a range of 2.625 tiles, which can be increased with a Celestial Magnet (and its upgrades) to 21.375 tiles.

When used, it rapidly fires Candy Corn shots that pierce up to two enemies and ricochet up to four times, dissipating on their fifth impact or upon hitting a third enemy. The projectiles are affected by gravity. The Candy Corn Rifle also has a base 10% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%, and has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance not to consume ammunition. The Candy Corn Rifle is dropped by the Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.5–12.5% (6.25–12.5%) chance depending on the current wave. When dropped, the Candy Corn Rifle is always accompanied by 50 to 100 Candy Corn. Additional Candy Corn can also be bought from the Arms Dealer for 5 Copper each if the Candy Corn Rifle is in the player's inventory. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Candy Corn.name: Candy Corn
Candy Corn.tooltip: The Candy Corn Rifle is a Hardmode, post-Plantera gun that consumes Candy Corn as ammunition. When used, it rapidly fires Candy Corn shots that pierce up to two enemies and ricochet up to four times, dissipating on their fifth impact or upon hitting a third enemy. The projectiles are affected by gravity. The Candy Corn Rifle also has a base 10% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%, and has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance not to consume ammunition. The Candy Corn Rifle is dropped by the Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.5–12.5% (6.25–12.5%) chance depending on the current wave. When dropped, the Candy Corn Rifle is always accompanied by 50 to 100 Candy Corn. Additional Candy Corn can also be bought from the Arms Dealer for 5 Copper each if the Candy Corn Rifle is in the player's inventory. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Jack 'O Lantern Launcher.name: Jack 'O Lantern Launcher
Jack 'O Lantern Launcher.tooltip: The Jack 'O Lantern Launcher is a Hardmode, post-Plantera launcher that consumes Explosive Jack 'O Lanterns as ammunition. Explosive Jack 'O Lanterns bounce off blocks before exploding upon contact with an enemy or after 5 seconds. The Jack 'O Lantern Launcher has a base 10% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. The Jack 'O Lantern Launcher is dropped by the Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.5–12.5% (6.25–12.5%) chance depending on the current wave. When dropped, the Jack 'O Lantern Launcher is always accompanied by 25 to 50 Explosive Jack 'O Lanterns. Explosive Jack 'O Lanterns can also be bought from the Arms Dealer for 15 Copper each if the Jack 'O Lantern Launcher is in the player's inventory. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Explosive Jack 'O Lantern.name: Explosive Jack 'O Lantern
Explosive Jack 'O Lantern.tooltip: The Jack 'O Lantern Launcher is a Hardmode, post-Plantera launcher that consumes Explosive Jack 'O Lanterns as ammunition. Explosive Jack 'O Lanterns bounce off blocks before exploding upon contact with an enemy or after 5 seconds. The Jack 'O Lantern Launcher has a base 10% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. The Jack 'O Lantern Launcher is dropped by the Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.5–12.5% (6.25–12.5%) chance depending on the current wave. When dropped, the Jack 'O Lantern Launcher is always accompanied by 25 to 50 Explosive Jack 'O Lanterns. Explosive Jack 'O Lanterns can also be bought from the Arms Dealer for 15 Copper each if the Jack 'O Lantern Launcher is in the player's inventory. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Sickle.name: Sickle
Sickle.tooltip: The Sickle is a tool that produces Hay blocks when used to cut wild grass plants and sea oats. The collected Hay can be used for building purposes and crafted into Target Dummies and Hay Walls. The Sickle is purchased from the Merchant for 60 Silver. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Pumpkin Pie.name: Pumpkin Pie
Pumpkin Pie.tooltip: Pumpkin Pie is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().

Scarecrow Hat.name: Scarecrow Hat
Scarecrow Hat.tooltip: The Scarecrow set is a vanity set which consists of the Scarecrow Hat, the Scarecrow Shirt and the Scarecrow Pants. All three parts of the set are dropped by Scarecrows during the Pumpkin Moon event, each with a 0.37%–3.33% (0.56%–3.33%) chance depending on the current wave. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Scarecrow Shirt.name: Scarecrow Shirt
Scarecrow Shirt.tooltip: The Scarecrow set is a vanity set which consists of the Scarecrow Hat, the Scarecrow Shirt and the Scarecrow Pants. All three parts of the set are dropped by Scarecrows during the Pumpkin Moon event, each with a 0.37%–3.33% (0.56%–3.33%) chance depending on the current wave. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Scarecrow Pants.name: Scarecrow Pants
Scarecrow Pants.tooltip: The Scarecrow set is a vanity set which consists of the Scarecrow Hat, the Scarecrow Shirt and the Scarecrow Pants. All three parts of the set are dropped by Scarecrows during the Pumpkin Moon event, each with a 0.37%–3.33% (0.56%–3.33%) chance depending on the current wave. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Cauldron.name: Cauldron
Cauldron.tooltip: The Cooking Pot is a crafting station that is solely used to turn various items into food, consumables that induce the Well Fed, Plenty Satisfied and Exquisitely Stuffed buffs. Such food material include the Bowl of Soup, Cooked Fish, Cooked Shrimp, and Grub Soup. The Cauldron is the Halloween-themed variant of the Cooking Pot that is functionally identical in every way, except for its animated sprite and the small amount of light it emits. Unlike the Cooking Pot, the Cauldron cannot be crafted, and can only be purchased from the Witch Doctor for 1 Gold 50 Silver during Halloween.

Pumpkin Chair.name: Pumpkin Chair
Pumpkin Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Pumpkin Door.name: Pumpkin Door
Pumpkin Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Pumpkin Table.name: Pumpkin Table
Pumpkin Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Pumpkin Work Bench.name: Pumpkin Work Bench
Pumpkin Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Pumpkin Platform.name: Pumpkin Platform
Pumpkin Platform.tooltip: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Tattered Fairy Wings.name: Tattered Fairy Wings
Tattered Fairy Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Spider Egg.name: Spider Egg
Spider Egg.tooltip: The Spider Egg is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pet-summoning item that spawns a Pet Spider to follow the player around. The Pet Spider climbs on background walls and has similar behavior to the Spider AI. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Pet Spider rides on a white spiderweb, as if it were standing on a wall, to keep up with the player. The Spider Egg is dropped by the Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.5–12.5% (6.25–12.5%) chance depending on the current wave.

Magical Pumpkin Seed.name: Magical Pumpkin Seed
Magical Pumpkin Seed.tooltip: The Magical Pumpkin Seed is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Squashling that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Squashling will twirl and fly after the player to catch up to them. The Magical Pumpkin Seed has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of being obtained from harvesting fully-grown Pumpkins during the Halloween seasonal event.

Bat Hook.name: Bat Hook
Bat Hook.tooltip: The Bat Hook is a rare pre-Hardmode grappling hook that fires a single hook which reaches 31.25 tiles at maximum length, and has the longest reach of all pre-Hardmode hooks. The Bat Hook has a 149/22500 (0.66%) chance of being obtained from Goodie Bags. The Bat Hook has a pull-in speed of 72 mph and a hook velocity of 13.5, which makes it a very fast hook that can be acquired in the early game. However, some players may find a multi-hook (such as the Ivy Whip) preferable. The Bat Hook can be found in naturally-generated chests in the Vampirism secret world seed.

Bat Scepter.name: Bat Scepter
Bat Scepter.tooltip: The Bat Scepter is a Hardmode, post-Plantera wand that is dropped by the Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.5–12.5% (6.25–12.5%) chance depending on the current wave. When used, it fires a burst of 2–3 homing bats, which do not pierce enemies or pass through blocks. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Raven Staff.name: Raven Staff
Raven Staff.tooltip: The Raven Staff is a Hardmode, post-Plantera summon weapon that summons a Raven minion. It flies and charges through enemies. The Raven Staff is dropped by the Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.5–12.5% (6.25–12.5%) chance depending on the current wave. Its best modifier is Fabled.

Jungle Key Mold.name: Jungle Key Mold
Jungle Key Mold.tooltip: Biome Key Molds are extremely rare Hardmode crafting materials that are used to craft Biome Keys, which open Biome Chests once Plantera is defeated. After the Wall of Flesh is defeated, every enemy killed within an eligible biome has a 1/2500 (0.04%) chance of dropping a Biome Key Mold, with the exception of Meteor Heads and statue-spawned enemies. The type of key mold that is dropped depends on the biome the player is currently in (Jungle, Corruption, Crimson, Hallow, or Snow). On the  Desktop,  Console, and  Mobile versions, Biome Keys drop instead of Key Molds, and all existing Key Molds will change into their respective Keys if any exist in the world.

Corruption Key Mold.tooltip: Biome Key Molds are extremely rare Hardmode crafting materials that are used to craft Biome Keys, which open Biome Chests once Plantera is defeated. Hanging Jack 'O Lantern.name: Hanging Jack 'O Lantern
Hanging Jack 'O Lantern.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Rotten Egg.name: Rotten Egg
Rotten Egg.tooltip: The Rotten Egg is a consumable ranged weapon obtained commonly from Goodie Bags, which are dropped during the Halloween season, and from shaking trees during that time. They explode on impact, with no chance of being retrieved. Rotten Eggs are unique in that they are one of the two player-wielded weapons that can damage friendly entities (including NPCs) by default, the other being the Flymeal (the Clothier and Guide Voodoo Dolls allow killing their respective NPCs, but are not wielded as weapons). They are a slow but effective way of killing NPCs.
Rotten Egg.drops_summary: Ash tree (2.449%), Boreal tree (2.449%), Ebonwood Palm tree (2.8571%), +10 more

Unlucky Yarn.name: Unlucky Yarn
Unlucky Yarn.tooltip: The Unlucky Yarn is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Black Cat that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Black Cat flies on a broom to catch up with them. The Unlucky Yarn has a 1/150 (0.67%) chance of being obtained from Goodie Bags during the Halloween seasonal event.

Black Fairy Dust.name: Black Fairy Dust
Black Fairy Dust.tooltip: Black Fairy Dust is a crafting material used solely to craft Tattered Fairy Wings. It is dropped by the Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.5–12.5% (6.25–12.5%) chance depending on the current wave.

Jackelier.name: Jackelier
Jackelier.tooltip: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers come in many varieties which differ only in appearance and sell value. All chandeliers can be picked up using a pickaxe, drill, or explosives. Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.

Jack 'O Lantern.tooltip: The Jack 'O Lantern is a placeable furniture item that gives off light. It can have different faces when placed.

Reaper Hood.name: Reaper Hood
Reaper Hood.tooltip: The Reaper set is a vanity set which consists of the Reaper Hood and Reaper Robe. It has a 2/57 (3.51%) chance to be obtained from Goodie Bags during Halloween. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Its male and female variants look identical.

These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Its male and female variants look identical.

Fox Mask.name: Fox Mask
Fox Mask.tooltip: The Fox set is a vanity set. It has a 2/57 (3.51%) chance to drop from Goodie Bags during Halloween. The set consists of the Fox Mask, Fox Shirt, and Fox Pants. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) Its male and female variants look identical.

Cat Ears.name: Cat Ears
Cat Ears.tooltip: Cat Ears are a headpiece vanity item that can be obtained from Goodie Bags during Halloween with a 2/57 (3.51%) chance.

Bloody Machete.name: Bloody Machete
Bloody Machete.tooltip: The Bloody Machete is a pre-Hardmode boomerang that has a 1/2000 (0.05%) chance of being dropped by any weak enemy during the Halloween seasonal event. When thrown, it falls downward after reaching a medium range, then returns to the player upon contact with a block or an enemy. It also inflicts the Bleeding debuff on hit. On the I am error secret world seed, the Bloody Machete has a chance of being obtained from any Chest. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

The Horseman's Blade.name: The Horseman's Blade
The Horseman's Blade.tooltip: The Horseman's Blade is a Hardmode, post-Plantera broadsword that can be dropped by the Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.5–12.5% (6.25–12.5%) chance depending on the current wave. When swung, an orange aura follows the swing, reaching farther than the sword itself. The aura can hit up to three enemies. Upon striking an enemy, The Horseman's Blade summons a Flaming Jack, a homing pumpkin head projectile that can pass through blocks. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Bladed Glove.name: Bladed Glove
Bladed Glove.tooltip: The Bladed Glove is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that has a roughly 1/2000 (0.05%) chance of being dropped by any weak enemy during the Halloween seasonal event. It has a very short range, but an exceptionally high attack speed. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Pumpkin Seed.name: Pumpkin Seed
Pumpkin Seed.tooltip: The Pumpkin Seed is a seed which is used to plant Pumpkins. They may be planted on normal green grass or Hallowed grass (including their mowed versions), and will eventually grow into Pumpkins. They need 2 blocks width and 2 blocks height of clear space to grow, and can grow anywhere grass will grow. Pumpkin Seeds are purchased from the Dryad for 2 Silver 50 Copper each.

Spooky Hook.name: Spooky Hook
Spooky Hook.tooltip: Hooks are a class of tools which aid the player in traversing terrain. When used, hooks fire a chain that latches to a surface or platform and pulls the player towards it. A hook is an essential tool which offers significant freedom from terrain height restrictions as well as being a fast movement option, and will often be the first major mobility tool a player acquires. A variety of hooks are available at all stages of the game (see table below). The Grapple hotkey activates the equipped hook in the player's equipment slot, or the first hook from the inventory (from left to right, top to bottom) without requiring it to be in the player's hotbar.Verify Several higher-tier hooks, such as the Ivy Whip, allow the player to grapple multiple surfaces simultaneously. If the character grapples one surface, then fires the hook a second time, another chain extends from the player without dislodging the first. Upon grappling a second surface, the player will be suspended in midair at a point midway between the two surfaces. This allows players more freedom during construction, or for navigating hazardous areas, such as above lava or Meteorite. All Journey Mode characters will spawn with the basic Grappling Hook already in their inventory.

Spooky Wings.name: Spooky Wings
Spooky Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Spooky Twig.name: Spooky Twig
Spooky Twig.tooltip: The Spooky Twig is a Hardmode, post-Plantera crafting material used solely for crafting Spooky Wings. It is dropped by the Mourning Wood during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.86–20% (5–20%) chance depending on the current wave.

Spooky Helmet.name: Spooky Helmet
Spooky Helmet.tooltip: Spooky armor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera summoner armor set consisting of the Spooky Helmet, Spooky Breastplate, and Spooky Leggings. Crafting the full set requires a total of 750 Spooky Wood. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +30 defense +58% summon damage +4 minion slots +20% movement speed A visual glowing effect around the player.

Spooky Breastplate.name: Spooky Breastplate
Spooky Breastplate.tooltip: Spooky armor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera summoner armor set consisting of the Spooky Helmet, Spooky Breastplate, and Spooky Leggings. Crafting the full set requires a total of 750 Spooky Wood. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +30 defense +58% summon damage +4 minion slots +20% movement speed A visual glowing effect around the player.

Spooky Leggings.name: Spooky Leggings

The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +30 defense +58% summon damage +4 minion slots +20% movement speed A visual glowing effect around the player.

Stake Launcher.name: Stake Launcher
Stake Launcher.tooltip: The Stake Launcher is a Hardmode, post-Plantera repeater that consumes Stakes as ammunition. When used, it fires Stakes that pierce nine enemies, are unaffected by gravity, and have a higher velocity than most arrows. The Stake Launcher applies a 10% damage penalty to the next hit for each enemy pierced. The Stake Launcher has a base 14% critical strike chance, as opposed to the usual 4%. The Stake Launcher is dropped by the Mourning Wood during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.86–20% (5–20%) chance depending on the current wave. When dropped, the Stake Launcher is always accompanied by 30 to 60 Stakes. Additional Stakes are sold by the Witch Doctor and Arms Dealer for 15 Copper each while the Stake Launcher is in the player's inventory.  Its best modifier is Unreal.

Cursed Sapling.name: Cursed Sapling
Cursed Sapling.tooltip: The Cursed Sapling is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pet-summoning item that spawns a Cursed Sapling that follows the player. It appears as a small, dark blue tree stump with a jagged head, a jack-o-lantern face, and roots on which it walks. The Cursed Sapling is dropped by the Mourning Wood during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.86–20% (5–20%) chance depending on the current wave.

Space Creature Mask.name: Space Creature Mask
Space Creature Mask.tooltip: The Space Creature set is a vanity set consisting of the Space Creature Mask, Space Creature Shirt, and Space Creature Pants. Its male and female variants look identical. It has a 2/57 (3.51%) chance to drop from Goodie Bags during Halloween. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Pumpkin Moon Medallion.name: Pumpkin Moon Medallion
Pumpkin Moon Medallion.tooltip: The Pumpkin Moon Medallion is a Hardmode, post-Plantera event-summoning item used to summon the Pumpkin Moon event. It can only be used at night. Attempting to use it during the day will not begin the event, and the item will not be consumed from the player's inventory.

Necromantic Scroll.name: Necromantic Scroll
Necromantic Scroll.tooltip: The Necromantic Scroll is a Hardmode, post-Plantera accessory that increases the player's minion slots by one and increases the damage of all summon weapons by 10%. It is dropped by the Mourning Wood during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.86–20% (5–20%) chance depending on the current wave.

Jacking Skeletron.name: Jacking Skeletron
Jacking Skeletron.tooltip: Paintings are decorative furniture items that can be placed on background walls. Each one is a framed image that depicts a particular scene, usually Terraria-related. Their tooltips generally contain a person's name, intended to credit each painting's artist; although the names appear to be fictional, most of them correspond to known Terraria developers, artists, testing staff, and community members (see Trivia below). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions, the Magic Lantern, Spelunker Glowsticks, and Spelunker Flares. There are a total of 193 paintings, 25 of which are sold by the Painter, 7 by the Princess, 4 by the Golfer, 2 by the Zoologist, 2 by the Clothier, 1 by the Truffle, and 27 are randomly sold by the Traveling Merchant. 35 paintings can be found in Underground Cabins, another 14 in the Underground Desert Cabins, 26 in the Dungeon, 12 in The Underworld, 6 from Floating Islands, 5 obtained by fishing, 1 from the Jungle Temple, 5 randomly acquired from Goodie Bags, 8 dropped by Solar Eclipse enemies, 8 awarded randomly by the Angler for completing fishing quests, 1 from the Living Tree, and 4 dropped by enemies.

Treasure Hunter Shirt.name: Treasure Hunter Shirt
Treasure Hunter Shirt.tooltip: The Treasure Hunter set is a vanity set. It consists of a Treasure Hunter Shirt and Treasure Hunter Pants. It has a 2/57 (3.51%) chance of being obtained from opening Goodie Bags. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Treasure Hunter Pants.name: Treasure Hunter Pants
Treasure Hunter Pants.tooltip: The Treasure Hunter set is a vanity set. It consists of a Treasure Hunter Shirt and Treasure Hunter Pants. It has a 2/57 (3.51%) chance of being obtained from opening Goodie Bags. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Dryad Coverings.name: Dryad Coverings
Dryad Coverings.tooltip: The Dryad set is a vanity set which is purchased from the Dryad for 6 Gold (set), during Halloween. It resembles the clothing that the Dryad wears regularly. It consists of the Dryad Coverings and Dryad Loincloth.

Dryad Loincloth.name: Dryad Loincloth
Dryad Loincloth.tooltip: The Dryad set is a vanity set which is purchased from the Dryad for 6 Gold (set), during Halloween. It resembles the clothing that the Dryad wears regularly. It consists of the Dryad Coverings and Dryad Loincloth.

Mourning Wood Trophy.name: Mourning Wood Trophy
Mourning Wood Trophy.tooltip: Trophies are decorative furniture items which usually have a 1/10 (10%) chance to be dropped from most bosses. While they can be considered the "boss version of banners", they are purely cosmetic and do not provide any bonuses. Some trophies can only be rewarded by the Angler for completing fishing quests. In total, there are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 33 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 24 trophies.

Pumpking Trophy.name: Pumpking Trophy
Pumpking Trophy.tooltip: Trophies are decorative furniture items which usually have a 1/10 (10%) chance to be dropped from most bosses. While they can be considered the "boss version of banners", they are purely cosmetic and do not provide any bonuses. Some trophies can only be rewarded by the Angler for completing fishing quests. In total, there are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 33 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 24 trophies.

Jack 'O Lantern Mask.name: Jack 'O Lantern Mask
Jack 'O Lantern Mask.tooltip: The Jack 'O Lantern Mask is a vanity item for the helmet slot. It is dropped by Headless Horsemen during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 0.71%–5% (1.25%–5%) chance depending on the current wave.

Sniper Scope.name: Sniper Scope
Sniper Scope.tooltip: The Sniper Scope is a Hardmode, post-Golem accessory. It grants the following effects while equipped: +10% ranged damage +10% ranged critical strike chance The ability to "zoom", increasing view range while holding a bullet-firing gun by pressing and holding ⚷ Open / Activate and moving the cursor.

Heart Lantern.name: Heart Lantern
Heart Lantern.tooltip: The Heart Lantern is a functional lantern that grants the Heart Lamp buff, providing a health regeneration of 1 HP per second to all players within a rectangular area of 170×125 (  ) / 100×84 ( ) tiles. Like other lanterns, the Heart Lantern is a mechanism that can be toggled on or off if wired, though this does not affect the buff.

Jellyfish Diving Gear.name: Jellyfish Diving Gear
Jellyfish Diving Gear.tooltip: Jellyfish Diving Gear is an accessory crafted by combining Jellyfish Necklace and Diving Gear at a Tinkerer's Workshop. It combines the functionalities of its ingredients: The player can swim upwards in any liquid by holding or pressing ↷ Jump repeatedly. The player's breath meter will deplete much slower, and the rate at which drowning damage is taken is slowed. The player emit light when submerged in water and honey, and emits very faint light out of water and honey.

Arctic Diving Gear.name: Arctic Diving Gear
Arctic Diving Gear.tooltip: The Arctic Diving Gear is an accessory which is crafted by combining the Jellyfish Diving Gear and Ice Skates at a Tinkerer's Workshop. It combines the functionalities of its ingredients: The player can swim upwards in any liquid by holding or pressing ↷ Jump repeatedly. The player's breath meter will deplete much slower, and the rate at which drowning damage is taken is slowed. The player emits light when submerged in water and honey, and emits very faint light out of water and honey. Increased acceleration and deceleration on all Ice Blocks, Thin Ice, Frozen Slime Blocks, and Aetherium Blocks. The player will no longer cause Thin Ice to break upon landing. Besides these effects, it also prevents the Chilled debuff when touching water in Snow or Ice biomes in Expert Mode.

Frostspark Boots.name: Frostspark Boots
Frostspark Boots.tooltip: The Frostspark Boots are a pre-Hardmode accessory crafted from Lightning Boots and Ice Skates, and combines their functionality. They grant the following effects while equipped: The ability to sprint, allowing the player to reach maximum running speed faster. The player will leave behind a visual trail of snow clouds as they sprint. Increased maximum movement speed to 35 mph (25.67 tiles/second). The ability to hold ↷ Jump in midair to fly for a total of 1.17 seconds. While flying, the boots emit a visual cloud trail. When paired with wings, this flight is disabled to give the wings an additional 0.7 seconds of flight time. Increased acceleration and deceleration on all Ice Blocks, Thin Ice, Frozen Slime Blocks, and Aetherium Blocks. The player will no longer cause Thin Ice to break upon landing.

Fart in a Balloon.name: Fart in a Balloon
Fart in a Balloon.tooltip: The Fart in a Balloon is an accessory that combines the effects of the Fart in a Jar and the Shiny Red Balloon. It boosts jump duration by 33% and jump speed by 30%, increasing the player's first jump's height to ~10.5 tiles (~75% increase), and provides a double jump that can reach a height of 18.5 tiles, for a total of 29 tiles. Unlike most other double-jump balloons, the Fart in a Balloon's full jump is high enough for the player to take minor fall damage, unless the player has fall damage immunity accessories like the Lucky Horseshoe.

Papyrus Scarab.name: Papyrus Scarab
Papyrus Scarab.tooltip: The Papyrus Scarab is a Hardmode, post-Plantera accessory that combines the bonuses of the Necromantic Scroll and the Hercules Beetle. It grants the following effects while equipped: +15% summon damage +2 summon knockback +1 minion slot

Celestial Stone.name: Celestial Stone
Celestial Stone.tooltip: The Celestial Stone is a Hardmode post-Golem accessory crafted from a Moon Stone and a Sun Stone at the Tinkerer's Workshop. It offers the same boosts as its components do, and as such, it is active during both day and night. It can be combined with the Moon Shell to form a Celestial Shell. Stat boosts: +10% melee speed +10% damage (all types) +2% critical strike chance +1 HP/s life regeneration +4 defense +15% mining speed +0.5 summon knockback

Hoverboard.name: Hoverboard
Hoverboard.tooltip: The Hoverboard is a Hardmode wing-type accessory. It functions like a regular pair of wings, but with the added ability to hover by holding ↷ Jump and ▼ Down. The Hoverboard has a flight height of 94 tiles, and a hover speed of 52 mph.

Candy Cane.name: Candy Cane
Candy Cane.tooltip: Hearts (or Candy Apples during Halloween and Candy Canes during Christmas) are common power-ups which can be dropped by slain enemies, broken pots, or as a bonus drop from slimes. Enemies and pots will only drop Hearts when the closest player does not have full health. They are not inventory items, but are instead instantly consumed and restore 20 health. They emit a faint red light. The drop rate of Hearts from enemies is linked to that of Stars. If the closest player is below full health but has full mana, then the chance to drop a Heart is 1/12 (8.33%). If they are below full health and full mana, however, then Stars take priority and the chance to drop a Heart is reduced to 1/24 (4.17%). For the drop rate of Hearts from pots, see Pot § Upon breaking. It is also possible to spawn Hearts (and their seasonal counterparts) with a Heart Statue. Hearts can be collected within a range of 2.625 tiles, which can be increased with a Heartreach Potion to 18.25 tiles.

Sugar Plum.name: Sugar Plum
Sugar Plum.tooltip: Stars (or Soul Cakes during Halloween and Sugar Plums during Christmas) are common power-ups which can be dropped by any enemy with a chance of 13/24 (54.17%), as long as the closest player does not have full mana. They are not inventory items, but are instead instantly consumed, restoring 100 mana and providing the Mana Surge buff, which increases magic damage by up to 20% for a brief duration. It is also possible to spawn Stars (and their seasonal counterparts) with a Star Statue. Stars can be collected within a range of 2.625 tiles, which can be increased with a Celestial Magnet (and its upgrades) to 21.375 tiles.

Present.name: Present
Present.tooltip: The Present is a grab bag item available during the Christmas seasonal event which contains a random Christmas-themed reward. It can be opened by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it in the player's inventory, similar to all other grab bags. Presents can be opened anytime, even outside the Christmas season. Presents are dropped with a 1/13 (7.69%) chance by any enemy that has more than 1 maximum health, deals more than 0 damage, and drops coins, during Christmas only. Therefore, enemies spawned by statues, enemies from the Old One's Army and Lunar Events, etc. can never drop Presents (see Coin drops for the full list). Moreover, Meteor Heads cannot drop Presents either. Presents can be placed down as furniture, and one of eight possible appearances can be cycled through  by pressing ▲ Up and ▼ Down.

Red Ryder.name: Red Ryder
Red Ryder.tooltip: The Red Ryder is a pre-Hardmode gun dropped from Presents obtained during Christmas, with a 0.643% chance in pre-Hardmode and 0.6% chance in Hardmode. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Festive Wings.name: Festive Wings
Festive Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Pine Tree Block.name: Pine Tree Block
Pine Tree Block.tooltip: Pine Tree Blocks are blocks that are dropped in stacks of 20–49 from Presents obtained during the Christmas seasonal event (December 15–December 31), with a chance of 16.803% in pre-Hardmode and 15.683% in Hardmode. When placed, a Pine Tree Block appears to be a small sapling, but will become bigger as more are added. If one or more are stacked on a single block, it will appear as a trunk. Pine Tree Blocks can be used to craft the alternative Pine Wood block, and they both can be used to craft Pine furniture.

Christmas Tree.name: Christmas Tree
Christmas Tree.tooltip: The Christmas Tree is a decorative Hardmode furniture item purchased from Santa Claus for 25 Silver. It can be decorated with toppers, garlands, bulbs, and lights to alter its appearance.

Star Topper 1.name: Star Topper 1
Star Topper 1.tooltip: Christmas Tree decorations are Hardmode furniture items used to decorate Christmas Trees. There are four categories: toppers, bulbs, lights, and garlands. Each tree can only include one of each type. Most decorations can be purchased from Santa Claus for 5 Silver each, except for the  Old-gen console-exclusive Star Topper 4, which can be found in Presents. Decorations can only be removed by replacing specific decorations with another of the same type, or by removing the tree with a pickaxe, drill, or explosives and placing it again.

Decorations can only be removed by replacing specific decorations with another of the same type, or by removing the tree with a pickaxe, drill, or explosives and placing it again.

Giant Bow.name: Giant Bow
Giant Bow.tooltip: The Giant Bow is a festive vanity item that has a 1/20 (5%) chance to drop during Christmas by Present Slimes, which visually have a large bow on. The Bow itself is red, but it can drop from any of the four colors of Present Slime. When worn in the helmet slot, a bow appears on top of the player's head.

Reindeer Antlers.name: Reindeer Antlers
Reindeer Antlers.tooltip: The Reindeer Antlers are a vanity item that is dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas seasonal event, with a chance of 2.308% in pre-Hardmode and 2.154% in Hardmode. When worn in the helmet slot, they place antlers on the player's head.

Holly.name: Holly
Holly.tooltip: The Holly is a decorative item resembling an Advent wreath, a typical Christmas ornament. It can be placed on a background wall, similar to paintings. It is dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas event, with a chance of 9.001% in pre-Hardmode and 8.401% in Hardmode.

Candy Cane Sword.name: Candy Cane Sword
Candy Cane Sword.tooltip: The Candy Cane Sword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that has a 0.639% (pre-Hardmode) / 0.596% (Hardmode) chance to be obtained from Presents dropped during the Christmas event. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Elf Melter.name: Elf Melter
Elf Melter.tooltip: The Elf Melter is a Hardmode, post-Plantera ranged weapon that uses Gel for ammunition. It is an indirect upgrade to the Flamethrower. When used, it consumes one Gel and releases five bursts of fire in quick succession. The fire expands as it travels, creating a cone-like area of effect, before dissipating shortly after. The fire has 15 armor penetration, inflicts the Frostbite debuff for 20 seconds, and can pierce through three enemies. The fire's damage decreases by 15% per enemy pierced. The Elf Melter is dropped by Santa-NK1 during the Frost Moon event with a 6.25%–16.67% / 12.5%–50% chance depending on the current wave. Its best modifier is Unreal. A modifier granting +10% speed will increase the number of flame streams per use from five to six while still consuming 1 Gel. A modifier with added velocity will increase the range of each stream, i.e. by about 5 tiles for +15% and about 3 tiles for +10%.

Christmas Pudding.name: Christmas Pudding
Christmas Pudding.tooltip: Christmas Pudding is a food item that grants the Exquisitely Stuffed buff when consumed. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). Christmas Pudding can be dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas seasonal event, with a chance of 3.601% in pre-Hardmode and 3.361% in Hardmode.

Eggnog.name: Eggnog
Eggnog.tooltip: Eggnog is a pre-Hardmode recovery potion that can be dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas seasonal event, with a chance of 8.101% in pre-Hardmode and 7.561% in Hardmode. When used, it restores 80 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for 40 seconds. This duration can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths.

Star Anise.name: Star Anise
Star Anise.tooltip: The Star Anise is a consumable ranged weapon, similar to Shurikens although slightly stronger. It can hit up to 6 targets. 20–40 can drop from Presents obtained during the Christmas event, with a 6.301% chance in pre-Hardmode and a 5.881% chance in Hardmode.

Reindeer Bells.name: Reindeer Bells
Reindeer Bells.tooltip: The Reindeer Bells are a Hardmode, post-Plantera mount-summoning item that summons the rideable Rudolph mount, which greatly speeds a player's movement and adds the ability to fly. The Reindeer Bells are dropped by the Ice Queen during or after wave 15 of the Frost Moon event with a 1.33%–2.22% / 6.67% chance depending on the current wave. Similar to the Hoverboard, flight height can be constrained by holding the ▼ Down key in addition to the ↷ Jump key, so movement will be horizontal only.

Candy Cane Hook.name: Candy Cane Hook
Candy Cane Hook.tooltip: Hooks are a class of tools which aid the player in traversing terrain. When used, hooks fire a chain that latches to a surface or platform and pulls the player towards it. A hook is an essential tool which offers significant freedom from terrain height restrictions as well as being a fast movement option, and will often be the first major mobility tool a player acquires. A variety of hooks are available at all stages of the game (see table below). The Grapple hotkey activates the equipped hook in the player's equipment slot, or the first hook from the inventory (from left to right, top to bottom) without requiring it to be in the player's hotbar.Verify Several higher-tier hooks, such as the Ivy Whip, allow the player to grapple multiple surfaces simultaneously. If the character grapples one surface, then fires the hook a second time, another chain extends from the player without dislodging the first. Upon grappling a second surface, the player will be suspended in midair at a point midway between the two surfaces. This allows players more freedom during construction, or for navigating hazardous areas, such as above lava or Meteorite. All Journey Mode characters will spawn with the basic Grappling Hook already in their inventory.

Christmas Hook.name: Christmas Hook
Christmas Hook.tooltip: Hooks are a class of tools which aid the player in traversing terrain. When used, hooks fire a chain that latches to a surface or platform and pulls the player towards it. Candy Cane Pickaxe.name: Candy Cane Pickaxe
Candy Cane Pickaxe.tooltip: The Candy Cane Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe. It can mine blocks up to Demonite Ore, Crimtane Ore, and Obsidian. It is obtained from Presents dropped during the Christmas event, with a chance of 0.634% in pre-Hardmode and 0.592% in Hardmode. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Fruitcake Chakram.name: Fruitcake Chakram
Fruitcake Chakram.tooltip: The Fruitcake Chakram is a pre-Hardmode boomerang dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas seasonal event, with a chance of 0.626% in pre-Hardmode and 0.584% in Hardmode. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Sugar Cookie.name: Sugar Cookie
Sugar Cookie.tooltip: The Sugar Cookie is a food item that grants the Exquisitely Stuffed buff when consumed. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Sugar Cookie can be dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas seasonal event, with a chance of 3.601% in pre-Hardmode and 3.361% in Hardmode.

Gingerbread Cookie.name: Gingerbread Cookie
Gingerbread Cookie.tooltip: The Gingerbread Cookie is a food item that grants the Exquisitely Stuffed buff when consumed. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Gingerbread Cookie can be dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas seasonal event, with a chance of 3.601% in pre-Hardmode and 3.361% in Hardmode.

Hand Warmer.name: Hand Warmer
Hand Warmer.tooltip: The Hand Warmer is a pre-Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Chilled and Frozen debuffs. It is obtained from Presents, with a chance of about 0.622% in pre-Hardmode and about 0.580% in Hardmode.

Coal.name: Coal
Coal.tooltip: Coal is an item with no use. It can drop from Presents obtained during the Christmas seasonal event, with a chance of 1/30 (3.33%) in pre-Hardmode and 7/225 (3.11%) in Hardmode. It also has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to be dropped from Jungle Mimics, which only spawn when the Celebration Mk 10 special seed is active.

Toolbox.name: Toolbox
Toolbox.tooltip: The Toolbox is a construction accessory that is obtained when opening Presents dropped during the Christmas seasonal event, with a chance of 0.309% in pre-Hardmode and 0.288% in Hardmode. While equipped, it grants +1 placement range and tool range.

Pine Door.name: Pine Door
Pine Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Pine Chair.name: Pine Chair
Pine Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Pine Table.name: Pine Table
Pine Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Dog Whistle.name: Dog Whistle
Dog Whistle.tooltip: The Dog Whistle is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Puppy that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Puppy flies by twirling its tail like a propeller to catch up to them. The Dog Whistle can be dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas seasonal event, with a 29/12,000 (0.24%) chance in pre-Hardmode and 203/90,000 (0.23%) chance in Hardmode.

Christmas Tree Sword.name: Christmas Tree Sword
Christmas Tree Sword.tooltip: The Christmas Tree Sword is a Hardmode, post-Plantera broadsword that is dropped by the Everscream during the Frost Moon event with a 3.46%–10.37% (6.22%–31.11%) chance depending on the current wave. When swung, it fires a star ornament that releases a ball ornament every 0.17 seconds while traveling. The stars dissipate after piercing one enemy or after 1.67 seconds. The balls linger for 0.83 seconds before falling. Both types of projectiles cannot pass through blocks or enemies. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Chain Gun.name: Chain Gun
Chain Gun.tooltip: The Chain Gun is a Hardmode, post-Plantera gun that is dropped by Santa-NK1 during the Frost Moon event with a 6.25%–16.67% / 12.5%–50% chance depending on the current wave. When used, it very rapidly fires bullets in a wide spread. It also has a 66% chance not to consume ammunition. Its best modifier is Rapid. However, Godly may be preferred to save ammo. Due to its low use time, it can only gain modifiers that give a speed boost of 15%, thus it cannot have the Unreal modifier.

Razorpine.name: Razorpine
Razorpine.tooltip: The Razorpine is a Hardmode, post-Plantera wand that is dropped by the Everscream during the Frost Moon event with a 3.46%–10.37% (6.22%–31.11%) chance depending on the current wave. When used, it rapidly fires 2–4 high-velocity pine needles in a spread, which do not pierce enemies or pass through blocks. The needles become affected by gravity after traveling a medium distance. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Blizzard Staff.name: Blizzard Staff
Blizzard Staff.tooltip: The Blizzard Staff is a Hardmode, post-Plantera wand that is dropped from the Ice Queen during the Frost Moon event with a 5.19%–10.37% (15.56%–31.11%) chance depending on the current wave. When used, it causes a wide spread of icicles to rain from the sky, directed towards the cursor. It summons four icicles per use, which do not pierce enemies or pass through blocks. Its best modifier is Mythical. It also makes the weapon fire six icicles per use instead of four.

Mrs. Claus Hat.name: Mrs. Claus Hat
Mrs. Claus Hat.tooltip: The Mrs. Claus set is a vanity set. It is dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas event, with a chance of 1.08% in pre-Hardmode and 1.008% in Hardmode. It consists of a Mrs. Claus Hat, Mrs. Claus Shirt and Mrs. Claus Heels. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Snow Hat.tooltip: The Snow Hat is a vanity item dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas event, with a chance of 1.08% in pre-Hardmode and 1.008% in Hardmode.

Ugly Sweater.name: Ugly Sweater
Ugly Sweater.tooltip: The Ugly Sweater is a vanity item dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas event, with a chance of 1.08% in pre-Hardmode and 1.008% in Hardmode.

Tree Mask.name: Tree Mask
Tree Mask.tooltip: The Tree set is a vanity set consisting of the Tree Mask, Tree Shirt, and Tree Trunks. It is dropped from Presents obtained during the Christmas event, with a chance of 1.08% in pre-Hardmode and 1.008% in Hardmode. Its male and female variants look identical. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.
