Elf Hat.name: Elf Hat
Elf Hat.tooltip: The Elf set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Elf Hat, the Elf Shirt, and the Elf Pants. Each piece has a 1/600 (0.17%) chance of being dropped by a Zombie Elf.

Elf Shirt.name: Elf Shirt
Elf Shirt.tooltip: The Elf set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Elf Hat, the Elf Shirt, and the Elf Pants. Each piece has a 1/600 (0.17%) chance of being dropped by a Zombie Elf.

Elf Pants.tooltip: The Elf set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Elf Hat, the Elf Shirt, and the Elf Pants. Each piece has a 1/600 (0.17%) chance of being dropped by a Zombie Elf.

Snowman Cannon.name: Snowman Cannon
Snowman Cannon.tooltip: The Snowman Cannon is a Hardmode, post-Plantera launcher that is dropped from the Ice Queen during the Frost Moon event with a 5.19%–10.37% (15.56%–31.11%) chance depending on the current wave.. When used, it consumes rockets and fires homing snowman-shaped rockets that explode on impact with enemies. For combat purposes, its best modifier is Unreal. For mining and usage of liquid rockets, its best modifier is Unreal on  Desktop and Rapid elsewhere. This is due to differences in how use time is rounded between versions, with Unreal Snowman Cannon having a use time of 13 on vanilla desktop versions and 14 elsewhere.Verify

North Pole.name: North Pole
North Pole.tooltip: The North Pole is a Hardmode, post-Plantera spear that is dropped by the Ice Queen during the Frost Moon event with a 5.19%–10.37% (15.56%–31.11%) chance depending on the current wave. When thrust, it fires an icy spear projectile that is unaffected by gravity until after traveling for 0.5 seconds. It can pierce enemies twice and cannot pass through blocks. The spear also releases a trail of damaging snowflakes that rain down, dissipating upon contact with an enemy or block. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Christmas Tree Wallpaper.name: Christmas Tree Wallpaper
Christmas Tree Wallpaper.tooltip: Wallpapers are a group of walls purchased from the Painter. Despite the name, they work just like any other type of wall and do not have to be applied onto other walls. As such, they can be placed and used to prevent enemies from spawning, and can be used to fulfill the requirements of a house. Christmas-themed wallpapers can only be purchased during the Christmas seasonal event.

Ornament Wallpaper.name: Ornament Wallpaper
Ornament Wallpaper.tooltip: Wallpapers are a group of walls purchased from the Painter. Despite the name, they work just like any other type of wall and do not have to be applied onto other walls. As such, they can be placed and used to prevent enemies from spawning, and can be used to fulfill the requirements of a house. Christmas-themed wallpapers can only be purchased during the Christmas seasonal event.

Naughty Present.name: Naughty Present
Naughty Present.tooltip: The Naughty Present is a Hardmode, post-Plantera event-summoning item used to summon the Frost Moon event. It can only be used at night. Attempting to use it during the day will not begin the event, and the item will not be consumed from the player's inventory.

Baby Grinch's Mischief Whistle.name: Baby Grinch's Mischief Whistle
Baby Grinch's Mischief Whistle.tooltip: The Baby Grinch's Mischief Whistle is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Grinch that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, a red balloon will carry the Baby Grinch to catch up with them. The Baby Grinch's Mischief Whistle is dropped by the Ice Queen during the Frost Moon event with a 1.11%–2.22% (3.33%–6.67%) chance depending on the current wave.

Ice Queen Trophy.name: Ice Queen Trophy
Ice Queen Trophy.tooltip: Trophies are decorative furniture items which usually have a 1/10 (10%) chance to be dropped from most bosses. While they can be considered the "boss version of banners", they are purely cosmetic and do not provide any bonuses. Some trophies can only be rewarded by the Angler for completing fishing quests. In total, there are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 33 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 24 trophies.

Music Box (Pumpkin Moon).name: Music Box (Pumpkin Moon)
Music Box (Pumpkin Moon).tooltip: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End), which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 Gold after defeating the Moon Lord. A recorded Music Box can be played back in one of two ways: Equipping it as an accessory. Placing it as furniture and activating it, either by the ⚷ Open / Activate button or with wires. Recorded Music Boxes can be reverted into blank ones through Shimmer transmutation. There are 101 different Music Boxes available.

Brown Paint.name: Brown Paint
Brown Paint.tooltip: Paint is used to modify the color of objects. Nearly anything can be painted, including blocks, background walls, and furniture, along with non-collectable environment objects like trees, tall grass, flowers, and other ambient growth. Basic paint is purchased from the Painter NPC. Two of the same color can be combined at a Dye Vat to create "deep" color versions, which apply their color more vividly and are required in order to paint certain objects. Coating(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is used to apply a special effect over a block and can be applied in tandem with paint and other coatings. It is purchased from the Painter NPC. Paint and coatings are applied to blocks and furniture with the Paintbrush, and to walls with the Paint Roller, with each tile consuming one item of paint/coating. The Paint Sprayer will automatically paint items when placing them. Paint and coatings can be removed with the Paint Scraper, although they will never be retrieved upon doing so. Destroying a painted block will not drop the paint item either. Paint can be placed in ammo slots. If more than one type of paint or coating is present in the player's inventory, the paint or coating in the earliest inventory slot is used first (starting from the top-left slot).

Team Dye.name: Team Dye
Team Dye.tooltip: Team Dye is a dye that can be purchased from the Dye Trader while playing multiplayer. The color of this dye will correspond to the team the player is on; if the player is not on a team, it acts as though no dye was equipped.

Amethyst Gemspark Block.name: Amethyst Gemspark Block
Amethyst Gemspark Block.tooltip: Gemspark Blocks are pre-Hardmode blocks. They glow when placed or dropped as an item, with the color of the glow depending on the gem used to craft the block. They are also considered mechanisms, as their glow can be toggled by wiring them to a trigger. If a waterfall passes through a Gemspark Block, it will also color and add a glowing effect to it. When the Gemspark Block is in its active state, the resulting waterfall will take on the color of the Gemspark Block, and will glow for its entire length. Glowing waterfalls emit a very faint light onto other objects. Gemspark Blocks will not change the color of lavafalls, honeyfalls, or Shimmerfalls(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

Angel Halo.name: Angel Halo
Angel Halo.tooltip: The Angel Halo is a vanity accessory purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 40 Gold. The Angel Halo cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Fez.name: Fez
Fez.tooltip: The Fez is a head piece vanity item purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 3 Gold 50 Silver.

Womannequin.name: Womannequin
Womannequin.tooltip: The Womannequin is a furniture item that can be used to display armor and vanity items, as well as accessories and dyes. Items can be placed on a Womannequin by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it, which opens a small set of inventory-like slots beneath the player's main inventory. There are three slots for helmet, shirt, and pants, five slots for accessories, and one slot for weapons. In addition, each slot besides the weapons slot has an associated dye slot underneath it. Placing items in these slots immediately displays them on the Womannequin. Womannequins can only be removed if no items are placed on them. The Womannequin always displays armor and clothing in their female sprite forms. The Mannequin can be used to display them in their male counterparts.

Hair Dye Remover.name: Hair Dye Remover
Hair Dye Remover.tooltip: Hair Dyes are consumable items sold by the Stylist NPC. When used, they replace a player's hair color with a dynamic effect.

Bug Net.name: Bug Net
Bug Net.tooltip: The Bug Net is a tool used to capture most critters as inventory items. It is swung like a broadsword, but it deals no damage. The Bug Net is nearly required in order to go fishing, as it is the initial and primary method of obtaining bait. Most critters that are insects, worms, or snails can function as bait once captured. The Bug Net can be purchased from the Merchant for (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 25 Silver / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 1 Gold. The Lavaproof Bug Net(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Golden Bug Net(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are upgraded versions of the Bug Net that are bigger, swing faster, and can destroy tall grass, vines, and uproot plants just like swords and other weapons do, despite dealing no damage. They are also able to catch Underworld critters (Lavafly(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Hell Butterfly(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Magma Snail(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)), unlike the standard Bug Net; attempting to catch one with a standard Bug Net will deal 1 damage to the player and inflict the On Fire! debuff for 5 seconds / 10 seconds / 13 seconds.

Firefly.name: Firefly
Firefly.tooltip: The Firefly is a harmless critter that gives off a tiny amount of light. Fireflies will spawn near grass on the surface at night, except inside houses. Their spawn rate will be randomly set everyday, making their spawn amount varying greatly each night. The Firefly has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Firefly can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Firefly in a Bottle). Once crafted, the Firefly cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The Firefly can be used as bait for fishing, with 20% bait power. The Firefly can be spawned by the Firefly Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so. Its Hallow counterpart is the Lightning Bug.

Firefly in a Bottle.name: Firefly in a Bottle
Firefly in a Bottle.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Monarch Butterfly.name: Monarch Butterfly
Monarch Butterfly.tooltip: Butterflies are small critters that can naturally spawn on Surface in Forest and the Hallow, and also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Forest or Pearlwood tree. In both cases, they can only spawn during daytime if wind speed is lower than 20 mph, and if it is not currently raining. There are 8 variants of ordinary Butterflies with different appearences, chosen randomly when they spawn. They can be caught with a Bug Net and carried in the inventory. When an ordinary Butterfly is being spawned, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance (affected by luck) for it to be replaced by a Gold Butterfly, which can be caught with a Bug Net and crafted into Golden Delight. The Hell Butterfly(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can naturally spawn in the Underworld during daytime. It can also spawn from shaking an Ash tree in the Underworld, or from destroying wild Ash grass plants. It can only be caught with the Lavaproof Bug Net(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or the Golden Bug Net(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Attempting to catch it with a standard Bug Net will not work, and the player will take 1 damage and be inflicted with On Fire! for 5 seconds / 10 seconds / 12.5 seconds. All Butterflies can be crafted into butterfly jars, and can be be used as bait for fishing.

When an ordinary Butterfly is being spawned, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance (affected by luck) for it to be replaced by a Gold Butterfly, which can be caught with a Bug Net and crafted into Golden Delight. The Hell Butterfly(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can naturally spawn in the Underworld during daytime. It can also spawn from shaking an Ash tree in the Underworld, or from destroying wild Ash grass plants. It can only be caught with the Lavaproof Bug Net(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or the Golden Bug Net(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Attempting to catch it with a standard Bug Net will not work, and the player will take 1 damage and be inflicted with On Fire! for 5 seconds / 10 seconds / 12.5 seconds. All Butterflies can be crafted into butterfly jars, and can be be used as bait for fishing.

Julia Butterfly.name: Julia Butterfly
Julia Butterfly.tooltip: Butterflies are small critters that can naturally spawn on Surface in Forest and the Hallow, and also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Forest or Pearlwood tree. In both cases, they can only spawn during daytime if wind speed is lower than 20 mph, and if it is not currently raining. There are 8 variants of ordinary Butterflies with different appearences, chosen randomly when they spawn. They can be caught with a Bug Net and carried in the inventory. When an ordinary Butterfly is being spawned, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance (affected by luck) for it to be replaced by a Gold Butterfly, which can be caught with a Bug Net and crafted into Golden Delight. The Hell Butterfly(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can naturally spawn in the Underworld during daytime. Worm.name: Worm
Worm.tooltip: The Worm is a critter that spawns in the Underground layer at any time, or on the surface while it is raining. It also has a chance to spawn when grass plants or certain ambient dirt or stone piles are destroyed, jumping out of the destroyed object. Worms are always replaced by Maggots(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) in Graveyard biomes. The Worm has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Worm can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Worm Cage). Once crafted, the Worm cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The Worm can be used as bait for fishing, with 25% bait power. The Worm can be spawned by the Worm Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Worm to spawn in place of an ordinary one. Worms can be obtained directly in item form by opening a Can Of Worms.

Mouse.name: Mouse
Mouse.tooltip: The Mouse is a critter that spawns in the Underground and Cavern layers, but not in Ice, Crimson, Corruption, Jungle or Hallow biomes. It can also spawn in front of unsafe Living Wood Walls below the surface at a much higher rate. Its small size and speed can make it difficult to spot even in well-lit conditions, although it occasionally squeaks. The Mouse has only 5 health and no defense, and can only be damaged by players. The Mouse can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Mouse Cage). Once crafted, the Mouse cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The Mouse can be spawned by the Mouse Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Mouse to spawn in place of an ordinary one.

Lightning Bug.name: Lightning Bug
Lightning Bug.tooltip: The Lightning Bug is a harmless Hardmode critter that gives off a tiny amount of light, similarly to the Firefly. It spawns on Hallowed grass blocks during the night. The Lightning Bug has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Lightning Bug can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Lightning Bug in a Bottle). Once crafted, the Lightning Bug cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The Lightning Bug can be used as bait for fishing, with 35% bait power. The Lightning Bug can be spawned by the Firefly Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so. Its counterpart is the Firefly.

Lightning Bug in a Bottle.name: Lightning Bug in a Bottle
Lightning Bug in a Bottle.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Snail.name: Snail
Snail.tooltip: The Snail is a rather rare critter that spawns in the Underground and Cavern layers, but not in Ice, Crimson, Corruption, or Hallow biomes. It can also spawn in front of unsafe Living Wood Walls below the surface at a much higher rate. The Snail has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Snail can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Snail Cage). Once crafted, the Snail cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The Snail can be used as bait for fishing, with 10% bait power. The Snail can be spawned by the Snail Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.

Glowing Snail.name: Glowing Snail
Glowing Snail.tooltip: The Glowing Snail is an uncommon critter that only spawns in either surface or underground Glowing Mushroom biomes. It emits light and is quite large compared to its normal counterpart. The Glowing Snail has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Glowing Snail can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Glowing Snail Cage). Once crafted, the Glowing Snail cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The Glowing Snail can be used as bait for fishing, with 15% bait power. The Glowing Snail can be spawned by the Snail Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.

Fancy Gray Wallpaper.name: Fancy Gray Wallpaper
Fancy Gray Wallpaper.tooltip: Wallpapers are a group of walls purchased from the Painter. Despite the name, they work just like any other type of wall and do not have to be applied onto other walls. As such, they can be placed and used to prevent enemies from spawning, and can be used to fulfill the requirements of a house. Christmas-themed wallpapers can only be purchased during the Christmas seasonal event.

Bird.name: Bird
Bird.tooltip: The Bird, Blue Jay, and Cardinal are flying critters that can spawn in the Forest biome. They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Forest or Pearlwood tree. Much like the Vulture, Birds remain still until approached, whereupon they will fly away. Birds will occasionally chirp when nearby. Birds may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details. Birds have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. Birds can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Bird / Blue Jay / Cardinal Cage). Once crafted, the Birds cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Birds can be spawned by the Bird Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Bird to spawn in place of an ordinary one.

Bunny.name: Bunny
Bunny.tooltip: The Bunny is a harmless critter that spawns in the Forest biome. They are the most common critters in Terraria, and are usually the first ones a new player will see. Bunnies have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. Bunnies can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Bunny Cage). Once crafted, the Bunnies cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. Bunnies can be spawned by the Bunny Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Bunny to spawn in place of an ordinary one. During a Blood Moon, or when hit with Vile Powder/Vicious Powder, Bunnies will turn into Corrupt Bunnies or Vicious Bunnies. During the Halloween seasonal event, Bunnies spawn wearing Green Slime costumes, during Christmas, Bunnies will spawn wearing Santa costumes, and during a Party, Bunnies can spawn with Party Hats. Gem Bunnies spawn near towns in the Cavern layer.

Cactus Bookcase.name: Cactus Bookcase
Cactus Bookcase.tooltip: Bookcases are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station used for the crafting of three Hardmode magic weapons (the Crystal Storm, Cursed Flames, and Golden Shower) as well as the Librarian furniture out of Librarian Blocks. Bookcases also fulfill a house's table requirement. There is a total of 65 types of Bookcases: 60 craftable Bookcases, and 5 looted from the environment: one from the Underworld, three from the Dungeon, and one from the Pirate Invasion. Some bookcases can also be found in Underground Cabins; their style follows the theme of the cabin where they are found.

The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Frozen Door.name: Frozen Door
Frozen Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Cactus Candle.name: Cactus Candle
Cactus Candle.tooltip: Candles are a type of furniture and light source. Candles can only be placed on flat-surface items. Candles will produce light underwater if placed and can be toggled on and off with ⚷ Open / Activate and by mechanisms. Certain types of candles provide buffs or debuffs. The Water Candle is a special type of candle found in Dungeons which increases enemy spawn rates by 33% and the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50% when placed or held. The Peace Candle reduces spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%, in contrast to the Water Candle. The Shadow Candle(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns in the area. For Water Candles and Peace Candles, multiple candles cannot stack, even if one is placed and the other is held.

Cactus Bed.name: Cactus Bed
Cactus Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration. Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 craftable Beds and 5 that can be acquired from the environment. All Beds are functionally identical and differ only in appearance.

Cactus Lamp.name: Cactus Lamp
Cactus Lamp.tooltip: Lamps are a type of furniture and light source. They also count as valid house lighting and can be toggled on and off by mechanisms. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 59 types of craftable Lamps, three types that are found in the Dungeon (Green, Blue, or Pink Dungeon Lamp), one found in Underworld houses (Obsidian Lamp), and one that can be dropped during a Pirate Invasion (Golden Lamp). Most lamps are dislodged by liquids, but Obsidian Lamp and Ash Wood Lamp are not dislodged by Lava. The Tiki Torch shares its Tile ID with the rest of these Lamps. Also see Lamp Post ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions) which does not count as valid House lighting.)

Brain of Cthulhu Mask.name: Brain of Cthulhu Mask

They are worn in the social head slot. Each boss has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance to drop its own mask in all difficulties, with the following exceptions: The Skeletron Mask has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to drop from Skeletron's Treasure Bag. The Dark Mage Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 1) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Dark Mage. The Ogre Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 2) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Ogre.

Stone Slab.name: Stone Slab
Stone Slab.tooltip: The Stone Slab is a block similar in appearance to regular stone, but smoother, and the texture is made up of much larger bricks. It is extremely easy to produce, although it requires a Heavy Assembler which cannot easily be obtained very early on. Stone Slabs are more efficient to build with than Gray Bricks due to their recipe.

Sandstone Slab.name: Sandstone Slab
Sandstone Slab.tooltip: Sandstone Slab is a building material which is similar in appearance to Sandstone Bricks, but darker and larger. Unlike most other building blocks (Stone Slabs in particular), the Sandstone Slab does not have a wall counterpart. As Sand is affected by gravity, Sandstone Slabs can be used instead of sand when building sand-related structures, as they look almost identical.

Frog.name: Frog
Frog.tooltip: The Frog is a harmless critter that spawns in the Jungle at any time. When in water, Frogs will swim along the water's surface. Frogs will occasionally croak when nearby. The Frog has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Frog can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Frog Cage). Once crafted, the Frog cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The Frog can be spawned by the Frog Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Frog to spawn in place of an ordinary one. There is also a 1/30 (3.33%) chance to spawn a Mystic Frog(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) in place of an ordinary one.

Mallard Duck.name: Mallard Duck
Mallard Duck.tooltip: The Duck and Mallard Duck are critters. They can usually only spawn in the middle third of the above-ground world, or in areas near an NPC's house if water is present. They only appear in pools of water, regardless of their size or if they are naturally generated. They quite frequently make a "quack" sound when nearby. Ducks may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details. Ducks will passively wander the surface until they fall a certain distance or are submerged, at which point they will switch to their alternate flying form, where they will fly in a given direction for a certain amount of time before landing and switching back to their passive form. Despite their spawn conditions, they do not prioritize water whenever landing. Ducks have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. Ducks can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Duck / Mallard Duck Cage). Once crafted, the Ducks cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Ducks can be spawned by the Duck Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.

Living Wood Bookcase.name: Living Wood Bookcase
Living Wood Bookcase.tooltip: Bookcases are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station used for the crafting of three Hardmode magic weapons (the Crystal Storm, Cursed Flames, and Golden Shower) as well as the Librarian furniture out of Librarian Blocks. Bookcases also fulfill a house's table requirement. There is a total of 65 types of Bookcases: 60 craftable Bookcases, and 5 looted from the environment: one from the Underworld, three from the Dungeon, and one from the Pirate Invasion. Some bookcases can also be found in Underground Cabins; their style follows the theme of the cabin where they are found.

Living Wood Bed.name: Living Wood Bed
Living Wood Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration. Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it. Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.

Living Wood Lantern.name: Living Wood Lantern
Living Wood Lantern.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Living Wood Candle.name: Living Wood Candle
Living Wood Candle.tooltip: Candles are a type of furniture and light source. Candles can only be placed on flat-surface items. Candles will produce light underwater if placed and can be toggled on and off with ⚷ Open / Activate and by mechanisms. Certain types of candles provide buffs or debuffs. The Water Candle is a special type of candle found in Dungeons which increases enemy spawn rates by 33% and the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50% when placed or held. The Peace Candle reduces spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%, in contrast to the Water Candle. The Shadow Candle(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns in the area. For Water Candles and Peace Candles, multiple candles cannot stack, even if one is placed and the other is held.

Black Scorpion.name: Black Scorpion
Black Scorpion.tooltip: The Scorpion and Black Scorpion are harmless critters that are most commonly found in a Desert. For detailed spawning conditions, see Notes. Scorpions have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. Scorpions can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Scorpion/Black Scorpion Cage). Once crafted, the Scorpions cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. Scorpions can be used as bait for fishing, with 10% (regular) / 15% (black) bait power. Scorpions can be spawned by the Scorpion Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.

Bunny Cage.name: Bunny Cage
Bunny Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters. A critter caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item. Gold cages are regular cages containing gold critters. Aside from their higher sell value and rarity, they are the same as regular cages. Placed cages are partially transparent. They can be stacked on top of each other, but no other types of furniture can be placed on a cage. Players can stand on top of cages like platforms, even though they are otherwise background furniture.

Crimson Seeds.name: Crimson Seeds
Crimson Seeds.tooltip: Crimson Seeds are seeds used to plant Crimson grass on Dirt Blocks, which will then spread The Crimson in all directions. They drop from the Eye of Cthulhu and can be purchased from the Dryad for 5 Silver each during a Blood Moon in a world with Crimson. In a world with Corruption, Crimson Seeds can be purchased from the Dryad if she is spoken to in a Hardmode Graveyard. Crimson Seeds can be used to farm Vicious Mushrooms and may be used to spread Crimson in Corrupt worlds. Crimson Seeds can also be planted on Mud Blocks to create Crimson Jungle grass.

Shroomite Digging Claw.name: Shroomite Digging Claw
Shroomite Digging Claw.tooltip: The Shroomite Digging Claw is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pickaxe and axe. It can mine blocks up to Chlorophyte Ore. It is the pickaxe with the fastest mining speed. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Ammo Box.name: Ammo Box
Ammo Box.tooltip: The Ammo Box is a furniture item. It can be purchased from the Arms Dealer for 10 Gold in Hardmode. Placing and pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Ammo Box grants the Ammo Box buff, which provides ranged weapons with a 1/5 (20%) chance per shot not to consume ammunition. This lasts until the player dies or leaves the world. The buff can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). Unlike equipment buff items, the Ammo Box must be placed in order to activate the buff. It can be mined with a pickaxe or drill and picked up again, even while the buff is active, which will not cancel the buff. Placement is only dependent on an adequate space of 2×2 tiles being available.

By throwing a butterfly jar into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the butterfly as an item.  Butterfly jars function the same way as cages for other critters. They have an animated sprite when placed down, and the butterflies will fly around inside the jars.

Flesh Cloning Vat.name: Flesh Cloning Vat
Flesh Cloning Vat.tooltip: The Flesh Cloning Vat is a Hardmode crafting station used to craft Flesh furniture (Crimson-themed furniture) out of Flesh Blocks. The Flesh Cloning Vat can be purchased from the Steampunker for 10 Gold, but only appears for sale in worlds that are generated with The Crimson. It can also be crafted from the Decay Chamber, its Corruption counterpart. Flesh Blocks are crafted using a Meat Grinder, so the Flesh Cloning Vat is of little use without one.

Glass Kiln.name: Glass Kiln
Glass Kiln.tooltip: The Glass Kiln is a crafting station used to craft Glass furniture out of Glass. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, it also has the ability to produce all normal Furnace recipes. Like the Furnace, it emits light when placed.

Lihzahrd Furnace.name: Lihzahrd Furnace
Lihzahrd Furnace.tooltip: The Lihzahrd Furnace is a Hardmode, post-Plantera crafting station used to craft Lihzahrd furniture out of Lihzahrd Bricks. It is always found in every Lihzahrd Chest in the Jungle Temple. Once Golem has been defeated, it can also be purchased from the Steampunker for 10 Gold when she is spoken to in the Jungle.

Living Loom.name: Living Loom
Living Loom.tooltip: The Living Loom is a crafting station used to craft Living Wood furniture out of any kind of Wood.

Sky Mill.name: Sky Mill
Sky Mill.tooltip: The Sky Mill is a crafting station used to craft the Cloud, Duskware, Harpy, and Skyware furniture sets; Rain, Rainbow, Snow, Star, and Lava Cloud blocks; and Sunplate Blocks, and Harpy Blocks. The Sky Mill has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being obtained from Skyware Chests on Floating Islands. It can also be purchased from the Steampunker for 10 Gold if she is spoken to in Space (above 65% altitude of the surface). The Sky Mill also has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being obtained from Sky or Azure Crates if the Skyblock special world seed is active and the tile threshold is not exceeded.

Ice Machine.name: Ice Machine
Ice Machine.tooltip: The Ice Machine is a crafting station used to craft Frozen furniture out of Ice Blocks and Snow furniture out of Snow Blocks. The Ice Machine has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from Frozen Chests in the Ice biome. On  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, it can also be purchased from the Steampunker for 10 Gold while in the Snow biome.

Beetle Helmet.name: Beetle Helmet
Beetle Helmet.tooltip: Beetle armor is a Hardmode, post-Golem melee armor set consisting of the Beetle Helmet and Beetle Leggings, as well as two different chestpieces: the Beetle Scale Mail and Beetle Shell, providing offensive and defensive bonuses respectively. Crafting the full set with one chestpiece requires a total of 18 Beetle Husks and a full set of Turtle armor (54 Chlorophyte Bars (270 Chlorophyte Ore), and 3 Turtle Shells). Crafting all four pieces requires a total of 26 Beetle Husks, 78 Chlorophyte Bars (390 Chlorophyte Ore), and 4 Turtle Shells. The full set grants the following effects while equipped:

Steampunk Boiler.name: Steampunk Boiler
Steampunk Boiler.tooltip: The Steampunk Boiler is a Hardmode crafting station used to craft Steampunk furniture out of Cogs. The Steampunk Boiler can be purchased from the Steampunker for 10 Gold, once the Eye of Cthulhu, Eater of Worlds/Brain of Cthulhu and Skeletron have been defeated.

Honey Dispenser.name: Honey Dispenser
Honey Dispenser.tooltip: The Honey Dispenser is a crafting station used to craft Honey furniture out of Honey Blocks. The Honey Dispenser has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being obtained from Ivy Chests in the Underground Jungle. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, it can also be purchased from the Steampunker for 10 Gold in the Jungle.

Penguin.name: Penguin
Penguin.tooltip: The Penguin is a harmless critter that only spawns in the Snow biome and may spawn with different colors. The Penguin has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Penguin can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Penguin Cage). Once crafted, the Penguin cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The Penguin can be spawned by the Penguin Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so. During a Blood Moon, or when hit with Vile/Vicious Powder, Penguins will turn into Corrupt Penguins or Vicious Penguins.

Penguin Cage.name: Penguin Cage
Penguin Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters. A critter caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item. Gold cages are regular cages containing gold critters. Aside from their higher sell value and rarity, they are the same as regular cages. Placed cages are partially transparent. They can be stacked on top of each other, but no other types of furniture can be placed on a cage. Players can stand on top of cages like platforms, even though they are otherwise background furniture.

Worm Cage.name: Worm Cage
Worm Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters. A critter caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item. Gold cages are regular cages containing gold critters. Aside from their higher sell value and rarity, they are the same as regular cages. Placed cages are partially transparent. They can be stacked on top of each other, but no other types of furniture can be placed on a cage. Players can stand on top of cages like platforms, even though they are otherwise background furniture.

Terrarium.name: Terrarium
Terrarium.tooltip: The Terrarium is an item used to make Cages for critters caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net.

Super Mana Potion.name: Super Mana Potion
Super Mana Potion.tooltip: The Super Mana Potion is a Hardmode, post-Plantera recovery potion that restores 400 mana and inflicts the Mana Sickness debuff upon use. It is the most potent of all mana restoration items. It is the fourth and final tier of mana potion, succeeding the Lesser Mana Potion, Mana Potion, and Greater Mana Potion.

Ebonwood Fence.name: Ebonwood Fence
Ebonwood Fence.tooltip: Fences are a type of safe wall that are visually thin with most of them having transparency to allow view of the background. The only fences that have no transparency to them are Palm Fence, Rich Mahogany Fence, and Shadewood Fence. Unlike most other safe walls, they allow for wild plants and trees to grow. The safe Grass Wall, Flower Wall, and Jungle Wall are functionally identical to fences. All fences are obtained by crafting, and the Wrought Iron Fence can also be found on certain designs of the Dungeon.

Brick Layer.name: Brick Layer
Brick Layer.tooltip: The Brick Layer is a construction accessory that is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 10 Gold. While equipped, it grants +50% placement speed when placing blocks.

Extendo Grip.name: Extendo Grip
Extendo Grip.tooltip: The Extendo Grip is a construction accessory that is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 10 Gold. While equipped, it increases placement range and tool range by 2 tiles vertically and 3 tiles horizontally.

Paint Sprayer.name: Paint Sprayer
Paint Sprayer.tooltip: The Paint Sprayer is a construction accessory that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 10 Gold. While equipped, or (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) when held in the inventory, it automatically applies paint or coating to any object when placing it. Like the Paintbrush and the Paint Roller, it will use the paint that is first in order in the inventory.

Portable Cement Mixer.name: Portable Cement Mixer
Portable Cement Mixer.tooltip: The Portable Cement Mixer is a construction accessory that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 10 Gold. While equipped, it grants +50% placement speed when placing walls.

Beetle Husk.name: Beetle Husk
Beetle Husk.tooltip: The Beetle Husk is a Hardmode, post-Golem crafting material dropped by Golem. Crafting all Beetle Husk items requires (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 42 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 26 Beetle Husks. Crafting one full set of Beetle armor (without wings) requires 18 Beetle Husks, meaning the player will have to fight Golem 3–5 times / 1 time to guarantee enough Beetle Husks for a full set.

Celestial Magnet.name: Celestial Magnet
Celestial Magnet.tooltip: The Celestial Magnet is a pre-Hardmode accessory that greatly increases the pickup range for Stars. The increase in pickup range is 18.75 tiles, extending the base range of 2.625 tiles to 21.375 tiles. This effect does not stack with the Celestial Magnet's upgrades. The Celestial Magnet has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being found inside Skyware Chests on Floating Islands, as well as a 1/4 (25%) chance of being obtained from Sky Crates and Azure Crates.
Celestial Magnet.drops_summary: Azure Crate (25%), Sky Crate (25%), Skyware Chest (25%)

Celestial Emblem.name: Celestial Emblem
Celestial Emblem.tooltip: The Celestial Emblem is a Hardmode accessory that offers 15% increased magic damage and a 18.75-tile increased pickup range for Stars (21.375 tile total range).

Celestial Cuffs.name: Celestial Cuffs
Celestial Cuffs.tooltip: The Celestial Cuffs are a pre-Hardmode accessory that grant the following effects while equipped: +2 defense +40 maximum mana Increases the pickup range for Stars by 18.75 tiles. Restores mana when the player takes damage. Mana restored is equal to the damage of the attack before factoring defense and damage reduction.

Peddler's Hat.name: Peddler's Hat
Peddler's Hat.tooltip: The Peddler's Hat is a vanity item that always drops from the Traveling Merchant if he is killed. It appears identical to the hat that the Traveling Merchant wears. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) When dropped into Shimmer, it turns into a Peddler's Satchel.

Pulse Bow.name: Pulse Bow
Pulse Bow.tooltip: The Pulse Bow is a Hardmode bow that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 45 Gold after defeating all three mechanical bosses. When used, it converts any type of arrow into a high-velocity Pulse Bolt. The Pulse Bolt is unaffected by gravity, can either pierce enemies or bounce off blocks up to five times, and travels for 3.33 seconds before dissipating. The Pulse Bow also has a base 11% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Large Dynasty Lantern.name: Large Dynasty Lantern
Large Dynasty Lantern.tooltip: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers come in many varieties which differ only in appearance and sell value. All chandeliers can be picked up using a pickaxe, drill, or explosives. Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.

Dynasty Lamp.name: Dynasty Lamp
Dynasty Lamp.tooltip: Lamps are a type of furniture and light source. They also count as valid house lighting and can be toggled on and off by mechanisms. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 59 types of craftable Lamps, three types that are found in the Dungeon (Green, Blue, or Pink Dungeon Lamp), one found in Underworld houses (Obsidian Lamp), and one that can be dropped during a Pirate Invasion (Golden Lamp). Most lamps are dislodged by liquids, but Obsidian Lamp and Ash Wood Lamp are not dislodged by Lava. The Tiki Torch shares its Tile ID with the rest of these Lamps. Also see Lamp Post ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions) which does not count as valid House lighting.)

Dynasty Lantern.name: Dynasty Lantern
Dynasty Lantern.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Large Dynasty Candle.name: Large Dynasty Candle
Large Dynasty Candle.tooltip: Candelabras are a type of furniture and light source that emits light when placed on a flat surface such as blocks, platforms, and flat furniture items. It is not destroyed by water. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 23 /  12 craftable and 5 looted variations of the Candelabra.

Dynasty Chair.name: Dynasty Chair
Dynasty Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Dynasty Work Bench.name: Dynasty Work Bench
Dynasty Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Dynasty Chest.name: Dynasty Chest
Dynasty Chest.tooltip: Chests are a type of furniture functioning as storage items. They are accessed using ⚷ Open / Activate and can store up to 40 item stacks in rows of  10×4 /   8×5. In addition to many being craftable, a number of Chests are placed in random locations during world generation. The loot contained in these Chests is determined during world generation, and will not change if the world enters Hardmode. Chests cannot be broken with items inside (the blocks a filled Chest is placed on would also have this trait). However, the Block Swap feature allows the player to change the type of a Chest without having to destroy it. Some types of Chests can be locked by the player using a Chest Lock. When doing so, they will require a key to open again. There are 23 varieties of naturally-occurring Chests (12 of which cannot be crafted), 53 that can only be crafted, and 1 purchasable Chest, for a total of 77 Chest types.

Dynasty Bed.name: Dynasty Bed
Dynasty Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration. Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 craftable Beds and 5 that can be acquired from the environment. All Beds are functionally identical and differ only in appearance.

Dynasty Bathtub.name: Dynasty Bathtub
Dynasty Bathtub.tooltip: Bathtubs are furniture items which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 65 / (Old-gen console version) 16 / (3DS version) 11 Bathtub types, all being functionally identical but presenting different appearances.

Dynasty Bookcase.name: Dynasty Bookcase
Dynasty Bookcase.tooltip: Bookcases are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station used for the crafting of three Hardmode magic weapons (the Crystal Storm, Cursed Flames, and Golden Shower) as well as the Librarian furniture out of Librarian Blocks. Bookcases also fulfill a house's table requirement. There is a total of 65 types of Bookcases: 60 craftable Bookcases, and 5 looted from the environment: one from the Underworld, three from the Dungeon, and one from the Pirate Invasion. Some bookcases can also be found in Underground Cabins; their style follows the theme of the cabin where they are found.

Dynasty Cup.name: Dynasty Cup
Dynasty Cup.tooltip: Cups are a type of decorative furniture that can be placed on a table, Work Bench, or other flat furniture item. Once placed, all cups function as Placed Bottle crafting stations. There are four cup variants. Three are crafted and one (the Chalice) is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 50 Silver.

Dynasty Bowl.name: Dynasty Bowl
Dynasty Bowl.tooltip: Bowls are a type of decorative furniture that can be placed on flat-surface items. Unlike plates, food cannot be placed in bowls. Only the regular Bowl can be used in crafting. The regular Bowl can also occasionally be found in the Dungeon on top of Tables and Work Benches.

Dynasty Candle.name: Dynasty Candle
Dynasty Candle.tooltip: Candles are a type of furniture and light source. Candles can only be placed on flat-surface items. Candles will produce light underwater if placed and can be toggled on and off with ⚷ Open / Activate and by mechanisms. Certain types of candles provide buffs or debuffs. The Water Candle is a special type of candle found in Dungeons which increases enemy spawn rates by 33% and the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50% when placed or held. The Peace Candle reduces spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%, in contrast to the Water Candle. The Shadow Candle(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns in the area. For Water Candles and Peace Candles, multiple candles cannot stack, even if one is placed and the other is held.

Dynasty Clock.name: Dynasty Clock
Dynasty Clock.tooltip: Grandfather Clocks are furniture items which provide information about the in-game time. If a player is nearby a Grandfather Clock (about 80 tiles horizontally and 50 tiles vertically), the time is displayed on the right side of the screen, underneath the minimap. The time is rounded to the last hour, similar to Tin and Copper Watches, but pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it will show precise time in minutes as a status message on the bottom left corner. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 21 /  5 craftable versions and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 5 / (Old-gen console version) 2 noncraftable (but still lootable) versions. The regular Grandfather Clock can rarely be found in Underground Cabins. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.
