Honey Work Bench.name: Honey Work Bench
Honey Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Frozen Work Bench.name: Frozen Work Bench
Frozen Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Steampunk Work Bench.name: Steampunk Work Bench
Steampunk Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Glass Piano.name: Glass Piano
Glass Piano.tooltip: Pianos are a type of furniture which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 15 /  10 craftable Pianos, and 5 non-craftable Pianos that can be found in the Dungeon, Ruined Houses, and Pirate Invasion event. Some Pianos can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin that they are found in.

Honey Piano.name: Honey Piano
Honey Piano.tooltip: Pianos are a type of furniture which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 15 /  10 craftable Pianos, and 5 non-craftable Pianos that can be found in the Dungeon, Ruined Houses, and Pirate Invasion event. Some Pianos can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin that they are found in.

Steampunk Piano.name: Steampunk Piano
Steampunk Piano.tooltip: Pianos are a type of furniture which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 15 /  10 craftable Pianos, and 5 non-craftable Pianos that can be found in the Dungeon, Ruined Houses, and Pirate Invasion event. Some Pianos can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin that they are found in.

Honey Cup.name: Honey Cup
Honey Cup.tooltip: Cups are a type of decorative furniture that can be placed on a table, Work Bench, or other flat furniture item. Once placed, all cups function as Placed Bottle crafting stations. There are four cup variants. Three are crafted and one (the Chalice) is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 50 Silver.

Chalice.name: Chalice
Chalice.tooltip: Cups are a type of decorative furniture that can be placed on a table, Work Bench, or other flat furniture item. Once placed, all cups function as Placed Bottle crafting stations. There are four cup variants. Three are crafted and one (the Chalice) is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 50 Silver.

Dynasty Table.name: Dynasty Table
Dynasty Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Dynasty Wood.name: Dynasty Wood
Dynasty Wood.tooltip: Dynasty Wood is a type of wood purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 50 Copper per block. When placed, it forms continuous structures with automatic frames.

Red Dynasty Shingles.name: Red Dynasty Shingles
Red Dynasty Shingles.tooltip: Dynasty Shingles are blocks purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 50 Copper each, and are only sold when the Traveling Merchant is also selling Dynasty Wood. They cannot be crafted into any background walls.

Blue Dynasty Shingles.name: Blue Dynasty Shingles
Blue Dynasty Shingles.tooltip: Dynasty Shingles are blocks purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 50 Copper each, and are only sold when the Traveling Merchant is also selling Dynasty Wood. They cannot be crafted into any background walls.

White Dynasty Wall.name: White Dynasty Wall
White Dynasty Wall.tooltip: White Dynasty Wall and Blue Dynasty Wall are background walls crafted from Dynasty Wood, which is sold by the Traveling Merchant.

Blue Dynasty Wall.name: Blue Dynasty Wall
Blue Dynasty Wall.tooltip: White Dynasty Wall and Blue Dynasty Wall are background walls crafted from Dynasty Wood, which is sold by the Traveling Merchant.

Dynasty Door.name: Dynasty Door
Dynasty Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Sake.name: Sake
Sake.tooltip: Sake is a potion that grants the Tipsy debuff when consumed, which increases many of the player's stats but lowers the player's defense for 4 minutes, twice the duration of Ale. Sake can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 5 Silver. The Tipsy debuff has the following effects: This content is transcluded from Tipsy. -4 defense +10% melee damage +2% melee critical strike chance +10% melee speed +5 Fishing Power Reduces the time to produce Poo by 66.67%

Pad Thai.name: Pad Thai
Pad Thai.tooltip: Pad Thai is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). Pad Thai can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 55 Silver.

Pho.name: Pho
Pho.tooltip: Pho is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). Pho can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 75 Silver.

Revolver.name: Revolver
Revolver.tooltip: The Revolver is a pre-Hardmode gun that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 15 Gold after a Shadow Orb or Crimson Heart has been smashed. Firing the Revolver just as it comes off cooldown will gradually increase its attack speed (up to 100%) and critical strike chance (up to 20%). This effect will not be triggered if the player is autofiring the weapon. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Gatligator.name: Gatligator
Gatligator.tooltip: The Gatligator is a Hardmode gun that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 35 Gold. When used, it rapidly fires bullets in a roughly 30° spread, at a varying velocity. It also has a 50% chance not to consume ammunition. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Arcane Rune Wall.name: Arcane Rune Wall
Arcane Rune Wall.tooltip: Arcane Rune Wall is a background wall that is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 Silver 50 Copper each. It is one of the few animated walls, as the runes displayed change every few seconds.

Water Gun.name: Water Gun
Water Gun.tooltip: The Water Gun is a tool that sprays a stream of water which inflicts the Wet debuff on players, enemies, and NPCs for 25 seconds. Additionally, the stream turns off most light sources, as opposed to the slime of the Slime Gun, which turns them on. The Water Gun can be used limitlessly and does not consume any ammunition or mana. The Water Gun can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 1 Gold 50 Silver and also has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to be dropped by Jungle Mimics, which spawn in worlds with the Celebration Mk 10 seed enabled. The Water Gun cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Katana.name: Katana
Katana.tooltip: The Katana is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 5 Gold. The Katana has a base 19% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Ultrabright Torch.name: Ultrabright Torch
Ultrabright Torch.tooltip: Torches are furniture items that function as light sources when placed, held, or dropped (via the Throw button). Regular Torches can be found randomly in Chests and Pots, as a bonus drop from slimes, Torch Zombies, or purchased from the Merchant or Skeleton Merchant for 50 Copper each. Placing at least 101 Torches in close proximity below the surface layer in any biome will start the Torch God mini-event. Completing the event will grant the Torch God's Favor, which allows the player to automatically convert ordinary Torches to one of the biome types.

Magic Hat.name: Magic Hat
Magic Hat.tooltip: The Magic Hat is a pre-Hardmode armor piece that can be equipped in the helmet slot. While equipped, it grants +2 defense and increases the player's magic damage and magic critical strike chance by 6% each. It is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 3 Gold. The Magic Hat is part of the Wizard set, which further consists of a Mystic Robe or any gem-augmented Robe. The Wizard set provides a Set Bonus of +60 maximum mana with the Magic Hat equipped. The Magic Hat's alternative is the Wizard Hat.

Diamond Ring.name: Diamond Ring
Diamond Ring.tooltip: The Diamond Ring is a vanity accessory. When worn, it places a blue dot on each of the player's wrists. It is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 Platinum. The Diamond Ring cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Gi.name: Gi
Gi.tooltip: The Gi is an armor item that can be equipped in the shirt slot. It provides 4 defense along with a 5% damage and critical strike chance boost to weapons. It also provides a 10% melee and movement speed increase. It is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 Gold. The Gi will visually cover up what is equipped in the pants slot.

Kimono.name: Kimono
Kimono.tooltip: The Kimono is a vanity item purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 1 Gold.

Mystic Robe.name: Mystic Robe
Mystic Robe.tooltip: The Mystic Robe is an armor item that can be worn in the shirt slot. It provides minimal defense (2) but a 6% damage and critical strike boost to magic weapons, along with a 10% reduction in mana use. It is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 3 Gold 50 Silver. Wearing the Wizard Hat alongside the robe provides a set bonus of +10% magic critical strike chance, while wearing a Magic Hat alongside it provides a set bonus of +60 Mana. Any leg-slot equipment can be worn with these set bonuses intact.

Beetle Wings.name: Beetle Wings
Beetle Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Tiger Skin.name: Tiger Skin
Tiger Skin.tooltip: The animal skins are decorative furniture items that are used like paintings. They are purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 1 Gold each.

Leopard Skin.name: Leopard Skin
Leopard Skin.tooltip: The animal skins are decorative furniture items that are used like paintings. They are purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 1 Gold each.

Zebra Skin.name: Zebra Skin
Zebra Skin.tooltip: The animal skins are decorative furniture items that are used like paintings. They are purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 1 Gold each.

Crimson Cloak.name: Crimson Cloak
Crimson Cloak.tooltip: Capes are vanity accessories which provide no stats or bonuses. Most are purchased from the Traveling Merchant, though the Hunter Cloak(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can also be purchased from the Clothier and the Prince Cape(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is exclusively sold by the Princess(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

Mysterious Cape.name: Mysterious Cape
Mysterious Cape.tooltip: Capes are vanity accessories which provide no stats or bonuses. Most are purchased from the Traveling Merchant, though the Hunter Cloak(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can also be purchased from the Clothier and the Prince Cape(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is exclusively sold by the Princess(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

Red Cape.name: Red Cape
Red Cape.tooltip: Capes are vanity accessories which provide no stats or bonuses. Most are purchased from the Traveling Merchant, though the Hunter Cloak(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can also be purchased from the Clothier and the Prince Cape(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is exclusively sold by the Princess(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

Winter Cape.name: Winter Cape
Winter Cape.tooltip: Capes are vanity accessories which provide no stats or bonuses. Most are purchased from the Traveling Merchant, though the Hunter Cloak(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can also be purchased from the Clothier and the Prince Cape(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is exclusively sold by the Princess(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

Frozen Chair.name: Frozen Chair
Frozen Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Wood Fishing Pole.name: Wood Fishing Pole
Wood Fishing Pole.tooltip: Fishing poles are tools used with bait for fishing.

Bass.name: Bass
Bass.tooltip: Bass are a type of fish which are found plentifully by fishing in any biome that is not the Ocean or Desert in any layer.

Reinforced Fishing Pole.name: Reinforced Fishing Pole
Reinforced Fishing Pole.tooltip: Fishing poles are tools used with bait for fishing.

Fiberglass Fishing Pole.name: Fiberglass Fishing Pole
Fiberglass Fishing Pole.tooltip: Fishing poles are tools used with bait for fishing.

Fisher of Souls.name: Fisher of Souls
Fisher of Souls.tooltip: Fishing poles are tools used with bait for fishing.

Golden Fishing Rod.name: Golden Fishing Rod
Golden Fishing Rod.tooltip: Fishing poles are tools used with bait for fishing.

Mechanic's Rod.name: Mechanic's Rod
Mechanic's Rod.tooltip: Fishing poles are tools used with bait for fishing.

Sitting Duck's Fishing Pole.name: Sitting Duck's Fishing Pole
Sitting Duck's Fishing Pole.tooltip: Fishing poles are tools used with bait for fishing.

Trout.name: Trout
Trout.tooltip: Trout are a type of fish which are found plentifully by fishing in the Ocean in the Sky or Surface layers.

Salmon.name: Salmon
Salmon.tooltip: Salmon are a type of fish which are found plentifully by fishing in a Forest in the Sky or Surface layers. They can only be caught in lakes with more than 1,000 tiles of water.

Atlantic Cod.name: Atlantic Cod
Atlantic Cod.tooltip: Atlantic Cods are a type of fish which are found commonly by fishing in a Snow biome in any layer.

Tuna.name: Tuna
Tuna.tooltip: Tuna are a type of fish which are found commonly by fishing in the Ocean in the Sky or Surface layers.

Red Snapper.name: Red Snapper
Red Snapper.tooltip: Red Snappers are a type of fish which are found commonly by fishing in the Ocean in the Sky or Surface layers.

Neon Tetra.name: Neon Tetra
Neon Tetra.tooltip: Neon Tetras are a type of fish which are found commonly by fishing in the Jungle in any layer. They sell for twice what other fish in their catch quality do, and on the  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version they have no use except for this sell price.

Armored Cavefish.name: Armored Cavefish
Armored Cavefish.tooltip: Armored Cavefish are a type of fish which are found uncommonly by fishing in the Underground, Cavern, and Underworld layers, in any biome (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) except the Desert. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners and Endurance Potions.

Damselfish.name: Damselfish
Damselfish.tooltip: Damselfish are a type of fish which are found uncommonly by fishing in pure Space layer. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners and Calming Potions.

Crimson Tigerfish.name: Crimson Tigerfish
Crimson Tigerfish.tooltip: Crimson Tigerfish are a type of fish which are found commonly by fishing in The Crimson in any layer. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners and Heartreach Potions.

Frost Minnow.name: Frost Minnow
Frost Minnow.tooltip: Frost Minnows are a type of fish which are found uncommonly by fishing in a Snow biome in any layer. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners and Warmth Potions.

Princess Fish.name: Princess Fish
Princess Fish.tooltip: Princess Fish are a type of Hardmode fish which are found uncommonly by fishing in The Hallow in any layer. They are used to craft Love Potions and Seafood Dinners(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

Golden Carp.name: Golden Carp
Golden Carp.tooltip: Golden Carp are a type of fish which are found extremely rarely by fishing in any biome in the Underground, Cavern and Underworld layers, with the exception of the Desert. They have an extraordinarily high sell value of 10 Gold.
quality_issues: NO_ITEM_NAME: 'Quite shiny. This will probably sell well.'

Specular Fish.name: Specular Fish
Specular Fish.tooltip: Specular Fish are a type of fish that are commonly found by fishing in a Forest or Snow biome in the Underground, Cavern, and Underworld layers. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners, Recall Potions, and Wormhole Potions.

Prismite.name: Prismite
Prismite.tooltip: Prismites are a type of Hardmode fish which are found rarely by fishing in The Hallow in any layer. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Lifeforce Potions.

Variegated Lardfish.name: Variegated Lardfish
Variegated Lardfish.tooltip: Variegated Lardfish are a type of fish which are found uncommonly by fishing in the Underground Jungle. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners and Summoning Potions.

Flarefin Koi.name: Flarefin Koi
Flarefin Koi.tooltip: Flarefin Koi are a type of pre-Hardmode ((Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)) / Hardmode ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions)) fish which are found very rarely by fishing in any biome in any layer, but only in lava. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners and Inferno Potions.

Double Cod.name: Double Cod
Double Cod.tooltip: Double Cod are a type of fish which are found uncommonly by fishing in the Sky or Surface layers of the Jungle. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners and Ammo Reservation Potions.

Honeyfin.name: Honeyfin
Honeyfin.tooltip: The Honeyfin is a pre-Hardmode fish and recovery potion that restores 120 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for 60 seconds when used. This duration can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths. It can also be used to craft Seafood Dinners. The Honeyfin can only be fished from honey, e.g. in Bee Hives within the Underground Jungle. Other than the Bumblebee Tuna that can be found during Angler quests, Honeyfins are the only fish that can be caught in honey.

Obsidifish.name: Obsidifish
Obsidifish.tooltip: Obsidifish are a type of pre-Hardmode ((Desktop, Console and Mobile versions)) / Hardmode ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions)) fish which are found rarely by fishing in any biome in any layer, but only in lava. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners, Inferno Potions, and Potions of Return.

Shrimp.name: Shrimp
Shrimp.tooltip: Shrimp are a type of fishing catch which are found uncommonly by fishing in the Ocean in the Sky or Surface layers.

Chaos Fish.name: Chaos Fish
Chaos Fish.tooltip: Chaos Fish are a type of fish which are found rarely by fishing in the Underground Hallow. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and Teleportation Potions.

Ebonkoi.name: Ebonkoi
Ebonkoi.tooltip: Ebonkoi are a type of fish which are found uncommonly by fishing in The Corruption in any layer. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners and Wrath Potions.

Hemopiranha.name: Hemopiranha
Hemopiranha.tooltip: Hemopiranha are a type of fish which are found uncommonly by fishing in The Crimson in any layer. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners and Rage Potions.

Rockfish.name: Rockfish
Rockfish.tooltip: The Rockfish is a pre-Hardmode hammer. It can be fished from the Underground layer within any biome. Its hammer power and tool speed are equal to that of the Molten Hamaxe. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Stinkfish.name: Stinkfish
Stinkfish.tooltip: Stinkfish are a type of fish which are found rarely by fishing in any biome in the Underground layer or below, with the exception of The Corruption, The Hallow and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) the Desert. They are used to craft Seafood Dinners and Stink Potions.

Mining Potion.name: Mining Potion
Mining Potion.tooltip: The Mining Potion is a buff potion which grants the Mining buff when consumed. The buff increases mining speed by 25%. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Mining Potions can be found in pots, chests, and crates, and have a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes.
Mining Potion.drops_summary: Azure Crate (4.17%), Baby Slime (0.18%), Black Slime (0.18%), +34 more

Heartreach Potion.name: Heartreach Potion
Heartreach Potion.tooltip: The Heartreach Potion is a buff potion which grants the Heartreach buff when consumed. The buff increases the pickup range of life recovery Hearts by 15.625 tiles, from 2.625 tiles to a total of 18.25 tiles. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Heartreach Potions can be found in Pots and crates.
Heartreach Potion.drops_summary: Most crates (4.17%), Golden Crate (6.67%), Iron Crate (3.13%), +5 more

Calming Potion.name: Calming Potion
Calming Potion.tooltip: The Calming Potion is a buff potion which grants the Calm buff when consumed. The buff reduces the enemy spawn rate by 39%, and the maximum number of enemies on-screen is reduced by 40%. This lasts for 12 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Calming Potions can be found in Pots and Crates.

Builder Potion.name: Builder Potion
Builder Potion.tooltip: The Builder Potion is a buff potion that grants the Builder buff when consumed. It grants the following effects: +1 placement range +25% placement speed when placing blocks and walls This lasts for 45 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Builder Potions can be found in pots and chests.

Titan Potion.name: Titan Potion
Titan Potion.tooltip: The  Titan Potion is a buff potion which grants the Titan buff when consumed. The buff increases the amount of knockback the player inflicts on enemies by 50%. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Titan Potions can be found in Pots in the Underworld, as well as in Chests.

Flipper Potion.name: Flipper Potion
Flipper Potion.tooltip: The Flipper Potion is a buff potion which grants the Flipper buff when consumed. The buff allows the player to move horizontally and vertically through water, lava, and honey without slowing down, and also allows the player to swim without equipping any swimming accessories, such as the Flipper. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Flipper Potions can be found in Pots and crates.

Summoning Potion.name: Summoning Potion
Summoning Potion.tooltip: The Summoning Potion is a buff potion which grants the Summoning buff when consumed. The buff increases the player's minion slots by 1. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().

Dangersense Potion.name: Dangersense Potion
Dangersense Potion.tooltip: The Dangersense Potion is a buff potion which grants the Dangersense buff when consumed. The buff reveals hazardous traps, blocks, and objects that can potentially harm or impede the player by highlighting them in red, even in complete darkness. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Dangersense Potions can be found in Pots, Chests, and crates.
Dangersense Potion.drops_summary: Gold Chest (9.52%), Pearlwood Crate (1.43%), Wooden Crate (1.43%)

Purple Clubberfish.name: Purple Clubberfish
Purple Clubberfish.tooltip: The Purple Clubberfish is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that can be obtained by fishing in The Corruption with a 1/10 (10%) chance with 100 Fishing Power, up to a maximum 1/4 (25%) chance with 300 Fishing Power. It has a 1/2 (50%) chance to inflict the Confused debuff for 1–3 seconds on hit. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Obsidian Swordfish.name: Obsidian Swordfish
Obsidian Swordfish.tooltip: The Obsidian Swordfish is a Hardmode spear that is obtained via fishing in lava, by using any lava fishing method (including lava bait or Lavaproof Fishing Hook). When thrust, it fires 1–3 piercing gravity-affected embers that each deal 50% of the weapon's damage (35 base damage) and inflict the Hellfire debuff for 3-6 seconds. The embers can hit a total of 3 enemies and do not inflict any knockback. The Obsidian Swordfish also has a 24% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Swordfish.name: Swordfish
Swordfish.tooltip: The Swordfish is a pre-Hardmode spear obtainable through fishing in the Ocean biome. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Iron Fence.name: Iron Fence
Iron Fence.tooltip: Fences are a type of safe wall that are visually thin with most of them having transparency to allow view of the background. The only fences that have no transparency to them are Palm Fence, Rich Mahogany Fence, and Shadewood Fence. Unlike most other safe walls, they allow for wild plants and trees to grow. The safe Grass Wall, Flower Wall, and Jungle Wall are functionally identical to fences. All fences are obtained by crafting, and the Wrought Iron Fence can also be found on certain designs of the Dungeon.

Wooden Crate.name: Wooden Crate
Wooden Crate.tooltip: The Wooden Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can be obtained by fishing in any biome, at any height. It is the lowest tier of standard crate, having the least value if sold directly. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Pearlwood Crate.

Iron Crate.name: Iron Crate
Iron Crate.tooltip: The Iron Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can be obtained by fishing in any biome, at any height. It is the middle tier of standard crate. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Mythril Crate.

Golden Crate.name: Golden Crate
Golden Crate.tooltip: The Golden Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can be obtained by fishing in any biome, at any layer. It is the highest tier of standard crate, having the greatest value if sold directly. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Titanium Crate.

Old Shoe.name: Old Shoe
Old Shoe.tooltip: Junk items are fished instead of regular fishing catches when the player's fishing conditions are particularly unfavorable. Their only use is being converted by the Extractinator or Chlorophyte Extractinator to obtain low-level bait. There are three different junk items, all of which are functionally identical: Old Shoe, Seaweed, and Tin Can. Junk items can only be caught if either of the following two conditions are met: The lake is smaller than 300 tiles (water) or 200 tiles (honey). The player's Fishing Power is lower than 50. If both conditions are not met (i.e., the lake size and the player's Fishing Power are both high enough), then regular fishing catches are caught instead of junk items. If both conditions are met, the chances to fish a junk item are very high (except during a Blood Moon, during which enemies will commonly be caught instead of other drops). There is a 1/8 (12.5%) chance for a Joja Cola to be fished up in place of a junk item.

Tin Can.name: Tin Can
Tin Can.tooltip: Junk items are fished instead of regular fishing catches when the player's fishing conditions are particularly unfavorable. Their only use is being converted by the Extractinator or Chlorophyte Extractinator to obtain low-level bait. There are three different junk items, all of which are functionally identical: Old Shoe, Seaweed, and Tin Can. Junk items can only be caught if either of the following two conditions are met: The lake is smaller than 300 tiles (water) or 200 tiles (honey). The player's Fishing Power is lower than 50. If both conditions are not met (i.e., the lake size and the player's Fishing Power are both high enough), then regular fishing catches are caught instead of junk items. If both conditions are met, the chances to fish a junk item are very high (except during a Blood Moon, during which enemies will commonly be caught instead of other drops). There is a 1/8 (12.5%) chance for a Joja Cola to be fished up in place of a junk item.

Minecart Track.name: Minecart Track
Minecart Track.tooltip: Minecart Tracks are placeable furniture-type blocks that allow for rapid transportation over long distances. They form a continuous track when placed next to each other, and form slopes when placed diagonally. Although they cannot be walked on, they can be grappled using a hook. Minecart Tracks generate in large quantities in Abandoned Minecart Tracks(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), but can also be obtained via crafting. When the player is near a Minecart Track, pressing the Quick Mount hotkey or pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on a point on the track causes a Minecart to spawn, which the player is automatically placed in. Once inside, the ▶ Right and ◀ Left direction keys either accelerate, decelerate, or reverse the cart's movement. The cart will maintain its current speed and direction if no keys are pressed and no obstacles are reached. The cart can also "jump" with the ↷ Jump key. To exit the Minecart (which causes the Minecart to despawn), the player can use a hook, press the Quick Mount hotkey, or cancel the buff ( right-clicking the icon,   selecting the icon and canceling it in the equipment menu,  double-tapping the icon, or  canceling the buff from the buffs screen). The Minecart will also despawn if the player jumps off the tracks, lands on blocks, and attempts to move sideways. Weapons and tools, as well as most other items except hooks, can be used while riding a Minecart. The player can alternatively move on top of Minecart Tracks using Roller Skates.

Reaver Shark.name: Reaver Shark
Reaver Shark.tooltip: The Reaver Shark is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe obtained by fishing in the Ocean. It can mine blocks up to Demonite Ore, Crimtane Ore, and Obsidian. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Sawtooth Shark.name: Sawtooth Shark
Sawtooth Shark.tooltip: The Sawtooth Shark is a pre-Hardmode chainsaw that can be fished from an Ocean biome. It can be caught at a rate of 1/100 (1%) with 50% Fishing Power and 1/50 (2%) with 100% Fishing Power. In terms of axe power, it is equal to the Cobalt Chainsaw. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Minecart.name: Minecart
Minecart.tooltip: Minecarts are mounts that allow players to ride on Minecart Tracks. When the player is near a Minecart Track, pressing the Quick Mount hotkey or pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on a point on the track causes a Minecart to spawn, which the player is automatically placed in. Once inside, the ▶ Right and ◀ Left direction keys either accelerate, decelerate, or reverse the cart's movement. The cart will maintain its current speed and direction if no keys are pressed and no obstacles are reached. The cart can also "jump" with the ↷ Jump key. Weapons and tools, as well as most other items except hooks, can be used while riding a Minecart. The Minecart will deal damage to enemies it collides with and knock them back, with higher potency at higher speeds (see below for details). To exit the Minecart (which causes the Minecart to despawn), the player can use a hook, press the Quick Mount hotkey, or cancel the buff  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Minecart will also despawn if the player jumps off the tracks, lands on blocks, and attempts to move sideways. By default, a Wooden Minecart is spawned for the player. This can be overridden by equipping other Minecart items in the Minecart equipment slot of the player's inventory. The corresponding dye slot allows dyeing the Minecart. Using a Minecart Upgrade Kit will significantly boost the speed of all Minecarts, equip them with a laser that fires at nearby enemies, and increase the player's defense while moving. The boost effect is permanently available after using the item, though it can be toggled on and off through a probe icon next to the Minecart slot.

Ammo Reservation Potion.name: Ammo Reservation Potion
Ammo Reservation Potion.tooltip: The Ammo Reservation Potion is a buff potion which grants the Ammo Reservation buff when consumed. The buff reduces the chance of consuming any ammunition by 20%. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().

Lifeforce Potion.name: Lifeforce Potion
Lifeforce Potion.tooltip: The  Lifeforce Potion is a buff potion that grants the Lifeforce buff when consumed. The buff increases the player's health capacity by up to 20% (see below for details). This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). Maximum health granted by the Lifeforce buff will not be counted by health conditions of certain game mechanics (e.g. the spawning of Nurse, Eye of Cthulhu, and Goblin Army, etc.). The player have to increase their permanent maximum health (with permanent boosters) to fulfill these conditions.

Endurance Potion.name: Endurance Potion
Endurance Potion.tooltip: The Endurance Potion is a buff potion that grants the Endurance buff when consumed, which provides +10% damage reduction. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().

Rage Potion.name: Rage Potion
Rage Potion.tooltip: The Rage Potion is a buff potion which grants the Rage buff when consumed. The buff increases the player's critical strike chance by 10%. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().

Inferno Potion.name: Inferno Potion
Inferno Potion.tooltip: The Inferno Potion is a buff potion that grants the Inferno buff when consumed. The buff casts a spinning ring of fire around the player that deals 20 damage per second and inflicts the Hellfire debuff for 2 seconds to all enemies inside of it while also giving off light. Critters and other passive NPCs are unaffected. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). In addition to being crafted, Inferno Potions can be found in Shadow Chests.

Wrath Potion.name: Wrath Potion
Wrath Potion.tooltip: The Wrath Potion is a buff potion which grants the Wrath buff when consumed. The buff increases the damage dealt by melee, ranged, magic, and summon weapons by 10%. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().

Recall Potion.name: Recall Potion
Recall Potion.tooltip: The Recall Potion is a potion that will teleport the player to their spawn point 0.167 seconds (10 ticks) after being used. It is identical in function to a Magic Mirror or Ice Mirror, but significantly faster in use time.  In addition to being crafted, Recall Potions can be found in Pots and Chests, and have a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes.
Recall Potion.drops_summary: Most slimes (0.27%), Chest (66.67%), Gold Chest (66.67%), +1 more

Teleportation Potion.name: Teleportation Potion
Teleportation Potion.tooltip: The Teleportation Potion is a potion that teleports the user to a random location. In addition to being crafted, it can be found in Chests located in the Cavern layer and in Shadow Chests. In choosing a destination, the following rules apply:Verify The player will always be placed on top of a solid block and never inside blocks. The player can never be placed in front of a natural, below-surface Dungeon wall before Skeletron has been defeated. The player can never be placed in front of a natural, below-surface Lihzahrd Brick Wall (i.e., in the Jungle Temple) before Plantera has been defeated.

Love Potion.name: Love Potion
Love Potion.tooltip: The Love Potion is a Hardmode thrown potion that functions similarly to Thrown Water. Upon colliding with solid blocks, it inflicts the Lovestruck debuff on players (including the user), enemies, critters, and NPCs within a radius of 9 tiles, causing them to emit red hearts for 30 seconds. It also increases affected NPCs' happiness by 10% for the duration of the effect. Its counterpart is the Stink Potion.

Stink Potion.name: Stink Potion
Stink Potion.tooltip: The Stink Potion is a thrown potion that functions similarly to Thrown Waters. Upon colliding with solid blocks, it inflicts the Stinky debuff on players (including the user), enemies, critters, and NPCs within a radius of 9 tiles. Its counterpart is the Love Potion.

Fishing Potion.name: Fishing Potion
Fishing Potion.tooltip: The Fishing Potion is a buff potion which grants the Fishing buff when consumed. The buff increases Fishing Power by 15. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Fishing Potion can be obtained both from crafting and as a reward from the Angler for completing fishing quests.

Sonar Potion.name: Sonar Potion
Sonar Potion.tooltip: The Sonar Potion is a buff potion which grants the Sonar buff when consumed. The buff displays the name of a fishing catch above a fishing pole's bobber when it receives a bite while fishing, along with a sound effect. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Sonar Potion can be obtained both from crafting and as a reward from the Angler for completing fishing quests.

Crate Potion.name: Crate Potion
Crate Potion.tooltip: The Crate Potion is a buff potion which grants the Crate buff when consumed. The buff increases the chance of getting a crate from 1/10 (10%) to 1/4 (25%) when fishing. This lasts for 4 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().  The Crate Potion can be obtained both from crafting and as a reward from the Angler for completing fishing quests.

Shiverthorn Seeds.name: Shiverthorn Seeds
Shiverthorn Seeds.tooltip: Shiverthorn Seeds are a type of seed that can be obtained from harvesting Shiverthorns while they are blooming or using the Staff of Regrowth on a naturally grown Shiverthorns while they are fully grown. Shiverthorn will always bloom after a period of growth, and unlike other herbs, remains in-bloom permanently thereafter. Blooming Shiverthorn emits a glowing particle effect. Each plant drops 1–3 Shiverthorn Seeds when harvested while blooming. Shiverthorn Seeds can be placed on Snow Blocks and any type of Ice Blocks, empty Clay Pots, or any types of Planter Boxes, and will grow into harvestable Shiverthorns. They will grow anywhere, not just in the Snow biome, but will only yield seeds when blooming.

Shiverthorn.name: Shiverthorn
Shiverthorn.tooltip: Shiverthorn is a type of herb which appears as an icy-blue flower. It grows naturally on Snow and Ice Blocks of any type. Shiverthorn can be harvested with virtually any weapon or tool, and can be planted manually using Shiverthorn Seeds in Clay Pots and Planter Boxes, or on suitable soil tiles. Shiverthorn blooms randomly, and unlike other herbs, remains bloomed permanently thereafter. Its blooming is indicated by the blue flower and blue-green light emitted. Harvesting mature Shiverthorn yields 1 Shiverthorn item. Harvesting blooming Shiverthorn yields 1 Shiverthorn item and 1–3 Shiverthorn Seeds. Harvesting blooming Shiverthorn with the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth yields 1–2 Shiverthorns and 1–5 Shiverthorn Seeds instead. Both Shiverthorn and Shiverthorn Seeds have a chance to be obtained from the Herb Bag.

Warmth Potion.name: Warmth Potion
Warmth Potion.tooltip: The Warmth Potion is a buff potion that grants the Warmth buff when consumed, which provides +30% damage reduction from cold-themed enemies (see below). It also reduces the duration of Chilled by 75% and Frozen by 50%. This lasts for 15 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().

Fish Hook.name: Fish Hook
Fish Hook.tooltip: Hooks are a class of tools which aid the player in traversing terrain. When used, hooks fire a chain that latches to a surface or platform and pulls the player towards it. A hook is an essential tool which offers significant freedom from terrain height restrictions as well as being a fast movement option, and will often be the first major mobility tool a player acquires. A variety of hooks are available at all stages of the game (see table below). The Grapple hotkey activates the equipped hook in the player's equipment slot, or the first hook from the inventory (from left to right, top to bottom) without requiring it to be in the player's hotbar.Verify Several higher-tier hooks, such as the Ivy Whip, allow the player to grapple multiple surfaces simultaneously. If the character grapples one surface, then fires the hook a second time, another chain extends from the player without dislodging the first. Upon grappling a second surface, the player will be suspended in midair at a point midway between the two surfaces. This allows players more freedom during construction, or for navigating hazardous areas, such as above lava or Meteorite. All Journey Mode characters will spawn with the basic Grappling Hook already in their inventory.

Bee Headgear.name: Bee Headgear
Bee Headgear.tooltip: Bee armor is a pre-Hardmode summoner armor set consisting of the Bee Headgear, Bee Breastplate, and Bee Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 30 Bee Wax. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +13 defense +23% summon damage +2 minion slots

Bee Breastplate.name: Bee Breastplate
Bee Breastplate.tooltip: Bee armor is a pre-Hardmode summoner armor set consisting of the Bee Headgear, Bee Breastplate, and Bee Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 30 Bee Wax. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +13 defense +23% summon damage +2 minion slots

Bee Greaves.name: Bee Greaves
Bee Greaves.tooltip: Bee armor is a pre-Hardmode summoner armor set consisting of the Bee Headgear, Bee Breastplate, and Bee Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 30 Bee Wax. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +13 defense +23% summon damage +2 minion slots

Hornet Staff.name: Hornet Staff
Hornet Staff.tooltip: The Hornet Staff is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Hornet minion. It hovers above enemies, firing stingers that inflict the Poisoned debuff for 4–7 seconds and do not pierce. Its best modifier is Fabled.

Imp Staff.name: Imp Staff
Imp Staff.tooltip: The Imp Staff is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Flying Imp minion. It hovers near enemies, shooting fireballs that inflict the On Fire! debuff for 3–6 seconds and can pierce up to 4 times, dissipating on the 5th hit. Its best modifier is Fabled.

Queen Spider Staff.name: Queen Spider Staff
Queen Spider Staff.tooltip: The Queen Spider Staff is a Hardmode summon weapon that summons the Spider Turret sentry. It fires Spider Eggs towards enemies once per second, which can bounce and roll on blocks, and are heavily affected by gravity. The Spider Eggs deal no damage themselves, and upon colliding with enemies or after 1 second, they will break and spawn 2–4 Baby Spiders that attack enemies. The Baby Spiders will disappear upon contact with an enemy, dealing damage and inflicting the Acid Venom debuff for 2–4 seconds. If there are no enemies within range, the Baby Spiders will persist for 5 seconds before dissipating. Its best modifier is Fabled.

Angler Hat.name: Angler Hat
Angler Hat.tooltip: Angler armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Angler Hat, Angler Vest, and Angler Pants. The Hat is given by the Angler after completing 10 fishing quests, the Vest after 15, and the Pants after 20. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +4 defense +15 Fishing Power -24% enemy spawn rates and -30% maximum enemy count Angler armor pieces are interchangeable with pieces from Captain armor, still providing the set bonus. The only difference is the defense.

Angler Vest.name: Angler Vest
Angler Vest.tooltip: Angler armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Angler Hat, Angler Vest, and Angler Pants. The Hat is given by the Angler after completing 10 fishing quests, the Vest after 15, and the Pants after 20. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +4 defense +15 Fishing Power -24% enemy spawn rates and -30% maximum enemy count Angler armor pieces are interchangeable with pieces from Captain armor, still providing the set bonus. The only difference is the defense.

The Hat is given by the Angler after completing 10 fishing quests, the Vest after 15, and the Pants after 20. Spider Mask.name: Spider Mask
Spider Mask.tooltip: Spider armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Spider Mask, Spider Breastplate, and Spider Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 36 Spider Fangs. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +20 defense +28% summon damage +3 minion slots

Spider Breastplate.name: Spider Breastplate

Spider Greaves.name: Spider Greaves

High Test Fishing Line.name: High Test Fishing Line
High Test Fishing Line.tooltip: The High Test Fishing Line is an accessory that prevents fishing line from breaking while fishing when equipped. Without the High Test Fishing Line equipped, there is a 1/7 (14.29%) chance that the line will break on any reel-in that was supposed to yield a catch. The High Test Fishing Line can be acquired as a 1/34 (2.94%) chance reward for completing a fishing quest for the Angler NPC, depending on the number of completed quests and other factors (see Angler § Quest rewards for details). The Angler will not give the player a High Test Fishing Line as a reward if they already have one in their inventory or in any of their portable storage items or loadouts. However, if the player has all of the Angler's fishing and informational accessories (or their upgrades like the Angler Tackle Bag and Fish Finder) in their inventories, this rule will be ignored.

Angler Earring.name: Angler Earring
Angler Earring.tooltip: The Angler Earring is an accessory that increases the player's current Fishing Power by 10 when equipped. The Angler Earring can be acquired as a 1/34 (2.94%) chance reward for completing a fishing quest for the Angler NPC, depending on the number of completed quests and other factors (see Angler § Quest rewards for details). The Angler will not give the player an Angler Earring as a reward if they already have one in their inventory or in any of their portable storage items or loadouts. However, if the player has all of the Angler's fishing and informational accessories (or their upgrades like the Angler Tackle Bag and Fish Finder) in their inventories, this rule will be ignored.

Tackle Box.name: Tackle Box
Tackle Box.tooltip: The Tackle Box is an accessory that decreases the chance of bait consumption while fishing. The Tackle Box can be acquired as a 1/34 (2.94%) chance reward for completing a fishing quest for the Angler NPC, depending on the number of completed quests and other factors (see Angler § Quest rewards for details). The Angler will not give the player a Tackle Box as a reward if they already have one in their inventory or in any of their portable storage items or loadouts. However, if the player has all of the Angler's fishing and informational accessories (or their upgrades like the Angler Tackle Bag and Fish Finder) in their inventories, this rule will be ignored.

Blue Dungeon Piano.name: Blue Dungeon Piano
Blue Dungeon Piano.tooltip: Pianos are a type of furniture which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 15 /  10 craftable Pianos, and 5 non-craftable Pianos that can be found in the Dungeon, Ruined Houses, and Pirate Invasion event. Some Pianos can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin that they are found in.

Blue Dungeon Dresser.name: Blue Dungeon Dresser

Sofa.name: Sofa
Sofa.tooltip: Sofas are furniture items which fulfill a house's chair requirement. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Players can sit in sofas by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Players can choose to sit on the left, middle, or right positions, and thus up to 3 players can sit on a sofa at a time. Sitting on sofas gives a boost to health regeneration, similar to chairs and beds. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Sofa will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 21 craftable sofas and 5 noncraftable sofas. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Seashell Hairpin.name: Seashell Hairpin
Seashell Hairpin.tooltip: The Mermaid set is a vanity set composed of the Seashell Hairpin, Mermaid Adornment, and Mermaid Tail. The complete set is awarded randomly for completing a fishing quest for the Angler NPC. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Mermaid Adornment.name: Mermaid Adornment
Mermaid Adornment.tooltip: The Mermaid set is a vanity set composed of the Seashell Hairpin, Mermaid Adornment, and Mermaid Tail. The complete set is awarded randomly for completing a fishing quest for the Angler NPC. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Mermaid Tail.name: Mermaid Tail
Mermaid Tail.tooltip: The Mermaid set is a vanity set composed of the Seashell Hairpin, Mermaid Adornment, and Mermaid Tail. The complete set is awarded randomly for completing a fishing quest for the Angler NPC. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Zephyr Fish.name: Zephyr Fish
Zephyr Fish.tooltip: The Zephyr Fish is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Zephyr Fish pet that follows the player. (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) The pet will not teleport to the player when it is far away, unlike most other pets. The Zephyr Fish is rarely caught from fishing in any body of water. The chance to catch it is 2/3125 (0.06%) with 50% Fishing Power and 4/3125 (0.13%) with 100% Fishing Power.

Fleshcatcher.name: Fleshcatcher
Fleshcatcher.tooltip: Fishing poles are tools used with bait for fishing.

Hotline Fishing Hook.name: Hotline Fishing Hook
Hotline Fishing Hook.tooltip: Fishing poles are tools used with bait for fishing.

Frog Leg.name: Frog Leg
Frog Leg.tooltip: The Frog Leg is an accessory that can be fished in any viable body of water. It aids jumping in the following ways: Increases the player's jump speed by 1.6. The player automatically jumps while the ↷ Jump key is held. Increases the maximum safe falling distance by 10 tiles. These effects also apply with wings equipped.

Anchor.name: Anchor
Anchor.tooltip: The Anchor is a Hardmode flail that has a 3.78% chance of being found in Pearlwood Crates, obtained from fishing. When used, it fires an Anchor in an arc, which is attached to the player via a rope. The Anchor can pierce an unlimited number of enemies in its way and returns upon hitting solid blocks or after traveling for more than 50 tiles away from the player. If it has traveled for at least 0.17 seconds, it creates a shockwave upon colliding with blocks that deals 60% of the weapon's damage (42 base damage) and 150% of its knockback (base knockback of 12 (Insane)) to enemies within a 18.75×18.75-tile square area centered on the projectile. Both the Anchor and its shockwave have a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to inflict the Confused debuff for 1–2 seconds on hit. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Cooked Fish.name: Cooked Fish
Cooked Fish.tooltip: The Cooked Fish is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().

Cooked Shrimp.name: Cooked Shrimp
Cooked Shrimp.tooltip: The Cooked Shrimp is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().

Sashimi.name: Sashimi
Sashimi.tooltip: Sashimi is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().

Fuzzy Carrot.name: Fuzzy Carrot
Fuzzy Carrot.tooltip: The Fuzzy Carrot is a mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Bunny Mount. It has a top speed of 40 mph. The Fuzzy Carrot is obtained from the Angler as a reward for completing his 5th fishing quest.

Scaly Truffle.name: Scaly Truffle
Scaly Truffle.tooltip: The Scaly Truffle is a Hardmode mount-summoning item that summons a Pigron Mount that allows the player to fly for a limited time and run faster on land. The Scaly Truffle is obtained by fishing in the cavern layer of an Ice biome overlapping a Hallow, Corruption, or Crimson biome in Hardmode.

Slimy Saddle.name: Slimy Saddle
Slimy Saddle.tooltip: The Slimy Saddle is a pre-Hardmode mount-summoning item that summons a friendly Slime Mount. The Slime Mount offers increased jump height (21 tiles) and movement speed (20 mph), increases the maximum safe falling distance by 10 tiles, reduces fall damage by 50%, and enables floating on surfaces of all liquids and continuous auto-jump by holding the ↷ Jump key. Landing on an enemy while riding this mount will deal 40 summon damage and a knockback of 5 (Average), and causes the player to bounce off them. The Slime Mount is affected by summon damage bonuses. The Slimy Saddle has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by King Slime and a 1/2 (50%) chance of being found in King Slime's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.

Bee Wax.name: Bee Wax
Bee Wax.tooltip: Bee Wax is a crafting material dropped by the Queen Bee. It cannot be crafted or placed. It takes 44 to craft a set of Bee armor and the Hornet Staff, which amounts to killing Queen Bee 2–3 times.

Copper Plating Wall.name: Copper Plating Wall
Copper Plating Wall.tooltip: Copper Plating Wall is a background wall made of Copper Plating.

Stone Slab Wall.name: Stone Slab Wall
Stone Slab Wall.tooltip: Stone Slab Wall is a background wall that can be used for housings.

Sail.name: Sail
Sail.tooltip: The Sail is a type of background wall purchased from the Pirate for 50 Copper each. It is considered a valid wall for housing.

Coralstone Block.name: Coralstone Block
Coralstone Block.tooltip: Coralstone Blocks are decorative blocks. When placed, they can have one of the many kinds of coral on it. Much like Sunplate Blocks, Coralstone Blocks show a special, non-changing image if a square of nine or more are put next to each other. In this case, the image is a coral that looks much like a sponge.

Blue Jellyfish.name: Blue Jellyfish
Blue Jellyfish.tooltip: Jellyfish are enemies found in water. When underwater, they attack by propelling themselves towards the player in short bursts. When outside of water, they will be unable to move or pursue the player in any way. Jellyfish are able to jump out of the water to attack players, often leaving them stranded on land. Most varieties of Jellyfish produce light, making them easy to spot in dark areas. There are 5 Jellyfish variants, 3 of which only appear during Hardmode. In Expert Mode(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), a Jellyfish will periodically become "electrified" (except for Fungo Fish). During this electrified state, it is invincible, and will constantly maintain its speed unless it comes into contact with a solid block or the water's surface. Certain attacks to Jellyfish in this state will hurt the player by 1.3× the contact damage of the Jellyfish (see Notes for details). Unlike other damage sources, this damage will not be reduced by banners.

Blue Jellyfish Jar.name: Blue Jellyfish Jar
Blue Jellyfish Jar.tooltip: Jellyfish jars are animated decorative furniture items. The Jellyfish needed to craft these decorations are bait items obtained by fishing, not by killing the actual Jellyfish enemies. By throwing a jellyfish jar into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the jellyfish as an item. Jellyfish jars can be placed on top of solid blocks and platforms, and give off a faint light. They function as valid light sources for houses and illuminate underwater, but are not controllable mechanisms like some other light sources.

While they can be considered the "boss version of banners", they are purely cosmetic and do not provide any bonuses. Some trophies can only be rewarded by the Angler for completing fishing quests. In total, there are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 33 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 24 trophies.
