King Slime Trophy.name: King Slime Trophy
King Slime Trophy.tooltip: Trophies are decorative furniture items which usually have a 1/10 (10%) chance to be dropped from most bosses. While they can be considered the "boss version of banners", they are purely cosmetic and do not provide any bonuses. Some trophies can only be rewarded by the Angler for completing fishing quests. In total, there are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 33 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 24 trophies.

Ship in a Bottle.name: Ship in a Bottle
Ship in a Bottle.tooltip: The Ship in a Bottle is a decorative furniture item acquired by completing Angler NPC quests.

Hardy Saddle.name: Hardy Saddle
Hardy Saddle.tooltip: The Hardy Saddle is a mount-summoning item that summons a Turtle Mount that can swim and has increased movement speed in liquids (51 mph maximum), but reduced movement speed (26 mph maximum) and jump reach (3.53 tiles maximum) on land. It also allows the player to breathe underwater. The Hardy Saddle has a 7/80 (8.75%) chance of being obtained from Golden Crates and a 133/1600 (8.31%) chance of being obtained from Titanium Crates.

Pressure Plate Track.name: Pressure Plate Track
Pressure Plate Track.tooltip: Pressure Plate Tracks are activation mechanisms that work similarly to Pressure Plates and are activated while riding over with a Minecart. They can be crafted using any type of Pressure Plate.

King Slime Mask.name: King Slime Mask
King Slime Mask.tooltip: Masks are vanity items dropped by all non-event bosses, as well as those from the Old One's Army(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). They are worn in the social head slot. Each boss has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance to drop its own mask in all difficulties, with the following exceptions: The Skeletron Mask has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to drop from Skeletron's Treasure Bag. The Dark Mage Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 1) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Dark Mage. The Ogre Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 2) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Ogre.

Fin Wings.name: Fin Wings
Fin Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Treasure Map.name: Treasure Map
Treasure Map.tooltip: The Treasure Map is a decorative wall hanging randomly obtained as a reward for Angler fishing quests (1% chance).

Seaweed Planter.name: Seaweed Planter
Seaweed Planter.tooltip: The Seaweed Planter is a decorative furniture item acquired as a random reward for completing quests from the Angler NPC with a 1/30 (3.33%) chance.

Pillagin' Me Pixels.name: Pillagin' Me Pixels
Pillagin' Me Pixels.tooltip: Paintings are decorative furniture items that can be placed on background walls. Each one is a framed image that depicts a particular scene, usually Terraria-related. Their tooltips generally contain a person's name, intended to credit each painting's artist; although the names appear to be fictional, most of them correspond to known Terraria developers, artists, testing staff, and community members (see Trivia below). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions, the Magic Lantern, Spelunker Glowsticks, and Spelunker Flares. There are a total of 193 paintings, 25 of which are sold by the Painter, 7 by the Princess, 4 by the Golfer, 2 by the Zoologist, 2 by the Clothier, 1 by the Truffle, and 27 are randomly sold by the Traveling Merchant. 35 paintings can be found in Underground Cabins, another 14 in the Underground Desert Cabins, 26 in the Dungeon, 12 in The Underworld, 6 from Floating Islands, 5 obtained by fishing, 1 from the Jungle Temple, 5 randomly acquired from Goodie Bags, 8 dropped by Solar Eclipse enemies, 8 awarded randomly by the Angler for completing fishing quests, 1 from the Living Tree, and 4 dropped by enemies.

Fish Costume Mask.name: Fish Costume Mask
Fish Costume Mask.tooltip: The Fish Costume set is a vanity set composed of the Fish Costume Mask, Fish Costume Shirt, and Fish Costume Finskirt. The complete set can be acquired randomly as a reward for completing a Fishing quest from the Angler NPC. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Fish Costume Shirt.name: Fish Costume Shirt
Fish Costume Shirt.tooltip: The Fish Costume set is a vanity set composed of the Fish Costume Mask, Fish Costume Shirt, and Fish Costume Finskirt. The complete set can be acquired randomly as a reward for completing a Fishing quest from the Angler NPC. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Fish Costume Finskirt.name: Fish Costume Finskirt
Fish Costume Finskirt.tooltip: The Fish Costume set is a vanity set composed of the Fish Costume Mask, Fish Costume Shirt, and Fish Costume Finskirt. The complete set can be acquired randomly as a reward for completing a Fishing quest from the Angler NPC. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Ginger Beard.name: Ginger Beard
Ginger Beard.tooltip: The Ginger Beard is a vanity accessory found in Iron and Mythril Crates(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), which can be obtained by fishing in any biome, at any height. The Ginger Beard cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Honeyed Goggles.name: Honeyed Goggles
Honeyed Goggles.tooltip: The Honeyed Goggles is a pre-Hardmode mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Bee Mount which grants limited flight. The Honeyed Goggles have a 1/20 (5%) / 11/100 (11%) chance of being dropped from the Queen Bee. While the Bee Mount is slow on the ground, it is capable of flying and will greatly increase in speed while doing so. While flying, the player's vertical speed is kept constant. The Bee Mount can fly in the air for 10.66 seconds before it enters a "tired" state, during which it slows and glides down. The glide can be accelerated using the ▼ Down key. Afterwards, it requires a 3-second rest period on the ground in order to begin flying at full speed again. If the player takes off again immediately after landing an exhausted bee, it will fly, but much slower than usual. Its rest period is indicated by a "heavy breathing" animation that stops when the Bee Mount has fully recovered.

Boreal Wood.name: Boreal Wood
Boreal Wood.tooltip: Boreal Wood is a type of wood harvested from Boreal trees found naturally growing in the Snow biome, or from Underground Cabins in the Ice biome. Boreal trees can be cultivated by placing Acorns on top of Snow Blocks above surface.

Palm Wood.name: Palm Wood
Palm Wood.tooltip: Palm Wood is a type of wood harvested from Palm trees found naturally growing in the Ocean biome and Oasis biome. Palm trees can be cultivated by placing Acorns on top of regular Sand Blocks above surface. Only regular Palm trees growing on regular Sand will drop Palm Wood. Palm trees that are growing on Ebonsand, Crimsand, or Pearlsand will instead drop Ebonwood, Shadewood or Pearlwood, respectively.

Boreal Wood Wall.name: Boreal Wood Wall
Boreal Wood Wall.tooltip: Boreal Wood Wall is a type of background wall crafted from Boreal Wood.

Palm Wood Wall.name: Palm Wood Wall
Palm Wood Wall.tooltip: Palm Wood Wall is a background wall made from Palm Wood.

Boreal Wood Fence.name: Boreal Wood Fence
Boreal Wood Fence.tooltip: Fences are a type of safe wall that are visually thin with most of them having transparency to allow view of the background. The only fences that have no transparency to them are Palm Fence, Rich Mahogany Fence, and Shadewood Fence. Unlike most other safe walls, they allow for wild plants and trees to grow. The safe Grass Wall, Flower Wall, and Jungle Wall are functionally identical to fences. All fences are obtained by crafting, and the Wrought Iron Fence can also be found on certain designs of the Dungeon.

Palm Wood Fence.name: Palm Wood Fence
Palm Wood Fence.tooltip: Fences are a type of safe wall that are visually thin with most of them having transparency to allow view of the background. The only fences that have no transparency to them are Palm Fence, Rich Mahogany Fence, and Shadewood Fence. Unlike most other safe walls, they allow for wild plants and trees to grow. The safe Grass Wall, Flower Wall, and Jungle Wall are functionally identical to fences. All fences are obtained by crafting, and the Wrought Iron Fence can also be found on certain designs of the Dungeon.

Boreal Wood Helmet.name: Boreal Wood Helmet
Boreal Wood Helmet.tooltip: Boreal Wood armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Boreal Wood Helmet, Boreal Wood Breastplate, and Boreal Wood Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Boreal Wood. The full set grants 4 defense while equipped.

Boreal Wood Breastplate.name: Boreal Wood Breastplate
Boreal Wood Breastplate.tooltip: Boreal Wood armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Boreal Wood Helmet, Boreal Wood Breastplate, and Boreal Wood Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Boreal Wood. The full set grants 4 defense while equipped.

Boreal Wood Greaves.name: Boreal Wood Greaves
Boreal Wood Greaves.tooltip: Boreal Wood armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Boreal Wood Helmet, Boreal Wood Breastplate, and Boreal Wood Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Boreal Wood. The full set grants 4 defense while equipped.

Palm Wood Helmet.name: Palm Wood Helmet
Palm Wood Helmet.tooltip: Palm Wood armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Palm Wood Helmet, Palm Wood Breastplate, and Palm Wood Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Palm Wood. The full set grants 4 defense while equipped.

Palm Wood Breastplate.name: Palm Wood Breastplate
Palm Wood Breastplate.tooltip: Palm Wood armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Palm Wood Helmet, Palm Wood Breastplate, and Palm Wood Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Palm Wood. The full set grants 4 defense while equipped.

Palm Wood Greaves.name: Palm Wood Greaves
Palm Wood Greaves.tooltip: Palm Wood armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Palm Wood Helmet, Palm Wood Breastplate, and Palm Wood Greaves. Crafting a full set requires a total of 75 Palm Wood. The full set grants 4 defense while equipped.

Palm Wood Bow.name: Palm Wood Bow
Palm Wood Bow.tooltip: The Palm Wood Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow and a variation of the Wooden Bow. Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.

Palm Wood Hammer.name: Palm Wood Hammer
Palm Wood Hammer.tooltip: The Palm Wood Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Palm Wood Sword.name: Palm Wood Sword
Palm Wood Sword.tooltip: The Palm Wood Sword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword and a variation of the Wooden Sword. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Palm Wood Platform.name: Palm Wood Platform
Palm Wood Platform.tooltip: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Palm Wood Bathtub.name: Palm Wood Bathtub
Palm Wood Bathtub.tooltip: Bathtubs are furniture items which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 65 / (Old-gen console version) 16 / (3DS version) 11 Bathtub types, all being functionally identical but presenting different appearances.

Palm Wood Bed.name: Palm Wood Bed
Palm Wood Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration. Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 craftable Beds and 5 that can be acquired from the environment. All Beds are functionally identical and differ only in appearance.

Palm Wood Bench.name: Palm Wood Bench
Palm Wood Bench.tooltip: Benches are furniture items that fulfill a house's chair requirement. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Bench will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5.

Palm Wood Candelabra.name: Palm Wood Candelabra
Palm Wood Candelabra.tooltip: Candelabras are a type of furniture and light source that emits light when placed on a flat surface such as blocks, platforms, and flat furniture items. It is not destroyed by water. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 23 /  12 craftable and 5 looted variations of the Candelabra.

Palm Wood Candle.name: Palm Wood Candle
Palm Wood Candle.tooltip: Candles are a type of furniture and light source. Candles can only be placed on flat-surface items. Candles will produce light underwater if placed and can be toggled on and off with ⚷ Open / Activate and by mechanisms. Certain types of candles provide buffs or debuffs. The Water Candle is a special type of candle found in Dungeons which increases enemy spawn rates by 33% and the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50% when placed or held. The Peace Candle reduces spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%, in contrast to the Water Candle. The Shadow Candle(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns in the area. For Water Candles and Peace Candles, multiple candles cannot stack, even if one is placed and the other is held.

Palm Wood Chair.name: Palm Wood Chair
Palm Wood Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Palm Wood Chandelier.name: Palm Wood Chandelier
Palm Wood Chandelier.tooltip: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers come in many varieties which differ only in appearance and sell value. All chandeliers can be picked up using a pickaxe, drill, or explosives. Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.

Palm Wood Chest.name: Palm Wood Chest
Palm Wood Chest.tooltip: Chests are a type of furniture functioning as storage items. They are accessed using ⚷ Open / Activate and can store up to 40 item stacks in rows of  10×4 /   8×5. In addition to many being craftable, a number of Chests are placed in random locations during world generation. The loot contained in these Chests is determined during world generation, and will not change if the world enters Hardmode. Chests cannot be broken with items inside (the blocks a filled Chest is placed on would also have this trait). However, the Block Swap feature allows the player to change the type of a Chest without having to destroy it. Some types of Chests can be locked by the player using a Chest Lock. When doing so, they will require a key to open again. There are 23 varieties of naturally-occurring Chests (12 of which cannot be crafted), 53 that can only be crafted, and 1 purchasable Chest, for a total of 77 Chest types.

Palm Wood Sofa.name: Palm Wood Sofa
Palm Wood Sofa.tooltip: Sofas are furniture items which fulfill a house's chair requirement. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Players can sit in sofas by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Players can choose to sit on the left, middle, or right positions, and thus up to 3 players can sit on a sofa at a time. Sitting on sofas gives a boost to health regeneration, similar to chairs and beds. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Sofa will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 21 craftable sofas and 5 noncraftable sofas. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Palm Wood Door.name: Palm Wood Door
Palm Wood Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Palm Wood Dresser.name: Palm Wood Dresser
Palm Wood Dresser.tooltip: Dressers are a type of flat-surface furniture (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and storage item. They also fulfill house's table requirement. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 19 / (3DS version) 5 craftable versions, and (Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) 5 noncraftable versions which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Palm Wood Lantern.name: Palm Wood Lantern
Palm Wood Lantern.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Palm Wood Piano.name: Palm Wood Piano
Palm Wood Piano.tooltip: Pianos are a type of furniture which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 15 /  10 craftable Pianos, and 5 non-craftable Pianos that can be found in the Dungeon, Ruined Houses, and Pirate Invasion event. Some Pianos can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin that they are found in.

Palm Wood Table.name: Palm Wood Table
Palm Wood Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Palm Wood Lamp.name: Palm Wood Lamp
Palm Wood Lamp.tooltip: Lamps are a type of furniture and light source. They also count as valid house lighting and can be toggled on and off by mechanisms. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 59 types of craftable Lamps, three types that are found in the Dungeon (Green, Blue, or Pink Dungeon Lamp), one found in Underworld houses (Obsidian Lamp), and one that can be dropped during a Pirate Invasion (Golden Lamp). Most lamps are dislodged by liquids, but Obsidian Lamp and Ash Wood Lamp are not dislodged by Lava. The Tiki Torch shares its Tile ID with the rest of these Lamps. Also see Lamp Post ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions) which does not count as valid House lighting.)

Palm Wood Work Bench.name: Palm Wood Work Bench
Palm Wood Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Optic Staff.name: Optic Staff
Optic Staff.tooltip: The Optic Staff is a Hardmode summon weapon that summons a miniature version of The Twins as minions. The pair of minions, named Spazmamini and Retanimini, fly towards enemies to dash through them and fire lasers at them, respectively. Each pair of Twins counts as a single minion towards the minion slot cap. Its best modifier is Fabled.

Palm Wood Bookcase.name: Palm Wood Bookcase
Palm Wood Bookcase.tooltip: Bookcases are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station used for the crafting of three Hardmode magic weapons (the Crystal Storm, Cursed Flames, and Golden Shower) as well as the Librarian furniture out of Librarian Blocks. Bookcases also fulfill a house's table requirement. There is a total of 65 types of Bookcases: 60 craftable Bookcases, and 5 looted from the environment: one from the Underworld, three from the Dungeon, and one from the Pirate Invasion. Some bookcases can also be found in Underground Cabins; their style follows the theme of the cabin where they are found.

Mushroom Bathtub.name: Mushroom Bathtub
Mushroom Bathtub.tooltip: Bathtubs are furniture items which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 65 / (Old-gen console version) 16 / (3DS version) 11 Bathtub types, all being functionally identical but presenting different appearances.

Mushroom Bed.name: Mushroom Bed
Mushroom Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration. Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it. Mushroom Chest.name: Mushroom Chest

Mushroom Lantern.name: Mushroom Lantern
Mushroom Lantern.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Mushroom Lamp.name: Mushroom Lamp
Mushroom Lamp.tooltip: Lamps are a type of furniture and light source. They also count as valid house lighting and can be toggled on and off by mechanisms. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 59 types of craftable Lamps, three types that are found in the Dungeon (Green, Blue, or Pink Dungeon Lamp), one found in Underworld houses (Obsidian Lamp), and one that can be dropped during a Pirate Invasion (Golden Lamp). Mushroom Piano.name: Mushroom Piano

Mushroom Platform.name: Mushroom Platform

The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Mushroom Table.name: Mushroom Table
Mushroom Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Spider Staff.name: Spider Staff
Spider Staff.tooltip: The Spider Staff is a Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Spider minion. It runs towards enemies and latches onto them, repeatedly dealing damage while latched and inflicting the Acid Venom debuff for 2–4 seconds. It can climb background walls and jump high. Its best modifier is Fabled.

Boreal Wood Bathtub.name: Boreal Wood Bathtub
Boreal Wood Bathtub.tooltip: Bathtubs are furniture items which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 65 / (Old-gen console version) 16 / (3DS version) 11 Bathtub types, all being functionally identical but presenting different appearances.

Boreal Wood Bed.name: Boreal Wood Bed
Boreal Wood Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration. Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 craftable Beds and 5 that can be acquired from the environment. All Beds are functionally identical and differ only in appearance.

Boreal Wood Chest.name: Boreal Wood Chest
Boreal Wood Chest.tooltip: Chests are a type of furniture functioning as storage items. They are accessed using ⚷ Open / Activate and can store up to 40 item stacks in rows of  10×4 /   8×5. In addition to many being craftable, a number of Chests are placed in random locations during world generation. The loot contained in these Chests is determined during world generation, and will not change if the world enters Hardmode. Chests cannot be broken with items inside (the blocks a filled Chest is placed on would also have this trait). However, the Block Swap feature allows the player to change the type of a Chest without having to destroy it. Some types of Chests can be locked by the player using a Chest Lock. When doing so, they will require a key to open again. There are 23 varieties of naturally-occurring Chests (12 of which cannot be crafted), 53 that can only be crafted, and 1 purchasable Chest, for a total of 77 Chest types.

Boreal Wood Clock.name: Boreal Wood Clock
Boreal Wood Clock.tooltip: Grandfather Clocks are furniture items which provide information about the in-game time. If a player is nearby a Grandfather Clock (about 80 tiles horizontally and 50 tiles vertically), the time is displayed on the right side of the screen, underneath the minimap. The time is rounded to the last hour, similar to Tin and Copper Watches, but pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it will show precise time in minutes as a status message on the bottom left corner. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 21 /  5 craftable versions and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 5 / (Old-gen console version) 2 noncraftable (but still lootable) versions. The regular Grandfather Clock can rarely be found in Underground Cabins. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Boreal Wood Door.name: Boreal Wood Door
Boreal Wood Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Pirate Staff.name: Pirate Staff
Pirate Staff.tooltip: The Pirate Staff is a Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Pirate minion. It runs and jumps towards enemies, attacking with a sword up close. When trying to reach an enemy that is too high above it, the Pirate minion can also double jump or use a grappling hook while mid-air to reach it. The Pirate Staff has a 1/1000 (0.1%) chance to be dropped by regular pirates (except Parrots) during the Pirate Invasion event. The Pirate Staff has an increased 1/250 (0.4%) chance to be dropped from Pirate Captains, and a higher 1/15 (6.67%) chance to be dropped by the Flying Dutchman. Its best modifier is Fabled.
Pirate Staff.drops_summary: Most pirates (0.1%), Flying Dutchman (6.67%), Pirate Captain (0.4%)

Slime Hook.name: Slime Hook
Slime Hook.tooltip: Hooks are a class of tools which aid the player in traversing terrain. When used, hooks fire a chain that latches to a surface or platform and pulls the player towards it. A hook is an essential tool which offers significant freedom from terrain height restrictions as well as being a fast movement option, and will often be the first major mobility tool a player acquires. A variety of hooks are available at all stages of the game (see table below). The Grapple hotkey activates the equipped hook in the player's equipment slot, or the first hook from the inventory (from left to right, top to bottom) without requiring it to be in the player's hotbar.Verify Several higher-tier hooks, such as the Ivy Whip, allow the player to grapple multiple surfaces simultaneously. If the character grapples one surface, then fires the hook a second time, another chain extends from the player without dislodging the first. Upon grappling a second surface, the player will be suspended in midair at a point midway between the two surfaces. This allows players more freedom during construction, or for navigating hazardous areas, such as above lava or Meteorite. All Journey Mode characters will spawn with the basic Grappling Hook already in their inventory.

Sticky Grenade.name: Sticky Grenade
Sticky Grenade.tooltip: The Sticky Grenade is an explosive consumable ranged weapon. It can be made by combining Grenades with Gel. Like the Sticky Bomb, it will not roll, and will instead stick to the first block it touches until it explodes. Like normal Grenades, they will detonate upon touching an enemy, or the player that threw it.

Tartar Sauce.name: Tartar Sauce
Tartar Sauce.tooltip: It is named the Tartar Sauce and summons the Mini Minotaur pet.

Duke Fishron Mask.name: Duke Fishron Mask
Duke Fishron Mask.tooltip: Masks are vanity items dropped by all non-event bosses, as well as those from the Old One's Army(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). They are worn in the social head slot. Each boss has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance to drop its own mask in all difficulties, with the following exceptions: The Skeletron Mask has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to drop from Skeletron's Treasure Bag. The Dark Mage Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 1) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Dark Mage. The Ogre Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 2) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Ogre.

Duke Fishron Trophy.name: Duke Fishron Trophy
Duke Fishron Trophy.tooltip: Trophies are decorative furniture items which usually have a 1/10 (10%) chance to be dropped from most bosses. While they can be considered the "boss version of banners", they are purely cosmetic and do not provide any bonuses. Some trophies can only be rewarded by the Angler for completing fishing quests. In total, there are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 33 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 24 trophies.

Molotov Cocktail.name: Molotov Cocktail
Molotov Cocktail.tooltip: The Molotov Cocktail is a consumable ranged weapon with a relatively short throwing arc. Upon hitting a solid object or enemy, it will explode and release 6 Molotov Fire light emitting projectiles, which can hit up to 3 targets. These smaller projectiles deal 50% damage (11 base damage), apply no knockback and inflict the On Fire! debuff on enemies for 3–6 seconds. Its high damage and ability to inflict fire damage make it a powerful early- to mid-pre-Hardmode weapon.

Bone Clock.name: Bone Clock
Bone Clock.tooltip: Grandfather Clocks are furniture items which provide information about the in-game time. If a player is nearby a Grandfather Clock (about 80 tiles horizontally and 50 tiles vertically), the time is displayed on the right side of the screen, underneath the minimap. The time is rounded to the last hour, similar to Tin and Copper Watches, but pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it will show precise time in minutes as a status message on the bottom left corner. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 21 /  5 craftable versions and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 5 / (Old-gen console version) 2 noncraftable (but still lootable) versions. The regular Grandfather Clock can rarely be found in Underground Cabins. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Spider Fang.name: Spider Fang
Spider Fang.tooltip: The Spider Fang is a Hardmode crafting material dropped by Black Recluses in Spider Nests with a 1/2 (50%) / 9/10 (90%) chance. It can be used to craft several minion-related items and armor.

Falcon Blade.name: Falcon Blade
Falcon Blade.tooltip: The Falcon Blade is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that has a 38/625 (6.08%) chance of being obtained from Iron Crates and a 299/5000 (5.98%) chance from Mythril Crates. Striking enemies with the weapon increases its damage by 12% per hit, up to a maximum of 50%. This damage bonus decays at a rate of 0.5% per tick or 30% per second. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Fishron Wings.name: Fishron Wings
Fishron Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Slime Gun.name: Slime Gun
Slime Gun.tooltip: The Slime Gun is a novelty item that auto-fires an arc of slime which inflicts the Slime debuff on players, enemies, and NPCs, causing them to drip blue goo for 30 seconds.

Flairon.name: Flairon
Flairon.tooltip: The Flairon is a Hardmode flail that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Duke Fishron. When used, it swings like a thrown flail and releases non-piercing, homing bubbles.  Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the item switches it into the Flairoon. When used, it is launched like a launched flail that also releases homing bubbles while traveling. The flail retracts after contact with enemies or blocks, or after extending for more than 25 tiles. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Green Dungeon Chest.name: Green Dungeon Chest
Green Dungeon Chest.tooltip: Chests are a type of furniture functioning as storage items. They are accessed using ⚷ Open / Activate and can store up to 40 item stacks in rows of  10×4 /   8×5. In addition to many being craftable, a number of Chests are placed in random locations during world generation. The loot contained in these Chests is determined during world generation, and will not change if the world enters Hardmode. Chests cannot be broken with items inside (the blocks a filled Chest is placed on would also have this trait). However, the Block Swap feature allows the player to change the type of a Chest without having to destroy it. Some types of Chests can be locked by the player using a Chest Lock. When doing so, they will require a key to open again. There are 23 varieties of naturally-occurring Chests (12 of which cannot be crafted), 53 that can only be crafted, and 1 purchasable Chest, for a total of 77 Chest types.

Tempest Staff.name: Tempest Staff
Tempest Staff.tooltip: The Tempest Staff is a Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Sharknado minion.

Razorblade Typhoon.name: Razorblade Typhoon
Razorblade Typhoon.tooltip: The Razorblade Typhoon is a Hardmode spell book that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Duke Fishron. When used, it fires a high-velocity homing typhoon. The typhoon can pierce enemies and bounce off blocks infinitely, and it lasts for 1.67 seconds. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Bubble Gun.name: Bubble Gun
Bubble Gun.tooltip: The Bubble Gun is a Hardmode magic gun that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Duke Fishron. When used, it rapidly fires a large spread of short-range bubbles, with three bubbles per use. Bubble projectiles gradually slow down and dissipate upon contact with an enemy or block, or after 1.67 seconds. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Tsunami.name: Tsunami
Tsunami.tooltip: The Tsunami is a Hardmode bow that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Duke Fishron. When used, it fires a volley of five parallel arrows, consuming one arrow per use. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Seashell.name: Seashell
Seashell.tooltip: Seashells are decorative items that can be found in the Ocean biomes. They can spawn on Sand Blocks within the biome, both on the beach and underwater. When placed, they can appear as one of three variants. Seashells can appear back on beaches and underwater, as long as no more than 3 Corals or Seashells are within an 8-tile range. Spawn rates scale with Rain, Wind, and empty space up to 14 tiles above the Sand Block. When a Seashell spawns, there is a 79.4% chance for either a regular Seashell or a Starfish, 9.8% chance for a Tulip Shell, 8.8% chance for a Lightning Whelk Shell, and 2% chance for a Junonia Shell.

Starfish.name: Starfish
Starfish.tooltip: Seashells are decorative items that can be found in the Ocean biomes. They can spawn on Sand Blocks within the biome, both on the beach and underwater. When placed, they can appear as one of three variants. Seashells can appear back on beaches and underwater, as long as no more than 3 Corals or Seashells are within an 8-tile range. Spawn rates scale with Rain, Wind, and empty space up to 14 tiles above the Sand Block. When a Seashell spawns, there is a 79.4% chance for either a regular Seashell or a Starfish, 9.8% chance for a Tulip Shell, 8.8% chance for a Lightning Whelk Shell, and 2% chance for a Junonia Shell.

Steampunk Platform.name: Steampunk Platform
Steampunk Platform.tooltip: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Skyware Work Bench.name: Skyware Work Bench
Skyware Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Living Wood Work Bench.name: Living Wood Work Bench
Living Wood Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Flesh Sofa.name: Flesh Sofa
Flesh Sofa.tooltip: Sofas are furniture items which fulfill a house's chair requirement. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Players can sit in sofas by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Players can choose to sit on the left, middle, or right positions, and thus up to 3 players can sit on a sofa at a time. Sitting on sofas gives a boost to health regeneration, similar to chairs and beds. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Sofa will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 21 craftable sofas and 5 noncraftable sofas. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Pumpkin Lantern.name: Pumpkin Lantern
Pumpkin Lantern.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Pumpkin Lamp.name: Pumpkin Lamp
Pumpkin Lamp.tooltip: Lamps are a type of furniture and light source. They also count as valid house lighting and can be toggled on and off by mechanisms. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 59 types of craftable Lamps, three types that are found in the Dungeon (Green, Blue, or Pink Dungeon Lamp), one found in Underworld houses (Obsidian Lamp), and one that can be dropped during a Pirate Invasion (Golden Lamp). Most lamps are dislodged by liquids, but Obsidian Lamp and Ash Wood Lamp are not dislodged by Lava. The Tiki Torch shares its Tile ID with the rest of these Lamps. Also see Lamp Post ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions) which does not count as valid House lighting.)

Honey Candle.name: Honey Candle
Honey Candle.tooltip: Candles are a type of furniture and light source. Candles can only be placed on flat-surface items. Candles will produce light underwater if placed and can be toggled on and off with ⚷ Open / Activate and by mechanisms. Certain types of candles provide buffs or debuffs. The Water Candle is a special type of candle found in Dungeons which increases enemy spawn rates by 33% and the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50% when placed or held. The Peace Candle reduces spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%, in contrast to the Water Candle. The Shadow Candle(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns in the area. For Water Candles and Peace Candles, multiple candles cannot stack, even if one is placed and the other is held.

Blue Dungeon Chandelier.tooltip: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.

Pumpkin Bed.name: Pumpkin Bed
Pumpkin Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration. Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 craftable Beds and 5 that can be acquired from the environment. All Beds are functionally identical and differ only in appearance.

Pumpkin Bookcase.name: Pumpkin Bookcase
Pumpkin Bookcase.tooltip: Bookcases are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station used for the crafting of three Hardmode magic weapons (the Crystal Storm, Cursed Flames, and Golden Shower) as well as the Librarian furniture out of Librarian Blocks. Bookcases also fulfill a house's table requirement. There is a total of 65 types of Bookcases: 60 craftable Bookcases, and 5 looted from the environment: one from the Underworld, three from the Dungeon, and one from the Pirate Invasion. Some bookcases can also be found in Underground Cabins; their style follows the theme of the cabin where they are found.

Pumpkin Piano.name: Pumpkin Piano
Pumpkin Piano.tooltip: Pianos are a type of furniture which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 15 /  10 craftable Pianos, and 5 non-craftable Pianos that can be found in the Dungeon, Ruined Houses, and Pirate Invasion event. Some Pianos can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin that they are found in.

Shark Statue.name: Shark Statue
Shark Statue.tooltip: Statues are furniture items. While some are purely decorative, others have a functional effect when activated via Wire—depending on the statue, it may spawn enemies, drop items, or teleport an NPC to the statue's location. Most statues can be found already placed in any area underground (most frequently in the Dungeon, Underground Cabins, and Cavern level), though Angel Statues also appear in Chests. Like all furniture, a pickaxe, a drill, or explosives are used to collect them. There are a total of 117 different statues: 25 decoration statues, 36 text and numerical statues, and 56 functional mechanisms.

Truffle Worm.name: Truffle Worm
Truffle Worm.tooltip: The Truffle Worm is a rare Hardmode critter and boss-summoning item that spawns in the underground Glowing Mushroom biome. It summons Duke Fishron when used as bait. It can only be used in the Ocean, at any time. It emits a small amount of light. The Truffle Worm can be caught with a Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net and Golden Bug Net, however, it is more difficult to catch than other critters, as it burrows away when a player comes too close. It must be approached quickly in order to successfully catch it. After being caught, it can be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Truffle Worm Cage). Once crafted, the Truffle Worm cannot be released again unless decrafted via Shimmer.

Apprentice Bait.name: Apprentice Bait
Apprentice Bait.tooltip: Bait is a category of items required for fishing. When a fishing pole is cast, at least one bait item must be in the player's inventory; otherwise, nothing can be caught. Fishing poles will cast their lines with no baits, but there will be no "bites" and no catches. The bait item is only consumed once the player reels in the line with a catch on the hook. It is not consumed upon the player casting the line or the line being reeled in with no catch. Even when the player does reel in a fish, there is only a chance that the bait will be consumed. There are several items that can serve as bait, and they must be obtained in different ways depending on the type: Most critters that are invertebrates (insects, scorpions, snails, worms) can be used as bait, and must be caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), or Golden Bug Net(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Worms from a Can Of Worms found in surface chests can be used for fishing before the Bug Net can be bought. The Truffle Worm is unique in that it is only used for summoning Duke Fishron. It cannot be used for ordinary fishing. The Magma Snail(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Hell Butterfly(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Lavafly(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can only be caught with a Lavaproof Bug Net or Golden Bug Net. When used as bait, they have the special property of allowing the player to fish in lava. Blue, Green, and Pink Jellyfish bait items are unrelated to the Jellyfish enemies. They are themselves caught via fishing. Apprentice Bait, Journeyman Bait, and Master Bait are acquired as rewards for completing quests for the Angler NPC, as well as from crates. Apprentice Bait and Journeyman bait can also be obtained by putting one of the three Junk items in an Extractinator, while Master Bait is also dropped by Jungle Mimics(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

Amber Gemspark Wall.name: Amber Gemspark Wall
Amber Gemspark Wall.tooltip: Gemspark Walls are the wall equivalent of Gemspark Blocks, and come in Online and Offline variants. Like Gemspark Blocks, Online Gemspark Walls emit light when placed or dropped as an item, but do not count as a light source for NPC housing. Unlike Gemspark Blocks, Gemspark Walls do not act as Mechanisms and their online and offline states cannot be switched after being placed. Online Gemspark Walls placed behind blocks will cause the blocks to appear fully lit, similar to the effect of Illuminant Coating.

Offline Amber Gemspark Wall.name: Offline Amber Gemspark Wall
Offline Amber Gemspark Wall.tooltip: Offline Gemspark Walls are a group of walls made from Gemspark Blocks. Unlike Gemspark Blocks, they produce no light, and have no mechanical function. Gemspark Walls are the illuminant variant.

Diamond Gemspark Wall.tooltip: Gemspark Walls are the wall equivalent of Gemspark Blocks, and come in Online and Offline variants. Like Gemspark Blocks, Online Gemspark Walls emit light when placed or dropped as an item, but do not count as a light source for NPC housing. Unlike Gemspark Blocks, Gemspark Walls do not act as Mechanisms and their online and offline states cannot be switched after being placed. Online Gemspark Walls placed behind blocks will cause the blocks to appear fully lit, similar to the effect of Illuminant Coating.

Tin Plating Wall.name: Tin Plating Wall
Tin Plating Wall.tooltip: Tin Plating Wall is a background wall made of Tin Plating.

Tin Plating.name: Tin Plating
Tin Plating.tooltip: Tin Plating is a pre-Hardmode brick. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Copper Plating.

Waterfall Block.name: Waterfall Block
Waterfall Block.tooltip: The Waterfall Block is an animated block type which shows flowing water.

Lavafall Block.name: Lavafall Block
Lavafall Block.tooltip: The Lavafall Block is an animated block type that shows flowing lava, which glows when placed. It does not satisfy the need for a light source in an NPC house.

Confetti Block.name: Confetti Block
Confetti Block.tooltip: The Confetti Block is an animated block type showing falling confetti. It is one of the few items that uses the Crystal Ball as a crafting station. Besides the confetti, it is transparent, like Glass. The Midnight Confetti Block is a dark, non-transparent version of it.

Confetti Wall.name: Confetti Wall
Confetti Wall.tooltip: Confetti Walls are a type of background wall made from Confetti Blocks. They resemble Glass Walls with falling confetti. They are one of only a few animated background walls. Midnight Confetti Walls are an opaque version of them.

Midnight Confetti Block.name: Midnight Confetti Block
Midnight Confetti Block.tooltip: The Midnight Confetti Block is an animated block type showing falling confetti. It is one of the few items that uses the Crystal Ball as a crafting station. It is a dark, non-transparent version of the Confetti Block.

Midnight Confetti Wall.name: Midnight Confetti Wall
Midnight Confetti Wall.tooltip: Midnight Confetti Walls are a type of background wall made from Midnight Confetti Blocks. They depict falling confetti.They are one of only a few animated background walls. Confetti Walls are a transparent version of them.

Weapon Rack.name: Weapon Rack
Weapon Rack.tooltip: The Weapon Rack is a furniture item that can be placed on background walls. By pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it, a player can mount any weapon-type item for display, including damage-dealing tools.  Displayed items are oriented the same way the rack was placed, and large item graphics may be resized to fit on it. A pickaxe or drill will remove the displayed item before freeing the Weapon Rack itself.

Fireworks Box.name: Fireworks Box
Fireworks Box.tooltip: The Fireworks Box is a placed novelty mechanism that is purchased from the Party Girl for 5 Gold. Once placed, it can be activated via Wire (with a 0.5 second cooldown) or by interacting with the Box directly via ⚷ Open / Activate (no cooldown). Each activation causes the Box to randomly fire one of the four possible firework rockets that cause no damage. The firework rockets explode upon colliding with solid blocks or after traveling for 0.75 seconds (22.5 tiles of distance), creating a visual firework effect. It can be used infinitely at no cost.

Living Fire Block.name: Living Fire Block
Living Fire Block.tooltip: Living Fire Blocks are Hardmode animated background furniture blocks that, when placed, resemble small animated flames and emit faint orange light. They deal no damage on contact and can be freed with any pickaxe or drill. Living Fire Blocks have a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by any enemy killed in the Underworld during Hardmode, including the Wall of Flesh, and drop in stacks of 20–50 at a time. While Living Fire Blocks can be placed in a manner similar to traditional, foreground blocks, they are actually in the background, similar to furniture, allowing the player to walk directly through them. They can attach to each other horizontally as well as vertically, but other traditional, foreground block types will not attach to them. There are five color variations of the base Living Fire Block, all of which are crafted from it. They are functionally identical.

'0' Statue.name: '0' Statue
'0' Statue.tooltip: Statues are furniture items. While some are purely decorative, others have a functional effect when activated via Wire—depending on the statue, it may spawn enemies, drop items, or teleport an NPC to the statue's location. Most statues can be found already placed in any area underground (most frequently in the Dungeon, Underground Cabins, and Cavern level), though Angel Statues also appear in Chests. Like all furniture, a pickaxe, a drill, or explosives are used to collect them. There are a total of 117 different statues: 25 decoration statues, 36 text and numerical statues, and 56 functional mechanisms.

Firework Fountain.name: Firework Fountain
Firework Fountain.tooltip: The Firework Fountain is a placed novelty mechanism that is purchased from the Party Girl for 3 Gold. Once placed, it can be activated via Wire, or by interacting with the Fountain directly via ⚷ Open / Activate. Each activation causes the Fountain to randomly fire one of four colorful sparkle fountain effects, which lasts for 10 seconds. Its effect is purely visual, causes no damage, and can be used infinitely at no cost.

Booster Track.name: Booster Track
Booster Track.tooltip: Booster Tracks are placeable furniture-type blocks that can be placed next to Minecart Tracks to automatically boost the speed of a Minecart that rides over it. The direction of the boost is indicated by the animated red arrow it displays, which can be toggled using a Hammer or wire. Each Booster Track increases speed by 20 mph, regardless of the Minecart variant used. The Booster Track can be purchased from the Mechanic for 50 Silver.

Grasshopper.name: Grasshopper
Grasshopper.tooltip: The Grasshopper is a type of critter that can be found when destroying grass plants and moves by hopping along the ground identically to slimes. The Grasshopper has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Grasshopper can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Grasshopper Cage). Once crafted, the Grasshopper cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The Grasshopper can be used as bait for fishing, with 10% bait power. The Grasshopper can be spawned by the Grasshopper Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Grasshopper to spawn in place of an ordinary one.

Grasshopper Cage.name: Grasshopper Cage
Grasshopper Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters. A critter caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item. Gold cages are regular cages containing gold critters. Aside from their higher sell value and rarity, they are the same as regular cages. Placed cages are partially transparent. They can be stacked on top of each other, but no other types of furniture can be placed on a cage. Players can stand on top of cages like platforms, even though they are otherwise background furniture.

Music Box (Underground Crimson).name: Music Box (Underground Crimson)
Music Box (Underground Crimson).tooltip: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End), which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 Gold after defeating the Moon Lord. A recorded Music Box can be played back in one of two ways: Equipping it as an accessory. Placing it as furniture and activating it, either by the ⚷ Open / Activate button or with wires. Recorded Music Boxes can be reverted into blank ones through Shimmer transmutation. There are 101 different Music Boxes available.

Cactus Table.name: Cactus Table
Cactus Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Cactus Platform.name: Cactus Platform
Cactus Platform.tooltip: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Boreal Wood Sword.name: Boreal Wood Sword
Boreal Wood Sword.tooltip: The Boreal Wood Sword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword and a variation of the Wooden Sword. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Boreal Wood Hammer.name: Boreal Wood Hammer
Boreal Wood Hammer.tooltip: The Boreal Wood Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Boreal Wood Bow.name: Boreal Wood Bow
Boreal Wood Bow.tooltip: The Boreal Wood Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow and a variation of the Wooden Bow. Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.

Glass Chest.name: Glass Chest
Glass Chest.tooltip: Chests are a type of furniture functioning as storage items. They are accessed using ⚷ Open / Activate and can store up to 40 item stacks in rows of  10×4 /   8×5. In addition to many being craftable, a number of Chests are placed in random locations during world generation. The loot contained in these Chests is determined during world generation, and will not change if the world enters Hardmode. Chests cannot be broken with items inside (the blocks a filled Chest is placed on would also have this trait). However, the Block Swap feature allows the player to change the type of a Chest without having to destroy it. Some types of Chests can be locked by the player using a Chest Lock. When doing so, they will require a key to open again. There are 23 varieties of naturally-occurring Chests (12 of which cannot be crafted), 53 that can only be crafted, and 1 purchasable Chest, for a total of 77 Chest types.

Xeno Staff.name: Xeno Staff
Xeno Staff.tooltip: The Xeno Staff is a Hardmode, post-Golem summon weapon that summons a UFO minion. It hovers above enemies, firing blue lasers that hit the target instantaneously. If an enemy is 18.75 to 50 tiles away, it will instantly teleport above it. The Xeno Staff has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being dropped by the Martian Saucer during the Martian Madness event. Its best modifier is Fabled.

Meteor Staff.name: Meteor Staff
Meteor Staff.tooltip: The Meteor Staff is a Hardmode wand. When used, it rapidly summons meteors from the sky which fall in the direction of the cursor and explode upon impact with an enemy or block. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Living Cursed Fire Block.name: Living Cursed Fire Block
Living Cursed Fire Block.tooltip: Living Fire Blocks are Hardmode animated background furniture blocks that, when placed, resemble small animated flames and emit faint orange light. They deal no damage on contact and can be freed with any pickaxe or drill. Living Fire Blocks have a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by any enemy killed in the Underworld during Hardmode, including the Wall of Flesh, and drop in stacks of 20–50 at a time. While Living Fire Blocks can be placed in a manner similar to traditional, foreground blocks, they are actually in the background, similar to furniture, allowing the player to walk directly through them. They can attach to each other horizontally as well as vertically, but other traditional, foreground block types will not attach to them. There are five color variations of the base Living Fire Block, all of which are crafted from it. They are functionally identical.

Gender Change Potion.name: Gender Change Potion
Gender Change Potion.tooltip: The Gender Change Potion is a pre-Hardmode potion that allows the player to swap their character style between male and female. Hurt sounds and equipment sprites change accordingly. The effect lasts until another Gender Change Potion is used.

Vortex Helmet.name: Vortex Helmet
Vortex Helmet.tooltip: Vortex armor is a Hardmode , post- Moon Lord ranged armor set consisting of the Vortex Helmet , Vortex Breastplate , and Vortex Leggings . Crafting the full set requires a total of 36 Luminite Bars (144 Luminite ) and 45 Vortex Fragments .

Vortex Breastplate.name: Vortex Breastplate
Vortex Breastplate.tooltip: Vortex armor is a Hardmode , post- Moon Lord ranged armor set consisting of the Vortex Helmet , Vortex Breastplate , and Vortex Leggings . Crafting the full set requires a total of 36 Luminite Bars (144 Luminite ) and 45 Vortex Fragments .

Vortex Leggings.name: Vortex Leggings
Vortex Leggings.tooltip: Vortex armor is a Hardmode , post- Moon Lord ranged armor set consisting of the Vortex Helmet , Vortex Breastplate , and Vortex Leggings . Crafting the full set requires a total of 36 Luminite Bars (144 Luminite ) and 45 Vortex Fragments .

Nebula Helmet.name: Nebula Helmet
Nebula Helmet.tooltip: Nebula armor is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord mage armor set consisting of the Nebula Helmet, Nebula Breastplate, and Nebula Leggings. Crafting the full set requires a total of 36 Luminite Bars (144 Luminite) and 45 Nebula Fragments. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +46 defense +26% magic damage +16% magic critical strike chance +60 maximum mana +15% mana cost reduction +10% movement speed Grants a chance for special booster items to spawn upon striking enemies with magic weapons. Each booster provides a buff, indicated by the booster orbiting the player. Boosters of the same type can stack with each other up to 3 times. Boosters expire after 8 seconds and the buff decreases by one level. Boosters can float in the air and have a greater pickup range than normal. The boosters are not tied to the armor, so any player can pick up the booster items, even if they are not wearing the armor set. In multiplayer, picking up a booster item will also grant nearby teammates (within a 43.75-tile radius) the buff. Players without a team will give the buff to all nearby players.

Solar Flare Helmet.name: Solar Flare Helmet
Solar Flare Helmet.tooltip: Solar Flare armor is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord melee armor set consisting of the Solar Flare Helmet, Solar Flare Breastplate, and Solar Flare Leggings. Crafting the full set requires a total of 36 Luminite Bars (144 Luminite) and 45 Solar Fragments. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +78 defense +12% damage reduction +29% melee damage +26% melee critical strike chance +15% melee speed +900 aggro +15% movement speed +3 HP/second health regeneration Grants the Solar Blaze buff, which builds the longer the player avoids taking damage, gaining up to a maximum of three charges. Each charge takes 3 seconds to build. The number of charges built is indicated by a shield that appears in front of the player, with two and three spikes appearing on the shield, corresponding with the charge count. Taking damage depletes one charge and creates an explosion called Solar Radiance around the player. While there is at least one charge built, the player can activate a special dash attack by double-tapping either the ◀ Left or ▶ Right key. Striking an enemy with the dash damages it and causes a damaging Solar Radiance explosion, so enemies always take damage twice. A Solar Blaze charge is consumed if at least one enemy was hit. The dash has a 1-second cooldown. Furthermore, the Solar Blaze buff provides +20% damage reduction, regardless of the number of charges. Combined with the base damage reduction from the armor's set bonus, it grants a total of 29.6% damage reduction. Each piece equipped (even if hidden by vanity items) causes the player to emit light, with a higher light level for each additional piece equipped. Additionally, equipping the full set causes the player to emit pulses and afterimages while moving.

Solar Tablet Fragment.name: Solar Tablet Fragment
Solar Tablet Fragment.tooltip: The Solar Tablet Fragment is a post-Plantera Hardmode crafting material solely used to craft the Solar Tablet, which summons the Solar Eclipse event. Solar Tablet Fragments have a 4/5 (80%) chance of being found in Lihzahrd Chests, and also have a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Lihzahrds and Flying Snakes in the Jungle Temple.

Solar Tablet.name: Solar Tablet
Solar Tablet.tooltip: The Solar Tablet is a Hardmode event-summoning item used to summon a Solar Eclipse. It may only be used during the day (from 4:30 AM to 7:29 PM), causing the eclipse to begin immediately, regardless of the time. The eclipse lasts until 7:30 PM of the current day. Solar Tablets have a 1/5 (20%) chance to be found in Lihzahrd Chests in the Jungle Temple. Additionally, Lihzahrds and Flying Snakes have a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of dropping 1–2 Solar Tablet Fragments, which can be used to craft a Solar Tablet.

Drill Containment Unit.name: Drill Containment Unit
Drill Containment Unit.tooltip: The Drill Containment Unit (sometimes abbreviated to DCU) is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord mount-summoning item that summons a Drill Mount, a rideable, flying vehicle that mines tiles extremely quickly via a stream of blue lasers. It can fly and hover indefinitely and has a mining range of 15 tiles. The Drill Mount is one of the fastest controllable ways to mine in Terraria, but it has a number of special characteristics: Unlike other mounts, players cannot use any tools or weapons while riding the Drill Mount. Unlike most other mounts, players can fly through liquids while riding the Drill Mount, though they can still drown. Unlike other mining tools, the Drill Mount does not inflict damage on enemies. It also cannot mine blocks behind other blocks, rather always drilling tunnels through all blocks directly ahead of the player. Mining speed bonuses do not affect Drill Mount's mining speed. The Drill Mount flies at 41 mph vertically, 31 mph horizontally, and 51 mph diagonally. Pressing ⚒ Use / Attack makes the Drill Mount mine all mineable blocks, including furniture, objects, trees, Lihzahrd Bricks, Altars (during Hardmode), and Shadow Orbs / Crimson Hearts, among others. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate makes the Drill Mount mine background walls. Holding ⚷ Open / Activate and ⚒ Use / Attack simultaneously will mine both blocks and walls. Crafting the Drill Containment Unit requires a total of 160 Luminite (thus requiring defeating the Moon Lord at least twice), 600 Chlorophyte Ore, 600 Glowing Mushrooms, 20 Ectoplasm, 120 each of Hellstone and Meteorite ores, and 40 Obsidian. This also requires four different crafting stations: a Hardmode Forge for the Chlorophyte and Spectre Bars, an Autohammer for the Shroomite Bars, an Ancient Manipulator for the Luminite Bars, and a Hardmode Anvil for the Drill Containment Unit itself.

Cosmic Car Key.name: Cosmic Car Key
Cosmic Car Key.tooltip: The Cosmic Car Key is a Hardmode, post-Golem mount-summoning item. When used, it summons a rideable UFO Mount that allows the player to fly and hover indefinitely. The Cosmic Car Key has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being dropped by the Martian Saucer during the Martian Madness event.

Mothron Wings.name: Mothron Wings
Mothron Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Brain Scrambler.name: Brain Scrambler
Brain Scrambler.tooltip: The Brain Scrambler is a Hardmode, post-Golem enemy that appears during the Martian Madness event. It fires green laser projectiles, at a maximum fire rate of once every 0.67 seconds (40 ticks), which have a chance to inflict the Confused debuff.

Vortex Axe.name: Vortex Axe
Vortex Axe.tooltip: Luminite Axes are unobtainable tools. The four types are the Solar Flare Axe, Vortex Axe, Nebula Axe, and the Stardust Axe, each themed after a different Celestial Tower. They are all unable to be crafted, and instead the player must craft the Luminite Hamaxes. Even with Terrasavr and some other inventory editors, they seem to disappear, leaving an empty slot. Their best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Vortex Chainsaw.name: Vortex Chainsaw
Vortex Chainsaw.tooltip: Luminite Chainsaws are unobtainable tools. All of the chainsaws share the same stats. The four types are the Solar Flare Chainsaw, Vortex Chainsaw, Nebula Chainsaw, and the Stardust Chainsaw, each themed after different Celestial Pillars. They are all unable to be crafted, and instead the player must craft the Luminite Hamaxes. Like all axes and chainsaws, they are used to cut down Trees, Cacti, and Giant Glowing Mushrooms, so the best possible modifier is Godly. With current methods, it is impossible to hack these items into a character's inventory using external editors, as they will disappear from that character's inventory as soon as they load into a world.

Vortex Drill.name: Vortex Drill
Vortex Drill.tooltip: The Luminite Drills are Hardmode, post-Moon Lord drills. The four types are the  Vortex Drill, Nebula Drill, Solar Flare Drill, and Stardust Drill. They are the alternative versions of the Luminite Pickaxes, having a higher base mining speed but shorter range and lacking the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. All four drills have identical stats and can mine all blocks. Their best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Vortex Hammer.name: Vortex Hammer
Vortex Hammer.tooltip: Luminite Hammers are unobtainable tools . The four types are the Solar Flare Hammer , Vortex Hammer , Nebula Hammer , and the Stardust Hammer , each themed after a different Celestial Tower . They are all unable to be crafted, and instead the player must craft the Luminite Hamaxes .

Vortex Pickaxe.name: Vortex Pickaxe
Vortex Pickaxe.tooltip: Luminite Pickaxes are Hardmode, post-Moon Lord pickaxes. The four types are the Solar Flare Pickaxe, Vortex Pickaxe, Nebula Pickaxe, and Stardust Pickaxe. They are the alternate versions of the Luminite Drills, having a lower base mining speed but longer range and the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. All four pickaxes have identical stats and can mine all blocks. Their best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for these tools.
