Solar Flare Drill.name: Solar Flare Drill
Solar Flare Drill.tooltip: The Luminite Drills are Hardmode, post-Moon Lord drills. The four types are the  Vortex Drill, Nebula Drill, Solar Flare Drill, and Stardust Drill. They are the alternative versions of the Luminite Pickaxes, having a higher base mining speed but shorter range and lacking the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. All four drills have identical stats and can mine all blocks. Their best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Solar Flare Hammer.name: Solar Flare Hammer
Solar Flare Hammer.tooltip: Luminite Hammers are unobtainable tools . The four types are the Solar Flare Hammer , Vortex Hammer , Nebula Hammer , and the Stardust Hammer , each themed after a different Celestial Tower . They are all unable to be crafted, and instead the player must craft the Luminite Hamaxes .

Solar Flare Pickaxe.name: Solar Flare Pickaxe
Solar Flare Pickaxe.tooltip: Luminite Pickaxes are Hardmode, post-Moon Lord pickaxes. The four types are the Solar Flare Pickaxe, Vortex Pickaxe, Nebula Pickaxe, and Stardust Pickaxe. They are the alternate versions of the Luminite Drills, having a lower base mining speed but longer range and the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. All four pickaxes have identical stats and can mine all blocks. Their best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for these tools.

Honeyfall Block.name: Honeyfall Block
Honeyfall Block.tooltip: The Honeyfall Block is a block which shows an animated texture of flowing honey.

Honeyfall Wall.name: Honeyfall Wall
Honeyfall Wall.tooltip: The Honeyfall Wall is one of only a few animated background wall types. It depicts flowing honey.

Chlorophyte Brick Wall.name: Chlorophyte Brick Wall
Chlorophyte Brick Wall.tooltip: Chlorophyte Brick Walls are Walls that can be manually crafted. When placed, it presents a dark shade of green followed by a gemstone-like pattern.

Crimtane Brick Wall.name: Crimtane Brick Wall
Crimtane Brick Wall.tooltip: The Crimtane Brick Wall is a background wall. It emits faint red light when placed.

Shroomite Plating Wall.name: Shroomite Plating Wall
Shroomite Plating Wall.tooltip: The Shroomite Plating Wall is a type of wall made from Shroomite Plating. It glows when placed like the block it is made from.

Chlorophyte Brick.name: Chlorophyte Brick
Chlorophyte Brick.tooltip: Chlorophyte Bricks are Hardmode bricks crafted from Chlorophyte Ore and Stone Blocks. Similarly to Chlorophyte Ore, Chlorophyte Bricks can convert adjacent Mud and Jungle grass into Chlorophyte Ore. Chlorophyte Bricks can also restrict the spread of the evil biomes around them. See Chlorophyte Ore § Mechanics for further information.

Crimtane Brick.name: Crimtane Brick
Crimtane Brick.tooltip: Crimtane Brick is a brick made from Crimtane Ore and Crimstone. A box of it appears after the Wall of Flesh has been defeated in a Crimson world. It is red and black in color, it is not resistant to explosions, and it gives off a faint red glow when placed.

Shroomite Plating.name: Shroomite Plating
Shroomite Plating.tooltip: Shroomite Plating is a building material crafted from Stone Blocks and Shroomite Bars. It produces a small amount of light when placed but it does not count as a light source for housing. It is essentially the Shroomite equivalent of a brick.

Laser Machinegun.name: Laser Machinegun
Laser Machinegun.tooltip: The Laser Machinegun is a Hardmode, post-Golem magic gun that has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being dropped by the Martian Saucer during the Martian Madness event. When used, it fires two inaccurate blue lasers that do not pierce enemies or pass through blocks. The weapon accelerates while the ⚒ Use / Attack button is held down, reaching its maximum fire rate after nearly two seconds of continuous usage. Its best modifier is Mythical. Since it does not benefit from speed modifiers, Godly and Demonic provide the same DPS bonus as Mythical.

Electrosphere Launcher.name: Electrosphere Launcher
Electrosphere Launcher.tooltip: The Electrosphere Launcher is a Hardmode, post-Golem launcher that has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being dropped by the Martian Saucer during the Martian Madness event. When used, it consumes rockets and fires blue missiles that form an Electrosphere upon impact with blocks, enemies, or reaching the cursor's position when fired. Electrospheres deal damage repeatedly and last for 5 seconds, but do not inflict any knockback. Multiple Electrospheres cannot overlap, with newly summoned ones replacing older ones. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Xenopopper.name: Xenopopper
Xenopopper.tooltip: The Xenopopper is a Hardmode, post-Golem gun that has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being dropped by the Martian Saucer during the Martian Madness event. When used, it fires a burst of 4–5 purple bubbles, consuming one bullet. The bubbles deal no damage and will bounce off solid blocks, but pop after a 0.5-second delay, each firing a bullet directly towards the cursor. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Laser Drill.name: Laser Drill
Laser Drill.tooltip: The Laser Drill is a Hardmode, post-Golem drill that has a 1/800 (0.13%) chance of being dropped from all basic enemies during the Martian Madness event. It produces a green glowing drill-like beam that extends up to a base distance of 16 tiles. It can mine all blocks. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Mechanical Ruler.name: Mechanical Ruler
Mechanical Ruler.tooltip: The Mechanical Ruler is an informational accessory that, when equipped, draws a cyan, semi-transparent grid overlay on the screen, making individual block distances much clearer. This grid fades out when the player begins moving and returns once movement stops. The row and column of the block the mouse is hovering over are also highlighted in red, drawing a cross on the screen with the cursor at its center. The Mechanical Ruler can be purchased from the Mechanic for 1 Gold. When the Mechanical Ruler is in the inventory or equipped, a toggle for controlling its function appears  to the left of the main inventory /  in the tools menu below the inventory.

Anti-Gravity Hook.name: Anti-Gravity Hook
Anti-Gravity Hook.tooltip: The Anti-Gravity Hook is a Hardmode, post-Golem grappling hook that fires up to three hooks which reach 31.25 tiles at maximum. When any hook latches onto a block, the player will be pushed 12 blocks away from the latch point if there is room to do so. While latched to a block, the player can use the movement keys to orbit around the latch point, or reposition themselves if they are caught between two or three latch points; however, they will return to the farthest point when they let go of the movement keys.  The Anti-Gravity Hook has a 1/800 (0.13%) chance of being dropped from all basic enemies during the Martian Madness event.

Moon Mask.name: Moon Mask
Moon Mask.tooltip: The Moon Mask is a vanity headpiece dropped by Lamias in Underground Deserts tainted with The Corruption or The Crimson.

Sun Mask.name: Sun Mask
Sun Mask.tooltip: The Sun Mask is a vanity helmet dropped by Lamias in normal Underground Deserts with a 1/25 (4%) chance.

Martian Costume Mask.name: Martian Costume Mask
Martian Costume Mask.tooltip: The Martian Costume set is a Hardmode, post-Golem vanity set consisting of the Martian Costume Mask, Martian Costume Shirt, and Martian Costume Pants. Each piece has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of being dropped by Gray Grunts, Ray Gunners, Scutlix Gunners, and Brain Scramblers during the Martian Madness event. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Martian Costume Shirt.name: Martian Costume Shirt
Martian Costume Shirt.tooltip: The Martian Costume set is a Hardmode, post-Golem vanity set consisting of the Martian Costume Mask, Martian Costume Shirt, and Martian Costume Pants. Each piece has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of being dropped by Gray Grunts, Ray Gunners, Scutlix Gunners, and Brain Scramblers during the Martian Madness event. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Martian Costume Pants.name: Martian Costume Pants
Martian Costume Pants.tooltip: The Martian Costume set is a Hardmode, post-Golem vanity set consisting of the Martian Costume Mask, Martian Costume Shirt, and Martian Costume Pants. Each piece has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of being dropped by Gray Grunts, Ray Gunners, Scutlix Gunners, and Brain Scramblers during the Martian Madness event. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Martian Uniform Helmet.name: Martian Uniform Helmet
Martian Uniform Helmet.tooltip: The Martian Uniform set is a Hardmode, post-Golem vanity set consisting of the Martian Uniform Helmet, Martian Uniform Torso, and Martian Uniform Pants. Each piece has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of being dropped by Gigazappers, Martian Engineers, and Martian Officers during the Martian Madness event. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Martian Uniform Torso.name: Martian Uniform Torso
Martian Uniform Torso.tooltip: The Martian Uniform set is a Hardmode, post-Golem vanity set consisting of the Martian Uniform Helmet, Martian Uniform Torso, and Martian Uniform Pants. Each piece has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of being dropped by Gigazappers, Martian Engineers, and Martian Officers during the Martian Madness event. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Martian Uniform Pants.name: Martian Uniform Pants
Martian Uniform Pants.tooltip: The Martian Uniform set is a Hardmode, post-Golem vanity set consisting of the Martian Uniform Helmet, Martian Uniform Torso, and Martian Uniform Pants. Each piece has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance of being dropped by Gigazappers, Martian Engineers, and Martian Officers during the Martian Madness event. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Martian Astro Clock.name: Martian Astro Clock
Martian Astro Clock.tooltip: Grandfather Clocks are furniture items which provide information about the in-game time. If a player is nearby a Grandfather Clock (about 80 tiles horizontally and 50 tiles vertically), the time is displayed on the right side of the screen, underneath the minimap. The time is rounded to the last hour, similar to Tin and Copper Watches, but pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it will show precise time in minutes as a status message on the bottom left corner. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 21 /  5 craftable versions and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 5 / (Old-gen console version) 2 noncraftable (but still lootable) versions. The regular Grandfather Clock can rarely be found in Underground Cabins. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Martian Bathtub.name: Martian Bathtub
Martian Bathtub.tooltip: Bathtubs are furniture items which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 65 / (Old-gen console version) 16 / (3DS version) 11 Bathtub types, all being functionally identical but presenting different appearances.

Martian Bed.name: Martian Bed
Martian Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration. Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 craftable Beds and 5 that can be acquired from the environment. All Beds are functionally identical and differ only in appearance.

Martian Hover Chair.name: Martian Hover Chair
Martian Hover Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Martian Chandelier.name: Martian Chandelier
Martian Chandelier.tooltip: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers come in many varieties which differ only in appearance and sell value. All chandeliers can be picked up using a pickaxe, drill, or explosives. Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.

Martian Chest.name: Martian Chest
Martian Chest.tooltip: Chests are a type of furniture functioning as storage items. They are accessed using ⚷ Open / Activate and can store up to 40 item stacks in rows of  10×4 /   8×5. In addition to many being craftable, a number of Chests are placed in random locations during world generation. The loot contained in these Chests is determined during world generation, and will not change if the world enters Hardmode. Chests cannot be broken with items inside (the blocks a filled Chest is placed on would also have this trait). However, the Block Swap feature allows the player to change the type of a Chest without having to destroy it. Some types of Chests can be locked by the player using a Chest Lock. When doing so, they will require a key to open again. There are 23 varieties of naturally-occurring Chests (12 of which cannot be crafted), 53 that can only be crafted, and 1 purchasable Chest, for a total of 77 Chest types.

Martian Door.name: Martian Door
Martian Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Martian Dresser.name: Martian Dresser
Martian Dresser.tooltip: Dressers are a type of flat-surface furniture (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and storage item. They also fulfill house's table requirement. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 19 / (3DS version) 5 craftable versions, and (Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) 5 noncraftable versions which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Martian Holobookcase.name: Martian Holobookcase
Martian Holobookcase.tooltip: Bookcases are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station used for the crafting of three Hardmode magic weapons (the Crystal Storm, Cursed Flames, and Golden Shower) as well as the Librarian furniture out of Librarian Blocks. Bookcases also fulfill a house's table requirement. There is a total of 65 types of Bookcases: 60 craftable Bookcases, and 5 looted from the environment: one from the Underworld, three from the Dungeon, and one from the Pirate Invasion. Some bookcases can also be found in Underground Cabins; their style follows the theme of the cabin where they are found.

Martian Hover Candle.name: Martian Hover Candle
Martian Hover Candle.tooltip: Candles are a type of furniture and light source. Candles can only be placed on flat-surface items. Candles will produce light underwater if placed and can be toggled on and off with ⚷ Open / Activate and by mechanisms. Certain types of candles provide buffs or debuffs. The Water Candle is a special type of candle found in Dungeons which increases enemy spawn rates by 33% and the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50% when placed or held. The Peace Candle reduces spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%, in contrast to the Water Candle. The Shadow Candle(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns in the area. For Water Candles and Peace Candles, multiple candles cannot stack, even if one is placed and the other is held.

Martian Lamppost.name: Martian Lamppost
Martian Lamppost.tooltip: Lamps are a type of furniture and light source. They also count as valid house lighting and can be toggled on and off by mechanisms. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 59 types of craftable Lamps, three types that are found in the Dungeon (Green, Blue, or Pink Dungeon Lamp), one found in Underworld houses (Obsidian Lamp), and one that can be dropped during a Pirate Invasion (Golden Lamp). Most lamps are dislodged by liquids, but Obsidian Lamp and Ash Wood Lamp are not dislodged by Lava. The Tiki Torch shares its Tile ID with the rest of these Lamps. Also see Lamp Post ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions) which does not count as valid House lighting.)

Martian Lantern.name: Martian Lantern
Martian Lantern.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Martian Piano.name: Martian Piano
Martian Piano.tooltip: Pianos are a type of furniture which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 15 /  10 craftable Pianos, and 5 non-craftable Pianos that can be found in the Dungeon, Ruined Houses, and Pirate Invasion event. Some Pianos can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin that they are found in.

Martian Platform.name: Martian Platform
Martian Platform.tooltip: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Martian Sofa.name: Martian Sofa
Martian Sofa.tooltip: Sofas are furniture items which fulfill a house's chair requirement. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Players can sit in sofas by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Players can choose to sit on the left, middle, or right positions, and thus up to 3 players can sit on a sofa at a time. Sitting on sofas gives a boost to health regeneration, similar to chairs and beds. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Sofa will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 21 craftable sofas and 5 noncraftable sofas. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Martian Table.name: Martian Table
Martian Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Martian Table Lamp.name: Martian Table Lamp
Martian Table Lamp.tooltip: Candelabras are a type of furniture and light source that emits light when placed on a flat surface such as blocks, platforms, and flat furniture items. It is not destroyed by water. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 23 /  12 craftable and 5 looted variations of the Candelabra.

Martian Work Bench.name: Martian Work Bench
Martian Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Wooden Sink.name: Wooden Sink
Wooden Sink.tooltip: The Sink is a type of furniture item and crafting station. Like Fountains, it can be used to craft items that require water as a crafting station. There is a total of 66 Sink types, all being functionally identical.

Solar Cultist Hood.name: Solar Cultist Hood
Solar Cultist Hood.tooltip: The Cultist set is a vanity set purchased from the Clothier for 20 Gold (set) after the Lunatic Cultist has been defeated. Its appearance is based on the clothing worn by Cultists, but its design is different from the robes worn either by normal Lunatic Devotees or the Lunatic Cultist itself. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. The Solar Cultist set consists of the Solar Cultist Hood and the Solar Cultist Robe, which are sold during the day. The Lunar Cultist set consists of the Lunar Cultist Hood and the Lunar Cultist Robe, which are sold during the night.

Lunar Cultist Hood.name: Lunar Cultist Hood
Lunar Cultist Hood.tooltip: The Cultist set is a vanity set purchased from the Clothier for 20 Gold (set) after the Lunatic Cultist has been defeated. Its appearance is based on the clothing worn by Cultists, but its design is different from the robes worn either by normal Lunatic Devotees or the Lunatic Cultist itself. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. The Solar Cultist set consists of the Solar Cultist Hood and the Solar Cultist Robe, which are sold during the day. The Lunar Cultist set consists of the Lunar Cultist Hood and the Lunar Cultist Robe, which are sold during the night.

Martian Conduit Plating.name: Martian Conduit Plating
Martian Conduit Plating.tooltip: Martian Conduit Plating is a post-Golem block dropped by most enemies during the Martian Madness event, and is used to create a variety of space- or Martian-themed furniture. Like Spooky Wood, it can only be obtained during its respective event; it can only be crafted by uncrafting its platforms and wall. When placed in dark areas, the block has a notable pulsating light effect. Crafting all pieces of furniture requires 161 Martian Conduit Plating blocks.

Martian Conduit Wall.name: Martian Conduit Wall
Martian Conduit Wall.tooltip: Martian Conduit Wall is a background wall type crafted from Martian Conduit Plating. It emits a faint glow when placed.

HiTek Sunglasses.name: HiTek Sunglasses
HiTek Sunglasses.tooltip: The HiTek Sunglasses are a Hardmode, post-Golem vanity item for the social helmet slot. They are similar to the Sunglasses and Goggles, in that they provide eye graphics without concealing the player's hair. HiTek Sunglasses are purchased from the Cyborg for 5 Gold, after the Martian Madness event has been defeated.

Martian Hair Dye.name: Martian Hair Dye
Martian Hair Dye.tooltip: Hair Dyes are consumable items sold by the Stylist NPC. When used, they replace a player's hair color with a dynamic effect.

Martian Dye.name: Martian Dye
Martian Dye.tooltip: Martian Dye is a Hardmode, post-Golem dye that is sometimes acquired from the Dye Trader after completing a Strange Plant quest. It is only obtainable after completing a Martian Madness event. When equipped, it gives items a cyan and white color palette which glows in the dark. The brightness of the glow depends on how close each color in the color palette is to cyan. Pure cyan glows at full brightness, while pure white does not glow at all.

Castle Marsberg.name: Castle Marsberg
Castle Marsberg.tooltip: Paintings are decorative furniture items that can be placed on background walls. Each one is a framed image that depicts a particular scene, usually Terraria-related. Their tooltips generally contain a person's name, intended to credit each painting's artist; although the names appear to be fictional, most of them correspond to known Terraria developers, artists, testing staff, and community members (see Trivia below). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions, the Magic Lantern, Spelunker Glowsticks, and Spelunker Flares. There are a total of 193 paintings, 25 of which are sold by the Painter, 7 by the Princess, 4 by the Golfer, 2 by the Zoologist, 2 by the Clothier, 1 by the Truffle, and 27 are randomly sold by the Traveling Merchant. 35 paintings can be found in Underground Cabins, another 14 in the Underground Desert Cabins, 26 in the Dungeon, 12 in The Underworld, 6 from Floating Islands, 5 obtained by fishing, 1 from the Jungle Temple, 5 randomly acquired from Goodie Bags, 8 dropped by Solar Eclipse enemies, 8 awarded randomly by the Angler for completing fishing quests, 1 from the Living Tree, and 4 dropped by enemies.

Smoke Block.name: Smoke Block
Smoke Block.tooltip: Smoke Blocks are animated background furniture blocks that can be purchased from the Party Girl for 1 Silver in Hardmode. When placed together, they will connect in a way that each block on the outer left and right sides visually take up half of a block. For example, if a player were to make a 3×3 arrangement of Smoke Blocks, the entire left and right columns of smoke will appear to be halved, resulting in a slimmer appearance.

Living Flame Dye.name: Living Flame Dye
Living Flame Dye.tooltip: Living Flame Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. It can only be obtained after defeating a mechanical boss. Upon application, the dye will cause all items in the slot equipped to change colors to a fiery red, with a yellow-to-red rippling effect. Additionally, any items affected by this dye will flash upon taking damage.

Living Rainbow Dye.name: Living Rainbow Dye
Living Rainbow Dye.tooltip: Living Rainbow Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. It is only obtainable after defeating a mechanical boss.

Shadow Dye.name: Shadow Dye
Shadow Dye.tooltip: Shadow Dye is a type of dye bought from the Dye Trader during a full moon, or given as a possible reward for turning in a Strange Plant in Hardmode. When applied, it will darken the color of an item to almost pure black. Shadow Dye also leaves black colored particles while moving.

Negative Dye.name: Negative Dye
Negative Dye.tooltip: Negative Dye is a type of dye bought from the Dye Trader during a full moon, or given as a possible reward for turning in a Strange Plant in Hardmode. When applied, it will completely invert the color of dyed armor or accessories. It is not combinable with other dyes.

Living Ocean Dye.name: Living Ocean Dye
Living Ocean Dye.tooltip: Living Ocean Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. It is only obtainable after defeating any mechanical boss.

Brown Dye.name: Brown Dye
Brown Dye.tooltip: Dyes are items that can be placed in the "dye slots" of a player's inventory to alter the colors and/or textures of equipped armor, vanity items, and accessories. The Dye Trader NPC sells two dyes (Silver Dye and Brown Dye) as well as the Dye Vat (5 Gold). The other dyes must be crafted using the Dye Vat or obtained through trading in Strange Plants to the Dye Trader. Primary crafted dyes can be further combined to craft Bright, Gradient, and Compound dyes. There are 119 different dyes in the game (118 on single-player worlds, as Team Dye is not available in single-player worlds). Some dyes will make sprites visible in complete darkness, most of which are Strange Dyes. If the Critter Shampoo is dyed (by placing a dye in the respective accessory dye slot), the dye will be applied to all of the player's minions.

Wisp Dye.name: Wisp Dye
Wisp Dye.tooltip: Wisp Dye is a Hardmode, post-Plantera dye obtained from the Dye Trader when turning in a Strange Plant. It causes equipment it is applied to gain a solid bright cyan texture with no animation. It is based off the light pet summoned by the Wisp in a Bottle.

Pixie Dye.name: Pixie Dye
Pixie Dye.tooltip: Pixie Dye is a Hardmode dye sometimes acquired from the Dye Trader as a reward for completing a Strange Plant quest. It can only be obtained after defeating Plantera. When equipped, it turns the player yellow-orange, mimicking the slight glow that Pixies give off.

Influx Waver.name: Influx Waver
Influx Waver.tooltip: The Influx Waver is a Hardmode, post-Golem broadsword that has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance of being dropped by the Martian Saucer during the Martian Madness event. When swung, it fires a blue sword projectile. Upon contact with enemies, the sword projectile will teleport onto nearby enemies two times, hitting three times in total. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Phasic Warp Ejector.name: Phasic Warp Ejector
Phasic Warp Ejector.tooltip: The Phasic Warp Ejector is an unimplemented and incomplete item. Its only remains in the game files are an item ID and an image, containing no stats or behavior. The Phasic Warp Ejector has an associated projectile named the "Phasic Warp Disc", although its intended function is unknown.

Charged Blaster Cannon.name: Charged Blaster Cannon
Charged Blaster Cannon.tooltip: The Charged Blaster Cannon is a Hardmode, post-Golem magic gun that has a 1/800 (0.13%) chance to drop from all basic enemies during the Martian Madness event. It possesses multiple firing modes with escalating speed, damage, and method of attack depending on how long the ⚒ Use / Attack key is held while firing it. A single tap of the ⚒ Use / Attack key fires a small energy orb that dissipates after hitting an enemy. Holding ⚒ Use / Attack rapidly fires small orbs at a rate of once every 0.17 seconds, up to a total of 6 small orbs. Mana is only consumed upon firing the first small orb. After holding ⚒ Use / Attack for 1.5 seconds (i.e., 0.67 seconds after the 6th small orb has been fired), it will shoot a larger orb with infinite piercing and 250% of the weapon's damage (250 base damage). Continuing to hold ⚒ Use / Attack fires larger orbs at a rate of once every 0.5 seconds. Mana is only consumed upon firing the first large orb. Holding ⚒ Use / Attack continuously for an additional 1.5 seconds (i.e., 0.5 seconds after the 3rd large orb has been fired) fires a large, solid blue energy beam that pierces infinitely, travels for a maximum of 150 tiles, and deals 150% of the weapon's damage (150 base damage) to enemies at a rate of every 10 ticks or six times per second. Mana is consumed at the rate of once every 0.33 seconds, i.e. 42 base mana per second. The attack is immediately canceled when mana is depleted, or when the ⚒ Use / Attack key is released, or after the beam is fired for 5 seconds.  Its best modifier is Mythical.

Chlorophyte Dye.name: Chlorophyte Dye
Chlorophyte Dye.tooltip: Chlorophyte Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. It can only be obtained after defeating any mechanical boss. When equipped, it gives items a black and green color palette which glows in the dark.

Unicorn Wisp Dye.name: Unicorn Wisp Dye
Unicorn Wisp Dye.tooltip: Unicorn Wisp Dye is a Hardmode, post-Plantera dye that can be acquired by bringing a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When equipped, it turns the affected item into a deep shade of pink, and produces a glow effect similar to that of the Wisp in a Bottle.

Infernal Wisp Dye.name: Infernal Wisp Dye
Infernal Wisp Dye.tooltip: Infernal Wisp Dye is a Hardmode, post-Plantera dye obtained by turning in Strange Plants to the Dye Trader. Any equipment it is applied to is colored bright orange, while also emitting an orange glow.

Vicious Powder.name: Vicious Powder
Vicious Powder.tooltip: Thrown Powders are consumable items that can be used to convert blocks and walls between their pure, Crimson, or Corrupt forms. When thrown, they release a cloud of sparkling powder with a very short range, comparable to that of a broadsword, and produce a fair amount of light. Thrown Powder comes in three variants: Purification Powder is able to revert any Corrupted, Crimson, or Hallowed blocks and walls back into their pure form, such as reverting Ebonstone into Stone, Crimsand into Sand, or Pink Ice into Ice. It is purchased solely from the Dryad for 75 Copper each, while a Blood Moon is not active. Purification Powder can also be used on a Tortured Soul in order to transform him into the Tax Collector NPC, as well as on a Mystic Frog to transform it into the Mystic Slime town pet. Vile Powder is able to convert blocks and walls, including the Crimson and the Hallowed ones, into their Corrupted form, such as converting Pearlstone into Ebonstone. If thrown at a Bunny, Penguin, or Goldfish, it will turn into its Corrupted variants: the Corrupt Bunny, Corrupt Penguin, and Corrupt Goldfish, respectively. It can be crafted from Vile Mushrooms or purchased from the Dryad for 1 Silver each during a Blood Moon in a Corrupt world. Vile Powder can be used to spread the Corruption onto convertible tiles. Vicious Powder is functionally identical to its counterpart, Vile Powder, to where it can convert blocks and walls, including the Corrupted and the Hallowed ones, into their Crimson form. If thrown at a Bunny, Penguin, or Goldfish, it will turn into its Crimson variants: the Vicious Bunny, Vicious Penguin, and Vicious Goldfish, respectively. It can be crafted from Vicious Mushrooms or purchased from the Dryad for 1 Silver each during a Blood Moon in a Crimson world. Vicious Powder can be used to spread the Crimson onto convertible tiles.

Vicious Mushroom.name: Vicious Mushroom
Vicious Mushroom.tooltip: The Vicious Mushroom is a type of mushroom growing on Crimson grass or Crimson Jungle grass, where they can be cut and collected with a single swing of any weapon or tool.  Vicious Mushroom can only grow when there are proper walls behind the soil block, or no walls at all. Vicious Mushroom cannot be eaten or brewed into any potions; they are used solely to craft Vicious Powder.

The Bee's Knees.name: The Bee's Knees
The Bee's Knees.tooltip: The Bee's Knees is a pre-Hardmode bow that has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by the Queen Bee. When used, it converts Wooden Arrows into a line of Bee Arrows. Bee Arrows are unaffected by gravity and disperse upon contact with an enemy or solid block, spawning three small homing bee projectiles with three independent 1/3 (33.33%) chances to spawn an extra bee. The bee projectiles deal 1/3 (33.33%) of the weapon and ammo's damage (9 base damage) before dissipating after a 10-second duration or upon contact with water or lava, and have a 1/2 (50%) chance to deal 1 extra damage. Individual bees can either pierce one enemy or ricochet off of blocks once. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Gold Bird.name: Gold Bird
Gold Bird.tooltip: The Gold Bird is a harmless critter. It may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Bird, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version. The Gold Bird has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Gold Bird can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gold Bird Cage). Once crafted, the Gold Bird cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Gold Bird itself or the crafted furniture can be sold for 10 Gold. It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.

Gold Bunny.name: Gold Bunny
Gold Bunny.tooltip: The Gold Bunny is a harmless critter. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Bunny, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version. The Gold Bunny has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Gold Bunny can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gold Bunny Cage). It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.

Gold Butterfly.name: Gold Butterfly
Gold Butterfly.tooltip: The Gold Butterfly is a harmless critter. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Butterfly, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version. Gold Mouse.name: Gold Mouse
Gold Mouse.tooltip: The Gold Mouse is a harmless critter. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Mouse, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version. The Gold Mouse has only 5 health and no defense, and can only be damaged by players. The Gold Mouse can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gold Mouse Cage). It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.

Gold Worm.name: Gold Worm
Gold Worm.tooltip: The Gold Worm is a critter. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Worm, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version. The Gold Worm has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Gold Worm can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gold Worm Cage). Once crafted, the Gold Worm cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Gold Worm itself or the crafted furniture can be sold for 10 Gold. The Gold Worm can be used as bait for fishing, with 50% bait power.  Gold Worms have a 1/20 (5%) chance of being obtained from opening a Can Of Worms. Uniquely, the Gold Worm has an exceptionally low chance of being consumed as bait of 1/20 (5%). It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.

Sticky Dynamite.name: Sticky Dynamite
Sticky Dynamite.tooltip: Sticky Dynamite is an explosive that functions like Dynamite, but sticks onto any block on contact. If the block it sticks to is removed by some means, it will fall until it hits another.

Angry Trapper Banner.name: Angry Trapper Banner
Angry Trapper Banner.tooltip: Enemy banners are functional furniture items that can be placed on the underside of blocks and platforms. They are obtained by killing most enemies and a few critters. When placed, enemy banners provide a Banner buff to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the banner. The buff grants players +50%/+100% damage inflicted with all damage to the corresponding enemy and −25%/−50% damage taken from attacks by the enemy. The banners of Old One's Army enemies will apply a weaker banner buff to the respective enemy, granting the players +10%/+20% damage inflicted and −8.33% / −16.67% damage taken. Multiple banners of the same type will not grant stacked buffs. Multiple different banner types in the vicinity will, however, all take effect and consolidate into a single buff icon. There are a total of 286 obtainable enemy banners: 115 in pre-Hardmode, 171 in Hardmode. Out of these, 118 belong to event enemies (28 in pre-Hardmode and 90 in Hardmode). In addition, there are 6 unobtainable enemy banners.

Pinky Banner.tooltip: Enemy banners are functional furniture items that can be placed on the underside of blocks and platforms. They are obtained by killing most enemies and a few critters. When placed, enemy banners provide a Banner buff to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the banner. The buff grants players +50%/+100% damage inflicted with all damage to the corresponding enemy and −25%/−50% damage taken from attacks by the enemy. The banners of Old One's Army enemies will apply a weaker banner buff to the respective enemy, granting the players +10%/+20% damage inflicted and −8.33% / −16.67% damage taken. Multiple banners of the same type will not grant stacked buffs. Multiple different banner types in the vicinity will, however, all take effect and consolidate into a single buff icon. There are a total of 286 obtainable enemy banners: 115 in pre-Hardmode, 171 in Hardmode. Out of these, 118 belong to event enemies (28 in pre-Hardmode and 90 in Hardmode). When placed, enemy banners provide a Banner buff to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the banner. The buff grants players +50%/+100% damage inflicted with all damage to the corresponding enemy and −25%/−50% damage taken from attacks by the enemy. The banners of Old One's Army enemies will apply a weaker banner buff to the respective enemy, granting the players +10%/+20% damage inflicted and −8.33% / −16.67% damage taken. Multiple banners of the same type will not grant stacked buffs. Multiple different banner types in the vicinity will, however, all take effect and consolidate into a single buff icon. There are a total of 286 obtainable enemy banners: 115 in pre-Hardmode, 171 in Hardmode. Out of these, 118 belong to event enemies (28 in pre-Hardmode and 90 in Hardmode). In addition, there are 6 unobtainable enemy banners.

Sparky.name: Sparky
Sparky.tooltip: Paintings are decorative furniture items that can be placed on background walls. Each one is a framed image that depicts a particular scene, usually Terraria-related. Their tooltips generally contain a person's name, intended to credit each painting's artist; although the names appear to be fictional, most of them correspond to known Terraria developers, artists, testing staff, and community members (see Trivia below). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions, the Magic Lantern, Spelunker Glowsticks, and Spelunker Flares. There are a total of 193 paintings, 25 of which are sold by the Painter, 7 by the Princess, 4 by the Golfer, 2 by the Zoologist, 2 by the Clothier, 1 by the Truffle, and 27 are randomly sold by the Traveling Merchant. 35 paintings can be found in Underground Cabins, another 14 in the Underground Desert Cabins, 26 in the Dungeon, 12 in The Underworld, 6 from Floating Islands, 5 obtained by fishing, 1 from the Jungle Temple, 5 randomly acquired from Goodie Bags, 8 dropped by Solar Eclipse enemies, 8 awarded randomly by the Angler for completing fishing quests, 1 from the Living Tree, and 4 dropped by enemies.

Vine Rope.name: Vine Rope
Vine Rope.tooltip: Ropes are placeable items that primarily provide quick vertical mobility. They can be placed adjacent to blocks in any direction, or in midair where background walls are present. Ropes can also be placed atop any existing placed Rope, which extends the total length of the Rope downward without the player having to be at the bottom of the Rope column. Once placed, Ropes are used by pressing ▲ Up or ▼ Down while moving over them. There are four different types of Rope, which are acquired in different ways: Rope can be found randomly in Chests and Pots, as a bonus drop from slimes, or purchased from the Merchant and Skeleton Merchant for 10 Copper each. Vine Rope is acquired by destroying vines while the Guide to Plant Fiber Cordage is equipped. Silk Rope is crafted from Silk at a Loom. Web Rope is crafted By Hand from Cobwebs. All Rope variants operate identically, but Silk and Web Ropes are immune to falling lava, as opposed to normal and Vine Ropes, which will be dislodged similarly to Torches. All types can be crafted into their respective Rope Coils, consumable items useful for placing Ropes in inaccessible locations. Vertical movement speed on a Rope equals that of a free fall, though moving down via the Rope and hitting the ground does not cause fall damage. Horizontal movement is also possible by placing adjacent Rope horizontally, but is much slower. Visually, the player appears to move along a Rope using a mechanical tool with wheels, as though they were riding a rail. This tool appears automatically when using Rope, does not exist as a separate item, and is available from the beginning of the game.

Wormhole Potion.name: Wormhole Potion
Wormhole Potion.tooltip: The Wormhole Potion is a potion which allows a player to instantly teleport to another team member's location in multiplayer, done by selecting their player icon in the full-screen map (accessible by pressing the Toggle Full Map key) once consumed. It is only possible to teleport to players of the same team, and the teleport will be announced in a status message. It is not possible to use Wormhole Potions if the player has the minimap disabled. In addition to being crafted, Wormhole Potions can be found in Pots and have a small chance to appear as a bonus drop from slimes, but only in multiplayer. Other players do not have to be online for Wormhole Potions to drop, so just selecting multiplayer and hosting the game can allow them to drop. Wormhole Potions are still craftable in single-player worlds.

Summoner Emblem.name: Summoner Emblem
Summoner Emblem.tooltip: The Summoner Emblem is a Hardmode accessory that increases summon damage by 15%. It has a 1/4 (25%) chance to drop from the Wall of Flesh.
Summoner Emblem.drops_summary: Treasure Bag (Wall of Flesh) (25%), Wall of Flesh (25%)

Bewitching Table.name: Bewitching Table
Bewitching Table.tooltip: The Bewitching Table is a furniture item found naturally placed in the Dungeon and can be obtained by fishing in the Dungeon. In Hardmode, it is also sold by the Witch Doctor for 10 Gold if the Wizard is present. It emits light when placed. It fulfills a house's table requirement. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on a placed Bewitching Table grants the Bewitched buff, which increases the player's minion slots by 1. This lasts until the player dies or leaves the world, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). Unlike equipment buff items, the Bewitching Table must be placed in order to activate the buff. It can be mined with a pickaxe or drill and picked up again, even while the buff is active, which will not cancel the buff. Placement is only dependent on an adequate space of 3×3 tiles being available.

Alchemy Table.name: Alchemy Table
Alchemy Table.tooltip: The Alchemy Table is a post-Skeletron crafting station that shares recipes with Placed Bottles. When a potion is crafted with the Alchemy Table, there is a 1/3 (33.33%) chance for each ingredient not to be consumed. There is a separate probability check for each of the ingredients used in making the potion, including each of those in a stack. The Alchemy Table can be found randomly in the Dungeon and can also be obtained by fishing in the Dungeon. It fulfills a house's table requirement.

Strange Brew.name: Strange Brew
Strange Brew.tooltip: The Strange Brew is a pre-Hardmode recovery potion that can be purchased from the Skeleton Merchant during certain moon phases for 5 Silver. When used, it restores 70–120 health, inflicts 40–70 seconds of Potion Sickness, and has a 3/5 (60%) chance to grant up to 4 seconds of invincibility. The duration of Potion Sickness can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths.

Spelunker Glowstick.name: Spelunker Glowstick
Spelunker Glowstick.tooltip: The Spelunker Glowstick is a consumable light source that can be held or tossed a fair distance, similar to the regular Glowstick.

Bone Arrow.name: Bone Arrow
Bone Arrow.tooltip: The Bone Arrow is a pre-Hardmode arrow purchased from the Skeleton Merchant for 15 Copper each, during moon phases 1 (full), 2, 5 (new), and 6. Bone Arrows can pierce one enemy.

Bone Torch.name: Bone Torch
Bone Torch.tooltip: Torches are furniture items that function as light sources when placed, held, or dropped (via the Throw button). Regular Torches can be found randomly in Chests and Pots, as a bonus drop from slimes, Torch Zombies, or purchased from the Merchant or Skeleton Merchant for 50 Copper each. Placing at least 101 Torches in close proximity below the surface layer in any biome will start the Torch God mini-event. Completing the event will grant the Torch God's Favor, which allows the player to automatically convert ordinary Torches to one of the biome types.

Vine Rope Coil.name: Vine Rope Coil
Vine Rope Coil.tooltip: Rope Coils are consumable mobility items that, when thrown by the player, travel in an arc affected by gravity until striking a block. On making contact, a vertical string of ten pieces of the respective Rope type will be placed, starting from the point of contact and descending until the Rope runs out or makes contact with another block below. Once in place, the Ropes created by a Rope Coil are ordinary Rope items that can be climbed, expanded with other placed Ropes, and collected with a pickaxe or drill. If a thrown Rope Coil strikes the top of an already placed Rope, it will automatically extend the existing Rope. If the coil cannot extend lower than ten tiles because of an obstacle, the excess Rope pieces will drop as items. If the coil cannot extend at all, the excess Rope will drop as the coil item. There are no rope coil analogues for chains nor streamers.

Life Drain.name: Life Drain
Life Drain.tooltip: The Life Drain is a Hardmode wand that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by Crimson Mimics. When used, it creates an invisible aura that deals continuous damage to all enemies near the cursor's position, as long as the line of sight between the player and the cursor is unobstructed. A stream of red particles flows toward the player from each targeted enemy. While the aura is hitting enemies, the user receives the Life Drain buff, which adds 1.5 health per second to existing health regeneration, plus 0.5 health per second for every two extra enemies hit, while also increasing the ramp-up speed of natural regeneration greatly. Enemies that are being damaged by the Life Drain's aura are additionally inflicted with a unique debuff that deals 25 damage per second (5 damage displayed every 0.2 seconds). Its best modifier is Mythical for damage output, or Celestial for mana conservation.

Dart Pistol.name: Dart Pistol
Dart Pistol.tooltip: The Dart Pistol is a Hardmode ranged weapon that autofires darts as ammunition, and is the Crimson counterpart to the Corruption's Dart Rifle, with a higher rate of fire but lower damage. It has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by Crimson Mimics. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Dart Rifle.name: Dart Rifle
Dart Rifle.tooltip: The Dart Rifle is a Hardmode ranged weapon that autofires darts as ammunition, and is the Corruption counterpart to the Crimson's Dart Pistol, with higher damage but a lower rate of fire. It has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by Corrupt Mimics. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Crystal Dart.name: Crystal Dart
Crystal Dart.tooltip: The Crystal Dart is a Hardmode dart. It can bounce between enemies and blocks, automatically targeting nearby enemies. The Crystal Dart can either bounce off blocks or hit enemies for a total of 5 times, reducing its damage by 15% per bounce.

Cursed Dart.name: Cursed Dart
Cursed Dart.tooltip: The Cursed Dart is a Hardmode dart. As it travels, it releases cursed flames that fall and land on blocks, lingering for 3 seconds before dissipating. The Cursed Dart can hit up to 3 targets. The cursed flames cannot pierce enemies and deal 80% of the Cursed Dart's damage and 50% of its knockback. The darts and flames both inflict the Cursed Inferno debuff for 3–6 seconds on hit. It is the Corruption's counterpart to the Crimson's Ichor Dart.

Ichor Dart.name: Ichor Dart
Ichor Dart.tooltip: The Ichor Dart is a Hardmode dart. It can pierce infinitely when initially fired. After traveling for a random duration between 0.1 seconds to 0.5 seconds, the Ichor Dart splits into 3–5 non-piercing darts (average of 3.75 darts). Ichor Darts inflict the Ichor debuff for 7–14 seconds. They are the Crimson's counterpart to the Corruption's Cursed Darts.

Chain Guillotines.name: Chain Guillotines
Chain Guillotines.tooltip: The Chain Guillotines are a Hardmode flail that have a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by Corrupt Mimics. When used, they fire two blades attached to chains in rapid succession, with a maximum range of 32 tiles. They can pierce enemies that are very close by. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Fetid Baghnakhs.name: Fetid Baghnakhs
Fetid Baghnakhs.tooltip: The Fetid Baghnakhs are a Hardmode broadsword that have a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by Crimson Mimics. They have a very short range, but an exceptionally high attack speed. Their best modifier is Legendary.

Clinger Staff.name: Clinger Staff
Clinger Staff.tooltip: The Clinger Staff is a Hardmode magic weapon that generates a 15-tile high wall of Cursed Flame, which deals damage and inflicts the Cursed Inferno debuff to enemies that walk through it for a duration of 7 seconds. The point at which the wall is generated must be in a direct line of sight; otherwise, the wall will not generate, though still consume mana. The Clinger Staff's wall lasts for 5 minutes before dissipating, but can be also forced to dissipate instantly by using ⚷ Open / Activate on the wall while the player is within 15 tiles of it. Only one wall may be generated at a time; if another is summoned, the first one will vanish. The Clinger Staff has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by Corrupt Mimics. Its best modifier is Ruthless. The Mythical modifier provides the widest array of stat bonuses, but the only stats that improve damage output are damage and critical chance. Switching to a different weapon causes existing projectiles to use that weapon's base critical chance instead, meaning that the Clinger Staff's DPS is optimized with the Ruthless modifier when used in the intended way.

Putrid Scent.name: Putrid Scent
Putrid Scent.tooltip: The Putrid Scent is a Hardmode accessory that has a 1/5 (20%) chance to be dropped by Corrupt Mimics. While equipped, it increases the player's damage and critical strike chance by 5% and decreases aggro by 400. It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Flesh Knuckles; both can be exchanged via Shimmer.

Flesh Knuckles.name: Flesh Knuckles
Flesh Knuckles.tooltip: The Flesh Knuckles are a Hardmode accessory that have a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by Crimson Mimics. While equipped, they increase the player's defense by 8 and aggro by 400. They are the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Putrid Scent; both can be exchanged via Shimmer.

Flower Boots.name: Flower Boots
Flower Boots.tooltip: Flower Boots are a rare accessory which cause flowers to grow when the player walks on regular, Jungle, Hallowed, and Ash grass. These flowers are functionally the same as the wild grass plants that grow naturally on grass, and drop Seeds and Hay normally. Wearing Flower Boots drastically decreases the chance of critters spawning from destroyed flowers. Flower Boots can occasionally be found in Ivy Chests, Jungle Crates, and Bramble Crates.
Flower Boots.drops_summary: Bramble Crate (5%), Ivy Chest (4.57%), Jungle Crate (5%)

Seedler.name: Seedler
Seedler.tooltip: The Seedler is a Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Plantera. When swung, it fires Seedler Nut projectiles that travel in a downwards arc before exploding into 4–7 Seedler Thorns upon hitting an enemy or after 0.33–2.15 seconds. Seedler Thorns deal 70% of the weapon's damage (35 base damage) and knockback (base knockback of 4.2 (Average)), are unaffected by gravity, and target nearby enemies when fired. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Hellwing Bow.name: Hellwing Bow
Hellwing Bow.tooltip: The Hellwing Bow is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron bow that fires arrows inaccurately. When used, it converts Wooden Arrows into flaming bat projectiles that are unaffected by gravity, can pierce infinitely, and cannot pass through blocks. The Hellwing Bow has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Shadow Chests in the Underworld, as well as a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Obsidian Lock Boxes obtained from Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Tendon Hook.name: Tendon Hook
Tendon Hook.tooltip: Hooks are a class of tools which aid the player in traversing terrain. When used, hooks fire a chain that latches to a surface or platform and pulls the player towards it. A hook is an essential tool which offers significant freedom from terrain height restrictions as well as being a fast movement option, and will often be the first major mobility tool a player acquires. A variety of hooks are available at all stages of the game (see table below). The Grapple hotkey activates the equipped hook in the player's equipment slot, or the first hook from the inventory (from left to right, top to bottom) without requiring it to be in the player's hotbar.Verify Several higher-tier hooks, such as the Ivy Whip, allow the player to grapple multiple surfaces simultaneously. If the character grapples one surface, then fires the hook a second time, another chain extends from the player without dislodging the first. Upon grappling a second surface, the player will be suspended in midair at a point midway between the two surfaces. This allows players more freedom during construction, or for navigating hazardous areas, such as above lava or Meteorite. All Journey Mode characters will spawn with the basic Grappling Hook already in their inventory.

Skiphs' Blood.name: Skiphs' Blood
Skiphs' Blood.tooltip: Skiphs' Blood is a Hardmode dye obtained from Hardmode bosses' Treasure Bags (except Queen Slime's) along with Skiphs' set. It can also be a random reward from the Dye Trader for completing a Strange Plant quest after the Moon Lord has been defeated. When equipped, it gives the player a dark purple tone, also adding a Shimmering purple effect to the player's body.

Purple Ooze Dye.name: Purple Ooze Dye
Purple Ooze Dye.tooltip: Purple Ooze Dye is a dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When equipped, it gives the player a purple tone, with parts of the dye distorting and varying in different shades of purple.

Reflective Silver Dye.name: Reflective Silver Dye
Reflective Silver Dye.tooltip: Reflective Silver Dye is a dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When equipped, it will give the selected accessory/armor a silver-plated, "shiny" effect, reflecting the surrounding light around the player. The reflection is more pronounced the closer the player is to a light source. The dye will prioritize light from the sun when the player is outside. From some perspectives, the player may look 3D when this dye is equipped all over. As with other reflective dyes, this dye is not animated when standing still, but the shading on a dyed piece of equipment will change according to the surrounding light, giving it the appearance of light reflecting off of a shining metallic object.

Reflective Gold Dye.name: Reflective Gold Dye
Reflective Gold Dye.tooltip: Reflective Gold Dye is a dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When equipped, it will give the selected accessory/armor a gold-plated, "shiny" effect, reflecting the surrounding light around the player. The reflection is more pronounced the closer the player is to a light source. The dye will prioritize light from the sun when the player is outside. From some perspectives, the player may look 3D when this dye is equipped all over. As with other reflective dyes, this dye is not animated when standing still, but the shading on a dyed piece of equipment will change according to the surrounding light, giving it the appearance of light reflecting off of a shining metallic object.

Blue Acid Dye.name: Blue Acid Dye
Blue Acid Dye.tooltip: Blue Acid Dye is a dye acquired as a random reward from the Dye Trader for giving him a Strange Plant. When equipped in a dye slot, it applies a dark blue rippling effect that pulses outward, similar to Acid Dye and Red Acid Dye. Items dyed by it can be seen in the dark, but do not emit light.

Daedalus Stormbow.name: Daedalus Stormbow
Daedalus Stormbow.tooltip: The Daedalus Stormbow is a Hardmode bow that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Hallowed Mimics. When used, it causes a wide spread of arrows to rain from the sky, directed towards the cursor. It fires two to four arrows per use, while only consuming a single arrow from the player's inventory. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Flying Knife.name: Flying Knife
Flying Knife.tooltip: The Flying Knife is a Hardmode melee weapon that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Hallowed Mimics. When used, it fires a controllable knife. Holding the ⚒ Use / Attack button directs the projectile's general path, although it also continuously moves on its own and ricochets off blocks. When the ⚒ Use / Attack button is released or after one minute of continuous use, the knife returns to the player. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount. However, the bonus knockback granted by the Godly modifier is not always beneficial and makes it tricky to damage the same targets. For example, the knife will not necessarily be knocking enemies away from the player. Alternatively, modifiers that reduce knockback (the best being Ruthless) can be beneficial, reducing the distance enemies are knocked away from the cursor.

Bottomless Water Bucket.name: Bottomless Water Bucket
Bottomless Water Bucket.tooltip: Bottomless Buckets are tools that are capable of placing an infinite amount of liquids by pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button. There are four different types of Bottomless Buckets, one for each type of liquid: Bottomless Water Bucket, Bottomless Lava Bucket, Bottomless Honey Bucket, and Bottomless Shimmer Bucket. Bottomless Buckets can be used limitlessly and are never depleted. They are also slightly faster at placing liquids when compared to standard buckets (especially when moving the cursor around while placing).

Super Absorbant Sponge.name: Super Absorbant Sponge
Super Absorbant Sponge.tooltip: Sponges are tools used to erase liquids by pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button on them. This causes the liquid to disappear from the environment without storing it. There are four different types of sponges: Super Absorbant Sponge for absorbing water and Shimmer Lava Absorbant Sponge for absorbing lava Honey Absorbant Sponge for absorbing honey Ultra Absorbant Sponge for absorbing all kinds of liquid Attempting to use a sponge on a different type of liquid has no effect. Sponges can be used limitlessly and are never depleted. They are also slightly faster at draining liquids when compared to using a standard Empty Bucket (especially when moving the cursor around while draining).

Gold Ring.name: Gold Ring
Gold Ring.tooltip: The Gold Ring is a Hardmode accessory that greatly increases the pickup range for coins. It has a 1/500 (0.2%) chance to be dropped by pirates (except Parrots) during Pirate Invasions, with a 1/125 (0.8%) chance from the Pirate Captain. It also has a 1/15 (6.67%) chance to be dropped by the Flying Dutchman(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). The increase in pickup range is 21.875 tiles, extending the base range of 2.625 tiles to 24.5 tiles. This effect does not stack with that of any of the Gold Ring's upgrades.
Gold Ring.drops_summary: Most pirates (0.2%), Flying Dutchman (6.67%), Pirate Captain (0.8%)

Coin Ring.name: Coin Ring
Coin Ring.tooltip: The Coin Ring is a Hardmode accessory created by other accessories exclusively dropped from pirate enemies during Pirate Invasion. It combines the effect of Gold Ring and Lucky Coin, which increases the pickup range for coins, and causes enemies to occasionally drop 1 to 10 more coins when hit and grants +0.05 luck.

Greedy Ring.name: Greedy Ring
Greedy Ring.tooltip: The Greedy Ring is a Hardmode accessory that combines the Discount Card's 20% discount off at any NPC shop, the Lucky Coin's 20% chance of spawning 1–10 extra coins whenever an enemy is hit and +0.05 luck, and the Gold Ring's increased coin pickup range.

Fish Finder.name: Fish Finder
Fish Finder.tooltip: The Fish Finder is an informational accessory that enables an on-screen display of the weather, wind speed, moon phase, and the player's Fishing Power.

Weather Radio.name: Weather Radio
Weather Radio.tooltip: The Weather Radio is an informational accessory that displays the current weather and wind speed on the Surface, even if the player is in the Underground, Cavern, or Underworld layers. The Weather Radio can be received as a 1/34 (2.94%) chance reward for completing a fishing quest for the Angler NPC, depending on the number of completed quests and other factors (see Angler § Quest rewards for details). The Angler will not give the player a Weather Radio as a reward if they already have one in their inventory or in any of their portable storage items or loadouts. However, if the player has all of the Angler's fishing and informational accessories (or their upgrades like the Angler Tackle Bag and Fish Finder) in their inventories, this rule will be ignored.

Hades Dye.name: Hades Dye
Hades Dye.tooltip: Hades Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When equipped, it turns the dyed armor, accessory, or equipment blue, also adding a blue flames effect.

Twilight Dye.name: Twilight Dye
Twilight Dye.tooltip: Twilight Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. It can, like other dyes, be equipped in the dyes slot in the player's equipment or accessory tabs in their inventory. When the dye is used, the armor or vanity item associated with it will get a very night-sky-like effect which will move dynamically with the player.

Acid Dye.name: Acid Dye
Acid Dye.tooltip: Acid Dye is a dye acquired as a random reward from the Dye Trader for giving him a Strange Plant. When equipped in the dye slot, it applies a dark green rippling effect that pulses outward, similar to Blue Acid Dye and Red Acid Dye. Items dyed by it can be seen in the dark but do not emit light.

Glowing Mushroom Dye.name: Glowing Mushroom Dye
Glowing Mushroom Dye.tooltip: Glowing Mushroom Dye is a dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When equipped, it gives items a blue and black color palette which glows in the dark.

Phase Dye.name: Phase Dye
Phase Dye.tooltip: Phase Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. It seems to invert the colors of the object it is attached to as well as giving a strange purple aura. When the user is damaged, the dye flashes very quickly.

Magic Lantern.name: Magic Lantern
Magic Lantern.tooltip: The Magic Lantern is a light pet-summoning item that spawns a small glowing Magic Lantern which hovers above the player, emitting dim yellow light. The lantern will also highlight all treasure within up to 15 tiles from the lantern's location, overlaying small yellow sparkles over nearby valuable treasure, which is similar to the sparkling effect produced by a Spelunker Potion. The Magic Lantern can be purchased from the Skeleton Merchant for 10 Gold during the night of a full moon. The lantern will always try to maintain a position just forward of and above the player, passing through blocks as needed. If the player is far enough away or in midair, the lantern will propel itself with a rocket exhaust in order to catch up to them. The lantern's position can block objects of interest at ceiling height, but if the player just turns around, the lantern will move to their other side.

Music Box (Lunar Boss).name: Music Box (Lunar Boss)
Music Box (Lunar Boss).tooltip: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End), which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 Gold after defeating the Moon Lord. A recorded Music Box can be played back in one of two ways: Equipping it as an accessory. Placing it as furniture and activating it, either by the ⚷ Open / Activate button or with wires. Recorded Music Boxes can be reverted into blank ones through Shimmer transmutation. There are 101 different Music Boxes available.

Rainbow Torch.name: Rainbow Torch
Rainbow Torch.tooltip: Torches are furniture items that function as light sources when placed, held, or dropped (via the Throw button). Regular Torches can be found randomly in Chests and Pots, as a bonus drop from slimes, Torch Zombies, or purchased from the Merchant or Skeleton Merchant for 50 Copper each. Placing at least 101 Torches in close proximity below the surface layer in any biome will start the Torch God mini-event. Completing the event will grant the Torch God's Favor, which allows the player to automatically convert ordinary Torches to one of the biome types.

Cursed Campfire.name: Cursed Campfire
Cursed Campfire.tooltip: Campfires are a type of furniture and crafting station that emit light and grant the Cozy Fire buff to players in their vicinity, which provides 10% increased innate health regeneration and additionally grants 0.5 HP/s constant regeneration. The buff is applied to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the campfire, similar to Heart Lanterns and Sunflowers. Campfires are also minor crafting stations, and uniquely, campfires are used to cook Marshmallow on a Stick (see their page for details). Campfires can be toggled off and on with ⚷ Open / Activate, which extinguishes the flame, light, and disables the Cozy Fire buff. They can also be extinguished and lit with the Water Gun and Slime Gun respectively, and as mechanisms, they can be toggled with wire. Campfires are extinguished by rain in The Constant special world seed.

Crystal Vile Shard.name: Crystal Vile Shard
Crystal Vile Shard.tooltip: The Crystal Vile Shard is a Hardmode wand that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Hallowed Mimics. When used, it extends a crystal spike from the player's position, which passes through blocks, pierces infinite enemies, and deals 0.17 s global invincibility. The crystal spike has 7–8 shaft segments followed by 1 head segment, and each has a length of 2 tiles. The head deals 125% of the weapon's damage and knockback. The spike extends segmentally every 0.05 s, with each individual segment lasting 0.15 s. The projectiles of Crystal Vile Shard have 10 armor penetration, which stacks with the former segment.Hence the actual armor penetration increases with segments, from the root's 10 to the head's 80 or 90. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Shadowflame Bow.name: Shadowflame Bow
Shadowflame Bow.tooltip: The Shadowflame Bow is a Hardmode bow that has a 1/6 (16.67%) / 1/3 (33.33%) chance to drop from Goblin Warlocks during a Hardmode Goblin Army. When used, it converts any type of arrow into Shadowflame Arrows. Shadowflame Arrows can pierce two enemies and inflict the Shadowflame debuff for 2–5 seconds. Shadowflame Arrows have a medium velocity but a significantly longer arc. The Shadowflame Bow also has a base 7% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Shadowflame Hex Doll.name: Shadowflame Hex Doll
Shadowflame Hex Doll.tooltip: The Shadowflame Hex Doll is a Hardmode magic weapon that fires a spread of three curving purple tentacle projectiles per use at a medium range, inflicting the Shadowflame debuff onto enemies for 4–8 seconds, and piercing 2 targets before dissipating on the 3rd hit. The third tentacle fired in each use is always aimed directly towards the cursor, but the first two keep their random spread. The Shadowflame Hex Doll also has a base 7% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. The Shadowflame Hex Doll has a 1/6 (16.67%) / 1/3 (33.33%) chance to drop from Goblin Warlocks during a Hardmode Goblin Army. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Shadowflame Knife.name: Shadowflame Knife
Shadowflame Knife.tooltip: The Shadowflame Knife is a Hardmode melee weapon that has a 1/6 (16.67%) / 1/3 (33.33%) chance to drop from Goblin Warlocks during the Goblin Army event. When used, it fires a small gravity-affected knife projectile that can bounce off enemies up to two times, but dissipates upon contact with blocks. It inflicts the Shadowflame debuff for 1–3 seconds on hit. The Shadowflame Knife also has a base 7% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Acorns.name: Acorns
Acorns.tooltip: The Acorn is a type of seed used to plant trees. Acorns can be planted on regular green grass, Hallowed grass, Corrupt grass, Crimson grass, Jungle grass, Sand, or Snow, where they will create saplings that will grow into trees, under the right conditions. Acorns are randomly dropped when cutting down or shaking trees and can also be purchased from the Dryad for 10 Copper each. Acorns cannot be retrieved after being placed. Destroying the sapling will not yield any items. Trees grown from Acorns will be much shorter than ones naturally generated at world creation. This can be circumvented by Infused Fertilizer. Acorns can be used as ammunition for the Acorn Slingshot.

Cold Snap.name: Cold Snap
Cold Snap.tooltip: Paintings are decorative furniture items that can be placed on background walls. Each one is a framed image that depicts a particular scene, usually Terraria-related. Their tooltips generally contain a person's name, intended to credit each painting's artist; although the names appear to be fictional, most of them correspond to known Terraria developers, artists, testing staff, and community members (see Trivia below). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions, the Magic Lantern, Spelunker Glowsticks, and Spelunker Flares. There are a total of 193 paintings, 25 of which are sold by the Painter, 7 by the Princess, 4 by the Golfer, 2 by the Zoologist, 2 by the Clothier, 1 by the Truffle, and 27 are randomly sold by the Traveling Merchant. 35 paintings can be found in Underground Cabins, another 14 in the Underground Desert Cabins, 26 in the Dungeon, 12 in The Underworld, 6 from Floating Islands, 5 obtained by fishing, 1 from the Jungle Temple, 5 randomly acquired from Goodie Bags, 8 dropped by Solar Eclipse enemies, 8 awarded randomly by the Angler for completing fishing quests, 1 from the Living Tree, and 4 dropped by enemies.
