Bone Rattle.name: Bone Rattle
Bone Rattle.tooltip: The Bone Rattle is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Face Monster that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Baby Face Monster will appear to hold onto a flying Crimera-like creature to catch up to them. The Bone Rattle has a 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped by the Brain of Cthulhu.
Bone Rattle.drops_summary: Brain of Cthulhu (5%), Treasure Bag (Brain of Cthulhu) (5%)

Architect Gizmo Pack.name: Architect Gizmo Pack
Architect Gizmo Pack.tooltip: The Architect Gizmo Pack is an accessory which increases block and wall placement speed and reach and automatically paints placed objects, essentially granting all of the effects of the accessories used to craft it.

Crimson Heart.name: Crimson Heart
Crimson Heart.tooltip: The Crimson Heart is a background object found deep in the chasms of The Crimson. A world generated with the Crimson features several Crimson Hearts, and destroying at least three of them (in a single world) is usually a crucial step in game advancement. This can be done using any hammer or explosives. Crimson Hearts release a fair amount of their own flickering light, similar to Crimson Altars. They are the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Shadow Orbs. Crimson Hearts are usually located at the ends of the branches that split from the main circular room of the Crimson's caves, surrounded by Crimstone Blocks. In order to reach them, the player may use a Deathbringer Pickaxe or better pickaxe, explosives, or Purification Powder.

Meowmere.name: Meowmere
Meowmere.tooltip: The Meowmere is a Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord. When swung, it fires a cat head projectile with a visual rainbow trail every 0.23 seconds. The cat head deals 125% of the weapon's damage (250 base damage), is affected by gravity, and can pierce enemies or bounce off blocks up to four times. Upon bouncing off a block, the cat head makes a "meow" sound and emits damaging rainbow explosions that grow in size with each bounce. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Enchanted Sundial.name: Enchanted Sundial
Enchanted Sundial.tooltip: The Enchanted Sundial is a Hardmode furniture item. It can be triggered by the ⚷ Open / Activate key or wires, doing so will advance time to sunrise (4:30 AM) the following day. It has a 7-day cooldown period, so once used, it will not be usable again until 7 in-game days have passed (see Notes for details). When the Enchanted Sundial is ready to be used, the dial at the top of its sprite and the sun in the middle will both glow bright yellow. The Enchanted Sundial is obtained from fished Pearlwood (1/200 (0.5%) chance), Mythril (1/60 (1.67%) chance), and Titanium Crates (1/20 (5%) chance). The Enchanted Sundial does not turn the time to the next day immediately. It instead "fast-forwards" time, causing it to pass 60 times faster than usual (1 hour of in-game time, which would usually take 1 minute of real-life time, takes only 1 second while the Enchanted Sundial is active). When the Enchanted Sundial is taking effect, the effect of other time-accelerating methods (bed and Journey Mode Time Menu) will be ignored. However, unlike these methods, the Enchanted Sundial does not increase tile update rate in world, meaning that things like plant growth and biome spread is unaffected when it is active. The Enchanted Moondial is its night counterpart, allowing the player to advance time to dusk (7:30 PM) of the current or following day.
Enchanted Sundial.drops_summary: Mythril Crate (1.67%), Pearlwood Crate (0.5%), Titanium Crate (5%)

Star Wrath.name: Star Wrath
Star Wrath.tooltip: The Star Wrath is a Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord. When swung, it causes three pink stars to fall toward the cursor. The stars can pierce one enemy and pass through blocks until they are at the cursor's altitude or less than 12.5 tiles above the player's center, after which they will dissipate upon contact with a block. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Smooth Marble Block.name: Smooth Marble Block
Smooth Marble Block.tooltip: The Smooth Marble Block is a smoother version of the Marble Block. It can be used to craft the Marble furniture set.

Hellstone Brick Wall.name: Hellstone Brick Wall
Hellstone Brick Wall.tooltip: The Hellstone Brick Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Ruined Houses in the Underworld, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player.

Guide to Plant Fiber Cordage.name: Guide to Plant Fiber Cordage
Guide to Plant Fiber Cordage.tooltip: The Guide to Plant Fiber Cordage is an accessory that, when equipped, causes destroyed vines to drop Vine Ropes. It has a 1/11 (9.09%) chance of being found in surface Chests, or a 1/120 (0.83%) chance in Wooden Crates and Pearlwood Crates obtained from fishing. It can also be purchased from the Skeleton Merchant for 2 Gold 50 Silver during First Quarter moons.

Wand of Sparking.name: Wand of Sparking
Wand of Sparking.tooltip: The Wand of Sparking is a pre-Hardmode wand. When used, it fires a spark that travels in a slight curve for about 23 tiles before dissipating. The spark can pierce one enemy and has a 1/2 (50%) chance to inflict the On Fire! debuff. The Wand of Sparking also has a base 14% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. The Wand of Sparking has a 1/11 (9.09%) chance of being obtained from wooden Chests on the Surface or in the Underground layer, and can also be sold by the Skeleton Merchant during a third quarter moon for 1 Gold. Its best modifier is Demonic or Deadly, with the former granting improved critical strike chance and the latter granting improved speed. It cannot get modifiers that affect knockback or mana cost.

Gold Bird Cage.name: Gold Bird Cage
Gold Bird Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters. A critter caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item. Gold cages are regular cages containing gold critters. Aside from their higher sell value and rarity, they are the same as regular cages. Placed cages are partially transparent. They can be stacked on top of each other, but no other types of furniture can be placed on a cage. Players can stand on top of cages like platforms, even though they are otherwise background furniture.

Gold Butterfly Jar.name: Gold Butterfly Jar
Gold Butterfly Jar.tooltip: Butterfly jars are pieces of decorative furniture created by combining a butterfly, captured with a Bug Net, with a Bottle. By throwing a butterfly jar into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the butterfly as an item.  Butterfly jars function the same way as cages for other critters. They have an animated sprite when placed down, and the butterflies will fly around inside the jars.

Silk Rope.name: Silk Rope
Silk Rope.tooltip: Ropes are placeable items that primarily provide quick vertical mobility. They can be placed adjacent to blocks in any direction, or in midair where background walls are present. Ropes can also be placed atop any existing placed Rope, which extends the total length of the Rope downward without the player having to be at the bottom of the Rope column. Once placed, Ropes are used by pressing ▲ Up or ▼ Down while moving over them. There are four different types of Rope, which are acquired in different ways: Rope can be found randomly in Chests and Pots, as a bonus drop from slimes, or purchased from the Merchant and Skeleton Merchant for 10 Copper each. Vine Rope is acquired by destroying vines while the Guide to Plant Fiber Cordage is equipped. Silk Rope is crafted from Silk at a Loom. Web Rope is crafted By Hand from Cobwebs. All Rope variants operate identically, but Silk and Web Ropes are immune to falling lava, as opposed to normal and Vine Ropes, which will be dislodged similarly to Torches. All types can be crafted into their respective Rope Coils, consumable items useful for placing Ropes in inaccessible locations. Vertical movement speed on a Rope equals that of a free fall, though moving down via the Rope and hitting the ground does not cause fall damage. Horizontal movement is also possible by placing adjacent Rope horizontally, but is much slower. Visually, the player appears to move along a Rope using a mechanical tool with wheels, as though they were riding a rail. This tool appears automatically when using Rope, does not exist as a separate item, and is available from the beginning of the game.

Web Rope.name: Web Rope
Web Rope.tooltip: Ropes are placeable items that primarily provide quick vertical mobility. They can be placed adjacent to blocks in any direction, or in midair where background walls are present. Ropes can also be placed atop any existing placed Rope, which extends the total length of the Rope downward without the player having to be at the bottom of the Rope column. Once placed, Ropes are used by pressing ▲ Up or ▼ Down while moving over them. There are four different types of Rope, which are acquired in different ways: Rope can be found randomly in Chests and Pots, as a bonus drop from slimes, or purchased from the Merchant and Skeleton Merchant for 10 Copper each. Vine Rope is acquired by destroying vines while the Guide to Plant Fiber Cordage is equipped. Silk Rope is crafted from Silk at a Loom. Web Rope is crafted By Hand from Cobwebs. All Rope variants operate identically, but Silk and Web Ropes are immune to falling lava, as opposed to normal and Vine Ropes, which will be dislodged similarly to Torches. All types can be crafted into their respective Rope Coils, consumable items useful for placing Ropes in inaccessible locations. Vertical movement speed on a Rope equals that of a free fall, though moving down via the Rope and hitting the ground does not cause fall damage. Horizontal movement is also possible by placing adjacent Rope horizontally, but is much slower. Visually, the player appears to move along a Rope using a mechanical tool with wheels, as though they were riding a rail. This tool appears automatically when using Rope, does not exist as a separate item, and is available from the beginning of the game.

Silk Rope Coil.name: Silk Rope Coil
Silk Rope Coil.tooltip: Rope Coils are consumable mobility items that, when thrown by the player, travel in an arc affected by gravity until striking a block. On making contact, a vertical string of ten pieces of the respective Rope type will be placed, starting from the point of contact and descending until the Rope runs out or makes contact with another block below. Once in place, the Ropes created by a Rope Coil are ordinary Rope items that can be climbed, expanded with other placed Ropes, and collected with a pickaxe or drill. If a thrown Rope Coil strikes the top of an already placed Rope, it will automatically extend the existing Rope. If the coil cannot extend lower than ten tiles because of an obstacle, the excess Rope pieces will drop as items. If the coil cannot extend at all, the excess Rope will drop as the coil item. There are no rope coil analogues for chains nor streamers.

Web Rope Coil.name: Web Rope Coil
Web Rope Coil.tooltip: Rope Coils are consumable mobility items that, when thrown by the player, travel in an arc affected by gravity until striking a block. On making contact, a vertical string of ten pieces of the respective Rope type will be placed, starting from the point of contact and descending until the Rope runs out or makes contact with another block below. Once in place, the Ropes created by a Rope Coil are ordinary Rope items that can be climbed, expanded with other placed Ropes, and collected with a pickaxe or drill. If a thrown Rope Coil strikes the top of an already placed Rope, it will automatically extend the existing Rope. If the coil cannot extend lower than ten tiles because of an obstacle, the excess Rope pieces will drop as items. If the coil cannot extend at all, the excess Rope will drop as the coil item. There are no rope coil analogues for chains nor streamers.

Marble Block.name: Marble Block
Marble Block.tooltip: The Marble Block is a natural block found in Marble Caves. It can be crafted into Smooth Marble Blocks in order to craft the Marble-themed furniture set.

Marble Wall.name: Marble Wall
Marble Wall.tooltip: The Marble Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Marble Caves, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed. It can also be generated as part of an Underground Cabin in a Marble Cave, considered safe. It is also considered a safe wall when placed by the player.

Smooth Marble Wall.name: Smooth Marble Wall
Smooth Marble Wall.tooltip: Smooth Marble Walls are background walls made from Smooth Marble Blocks.

Radar.name: Radar
Radar.tooltip: The Radar is an informational accessory that displays the number of nearby enemies in a 125-tile radius around the player. The Radar has a 1/11 (9.09%) chance of being found inside surface Chests, or a 1/120 (0.83%) chance in Wooden Crates and Pearlwood Crates obtained from fishing. The Radar can also be purchased from the Skeleton Merchant during a Waxing Gibbous for 2 Gold 50 Silver.

Golden Lock Box.name: Golden Lock Box
Golden Lock Box.tooltip: The Golden Lock Box is a grab bag item that is always obtained from Dungeon Crates or Stockade Crates. It always contains one rare item normally found in locked Gold Chests in the Dungeon. It requires one Golden Key to open, which can be obtained from any Dungeon enemy, generally a Dungeon Slime.

Granite Block.name: Granite Block
Granite Block.tooltip: Granite is a block found underground in Granite Caves. In addition to being found in placed form, it can also drop from Granite Elementals and Granite Golems.

Smooth Granite Block.name: Smooth Granite Block
Smooth Granite Block.tooltip: Smooth Granite Blocks are blocks with a dark blue appearance. The block can be crafted or found as walls in underground houses in Granite Caves. They can be used to craft the Granite furniture set.

Granite Wall.name: Granite Wall
Granite Wall.tooltip: The Granite Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Granite Caves, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed. It can also be generated as part of an Underground Cabin in a Granite Cave, considered safe. It is also considered a safe wall when placed by the player.

Smooth Granite Wall.name: Smooth Granite Wall
Smooth Granite Wall.tooltip: Smooth Granite Wall is a type of Wall that can be crafted with Smooth Granite Blocks.

Royal Gel.name: Royal Gel
Royal Gel.tooltip: The Royal Gel is a pre-Hardmode accessory that pacifies most slimes when equipped, causing them to no longer pursue the player, and will deal no contact damage or fire projectiles, even if the player deals damage to them. The Royal Gel is always dropped from King Slime's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode. This does not apply to the following slimes: King Slime and his Spiked Slimes, though the normal Blue Slimes that King Slime spawns remain docile. Queen Slime and her Bouncy Slimes, Crystal Slimes, and Heavenly Slimes.

Key of Night.name: Key of Night
Key of Night.tooltip: The Key of Night is a craftable item that spawns a Corrupt Mimic or a Crimson Mimic when placed in any slot of any empty Chest, depending on whether the world generated with The Corruption or The Crimson, respectively. The world must be in Hardmode and the only item inside the Chest must be a single Key of Night. The Corrupt/Crimson Mimic is spawned as soon as the Chest is closed, consuming both the Key of Night and the Chest.

Key of Light.name: Key of Light
Key of Light.tooltip: The Key of Light is a craftable item which spawns a Hallowed Mimic when placed in any slot of any empty Chest. The world must be in Hardmode and the only item inside the Chest must be a single Key of Light. The Hallowed Mimic is spawned as soon as the Chest is closed, consuming both the Key of Light and the Chest.

Herb Bag.name: Herb Bag
Herb Bag.tooltip: The Herb Bag is a consumable grab bag item, which when opened with ⚷ Open / Activate from within the player's inventory, contains 2–40 herbs and/or herb seeds. Herb Bags can be found in Chests on the surface. A Herb Bag contains 2–5 stacks of 2–8 items each, determined randomly when opened (see Notes for details). It is possible that some or all stacks are of the same item, in which case the stacks are merged. Therefore, Herb Bags always contain at least one and at most five different items.

Javelin.name: Javelin
Javelin.tooltip: The Javelin is a consumable ranged weapon that are dropped by Hoplites, which have a 1/2 (50%) chance to drop 40–80 Javelins. When used, it flies straight for approximately 36 tiles before dropping abruptly. It can hit up to 3 targets. Javelins do not drop themselves as items after hitting a block or enemy.

Tally Counter.name: Tally Counter
Tally Counter.tooltip: The Tally Counter is a post-Skeletron informational accessory that displays the number of enemies of a specific type that have been killed. The Tally Counter will first display "Kill count unavailable" underneath the minimap. After an enemy has been attacked, the text will display how many times that enemy has ever been killed by all players combined in that world. Only the last attacked enemy's count is displayed. The Tally Counter has a 1/100 (1%) chance of being dropped from Angry Bones, Cursed Skulls, Librarian Skeletons and Dark Casters, all of which are found in the Dungeon.
Tally Counter.drops_summary: Angry Bones (1%), Cursed Skull (1%), Dark Caster (1%)

Sextant.name: Sextant
Sextant.tooltip: The Sextant is an informational accessory that displays the current moon phase. The Sextant can be received as a 1/34 (2.94%) chance reward for completing a fishing quest for the Angler NPC, depending on the number of completed quests and other factors (see Angler § Quest rewards for details). The Angler will not give the player a Sextant as a reward if they already have one in their inventory or in any of their portable storage items or loadouts. However, if the player has all of the Angler's fishing and informational accessories (or their upgrades like the Angler Tackle Bag and Fish Finder) in their inventories, this rule will be ignored.

Shield of Cthulhu.name: Shield of Cthulhu
Shield of Cthulhu.tooltip: The Shield of Cthulhu is a pre-Hardmode shield accessory that is always dropped from the Eye of Cthulhu's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode. While equipped, it grants 2 defense and allows the player to perform a dash attack by double-tapping either the ◀ Left or ▶ Right button, or the Dash button once. Dashing into an enemy deals damage to it, causes the player to bounce backward, and grants 0.07 seconds of invincibility frames and 0.17 seconds of immunity to contact damage from the hit enemy. The cooldown between dashes is 0.5 seconds.

Butcher's Chainsaw.name: Butcher's Chainsaw
Butcher's Chainsaw.tooltip: The Butcher's Chainsaw is a Hardmode, post-Plantera chainsaw that has a 1/40 (2.5%) / 79/1600 (4.94%) chance to drop from Butchers during the Solar Eclipse event. Upon hitting an enemy, it fires a spread of 2–5 glowing sparks that are lightly affected by gravity, can pierce once before dissipating on the second hit, deal 50% of the weapon's damage (60 base damage), and inflict 20% of its knockback (base knockback of 1.6 (Very weak)). Sparks also have a 1/2 (50%) chance to inflict the Hellfire debuff for 1–4 seconds. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Stopwatch.name: Stopwatch
Stopwatch.tooltip: The Stopwatch is an informational accessory that displays the player's current movement speed in miles per hour, e.g. "34 mph". The Stopwatch can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 5 Gold.

Meteorite Brick.name: Meteorite Brick
Meteorite Brick.tooltip: Meteorite Brick is a type of decorative brick crafted with Meteorite. It emits a small amount of light when placed. Unlike plain Meteorite, Meteorite Bricks do not inflict the Burning debuff or deal damage to players on contact. They are vulnerable to explosions.

Meteorite Brick Wall.name: Meteorite Brick Wall
Meteorite Brick Wall.tooltip: Meteorite Brick Wall is a wall made from crafting Meteorite Bricks at a Work Bench. It emits light when placed. Like most walls, they will stop enemy spawning, and can be used for NPC houses.

Metal Detector.name: Metal Detector
Metal Detector.tooltip: The Metal Detector is an informational accessory that detects valuable objects, including ores, chests, Life Crystals, and Life Fruit, within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the player. The Metal Detector displays the specific type of what was detected, for instance, "Chlorophyte detected nearby!" When multiple valuables are detected, only the one with the highest value is noted. The Metal Detector has a 1/2 (50%) / 100% chance of being dropped by Nymphs, a rare cavern enemy.

Endless Quiver.name: Endless Quiver
Endless Quiver.tooltip: The Endless Quiver is a Hardmode ammunition item. While in the user's inventory, it acts as a Wooden Arrow that cannot be depleted. It is also compatible with bows that convert Wooden Arrows into a special type (e.g. The Bee's Knees).

Endless Musket Pouch.name: Endless Musket Pouch
Endless Musket Pouch.tooltip: The Endless Musket Pouch is a Hardmode ammunition item. While in the inventory, it acts as an infinite source of Musket Balls.

Toxic Flask.name: Toxic Flask
Toxic Flask.tooltip: The Toxic Flask is a Hardmode, post-Plantera magic weapon that has a 1/40 (2.5%) / 79/1600 (4.94%) chance of being dropped by Dr. Man Flies during the Solar Eclipse event. When used, it throws a flask with low velocity and a heavy arc that explodes into a cluster of small, damaging toxic clouds upon colliding with an enemy or surface. The clouds last for one to two seconds and cannot pass through blocks. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Psycho Knife.name: Psycho Knife
Psycho Knife.tooltip: The Psycho Knife is a Hardmode, post-Plantera broadsword that has a 1/40 (2.5%) / 79/1600 (4.94%) chance of being dropped by Psychos during the Solar Eclipse event. When holding the Psycho Knife and standing still, the player will quickly enter stealth, causing them to turn almost invisible, move much more slowly, and no longer be targeted by certain enemies' projectile attacks. Stealth is engaged gradually over the course of 0.83 seconds, during which the player gains several stat boosts that linearly increase to the following values: +300% melee damage (increases the weapon's damage to 340 without additional melee bonuses) +30% melee critical strike chance (34% base chance) +100% melee knockback (7 (Strong) base knockback) −750 aggro −50% movement speed; then sets sprint speed equal to move speed As a result of the aggro reduction while in stealth, enemies will prefer to target other players, and many kinds of enemies will not chase after the player while they are not using items (see Aggro § Target chasing for details). Stealth mode additionally prevents Fighter AI and Flying AI enemies from firing projectiles at the player while they are not using items. Stealth mode is deactivated upon hitting an target, switching to a different item, riding a mount, or taking damage. Swinging the weapon alone does not cancel stealth, nor does moving. However, moving or swinging the weapon before stealth mode is fully engaged will quickly deactivate stealth. Its best modifier is Legendary. Due to rounding, the Light modifier gives the same speed bonus as Legendary, with fewer other bonuses.

Nail Gun.name: Nail Gun
Nail Gun.tooltip: The Nail Gun is a Hardmode, post-Plantera launcher that consumes Nails as ammunition. When used, it fires a Nail that deals 15% of the weapon's damage (17 base damage) and sticks to enemies or blocks before exploding after 1.5 seconds, dealing 135% damage (155 base damage). Nails are unaffected by gravity until they have traveled roughly 30 tiles, after which they move with an arc similar to that of arrows. The Nail Gun has a 1/25 (4%) / 49/625 (7.84%) chance of being dropped by Nailheads during the Solar Eclipse event. The Nail Gun is always dropped alongside 100–200 Nails. Additional Nails are also sold by both the Merchant and the Arms Dealer for 1 Silver each when the player has the Nail Gun in their inventory. Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.

Nail.name: Nail
Nail.tooltip: The Nail Gun is a Hardmode, post-Plantera launcher that consumes Nails as ammunition. When used, it fires a Nail that deals 15% of the weapon's damage (17 base damage) and sticks to enemies or blocks before exploding after 1.5 seconds, dealing 135% damage (155 base damage). Nails are unaffected by gravity until they have traveled roughly 30 tiles, after which they move with an arc similar to that of arrows. The Nail Gun has a 1/25 (4%) / 49/625 (7.84%) chance of being dropped by Nailheads during the Solar Eclipse event. The Nail Gun is always dropped alongside 100–200 Nails. Additional Nails are also sold by both the Merchant and the Arms Dealer for 1 Silver each when the player has the Nail Gun in their inventory. Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.

Night Vision Helmet.name: Night Vision Helmet
Night Vision Helmet.tooltip: The Night Vision Helmet is an armor piece for the helmet slot. For the player wearing it, it increases the apparent light level provided by all light sources on the screen, similarly to the Night Owl buff. The Night Vision Helmet has a 1/30 (3.33%) chance to be dropped by Granite Elementals and Granite Golems. It can also be purchased from the Cyborg for 5 Gold, after the Martian Madness event has been completed in the current world.

Celestial Shell.name: Celestial Shell
Celestial Shell.tooltip: The Celestial Shell is a Hardmode, post-Golem accessory that combines the stat-boosting powers of the Celestial Stone with the transformation powers of the Moon Shell, allowing both of their effects to happen simultaneously while taking only one accessory slot.

Pink Gel.name: Pink Gel
Pink Gel.tooltip: Pink Gel is a rare crafting material dropped by Pinky in stacks of 25–50. It is primarily used to craft "bouncy" versions of certain consumable items, as well as Restoration Potions. "Bouncy" items act like their normal variants, but bounce more times and more vigorously before losing momentum. Crafting one of each item requires 22 Pink Gel, meaning that killing a single Pinky is sufficient to craft all items at least once.

Bouncy Glowstick.name: Bouncy Glowstick
Bouncy Glowstick.tooltip: The Bouncy Glowstick is a consumable light source that bounces off surfaces while also providing light. Bouncy Glowsticks are the opposite of Sticky Glowsticks, bouncing off of surfaces instead of sticking to them.

Pink Slime Block.name: Pink Slime Block
Pink Slime Block.tooltip: The Pink Slime Block can be created with Pink Gel if the player is near a Solidifier. In a similar way to Silly Balloons, landing on Pink Slime Blocks negates fall damage and causes the player to bounce. Like with Slime Blocks, running over Pink Slime Blocks produces droplet particles. The height of the bounce is dependent on the player's speed, not on the distance they've fallen. Holding a Portal Gun or riding the Slime Mount can allow for higher bounce due to the higher speed limit.

Pink Torch.name: Pink Torch
Pink Torch.tooltip: Torches are furniture items that function as light sources when placed, held, or dropped (via the Throw button). Regular Torches can be found randomly in Chests and Pots, as a bonus drop from slimes, Torch Zombies, or purchased from the Merchant or Skeleton Merchant for 50 Copper each. Placing at least 101 Torches in close proximity below the surface layer in any biome will start the Torch God mini-event. Completing the event will grant the Torch God's Favor, which allows the player to automatically convert ordinary Torches to one of the biome types.

Bouncy Bomb.name: Bouncy Bomb
Bouncy Bomb.tooltip: The Bouncy Bomb is an explosive that functions like the Bomb, but bounces off blocks more intensely.

Bouncy Grenade.name: Bouncy Grenade
Bouncy Grenade.tooltip: The Bouncy Grenade is an explosive consumable ranged weapon made of Pink Gel and Grenades. Instead of rolling or sticking in place upon contact with tiles, it will bounce and retain much of its momentum. Like normal Grenades, they will detonate upon touching an enemy, or the player that threw it.

Peace Candle.name: Peace Candle
Peace Candle.tooltip: The Peace Candle is a furniture item that emits a low amount of light and can be placed only on flat-surface items. While placed nearby or while held, it grants the Peace Candle buff to the player. The Peace Candle buff decreases spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%. The buff is applied to any players holding a Peace Candle or standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on a Peace Candle. In order to be considered "holding" the candle, it must be in the player's hotbar and currently selected; merely being in a player's inventory will not suffice. Multiple Candles will not stack with each other, even if one is placed and the other held. Peace Candles can only be placed on platforms and flat furniture items like Work Benches and Tables. The Peace Candle can be made from a Pink Torch and either Gold Bars or Platinum Bars, meaning that the player needs to have defeated Pinky at least once to craft this item. Pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on Peace Candles shuts them off, and they will toggle when activated via wiring. Peace Candles that are turned off will not activate the Peace Candle buff. The Peace Candle's effect is the opposite of the Water Candle, which increases enemy spawn rate. If a Peace Candle and a Water Candle are active at the same time, they will cancel each other's effects out, resulting in no difference in spawn rate.

Lifeform Analyzer.name: Lifeform Analyzer
Lifeform Analyzer.tooltip: The Lifeform Analyzer is an informational accessory that displays the name of rare enemies, critters, and undiscovered NPCs (see list below) within 81.25 tiles around the player. The Lifeform Analyzer can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 5 Gold.

DPS Meter.name: DPS Meter
DPS Meter.tooltip: The DPS Meter is an informational accessory that displays the DPS of the weapon that last dealt damage to any entity, including enemies, critters, NPCs, Target Dummies, and other players. The DPS Meter can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 5 Gold.

Fisherman's Pocket Guide.name: Fisherman's Pocket Guide
Fisherman's Pocket Guide.tooltip: The Fisherman's Pocket Guide is an informational accessory that displays the player's current Fishing Power. The Fisherman's Pocket Guide can be received as a 1/34 (2.94%) chance reward for completing a fishing quest for the Angler NPC, depending on the number of completed quests and other factors (see Angler § Quest rewards for details). The Angler will not give the player a Fisherman's Pocket Guide as a reward if they already have one in their inventory or in any of their portable storage items or loadouts. However, if the player has all of the Angler's fishing and informational accessories (or their upgrades like the Angler Tackle Bag and Fish Finder) in their inventories, this rule will be ignored.

Goblin Tech.name: Goblin Tech
Goblin Tech.tooltip: The Goblin Tech is an informational accessory that enables an on-screen display of the most valuable block nearby, the player's current DPS, and their current movement speed.

R.E.K. 3000.name: R.E.K. 3000
R.E.K. 3000.tooltip: The R.E.K. 3000  is a post-Skeletron informational accessory that enables an on-screen display of nearby rare creatures, the number of nearby enemies, and the player's enemy kill count.

PDA.name: PDA
PDA.tooltip: The PDA is a post-Skeletron informational accessory that enables an on-screen display of the in-game time, the weather, wind speed, moon phase, the player's Fishing Power, the most valuable block nearby, nearby rare creatures, the number of nearby enemies, the player's enemy kill count, the player's current DPS, the player's current movement speed, the player's horizontal position, and the player's depth.

Cell Phone.name: Cell Phone
Cell Phone.tooltip: The Cell Phone is a post-Skeletron informational item and tool that combines the functions of the PDA and the Magic Mirrors, displaying all information and allowing the player to teleport to their spawn point. Unlike most informational items, the Cell Phone does not double as an accessory. It instead functions solely from the player's main inventory.

Granite Chest.name: Granite Chest
Granite Chest.tooltip: The Granite Chest is a chest storage item found only in Underground Cabins within Granite Caves. Like Marble Chests and Rich Mahogany Chests, Granite Chests have exactly the same loot as Gold Chests.

Meteorite Clock.name: Meteorite Clock
Meteorite Clock.tooltip: Grandfather Clocks are furniture items which provide information about the in-game time. If a player is nearby a Grandfather Clock (about 80 tiles horizontally and 50 tiles vertically), the time is displayed on the right side of the screen, underneath the minimap. The time is rounded to the last hour, similar to Tin and Copper Watches, but pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it will show precise time in minutes as a status message on the bottom left corner. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 21 /  5 craftable versions and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 5 / (Old-gen console version) 2 noncraftable (but still lootable) versions. The regular Grandfather Clock can rarely be found in Underground Cabins. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Meteorite Door.name: Meteorite Door
Meteorite Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Meteorite Lantern.name: Meteorite Lantern
Meteorite Lantern.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Meteorite Candle.name: Meteorite Candle
Meteorite Candle.tooltip: Candles are a type of furniture and light source. Candles can only be placed on flat-surface items. Candles will produce light underwater if placed and can be toggled on and off with ⚷ Open / Activate and by mechanisms. Certain types of candles provide buffs or debuffs. The Water Candle is a special type of candle found in Dungeons which increases enemy spawn rates by 33% and the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50% when placed or held. The Peace Candle reduces spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%, in contrast to the Water Candle. The Shadow Candle(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns in the area. For Water Candles and Peace Candles, multiple candles cannot stack, even if one is placed and the other is held.

Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.

Meteorite Chest.name: Meteorite Chest
Meteorite Chest.tooltip: Chests are a type of furniture functioning as storage items. They are accessed using ⚷ Open / Activate and can store up to 40 item stacks in rows of  10×4 /   8×5. In addition to many being craftable, a number of Chests are placed in random locations during world generation. The loot contained in these Chests is determined during world generation, and will not change if the world enters Hardmode. Chests cannot be broken with items inside (the blocks a filled Chest is placed on would also have this trait). However, the Block Swap feature allows the player to change the type of a Chest without having to destroy it. Some types of Chests can be locked by the player using a Chest Lock. When doing so, they will require a key to open again. There are 23 varieties of naturally-occurring Chests (12 of which cannot be crafted), 53 that can only be crafted, and 1 purchasable Chest, for a total of 77 Chest types.

Marble Chest.name: Marble Chest
Marble Chest.tooltip: The Marble Chest is a chest storage item found only in Underground Cabins within Marble Caves. Like Granite Chests and Rich Mahogany Chests, Marble Chests have exactly the same loot as Gold Chests.

Magic Water Dropper.name: Magic Water Dropper
Magic Water Dropper.tooltip: Magic Droppers are Hardmode items used to place "droplets" — dripping liquid effects on ceilings. Once placed, they permanently display an intermittent dripping effect. The effect is purely visual, and has no functional use. Magic Droppers are crafted with an Empty Dropper at Water, Lava, Honey, or with any Sand, with the Crystal Ball nearby. The Magic Shimmer Dropper is an exception, crafted by throwing an Empty Dropper into the Shimmer. Magic Droppers can be placed at the bottom side of a block, consuming the item in the process. Droplets can be removed by mining them with a pickaxe, but doing so will not drop any item. Droplets are also naturally generated in random areas on world generation. They spawn below ceilings that have their corresponding liquid above them, as though that liquid were "leaking through". Natural droplets can be mined just like the player-placed version, and similarly drip indefinitely until removed by a player.

Golden Bug Net.name: Golden Bug Net
Golden Bug Net.tooltip: The Golden Bug Net is an upgraded version of the Bug Net and Lavaproof Bug Net. It functions similarly, being a swung tool that captures critters, but is larger, faster, and can destroy any tiles that weapons can destroy (like tall grass, vines, or fully grown Pumpkins), and also allows the player to catch Underworld critters (Lavaflies, Hell Butterflies, and Magma Snails). The Golden Bug Net has a base 1/80 (1.25%) chance of being obtained from the Angler as a reward for completing fishing quests.

The effect is purely visual, and has no functional use. Magic Droppers are crafted with an Empty Dropper at Water, Lava, Honey, or with any Sand, with the Crystal Ball nearby. The Magic Shimmer Dropper is an exception, crafted by throwing an Empty Dropper into the Shimmer. Magic Droppers can be placed at the bottom side of a block, consuming the item in the process. Droplets can be removed by mining them with a pickaxe, but doing so will not drop any item. Droplets are also naturally generated in random areas on world generation. They spawn below ceilings that have their corresponding liquid above them, as though that liquid were "leaking through". Natural droplets can be mined just like the player-placed version, and similarly drip indefinitely until removed by a player.

Empty Dropper.name: Empty Dropper
Empty Dropper.tooltip: The Empty Dropper is a Hardmode crafting material purchased from the Wizard for 1 Silver. It is used in the crafting of Magic Droppers. The Crystal Ball must be near water, lava, or honey, to craft the respective liquid's dropper.

Gladiator Helmet.name: Gladiator Helmet
Gladiator Helmet.tooltip: Gladiator armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Gladiator Helmet, Gladiator Breastplate, and Gladiator Leggings. Each piece has a 1/21 (4.76%) chance of being dropped by Hoplites. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +16 defense Immunity to knockback

Gladiator Breastplate.name: Gladiator Breastplate
Gladiator Breastplate.tooltip: Gladiator armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Gladiator Helmet, Gladiator Breastplate, and Gladiator Leggings. Each piece has a 1/21 (4.76%) chance of being dropped by Hoplites. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +16 defense Immunity to knockback

Gladiator Leggings.name: Gladiator Leggings
Gladiator Leggings.tooltip: Gladiator armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Gladiator Helmet, Gladiator Breastplate, and Gladiator Leggings. Each piece has a 1/21 (4.76%) chance of being dropped by Hoplites. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +16 defense Immunity to knockback

Reflective Dye.name: Reflective Dye
Reflective Dye.tooltip: Reflective Dye is a dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When equipped, it will give the selected accessory/armor a "shiny" effect, reflecting the surrounding light around the player. The reflection is more pronounced the closer the player is to a light source. The dye will prioritize light from the sun when the player is outside. From some perspectives, the player may look 3D when this dye is equipped all over. As with other reflective dyes, this dye is not animated when standing still, but the shading on a dyed piece of equipment will change according to the surrounding light, giving it the appearance of light reflecting off of a shining metallic object.

Enchanted Nightcrawler.name: Enchanted Nightcrawler
Enchanted Nightcrawler.tooltip: The Enchanted Nightcrawler is a critter that appears as a glowing pink and sparkly Worm. Enchanted Nightcrawlers can spawn naturally during a Starfall when few clouds are in the sky (such as during a Lantern Night), can be obtained by crafting, and also have a 3/10 (30%) chance of being obtained from a Can Of Worms. The Enchanted Nightcrawler has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Enchanted Nightcrawler can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Enchanted Nightcrawler Cage). Once crafted, the Enchanted Nightcrawler cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Enchanted Nightcrawler can be used as bait for fishing, with 35% bait power.

Grubby.name: Grubby
Grubby.tooltip: Grubby is one of three critters that occasionally spawn in the Jungle or Underground Jungle biome when a player breaks a plant, the others being Sluggy (rarer) and Buggy (rarest). Grubby is the most common of the three. Grubby has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. Grubby can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Grubby Cage). Once crafted,  Grubby cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. Grubby can be used as bait for fishing, with 15% bait power. Grubby can be spawned by the Buggy Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.

Sluggy.name: Sluggy
Sluggy.tooltip: Sluggy is one of three critters that occasionally spawn in the Jungle or Underground Jungle biome when a player breaks a plant, the others being Grubby (more common) and Buggy (rarest). Sluggy has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. Sluggy can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Sluggy Cage). Once crafted,  Sluggy cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. Sluggy can be used as bait for fishing, with 25% bait power. Sluggy can be spawned by the Buggy Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.

Buggy.name: Buggy
Buggy.tooltip: Buggy is one of three critters that occasionally spawn in the Jungle or Underground Jungle biome when a player breaks a plant, the others being Sluggy (more common) and Grubby (most common). Buggy is the rarest of the three. Buggy has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. Buggy can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Buggy Cage). Once crafted,  Buggy cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. Buggy can be used as bait for fishing, with 40% bait power. Buggy can be spawned by the Buggy Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.

Grub Soup.name: Grub Soup
Grub Soup.tooltip: Grub Soup is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 14 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().

Bomb Fish.name: Bomb Fish
Bomb Fish.tooltip: The Bomb Fish is an explosive that functions identically to the Sticky Bomb, but does not slow down in water. It is obtained through fishing, with the number obtained depending on the player's Fishing Power.

Frost Daggerfish.name: Frost Daggerfish
Frost Daggerfish.tooltip: The Frost Daggerfish is a consumable ranged weapon. It can hit up to 3 targets. Depending to player's final Fishing Power, from 7 to 137 Frost Daggerfish can be fished from lakes in Snow biomes at a time. When thrown, the Frost Daggerfish acts similarly to Shurikens or Throwing Knives, flying in an arc and then spinning to the ground, where they break upon impact and cannot be recovered. The Angler uses Frost Daggerfish to defend himself against nearby enemies.

Sharpening Station.name: Sharpening Station
Sharpening Station.tooltip: The Sharpening Station is a furniture item found naturally generated in Underground Cabins in the Underground Jungle. In Hardmode, it is also sold by the Merchant for 10 Gold. Placing and pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Sharpening Station grants the Sharpened buff, which increases armor penetration of melee weapons and melee projectiles by 12. This lasts until the player dies or leaves the world, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). Unlike equipment buff items, the Sharpening Station must be placed in order to activate the buff. It can be mined with a pickaxe or drill and picked up again, even while the buff is active, which will not cancel the buff. Placement is only dependent on an adequate space of 3×2 tiles being available.

Ice Mirror.name: Ice Mirror
Ice Mirror.tooltip: The Magic Mirror is a pre-Hardmode tool. When used, it plays an animation before teleporting the player to their spawn point. Compared to the Recall Potion, the Magic Mirror has unlimited uses, but a delay of 0.75 seconds (45 ticks), which is longer than the Recall Potion's 0.167 seconds (10 ticks) before teleporting. The Ice Mirror(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is a functionally identical alternative to the Magic Mirror. Magic Mirrors can be found in Chests generated in the Underground and Cavern layers. Ice Mirrors can be found in Frozen Chests generated in the Ice biome. Newly created characters in Journey Mode(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) spawn with a Magic Mirror.

Sailfish Boots.name: Sailfish Boots
Sailfish Boots.tooltip: The Sailfish Boots are a pre-Hardmode accessory that can be found in Wooden Crates and Iron Crates. While equipped, they grant the ability to sprint, allowing the player to reach maximum running speed faster, and they increase the player's maximum movement speed to 31 mph (22.73 tiles/second). The player will leave behind a visual trail of water particles as they sprint. The Hermes Boots, Flurry Boots, and Sailfish Boots have the same functionality, and their effects do not stack with each other.
Sailfish Boots.drops_summary: Iron Crate (4.26%), Mythril Crate (4.19%), Pearlwood Crate (2.49%), +1 more

Tsunami in a Bottle.name: Tsunami in a Bottle
Tsunami in a Bottle.tooltip: The Tsunami in a Bottle is an accessory which can be found in Wooden, Iron, Pearlwood(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Mythril Crates(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Similar to the Cloud in a Bottle, it allows the player to double-jump. Instead of a cloud beneath the player's feet, it creates burst of water when jumping. The Tsunami jump goes 7 tiles into the air, totalling 13 tiles when put together with the first jump.
Tsunami in a Bottle.drops_summary: Iron Crate (4.04%), Mythril Crate (3.98%), Pearlwood Crate (2.24%), +1 more

Target Dummy.name: Target Dummy
Target Dummy.tooltip: The Target Dummy is a furniture item that serves as a test target for player attacks. It can be attacked repeatedly by players, displaying damage numbers just as enemies would, in order to test the effective damage output of a weapon as affected by any modifiers, current buffs, or equipped boost items. The Target Dummy is indestructible, regardless of the amount of damage it takes. It can be freed using any pickaxe, drill, or explosive. The Target Dummy will also display damage and visual effects caused by damage-producing debuffs, allowing players to test their damage output, frequency, and duration. Though it visually recoils when struck, the Target Dummy is unresponsive to knockback and will never move.

Corrupt Crate.name: Corrupt Crate
Corrupt Crate.tooltip: The Corrupt Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can only be fished in The Corruption. It contains items found in standard crates and always contains an item normally dropped by destroying a Shadow Orb. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Defiled Crate.

Crimson Crate.name: Crimson Crate
Crimson Crate.tooltip: The Crimson Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can only be fished in The Crimson. It contains items found in standard crates and always contains an item normally dropped by destroying a Crimson Heart. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Hematic Crate.

Dungeon Crate.name: Dungeon Crate
Dungeon Crate.tooltip: The Dungeon Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can only be fished in the Dungeon after Skeletron has been defeated. Opening Dungeon or Stockade Crates is the only way to obtain the Golden Lock Box, and therefore any Dungeon-exclusive items normally found in Locked Gold Chests, once the Dungeon has been fully looted. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Stockade Crate.

Sky Crate.name: Sky Crate
Sky Crate.tooltip: The Sky Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can only be fished in Space, e.g. in Floating Lakes. It contains items found in standard crates and always contains an item normally found in Skyware Chests (with the exception of the Sky Mill). Its Hardmode counterpart is the Azure Crate.

Hallowed Crate.name: Hallowed Crate
Hallowed Crate.tooltip: The Hallowed Crate is a crate that can only be fished in The Hallow. It contains items found in standard crates. The Hallowed Crate can be obtained by throwing a Divine Crate into Shimmer. It can also be obtained by building an artificial Hallowed biome in a pre-Hardmode world and fishing for it there. When fishing in the Hallow in Hardmode, only Divine Crates will be caught, the Hallowed Crate's Hardmode counterpart.

Jungle Crate.name: Jungle Crate
Jungle Crate.tooltip: The Jungle Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can only be fished in the Jungle. It contains items found in standard crates and always contains an item normally found in Ivy Chests within Jungle Shrines or Living Mahogany Trees. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Bramble Crate.

Crystal Serpent.name: Crystal Serpent
Crystal Serpent.tooltip: The Crystal Serpent is a Hardmode wand that can be obtained extremely rarely by fishing in The Hallow biome in any layer. When used, it fires a pink charge that shatters into 3–5 smaller sparks upon impact with an enemy or block, each of which deals 80% of the weapon's damage and knockback (32 base damage and a knockback of 3.52 (Weak)). These sparks are affected by gravity and bounce off blocks, lasting for 0.67 seconds before dissipating. It is the Hallowed counterpart to the Corruption's Toxikarp, the Crimson's Bladetongue, and the Jungle's Barnacle Staff. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Toxikarp.name: Toxikarp
Toxikarp.tooltip: The Toxikarp is a Hardmode ranged weapon that can be obtained extremely rarely by fishing in the Corruption biome in any layer. When used, it fires greenish bubbles that travel in the direction aimed for a short distance before ascending rapidly and inflict the Poisoned debuff for 10–29 seconds. If the bubbles do not strike a creature or a block, they will eventually ascend into space. The bubbles can pass through platforms without breaking. If they come into contact with water, they will instantly start to ascend instead. The Toxikarp has infinite ammunition and will continue to launch bubbles as long as the player is firing it. It is the Corruption counterpart to the Crimson's Bladetongue, the Hallow's Crystal Serpent, and the Jungle's Barnacle Staff. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Bladetongue.name: Bladetongue
Bladetongue.tooltip: The Bladetongue is a Hardmode broadsword that can be obtained extremely rarely by fishing in the Crimson biome in any layer. On enemy hits, it inflicts the Ichor debuff for 5–9 seconds and fires an ichor stream at a random angle in front of the player. The ichor stream is affected by gravity, deals 50% of the weapon's damage (27 base damage) and 70% of its knockback (base knockback of 4.025 (Average)), pierces 4 enemies before dissipating on the 5th hit, can bounce off blocks, and also inflicts the Ichor debuff for 3–7 seconds. It is the Crimson counterpart to the Corruption's Toxikarp, the Hallow's Crystal Serpent, and the Jungle's Barnacle Staff. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Shark Tooth Necklace.name: Shark Tooth Necklace
Shark Tooth Necklace.tooltip: The Shark Tooth Necklace is an accessory which has a 1/150 (0.67%) / 1/75 (1.33%) chance to drop from Blood Zombies and Dripplers found during a Blood Moon. It increases the player's armor penetration by 5 when equipped.

Money Trough.name: Money Trough
Money Trough.tooltip: The Money Trough is a portable storage item that temporarily summons a flying pet-like version of the Piggy Bank. The Money Trough enables players to access the contents of their Piggy Bank without having to manually place the Piggy Bank or any furniture for it to rest on. The floating Piggy Bank despawns after 3 minutes, but can be resummoned repeatedly at no cost. The Flying Piggy Bank does not follow the player like pets or minions would, instead it hovers stationarily at the point summoned. Once summoned, other players may use it as well to access their own Piggy Bank. The Money Trough has a 1/200 (0.5%) / 1/100 (1%) chance of being dropped by Blood Zombies and Dripplers during a Blood Moon, or with a much lower (1/4000 (0.025%) / 1/2000 (0.05%)) chance from their statue-spawned versions (regardless of whether a Blood Moon is occurring). It also has a 1/15 (6.67%) chance of being dropped by Wandering Eye Fish and Zombie Mermen, which can be fished up during a Blood Moon.
Money Trough.drops_summary: Blood Zombie (0.5%), Drippler (0.5%), Wandering Eye Fish (6.67%), +1 more

Bubble.name: Bubble
Bubble.tooltip: Bubbles are animated background furniture blocks, which have special behavior regarding liquids, interacting as if the Bubble was a solid block. When Bubbles are placed together in groups, they connect to make a larger Bubble or more complex structures. Bubbles are purchased from the Party Girl for 2 Silver each during Hardmode. Grates function as the opposite of Bubbles, acting as solid blocks but allowing liquids to flow through.

Daybloom Planter Box.name: Daybloom Planter Box
Daybloom Planter Box.tooltip: Planter Boxes are flat-surface items of furniture purchased from the Dryad for 1 Silver each in which herb or flower seeds can be planted. If left empty, wild grass plants will randomly grow out of them, provided the box is placed on the surface or in Space. The plant in a Planter Box cannot be cut in the regular manner, e.g. via nearby swinging tools. Instead, it needs to be removed with a pickaxe or drill, or the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth. Planter Boxes are placed and act like platforms: They do not require support beneath them and they can be walked on, but pressing ▼ Down will let a player fall through them. Although the various Planter Boxes have different seed names and appearances, the differences are purely cosmetic: Any herb seeds can grow in any Planter Box, and planting seeds in their respective Planter Boxes will not provide any extra benefit. Depending on the evil biome of the world, the Dryad will sell a Deathweed Planter Box showing either Corrupt grass or Crimson grass.

Brain of Confusion.name: Brain of Confusion
Brain of Confusion.tooltip: The Brain of Confusion is a pre-Hardmode accessory that is always dropped from the Brain of Cthulhu's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode. It grants the following effects while equipped: Upon taking damage, the player has a 1/6 (16.67%) of dodging an attack, negating damage from that attack. Upon dodging, the player also receives the Cerebral Mindtrick debuff for four seconds. Despite being a debuff, it increases critical strike chance and summon damage by 10%. While the debuff is active, the player cannot dodge another attack. Upon taking damage, nearby enemies have a 3/5 (60%) chance of receiving the Confused debuff. The chance, duration, and area of effect of the debuff are based on the amount of damage taken. It is the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Worm Scarf.

Worm Scarf.name: Worm Scarf
Worm Scarf.tooltip: The Worm Scarf is a pre-Hardmode accessory that is always dropped from the Eater of Worlds' Treasure Bag in Expert Mode. While equipped, it grants +17% damage reduction. It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Brain of Confusion.

Balloon Pufferfish.name: Balloon Pufferfish
Balloon Pufferfish.tooltip: The Balloon Pufferfish is an accessory that has identical function to the Shiny Red Balloon. It increases the player's jump duration by 33% and jump speed by 30%, increasing the height that the player can jump from 6 tiles to ~10½ tiles, effectively a ~75% boost; however, it reduces jump height when underwater, from 8 tiles to 7 tiles. It can be obtained via fishing in any biome.

Lazure's Valkyrie Circlet.name: Lazure's Valkyrie Circlet
Lazure's Valkyrie Circlet.tooltip: Lazure's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is the vanity set made for Lazure, a former artist at Re-Logic. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. Lazure's equipment also includes these non-vanity items, which will drop in addition to his clothing set: Lazure's Barrier Platform Valkyrie Yoyo

Lazure's Valkyrie Cloak.name: Lazure's Valkyrie Cloak
Lazure's Valkyrie Cloak.tooltip: Lazure's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is the vanity set made for Lazure, a former artist at Re-Logic. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. Lazure's equipment also includes these non-vanity items, which will drop in addition to his clothing set: Lazure's Barrier Platform Valkyrie Yoyo

Lazure's Barrier Platform.name: Lazure's Barrier Platform
Lazure's Barrier Platform.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Golden Cross Grave Marker.name: Golden Cross Grave Marker
Golden Cross Grave Marker.tooltip: A Tombstone is a furniture item that drops when a player dies. It can then be retrieved and used much like a sign or as a form of decoration. By default, it contains the death message generated based on how the player died along with the real-life date of the death. Upon death, a Tombstone will bounce around until it lands on a suitable 2-tile wide surface, where it will place itself. If a Tombstone cannot find a place to land (due to lack of suitable space), it cannot be retrieved and will eventually despawn. Two Tombstones cannot land on each other. Variants are chosen randomly upon death. Golden Tombstones drop when the player had more than 10 Gold in their inventory. Having 4–8 Tombstones placed in close proximity will gradually darken and desaturate the environment. Five or more Tombstones placed in close proximity will generate a Graveyard mini-biome. Breaking a Tombstone has 12.5% / 25% / 50% chance to spawn a Ghost off-screen. In Hardcore, Tombstones cannot be easily obtained because death is permanent. Instead, NPCs in worlds with Hardcore characters will drop Tombstones when they are killed. Variants are still chosen randomly; all NPCs drop a normal Tombstone except the Merchant and Tax Collector who drop a golden variant. In For the Worthy (including Zenith) worlds, the Tombstone projectiles dropped by players (but not those dropped by NPCs in Hardcore) deal 210 / 280 / 420 damage to players and 70 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters. Because Tombstones create Graveyards, and mark a place where a player had died, they are highlighted by Dangersense Potions. Abigail's Flower can be uncommonly found as a plant growing on grass near a placed Tombstone, regardless of world progression. Its spawn chance is increased in a The Constant world.

Instead, NPCs in worlds with Hardcore characters will drop Tombstones when they are killed. Variants are still chosen randomly; all NPCs drop a normal Tombstone except the Merchant and Tax Collector who drop a golden variant. In For the Worthy (including Zenith) worlds, the Tombstone projectiles dropped by players (but not those dropped by NPCs in Hardcore) deal 210 / 280 / 420 damage to players and 70 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters. Because Tombstones create Graveyards, and mark a place where a player had died, they are highlighted by Dangersense Potions. Abigail's Flower can be uncommonly found as a plant growing on grass near a placed Tombstone, regardless of world progression. Its spawn chance is increased in a The Constant world.

Golden Grave Marker.name: Golden Grave Marker
Golden Grave Marker.tooltip: A Tombstone is a furniture item that drops when a player dies. It can then be retrieved and used much like a sign or as a form of decoration. By default, it contains the death message generated based on how the player died along with the real-life date of the death. Upon death, a Tombstone will bounce around until it lands on a suitable 2-tile wide surface, where it will place itself. If a Tombstone cannot find a place to land (due to lack of suitable space), it cannot be retrieved and will eventually despawn. Two Tombstones cannot land on each other. Variants are chosen randomly upon death. Golden Tombstones drop when the player had more than 10 Gold in their inventory. Having 4–8 Tombstones placed in close proximity will gradually darken and desaturate the environment. Five or more Tombstones placed in close proximity will generate a Graveyard mini-biome. Breaking a Tombstone has 12.5% / 25% / 50% chance to spawn a Ghost off-screen. In Hardcore, Tombstones cannot be easily obtained because death is permanent. Instead, NPCs in worlds with Hardcore characters will drop Tombstones when they are killed. Variants are still chosen randomly; all NPCs drop a normal Tombstone except the Merchant and Tax Collector who drop a golden variant. Crystal Block.name: Crystal Block
Crystal Block.tooltip: The Crystal Block is a Hardmode decorative building block crafted from Crystal Shards at an Adamantite or Titanium Forge. It has a luminous shade with colors ranging from magenta to blue. It can be made into Crystal Block Walls and other Crystal furniture.

Music Box (Martian Madness).name: Music Box (Martian Madness)
Music Box (Martian Madness).tooltip: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End), which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 Gold after defeating the Moon Lord. A recorded Music Box can be played back in one of two ways: Equipping it as an accessory. Placing it as furniture and activating it, either by the ⚷ Open / Activate button or with wires. Recorded Music Boxes can be reverted into blank ones through Shimmer transmutation. There are 101 different Music Boxes available.

Music Box (Pirate Invasion).name: Music Box (Pirate Invasion)
Music Box (Pirate Invasion).tooltip: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Crystal Block Wall.name: Crystal Block Wall
Crystal Block Wall.tooltip: The Crystal Block Wall is a type of Wall that can be crafted with Crystal Blocks. It has a purple-blue color, along with a dark tone.

Trap Door.name: Trap Door
Trap Door.tooltip: Trap Doors are furniture items. They are essentially full-block horizontal Doors. Trap Doors can be opened using ⚷ Open / Activate, causing them to expand into a 2x2 block. They fulfill a house's door requirement. Trap Doors open upward if the character opening it is below the Trap Door's level, and downward if above. The reference point for character altitude seems to be the character's center, not the feet: the character's feet can be about one half tile below the bottom of a closed Trap Door (standing on a stair), and the door will still open downward. Trap Doors can be blocked by furniture and will then always open on the free side, regardless of character position. If a Trap Door is blocked on both sides, it will not open. An open Trap Door is too narrow to be used at the end of a ramp or stairway so that a character can climb through it without jumping, as it needs to be surrounded by solid blocks, not platforms or other Trap Doors. Like normal doors, Trap Doors can be wired to be opened and closed remotely. Unlike normal doors, Trap Doors cannot be opened by Zombies during a Blood Moon event and can be useful for early players in defending their base.

Tall Gate.name: Tall Gate
Tall Gate.tooltip: The Tall Gate is a furniture item which is essentially a tall, sliding door that can be opened and closed by pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it. Tall Gate fulfills a house's door requirement. Tall Gates differ from doors in the following ways: The Tall Gate is 5 tiles in height, which is large enough to allow players on mounts to pass through without dismounting (unlike doors, which are only 3 tiles tall). Unlike doors, Tall Gates do not occupy additional space when opened; hence blocks or furniture placed on either side will not prevent them from opening. Tall Gates come in only one variety (unlike doors, which have a different version available for each furniture theme).

Sharkron Balloon.name: Sharkron Balloon
Sharkron Balloon.tooltip: The Sharkron Balloon is an accessory that combines the effects of the Tsunami in a Bottle and the Balloon Pufferfish. It boosts jump duration by 33% and jump speed by 30% increasing the player's first jump's height to ~10½ tiles (~75% increase), and provides a double jump that can reach a height of 13 tiles, for a total height of 23½ tiles.  The total jump height of the Sharkron Balloon is reduced when underwater, reducing the total underwater jump height from 17½ tiles (8 tiles + 9½ tiles from Tsunami jump) to 15 tiles (7 tiles + 8 tiles from Tsunami jump). It can be combined with a Lucky Horseshoe at a Tinkerer's Workshop to craft a Pink Horseshoe Balloon.

Tax Collector's Hat.name: Tax Collector's Hat
Tax Collector's Hat.tooltip: The Tax Collector's set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Tax Collector's Hat, the Tax Collector's Suit and the Tax Collector's Pants. It is purchased from the Clothier for 9 Gold (set) when the Tax Collector is present in the world. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Tax Collector's Suit.name: Tax Collector's Suit
Tax Collector's Suit.tooltip: The Tax Collector's set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Tax Collector's Hat, the Tax Collector's Suit and the Tax Collector's Pants. It is purchased from the Clothier for 9 Gold (set) when the Tax Collector is present in the world. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Tax Collector's Pants.name: Tax Collector's Pants
Tax Collector's Pants.tooltip: The Tax Collector's set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Tax Collector's Hat, the Tax Collector's Suit and the Tax Collector's Pants. It is purchased from the Clothier for 9 Gold (set) when the Tax Collector is present in the world. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Bone Glove.name: Bone Glove
Bone Glove.tooltip: The Bone Glove is a pre-Hardmode accessory that throws ricocheting crossbones every time a weapon is used, at a maximum of once per second. The crossbones projectiles ricochet off walls three times or pierce two enemies before being destroyed, deal 25 classless damage, and additionally have 25 armor penetration. The Bone Glove is always dropped from Skeletron's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.

Clothier's Jacket.name: Clothier's Jacket
Clothier's Jacket.tooltip: The Clothier's set is a vanity set consisting of the Red Hat, Clothier's Jacket(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Clothier's Pants(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. The Red Hat will always drop from the Clothier NPC. The other parts of the set are sold by the Clothier for 3 Gold each, during Halloween.

Clothier's Pants.name: Clothier's Pants
Clothier's Pants.tooltip: The Clothier's set is a vanity set consisting of the Red Hat, Clothier's Jacket(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Clothier's Pants(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. The Red Hat will always drop from the Clothier NPC. The other parts of the set are sold by the Clothier for 3 Gold each, during Halloween.

Dye Trader's Turban.name: Dye Trader's Turban
Dye Trader's Turban.tooltip: The Dye Trader's set is a vanity set consisting up of the Dye Trader's Turban(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and the Dye Trader Robe. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. The items are purchased from the Dye Trader NPC for 6 Gold (set) during Halloween.

Deadly Sphere Staff.name: Deadly Sphere Staff
Deadly Sphere Staff.tooltip: The Deadly Sphere Staff is a Hardmode, post-Plantera summon weapon that summons a Deadly Sphere minion. It flies and charges through enemies at a high velocity but cannot move through blocks. Once every three attacks, it briefly stops in place to cycle through one of three forms before continuing to attack. The Deadly Sphere Staff has a 1/30 (3.33%) / 59/900 (6.56%) chance of being dropped by Deadly Spheres. Its best modifier is Fabled.

Green Horseshoe Balloon.name: Green Horseshoe Balloon
Green Horseshoe Balloon.tooltip: The Green Horseshoe Balloon is an accessory that grants immunity to fall damage, increases jump height by 33%, jump speed by 30%, grants a double jump, and grants +0.05 luck. The height of the first jump is increased from 6 blocks to 10.5 blocks (~75% increase), while the double jump's height is increased from 10.5 blocks to 18.5 blocks, reaching a total of 29 blocks with both jumps. The double jump also makes a fart sound. Jump height is oddly reduced when underwater, to 18 blocks (7 blocks + ~11 blocks from Fart jump).

Amber Horseshoe Balloon.name: Amber Horseshoe Balloon
Amber Horseshoe Balloon.tooltip: The Amber Horseshoe Balloon is an accessory that increases jump height by 75% (6 blocks → 10.5 blocks), reduces it by 15% when underwater (8 blocks → 7 blocks), makes the player immune to fall damage, and releases bees when attacked, which seek out and damage enemies. It also grants +0.05 luck(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). It can be crafted at a Tinkerer's Workshop with a Lucky Horseshoe and a Honey Balloon. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, it also grants the Honey buff after being damaged.

Pink Horseshoe Balloon.name: Pink Horseshoe Balloon
Pink Horseshoe Balloon.tooltip: The Pink Horseshoe Balloon is an accessory that grants immunity to fall damage, increases jump height by 33% and jump speed by 30%, grants a double jump, and grants +0.05 luck. The height of the first jump is increased from 6 blocks to 10.5 blocks (~75% increase), while the double jump's height is increased from 7 blocks to 13 blocks, reaching a total of 23.5 blocks with both jumps. Jump height is oddly reduced when underwater, reducing total underwater jump height from 17.5 blocks (8 blocks + 9½ blocks from Tsunami jump) to 15 blocks (7 blocks + 8 blocks from Tsunami jump).

Lava Lamp.name: Lava Lamp
Lava Lamp.tooltip: The Lava Lamp is a furniture item purchased from the Party Girl for 2 Gold, that emits a small amount of light and has an animated texture. It is not a mechanism but can be placed on tables. It is not considered a suitable light source for an NPC house. It is used purely as a decorative light source.

Enchanted Nightcrawler Cage.name: Enchanted Nightcrawler Cage
Enchanted Nightcrawler Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters. A critter caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item. Gold cages are regular cages containing gold critters. Aside from their higher sell value and rarity, they are the same as regular cages. Placed cages are partially transparent. They can be stacked on top of each other, but no other types of furniture can be placed on a cage. Players can stand on top of cages like platforms, even though they are otherwise background furniture.

Buggy Cage.name: Buggy Cage
Buggy Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters. A critter caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage.
