Slap Hand.name: Slap Hand
Slap Hand.tooltip: The Slap Hand is a Hardmode broadsword that can be purchased from the Skeleton Merchant for 25 Gold during a Blood Moon. It is notable for having extremely high base knockback – a rating of 20, one of the highest values among all player-caused sources of knockback. The Slap Hand also has a 19% base critical strike chance, as opposed to the usual 4%. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Twilight Hair Dye.name: Twilight Hair Dye
Twilight Hair Dye.tooltip: Hair Dyes are consumable items sold by the Stylist NPC. When used, they replace a player's hair color with a dynamic effect.

Blessed Apple.name: Blessed Apple
Blessed Apple.tooltip: The Blessed Apple is a Hardmode mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Unicorn Mount, capable of an extra jump as well as the ability to sprint and charge through enemies, damaging them in the process. The Blessed Apple has a 1/40 (2.5%) / 1/30 (3.33%) chance of being dropped by Unicorns. Once a high speed is reached, the Unicorn emits a sparkle effect, and from that point on, it will be able to damage enemies on contact. Dashing through an enemy grants 0.1 seconds of invincibility frames.

Spectre Bar.name: Spectre Bar
Spectre Bar.tooltip: The Spectre Bar is a Hardmode, post-Plantera bar.

Code 1.name: Code 1
Code 1.tooltip: The Code 1 is a pre-Hardmode yoyo that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 5 Gold once the Eye of Cthulhu has been defeated. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Buccaneer Bandana.name: Buccaneer Bandana
Buccaneer Bandana.tooltip: The Buccaneer set  is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Buccaneer Bandana, Buccaneer Tunic, and Buccaneer Pantaloons. Each piece has a 1/500 (0.2%) chance of being dropped by Pirate Deckhands, Pirate Corsairs,  Pirate Deadeyes, and Pirate Crossbowers during the Pirate Invasion event.  These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Buccaneer Tunic.name: Buccaneer Tunic
Buccaneer Tunic.tooltip: The Buccaneer set  is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Buccaneer Bandana, Buccaneer Tunic, and Buccaneer Pantaloons. Obsidian Outlaw Hat.name: Obsidian Outlaw Hat
Obsidian Outlaw Hat.tooltip: Obsidian armor is a pre-Hardmode summoner armor set consisting of the Obsidian Outlaw Hat, Obsidian Longcoat, and Obsidian Pants. Crafting a full set requires a total of 60 Obsidian, 30 Silk, and 20 Shadow Scales or Tissue Samples. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +15 defense +31% summon damage +1 minion slot +15% whip speed Unlike any other whip speed bonus, this stacks multiplicatively with melee speed bonuses. +30% whip range

Obsidian Longcoat.name: Obsidian Longcoat
Obsidian Longcoat.tooltip: Obsidian armor is a pre-Hardmode summoner armor set consisting of the Obsidian Outlaw Hat, Obsidian Longcoat, and Obsidian Pants. Crafting a full set requires a total of 60 Obsidian, 30 Silk, and 20 Shadow Scales or Tissue Samples. Medusa Head.name: Medusa Head
Medusa Head.tooltip: The Medusa Head is a Hardmode magic weapon that continuously fires close-range yellow beams up to four times per second, hitting up to three enemies per attack within a 20-tile radius of the player. 15 mana is consumed per each attack, regardless of the number of enemies struck. No mana is consumed if the Medusa Head is used while no enemies are within range. The Medusa Head has a 1/25 (4%) chance of being dropped by Medusa. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Item Frame.name: Item Frame
Item Frame.tooltip: The Item Frame is a furniture item that can be placed on a 2×2 area of background wall, placed on or hung from blocks, or placed on top of platforms. Once an Item Frame is placed, pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on it while holding any item places and displays that item in the Item Frame. Hitting the Item Frame with a pickaxe or drill, or pressing ⚷ Open / Activate again will retrieve the item.

Sandstone Block.name: Sandstone Block
Sandstone Block.tooltip: Sandstone Blocks are blocks found naturally placed in the Underground Desert biome. Like Sand and Hardened Sand, they are corruptable blocks in Hardmode, and have Corruption, Crimson, and Hallowed counterparts: Ebonsandstone, Crimsandstone, and Pearlsandstone respectively.

Hardened Sand Block.name: Hardened Sand Block
Hardened Sand Block.tooltip: The Hardened Sand Block is a type of block, along with Sandstone Blocks, that make up the Underground Desert biome. It looks similar to Sand Blocks, with an altered texture and slightly different color. Unlike sand, it is not affected by gravity. Like all sand-based blocks, it has Corruption, Crimson, and Hallowed counterparts: Hardened Ebonsand, Hardened Crimsand, and Hardened Pearlsand respectively.

Sandstone Wall.name: Sandstone Wall
Sandstone Wall.tooltip: The Sandstone Wall, Ebonsandstone Wall, Crimsandstone Wall, and Pearlsandstone Wall are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Underground Desert, considered unsafe. Underground Deserts generate by default the normal Sandstone Sand Wall which may be converted into the respective variant if exposed to the Corruption, Crimson, or Hallow. Converted Sandstone Walls may further spread conversion to other walls; see Biome spread for more information. Unsafe Sandstone Walls do not drop as items when destroyed, and can only be obtained via crafting. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player. The Treacherous Sandstone Wall is an item that places an unsafe Sandstone Wall. It is visually identical and is obtained by throwing a Sandstone Wall into Shimmer.

Hardened Ebonsand Block.name: Hardened Ebonsand Block
Hardened Ebonsand Block.tooltip: The Hardened Sand Block is a type of block, along with Sandstone Blocks, that make up the Underground Desert biome. It looks similar to Sand Blocks, with an altered texture and slightly different color. Unlike sand, it is not affected by gravity. Like all sand-based blocks, it has Corruption, Crimson, and Hallowed counterparts: Hardened Ebonsand, Hardened Crimsand, and Hardened Pearlsand respectively.

Hardened Crimsand Block.name: Hardened Crimsand Block
Hardened Crimsand Block.tooltip: The Hardened Sand Block is a type of block, along with Sandstone Blocks, that make up the Underground Desert biome. It looks similar to Sand Blocks, with an altered texture and slightly different color. Unlike sand, it is not affected by gravity. Like all sand-based blocks, it has Corruption, Crimson, and Hallowed counterparts: Hardened Ebonsand, Hardened Crimsand, and Hardened Pearlsand respectively.

Ebonsandstone Block.name: Ebonsandstone Block
Ebonsandstone Block.tooltip: Sandstone Blocks are blocks found naturally placed in the Underground Desert biome. Like Sand and Hardened Sand, they are corruptable blocks in Hardmode, and have Corruption, Crimson, and Hallowed counterparts: Ebonsandstone, Crimsandstone, and Pearlsandstone respectively.

Crimsandstone Block.name: Crimsandstone Block
Crimsandstone Block.tooltip: Sandstone Blocks are blocks found naturally placed in the Underground Desert biome. Like Sand and Hardened Sand, they are corruptable blocks in Hardmode, and have Corruption, Crimson, and Hallowed counterparts: Ebonsandstone, Crimsandstone, and Pearlsandstone respectively.

Wooden Yoyo.name: Wooden Yoyo
Wooden Yoyo.tooltip: The Wooden Yoyo is a pre-Hardmode yoyo. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Malaise.name: Malaise
Malaise.tooltip: The Malaise is a pre-Hardmode yoyo. It is the Corruption counterpart to The Crimson's Artery. The Malaise has slightly higher knockback and spin duration than the Artery, but slightly lower damage and reach. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Artery.name: Artery
Artery.tooltip: The Artery is a pre-Hardmode yoyo. It is the Crimson counterpart to The Corruption's Malaise. The Artery has slightly higher damage and reach than the Malaise, but slightly lower knockback and spin duration. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Amazon.name: Amazon
Amazon.tooltip: The Amazon is a pre-Hardmode yoyo. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Cascade.name: Cascade
Cascade.tooltip: The Cascade is a pre-Hardmode-exclusive, post-Skeletron yoyo that has a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of being dropped by any enemy in or near The Underworld. Once Hardmode begins, it will no longer drop, being replaced by the Hel-Fire. On every 2nd yoyo hit, the Cascade shoots a fiery explosion towards the nearest enemy within a 13-tile radius. The fiery explosion deals 200% of the Cascade's damage (54 base damage) and its full knockback, but does not pierce. The Cascade and its explosion both have a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to inflict the On Fire! debuff for 1–4 seconds. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Chik.name: Chik
Chik.tooltip: The Chik is a Hardmode yoyo. On every 3rd yoyo hit, the Chik deals 200% damage ((68 base damage) and also shoots a spread of 5 crystal shards in random directions that can pass through blocks and travel for a short distance before disappearing. The crystal shards do not pierce, and each deal 100% of the Chik's damage ((34 base damage) and knockback (base knockback of 3.3 (Weak)). Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Code 2.name: Code 2
Code 2.tooltip: The Code 2 is a Hardmode, post one-mechanical boss yoyo that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 25 Gold. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Rally.name: Rally
Rally.tooltip: The Rally is a pre-Hardmode yoyo that has a 6.5% chance of being dropped by Crawdads, Giant Shellies, and Salamanders in the Cavern layer.  Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Yelets.name: Yelets
Yelets.tooltip: The Yelets is a Hardmode, post one-mechanical boss yoyo that has a 1/200 (0.5%) chance to drop from any enemy killed in the Jungle and Underground Jungle, including in the Jungle Temple.

Red's Throw.name: Red's Throw
Red's Throw.tooltip: Red's Throw is a Hardmode, Expert Mode-exclusive yoyo that can be obtained from any Hardmode boss's Treasure Bag (except Queen Slime's) as part of Red's set.  Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Valkyrie Yoyo.name: Valkyrie Yoyo
Valkyrie Yoyo.tooltip: The Valkyrie Yoyo is a Hardmode, Expert Mode-exclusive yoyo that can be obtained from any Hardmode boss's Treasure Bag (except Queen Slime's) as part of Lazure's set. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Amarok.name: Amarok
Amarok.tooltip: The Amarok is a Hardmode yoyo that has a 1/300 (0.33%) chance of being dropped from any enemy in the Snow biome or Ice biome, and can also drop in a Corrupted, Crimsoned, or Hallowed version of these biomes. It has a 67/100 (67%) chance to inflict the Frostbite debuff for 2–5 seconds upon hit.  Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Hel-Fire.name: Hel-Fire
Hel-Fire.tooltip: The Hel-Fire is a Hardmode yoyo that has a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of being dropped by any enemy in or near The Underworld. It inflicts the Hellfire debuff for 3–8 seconds upon hit. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Kraken.name: Kraken
Kraken.tooltip: The Kraken is a Hardmode yoyo that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance to drop from Duke Fishron. It has a base 14% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. While in use, it constantly emits a whirlpool loop around the yoyo, which increases its hit detection range significantly. On every 4th yoyo hit, it fires a spread of three wave projectiles towards its target, which can pass through blocks and disappear after traveling a short distance. The waves pierce infinitely and each deal 50% of the Kraken's damage ((60 base damage) and 100% of its knockback. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

The Eye of Cthulhu.name: The Eye of Cthulhu
The Eye of Cthulhu.tooltip: The Eye of Cthulhu is a Hardmode, post-Plantera yoyo that has a 1/3 (33.33%) / 5/9 (55.56%) chance of being dropped by Mothrons during a Solar Eclipse.

Red String.name: Red String
Red String.tooltip: A string is an offensive accessory that boosts all yoyos. While equipped, the spin duration of all yoyos is increased by 50% and their maximum range is extended by 25%, plus an additional 1.9 tiles, and the maximum range of counterweights is increased from 7.8 tiles to 10.4 tiles. White String is first crafted by the player with 30 Cobwebs at a Loom, and can be combined with certain dyes to form colored variants. These colored strings will be displayed as the color of the string attached to yoyos and counterweights when they are thrown, in addition to providing the duration and range bonuses. They also change the color of the fishing line. They will apply their color changes even when equipped in a social slot.

Black Counterweight.name: Black Counterweight
Black Counterweight.tooltip: Counterweights are accessories sold by the Traveling Merchant and the Skeleton Merchant. They fire a second yoyo-type projectile after hitting an enemy with a yoyo, which travels towards it, then orbits around the player. Counterweights deal the yoyo's full damage and stay active until the yoyo is retracted towards the player. There are six different color variants with identical functionalities.

Format:C.name: Format:C
Format:C.tooltip: The Format:C is a Hardmode yoyo. It has a base 24% critical strike chance, as opposed to the usual 4%, and deals 250% damage on critical hits, as opposed to the usual 200%. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Gradient.name: Gradient
Gradient.tooltip: The Gradient is a Hardmode yoyo that can be purchased from the Skeleton Merchant for 20 Gold. It leaves behind a visual gradient trail when used. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Valor.name: Valor
Valor.tooltip: The Valor is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron yoyo that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from the Locked Gold Chests found in the Dungeon, as well as a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being obtained from Golden Lock Boxes. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Treasure Bag (King Slime).name: Treasure Bag (King Slime)
Treasure Bag (King Slime).tooltip: Treasure Bags are consumable grab bag-like items obtained in Expert Mode and Master Mode as a reward for defeating bosses. The contents and appearance of Treasure Bags depend on the boss it comes from, and are opened by using either ⚷ Open / Activate while inside the inventory, or ⚒ Use / Attack when selected in the hotbar. They emit light and have a special effect around them when dropped, making them easier to spot. In multiplayer, each player that deals damage to the boss receives one Treasure Bag upon defeating it. Treasure Bags are client-side and will despawn upon exiting the world. See Notes for details. Each Treasure Bag contains the boss's usual drops from Classic Mode, along with one Expert Mode-exclusive item (highlighted items below) – with the exception of the Lunatic Cultist, Dark Mage, Ogre, and Betsy, who do not provide an Expert Mode-exclusive item. Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses additionally have a 1/16 (6.25%) chance to contain one random set of developer items (with the exception of Queen Slime). Expert Mode-exclusive items all have the  rarity, with the exception of developer items, which have the  rarity.

Expert Mode-exclusive items all have the  rarity, with the exception of developer items, which have the  rarity.

Treasure Bag (Golem).name: Treasure Bag (Golem)
Treasure Bag (Golem).tooltip: Treasure Bags are consumable grab bag-like items obtained in Expert Mode and Master Mode as a reward for defeating bosses. The contents and appearance of Treasure Bags depend on the boss it comes from, and are opened by using either ⚷ Open / Activate while inside the inventory, or ⚒ Use / Attack when selected in the hotbar. They emit light and have a special effect around them when dropped, making them easier to spot. In multiplayer, each player that deals damage to the boss receives one Treasure Bag upon defeating it. Treasure Bags are client-side and will despawn upon exiting the world. See Notes for details. Hive Pack.name: Hive Pack
Hive Pack.tooltip: The Hive Pack is a pre-Hardmode accessory that is always dropped from the Queen Bee's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode. While equipped, it grants a 1/2 (50%) chance of replacing friendly Bee projectiles with stronger Giant Bees. Bees spawned by the following weapons may be upgraded: Bees spawned by the Honey Comb accessory and its upgrades may be upgraded as well:

Yoyo Glove.name: Yoyo Glove
Yoyo Glove.tooltip: The Yoyo Glove is a Hardmode accessory that is purchased from the Skeleton Merchant for 50 Gold. While equipped, hitting an enemy with a yoyo will create a duplicate of that yoyo that rapidly orbits around the main one. If a counterweight is also equipped, the Yoyo Glove will additionally cause a duplicate counterweight to spawn upon hit, for a total of four projectiles. Furthermore, while the secondary yoyo is deployed, yoyos will run out of spin duration 2–4× as quickly (randomized). Having a secondary counterweight does not amplify this effect.

Demon Heart.name: Demon Heart
Demon Heart.tooltip: The Demon Heart is a Hardmode permanent booster item that permanently grants the player an extra accessory slot, for use only within Expert and Master Mode worlds. This effect does not stack and may only be used once per player. The Demon Heart is always dropped from the Wall of Flesh's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode. If a player opens the Wall of Flesh's Treasure Bag after they have already consumed a Demon Heart, another one will not be obtained. When a player who consumed a Demon Heart is in a Classic Mode world (a non-Expert or Master world), the extra accessory slot is disabled, removing all functional or display effects from any items equipped in the slot, and darkening the slot itself. Players in Classic worlds are also prevented from equipping items in the sixth or seventh slot, though an equipped item in the slot may still be taken out, and placed back into the inventory.

Spore Sac.name: Spore Sac
Spore Sac.tooltip: The Spore Sac is a Hardmode accessory that is always dropped from Plantera's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode. While equipped, it continuously spawns multiple floating Spore Traps around the player, which will slowly home in on enemies. The Spore Traps can pass through blocks and deal 70 classless damage and a knockback of 1.5 (Extremely weak) upon hitting enemies, and inflict the Poisoned debuff for 5–10 seconds. After hitting a target, each Spore Trap turns into a Spore Gas cloud, which lingers for a short duration and repeatdely deals 70 classless damage, but does not inflict knockback or the Poisoned debuff. Spore Traps can only spawn near blocks or on background walls, up to 25 tiles away from the player. Without background walls to spawn on, Spore Traps can spawn up to about 3 tiles away from blocks.

Shiny Stone.name: Shiny Stone
Shiny Stone.tooltip: The Shiny Stone is a Hardmode, post-Golem accessory that is always dropped from Golem's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode. While the player is not moving, not using any items, and not being damaged, the Shiny Stone greatly boosts the player's base health regeneration (i.e., the natural health regeneration without any buffs or debuffs) by accelerating its buildup and increasing the maximum rate, as well as providing +10% base health regeneration. Additionally, the Shiny Stone reduces the damage taken from debuffs by half and gives +2HP/s flat health regeneration, increased to +2.5HP/s if the player has a positive health regeneration stat.

Hardened Pearlsand Block.name: Hardened Pearlsand Block
Hardened Pearlsand Block.tooltip: The Hardened Sand Block is a type of block, along with Sandstone Blocks, that make up the Underground Desert biome. It looks similar to Sand Blocks, with an altered texture and slightly different color. Unlike sand, it is not affected by gravity. Like all sand-based blocks, it has Corruption, Crimson, and Hallowed counterparts: Hardened Ebonsand, Hardened Crimsand, and Hardened Pearlsand respectively.

Pearlsandstone Block.name: Pearlsandstone Block
Pearlsandstone Block.tooltip: Sandstone Blocks are blocks found naturally placed in the Underground Desert biome. Like Sand and Hardened Sand, they are corruptable blocks in Hardmode, and have Corruption, Crimson, and Hallowed counterparts: Ebonsandstone, Crimsandstone, and Pearlsandstone respectively.

Hardened Sand Wall.name: Hardened Sand Wall
Hardened Sand Wall.tooltip: The Hardened Sand Wall, Hardened Ebonsand Wall, Hardened Crimsand Wall, and Hardened Pearlsand Wall are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Underground Desert, considered unsafe. Underground Deserts generate by default the normal Hardened Sand Wall which may be converted into the respective variant if exposed to the Corruption, Crimson, or Hallow. Converted Hardened Sand Walls may further spread conversion; see Biome spread for more information. Unsafe Hardened Sand Walls do not drop as items when destroyed, and can only be obtained via crafting. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player. The Treacherous Hardened Sand Wall is an item that places an unsafe Hardened Sand Wall. It is visually identical and is obtained by throwing a Hardened Sand Wall into Shimmer.

Hardened Ebonsand Wall.name: Hardened Ebonsand Wall
Hardened Ebonsand Wall.tooltip: The Hardened Sand Wall, Hardened Ebonsand Wall, Hardened Crimsand Wall, and Hardened Pearlsand Wall are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Underground Desert, considered unsafe. Desert Fossil.name: Desert Fossil
Desert Fossil.tooltip: Desert Fossil is a type of block found in the Underground Desert biome in medium to large veins. Desert Fossils can be used with an Extractinator or Chlorophyte Extractinator to produce Sturdy Fossils, along with regular Extractinator drops.

Desert Fossil Wall.name: Desert Fossil Wall
Desert Fossil Wall.tooltip: The Desert Fossil Wall is a type of background wall that can be crafted from Desert Fossils.

Exotic Scimitar.name: Exotic Scimitar
Exotic Scimitar.tooltip: The Exotic Scimitar is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped from the Dye Trader. Striking enemies with the weapon increases its damage by 12% per hit, up to a maximum of 50%. This damage bonus decays at a rate of 0.5% per tick or 30% per second. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Paintball Gun.name: Paintball Gun
Paintball Gun.tooltip: The Paintball Gun is a pre-Hardmode ranged weapon that fires a three-shot burst of slow-moving, arcing multicolored Paintball projectiles which consume no mana or ammunition, dissipating upon contact with an enemy or surface. The Paintball Gun has a 11% critical strike chance, as opposed to the usual 4%. It has a 1/10 (10%) chance of being dropped by the Painter. The Paintball projectiles cause certain slimes (see Notes for the full list) to change color on hit, according to the color of the Paintball. This is a purely visual change – it does not change the slime's type, AI, or stats. It lasts until the slime is hit by another Paintball, comes into contact with a painted block, or dies. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Classy Cane.name: Classy Cane
Classy Cane.tooltip: The Classy Cane is a Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance to be dropped by the Tax Collector. Like the Flymeal, it has the special ability to damage town NPCs, but will always only deal 1 damage to them. In addition, hitting an enemy or NPC with the Classy Cane drops 1–49 Copper Coins. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Stylish Scissors.name: Stylish Scissors
Stylish Scissors.tooltip: The Stylish Scissors are a pre-Hardmode broadsword that have a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by the Stylist. Letting go of ⚒ Use / Attack while swinging the weapon will throw the scissors in the direction of the cursor. The thrown scissors travel forward for 0.25 seconds before sharply dropping down, and can pierce through one enemy before dissipating on the second hit. The weapon and its projectiles both inflict the Bleeding debuff for 4–6 seconds on hit. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Mechanical Cart.name: Mechanical Cart
Mechanical Cart.tooltip: Minecarts are mounts that allow players to ride on Minecart Tracks. When the player is near a Minecart Track, pressing the Quick Mount hotkey or pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on a point on the track causes a Minecart to spawn, which the player is automatically placed in. Once inside, the ▶ Right and ◀ Left direction keys either accelerate, decelerate, or reverse the cart's movement. The cart will maintain its current speed and direction if no keys are pressed and no obstacles are reached. The cart can also "jump" with the ↷ Jump key. Weapons and tools, as well as most other items except hooks, can be used while riding a Minecart. The Minecart will deal damage to enemies it collides with and knock them back, with higher potency at higher speeds (see below for details). To exit the Minecart (which causes the Minecart to despawn), the player can use a hook, press the Quick Mount hotkey, or cancel the buff  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Minecart will also despawn if the player jumps off the tracks, lands on blocks, and attempts to move sideways. By default, a Wooden Minecart is spawned for the player. This can be overridden by equipping other Minecart items in the Minecart equipment slot of the player's inventory. The corresponding dye slot allows dyeing the Minecart. Using a Minecart Upgrade Kit will significantly boost the speed of all Minecarts, equip them with a laser that fires at nearby enemies, and increase the player's defense while moving. The boost effect is permanently available after using the item, though it can be toggled on and off through a probe icon next to the Minecart slot.

Mechanical Wheel Piece.name: Mechanical Wheel Piece
Mechanical Wheel Piece.tooltip: The Mechanical Wheel Piece is one of three parts needed to craft the Minecart Upgrade Kit. It is always dropped from The Twins' Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.

Mechanical Wagon Piece.name: Mechanical Wagon Piece
Mechanical Wagon Piece.tooltip: The Mechanical Wagon Piece is one of three parts needed to craft the Minecart Upgrade Kit. It is always dropped from The Destroyer's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.

Mechanical Battery Piece.name: Mechanical Battery Piece
Mechanical Battery Piece.tooltip: The Mechanical Battery Piece is one of three parts needed to craft the Minecart Upgrade Kit. It is always dropped from Skeletron Prime's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.

Lunatic Cultist Trophy.name: Lunatic Cultist Trophy
Lunatic Cultist Trophy.tooltip: Trophies are decorative furniture items which usually have a 1/10 (10%) chance to be dropped from most bosses. While they can be considered the "boss version of banners", they are purely cosmetic and do not provide any bonuses. Some trophies can only be rewarded by the Angler for completing fishing quests. In total, there are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 33 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 24 trophies.

Martian Saucer Trophy.tooltip: Trophies are decorative furniture items which usually have a 1/10 (10%) chance to be dropped from most bosses. In total, there are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 33 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 24 trophies.

In total, there are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 33 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 24 trophies.

Living Mahogany Wand.name: Living Mahogany Wand
Living Mahogany Wand.tooltip: Block-placing wands are special tools that allow the player to place blocks they would normally not be able to place. They do not consume any mana. Each wand consumes a specific material from the player's inventory (details listed below). There are 6 different block-placing wands.
Living Mahogany Wand.drops_summary: Angry Bones (0.4%), Cursed Skull (0.4%), Dark Caster (0.4%)

Rich Mahogany Leaf Wand.name: Rich Mahogany Leaf Wand
Rich Mahogany Leaf Wand.tooltip: Block-placing wands are special tools that allow the player to place blocks they would normally not be able to place. They do not consume any mana. Each wand consumes a specific material from the player's inventory (details listed below). There are 6 different block-placing wands.
Rich Mahogany Leaf Wand.drops_summary: Angry Bones (0.4%), Cursed Skull (0.4%), Dark Caster (0.4%)

Fallen Tuxedo Shirt.name: Fallen Tuxedo Shirt
Fallen Tuxedo Shirt.tooltip: The Fallen Tuxedo set is a set of vanity items consisting of the Fallen Tuxedo Shirt and the Fallen Tuxedo Pants. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. They are purchased from the Clothier for 50 Gold (set), during a Blood Moon.

Fallen Tuxedo Pants.name: Fallen Tuxedo Pants
Fallen Tuxedo Pants.tooltip: The Fallen Tuxedo set is a set of vanity items consisting of the Fallen Tuxedo Shirt and the Fallen Tuxedo Pants. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. They are purchased from the Clothier for 50 Gold (set), during a Blood Moon.

Fireplace.name: Fireplace
Fireplace.tooltip: The Fireplace is a decorative furniture item with a style similar to that of the Chimney. A Fireplace operates similarly to a Campfire, having the same dimensions, emitting light, and granting nearby players the Cozy Fire regeneration buff. The buff is applied to all players who are within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the Fireplace. A Fireplace differs from a Campfire in the following ways: A Fireplace has a flat surface on which other items can be placed, and will function as a valid surface for a Placed Bottle crafting station. A Fireplace functions as a valid light source for NPC housing, while the Campfire does not. A Fireplace cannot be toggled manually via the ⚷ Open / Activate button, while the Campfire can be. However, both can be toggled via Wire. A Fireplace cannot be used to produce a Cooked Marshmallow, while a Campfire can. A Fireplace will function within water, while most Campfires (those other than the Coral Campfire, Cursed Campfire, and Ichor Campfire) will not. A Fireplace is not a crafting station.

Chimney.name: Chimney
Chimney.tooltip: The Chimney is a decorative structure with a style similar to a Fireplace. It serves no in-game purpose, aside from cosmetics. It has 3 states that can be toggled via wire. In the first state, it is turned off; in the second, it adds a small smoke animation; and in the third, it adds smoke particles which behave like bubbles from the Bubble Machine.

Yoyo Bag.name: Yoyo Bag
Yoyo Bag.tooltip: The Yoyo Bag is a Hardmode accessory which combines the functionalities of the Yoyo Glove, a counterweight, and string. It grants the following effects while equipped: +50% yoyo spin duration +25% yoyo range, with an additional +2 tiles Creates a duplicate yoyo upon the first enemy hit with a yoyo Creates a counterweight upon the second enemy hit with a yoyo, and a duplicate counterweight upon the third enemy hit Like the Yoyo Glove, while the secondary yoyo is deployed, yoyos will run out of spin duration 2–4× as quickly (randomized). Having a secondary counterweight does not amplify this effect.

Shrimpy Truffle.name: Shrimpy Truffle
Shrimpy Truffle.tooltip: The Shrimpy Truffle is a Hardmode mount-summoning item that spawns Cute Fishron, a miniature rideable Duke Fishron-style mount that can fly and hover indefinitely. The Shrimpy Truffle is always dropped from Duke Fishron's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.  Cute Fishron has a base flight speed of 40 mph. Moving through liquids causes Cute Fishron to gain a drastic movement speed bonus of about +105% (to 82 mph, the fastest of any mount), as well as providing the rider with a +15% damage bonus, indicated by Cute Fishron's eyes glowing. These boosts continue for 6 seconds after it leaves liquid, though during this time, its speed boost drops to +100% (to 80 mph). Liquid boosts also take effect when Cute Fishron gets "wet" by flying in the rain, flying through Bubbles filled with liquids, being submerged in liquid from a filled Bucket, or being hit by a Water Gun. The +100% movement speed boost (80 mph) and +15% damage boost also take effect when the rider's health falls below half. Upon contact with any blocks, Cute Fishron's movement speed is drastically lowered to a very slow crawl (5 mph, or 10 mph if boosted). This speed penalty is removed as soon as it loses contact with blocks.

Arkhalis.name: Arkhalis
Arkhalis.tooltip: The Arkhalis is a Hardmode melee weapon that is part of Arkhalis' set and is only obtainable through Hardmode Treasure Bags in Expert Mode (except Queen Slime's). It appears to be a sword, but does not present an actual blade when used. Instead of an overhead broadsword swing or a shortsword stab, the Arkhalis autoswings and appears as a series of blurred slashes aimed in the direction of the cursor. Anything within this area takes constant damage at a rate far exceeding the weapon's stated use time. This damaging area has a rather wide spread, even attacking behind the player for a very short distance. In addition, the Arkhalis has 20 armor penetration. The Terragrim is the Arkhalis's weaker, pre-Hardmode variant that is obtainable from Enchanted Sword Shrines. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount. The Arkhalis's unique means of attack is unaffected by any size and speed modifiers.

Confetti Cannon.name: Confetti Cannon
Confetti Cannon.tooltip: The Confetti Cannon is a Hardmode novelty furniture/mechanism. It is purchased from the Party Girl for 25 Gold, when the Pirate is present. Once placed, it can be fired by pressing ⚒ Use / Attack key on it with any Torch (which is not consumed). The Confetti Cannon fires a burst of multicolored gravity-affected Confetti that is purely visual, dealing no damage or knockback. The Confetti Cannon has a cooldown of 0.33 seconds before it can be fired again by using Torches, which is shared between all Confetti Cannons in the world. The angle of a placed Confetti Cannon can be adjusted by pressing ⚷ Open / Activate key on either side of the Confetti Cannon to rotate it in that direction,  or tapping the side of the Confetti Cannon. It has 9 possible orientations and cannot fire downward. Each step tilts the Confetti Cannon by 1/16 of a circle (22.5°). The Confetti Cannon can also be triggered by Wire. Depending on where the wire is connected, it will either shoot Confetti (with a cooldown of 0.5 seconds) or rotate toward the side the Wire is on.

Music Box (The Towers).name: Music Box (The Towers)
Music Box (The Towers).tooltip: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End), which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 Gold after defeating the Moon Lord. A recorded Music Box can be played back in one of two ways: Equipping it as an accessory. Placing it as furniture and activating it, either by the ⚷ Open / Activate button or with wires. Recorded Music Boxes can be reverted into blank ones through Shimmer transmutation. There are 101 different Music Boxes available.

Music Box (Goblin Invasion).name: Music Box (Goblin Invasion)
Music Box (Goblin Invasion).tooltip: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End), which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 Gold after defeating the Moon Lord. A recorded Music Box can be played back in one of two ways: Equipping it as an accessory. Placing it as furniture and activating it, either by the ⚷ Open / Activate button or with wires. Recorded Music Boxes can be reverted into blank ones through Shimmer transmutation. There are 101 different Music Boxes available.

Lunatic Cultist Mask.name: Lunatic Cultist Mask
Lunatic Cultist Mask.tooltip: Masks are vanity items dropped by all non-event bosses, as well as those from the Old One's Army(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). They are worn in the social head slot. Each boss has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance to drop its own mask in all difficulties, with the following exceptions: The Skeletron Mask has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to drop from Skeletron's Treasure Bag. The Dark Mage Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 1) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Dark Mage. The Ogre Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 2) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Ogre.

Moon Lord Mask.name: Moon Lord Mask
Moon Lord Mask.tooltip: Masks are vanity items dropped by all non-event bosses, as well as those from the Old One's Army(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). They are worn in the social head slot. Each boss has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance to drop its own mask in all difficulties, with the following exceptions: The Skeletron Mask has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to drop from Skeletron's Treasure Bag. The Dark Mage Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 1) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Dark Mage. The Ogre Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 2) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Ogre.

Fossil Helmet.name: Fossil Helmet
Fossil Helmet.tooltip: Fossil armor is a pre-Hardmode ranged armor set consisting of the Fossil Helmet, Fossil Plate, and Fossil Greaves. Crafting the full set requires a total of 60 Sturdy Fossils. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +13 defense +5% ranged damage +8% ranged critical strike chance +20% ammo conservation

Fossil Plate.name: Fossil Plate
Fossil Plate.tooltip: Fossil armor is a pre-Hardmode ranged armor set consisting of the Fossil Helmet, Fossil Plate, and Fossil Greaves. Crafting the full set requires a total of 60 Sturdy Fossils. Amber Staff.name: Amber Staff
Amber Staff.tooltip: The Amber Staff is a pre-Hardmode wand and type of gem staff that fires an orange bolt which deals 80% of the weapon's damage (16 base damage) and 100% of its knockback, and can either pierce through enemies or bounce off blocks up to 2 times, dissipating upon the 3rd hit. While wearing a Gem robe, the fired bolt will be enchanted by ability of the corresponding gem type, granting it additional effects (see Notes for details). Its best modifier is Mythical.

Bone Javelin.name: Bone Javelin
Bone Javelin.tooltip: The Bone Javelin is a consumable ranged weapon crafted from Sturdy Fossils. Upon hitting an enemy, it will stick to the enemy and inflict the Penetrated debuff for 15 seconds, dealing 3 damage per second (3 damage displayed every 1 second). Up to six Bone Javelins can be stuck onto an enemy, dealing a total of 18 damage per second (18 damage displayed every 1 second).

Bone Throwing Knife.name: Bone Throwing Knife
Bone Throwing Knife.tooltip: The Bone Throwing Knife is a consumable ranged weapon similar to Throwing Knives. It can hit up to 6 targets. Combined with fossil armor, it can be an effective weapon against the Eater of Worlds due to its piercing.

Sturdy Fossil.name: Sturdy Fossil
Sturdy Fossil.tooltip: The Sturdy Fossil is a block and crafting material used to make bone- and fossil-themed gear. Sturdy Fossils are obtained by consuming Desert Fossils at an Extractinator, with a 10% chance of acquiring a Sturdy Fossil from each Desert Fossil. They can also be obtained from Tomb Crawlers, Basilisks, Oasis Crates, and Mirage Crates. Not counting the javelins or the throwing knives, crafting all of the fossil equipment requires 107 Sturdy Fossils.

Stardust Helmet.name: Stardust Helmet
Stardust Helmet.tooltip: Stardust armor is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord armor set consisting of the Stardust Helmet, Stardust Plate, and Stardust Leggings. Crafting the full set requires a total of 36 Luminite Bars (144 Luminite) and 45 Stardust Fragments. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +38 defense +66% summon damage +5 minion slots +1 sentry slot +30% whip range Summons a Stardust Guardian minion that floats behind the player. It is passive until an enemy is within a 30-tile radius from the player. It will then quickly charge through blocks towards the enemy, striking rapidly with punches that each deal 50 base summon damage. The Stardust Guardian will return behind the player once no enemies are within range. The Stardust Guardian is affected by summon damage bonuses, including those from whips.

Portal Gun.name: Portal Gun
Portal Gun.tooltip: The Portal Gun is a Hardmode tool that is always dropped from the Moon Lord. It launches projectiles that create up to two different portals upon contact with blocks: one fired using ⚒ Use / Attack, the other using ⚷ Open / Activate. Any player or NPC that touches one portal will be instantly transported to the other one, without losing momentum. Enemies, critters, projectiles, items, or liquids cannot be teleported. While selected, the Portal Gun will also alter the player's physics: their maximum fall speed is multiplied by 3.5 (from 51 mph to 179 mph) and horizontal momentum/inertia is kept while in the air. This effect is also applied if the last entity that affected the player's fall was a portal. The Cyborg sells the Portal Gun Station if the player has a Portal Gun in their inventory when speaking to him. On the We don't even test for that secret world seed, the Portal Gun has a 1/7 (14.29%) of being obtained from any Chest.

Strange Plant.name: Strange Plant
Strange Plant.tooltip: Strange Plants are Hardmode quest plant items that can be turned in to the Dye Trader by selecting the “Strange Plants” option in his dialogue window. In return, he rewards the player with six vials of one random special exclusive dye per plant. Up to 33 different types of dyes can be acquired this way, with more of them becoming available as the game progresses. Strange Plants are found at any altitude and can grow in most biomes, though with some restrictions (see below).

Terrarian.name: Terrarian
Terrarian.tooltip: The Terrarian is a Hardmode yoyo that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord. It rapidly fires short-lived green orbs towards nearby enemies that bounce off blocks. It also has a base 14% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%.  Its best modifier is Legendary. Although yoyos cannot normally obtain the Legendary modifier, the Terrarian is an exception and receives a unique set of boosts from the Legendary modifier: +17% damage, +8% critical strike chance, and +17% knockback.

Goblin Warlock Banner.name: Goblin Warlock Banner
Goblin Warlock Banner.tooltip: Enemy banners are functional furniture items that can be placed on the underside of blocks and platforms. They are obtained by killing most enemies and a few critters. When placed, enemy banners provide a Banner buff to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the banner. The buff grants players +50%/+100% damage inflicted with all damage to the corresponding enemy and −25%/−50% damage taken from attacks by the enemy. The banners of Old One's Army enemies will apply a weaker banner buff to the respective enemy, granting the players +10%/+20% damage inflicted and −8.33% / −16.67% damage taken. Multiple banners of the same type will not grant stacked buffs. Multiple different banner types in the vicinity will, however, all take effect and consolidate into a single buff icon. There are a total of 286 obtainable enemy banners: 115 in pre-Hardmode, 171 in Hardmode. Out of these, 118 belong to event enemies (28 in pre-Hardmode and 90 in Hardmode). In addition, there are 6 unobtainable enemy banners.

Multiple banners of the same type will not grant stacked buffs. Multiple different banner types in the vicinity will, however, all take effect and consolidate into a single buff icon. There are a total of 286 obtainable enemy banners: 115 in pre-Hardmode, 171 in Hardmode. Out of these, 118 belong to event enemies (28 in pre-Hardmode and 90 in Hardmode). In addition, there are 6 unobtainable enemy banners.

Damage Booster.name: Damage Booster
Damage Booster.tooltip: The Damage Booster is one of the three power-ups occasionally dropped when striking enemies while wearing a full set of Nebula armor. When picked up, it grants the Damage Nebula buff which immediately provides the player with a 15% damage boost for 8 seconds. When a Damage Booster is picked up while the Damage Nebula buff is already in effect, it stacks with the previous Damage Nebula, for up to 3 stacked boosts. Every 8 seconds, one stacked Damage Booster expires, and the Damage Nebula buff decreases by one level. Damage Boosters, like all Nebula boosters, float in the air and have a pickup range of 8.875 tiles. They cannot legitimately appear in a player's inventory.

Life Booster.name: Life Booster
Life Booster.tooltip: The Life Booster is one of the three power-ups occasionally dropped when striking enemies while wearing a full set of Nebula armor. When picked up, it grants the Life Nebula buff which immediately increases the player's health regeneration rate by 3 health per second for 8 seconds. When a Life Booster is picked up while the Life Nebula buff is already in effect, it stacks with the previous Life Nebula, for up to 3 stacked boosts. Every 8 seconds, one stacked Life Booster expires, and the Life Nebula buff decreases by one level. All levels of Life Booster nullify the effects of damaging debuffs, such as from Poisoned or On Fire!, with the exception of Hunger. Life Boosters, like all Nebula boosters, float in the air and have a pickup range of 8.875 tiles. They cannot legitimately appear in a player's inventory.

Mana Booster.name: Mana Booster
Mana Booster.tooltip: The Mana Booster is one of the three power-ups occasionally dropped when striking enemies while wearing a full set of Nebula armor. When picked up, it grants the Mana Nebula buff which immediately increases the player's mana regeneration rate by 10 mana per second for 8 seconds. When a Mana Booster is picked up while the Mana Nebula buff is already in effect, it stacks with the previous Mana Nebula, for up to 3 stacked boosts. Every 8 seconds, one stacked Mana Booster expires, and the Mana Nebula buff decreases by one level. Mana Boosters, like all Nebula boosters, float in the air and have a pickup range of 8.875 tiles. They cannot legitimately appear in a player's inventory.

Vortex Fragment.name: Vortex Fragment
Vortex Fragment.tooltip: The Vortex Fragment is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist crafting material. It is one of the four Lunar Fragments, dropped from the Vortex Pillar during the Lunar Events in stacks of 12–60 / 24–100. Vortex Fragments can be used to craft Vortex armor, an end-game armor set that benefits all types of ranged weapons, as well as Vortex-themed tools, weapons, wings, etc. Crafting all items requires 121 Vortex Fragments and 68 Luminite Bars (272 Luminite), which necessitates defeating the Vortex Pillar at least 3–11 / 2–8 times (note that the Vortex Fragment can also be crafted from the other fragments) and fighting the Moon Lord at least 4 / 3–4 times.

Nebula Fragment.name: Nebula Fragment
Nebula Fragment.tooltip: The Nebula Fragment is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist crafting material. It is one of the four Lunar Fragments, dropped from the Nebula Pillar during the Lunar Events in stacks of 12–60 / 24–100. Nebula Fragments can be used to craft Nebula armor, an end-game armor set that benefits all types of magic weapons, as well as Nebula-themed tools, weapons, wings, etc. Crafting all items requires 121 Nebula Fragments and 68 Luminite Bars (272 Luminite), which necessitates defeating the Nebula Pillar at least 3–11 / 2–8 times (note that the Nebula Fragment can also be crafted from the other fragments) and fighting the Moon Lord at least 4 / 3–4 times.

Solar Fragment.name: Solar Fragment
Solar Fragment.tooltip: The Solar Fragment is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist crafting material. It is one of the four Lunar Fragments, dropped from the Solar Pillar during the Lunar Events in stacks of 12–60 / 24–100. Solar Fragments can be used to craft Solar Flare armor, an end-game armor set that benefits all types of melee weapons, as well as Solar-themed tools, weapons, wings, etc. Crafting all items requires 121 Solar Fragments and 68 Luminite Bars (272 Luminite), which necessitates defeating the Solar Pillar at least 3–11 / 2–8 times (note that the Solar Fragment can also be crafted from the other fragments) and fighting the Moon Lord at least 4 / 3–4 times.

Stardust Fragment.name: Stardust Fragment
Stardust Fragment.tooltip: The Stardust Fragment is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist crafting material. It is one of the four Lunar Fragments, dropped from the Stardust Pillar during the Lunar Events in stacks of 12–60 / 24–100. Stardust Fragments can be used to craft Stardust armor, an end-game armor set that benefits all types of summon weapons, as well as Stardust-themed tools, weapons, wings, etc. Crafting all items requires 139 Stardust Fragments and 68 Luminite Bars (272 Luminite), which necessitates defeating the Stardust Pillar at least 3–11 / 2–8 times (note that the Stardust Fragment can also be crafted from the other fragments) and fighting the Moon Lord at least 4 / 3–4 times.

Luminite.name: Luminite
Luminite.tooltip: Luminite is a Hardmode ore dropped by the Moon Lord in stacks of 70–90 (90–110). It does not naturally generate in the world, and can be mined using any pickaxe. Crafting all items (excluding ammunition, dye, and bricks) requires a total of 362 Luminite Bars and 25 Luminite (1,473 Luminite; requires defeating the Moon Lord 17–22 / 14–17 times). Crafting all items pertaining to one type of Lunar Fragment (i.e., armor, wings, pickaxe/drill, and hamaxe) requires 68 Luminite Bars (272 Luminite) in addition to 85 of the Lunar Fragment; this requires defeating the Moon Lord only 4 / 3–4 times.

Luminite Brick.name: Luminite Brick
Luminite Brick.tooltip: Luminite Brick is a type of Brick and an aesthetic building material. Despite being made of Luminite, the highest tier of ore, it has no sell value. It can be used to craft Luminite Brick Walls.

Stardust Axe.name: Stardust Axe
Stardust Axe.tooltip: Luminite Axes are unobtainable tools. The four types are the Solar Flare Axe, Vortex Axe, Nebula Axe, and the Stardust Axe, each themed after a different Celestial Tower. They are all unable to be crafted, and instead the player must craft the Luminite Hamaxes. Even with Terrasavr and some other inventory editors, they seem to disappear, leaving an empty slot. Their best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Stardust Chainsaw.name: Stardust Chainsaw
Stardust Chainsaw.tooltip: Luminite Chainsaws are unobtainable tools. All of the chainsaws share the same stats. The four types are the Solar Flare Chainsaw, Vortex Chainsaw, Nebula Chainsaw, and the Stardust Chainsaw, each themed after different Celestial Pillars. They are all unable to be crafted, and instead the player must craft the Luminite Hamaxes. Like all axes and chainsaws, they are used to cut down Trees, Cacti, and Giant Glowing Mushrooms, so the best possible modifier is Godly. With current methods, it is impossible to hack these items into a character's inventory using external editors, as they will disappear from that character's inventory as soon as they load into a world.

Stardust Drill.name: Stardust Drill
Stardust Drill.tooltip: The Luminite Drills are Hardmode, post-Moon Lord drills. The four types are the  Vortex Drill, Nebula Drill, Solar Flare Drill, and Stardust Drill. They are the alternative versions of the Luminite Pickaxes, having a higher base mining speed but shorter range and lacking the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. All four drills have identical stats and can mine all blocks. Their best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Stardust Hammer.name: Stardust Hammer
Stardust Hammer.tooltip: Luminite Hammers are unobtainable tools . The four types are the Solar Flare Hammer , Vortex Hammer , Nebula Hammer , and the Stardust Hammer , each themed after a different Celestial Tower . They are all unable to be crafted, and instead the player must craft the Luminite Hamaxes .

Stardust Pickaxe.name: Stardust Pickaxe
Stardust Pickaxe.tooltip: Luminite Pickaxes are Hardmode, post-Moon Lord pickaxes. The four types are the Solar Flare Pickaxe, Vortex Pickaxe, Nebula Pickaxe, and Stardust Pickaxe. They are the alternate versions of the Luminite Drills, having a lower base mining speed but longer range and the ability to benefit from mining speed bonuses. All four pickaxes have identical stats and can mine all blocks. Their best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for these tools.

Luminite Bar.name: Luminite Bar
Luminite Bar.tooltip: The Luminite Bar is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord bar. Crafting all items pertaining to one type of Lunar Fragment (i.e., armor, wings, pickaxe, and hamaxe) requires 68 Luminite Bars (272 Luminite) in addition to 85 of the Lunar Fragment; this requires defeating the Moon Lord 4 / 3–4 times.

Solar Wings.name: Solar Wings
Solar Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Luminite Brick Wall.name: Luminite Brick Wall
Luminite Brick Wall.tooltip: Luminite Brick Wall is a background wall crafted from Luminite Bricks. It stops enemies from spawning on the tile where it's placed. It can be used to make houses for NPCs.

Solar Eruption.name: Solar Eruption
Solar Eruption.tooltip: The Solar Eruption is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist melee weapon that swings a long whipsword from the player's position towards the cursor. The whipsword sweeps in a narrow arc of varying length before quickly retracting. It can pass through blocks and pierce infinitely. The whipsword creates a Solar Explosion upon hit, dealing damage and inflicting the Daybroken debuff for 5 seconds, which deals 100 damage per second. Its best modifier is Ruthless. Since part of the Solar Eruption's damage output comes from the Solar Explosions which cannot critically hit, critical hit chance bonuses are less effective than direct increase in damage.

Stardust Cell Staff.name: Stardust Cell Staff
Stardust Cell Staff.tooltip: The Stardust Cell Staff is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist summon weapon that summons a Stardust Cell minion. It hovers near enemies, firing a homing mini-cell that attaches itself to the target, inflicting the Celled debuff to deal 20 damage per second (20 damage displayed every 1 second). A maximum of 10 mini-cells can be attached to one target at a time, for a total of 200 damage per second (200 damage displayed every 1 second). The Stardust Cell will teleport to enemies out of range. Its best modifier is Fabled.

Vortex Beater.name: Vortex Beater
Vortex Beater.tooltip: The Vortex Beater is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist gun. When used, it very rapidly fires bullets with inaccurate spread. It also fires a homing, explosive Vortex Rocket every 0.583 seconds without consuming additional ammo, which deals damage equal to the weapon's damage + 20 damage (50 + 7 + 20 = 77 base damage when using Musket Balls), and a knockback of 1.25× the weapon's knockback (base knockback of 5 (Average) when using Musket Balls). The Vortex Beater also has a 2/3 (66.67%) chance not to consume ammunition. Its best modifier is Unreal, Godly or Demonic, as it does not benefit from attack speed and velocity modifiers.

Nebula Arcanum.name: Nebula Arcanum
Nebula Arcanum.tooltip: The Nebula Arcanum is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist magic weapon that fires a swirling purple orb when used. The orb will slowly home in on enemies within a 50-tile range and bounce off blocks, hitting three times before exploding into 10–16 smaller shard projectiles that each deal 65% of the weapon's listed damage (45 base damage), inflict 80% of its knockback (base knockback of 4 (Weak)), and do not pierce. All three hits do not have to be on the same target, as it will continue to home in on other enemies in range if its target dies before the third hit. If the projectile does not hit enemies three times, it will explode after 11 seconds. As the main orb remains active, it also produces additional, smaller orb projectiles that orbit around it, each of which deals 50% of the weapon's listed damage (35 base damage), passes through blocks, inflicts no knockback, and pierces an unlimited number of enemies. A maximum of eight of these projectiles can be summoned per orb. Two to three of these projectiles appear per second for the first half of the projectile's lifetime and disappear at the same rate as it approaches its detonation. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Blood Water.name: Blood Water
Blood Water.tooltip: Thrown Water refers to a set of three consumable weapons that each convert a small area into a biome ( Hallow , Corruption , or Crimson for Holy Water , Unholy Water , and Blood Water respectively) when thrown. This conversion affects a roughly circular area with a radius of four tiles from the center. Enemies within this radius are also damaged slightly; this damage is not classified as any of the four damage types and therefore cannot be modified by any buffs or equipment.

Wedding Veil.name: Wedding Veil
Wedding Veil.tooltip: The Wedding set is a vanity set which consists of the Wedding Veil and the Wedding Dress. They are guaranteed to be dropped by The Bride, a rare enemy that spawns during a Blood Moon and in the Graveyard mini biome. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Wedding Dress.name: Wedding Dress
Wedding Dress.tooltip: The Wedding set is a vanity set which consists of the Wedding Veil and the Wedding Dress. They are guaranteed to be dropped by The Bride, a rare enemy that spawns during a Blood Moon and in the Graveyard mini biome. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Platinum Bow.name: Platinum Bow
Platinum Bow.tooltip: The Platinum Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Gold Bow. Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.

Platinum Hammer.name: Platinum Hammer
Platinum Hammer.tooltip: The Platinum Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Gold Hammer. Its best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for this tool.

Platinum Axe.name: Platinum Axe
Platinum Axe.tooltip: The Platinum Axe is a pre-Hardmode axe. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Gold Axe. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Platinum Shortsword.name: Platinum Shortsword
Platinum Shortsword.tooltip: The Platinum Shortsword is a pre-Hardmode shortsword. It is the counterpart to the Platinum Broadsword. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Gold Shortsword. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount. Due to invincibility frames, modifiers with speed boosts reduce the hit rate of the Platinum Shortsword to enemies.

Platinum Broadsword.name: Platinum Broadsword

Platinum Pickaxe.name: Platinum Pickaxe

Tungsten Pickaxe.name: Tungsten Pickaxe

Unlike the Silver Pickaxe, it can also mine Meteorite. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Solar Flare Hamaxe.name: Solar Flare Hamaxe
Solar Flare Hamaxe.tooltip: The Luminite Hamaxes are post-Moon Lord hamaxes. The four types are the Solar Flare Hamaxe, the Vortex Hamaxe, the Nebula Hamaxe, and the Stardust Hamaxe. All share the same stats. They have the highest hammer power in the game, along with The Axe. They are beaten only by The Axe in axe power, making them the second-strongest axes. Their best modifier is Legendary. However, due to rounding, Legendary, Light, Deadly, Agile, Quick, and Nasty provide equal boosts to mining speed for these tools.

Solar Dye.name: Solar Dye
Solar Dye.tooltip: Solar Dye is a Hardmode, endgame dye crafted from Solar Fragments dropped by the Solar Pillar from the Lunar Events. The dye gives a golden, metallic hue and a slight pulsating effect to anything used with it, similar to the Reflective Dyes obtainable from the Dye Trader's Strange Plants quest. Unlike the Metallic dyes, however, items dyed with Solar Dye do not appear to dynamically reflect light, and have the same appearance regardless of the player's proximity to light sources. Also unlike the metallic dyes, dyed items periodically glow (without casting light).

Nebula Dye.name: Nebula Dye
Nebula Dye.tooltip: Nebula Dye is a Hardmode, endgame dye crafted using Nebula Fragments dropped by the Nebula Pillar in the Lunar Events. The dye gives the player a pink/purple shiny look on armor, equipment or accessories and looks like stars are moving rapidly upward on anything with the dye. As with the other lunar dyes, the Nebula Dye can not be combined with any other dyes.

Vortex Dye.name: Vortex Dye
Vortex Dye.tooltip: Vortex Dye is a Hardmode dye crafted from Vortex Fragments dropped by the Vortex Pillar in the Lunar Events and Bottled Water. The effect produced is reminiscent of a green warp drive effect on all clothing and accessories the dye is applied to.

Stardust Dye.name: Stardust Dye
Stardust Dye.tooltip: Stardust Dye is a Hardmode, endgame dye crafted using Stardust Fragments obtained from the Stardust Pillar from the Lunar Events. It gives a fade bluish-white color, and it gives a white sparkling effect on the dyed armor pieces and accessories.

Void Dye.name: Void Dye
Void Dye.tooltip: Void Dye is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord dye crafted using Luminite Bars. The dye causes a pulsating effect, much like the pulsating effect that the Moon Lord creates moments before he spawns.

Stardust Dragon Staff.name: Stardust Dragon Staff
Stardust Dragon Staff.tooltip: The Stardust Dragon Staff is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist summon weapon that summons a Stardust Dragon minion. It flies towards enemies, dealing contact damage and dashing to catch up with its target. It can move through and target enemies through blocks. When the Stardust Dragon Staff is used more than once, multiple Stardust Dragons do not spawn; instead, the existing Stardust Dragon becomes longer and stronger for each additional summon. This damage scaling mechanic also affects the inital summon, causing it to have 69% more damage than what is listed in the tooltip. Each summon after the first provides an additional 46% of the tooltip's damage. At base values this means it would deal 67 damage with +18/+19 per extra summon. Its best modifier is Fabled. However, if the player's summon damage bonuses reach a certain threshold (including whip bonuses), the best modifier becomes Ruthless. The exact threshold varies depending on the number of summons, which is listed in Notes below.

Bacon.name: Bacon
Bacon.tooltip: The Bacon is a Hardmode food item that grants the Exquisitely Stuffed buff when consumed. This lasts for 24 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Bacon has a 1/15 (6.67%) chance of being dropped by Pigron. Statue-spawned Pigrons do not drop it, as it is a food item.

Shifting Sands Dye.name: Shifting Sands Dye
Shifting Sands Dye.tooltip: Shifting Sands Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When applied, it gives the item an appearance similar to falling sand. It can be used to craft Shifting Pearlsands Dye when one acquires Crystal Shards.

Mirage Dye.name: Mirage Dye
Mirage Dye.tooltip: Mirage Dye is a Hardmode dye obtained by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. Unlike other dyes, it does not change the color of objects, but instead applies a multicolored Shimmering effect.

Shifting Pearlsands Dye.name: Shifting Pearlsands Dye
Shifting Pearlsands Dye.tooltip: Shifting Pearlsands Dye is a Hardmode dye which is very similar to the Shifting Sands Dye, but more pink. It can only be crafted, and cannot be obtained any other way.

Vortex Monolith.name: Vortex Monolith
Vortex Monolith.tooltip: Monoliths are furniture items that activate backgrounds and other screen effects normally seen during events or under other special circumstances. When placed, they can be toggled with the ⚷ Open / Activate button or via wire, like other mechanisms, providing their effects in a small area around them. Monoliths only cause modified visuals; they do not spawn any event enemies or bosses, and they do not change the music. They can also be equipped as vanity accessories, which enables their effect globally for the player. There are 11 different monoliths: the Vortex, Nebula, Stardust, Solar, and Void Monoliths can be crafted at an Ancient Manipulator, the Blood Moon Monolith has a 1/10 (10%) chance of being dropped by Dreadnautiluses, the Radio Thing has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to be dropped by Deerclops, the Aether Monolith can be obtained via dropping an Angel Statue into Shimmer, the CRT and Retro Monoliths are sold by the Cyborg for 25 Gold, and the Film Projector can be obtained as part of Heroicis' set by dropping a Platinum Coin into the Water of an Oasis. The Nebula, Solar, Stardust, and Vortex Monoliths mimic effects that normally surround the corresponding Celestial Pillar during the Lunar Events. The Blood Moon Monolith mimics the effects seen during a Blood Moon. The Void Monolith mimics the screen effects of the Moon Lord boss fight. The Radio Thing activates the same sepia filter of The Constant world seed. In The Constant seed, however, it instead deactivates the filter. The Aether Monolith mimics the screen effects of the Aether mini-biome. Unlike the other monoliths, the Aether Monolith has three states: One off state (which disables the Aether effect entirely in its area, even if it would normally be present due to Shimmer) and two on states – low, which acts as if the monolith were not present (allowing the Aether effect if enough Shimmer is nearby but not forcing it on), and high, which forces the Aether effect on. The CRT Monolith mimics the effect of an old-fashioned CRT TV. The Retro Monolith mimics the effect of an old two-color green and black monitor, like the original Gameboy. The Film Projector adds a black-and-white effect to the screen.

Phantasm.name: Phantasm
Phantasm.tooltip: The Phantasm is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist bow. When used, it fires a burst of four arrows that are loosely grouped together, while only consuming one arrow per use. Its fire rate will gradually increase while in use. Upon enemy hits, the Phantasm fires an additional burst of three Phantasm Arrow projectiles. Phantasm Arrows home in on the hit target, move through blocks, deal 30% of the original projectile's damage, and inflict no knockback. The Phantasm has a 2/3 (66.67%) chance of not consuming ammunition. Its best modifier is Unreal, Godly or Demonic, as it does not benefit from attack speed and velocity modifiers.

Last Prism.name: Last Prism
Last Prism.tooltip: The Last Prism is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord magic weapon that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord. When used, it projects six rainbow-colored beams each dealing the weapon's listed damage, which immediately begin to rotate and converge into one concentrated beam over a duration of 3 seconds. The fully-converged beam instead deals 300% of the weapon's damage (300 base damage) per hit. While held, the Last Prism's aim works in a sweeping motion, meaning the turn rate is reduced. In addition to consuming mana on the initial use, the weapon will also consume mana while firing the beams, with the mana usage increasing exponentially as the beams converge: During the first 1.5 seconds of use, mana is consumed at a rate of once every 0.5 seconds, for up to 3 times. During the next 0.5 seconds of use, mana is consumed at a rate of once every 0.25 seconds, for up to 2 times. Afterwards, mana is consumed at a rate of once every 0.08 seconds, or 12 times per second. Its best modifier is Mythical or Masterful. The Last Prism is unaffected by attack speed bonuses, meaning that Mythical provides +5% critical strike chance while Masterful lowers the weapon's mana cost.

Nebula Blaze.name: Nebula Blaze
Nebula Blaze.tooltip: The Nebula Blaze is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist magic weapon that inaccurately fires pink, high-velocity projectiles which home in on nearby enemies, with a 1/5 (20%) chance to fire a larger blue Nebula Blaze Ex projectile that deals 300% of the weapon's damage (390 base damage) and moves 60% faster. When held, it appears as a pink glow covering the player's hand, which gives off a small amount of light and leaves behind a pink particle trail as the player moves. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Daybreak.name: Daybreak
Daybreak.tooltip: The Daybreak is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist melee weapon that fires a gravity-affected sun spear projectile. It sticks onto the targeted enemy upon contact, dealing damage and inflicting the Daybroken debuff, which deals 100 damage per second for a duration of 5 seconds. Up to eight sun spears can be stuck onto a single enemy at one time, resulting in 800 DPS for the debuff. When more than eight sun spears are attached, the earliest one will dissipate and cause a Solar Explosion. Additionally, a sun spear will dissipate and cause a Solar Explosion whenever it collides with blocks, when the target it is stuck to dies, or when its duration ends. Solar Explosions deal the weapon's damage and inflicts the Daybroken debuff, but cannot deal critical hits. Its best modifier is Ruthless. Since part of the Daybreak's damage output comes from the Solar Explosions which cannot critically hit, critical hit chance bonuses are less effective than direct increases in damage.

Super Healing Potion.name: Super Healing Potion
Super Healing Potion.tooltip: The Super Healing Potion is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist recovery potion that heals 200 health and inflicts Potion Sickness for 60 seconds when used. This duration can be reduced via the Philosopher's Stone or Charm of Myths. Though their crafting cost is fairly significant, they are the highest tier of healing potion in the game. They are also always dropped by the Moon Lord. It is the fifth and final tier of healing potion, succeeding the Lesser Healing Potion, Healing Potion, Greater Healing Potion, and Jungle Juice.

Detonator.name: Detonator
Detonator.tooltip: Detonators are activation mechanisms that can be found underground as part of traps, wired to Explosives. They are often found planted on top of suspiciously large veins of underground metals (e.g. Silver). A Detonator be tripped either with ⚷ Open / Activate or when a player falls on the plunger, while it cannot be triggered by enemies or NPCs. Detonators send an activation trigger to other mechanisms connected to it through Wire when tripped. Unlike pressure plates, a player has to actually fall from above to trigger a Detonator. Even walking off a 1.5 block high column will not work, while walking off a 2 block high column reliably triggers it. This makes explosive traps that use a Detonator instead of a pressure plate slightly less dangerous as they are more difficult to trigger accidentally (as well as much easier to see). When triggered by player, a Detonator disables itself for one second. When activated by a Wire, it is disabled until it is activated by Wire again. When it is disabled, plunger is stuck down and it cannot be triggered.

Celebration.name: Celebration
Celebration.tooltip: The Celebration is a Hardmode, post-Golem launcher that fires two firework rocket projectiles at once, consuming one rocket. The firework rockets travel for 0.75 seconds before exploding. The Celebration can be purchased from the Party Girl for 80 Gold. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Bouncy Dynamite.name: Bouncy Dynamite
Bouncy Dynamite.tooltip: Bouncy Dynamite is an explosive that functions like Dynamite, but bounces off blocks more intensely.

Happy Grenade.name: Happy Grenade
Happy Grenade.tooltip: The Happy Grenade is an explosive consumable ranged weapon that inflicts half the damage of an ordinary Grenade and displays a confetti effect. They must be acquired initially from being dropped by the Party Girl when she is killed, although she only has 1/4 (25%) chance of dropping them each time she is killed. Once the Party Girl respawns again, they can be purchased from her for 2 Silver 50 Copper each, while the player has them in their inventory.

Ancient Manipulator.name: Ancient Manipulator
Ancient Manipulator.tooltip: The Ancient Manipulator is a Hardmode crafting station that is always dropped by the Lunatic Cultist. It is mainly used to craft items from Luminite and Lunar Fragments.

Flame and Silver Dye.name: Flame and Silver Dye
Flame and Silver Dye.tooltip: Dyes are items that can be placed in the "dye slots" of a player's inventory to alter the colors and/or textures of equipped armor, vanity items, and accessories. The Dye Trader NPC sells two dyes (Silver Dye and Brown Dye) as well as the Dye Vat (5 Gold). The other dyes must be crafted using the Dye Vat or obtained through trading in Strange Plants to the Dye Trader. Primary crafted dyes can be further combined to craft Bright, Gradient, and Compound dyes. There are 119 different dyes in the game (118 on single-player worlds, as Team Dye is not available in single-player worlds). Some dyes will make sprites visible in complete darkness, most of which are Strange Dyes. If the Critter Shampoo is dyed (by placing a dye in the respective accessory dye slot), the dye will be applied to all of the player's minions.

Green Flame and Silver Dye.name: Green Flame and Silver Dye

Reflective Copper Dye.name: Reflective Copper Dye
Reflective Copper Dye.tooltip: Reflective Copper Dye is a dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When equipped, it will give the selected accessory/armor a copper-plated, "shiny" effect, reflecting the surrounding light around the player. The reflection is more pronounced the closer the player is to a light source. The dye will prioritize light from the sun when the player is outside. From some perspectives, the player may look 3D when this dye is equipped all over. As with other reflective dyes, this dye is not animated when standing still, but the shading on a dyed piece of equipment will change according to the surrounding light, giving it the appearance of light reflecting off of a shining metallic object.

Reflective Obsidian Dye.name: Reflective Obsidian Dye
Reflective Obsidian Dye.tooltip: Reflective Obsidian Dye is a dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When equipped, it will give the respective equipment an obsidian-plated, "shiny" effect, reflecting the surrounding light around the player. The reflection is more pronounced the closer the player is to a light source. The dye will prioritize light from the sun when the player is outside. From some perspectives, the player may look three-dimensional when this dye is equipped in all slots. As with other reflective dyes, this dye is not animated when standing still, but the shading on a dyed piece of equipment will change according to the surrounding light, giving it the appearance of light reflecting off of a shining metallic object. Unlike the other reflective dyes, this dye is rather dark which results in dark highlights.

Reflective Metal Dye.name: Reflective Metal Dye
Reflective Metal Dye.tooltip: Reflective Metal Dye is a dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When equipped, it will give the selected accessory/armor a black, "shiny" effect, reflecting the surrounding light around the player. The reflection is more pronounced the closer the player is to a light source. The dye will prioritize light from the sun when the player is outside. From some perspectives, the player may look 3D when this dye is equipped all over. As with other reflective dyes, this dye is not animated when standing still, but the shading on a dyed piece of equipment will change according to the surrounding light, giving it the appearance of light reflecting off of a shining metallic object.

Midnight Rainbow Dye.name: Midnight Rainbow Dye
Midnight Rainbow Dye.tooltip: Midnight Rainbow Dye is a dye that creates a "reverse" rainbow effect that waves throughout the colors of the spectrum. This dye can be earned by trading a Strange Plant with the Dye Trader after defeating the Martian Madness event.
