Red Acid Dye.name: Red Acid Dye
Red Acid Dye.tooltip: Red Acid Dye is a dye acquired as a random reward from the Dye Trader for giving him a Strange Plant. When equipped in a dye slot, it applies a dark red rippling effect that pulses outward, similar to Acid Dye and Blue Acid Dye. Items dyed by it can be seen in the dark but do not emit light.

Gel Dye.name: Gel Dye
Gel Dye.tooltip: Gel Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. It is received as a random reward. When equipped, the Gel Dye produces an effect similar to that of the Slime debuff caused by the Slime Gun.

Pink Gel Dye.name: Pink Gel Dye
Pink Gel Dye.tooltip: Pink Gel Dye is a dye that is crafted from Gel Dye. The Gel Dye can be acquired from the Dye Trader, and can be combined with Pink Gel, a crafting material dropped by Pinky, at a Dye Vat. Just like the Gel Dye, the Pink Gel Dye will produce an effect similar to the Slime debuff caused by the Slime Gun, though it will be displayed in a color that's more pink than blue.

Red Squirrel.name: Red Squirrel
Red Squirrel.tooltip: The Squirrel and Red Squirrel(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are critters that spawn in the Forest biome. They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Forest or Pearlwood tree. Squirrels may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details. Squirrels have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. Squirrels can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Squirrel / Red Squirrel Cage). Once crafted, the Squirrels cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Squirrels can be spawned by the Squirrel Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so. On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Squirrel to spawn in place of an ordinary one.

Gold Squirrel.name: Gold Squirrel
Gold Squirrel.tooltip: The Gold Squirrel is a harmless critter. Gold Squirrel may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Squirrel, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version. The Gold Squirrel has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Gold Squirrel can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gold Squirrel Cage). Once crafted, the Gold Squirrel cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Gold Squirrel itself or the crafted furniture can be sold for 10 Gold. It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.

Red Squirrel Cage.name: Red Squirrel Cage
Red Squirrel Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters. A critter caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item. Gold cages are regular cages containing gold critters. Aside from their higher sell value and rarity, they are the same as regular cages. Placed cages are partially transparent. They can be stacked on top of each other, but no other types of furniture can be placed on a cage. Players can stand on top of cages like platforms, even though they are otherwise background furniture.

Gold Squirrel Cage.name: Gold Squirrel Cage
Gold Squirrel Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters. A critter caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item. Gold cages are regular cages containing gold critters. Aside from their higher sell value and rarity, they are the same as regular cages. Placed cages are partially transparent. They can be stacked on top of each other, but no other types of furniture can be placed on a cage. Players can stand on top of cages like platforms, even though they are otherwise background furniture.

Luminite Bullet.name: Luminite Bullet
Luminite Bullet.tooltip: The Luminite Bullet is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord bullet. The Luminite Bullet can hit an infinite number of targets. The damage of the Luminite Bullet decreases by 4% each time it hits a target. This can reduce its damage down to 0, but it will continue to travel. It will disappear after 1.67 seconds or upon hitting a block.

Luminite Arrow.name: Luminite Arrow
Luminite Arrow.tooltip: The Luminite Arrow is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord arrow. When a Luminite Arrow dissipates, a Luminite Arrow Trail projectile will be fired after a short delay which copies the arrow's flying trail and deals the same base damage as the arrow. The Luminite Arrow and its trail can pierce 3 enemies, and their damage decreases by 4% per enemy pierced. Both the arrow and its trail also dissipate upon contact with blocks or after 0.75 seconds.

Lunar Portal Staff.name: Lunar Portal Staff
Lunar Portal Staff.tooltip: The Lunar Portal Staff is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord summon weapon that summons a Lunar Portal sentry. It continuously fires beams that sweep across enemies, which pierce infinite enemies but cannot pass through blocks. Unlike most sentries, the Lunar Portal floats midair. The Lunar Portal Staff has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord. Its best modifier is Fabled. However, if the player's summon damage bonuses reach 164% (including whip bonuses) or 64% (excluding whip bonuses), the best modifier becomes Ruthless.

Lunar Flare.name: Lunar Flare
Lunar Flare.tooltip: The Lunar Flare is a Hardmode spell book that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord. When used, it summons a spread of three lunar flares that rain down towards the cursor. The flares explode upon impact with enemies and blocks, but can pass through blocks until they have reached the cursor's location, then exploding. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Rainbow Crystal Staff.name: Rainbow Crystal Staff
Rainbow Crystal Staff.tooltip: The Rainbow Crystal Staff is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord summon weapon that summons a Rainbow Crystal sentry. It fires spreads of three multicolored light beams towards enemies, but cannot target through blocks. Each beam releases a star that explodes shortly after. Unlike most sentries, the Rainbow Crystal floats midair. The Rainbow Crystal Staff has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord. Its best modifier is Fabled. However, if the player's summon damage bonuses reach 98.5% (including whip bonuses) or 24% (excluding whip bonuses), the best modifier becomes Ruthless.

Lunar Hook.name: Lunar Hook
Lunar Hook.tooltip: The Lunar Hook is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist grappling hook crafted from Lunar Fragments. It has four glowing hooks which can be launched simultaneously and reach up to 34.375 tiles. Each hook is themed after one of the four Celestial Pillars.

Solar Fragment Block.name: Solar Fragment Block
Solar Fragment Block.tooltip: Solar Fragment Blocks are blocks made from Solar Fragments which are dropped by the Solar Pillar. The blocks have a crystal-like appearance with intense shades of yellow, red, and orange. They can be crafted with the Ancient Manipulator. Walls cannot be crafted with them.

Vortex Fragment Block.name: Vortex Fragment Block
Vortex Fragment Block.tooltip: Vortex Fragment Blocks are blocks made from Vortex Fragments which are dropped by the Vortex Pillar. The blocks have a crystal-like appearance with intense shades of green and blue. They can be crafted with the Ancient Manipulator. Walls cannot be crafted with them.

Nebula Fragment Block.name: Nebula Fragment Block
Nebula Fragment Block.tooltip: Nebula Fragment Blocks are blocks made from Nebula Fragments which are dropped by the Nebula Pillar. The blocks have a crystal-like appearance with intense shades of pink and purple. They can be crafted with the Ancient Manipulator. Walls cannot be crafted with them.

Stardust Fragment Block.name: Stardust Fragment Block
Stardust Fragment Block.tooltip: Stardust Fragment Blocks are blocks made from Stardust Fragments which are dropped by the Stardust Pillar. The blocks have a crystal-like appearance with intense shades of blue and yellow. They can be crafted at the Ancient Manipulator. Walls cannot be crafted with them.

Suspicious Looking Tentacle.name: Suspicious Looking Tentacle
Suspicious Looking Tentacle.tooltip: The Suspicious Looking Tentacle is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord light pet-summoning item that spawns the Suspicious Looking Eye, a small tentacled floating eye that provides cyan light and follows the player. The Suspicious Looking Tentacle is always dropped from the Moon Lord's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.  The pet emits light from both itself and the player. In addition to providing light, the Suspicious Looking Tentacle senses nearby NPCs, enemies, treasure (Pots, Chests, etc.), and ores within a 17-tile radius. This is shown via its pupil and iris pointing in the direction of the entity sensed, as well as expanding for treasure and contracting for enemies. The eye will also sparkle when nearby ores and treasures are detected.

Yoraiz0r's Uniform.name: Yoraiz0r's Uniform
Yoraiz0r's Uniform.tooltip: Yoraiz0r's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is the vanity set made for Yoraiz0r, one of the programmers who develops Terraria. The Scowl will add a shadow effect over the character's eyes. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. Yoraiz0r's equipment also includes this non-vanity item, which will drop in addition to his clothing set: Yoraiz0r's Spell

Yoraiz0r's Skirt.name: Yoraiz0r's Skirt

Yoraiz0r's Spell.name: Yoraiz0r's Spell
Yoraiz0r's Spell.tooltip: Yoraiz0r's Spell is a developer wing. Like other developer items, it is dropped along with its respective developer's vanity set, which is Yoraiz0r's set. Yoraiz0r's Spell is unique in that it functions as wings but displays no wing or other item graphic, instead displaying a rocket effect similar to the Rocket Boots. It also grants the ability to hover via the ▼ Down+↷ Jump keys.

Yoraiz0r's Scowl.name: Yoraiz0r's Scowl

Jim's Wings.name: Jim's Wings
Jim's Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Living Leaf Wall.name: Living Leaf Wall
Living Leaf Wall.tooltip: Living Leaf Wall is a type of wall. Like other player-crafted walls, it can be used for valid housing. They naturally generate in the treetops of the living Trees in the save the rainforest seed.

Sand Slime Banner.name: Sand Slime Banner
Sand Slime Banner.tooltip: Enemy banners are functional furniture items that can be placed on the underside of blocks and platforms. They are obtained by killing most enemies and a few critters. When placed, enemy banners provide a Banner buff to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the banner. The buff grants players +50%/+100% damage inflicted with all damage to the corresponding enemy and −25%/−50% damage taken from attacks by the enemy. The banners of Old One's Army enemies will apply a weaker banner buff to the respective enemy, granting the players +10%/+20% damage inflicted and −8.33% / −16.67% damage taken. Multiple banners of the same type will not grant stacked buffs. Multiple different banner types in the vicinity will, however, all take effect and consolidate into a single buff icon. There are a total of 286 obtainable enemy banners: 115 in pre-Hardmode, 171 in Hardmode. Out of these, 118 belong to event enemies (28 in pre-Hardmode and 90 in Hardmode). In addition, there are 6 unobtainable enemy banners.

Sea Snail Banner.name: Sea Snail Banner
Sea Snail Banner.tooltip: Enemy banners are functional furniture items that can be placed on the underside of blocks and platforms. They are obtained by killing most enemies and a few critters. When placed, enemy banners provide a Banner buff to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the banner. The buff grants players +50%/+100% damage inflicted with all damage to the corresponding enemy and −25%/−50% damage taken from attacks by the enemy. The banners of Old One's Army enemies will apply a weaker banner buff to the respective enemy, granting the players +10%/+20% damage inflicted and −8.33% / −16.67% damage taken. Multiple banners of the same type will not grant stacked buffs. Multiple different banner types in the vicinity will, however, all take effect and consolidate into a single buff icon. There are a total of 286 obtainable enemy banners: 115 in pre-Hardmode, 171 in Hardmode. Out of these, 118 belong to event enemies (28 in pre-Hardmode and 90 in Hardmode). In addition, there are 6 unobtainable enemy banners.

Moon Lord Trophy.name: Moon Lord Trophy
Moon Lord Trophy.tooltip: Trophies are decorative furniture items which usually have a 1/10 (10%) chance to be dropped from most bosses. While they can be considered the "boss version of banners", they are purely cosmetic and do not provide any bonuses. Some trophies can only be rewarded by the Angler for completing fishing quests. In total, there are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 33 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 24 trophies.

Not a Kid, nor a Squid.name: Not a Kid, nor a Squid
Not a Kid, nor a Squid.tooltip: Paintings are decorative furniture items that can be placed on background walls. Each one is a framed image that depicts a particular scene, usually Terraria-related. Their tooltips generally contain a person's name, intended to credit each painting's artist; although the names appear to be fictional, most of them correspond to known Terraria developers, artists, testing staff, and community members (see Trivia below). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions, the Magic Lantern, Spelunker Glowsticks, and Spelunker Flares. There are a total of 193 paintings, 25 of which are sold by the Painter, 7 by the Princess, 4 by the Golfer, 2 by the Zoologist, 2 by the Clothier, 1 by the Truffle, and 27 are randomly sold by the Traveling Merchant. 35 paintings can be found in Underground Cabins, another 14 in the Underground Desert Cabins, 26 in the Dungeon, 12 in The Underworld, 6 from Floating Islands, 5 obtained by fishing, 1 from the Jungle Temple, 5 randomly acquired from Goodie Bags, 8 dropped by Solar Eclipse enemies, 8 awarded randomly by the Angler for completing fishing quests, 1 from the Living Tree, and 4 dropped by enemies.

Burning Hades Dye.name: Burning Hades Dye
Burning Hades Dye.tooltip: Burning Hades Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When applied, it turns the item orange and adds fire effects.

Grim Dye.name: Grim Dye
Grim Dye.tooltip: Grim Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When equipped, it turns the color of the armor or vanity currently selected into a blood red type color, while emitting a dark effect around the player, similar to Loki's Dye.

Loki's Dye.name: Loki's Dye
Loki's Dye.tooltip: Loki's Dye is a Hardmode dye that can be obtained from Hardmode bosses' Treasure Bags (except Queen Slime's), as part of Loki's set. It does not change the color of the armor, but rather adds a dark gray flames effect, similar to four other dyes which are obtained by trading Strange Plants with the Dye Trader in Hardmode. Equipping Loki's Dye in all 3 dye slots intensifies the effect. It also makes the item in whatever slot it’s in glow in the dark.

Shadowflame Hades Dye.name: Shadowflame Hades Dye
Shadowflame Hades Dye.tooltip: Shadowflame Hades Dye is a Hardmode dye acquired by giving a Strange Plant to the Dye Trader. When applied, it turns the item violet and adds fire effects that trail behind the player.

Celestial Sigil.name: Celestial Sigil
Celestial Sigil.tooltip: The Celestial Sigil is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist boss-summoning item that summons the Moon Lord when used. It can be used in any biome, at any time. Rather than summoning the Moon Lord instantly, it triggers a 12-second countdown before he spawns. The Celestial Sigil can only be used under the following circumstances: The world is in Hardmode. Golem has been defeated. There is no invasion event active, including the Lunar Events. There is no boss alive. The Moon Lord is not already being summoned. The Mysterious Tablet is not visible to any player.

Logic Gate Lamp (Off).name: Logic Gate Lamp (Off)
Logic Gate Lamp (Off).tooltip: A Logic Gate Lamp is a mechanism that is placed atop a Logic Gate or another Logic Gate Lamp. The Logic Gate is activated based on its type and the states of the Logic Gate Lamps atop it. The state of a Logic Gate Lamp is toggled via wire. The Logic Gate Lamps, along with the Logic Gates, are purchased from the Steampunker.

Logic Gate (AND).name: Logic Gate (AND)
Logic Gate (AND).tooltip: A Logic Gate is a mechanism used to provide logic to wiring setups. Input is provided using a stack of Logic Gate Lamps placed on top of it. The logic gate turns on and off depending on its inputs, and emits a signal every time its state changes. The logic gates, along with the Logic Gate Lamps, are purchased from the Steampunker for 2 Gold each.

Logic Gate (OR).tooltip: A Logic Gate is a mechanism used to provide logic to wiring setups. Input is provided using a stack of Logic Gate Lamps placed on top of it. Conveyor Belt (Clockwise).name: Conveyor Belt (Clockwise)
Conveyor Belt (Clockwise).tooltip: Conveyor Belts (Clockwise and Counter Clockwise) are blocks obtained from Conveyor Slimes or, in Hardmode, purchased from the Steampunker for 5 Silver each. The Conveyor Slime drops only the clockwise variant; however, the two variants are interchangeable via crafting. They have the unique ability to move certain entities in their respective direction upon contact. The following entities are affected by Conveyor Belts: Players Dropped items Placed Golf Balls Town NPCs Critters Slimes (and Hoppin' Jacks, who use Slime AI) The following stationary NPCS: Gnomes, non-Biome Mimics, Lost Girls, Bound NPCs, and the distressed forms of Cattiva and Foxparks. Falling blocks (Sand, Slush, Silt, Shell Piles, Cracked Dungeon Bricks, and Ash on worlds with the For the Worthy seed active) become items when falling onto Conveyor Belts. Conveyor Belts will remain active from the moment they are placed. Being powered with Wire reverses their direction, toggling between Clockwise and Counter Clockwise. Their direction can also be switched from the crafting menu. Like most other blocks, they can be shaped into half-blocks and angled slopes using a hammer, allowing for diagonal movement. Conveyor Belts can also carry items vertically.

Conveyor Belt (Counter Clockwise).name: Conveyor Belt (Counter Clockwise)
Conveyor Belt (Counter Clockwise).tooltip: Conveyor Belts (Clockwise and Counter Clockwise) are blocks obtained from Conveyor Slimes or, in Hardmode, purchased from the Steampunker for 5 Silver each. The Conveyor Slime drops only the clockwise variant; however, the two variants are interchangeable via crafting. The Grand Design.name: The Grand Design
The Grand Design.tooltip: The Grand Design is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron tool for working with wiring and mechanisms. It combines and extends the abilities of its components: It allows a controlled view of wiring (Mechanical Lens) and measure distances and relative positions (Mechanical Ruler), and allows the player to place or remove any color of wire (Multicolor Wrench and Wire Cutter); unlike its components, it also shows and works with Actuators. Creating the Grand Design costs 15 Gold in total. Its components are all bought from the Mechanic, and it is crafted at the Tinkerer's Workshop. The Grand Design can be used at any part of the screen, regardless of block placement range.  When pressing ⚷ Open / Activate with the tool, a menu with six different buttons will be displayed, five for selecting Actuator and four colors of wires, one for toggling between placing or harvesting selected colors of wires and Actuator.   The menu will pop up at the cursor's position, with buttons in a radial pattern.  The menu will pop up above the ⚷ Open / Activate button, with buttons listed in two rows. When the menu is closed, five small colored square icons will appear near the cursor, showing the current mode (placing/harvesting) and selected wires/actuator. In addition, as long as The Grand Design is anywhere in the inventory, it will provide seven toggles, controlling the functions of Mechanical Ruler and Mechanical Lens.

Yellow Wrench.name: Yellow Wrench
Yellow Wrench.tooltip: Wrenches are tools for placing Wires, which are used to connect mechanisms together, such as a trap with a Pressure Plate. There are four different wrenches: the Red Wrench, Green Wrench, Blue Wrench, and Yellow Wrench(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), each placing its respective color of Wire. All wrenches are purchased from the Mechanic for 2 Gold each. All Wrenches use the same ordinary Wire item as ammunition, but the color of wrench used will determine the color of Wire when placed. The colors all function identically but can be placed so as to overlap or intersect each other without interfering with each other. Junction Boxes(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can further be used to keep intersecting Wire paths of the same color from interfering with each other. All four wrenches can be combined to make a Multicolor Wrench(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), a single tool that can place Wire of any color. Ordinary wrenches cannot be used to remove placed Wires. Instead, a Wire Cutter or one of its derivatives is required. All Wire colors become the same ordinary Wire item again when freed.

Logic Sensor (Day).name: Logic Sensor (Day)
Logic Sensor (Day).tooltip: Sensors are Hardmode mechanisms that emit a signal under specific circumstances. They can be placed in midair without the support of background walls. There are 7 different types of sensors, split into 2 sub-categories: Logic Sensors and Liquid Sensors.

Logic Sensor (Night).name: Logic Sensor (Night)
Logic Sensor (Night).tooltip: Sensors are Hardmode mechanisms that emit a signal under specific circumstances. They can be placed in midair without the support of background walls. There are 7 different types of sensors, split into 2 sub-categories: Logic Sensors and Liquid Sensors.

Logic Sensor (Player Above).name: Logic Sensor (Player Above)
Logic Sensor (Player Above).tooltip: Sensors are Hardmode mechanisms that emit a signal under specific circumstances. They can be placed in midair without the support of background walls. There are 7 different types of sensors, split into 2 sub-categories: Logic Sensors and Liquid Sensors.

Junction Box.name: Junction Box
Junction Box.tooltip: The Junction Box is a mechanism that allows wires of the same color to cross without connecting. It is purchased from the Mechanic for 2 Silver. The Junction Box can be placed in midair, without the need for support. Hammering the Junction Box changes the directions that the different colored wires enter and exit the Junction Box.

Announcement Box.name: Announcement Box
Announcement Box.tooltip: The Announcement Box is a special sign that, when powered, will announce (in the chat) what was written on the sign. They support the usage of tags, allowing (for example) the display of messages in different colors.

Logic Gate Lamp (On).name: Logic Gate Lamp (On)
Logic Gate Lamp (On).tooltip: A Logic Gate Lamp is a mechanism that is placed atop a Logic Gate or another Logic Gate Lamp. The Logic Gate is activated based on its type and the states of the Logic Gate Lamps atop it. The state of a Logic Gate Lamp is toggled via wire. The Logic Gate Lamps, along with the Logic Gates, are purchased from the Steampunker.

Mechanical Lens.name: Mechanical Lens
Mechanical Lens.tooltip: The Mechanical Lens is an informational accessory which reveals placed Wire and Actuators. Each color of Wire can be shown at maximum brightness, regular, or faded, which is configurable via toggles. The Mechanical Lens is purchased from the Mechanic for 1 Gold.

Actuation Rod.name: Actuation Rod
Actuation Rod.tooltip: The Actuation Rod is a post-Skeletron, craftable tool which allows directly switching the states of Actuators without having to activate them via wire. It is compatible with Smart cursor.

Red Team Block.name: Red Team Block
Red Team Block.tooltip: Team Blocks are decorative blocks purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 1 Silver each. Team Blocks are available in six different colors, each representing one of the six team colors selectable in the player's inventory, including white for the neutral team. They can be transmuted into their respective "dull" variant via Shimmer. Unlike Team Dye and Team Hair Dye, these blocks have no special function and are always the same color. The Traveling Merchant will only ever sell one color of Team Block at a time, along with the Team Platform of the same color, meaning that multiple visits will be required to collect all colors.

Red Team Platform.name: Red Team Platform
Red Team Platform.tooltip: Team Platforms are decorative platforms purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 1 Silver each. They are available in six different colors, each representing one of the six team colors selectable in the player's inventory, including white for the neutral team. Unlike Team Dye and Team Hair Dye, these platforms have no special function and are always the same color. The Traveling Merchant will only ever sell one color of Team Platform at a time, along with the Team Block of the same color, meaning that multiple visits will be required to collect all colors.

Static Hook.name: Static Hook
Static Hook.tooltip: The Static Hook is a Hardmode grappling hook that fires up to two hooks which can be launched simultaneously, reaching up to 37.5 tiles (the longest reach of any hook). The Static Hook can be purchased from the Steampunker for 50 Gold. When a hook latches onto a block, the player will be immediately suspended at their current location, unaffected by gravity, momentum, or knockback. If a second hook is fired while in this state, the player will stay attached to the first until the second hook attaches, and will not move or fall by any means. Players can use the movement keys to retract or extend the hook manually, up to its full range. Movement keys correspond with direction, so pressing ▲ Up while directly under the grappling hook will move the player upwards, whereas pressing ◀ Left or ▶ Right will not move the player at all in this case.

Presserator.name: Presserator
Presserator.tooltip: The Presserator is a construction accessory that is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 10 Gold. It automatically places Actuators to objects when placing them. It requires Actuators to be in the player's inventory in order to function.  The Presserator can be used as long as it is in the player's inventory or equipped. When held or equipped, a toggle for controlling the function of this item appears  to the left of the main inventory /  in the tools menu below the inventory.

Multicolor Wrench.name: Multicolor Wrench
Multicolor Wrench.tooltip: The Multicolor Wrench is a tool that can place down any combination of Wire color, and also remove it. It can be used at any part of the screen, regardless of block placement range. When used with ⚷ Open / Activate, a menu with five different buttons will be displayed: four for selecting the four colors of Wire, and one for toggling between placing or harvesting selected colors of Wire.   The menu will pop up at the cursor's position, with buttons in a radial pattern.  The menu will pop up above the ⚷ Open / Activate button, with buttons listed in two rows.

Pink Weighted Pressure Plate.name: Pink Weighted Pressure Plate
Pink Weighted Pressure Plate.tooltip: Pressure Plates are activation mechanisms that trigger wired mechanisms when stepped on. A pressure plate's color determines which characters can trigger it. Red, Brown, Gray, Orange, and Lihzahrd Pressure Plates are randomly generated on the map during world creation as the trigger for traps. They only take up a very small space on top of blocks, so they may be difficult to spot. The color of naturally spawned pressure plates is dependent on the color of the block they are generated on top of. Except for Lihzahrd Pressure Plates, they can also be purchased from the Mechanic. Weighted Pressure Plates activate once on being depressed, and again on being released. All Weighted Pressure Plates of the same color share a single state. As long as one Weighted Pressure Plate of a given color is already pressed down within a circuit, stepping on another identical plate will not send a new signal. They can be crafted from regular pressure plates. The Teal Pressure Pad is a special kind of pressure plate that responds to projectiles impacting it, which includes pets that touch it. Unlike regular pressure plates, the Teal Pressure Pad can be placed on all four sides of a block, e.g. on the ceiling or sidewall. It can be purchased from the Mechanic.

Engineering Helmet.name: Engineering Helmet
Engineering Helmet.tooltip: The Engineering Helmet is a vanity item equipped on the Social Helmet Slot. It is purchased from the Mechanic for 1 Gold.

Companion Cube.name: Companion Cube
Companion Cube.tooltip: The Companion Cube is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Companion Cube that follows the player. The Companion Cube can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 5 Platinum. Normally, the Companion Cube follows the player by hopping towards them. However, when the player and the Companion Cube are in complete darkness (including the absence of light sources), the Cube can occasionally "stab" the player, inflicting 3 damage. When the Companion Cube falls into lava, it emits the Lunatic Cultist's death sound. When submerged in lava for long enough, there is a chance it may make the Moon Lord's death sound. The Companion Cube will also occasionally emit the flatulence sound normally produced by the Whoopie Cushion.

Wire Bulb.name: Wire Bulb
Wire Bulb.tooltip: The Wire Bulb is a light source that has multiple colors. It is purchased from the Mechanic for 5 Gold. Each corner can be lit up by wires. Each color of wire lights up a different corner. As there are four wire colors, there are four corners with four separate colors. The Wire Bulb can be placed in midair, without the need for support.

Green Team Block.name: Green Team Block
Green Team Block.tooltip: Team Blocks are decorative blocks purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 1 Silver each. Team Blocks are available in six different colors, each representing one of the six team colors selectable in the player's inventory, including white for the neutral team. They can be transmuted into their respective "dull" variant via Shimmer. Unlike Team Dye and Team Hair Dye, these blocks have no special function and are always the same color. The Traveling Merchant will only ever sell one color of Team Block at a time, along with the Team Platform of the same color, meaning that multiple visits will be required to collect all colors.

Large Amber.name: Large Amber
Large Amber.tooltip: Large Gems are items designed for the PvP game Capture the Gem, and are dropped when the player dies, even if they are in Classic or Softcore mode. With each different Large Gem that is held or carried in the player's inventory, a hologram of it appears above the player's head. If two or more different Large Gems are carried, their holograms will revolve in a circular pattern above the player's head. They are immediately deleted if placed in a player's trash slot. Large Gems can be placed into a Gem Lock to function as a key. This is primarily used in making adventure maps. Each Large Gem can also be combined with a Minecart at any Anvil to produce a Gem Minecart. The Gem Minecarts are mechanically identical to the regular Minecart, but are aesthetically representative of their Gem type, and sparkle.

Ruby Gem Lock.name: Ruby Gem Lock
Ruby Gem Lock.tooltip: Gem Locks are activation mechanisms that can be placed on background walls. They trigger when a Large Gem of the corresponding type is inserted or removed with ⚷ Open / Activate.

Sapphire Gem Lock.name: Sapphire Gem Lock
Sapphire Gem Lock.tooltip: Gem Locks are activation mechanisms that can be placed on background walls. They trigger when a Large Gem of the corresponding type is inserted or removed with ⚷ Open / Activate.

Emerald Gem Lock.name: Emerald Gem Lock

Squirrel Statue.name: Squirrel Statue
Squirrel Statue.tooltip: Statues are furniture items. While some are purely decorative, others have a functional effect when activated via Wire—depending on the statue, it may spawn enemies, drop items, or teleport an NPC to the statue's location. Most statues can be found already placed in any area underground (most frequently in the Dungeon, Underground Cabins, and Cavern level), though Angel Statues also appear in Chests. Like all furniture, a pickaxe, a drill, or explosives are used to collect them. There are a total of 117 different statues: 25 decoration statues, 36 text and numerical statues, and 56 functional mechanisms.

Logic Gate Lamp (Faulty).name: Logic Gate Lamp (Faulty)
Logic Gate Lamp (Faulty).tooltip: A Logic Gate Lamp is a mechanism that is placed atop a Logic Gate or another Logic Gate Lamp. The Logic Gate is activated based on its type and the states of the Logic Gate Lamps atop it. The state of a Logic Gate Lamp is toggled via wire. The Logic Gate Lamps, along with the Logic Gates, are purchased from the Steampunker.

Portal Gun Station.name: Portal Gun Station
Portal Gun Station.tooltip: The Portal Gun Station is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord furniture item and mechanism that can fire portals, similar to the Portal Gun. The Portal Gun Station can be purchased from the Cyborg for 10 Gold if the player has a Portal Gun or another Portal Gun Station in their inventory. Once placed, pressing ⚷ Open / Activate key on different spots on the Portal Gun Station triggers different effects: pressing at the top toggles between orange and blue portal colors; pressing at the base fires a portal; pressing at the left or right side rotates its shooting direction. There are 9 possible orientations and it cannot fire downward, each rotation tilts it by one step (22.5°). The Portal Gun Station can also be triggered by wire. Depending on where the wire is connected, it will either change portal color, shoot portal (with a cooldown of 0.5 seconds), or rotate toward the side the wire is on. Only a pair of portals can exist at a time for each player that has the Portal Gun or Portal Gun Station, whether created by the former or the latter.

Trapped Chest.name: Trapped Chest
Trapped Chest.tooltip: A Trapped Chest is a mechanical item that has the appearance of a normal chest. It cannot be used for storage, as it does not have any storage slots. When it is opened, it emits a signal and can be connected with wire. Any chest can be crafted into a Trapped Chest at the Heavy Assembler with the desired chest and 10 wire. The Trapped Chest can be sold for 1 Silver.

Teal Pressure Pad.name: Teal Pressure Pad
Teal Pressure Pad.tooltip: Pressure Plates are activation mechanisms that trigger wired mechanisms when stepped on. A pressure plate's color determines which characters can trigger it. Red, Brown, Gray, Orange, and Lihzahrd Pressure Plates are randomly generated on the map during world creation as the trigger for traps. They only take up a very small space on top of blocks, so they may be difficult to spot. The color of naturally spawned pressure plates is dependent on the color of the block they are generated on top of. Except for Lihzahrd Pressure Plates, they can also be purchased from the Mechanic. Weighted Pressure Plates activate once on being depressed, and again on being released. All Weighted Pressure Plates of the same color share a single state. As long as one Weighted Pressure Plate of a given color is already pressed down within a circuit, stepping on another identical plate will not send a new signal. They can be crafted from regular pressure plates. The Teal Pressure Pad is a special kind of pressure plate that responds to projectiles impacting it, which includes pets that touch it. Unlike regular pressure plates, the Teal Pressure Pad can be placed on all four sides of a block, e.g. on the ceiling or sidewall. It can be purchased from the Mechanic.

While some are purely decorative, others have a functional effect when activated via Wire—depending on the statue, it may spawn enemies, drop items, or teleport an NPC to the statue's location. Most statues can be found already placed in any area underground (most frequently in the Dungeon, Underground Cabins, and Cavern level), though Angel Statues also appear in Chests. Like all furniture, a pickaxe, a drill, or explosives are used to collect them. There are a total of 117 different statues: 25 decoration statues, 36 text and numerical statues, and 56 functional mechanisms.

Angler Tackle Bag.name: Angler Tackle Bag
Angler Tackle Bag.tooltip: The Angler Tackle Bag is an accessory that combines the functionality of its components: the Angler Earring's +10 boost to Fishing Power, the Tackle Box's chance to not consume bait, and the unbreakable quality of the High Test Fishing Line. The Angler Tackle Bag's increase in Fishing Power stacks with that of the Angler Earring and Lavaproof Tackle Bag, granting a total boost of +30 if all three are equipped. The decreased chance to consume bait does not stack with that of the Tackle Box or the Lavaproof Tackle Bag.

Geyser.name: Geyser
Geyser.tooltip: The Geyser is a trap that spews a vertical stream of fire which deals a base damage of 40 / 80 / 120 and a knockback of 2 (Very weak) emitting large amount of light. It will activate when a player touches it or when it is triggered via wire. Geysers are found naturally-placed in random areas that are deep enough to generate lava, including the Underworld and deeper Cavern areas. They are generated without Pressure Plates or wires attached to them. Geysers can be placed on the top or bottom of blocks, facing upward or downward respectively, but not sideways. Geysers consume no ammunition, and their output is limited only by a cooldown period of 3.33 seconds. Geyser fire streams extend up to 20 tiles up or down (which can be blocked by solid blocks) and last for 1 second. The stream also has the ability to move through solid blocks and liquids before creating the fire stream (see Notes for details).

Ultrabright Campfire.name: Ultrabright Campfire
Ultrabright Campfire.tooltip: Campfires are a type of furniture and crafting station that emit light and grant the Cozy Fire buff to players in their vicinity, which provides 10% increased innate health regeneration and additionally grants 0.5 HP/s constant regeneration. The buff is applied to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the campfire, similar to Heart Lanterns and Sunflowers. Campfires are also minor crafting stations, and uniquely, campfires are used to cook Marshmallow on a Stick (see their page for details). Campfires can be toggled off and on with ⚷ Open / Activate, which extinguishes the flame, light, and disables the Cozy Fire buff. They can also be extinguished and lit with the Water Gun and Slime Gun respectively, and as mechanisms, they can be toggled with wire. Campfires are extinguished by rain in The Constant special world seed.

Pixel Box.name: Pixel Box
Pixel Box.tooltip: The Pixel Box is a mechanism that can be bought from the Mechanic for 2 Silver. When activated, it looks fully illuminated but does not emit light. Pixel Boxes can be placed anywhere, even if a wall is not present, similarly to Logic Gates. They are always placed in the deactivated state. If a wire below or above the Pixel Box is turned on at the same time as a wire to the left or right of the Pixel Box, it will turn on. Turning on the wire only below or above or only to the left or right will have no effect. Wires must be placed on the Pixel Box in order for them to function.

Liquid Sensor (Water).name: Liquid Sensor (Water)
Liquid Sensor (Water).tooltip: Sensors are Hardmode mechanisms that emit a signal under specific circumstances. They can be placed in midair without the support of background walls. There are 7 different types of sensors, split into 2 sub-categories: Logic Sensors and Liquid Sensors.

Liquid Sensor (Lava).name: Liquid Sensor (Lava)

Bundled Party Balloons.name: Bundled Party Balloons
Bundled Party Balloons.tooltip: Bundled Party Balloons are a vanity accessory purchased from the Clothier for 2 Gold while a Party is active. When worn, the balloons will be shown being held by the player, bobbing up and down. The Bundled Party Balloons cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Balloon Animal.name: Balloon Animal
Balloon Animal.tooltip: The Balloon Animal is a vanity accessory purchased from the Clothier for 2 Gold while a Party is active. When worn, the Balloon Animal will be shown being held by the player, bobbing up and down. The Balloon Animal cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Party Hat.name: Party Hat
Party Hat.tooltip: The Party Hat is a Vanity item sold by the Party Girl NPC for 1 Gold.

Silly Sunflower Petals.name: Silly Sunflower Petals
Silly Sunflower Petals.tooltip: The Silly Sunflower set is a vanity set which consists of the Silly Sunflower Petals, Silly Sunflower Tops and Silly Sunflower Bottoms. They are purchased from the Clothier for 9 Gold (set) while a Party is active. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Silly Pink Balloon.name: Silly Pink Balloon
Silly Pink Balloon.tooltip: Silly Balloons are blocks that can be purchased during a Party from the Party Girl for 1 Silver each or obtained from killing Balloon Slimes. When a single one is placed, it has a round appearance, just like Bubbles and Smoke Blocks. When balloons of the same color are placed together in groups, they connect to make a seemingly single larger balloon block. If placed adjacent to balloon blocks of other colors, they do not connect, and each will remain a single round balloon. In a similar way to Pink Slime Blocks, landing on any silly balloon block negates fall damage and causes the player to bounce. Silly Balloons can also be used to craft balloon furniture.

Blue Streamer.name: Blue Streamer
Blue Streamer.tooltip: Streamers are placeable items that can be climbed on for mobility. They are available in three different colors: Blue Streamer, Green Streamer, and Pink Streamer. These are all functionally identical and can be purchased for 50 Copper each from the Party Girl during a Party. Despite their unique appearance, streamers are functionally the same as Rope. Their ascent speed is 41 mph, the descent speed is 51 mph, and the horizontal speed is 5 mph (although it is listed as 0 mph in the game, it is 7.55 feet per second), though they cannot be crafted into Rope Coils like other Rope variants can. When multiple streamers of the same color are hung in a single horizontal row, they will appear as a banner-style ribbon.

Silly Balloon Machine.tooltip: The Silly Balloon Machine is a novelty furniture item that can be purchased from the Party Girl for 5 Gold. Once placed, it continuously produces decorative pink, purple, and green balloons at short random intervals and at no cost. It can be deactivated and reactivated via Wire.

Silly Tied Balloon (Pink).name: Silly Tied Balloon (Pink)
Silly Tied Balloon (Pink).tooltip: Silly Tied Balloons are animated novelty furniture items that can be purchased during a Party from the Party Girl for 10 Silver each.

Silly Tied Balloon (Purple).name: Silly Tied Balloon (Purple)
Silly Tied Balloon (Purple).tooltip: Silly Tied Balloons are animated novelty furniture items that can be purchased during a Party from the Party Girl for 10 Silver each.

Pigronata.name: Pigronata
Pigronata.tooltip: The Pigronata is a placeable furniture item hung by the player from the underside of blocks, similar to banners. When hit with weapons or projectiles, it is destroyed in a shower of confetti, and drops coins and/or other loot. Pigronatas can be purchased from the Party Girl during a Party for 1 Gold each.

Party Center.name: Party Center
Party Center.tooltip: The Party Center is an animated novelty mechanism furniture item bought from the Party Girl NPC for 20 Gold. Pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on a Party Center toggles the Party event.

Silly Tied Bundle of Balloons.name: Silly Tied Bundle of Balloons
Silly Tied Bundle of Balloons.tooltip: The Silly Tied Bundle of Balloons is an animated novelty furniture item crafted from green, purple, and pink Silly Tied Balloons, which can be purchased during a Party from the Party Girl.

Party Present.name: Party Present
Party Present.tooltip: The Party Present is a decorative furniture item that can be purchased from the Party Girl during a Party for 20 Silver. It has one of several different appearances when placed, similar to Books.

Slice of Cake.name: Slice of Cake
Slice of Cake.tooltip: The Slice of Cake is a furniture item acquired by being the first player to talk to the Party Girl during a randomly occurring Party. Player-initiated Parties (caused by a Party Center), or the Party initiated at the creation of Celebration Mk 10 or Zenith worlds will not cause her to give players the Slice of Cake. Placing and pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Slice of Cake grants the Sugar Rush buff, which grants +20% movement speed and +20% mining speed. This lasts for 2 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). Unlike equipment buff items, the Slice of Cake must be placed in order to activate the buff. It can be mined with a pickaxe or drill and picked up again, even while the buff is active, which will not cancel the buff. Placement is only dependent on an adequate space of 2×2 tiles being available.

Cog Wall.name: Cog Wall
Cog Wall.tooltip: Cog Walls are a type of background wall made from Cogs. The wall is animated similar to placed cogs.

Sandfall Wall.name: Sandfall Wall
Sandfall Wall.tooltip: Sandfall Wall is one of only a few animated background walls. It depicts falling sand.

Snowfall Wall.name: Snowfall Wall
Snowfall Wall.tooltip: Snowfall Wall is one of only a few animated background walls. It depicts falling snow.

Sandfall Block.name: Sandfall Block
Sandfall Block.tooltip: The Sandfall Block is an animated block type showing falling sand. It is one of the few items that uses the Crystal Ball as a crafting station.

Snowfall Block.name: Snowfall Block
Snowfall Block.tooltip: The Snowfall Block is an animated block type which shows falling snow. Like related blocks such as the Waterfall Block or Lavafall Block, it is one of the few items that uses the Crystal Ball as a crafting station.

Snow Cloud.name: Snow Cloud
Snow Cloud.tooltip: Snow Cloud is a type of block that can be crafted at a Sky Mill from Cloud blocks in the Snow biome. Snow Cloud blocks cause purely decorative snowflakes to appear beneath them, continuing for about 8 tiles and then fading away for 5 more. Landing on Snow Clouds will not inflict fall damage. In Drunk worlds, Snow Clouds are generated naturally as part of snow-themed Floating Islands.

Pedguin's Hood.tooltip: Pedguin's set is a vanity set. Each piece has a 1/150 (0.67%) chance of being dropped by Corrupt and Vicious Penguins.

Pedguin's Jacket.name: Pedguin's Jacket
Pedguin's Jacket.tooltip: Pedguin's set is a vanity set. Each piece has a 1/150 (0.67%) chance of being dropped by Corrupt and Vicious Penguins.

Silly Purple Balloon Wall.tooltip: Silly Balloon Walls are background Walls crafted from Silly Balloons, which are purchased from the Party Girl during a party.

0x33's Aviators.name: 0x33's Aviators
0x33's Aviators.tooltip: 0x33's Aviators are a vanity item obtained by defeating the Eye of Cthulhu in Master Mode.

Blue Phasesaber.name: Blue Phasesaber
Blue Phasesaber.tooltip: Phasesabers are a group of Hardmode broadswords, direct upgrades to the phaseblades with much more damage and slightly faster use time. There are nine different color variations with identical statistics. Letting go of ⚒ Use / Attack while swinging will throw the weapons, causing them to sharply drop down after traveling for 0.5 seconds or upon contact with blocks, then embed themselves in the ground and continuously damage any enemy that touches them. They can be recalled by pressing ⚒ Use / Attack again, which will damage enemies along the way. They can also be recalled mid-throw. All phasesabers emit a small amount of light corresponding to their color when swung, thrown, or embedded in the ground. Their best modifier is Legendary.

Djinn's Curse.name: Djinn's Curse
Djinn's Curse.tooltip: Djinn's Curse is a Hardmode armor item that can be equipped in the "pants" slot.

Ancient Horn.name: Ancient Horn
Ancient Horn.tooltip: The Ancient Horn is a Hardmode mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Basilisk Mount, which gives the player an additional jump and the ability to charge through enemies, damaging them in the process. The Ancient Horn has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by Basilisks. The Basilisk mount provides accelerated land speed at 41 mph and provides increased jump height (14 tiles/28 feet), though is still hindered by water as usual. While mounted on the Basilisk, the player is immune to knockback and only takes 20% fall damage. If the Basilisk is moving at a speed of least 21 mph, running through enemies inflicts 90 base damage, not counting enemy defense. This damage is considered summon damage, meaning that minion-enhancing items will improve it. Enemies that are damaged by this attack do not inflict contact damage on the player, but the player will suffer contact damage from enemies that survive it, if the hitbox of the player gets hit. The mount emits a faint red glow from 27' underground downwards. This light does not grow stronger as the player descends, and its color is unaffected by dyes.

Mandible Blade.name: Mandible Blade
Mandible Blade.tooltip: The Mandible Blade is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by Antlion Chargers and Antlion Swarmers. Letting go of ⚒ Use / Attack while swinging will throw the weapon in direction of the cursor, which can travel forward for 0.25 seconds before sharply dropping down. The Mandible Blade has a base 11% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Ancient Headdress.name: Ancient Headdress
Ancient Headdress.tooltip: The Ancient set is a Hardmode vanity set that consists of the Ancient Headdress, Ancient Garments, and Ancient Slacks. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Ancient Garments.name: Ancient Garments
Ancient Garments.tooltip: The Ancient set is a Hardmode vanity set that consists of the Ancient Headdress, Ancient Garments, and Ancient Slacks. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Forbidden Mask.name: Forbidden Mask
Forbidden Mask.tooltip: Forbidden armor is a Hardmode mage/summoner armor set consisting of the Forbidden Mask, Forbidden Robes, and Forbidden Treads. Crafting the full set requires a total of 3 Forbidden Fragments and 46 Adamantite or Titanium Bars (184 ore). The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +26 defense +25% magic and summon damage +80 maximum mana +2 minion slots Summons a Forbidden Sign minion that floats behind the player. Double-tapping either ▼ Down or ▲ Up (depending on the "Activate Set Bonuses" setting) will consume 20 mana and send dust particles at the nearest solid block beneath the cursor's location, summoning an Ancient Storm. The storm rapidly deals 20 contact damage. The dust particles cannot pass through solid objects, so if they hit one before reaching the cursor, the Ancient Storm will not be summoned.

Forbidden Treads.name: Forbidden Treads
Forbidden Treads.tooltip: Forbidden armor is a Hardmode mage/summoner armor set consisting of the Forbidden Mask, Forbidden Robes, and Forbidden Treads. Crafting the full set requires a total of 3 Forbidden Fragments and 46 Adamantite or Titanium Bars (184 ore). The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +26 defense +25% magic and summon damage +80 maximum mana +2 minion slots Summons a Forbidden Sign minion that floats behind the player. Double-tapping either ▼ Down or ▲ Up (depending on the "Activate Set Bonuses" setting) will consume 20 mana and send dust particles at the nearest solid block beneath the cursor's location, summoning an Ancient Storm. The storm rapidly deals 20 contact damage. The dust particles cannot pass through solid objects, so if they hit one before reaching the cursor, the Ancient Storm will not be summoned.

Spirit Flame.name: Spirit Flame
Spirit Flame.tooltip: The Spirit Flame is a Hardmode magic weapon that causes a small purple flame to appear in a random location around the player and hovers in midair when used. When an enemy comes within 25 tiles and has a clear line of sight to the flame, it will home in on that enemy. Upon impact with any enemy or block, it will cause a small explosion, dealing splash damage. The Spirit Flame can be used repeatedly to summon multiple flames, and the flames dissipate if no target is acquired within 4 seconds of casting. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Sand Elemental Banner.name: Sand Elemental Banner
Sand Elemental Banner.tooltip: Enemy banners are functional furniture items that can be placed on the underside of blocks and platforms. They are obtained by killing most enemies and a few critters. When placed, enemy banners provide a Banner buff to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the banner. The buff grants players +50%/+100% damage inflicted with all damage to the corresponding enemy and −25%/−50% damage taken from attacks by the enemy. The banners of Old One's Army enemies will apply a weaker banner buff to the respective enemy, granting the players +10%/+20% damage inflicted and −8.33% / −16.67% damage taken. Multiple banners of the same type will not grant stacked buffs. Multiple different banner types in the vicinity will, however, all take effect and consolidate into a single buff icon. There are a total of 286 obtainable enemy banners: 115 in pre-Hardmode, 171 in Hardmode. Out of these, 118 belong to event enemies (28 in pre-Hardmode and 90 in Hardmode). In addition, there are 6 unobtainable enemy banners.

Pocket Mirror.name: Pocket Mirror
Pocket Mirror.tooltip: The Pocket Mirror is a Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Stoned debuff. It has a 1/40 (2.5%) / 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped by naturally spawned Medusas.

Magic Sand Dropper.name: Magic Sand Dropper
Magic Sand Dropper.tooltip: Magic Droppers are Hardmode items used to place "droplets" — dripping liquid effects on ceilings. Once placed, they permanently display an intermittent dripping effect. The effect is purely visual, and has no functional use. Magic Droppers are crafted with an Empty Dropper at Water, Lava, Honey, or with any Sand, with the Crystal Ball nearby. The Magic Shimmer Dropper is an exception, crafted by throwing an Empty Dropper into the Shimmer. Magic Droppers can be placed at the bottom side of a block, consuming the item in the process. Droplets can be removed by mining them with a pickaxe, but doing so will not drop any item. Droplets are also naturally generated in random areas on world generation. They spawn below ceilings that have their corresponding liquid above them, as though that liquid were "leaking through". Natural droplets can be mined just like the player-placed version, and similarly drip indefinitely until removed by a player.

Forbidden Fragment.name: Forbidden Fragment
Forbidden Fragment.tooltip: The Forbidden Fragment is a Hardmode crafting material which is always dropped by Sand Elementals, which spawn during Sandstorms in the Desert. To craft all items that require this material, 9 Forbidden Fragments are required.

Lamia Tail.name: Lamia Tail
Lamia Tail.tooltip: The Lamia set is a Hardmode vanity set which consists of the Lamia Mask, Lamia Wraps and the Lamia Tail. It is rarely dropped by Lamias, with a 1/120 (0.83%) chance per piece for both types of Lamia. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Lamia Wraps.name: Lamia Wraps
Lamia Wraps.tooltip: The Lamia set is a Hardmode vanity set which consists of the Lamia Mask, Lamia Wraps and the Lamia Tail. It is rarely dropped by Lamias, with a 1/120 (0.83%) chance per piece for both types of Lamia. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Lamia Mask.name: Lamia Mask
Lamia Mask.tooltip: The Lamia set is a Hardmode vanity set which consists of the Lamia Mask, Lamia Wraps and the Lamia Tail. It is rarely dropped by Lamias, with a 1/120 (0.83%) chance per piece for both types of Lamia. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Sky Fracture.name: Sky Fracture
Sky Fracture.tooltip: The Sky Fracture is a Hardmode wand. When used, it summons three energy swords in quick succession around the player, aiming at the cursor's location. The swords do not pierce enemies and cannot pass through blocks. The Sky Fracture also has a base 24% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Onyx Blaster.name: Onyx Blaster
Onyx Blaster.tooltip: The Onyx Blaster is a Hardmode gun and the direct upgrade to the Shotgun. When used, it fires a spread of 4 bullets, consuming one piece of ammunition. It also fires an onyx crystal that explodes upon impact with an enemy or a block, or after traveling for 0.33 seconds. The projectile deals 200% of the weapon's damage, e.g. 62 damage when using Musket Ball. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Ancient Cloth.tooltip: Ancient Cloth is an uncommon Hardmode crafting material which has a 1/10 (10%) chance of dropping from all types of Ghouls.

Desert Spirit Lamp.name: Desert Spirit Lamp
Desert Spirit Lamp.tooltip: The Desert Spirit Lamp is a decorative Hardmode furniture item and crafting material. It can only be placed on flat-surface furniture. It has a 1/40 (2.5%) chance of being dropped from Desert Spirits, which can be encountered in the Corrupted or Crimson Underground Desert.

Music Box (Sandstorm).name: Music Box (Sandstorm)
Music Box (Sandstorm).tooltip: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End), which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 Gold after defeating the Moon Lord. A recorded Music Box can be played back in one of two ways: Equipping it as an accessory. Placing it as furniture and activating it, either by the ⚷ Open / Activate button or with wires. Recorded Music Boxes can be reverted into blank ones through Shimmer transmutation. There are 101 different Music Boxes available.

Apprentice's Hat.name: Apprentice's Hat
Apprentice's Hat.tooltip: Apprentice armor is a Hardmode mage/summoner armor set consisting of the Apprentice's Hat, Apprentice's Robe, and Apprentice's Trousers. The set can be purchased from the Tavernkeep for a total of 45 Defender Medals after defeating any mechanical boss. The Dark Artist armor can be considered a direct upgrade of the Apprentice armor. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +32 defense +20% magic damage +20% magic critical strike chance +10% mana cost reduction +30% summon damage +2 sentry slots +20% movement speed Flameburst sentry summons have 50% increased attack range (84 tiles), 40% increased projectile velocity, and significantly increased field of view.

Squire's Great Helm.name: Squire's Great Helm
Squire's Great Helm.tooltip: Squire armor is a Hardmode melee/summoner armor set consisting of the Squire's Great Helm, Squire's Plating, and Squire's Greaves. The set can be purchased from the Tavernkeep for a total of 45 Defender Medals after defeating any mechanical boss. The Valhalla Knight armor can be considered a direct upgrade of the Squire armor. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +58 defense +15% melee damage +15% melee critical strike chance +30% summon damage +2 sentry slots +15% movement speed +2 HP/second health regeneration Ballista sentry summons have increased projectile velocity and increased pierce (3 to 6) Upon taking damage, grants the Ballista Panic! buff for 5 seconds, increasing the fire rate (from 3.1 seconds to 1.43 seconds) of all Ballista sentries summoned by the player.

Apprentice's Scarf.name: Apprentice's Scarf
Apprentice's Scarf.tooltip: The Apprentice's Scarf is an accessory that increases the player's sentry slots by one and increases summon damage by 10%. It is dropped by the Dark Mage with a 1/4 (25%) / 1/2 (50%) chance.

Squire's Shield.name: Squire's Shield
Squire's Shield.tooltip: The Squire's Shield is a shield accessory that increases the player's sentry slots by one and increases summon damage by 10%. It is dropped by the Dark Mage with a 1/4 (25%) / 1/2 (50%) chance.

Huntress's Buckler.name: Huntress's Buckler
Huntress's Buckler.tooltip: The Huntress's Buckler is a Hardmode shield accessory that increases the player's sentry slots by one and increases summon damage by 10%. The Huntress's Buckler is dropped by Ogres during the Old One's Army event with a 1/6 (16.67%) / 1/4 (25%) chance during Tier 2, and a 1/12 (8.33%) chance during Tier 3.

Monk's Belt.name: Monk's Belt
Monk's Belt.tooltip: The Monk's Belt is a Hardmode accessory that increases the player's sentry slots by one and increases summon damage by 10%.  The Monk's Belt is dropped by Ogres during the Old One's Army event with a 1/6 (16.67%) / 1/4 (25%) chance during Tier 2, and a 1/12 (8.33%) chance during Tier 3.

Defender's Forge.name: Defender's Forge
Defender's Forge.tooltip: The Defender's Forge is a portable, personal storage item which is purchased from the Tavernkeep for 50 Defender Medals. The storage provided by the Defender's Forge is separate from the Piggy Bank, Safe, and Void Vault, so it allows the player to carry significantly more items at any given time.

War Table.name: War Table
War Table.tooltip: The War Table is an animated furniture item which fulfills a house's table requirement that is dropped by the Dark Mage and the Ogre during the Old One's Army event, with a 1/2 (50%) / 1/1 (100%) chance during Tier 1, and a 1/8 (12.5%) / 1/4 (25%) chance during Tier 3. Placing and pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the War Table grants the Strategist buff, which increases the player's sentry capacity by 1. This lasts until the player dies or leaves the world, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). Unlike equipment buff items, the War Table must be placed in order to activate the buff. It can be mined with a pickaxe or drill and picked up again, even while the buff is active, which will not cancel the buff. Placement is only dependent on an adequate space of 5×4 tiles being available.

War Table Banner.name: War Table Banner
War Table Banner.tooltip: The War Table Banner is a decorative banner obtained by defeating the Dark Mage in the Old One's Army event. During the last Tier 1 wave, it has a 50% / 100% chance to drop; during the fourth and sixth Tier 3 waves, it has a 12.5% / 25% chance to drop. The Dark Mage drops 4 banners at a time.

Eternia Crystal Stand.name: Eternia Crystal Stand
Eternia Crystal Stand.tooltip: The Eternia Crystal Stand is a furniture item that initiates the Old One's Army event when an Eternia Crystal is placed on it with ⚷ Open / Activate. The Eternia Crystal Stand can be purchased from the Tavernkeep for 1 Gold.

Defender Medal.name: Defender Medal
Defender Medal.tooltip: Defender Medals are a form of currency used to purchase items from the Tavernkeep. They are obtained in the Old One's Army event, being dropped by the Eternia Crystal at the end of each wave, beginning with the third wave. Betsy's Expert Mode Treasure Bag also contains 30–49 Defender Medals. In addition, the player can obtain 10 Defender Medals by talking to the Tavernkeep and selecting the "Eternia Crystal" option, but this can only be done once per character.

Flameburst Rod.name: Flameburst Rod
Flameburst Rod.tooltip: The Flameburst Rod, Cane, and Staff are special sentry summon weapons that summon their respective sentries. Each Flameburst Tower shoots fireballs towards enemies, which explode on contact and have a chance to inflict the On Fire! or Hellfire debuff. Unlike other projectile sentries, the Flameburst Tower is unable to fire upward at an angle greater than 45°; thus it often ignores flying enemies. The higher the tier, the more damage the Flameburst Towers deal. The Rod is sold by the Tavernkeep for 5 Defender Medals. The Cane is sold for 15 Defender Medals after defeating one mechanical boss. The Staff is sold for 60 Defender Medals after defeating Golem. During the Old One's Army event, Etherian Mana can be collected, which allows the placement of multiple Flameburst Towers that remain permanently until the event is over. Etherian Mana cannot be used outside the event. These weapons cannot be used outside of the Old One's Army event until the event has been successfully completed. Flameburst Tower sentries are boosted by the Apprentice armor and Dark Artist armor set bonuses, which dramatically increase their range, field of view, and projectile velocity. The Dark Artist armor will also boost the explosion radius of the sentries' projectiles. Their best modifier is Fabled. However, if the player's summon damage bonuses reach 162% (including whip bonuses) or 62% (excluding whip bonuses), the Flameburst Staff's best modifier becomes Ruthless.

Ale Tosser.name: Ale Tosser
Ale Tosser.tooltip: The Ale Tosser is a pre-Hardmode ranged weapon that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped from the Tavernkeep. When used, it consumes and fires Ale, which is affected by gravity and shatters upon contact with an enemy or a block, damaging enemies and affecting entities in a 9×9-tile square area. It has a 1/20 (5%) chance to inflict the Confused debuff on players in PvP and enemies for 2–5 seconds, and always inflicts Tipsy debuff on players and NPCs for 1 minute 0.98 seconds. The Tipsy debuff on NPCs grants 1.1× defense, 1.1× damage, and 0.9× attack interval (about +11% attack speed). The player also gains 10% increased ranged damage and 5% increased ranged critical strike chance if they are holding Ale Tosser while having the Tipsy debuff. The Ale Tosser has a 69% chance not to consume ammunition. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Etherian Mana.name: Etherian Mana
Etherian Mana.tooltip: Etherian Mana is used to summon Tavernkeep's sentries during the Old One's Army event, and is dropped by all of the event's enemies. Each wave has a designated amount of mana to be dropped over its course (see wave chart), and it will be dropped in stacks of 1 by the respective number of enemies during the wave. When collected in the player's inventory, the amount of Etherian Mana they have will appear in the bottom right corner of any Tavernkeep's sentry summon weapons in the hotbar, similar to the way ammo is displayed for ranged weapons. Activating the Eternia Crystal gives the player a starting amount of 10 Etherian Mana, and each wave will produce between exactly 20, 30, or 40 Etherian Mana. Each Tavernkeep's sentry costs 10 Etherian Mana to summon, so conserving Etherian Mana and developing a strategy is key to the event. Once the Old One's Army event ends, all Etherian Mana dropped in the world and inside the player's inventory will despawn.

Brand of the Inferno.name: Brand of the Inferno
Brand of the Inferno.tooltip: The Brand of the Inferno is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss broadsword. It has a 1/4 (25%) chance of inflicting the Hellfire debuff for five seconds on hit and also allows the player to parry incoming damage while equipped with a shield. While holding the Brand of the Inferno with any equipped shield (excluding the Huntress's Buckler), pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button will cause the player to raise the shield. When timed correctly, up to 0.33 seconds before taking a hit, the enemy's attack will be parried, which negates the contact damage being dealt to the player, deals 200% of the contact damage of the attacking enemy, inflicts a knockback value of 5 (Average), and grants the player 30 invincibility frames (60 with the Cross Necklace equipped). Successfully parrying an attack also grants the Striking Moment buff, causing the next melee-based attack to deal 500% or five times its usual base damage for the next five seconds. Alternatively, if the shield is held in place, 20 defense is temporarily gained; this lasts until the shield is lowered. The Brand of the Inferno is dropped by Ogres during the Old One's Army event, with a 1/10 (10%) / 1/5 (20%) chance during Tier 2, and a 1/20 (5%) chance during Tier 3. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Ballista Rod.name: Ballista Rod
Ballista Rod.tooltip: The Ballista Rod, Cane, and Staff are special sentry summon weapons that summon their respective sentries. Each Ballista sentry fires Ballista Shot projectiles towards enemies, which pierce three times. Ballistas deal high damage but have a slow firing speed. The higher the tier, the more damage the Ballistas deal. The Rod is sold by the Tavernkeep for 5 Defender Medals. The Cane is sold for 15 Defender Medals after defeating one mechanical boss. The Staff is sold for 60 Defender Medals after defeating Golem. During the Old One's Army event, Etherian Mana can be collected, which allows the placement of multiple Ballistas that remain permanently until the event is over. Etherian Mana cannot be used outside the event. These weapons cannot be used outside of the Old One's Army event until the event has been successfully completed. Ballista sentries are boosted by the Squire armor and Valhalla Knight armor set bonuses, which increase the velocity of the Ballista Shot projectiles by 31.25%  and allow them to pierce through maximum of six enemies, before dissipating on the seventh hit. In addition, they grant the Ballista Panic! buff for 5 seconds when the player takes damage, which increases the sentries' fire rate. The Valhalla Knight armor also greatly increases the fire rate. Their best modifier is Fabled. However, if the player's summon damage bonuses reach 57.5% (including whip bonuses), the Ballista Staff's best modifier becomes Ruthless.

Flying Dragon.name: Flying Dragon
Flying Dragon.tooltip: The Flying Dragon is a Hardmode, post-Golem broadsword that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Betsy during Tier 3 of the Old One's Army event. When swung, it fires red crescent-shaped projectiles every 20 ticks, which pierce four enemies, pass through blocks, and dissipate after one second. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Eternia Crystal.name: Eternia Crystal
Eternia Crystal.tooltip: The Eternia Crystal is an event-summoning item. When used on the Eternia Crystal Stand while under the correct terrain requirements, the Old One's Army event begins. The Eternia Crystal can be purchased from the Tavernkeep for 25 Silver (pre-mechanical bosses), 1 Gold (post-one mechanical boss), or 4 Gold (post-Golem).

Lightning Aura Rod.name: Lightning Aura Rod
Lightning Aura Rod.tooltip: The Lightning Aura Rod, Cane, and Staff are special sentry summon weapons that summon their respective sentries. Each Lightning Aura sentry consists of an aura with a radius of 9 tiles, which damages enemies repeatedly while within. For enemies with less than 999 defense, Lightning Aura sentries have armor penetration equal to their defense, completely bypassing it. The higher the tier, the more damage the Lightning Auras deal. The Rod is sold by the Tavernkeep for 5 Defender Medals. The Cane is sold for 15 Defender Medals after defeating one mechanical boss. The Staff is sold for 60 Defender Medals after defeating Golem. During the Old One's Army event, Etherian Mana can be collected, which allows the placement of multiple Lightning Auras that remain permanently until the event is over. Etherian Mana cannot be used outside the event. These weapons cannot be used outside of the Old One's Army event until the event has been successfully completed. Lightning Aura sentries are boosted by the Monk armor and Shinobi Infiltrator armor set bonuses, which increase their attack rate and allow them to deal critical hits. These weapons will have a fixed 1/6 (16.67%) (Monk armor) or 1/4 (25%) (Shinobi Infiltrator armor) chance to deal critical strike. This critical strike is determined separately from the summon tag critical chance (from whips), meaning that these two critical strike chances are two independent events instead of additive values (see Notes for exact numbers). The Shinobi Infiltrator armor also increases the size of the Lightning Aura's circle. Their best modifier is generally Fabled. However, if using whips, the Rod's best modifier is Ballistic if the player's summon damage bonuses do not reach 110%.

Explosive Trap Rod.name: Explosive Trap Rod
Explosive Trap Rod.tooltip: The Explosive Trap Rod, Cane, and Staff are special sentry summon weapons that summon their respective sentries. Each Explosive Trap sentry causes an explosion when enemies are nearby. Explosive Traps do not disappear when exploding, and will remain until its duration has expired or when the Old One's Army event ends. The higher the tier, the more damage the Explosive Traps deal. The Rod is sold by the Tavernkeep for 5 Defender Medals. The Cane is sold for 15 Defender Medals after defeating one mechanical boss. The Staff is sold for 60 Defender Medals after defeating Golem. During the Old One's Army event, Etherian Mana can be collected, which allows the placement of multiple Explosive Traps that remain permanently until the event is over. Etherian Mana cannot be used outside the event. These weapons cannot be used outside of the Old One's Army event until the event has been successfully completed. Explosive Trap sentries are boosted by the Huntress armor and Red Riding armor set bonuses, which increase their fire rates and cause them to inflict the Oiled debuff on struck enemies for 4–8.5 seconds. Their best modifier is Fabled. However, if the player's summon damage bonuses reach 95% (including whip bonuses) or 20.5% (excluding whip bonuses), the Explosive Trap Staff's best modifier becomes Ruthless.

Sleepy Octopod.name: Sleepy Octopod
Sleepy Octopod.tooltip: The Sleepy Octopod is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss melee weapon that is dropped by Ogres during the Old One's Army event, with a 1/10 (10%) / 1/5 (20%) chance during Tier 2, and a 1/20 (5%) chance during Tier 3. When used, it is swung continuously in a 360° radius around the player. After swinging for 0.7 seconds, a large shockwave occurs, dealing 300% of the weapon's damage (150 base damage) with an additional 25% critical hit chance. However, the explosion does not infict knockback. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Ghastly Glaive.name: Ghastly Glaive
Ghastly Glaive.tooltip: The Ghastly Glaive is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss spear that is dropped by Ogres during the Old One's Army event, with a 1/10 (10%) chance / 1/5 (20%) chance during Tier 2, and a 1/20 (5%) chance during Tier 3. Unlike any other spear, it is thrust in a curved motion. Upon striking an enemy, a yellow ghast projectile appears next to a random nearby enemy and flies in a straight line through it for 1 second before dissipating. The ghast projectile pierces enemies infinitely and deals the weapon's full damage, but does not inflict knockback. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Etherian Goblin Bomber Banner.name: Etherian Goblin Bomber Banner
Etherian Goblin Bomber Banner.tooltip: Enemy banners are functional furniture items that can be placed on the underside of blocks and platforms. They are obtained by killing most enemies and a few critters. When placed, enemy banners provide a Banner buff to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the banner. The buff grants players +50%/+100% damage inflicted with all damage to the corresponding enemy and −25%/−50% damage taken from attacks by the enemy. The banners of Old One's Army enemies will apply a weaker banner buff to the respective enemy, granting the players +10%/+20% damage inflicted and −8.33% / −16.67% damage taken. Multiple banners of the same type will not grant stacked buffs. Multiple different banner types in the vicinity will, however, all take effect and consolidate into a single buff icon. There are a total of 286 obtainable enemy banners: 115 in pre-Hardmode, 171 in Hardmode. Out of these, 118 belong to event enemies (28 in pre-Hardmode and 90 in Hardmode). In addition, there are 6 unobtainable enemy banners.
