Tome of Infinite Wisdom.name: Tome of Infinite Wisdom
Tome of Infinite Wisdom.tooltip: The Tome of Infinite Wisdom is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss wand that possesses two different modes of attack. When used with ⚒ Use / Attack, it fires bursts of four high-velocity pages that dissipate upon contact with enemies or blocks. When used with ⚷ Open / Activate, it summons a large, high-velocity tornado that deals 175% of the weapon's damage (63 damage), pierces infinite enemies, travels along blocks and through one-block low roofs, and dissipates after a duration of four seconds or upon being stopped by a wall of solid blocks. The Tome of Infinite Wisdom is dropped by Ogres during the Old One's Army event, with a 1/10 (10%) / 1/5 (20%) chance during Tier 2, and a 1/20 (5%) chance during Tier 3. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Phantom Phoenix.name: Phantom Phoenix
Phantom Phoenix.tooltip: The Phantom Phoenix is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss bow. When used, it fires a slight spread of two arrows, alongside a large Phoenix projectile on every third use. The weapon only consumes 1 arrow per use, and its use time is increased by 50% after firing a Phoenix projectile (base use time of 27 (Average)) but returns to normal after firing arrows. The Phoenix projectile deals 200% of the weapon's damage (74 base damage when using Wooden Arrows) and 100% of its knockback (base knockback of 4 (Weak) when using Wooden Arrows), inflicts the Hellfire debuff for 8 seconds and pierces infinitely, but loses 5% of its damage per hit. The Phoenix explodes after traveling for 2 seconds or upon colliding with blocks and liquids, dealing damage within a 6×6-tile rectangular area centered around the point of impact. The Phantom Phoenix also converts Wooden Arrows into Flaming Arrows, without increasing their damage. The Phantom Phoenix is dropped by Ogres during the Old One's Army event, with a 1/10 (10%) / 1/5 (20%) chance during Tier 2, and a 1/20 (5%) chance during Tier 3. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Gato Egg.name: Gato Egg
Gato Egg.tooltip: The Gato Egg is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Propeller Gato that follows the player. The Gato Egg is dropped by Dark Mages during the Old One's Army event, with a 1/6 (16.67%) / 1/4 (25%) chance during Tier 1, and a 1/12 (8.33%) chance during Tier 3.

Creeper Egg.name: Creeper Egg
Creeper Egg.tooltip: The Creeper Egg is a Hardmode light pet-summoning item that spawns a Flickerwick to follow the player around. When active, it is similar to the Wisp in a Bottle, where it provides light wherever the player goes. The summoned Flickerwick has the same movement speed as the player, and cannot be left behind easily. The Creeper Egg is dropped by Ogres during the Old One's Army event, with a 1/5 (20%) / 1/4 (25%) chance during Tier 2, and a 1/10 (10%) chance during Tier 3. While equipped, light is produced not only around the pet, but also around the player.

Dragon Egg.name: Dragon Egg
Dragon Egg.tooltip: The Dragon Egg is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Hoardagron that follows the player. The Dragon Egg is dropped by Dark Mages during the Old One's Army event, with a 1/6 (16.67%) / 1/4 (25%) chance during Tier 1, and a 1/12 (8.33%) chance during Tier 3.

Sky Dragon's Fury.name: Sky Dragon's Fury
Sky Dragon's Fury.tooltip: The Sky Dragon's Fury is a Hardmode, post-Golem melee weapon that possesses two different modes of attack. When pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button while held, the Sky Dragon's Fury spins in a 360° radius around the player, dealing damage and emitting visual trails of blue energy. When pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button while held, the Sky Dragon's Fury performs an alternate attack: it swings once towards the cursor, firing three blue energy orbs at a spreading 45° angle during the swing. The energy orbs burst into damaging Electrospheres after traveling for 0.25 seconds or upon contact with enemies or blocks. The Electrospheres continuously damage entities within radius, and last for a random duration between 1 second and 2.5 seconds before dissipating. The Sky Dragon's Fury itself during this attack, the energy orbs, and the Electrospheres all deal 50% of the weapon's damage (70 base damage). The Sky Dragon's Fury has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Betsy during Tier 3 of the Old One's Army event. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Aerial Bane.name: Aerial Bane
Aerial Bane.tooltip: The Aerial Bane is a Hardmode, post-Golem bow that has a 1/4 (25%) of being dropped from Betsy during Tier 3 of the Old One's Army event. When used, it converts any type of arrow into Aerial Bane arrows. The Aerial Bane fires a volley of six arrows per use, which travel in a sharp arc. Upon hitting an enemy, each arrow splits into five separate arrows, which are spread downwards. All arrows explode upon impact with enemies and blocks and deal 150% of the weapon's damage (64 base damage when using Wooden Arrows) against airborne enemies (i.e. enemies are considered airborne if the arrow's point of impact with them is more than 11 tiles above solid blocks). The Aerial Bane also has a base 7% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Treasure Bag (Betsy).name: Treasure Bag (Betsy)
Treasure Bag (Betsy).tooltip: Treasure Bags are consumable grab bag-like items obtained in Expert Mode and Master Mode as a reward for defeating bosses. The contents and appearance of Treasure Bags depend on the boss it comes from, and are opened by using either ⚷ Open / Activate while inside the inventory, or ⚒ Use / Attack when selected in the hotbar. They emit light and have a special effect around them when dropped, making them easier to spot. In multiplayer, each player that deals damage to the boss receives one Treasure Bag upon defeating it. Treasure Bags are client-side and will despawn upon exiting the world. See Notes for details. Each Treasure Bag contains the boss's usual drops from Classic Mode, along with one Expert Mode-exclusive item (highlighted items below) – with the exception of the Lunatic Cultist, Dark Mage, Ogre, and Betsy, who do not provide an Expert Mode-exclusive item. Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses additionally have a 1/16 (6.25%) chance to contain one random set of developer items (with the exception of Queen Slime). Expert Mode-exclusive items all have the  rarity, with the exception of developer items, which have the  rarity.

Betsy Mask.name: Betsy Mask
Betsy Mask.tooltip: Masks are vanity items dropped by all non-event bosses, as well as those from the Old One's Army(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). They are worn in the social head slot. Each boss has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance to drop its own mask in all difficulties, with the following exceptions: The Skeletron Mask has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to drop from Skeletron's Treasure Bag. The Dark Mage Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 1) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Dark Mage. The Ogre Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 2) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Ogre.

Dark Mage Mask.name: Dark Mage Mask
Dark Mage Mask.tooltip: Masks are vanity items dropped by all non-event bosses, as well as those from the Old One's Army(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). They are worn in the social head slot. The Ogre Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 2) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Ogre.

Ogre Mask.name: Ogre Mask
Ogre Mask.tooltip: Masks are vanity items dropped by all non-event bosses, as well as those from the Old One's Army(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). They are worn in the social head slot. Betsy Trophy.name: Betsy Trophy
Betsy Trophy.tooltip: Trophies are decorative furniture items which usually have a 1/10 (10%) chance to be dropped from most bosses. While they can be considered the "boss version of banners", they are purely cosmetic and do not provide any bonuses. Some trophies can only be rewarded by the Angler for completing fishing quests. In total, there are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 33 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 24 trophies.

Music Box (Old One's Army).name: Music Box (Old One's Army)
Music Box (Old One's Army).tooltip: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End), which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 Gold after defeating the Moon Lord. A recorded Music Box can be played back in one of two ways: Equipping it as an accessory. Placing it as furniture and activating it, either by the ⚷ Open / Activate button or with wires. Recorded Music Boxes can be reverted into blank ones through Shimmer transmutation. There are 101 different Music Boxes available.

Betsy's Wrath.name: Betsy's Wrath
Betsy's Wrath.tooltip: Betsy's Wrath is a Hardmode, post-Golem wand that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Betsy during Tier 3 of the Old One's Army event. When used, it fires three fireballs that travel in arcs. The fireballs explode upon impact with an enemy or a block and inflict the Betsy's Curse debuff, which adds 40 armor penetration against affected entities for 10 seconds. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Valhalla Knight's Helm.name: Valhalla Knight's Helm
Valhalla Knight's Helm.tooltip: Valhalla Knight armor is a Hardmode, post-Golem melee/summoner armor set consisting of the Valhalla Knight's Helm, Valhalla Knight's Breastplate, and Valhalla Knight's Greaves. The set can be purchased from the Tavernkeep for a total of 150 Defender Medals. The Valhalla Knight armor can be considered a direct upgrade of the Squire armor. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +68 defense +10% melee damage +20% melee critical strike chance +60% summon damage +3 sentry slots +20% movement speed +4 HP/second health regeneration Ballista sentry summons have increased projectile velocity, greatly increased fire rate (from 3.1 seconds to 2.1 seconds), and increased pierce (3 to 6). Upon taking damage, grants the Ballista Panic! buff for 5 seconds, increasing the fire rate of all Ballista sentries summoned by the player (from 2.1 seconds to 0.93 seconds).

Valhalla Knight's Breastplate.name: Valhalla Knight's Breastplate

Upon taking damage, grants the Ballista Panic! buff for 5 seconds, increasing the fire rate of all Ballista sentries summoned by the player (from 2.1 seconds to 0.93 seconds).

Dark Artist's Hat.name: Dark Artist's Hat
Dark Artist's Hat.tooltip: Dark Artist armor is a Hardmode, post-Golem mage/summoner armor set consisting of the Dark Artist's Hat, Dark Artist's Robes, and Dark Artist's Leggings. The set can be purchased from the Tavernkeep for a total of 150 Defender Medals. The Dark Artist armor can be considered a direct upgrade of the Apprentice armor. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +42 defense +25% magic damage +25% magic critical strike chance +15% mana cost reduction +60% summon damage +3 sentry slots +20% movement speed Flameburst sentry summons have 50% increased attack range (84 tiles), 40% increased projectile velocity, a significantly increased field of view, and increased projectile explosion radius (from a 6×6 to 13×13-tile rectangle). The Phantom Phoenix's Phoenix projectile explosion radius is increased from a 6×6 to 13×13-tile rectangle.

Dark Artist's Robes.name: Dark Artist's Robes

The Phantom Phoenix's Phoenix projectile explosion radius is increased from a 6×6 to 13×13-tile rectangle.

Red Riding Hood.name: Red Riding Hood
Red Riding Hood.tooltip: Red Riding armor is a Hardmode, post-Golem ranged/summoner armor set consisting of the Red Riding Hood, Red Riding Dress, and Red Riding Leggings. The set can be purchased from the Tavernkeep for a total of 150 Defender Medals. The Red Riding armor can be considered a direct upgrade of the Huntress armor. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +48 defense +25% ranged damage +20% ranged critical strike chance +20% ammo conservation +60% summon damage +3 sentry slots +20% movement speed Explosive Trap sentry summons have greatly increased fire rate and inflict the Oiled debuff, which causes enemies to take extra damage while afflicted with a fire debuff.

Red Riding Dress.tooltip: Red Riding armor is a Hardmode, post-Golem ranged/summoner armor set consisting of the Red Riding Hood, Red Riding Dress, and Red Riding Leggings. Shinobi Infiltrator's Helmet.name: Shinobi Infiltrator's Helmet
Shinobi Infiltrator's Helmet.tooltip: Shinobi Infiltrator armor is a Hardmode, post-Golem melee/summoner armor set consisting of the Shinobi Infiltrator's Helmet, Shinobi Infiltrator's Torso, and Shinobi Infiltrator's Pants. The set can be purchased from the Tavernkeep for a total of 150 Defender Medals. The Shinobi Infiltrator armor can be considered a direct upgrade of the Monk armor. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +54 defense +20% melee damage +25% melee critical strike chance +20% melee speed +60% summon damage +3 sentry slots +30% movement speed Lightning Aura sentry summons have increased attack rate, can deal critical hits with a fixed 1/4 (25%) chance, and their radius is increased by 4 tiles.

Shinobi Infiltrator's Torso.tooltip: Shinobi Infiltrator armor is a Hardmode, post-Golem melee/summoner armor set consisting of the Shinobi Infiltrator's Helmet, Shinobi Infiltrator's Torso, and Shinobi Infiltrator's Pants. Shinobi Infiltrator's Pants.name: Shinobi Infiltrator's Pants
Shinobi Infiltrator's Pants.tooltip: Shinobi Infiltrator armor is a Hardmode, post-Golem melee/summoner armor set consisting of the Shinobi Infiltrator's Helmet, Shinobi Infiltrator's Torso, and Shinobi Infiltrator's Pants. Betsy's Wings.name: Betsy's Wings
Betsy's Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Crystal Chest.name: Crystal Chest
Crystal Chest.tooltip: Chests are a type of furniture functioning as storage items. They are accessed using ⚷ Open / Activate and can store up to 40 item stacks in rows of  10×4 /   8×5. In addition to many being craftable, a number of Chests are placed in random locations during world generation. The loot contained in these Chests is determined during world generation, and will not change if the world enters Hardmode. Chests cannot be broken with items inside (the blocks a filled Chest is placed on would also have this trait). However, the Block Swap feature allows the player to change the type of a Chest without having to destroy it. Some types of Chests can be locked by the player using a Chest Lock. When doing so, they will require a key to open again. There are 23 varieties of naturally-occurring Chests (12 of which cannot be crafted), 53 that can only be crafted, and 1 purchasable Chest, for a total of 77 Chest types.

Golden Chest.name: Golden Chest
Golden Chest.tooltip: Chests are a type of furniture functioning as storage items. They are accessed using ⚷ Open / Activate and can store up to 40 item stacks in rows of  10×4 /   8×5. In addition to many being craftable, a number of Chests are placed in random locations during world generation. The loot contained in these Chests is determined during world generation, and will not change if the world enters Hardmode. Chests cannot be broken with items inside (the blocks a filled Chest is placed on would also have this trait). However, the Block Swap feature allows the player to change the type of a Chest without having to destroy it. Some types of Chests can be locked by the player using a Chest Lock. When doing so, they will require a key to open again. There are 23 varieties of naturally-occurring Chests (12 of which cannot be crafted), 53 that can only be crafted, and 1 purchasable Chest, for a total of 77 Chest types.

Trapped Crystal Chest.name: Trapped Crystal Chest
Trapped Crystal Chest.tooltip: A Trapped Chest is a mechanical item that has the appearance of a normal chest. It cannot be used for storage, as it does not have any storage slots. When it is opened, it emits a signal and can be connected with wire. Any chest can be crafted into a Trapped Chest at the Heavy Assembler with the desired chest and 10 wire. The Trapped Chest can be sold for 1 Silver.

Trapped Golden Chest.name: Trapped Golden Chest
Trapped Golden Chest.tooltip: A Trapped Chest is a mechanical item that has the appearance of a normal chest. It cannot be used for storage, as it does not have any storage slots. When it is opened, it emits a signal and can be connected with wire. Any chest can be crafted into a Trapped Chest at the Heavy Assembler with the desired chest and 10 wire. The Trapped Chest can be sold for 1 Silver.

Crystal Door.name: Crystal Door
Crystal Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Crystal Chair.name: Crystal Chair
Crystal Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Crystal Candle.name: Crystal Candle
Crystal Candle.tooltip: Candles are a type of furniture and light source. Candles can only be placed on flat-surface items. Candles will produce light underwater if placed and can be toggled on and off with ⚷ Open / Activate and by mechanisms. Certain types of candles provide buffs or debuffs. The Water Candle is a special type of candle found in Dungeons which increases enemy spawn rates by 33% and the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50% when placed or held. The Peace Candle reduces spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%, in contrast to the Water Candle. The Shadow Candle(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns in the area. For Water Candles and Peace Candles, multiple candles cannot stack, even if one is placed and the other is held.

Crystal Lantern.name: Crystal Lantern
Crystal Lantern.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Crystal Lamp.name: Crystal Lamp
Crystal Lamp.tooltip: Lamps are a type of furniture and light source. They also count as valid house lighting and can be toggled on and off by mechanisms. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 59 types of craftable Lamps, three types that are found in the Dungeon (Green, Blue, or Pink Dungeon Lamp), one found in Underworld houses (Obsidian Lamp), and one that can be dropped during a Pirate Invasion (Golden Lamp). Most lamps are dislodged by liquids, but Obsidian Lamp and Ash Wood Lamp are not dislodged by Lava. The Tiki Torch shares its Tile ID with the rest of these Lamps. Also see Lamp Post ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions) which does not count as valid House lighting.)

Crystal Candelabra.name: Crystal Candelabra
Crystal Candelabra.tooltip: Candelabras are a type of furniture and light source that emits light when placed on a flat surface such as blocks, platforms, and flat furniture items. It is not destroyed by water. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 23 /  12 craftable and 5 looted variations of the Candelabra.

Crystal Chandelier.name: Crystal Chandelier
Crystal Chandelier.tooltip: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers come in many varieties which differ only in appearance and sell value. All chandeliers can be picked up using a pickaxe, drill, or explosives. Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.

Crystal Bathtub.name: Crystal Bathtub
Crystal Bathtub.tooltip: Bathtubs are furniture items which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 65 / (Old-gen console version) 16 / (3DS version) 11 Bathtub types, all being functionally identical but presenting different appearances.

Crystal Sink.name: Crystal Sink
Crystal Sink.tooltip: The Sink is a type of furniture item and crafting station. Like Fountains, it can be used to craft items that require water as a crafting station. There is a total of 66 Sink types, all being functionally identical.

Crystal Bed.name: Crystal Bed
Crystal Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration. Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 craftable Beds and 5 that can be acquired from the environment. All Beds are functionally identical and differ only in appearance.

Crystal Clock.name: Crystal Clock
Crystal Clock.tooltip: Grandfather Clocks are furniture items which provide information about the in-game time. If a player is nearby a Grandfather Clock (about 80 tiles horizontally and 50 tiles vertically), the time is displayed on the right side of the screen, underneath the minimap. The time is rounded to the last hour, similar to Tin and Copper Watches, but pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it will show precise time in minutes as a status message on the bottom left corner. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 21 /  5 craftable versions and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 5 / (Old-gen console version) 2 noncraftable (but still lootable) versions. The regular Grandfather Clock can rarely be found in Underground Cabins. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Sunplate Clock.name: Sunplate Clock
Sunplate Clock.tooltip: Grandfather Clocks are furniture items which provide information about the in-game time. If a player is nearby a Grandfather Clock (about 80 tiles horizontally and 50 tiles vertically), the time is displayed on the right side of the screen, underneath the minimap. The time is rounded to the last hour, similar to Tin and Copper Watches, but pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it will show precise time in minutes as a status message on the bottom left corner. Crystal Platform.name: Crystal Platform
Crystal Platform.tooltip: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Arkhalis' Lightwings.name: Arkhalis' Lightwings
Arkhalis' Lightwings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Celebration Mk2.name: Celebration Mk2
Celebration Mk2.tooltip: The Celebration Mk2 is a Hardmode launcher that has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord. When used, it consumes rockets and fires one of seven special rocket types, distinguished by color. The rockets are affected by gravity to varying extents and explode upon impact with blocks. Although their base damage, critical strike chance, and knockback are identical, they behave differently: The Celebration Mk2 also has a 1/2 (50%) chance not to consume ammunition. Its best modifier is Unreal, Godly or Demonic, as it does not benefit from attack speed and velocity modifiers.

Spider Bathtub.tooltip: Bathtubs are furniture items which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 65 / (Old-gen console version) 16 / (3DS version) 11 Bathtub types, all being functionally identical but presenting different appearances.

Spider Bed.name: Spider Bed
Spider Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration. Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 craftable Beds and 5 that can be acquired from the environment. All Beds are functionally identical and differ only in appearance.

Spider Candle.name: Spider Candle
Spider Candle.tooltip: Candles are a type of furniture and light source. Candles can only be placed on flat-surface items. Candles will produce light underwater if placed and can be toggled on and off with ⚷ Open / Activate and by mechanisms. Certain types of candles provide buffs or debuffs. The Water Candle is a special type of candle found in Dungeons which increases enemy spawn rates by 33% and the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50% when placed or held. The Peace Candle reduces spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%, in contrast to the Water Candle. The Shadow Candle(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns in the area. For Water Candles and Peace Candles, multiple candles cannot stack, even if one is placed and the other is held.

Spider Chair.name: Spider Chair
Spider Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Spider Chandelier.name: Spider Chandelier
Spider Chandelier.tooltip: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers come in many varieties which differ only in appearance and sell value. All chandeliers can be picked up using a pickaxe, drill, or explosives. Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.

Spider Chest.name: Spider Chest
Spider Chest.tooltip: Chests are a type of furniture functioning as storage items. They are accessed using ⚷ Open / Activate and can store up to 40 item stacks in rows of  10×4 /   8×5. In addition to many being craftable, a number of Chests are placed in random locations during world generation. The loot contained in these Chests is determined during world generation, and will not change if the world enters Hardmode. Chests cannot be broken with items inside (the blocks a filled Chest is placed on would also have this trait). However, the Block Swap feature allows the player to change the type of a Chest without having to destroy it. Some types of Chests can be locked by the player using a Chest Lock. When doing so, they will require a key to open again. There are 23 varieties of naturally-occurring Chests (12 of which cannot be crafted), 53 that can only be crafted, and 1 purchasable Chest, for a total of 77 Chest types.

Spider Door.name: Spider Door
Spider Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Spider Lamp.name: Spider Lamp
Spider Lamp.tooltip: Lamps are a type of furniture and light source. They also count as valid house lighting and can be toggled on and off by mechanisms. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 59 types of craftable Lamps, three types that are found in the Dungeon (Green, Blue, or Pink Dungeon Lamp), one found in Underworld houses (Obsidian Lamp), and one that can be dropped during a Pirate Invasion (Golden Lamp). Most lamps are dislodged by liquids, but Obsidian Lamp and Ash Wood Lamp are not dislodged by Lava. The Tiki Torch shares its Tile ID with the rest of these Lamps. Also see Lamp Post ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions) which does not count as valid House lighting.)

Spider Lantern.name: Spider Lantern
Spider Lantern.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Iron Brick.tooltip: Iron Brick is a type of Brick crafted from Iron Ore.

Iron Brick Wall.name: Iron Brick Wall
Iron Brick Wall.tooltip: Iron Brick Wall is a type of background wall.

Lead Brick.name: Lead Brick
Lead Brick.tooltip: Lead Brick is a type of Brick crafted from Lead Ore.

Lead Brick Wall.name: Lead Brick Wall
Lead Brick Wall.tooltip: Lead Brick Wall is a type of background wall.

Lesion Block.name: Lesion Block
Lesion Block.tooltip: The Lesion Block is a Hardmode block. It is used to craft Lesion furniture and Lesion Block Walls. Lesion Blocks will not spread the Corruption.

Lesion Block Wall.name: Lesion Block Wall
Lesion Block Wall.tooltip: The Lesion Block Wall is a type of background walls. Like most walls, they will stop enemy spawning, and can be used for NPC houses.

Lesion Platform.name: Lesion Platform
Lesion Platform.tooltip: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Lesion Bathtub.name: Lesion Bathtub
Lesion Bathtub.tooltip: Bathtubs are furniture items which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 65 / (Old-gen console version) 16 / (3DS version) 11 Bathtub types, all being functionally identical but presenting different appearances.

Lesion Bed.name: Lesion Bed
Lesion Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration. Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 craftable Beds and 5 that can be acquired from the environment. All Beds are functionally identical and differ only in appearance.

Lesion Bookcase.name: Lesion Bookcase
Lesion Bookcase.tooltip: Bookcases are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station used for the crafting of three Hardmode magic weapons (the Crystal Storm, Cursed Flames, and Golden Shower) as well as the Librarian furniture out of Librarian Blocks. Bookcases also fulfill a house's table requirement. There is a total of 65 types of Bookcases: 60 craftable Bookcases, and 5 looted from the environment: one from the Underworld, three from the Dungeon, and one from the Pirate Invasion. Some bookcases can also be found in Underground Cabins; their style follows the theme of the cabin where they are found.

Lesion Candelabra.name: Lesion Candelabra
Lesion Candelabra.tooltip: Candelabras are a type of furniture and light source that emits light when placed on a flat surface such as blocks, platforms, and flat furniture items. It is not destroyed by water. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 23 /  12 craftable and 5 looted variations of the Candelabra.

Lesion Candle.name: Lesion Candle
Lesion Candle.tooltip: Candles are a type of furniture and light source. Candles can only be placed on flat-surface items. Candles will produce light underwater if placed and can be toggled on and off with ⚷ Open / Activate and by mechanisms. Certain types of candles provide buffs or debuffs. The Water Candle is a special type of candle found in Dungeons which increases enemy spawn rates by 33% and the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50% when placed or held. The Peace Candle reduces spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%, in contrast to the Water Candle. The Shadow Candle(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns in the area. For Water Candles and Peace Candles, multiple candles cannot stack, even if one is placed and the other is held.

Lesion Chair.name: Lesion Chair
Lesion Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Lesion Chandelier.name: Lesion Chandelier
Lesion Chandelier.tooltip: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers come in many varieties which differ only in appearance and sell value. All chandeliers can be picked up using a pickaxe, drill, or explosives. Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.

Lesion Chest.name: Lesion Chest
Lesion Chest.tooltip: Chests are a type of furniture functioning as storage items. They are accessed using ⚷ Open / Activate and can store up to 40 item stacks in rows of  10×4 /   8×5. In addition to many being craftable, a number of Chests are placed in random locations during world generation. The loot contained in these Chests is determined during world generation, and will not change if the world enters Hardmode. Chests cannot be broken with items inside (the blocks a filled Chest is placed on would also have this trait). However, the Block Swap feature allows the player to change the type of a Chest without having to destroy it. Some types of Chests can be locked by the player using a Chest Lock. When doing so, they will require a key to open again. There are 23 varieties of naturally-occurring Chests (12 of which cannot be crafted), 53 that can only be crafted, and 1 purchasable Chest, for a total of 77 Chest types.

Lesion Clock.name: Lesion Clock
Lesion Clock.tooltip: Grandfather Clocks are furniture items which provide information about the in-game time. If a player is nearby a Grandfather Clock (about 80 tiles horizontally and 50 tiles vertically), the time is displayed on the right side of the screen, underneath the minimap. The time is rounded to the last hour, similar to Tin and Copper Watches, but pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it will show precise time in minutes as a status message on the bottom left corner. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 21 /  5 craftable versions and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 5 / (Old-gen console version) 2 noncraftable (but still lootable) versions. The regular Grandfather Clock can rarely be found in Underground Cabins. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Lesion Door.name: Lesion Door
Lesion Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Lesion Dresser.name: Lesion Dresser
Lesion Dresser.tooltip: Dressers are a type of flat-surface furniture (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and storage item. They also fulfill house's table requirement. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 19 / (3DS version) 5 craftable versions, and (Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) 5 noncraftable versions which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Lesion Lamp.name: Lesion Lamp
Lesion Lamp.tooltip: Lamps are a type of furniture and light source. They also count as valid house lighting and can be toggled on and off by mechanisms. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 59 types of craftable Lamps, three types that are found in the Dungeon (Green, Blue, or Pink Dungeon Lamp), one found in Underworld houses (Obsidian Lamp), and one that can be dropped during a Pirate Invasion (Golden Lamp). Most lamps are dislodged by liquids, but Obsidian Lamp and Ash Wood Lamp are not dislodged by Lava. The Tiki Torch shares its Tile ID with the rest of these Lamps. Also see Lamp Post ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions) which does not count as valid House lighting.)

Lesion Lantern.name: Lesion Lantern
Lesion Lantern.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Lesion Piano.name: Lesion Piano
Lesion Piano.tooltip: Pianos are a type of furniture which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 15 /  10 craftable Pianos, and 5 non-craftable Pianos that can be found in the Dungeon, Ruined Houses, and Pirate Invasion event. Some Pianos can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin that they are found in.

Lesion Sink.name: Lesion Sink
Lesion Sink.tooltip: The Sink is a type of furniture item and crafting station. Like Fountains, it can be used to craft items that require water as a crafting station. There is a total of 66 Sink types, all being functionally identical.

Lesion Sofa.name: Lesion Sofa
Lesion Sofa.tooltip: Sofas are furniture items which fulfill a house's chair requirement. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Players can sit in sofas by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Players can choose to sit on the left, middle, or right positions, and thus up to 3 players can sit on a sofa at a time. Sitting on sofas gives a boost to health regeneration, similar to chairs and beds. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Sofa will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 21 craftable sofas and 5 noncraftable sofas. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Lesion Table.name: Lesion Table
Lesion Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Lesion Work Bench.name: Lesion Work Bench
Lesion Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Trapped Lesion Chest.name: Trapped Lesion Chest
Trapped Lesion Chest.tooltip: A Trapped Chest is a mechanical item that has the appearance of a normal chest. It cannot be used for storage, as it does not have any storage slots. When it is opened, it emits a signal and can be connected with wire. Any chest can be crafted into a Trapped Chest at the Heavy Assembler with the desired chest and 10 wire. The Trapped Chest can be sold for 1 Silver.

Hat Rack.name: Hat Rack
Hat Rack.tooltip: The Hat Rack is a decorative furniture item that can be used to display up to two helmet-slot armor and vanity items, as well as dyes. Items can be placed on a Hat Rack by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on it, which opens a small set of inventory-like slots beneath the player's main inventory. There are two slots for two helmets, in addition to an associated dye slot underneath each one. Placing items in these slots immediately displays them on the Hat Rack. Items placed in the left slot are displayed on the upper part of the Hat Rack, while items placed in the right slot are displayed on the lower part. Items cannot be displayed on the middle, top part.

Pearlwood Crate.name: Pearlwood Crate
Pearlwood Crate.tooltip: The Pearlwood Crate is a Hardmode crate that can be obtained by fishing in any biome, at any height. It is the lowest tier of standard crate, having the least value if sold directly. Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Wooden Crate.

Mythril Crate.name: Mythril Crate
Mythril Crate.tooltip: The Mythril Crate is a Hardmode crate that can be obtained by fishing in any biome, at any height. It is the middle tier of standard crate. Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Iron Crate.

Titanium Crate.name: Titanium Crate
Titanium Crate.tooltip: The Titanium Crate is a Hardmode crate that can be obtained by fishing in any biome, at any layer. It is the highest tier of standard crate, having the greatest value if sold directly. Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Golden Crate.

Defiled Crate.name: Defiled Crate
Defiled Crate.tooltip: The Defiled Crate is a Hardmode crate that can only be fished in The Corruption. Defiled Crates contain items found in standard crates, and additionally always drop an item normally obtained by destroying a Shadow Orb. Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Corrupt Crate.

Hematic Crate.name: Hematic Crate
Hematic Crate.tooltip: The Hematic Crate is a Hardmode crate that can only be obtained by fishing in The Crimson. Hematic Crates contain items found in standard crates, and additionally always drop an item normally obtained by breaking a Crimson Heart. Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Crimson Crate.

Stockade Crate.name: Stockade Crate
Stockade Crate.tooltip: The Stockade Crate is a Hardmode crate that can only be fished in the Dungeon after Skeletron has been defeated. Opening Stockade or Dungeon Crates is the only way to obtain the Golden Lock Box, and therefore any Dungeon-exclusive items normally found in Locked Gold Chests, once the Dungeon has been fully looted. Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Dungeon Crate.

Azure Crate.name: Azure Crate
Azure Crate.tooltip: The Azure Crate is a Hardmode crate that can only be fished in Space, e.g. in Floating Lakes. It contains items found in standard crates and always contains an item normally found in Skyware Chests (with the exception of the Sky Mill). Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Sky Crate.

Divine Crate.name: Divine Crate
Divine Crate.tooltip: The Divine Crate is a Hardmode crate that can only be fished in The Hallow. Divine Crates contain items found in standard crates, and additionally have a chance to drop Crystal Shards or Souls of Light. Its pre-Hardmode equivalent is the Hallowed Crate, and its Corruption and Crimson variants are the Defiled Crate and Hematic Crate, respectively.

Bramble Crate.name: Bramble Crate
Bramble Crate.tooltip: The Bramble Crate is a Hardmode crate that can only be fished in the Jungle. Bramble Crates contain items found in standard crates, and they always contain an item normally found in Ivy Chests within Jungle Shrines. Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Jungle Crate.

Dead Man's Chest.name: Dead Man's Chest
Dead Man's Chest.tooltip: The Dead Man's Chest is a naturally-generated Chest rigged with a large variety of traps in order to kill the player upon opening it. This setup usually includes 3–5 Boulder traps, 2–6 Dart Traps, and 0–3 Explosives, with a possibility of 1–2 Geysers if generated at depths in which lava can spawn naturally. The Boulder traps are set up above the chest, the Dart Traps are set up horizontally, and the Explosives are hidden underneath. Dead Man's Chests will always generate alone, and never in an Underground Cabin. The Dead Man's Chest will contain standard Gold Chest loot based on where it is found, as well as having a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to contain the Dead Man's Sweater.

Golf Ball.name: Golf Ball
Golf Ball.tooltip: Golf Balls are accessories that are used in golf and come in a variety of colors. The plain, white Golf Ball can be purchased from the Golfer for 1 Gold and can be used for crafting the colored variants. The Golf Ball items are not required to play golf, as pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on an empty Golf Tee will always create a Golf Ball projectile. Their main purposes are: Changing the color of this projectile, which is a purely visual effect. The Golf Ball item does not need to be equipped for this, having it in the inventory is sufficient. Manually placing Golf Ball projectiles anywhere in the world, even outside of Golf Tees. This is done by pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button while the Golf Ball item is selected. The item will not be consumed, it can be reused to place an unlimited number of Golf Ball projectiles. Golf Ball projectiles can be hit with a Golf Club and despawn when entering a Golf Cup.

Amphibian Boots.name: Amphibian Boots
Amphibian Boots.tooltip: The Amphibian Boots are an accessory crafted by combining the Sailfish Boots and Frog Leg at a Tinkerer's Workshop. It provides the benefits of both. Equipping it has the following effects: Increases the player's maximum movement speed to 22.5 tiles/second (31 mph) Allows auto-jumping Increases the maximum safe falling distance by 10 tiles Increases jump speed by 1.6

Arcane Flower.name: Arcane Flower
Arcane Flower.tooltip: The Arcane Flower is a Hardmode accessory that grants the following effects while equipped: +5% magic damage +5% magic critical strike chance −400 aggro −8% mana cost Automatically consumes mana potions in the player's inventory or opened Void Bag when mana is depleted.

Berserker's Glove.name: Berserker's Glove
Berserker's Glove.tooltip: The Berserker's Glove is a Hardmode accessory. While equipped, it grants the following effects: +8 defense +400 aggro Enables autoswing for all melee weapons and whips +12% melee speed ×2 knockback for melee weapons +10% size for melee weapons

Fairy Boots.name: Fairy Boots
Fairy Boots.tooltip: Fairy Boots are an accessory that are made from the Spectre Boots and Flower Boots at a Tinkerer's Workshop. They combine both effects into one pair of boots.

Frog Flipper.name: Frog Flipper
Frog Flipper.tooltip: The Frog Flipper is an accessory crafted from a Frog Leg and a Flipper. It combines the abilities of these two items, increasing the player's jump speed and safe falling distance, allowing auto-jump, and giving the player the ability to swim.

Frog Gear.name: Frog Gear
Frog Gear.tooltip: The Frog Gear is an accessory that combines the effects of the Frog Leg, Flipper, and Tiger Climbing Gear.

Frog Webbing.name: Frog Webbing
Frog Webbing.tooltip: The Frog Webbing is an accessory crafted from a Frog Leg and a Tiger Climbing Gear. It combines the abilities of these two items, increasing the player's jump speed and safe falling distance, allowing auto-jump, and granting enhanced mobility on walls.

Frozen Shield.name: Frozen Shield
Frozen Shield.tooltip: The Frozen Shield is a Hardmode, post-Plantera shield that combines the functionalities of the Paladin's Shield and the Frozen Turtle Shell. While equipped, it grants the following effects: +6 defense Immunity to knockback While the wearer's health is above 25%, it grants all nearby players on their team (excluding themselves) the Paladin's Shield buff, which provides 25% damage reduction and redirects that damage to the wearer. While the wearer's health is at or below 50%, it grants the wearer +25% damage reduction.

Hero Shield.name: Hero Shield
Hero Shield.tooltip: The Hero Shield is a Hardmode post-Plantera shield accessory that redirects 25% of damage from players on the same team while above 25% health, similar to the effect of the Paladin's Shield. Furthermore, it increases defense by 10, increases aggro by 400, and grants immunity to knockback.

Magma Skull.name: Magma Skull
Magma Skull.tooltip: The Magma Skull is a pre-Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Burning debuff. It also grants immunity to lava for 7 seconds.

Magnet Flower.name: Magnet Flower
Magnet Flower.tooltip: The Magnet Flower is a pre-Hardmode accessory that grants the following effects while equipped: −8% mana cost Automatically consumes mana potions in the player's inventory or opened Void Bag when mana is depleted. Increases the pickup range for Stars by 18.75 tiles.

Mana Cloak.name: Mana Cloak
Mana Cloak.tooltip: The Mana Cloak is a Hardmode accessory that grants the following effects while equipped: 8% reduced mana cost. Automatically consume mana potions from the player's inventory or open Void Bag when mana is depleted. Causes three stars to fall around the player upon taking damage. (See #Taking damage.) Causes one star to fall near enemies struck with a magic weapon, which then transform into a Mana Cloak Star power-up that is similar to Stars. (See #Dealing damage.)

Molten Quiver.name: Molten Quiver
Molten Quiver.tooltip: The Molten Quiver is a Hardmode accessory that converts Wooden Arrows fired by the player into Flaming Arrows. In addition, it has the same effects as the Magic Quiver.

Molten Skull Rose.name: Molten Skull Rose
Molten Skull Rose.tooltip: The Molten Skull Rose is a pre-Hardmode immunity accessory. It grants 7 seconds of immunity to lava, immunity to the Burning debuff, and reduces damage taken from lava.

Obsidian Skull Rose.name: Obsidian Skull Rose
Obsidian Skull Rose.tooltip: The Obsidian Skull Rose is a pre-Hardmode immunity accessory that grants immunity to the Burning debuff and reduced damage from lava.

Recon Scope.name: Recon Scope
Recon Scope.tooltip: The Recon Scope is a Hardmode, post-Golem accessory. It grants the following effects while equipped: +10% ranged damage +10% ranged critical strike chance The ability to "zoom", increasing view range while holding a bullet-firing gun by pressing and holding ⚷ Open / Activate and moving the cursor. –400 aggro

Stalker's Quiver.name: Stalker's Quiver
Stalker's Quiver.tooltip: The Stalker's Quiver is a Hardmode accessory that combines the effects of the Magic Quiver with the aggro-reducing effect of the Putrid Scent.

Stinger Necklace.name: Stinger Necklace
Stinger Necklace.tooltip: The Stinger Necklace is a pre-Hardmode accessory that is obtainable after defeating the Queen Bee. This item combines the Shark Tooth Necklace and the Honey Comb accessories, giving the player 5 armor penetration as well as releasing 1–3 / 1–4 bees when the wearer takes damage and granting the Honey buff for 5 seconds.

Ultrabright Helmet.name: Ultrabright Helmet
Ultrabright Helmet.tooltip: The Ultrabright Helmet is an armor piece for the helmet slot that combines the functionalities of the Mining Helmet and the Night Vision Helmet.

Apple.name: Apple
Apple.tooltip: The Apple is a food and fruit item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). It has a small chance of dropping when shaking a Forest tree.

Apple Pie Slice.name: Apple Pie Slice
Apple Pie Slice.tooltip: The Apple Pie Slice is an unimplemented item.

Apple Pie.name: Apple Pie
Apple Pie.tooltip: The Apple Pie is a Hardmode food item that grants the Exquisitely Stuffed buff when consumed. This lasts for 16 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Apple Pie has a 1/150 (0.67%) chance of being dropped by Illuminant Bats, Illuminant Slimes, and Chaos Elementals.
Apple Pie.drops_summary: Chaos Elemental (0.67%), Illuminant Bat (0.67%), Illuminant Slime (0.67%)

Banana Split.name: Banana Split
Banana Split.tooltip: The Banana Split is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Banana Split has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by Antlions, Antlion Chargers, and Antlion Swarmers.

BBQ Ribs.name: BBQ Ribs
BBQ Ribs.tooltip: The BBQ Ribs are a Hardmode food item that grant the Exquisitely Stuffed buff when consumed. This lasts for 24 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The BBQ Ribs have a 1/21 (4.76%) chance of being dropped by Skeleton Commandos, Skeleton Snipers, and Tactical Skeletons, and a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Paladins.

Bunny Stew.name: Bunny Stew
Bunny Stew.tooltip: The Bunny Stew is a food item crafted at the Cooking Pot. When consumed, it grants the Well Fed buff. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().

Burger.name: Burger
Burger.tooltip: The Burger is a food item that grants the Exquisitely Stuffed buff when consumed. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Burger has a 1/100 (1%) chance of being dropped by Crimeras and Eaters of Souls. Statue-spawned Eaters of Souls do not drop it, as it is a food item.

Chicken Nugget.name: Chicken Nugget
Chicken Nugget.tooltip: The Chicken Nugget is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 14 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Chicken Nugget has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by Harpies. Statue-spawned Harpies do not drop it, as it is a food item.

Chocolate Chip Cookie.name: Chocolate Chip Cookie
Chocolate Chip Cookie.tooltip: The Chocolate Chip Cookie is a Hardmode food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 20 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Chocolate Chip Cookie has a 1/75 (1.33%) chance of being dropped by Gastropods.

Cream Soda.name: Cream Soda
Cream Soda.tooltip: The Cream Soda is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 16 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Cream Soda has a 1/70 (1.43%) chance of being dropped by Cursed Skulls, and a 1/35 (2.86%) chance of being dropped by Giant Cursed Skulls.

Escargot.name: Escargot
Escargot.tooltip: Escargot is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().

Fried Egg.name: Fried Egg
Fried Egg.tooltip: The Fried Egg is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 14 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Fried Egg has a 1/30 (3.33%) chance of being dropped by Wall Creepers, Black Recluses, and Sand Poachers. Statue-spawned Wall Creepers do not drop it, as it is a food item.
Fried Egg.drops_summary: Black Recluse (3.33%), Sand Poacher (3.33%), Wall Creeper (3.33%)

Fries.name: Fries
Fries.tooltip: Fries are a food item that grant the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). Fries have a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by Flying Fish.

Golden Delight.name: Golden Delight
Golden Delight.tooltip: The Golden Delight is a food item that grants the Exquisitely Stuffed buff when consumed. This lasts for 48 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). It is crafted at the Cooking Pot with any gold critter or Golden Carp.

Grapes.name: Grapes
Grapes.tooltip: Grapes are a Hardmode food item that grant the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 16 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). Grapes have a 1/40 (2.5%) chance of being dropped by Derplings and Giant Flying Foxes.

Grilled Squirrel.name: Grilled Squirrel
Grilled Squirrel.tooltip: The Grilled Squirrel is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().

Hotdog.name: Hotdog

The Hotdog has a 1/30 (3.33%) chance of being dropped by Bone Serpents and Red Devils.

Ice Cream.name: Ice Cream

Ice Cream.drops_summary: Ice Bat (0.67%), Ice Slime (0.67%), Spiked Ice Slime (0.67%)

Seafood Dinner.tooltip: Fishing foods are consumable food items crafted from various fish caught during fishing . They grant either the Well Fed or Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed.

Molten Charm.name: Molten Charm
Molten Charm.tooltip: The Molten Charm is a pre-Hardmode immunity accessory that combines the effects of the Lava Charm and Obsidian Skull. When the Molten Charm is equipped and the player comes into contact with lava, a 7-second countdown begins, signified by a lava meter that displays over the player's head. It operates similarly to the Breath meter, but displays flame icons instead of bubbles. Lava immunity time is recharged gradually by exiting lava, the same way breathing time is recharged by exiting water (albeit much more slowly). The Molten Charm also grants immunity to the Burning debuff inflicted by contact with Meteorite, Hellstone, and Hellstone Brick. It does not grant immunity to other fire-based damage.

Golf Club (Iron).name: Golf Club (Iron)
Golf Club (Iron).tooltip: Golf Clubs are tools used in the golf minigame. There are four types of Golf Clubs, the Driver, Iron, Wedge, and Putter, which are each used to hit the Golf Ball a different horizontal and vertical distance. Special variants of Golf Clubs can be unlocked by achieving different golf scores. All upgrades are purely aesthetic, despite being more expensive as the tier increases. They do not harm enemies or critters.

Golf Cup.name: Golf Cup
Golf Cup.tooltip: The Golf Cup is a block and activation mechanism used in Golf.

Blue Flower Seeds.name: Blue Flower Seeds
Blue Flower Seeds.tooltip: Flower Seeds are seeds used to plant a random flower. They can all be purchased from the Dryad for 5 Silver each. Flower Seeds can only be planted on pure grass and mowed grass blocks (not on any other type of grass), in Clay Pots, in Planter Boxes, and in Rock Golem Heads. When used on a grass or mowed grass block, Flower Seeds cannot be planted if there is a background wall behind the block or on the tile above the block (with a few exceptions). However, it is possible to plant the seed and then place a wall behind it without breaking the plant.
