Lawn Mower.name: Lawn Mower
Lawn Mower.tooltip: The Lawn Mower is a tool that can be purchased from the Golfer for 1 Gold and mows normal and Hallowed grass. Mowed grass has a different texture, reduces enemy spawn chance by 10%, prevents grass plants (and dye plants) from growing, and allows Golf Balls to travel on top of it with unhindered movement while golfing. The Lawn Mower deals a fixed 8 classless damage to entities only while the player is moving forwards, is not in the air, and is not grappled. When it is used on grass other than normal and hallowed, it only removes weeds and flowers.

Crimstone Brick.name: Crimstone Brick
Crimstone Brick.tooltip: Crimstone Brick is a type of brick. Unlike its raw block counterpart, the Crimstone Block, it does not spread The Crimson, nor does it turn the area into a Crimson biome, thus making it a safe construction material for NPC houses and other structures. Its Corruption counterpart is Ebonstone Brick.

Smooth Sandstone.name: Smooth Sandstone
Smooth Sandstone.tooltip: Smooth Sandstone is a type of block crafted from Sandstone Blocks. It can be used to craft the Sandstone furniture set.

Crimstone Brick Wall.name: Crimstone Brick Wall
Crimstone Brick Wall.tooltip: The Crimstone Brick Wall is a placeable item that looks like a blood-stained brick wall.

Smooth Sandstone Wall.name: Smooth Sandstone Wall
Smooth Sandstone Wall.tooltip: The Smooth Sandstone Wall is a type of background wall crafted from Smooth Sandstone Blocks. It is the only Sandstone Wall type not to generate naturally.

Blood Moon Monolith.name: Blood Moon Monolith
Blood Moon Monolith.tooltip: Monoliths are furniture items that activate backgrounds and other screen effects normally seen during events or under other special circumstances. When placed, they can be toggled with the ⚷ Open / Activate button or via wire, like other mechanisms, providing their effects in a small area around them. Monoliths only cause modified visuals; they do not spawn any event enemies or bosses, and they do not change the music. They can also be equipped as vanity accessories, which enables their effect globally for the player. There are 11 different monoliths: the Vortex, Nebula, Stardust, Solar, and Void Monoliths can be crafted at an Ancient Manipulator, the Blood Moon Monolith has a 1/10 (10%) chance of being dropped by Dreadnautiluses, the Radio Thing has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to be dropped by Deerclops, the Aether Monolith can be obtained via dropping an Angel Statue into Shimmer, the CRT and Retro Monoliths are sold by the Cyborg for 25 Gold, and the Film Projector can be obtained as part of Heroicis' set by dropping a Platinum Coin into the Water of an Oasis. The Nebula, Solar, Stardust, and Vortex Monoliths mimic effects that normally surround the corresponding Celestial Pillar during the Lunar Events. The Blood Moon Monolith mimics the effects seen during a Blood Moon. The Void Monolith mimics the screen effects of the Moon Lord boss fight. The Radio Thing activates the same sepia filter of The Constant world seed. In The Constant seed, however, it instead deactivates the filter. The Aether Monolith mimics the screen effects of the Aether mini-biome. Unlike the other monoliths, the Aether Monolith has three states: One off state (which disables the Aether effect entirely in its area, even if it would normally be present due to Shimmer) and two on states – low, which acts as if the monolith were not present (allowing the Aether effect if enough Shimmer is nearby but not forcing it on), and high, which forces the Aether effect on. The CRT Monolith mimics the effect of an old-fashioned CRT TV. The Retro Monolith mimics the effect of an old two-color green and black monitor, like the original Gameboy. The Film Projector adds a black-and-white effect to the screen.

Dunerider Boots.name: Dunerider Boots
Dunerider Boots.tooltip: The Dunerider Boots are an accessory that can be found in Sandstone Chests in the top 4/7ths of the Underground Desert, and in Oasis Crates and Mirage Crates obtained from fishing in the Oasis. They grant the following effects while equipped: The ability to sprint, allowing the player to reach maximum running speed faster. The player will leave behind a visual trail of sand clouds as they sprint. Increased maximum movement speed to 31 mph (22.73 tiles/second). While moving on Sand, Sandstone, or Hardened Sand: +75% movement speed (to 54 mph (39.6 tiles/second)) +75% acceleration and deceleration (from 0.3 tiles/second² to 0.525 tiles/second² and from 0.75 tiles/second² to 1.3125 tiles/second², respectively)
Dunerider Boots.drops_summary: Mirage Crate (12.5%), Oasis Crate (12.5%), Sandstone Chest (25%)

Ancient Chisel.name: Ancient Chisel
Ancient Chisel.tooltip: The Ancient Chisel is a construction accessory that increases mining speed by 25%, similarly to a Mining Potion. It can be found in Sandstone Chests in the top 4/7ths of the Underground Desert and in Oasis Crates and Mirage Crates obtained from fishing in the Oasis.
Ancient Chisel.drops_summary: Mirage Crate (12.5%), Oasis Crate (12.5%), Sandstone Chest (25%)

Rain Song.name: Rain Song
Rain Song.tooltip: The Rain Song is a novelty instrument that has a 1/100 (1%) chance of being dropped by Flying Fish, which spawn during rain. When used, the player strums a chord depending on how far the cursor is from the player.

Skull Bow.name: Skull Bow
Skull Bow.tooltip: The Skull Bow is an unobtainable bow. Apart from standard bow behavior, it can convert Bone Arrows (ID 474) into Bone Arrows from the Marrow (ID 117). Its best modifier is Unreal.

Fossil Pickaxe.name: Fossil Pickaxe
Fossil Pickaxe.tooltip: The Fossil Pickaxe is a pre-Hardmode pickaxe. It can mine blocks up to Demonite Ore, Crimtane Ore, and Obsidian. It is slightly faster than both the Gold Pickaxe and Platinum Pickaxe in terms of mining speed. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Super Star Shooter.name: Super Star Shooter
Super Star Shooter.tooltip: The Super Star Shooter is a Hardmode ranged weapon that, as a direct upgrade to the Star Cannon, consumes and fires Fallen Stars. The projectiles are not affected by gravity, pierce an infinite amount of enemies, and dissipate into visual light-emitting particles after 1 minute or upon impact with a block. Unlike the Star Cannon, each projectile releases light slashes onto damaged enemies, which deal 75% of the weapon's damage (45 base damage) and pierce infinitely over a small area, but do not inflict any knockback. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Storm Spear.name: Storm Spear
Storm Spear.tooltip: The Storm Spear is a pre-Hardmode spear that can be found in Sandstone Chests in the lower 3/7ths of the Underground Desert and in Oasis Crates and Mirage Crates obtained from fishing in the Oasis. When thrust, it fires an electric bolt that deals 160% of the weapon's damage (21 base damage) and inflicts 50% its knockback (base knockback of 3 (Very weak)). The bolt does not pierce enemies and cannot pass through blocks. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.
Storm Spear.drops_summary: Mirage Crate (12.5%), Oasis Crate (12.5%), Sandstone Chest (33.33%)

Thunder Zapper.name: Thunder Zapper
Thunder Zapper.tooltip: The Thunder Zapper is a pre-Hardmode wand that can be found in Sandstone Chests in the lower 3/7ths of the Underground Desert and in Oasis Crates and Mirage Crates obtained from fishing in the Oasis. When used, it fires a lightning bolt that travels in a zigzag pattern horizontally (but traveling straight when shooting directly up or down). The bolt dissipates with a visual explosion after traveling for about one second or upon hitting an enemy or a block. Its best modifier is Mythical.
Thunder Zapper.drops_summary: Mirage Crate (12.5%), Oasis Crate (12.5%), Sandstone Chest (33.33%)

Drum Set.name: Drum Set
Drum Set.tooltip: The Drum Set is a novelty furniture item used in conjunction with the Drumstick to produce drum sounds. The Drum Set and Drumstick can be purchased from the Merchant for 10 Gold and 50 Silver respectively after either the Eater of Worlds, the Brain of Cthulhu, Skeletron, or the Wall of Flesh has been defeated. To play drum sounds, the player holding the Drumstick must be standing directly over the Drum Set and press ⚒ Use / Attack. The particular drum sound played is determined by the distance from the character to the cursor. From closest to farthest, by distance from the player (approximate percentage of the screen away from the character): 0-2.5%: Kick Drum 2.5-5%: Low Tom 5-7.5%: Mid Tom 7.5-11%: Hi Tom 11-13.3%: Snare Drum 13.3-16.6%: Floor Tom 16.6-19%: Hi-Hat (closed) 19-22.5%: Hi-Hat (open) 22.5-25%: Cymbal 1 25%+: Cymbal 2

Picnic Table.name: Picnic Table
Picnic Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Fancy Picnic Table.name: Fancy Picnic Table
Fancy Picnic Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Desert Minecart.name: Desert Minecart
Desert Minecart.tooltip: Minecarts are mounts that allow players to ride on Minecart Tracks. When the player is near a Minecart Track, pressing the Quick Mount hotkey or pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on a point on the track causes a Minecart to spawn, which the player is automatically placed in. Once inside, the ▶ Right and ◀ Left direction keys either accelerate, decelerate, or reverse the cart's movement. The cart will maintain its current speed and direction if no keys are pressed and no obstacles are reached. The cart can also "jump" with the ↷ Jump key. Weapons and tools, as well as most other items except hooks, can be used while riding a Minecart. The Minecart will deal damage to enemies it collides with and knock them back, with higher potency at higher speeds (see below for details). To exit the Minecart (which causes the Minecart to despawn), the player can use a hook, press the Quick Mount hotkey, or cancel the buff  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Minecart will also despawn if the player jumps off the tracks, lands on blocks, and attempts to move sideways. By default, a Wooden Minecart is spawned for the player. This can be overridden by equipping other Minecart items in the Minecart equipment slot of the player's inventory. The corresponding dye slot allows dyeing the Minecart. Using a Minecart Upgrade Kit will significantly boost the speed of all Minecarts, equip them with a laser that fires at nearby enemies, and increase the player's defense while moving. The boost effect is permanently available after using the item, though it can be toggled on and off through a probe icon next to the Minecart slot.

Pink Fairy.name: Pink Fairy
Pink Fairy.tooltip: The Pink Fairy, Green Fairy, and Blue Fairy are critters that emit light, which will attempt to lead the player to valuable treasures, such as Life Crystals, Chests, or ore deposits. They spawn in the bottom half of the Underground layer and in the Cavern layer, but only if at least one Fallen Log is present in the world on the surface (see Fallen Log § Notes for the exact area). If all Fallen Logs have been destroyed, they will no longer spawn independently. The three fairy variants all function identically. Fairies can also spawn at Fallen Logs and from shaken Pearlwood trees on the surface at night. In this case, they will not lead players to treasure; instead, when approached, they try to flee much like Birds or Faelings. Unlike fairies spawned underground, these fairies can be caught with a Bug Net and carried around in the inventory. If released again, they act like the ones spawned underground and will attempt to lead the player to treasure. They can also be crafted into animated decorative furniture (Fairy jars). Once crafted, the fairies cannot be released again unless de-crafted via Shimmer. They are some of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.

Junonia Shell.name: Junonia Shell
Junonia Shell.tooltip: Seashells are decorative items that can be found in the Ocean biomes. They can spawn on Sand Blocks within the biome, both on the beach and underwater. When placed, they can appear as one of three variants. Seashells can appear back on beaches and underwater, as long as no more than 3 Corals or Seashells are within an 8-tile range. Spawn rates scale with Rain, Wind, and empty space up to 14 tiles above the Sand Block. When a Seashell spawns, there is a 79.4% chance for either a regular Seashell or a Starfish, 9.8% chance for a Tulip Shell, 8.8% chance for a Lightning Whelk Shell, and 2% chance for a Junonia Shell.

Lightning Whelk Shell.name: Lightning Whelk Shell
Lightning Whelk Shell.tooltip: Seashells are decorative items that can be found in the Ocean biomes. They can spawn on Sand Blocks within the biome, both on the beach and underwater. When placed, they can appear as one of three variants. Seashells can appear back on beaches and underwater, as long as no more than 3 Corals or Seashells are within an 8-tile range. Spawn rates scale with Rain, Wind, and empty space up to 14 tiles above the Sand Block. When a Seashell spawns, there is a 79.4% chance for either a regular Seashell or a Starfish, 9.8% chance for a Tulip Shell, 8.8% chance for a Lightning Whelk Shell, and 2% chance for a Junonia Shell.

Tulip Shell.name: Tulip Shell
Tulip Shell.tooltip: Seashells are decorative items that can be found in the Ocean biomes. They can spawn on Sand Blocks within the biome, both on the beach and underwater. When placed, they can appear as one of three variants. Seashells can appear back on beaches and underwater, as long as no more than 3 Corals or Seashells are within an 8-tile range. Spawn rates scale with Rain, Wind, and empty space up to 14 tiles above the Sand Block. When a Seashell spawns, there is a 79.4% chance for either a regular Seashell or a Starfish, 9.8% chance for a Tulip Shell, 8.8% chance for a Lightning Whelk Shell, and 2% chance for a Junonia Shell.

Pin Wheel.name: Pin Wheel
Pin Wheel.tooltip: The Pin Wheel is a novelty furniture. When placed, the wheel spins if it is windy, with its spin speed depending on the current wind speed in the area. It is purchased from the Merchant for 20 Silver during the Windy Day event.

Weather Vane.name: Weather Vane
Weather Vane.tooltip: The Weather Vane is a decoration piece that will periodically sway in the wind if placed in the surface or space layer, and without a background wall behind it. If the wind speed hits 5 mph or more, it will start swaying in the direction of the wind.

Void Vault.name: Void Vault
Void Vault.tooltip: The Void Vault is a placeable portable storage item that extends the player's inventory in a manner similar to the Piggy Bank, Safe, and Defender's Forge. Like all other storage items, the Void Vault provides 40 slots of storage. The Void Vault can also be accessed via the Void Bag, similar to the way a player can access the Piggy Bank using a Money Trough. When the player's inventory is full and a Void Bag is present in the inventory, newly collected items are placed in the Void Vault (indicated by purple pickup text). If the Void Bag in the player's inventory is opened, it also allows the player to interact with the items inside the Void Vault as if they were in the main inventory without opening the storage interface. See Void Bag § Notes for details.

Music Box (Ocean Night).name: Music Box (Ocean Night)
Music Box (Ocean Night).tooltip: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End), which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 Gold after defeating the Moon Lord. A recorded Music Box can be played back in one of two ways: Equipping it as an accessory. Placing it as furniture and activating it, either by the ⚷ Open / Activate button or with wires. Recorded Music Boxes can be reverted into blank ones through Shimmer transmutation. There are 101 different Music Boxes available.

White Pin Flag.tooltip: Pin Flags are furniture items used in golfing. They are purely decorative and come in multiple colors. They can be purchased from the Golfer for 20 Silver each.

Golf Tee.name: Golf Tee
Golf Tee.tooltip: The Golf Tee is a furniture item used in golfing purchased from the Golfer for 1 Gold. It assists in placement of Golf Balls, and balls struck from a Golf Tee will travel further. Pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on a Golf Tee places a Golf Ball on top of it.

Shell Pile.name: Shell Pile
Shell Pile.tooltip: Shell Piles are a decorative block found naturally in the Ocean biome in large clumps. They are affected by gravity and will fall if supporting blocks are removed, dealing damage to any player or enemy they land on. They can also be found in Ocean Crates or in Seaside Crates. Shell Piles can be converted into Sand Blocks when used on an Extractinator.

Anti-Portal Block.name: Anti-Portal Block
Anti-Portal Block.tooltip: The Anti-Portal Block is a Hardmode block that prevents portals from the Portal Gun or Portal Gun Station to form on it. It is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 1 Silver.

Golf Club (Putter).name: Golf Club (Putter)
Golf Club (Putter).tooltip: Golf Clubs are tools used in the golf minigame. There are four types of Golf Clubs, the Driver, Iron, Wedge, and Putter, which are each used to hit the Golf Ball a different horizontal and vertical distance. Special variants of Golf Clubs can be unlocked by achieving different golf scores. All upgrades are purely aesthetic, despite being more expensive as the tier increases. They do not harm enemies or critters.

Golf Club (Wedge).name: Golf Club (Wedge)
Golf Club (Wedge).tooltip: Golf Clubs are tools used in the golf minigame. There are four types of Golf Clubs, the Driver, Iron, Wedge, and Putter, which are each used to hit the Golf Ball a different horizontal and vertical distance. Golf Club (Driver).name: Golf Club (Driver)
Golf Club (Driver).tooltip: Golf Clubs are tools used in the golf minigame. Golf Whistle.name: Golf Whistle
Golf Whistle.tooltip: The Golf Whistle is a tool used in golf that allows a player to recover Golf Balls, returning it to the previous position before it was hit when used. Using the Golf Whistle adds one stroke to the player's golf score for the shot as a penalty. The Golf Whistle can be purchased from the Golfer for 10 Gold.

Ebonwood Toilet.name: Ebonwood Toilet
Ebonwood Toilet.tooltip: Toilets are furniture items which can be placed on the ground. They are functionally similar to chairs, and fulfill a house's chair requirement. Similarly to chairs, Toilets can be sat on by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Having any tier of Well Fed active while sitting on a Toilet allows the production of Poo. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Toilet will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Toilets act as mechanisms that can be activated via wire, which makes them appear to explosively eject sewage. This effect is purely a novelty visual. Ejected sewage on the ground fades after a few seconds. There are 67 Toilets.

Maid Bonnet.name: Maid Bonnet
Maid Bonnet.tooltip: The Maid set is a vanity set consisting of the Maid Bonnet, Maid Dress and Maid Shoes. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Maid Dress.name: Maid Dress
Maid Dress.tooltip: The Maid set is a vanity set consisting of the Maid Bonnet, Maid Dress and Maid Shoes. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Maid Shoes.name: Maid Shoes
Maid Shoes.tooltip: The Maid set is a vanity set consisting of the Maid Bonnet, Maid Dress and Maid Shoes. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Void Bag.name: Void Bag
Void Bag.tooltip: The Void Bag is a portable storage item that grants the player access to the Void Vault anywhere. When used, it will summon a temporary portal which lasts for 3 minutes, and pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the portal opens the player's Void Vault inventory. The Void Bag is never consumed and can be used limitlessly. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Void Bag item in the inventory turns it into the Closed Void Bag. Pressing the button again opens the Void Bag again. When opened, the Void Vault storage will effectively act as the player's secondary inventory, which automatically stores items collected after the player's main inventory is full, indicated by a purple mask on the pickup text. Additionally, it also allows the player to interact with the items inside it as if they were in the main inventory without opening the Void Vault storage interface. When closed, the Void Bag functions similarly to the Money Trough / Eye Bone, only acting as a regular portable storage item. This will prevent it from picking up items when the player has a full inventory, and it loses the function of the secondary inventory.

Pink Maid Bonnet.name: Pink Maid Bonnet
Pink Maid Bonnet.tooltip: The Pink Maid set is a vanity set consisting of the Pink Maid Bonnet, Pink Maid Dress and Pink Maid Shoes. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Pink Maid Dress.name: Pink Maid Dress
Pink Maid Dress.tooltip: The Pink Maid set is a vanity set consisting of the Pink Maid Bonnet, Pink Maid Dress and Pink Maid Shoes. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Pink Maid Shoes.name: Pink Maid Shoes
Pink Maid Shoes.tooltip: The Pink Maid set is a vanity set consisting of the Pink Maid Bonnet, Pink Maid Dress and Pink Maid Shoes. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Country Club Cap.name: Country Club Cap
Country Club Cap.tooltip: The Country Club set is a vanity set. It is purchased from the Golfer for 7 Gold 50 Silver (set). These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Country Club Vest.name: Country Club Vest
Country Club Vest.tooltip: The Country Club set is a vanity set. It is purchased from the Golfer for 7 Gold 50 Silver (set). These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Spider Nest Block.name: Spider Nest Block
Spider Nest Block.tooltip: Spider Nest Blocks are Hardmode blocks crafted from one Spider Fang and 10 Cobwebs at a Work Bench. They are used to craft Spider furniture and Spider Nest Walls. Crafting all items requires 153 Spider Nest Blocks.

Spider Nest Wall.name: Spider Nest Wall
Spider Nest Wall.tooltip: Spider Nest Walls are a type of wall. As with most placed walls, they are compatible with NPC housing and will prevent enemies from spawning.

Meteor Toilet.name: Meteor Toilet
Meteor Toilet.tooltip: Toilets are furniture items which can be placed on the ground. They are functionally similar to chairs, and fulfill a house's chair requirement. Similarly to chairs, Toilets can be sat on by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Having any tier of Well Fed active while sitting on a Toilet allows the production of Poo. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Toilet will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Toilets act as mechanisms that can be activated via wire, which makes them appear to explosively eject sewage. This effect is purely a novelty visual. Ejected sewage on the ground fades after a few seconds. There are 67 Toilets.

Decay Chamber.name: Decay Chamber
Decay Chamber.tooltip: The Decay Chamber is a Hardmode crafting station used to craft Lesion furniture (Corruption-themed furniture) out of Lesion Blocks. The Decay Chamber can be purchased from the Steampunker for 10 Gold but only appears for sale in worlds that are generated with The Corruption. It can also be crafted from the Flesh Cloning Vat, its Crimson counterpart. Lesion Blocks are crafted using a Meat Grinder, so the Decay Chamber is of little use without one.

Terragrim.name: Terragrim
Terragrim.tooltip: The Terragrim is a pre-Hardmode melee weapon. When used, it rapidly releases slashes aimed towards the cursor. Anything within this area takes constant damage at a rate exceeding the weapon's stated use time. It is obtainable from the unique background object found in an Enchanted Sword Shrine or very rarely in the Caverns layer. When the object is destroyed, it has a 1/30 (3.33%) chance to drop a Terragrim rather than an Enchanted Sword. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount. The Terragrim's unique means of attack is unaffected by any size and speed modifiers.

Solar Bathtub.name: Solar Bathtub
Solar Bathtub.tooltip: Bathtubs are furniture items which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 65 / (Old-gen console version) 16 / (3DS version) 11 Bathtub types, all being functionally identical but presenting different appearances.

Solar Bed.name: Solar Bed
Solar Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration. Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 craftable Beds and 5 that can be acquired from the environment. All Beds are functionally identical and differ only in appearance.

Solar Bookcase.name: Solar Bookcase
Solar Bookcase.tooltip: Bookcases are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station used for the crafting of three Hardmode magic weapons (the Crystal Storm, Cursed Flames, and Golden Shower) as well as the Librarian furniture out of Librarian Blocks. Bookcases also fulfill a house's table requirement. There is a total of 65 types of Bookcases: 60 craftable Bookcases, and 5 looted from the environment: one from the Underworld, three from the Dungeon, and one from the Pirate Invasion. Some bookcases can also be found in Underground Cabins; their style follows the theme of the cabin where they are found.

Solar Dresser.name: Solar Dresser
Solar Dresser.tooltip: Dressers are a type of flat-surface furniture (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and storage item. They also fulfill house's table requirement. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 19 / (3DS version) 5 craftable versions, and (Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) 5 noncraftable versions which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Solar Candelabra.name: Solar Candelabra
Solar Candelabra.tooltip: Candelabras are a type of furniture and light source that emits light when placed on a flat surface such as blocks, platforms, and flat furniture items. It is not destroyed by water. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 23 /  12 craftable and 5 looted variations of the Candelabra.

Solar Candle.name: Solar Candle
Solar Candle.tooltip: Candles are a type of furniture and light source. Candles can only be placed on flat-surface items. Candles will produce light underwater if placed and can be toggled on and off with ⚷ Open / Activate and by mechanisms. Certain types of candles provide buffs or debuffs. The Water Candle is a special type of candle found in Dungeons which increases enemy spawn rates by 33% and the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50% when placed or held. The Peace Candle reduces spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%, in contrast to the Water Candle. The Shadow Candle(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns in the area. For Water Candles and Peace Candles, multiple candles cannot stack, even if one is placed and the other is held.

Solar Chair.name: Solar Chair
Solar Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Solar Chandelier.name: Solar Chandelier
Solar Chandelier.tooltip: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers come in many varieties which differ only in appearance and sell value. All chandeliers can be picked up using a pickaxe, drill, or explosives. Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.

Solar Chest.name: Solar Chest
Solar Chest.tooltip: Chests are a type of furniture functioning as storage items. They are accessed using ⚷ Open / Activate and can store up to 40 item stacks in rows of  10×4 /   8×5. In addition to many being craftable, a number of Chests are placed in random locations during world generation. The loot contained in these Chests is determined during world generation, and will not change if the world enters Hardmode. Chests cannot be broken with items inside (the blocks a filled Chest is placed on would also have this trait). However, the Block Swap feature allows the player to change the type of a Chest without having to destroy it. Some types of Chests can be locked by the player using a Chest Lock. When doing so, they will require a key to open again. There are 23 varieties of naturally-occurring Chests (12 of which cannot be crafted), 53 that can only be crafted, and 1 purchasable Chest, for a total of 77 Chest types.

Solar Clock.name: Solar Clock
Solar Clock.tooltip: Grandfather Clocks are furniture items which provide information about the in-game time. If a player is nearby a Grandfather Clock (about 80 tiles horizontally and 50 tiles vertically), the time is displayed on the right side of the screen, underneath the minimap. The time is rounded to the last hour, similar to Tin and Copper Watches, but pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it will show precise time in minutes as a status message on the bottom left corner. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 21 /  5 craftable versions and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 5 / (Old-gen console version) 2 noncraftable (but still lootable) versions. The regular Grandfather Clock can rarely be found in Underground Cabins. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Solar Door.name: Solar Door
Solar Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Solar Lamp.name: Solar Lamp
Solar Lamp.tooltip: Lamps are a type of furniture and light source. They also count as valid house lighting and can be toggled on and off by mechanisms. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 59 types of craftable Lamps, three types that are found in the Dungeon (Green, Blue, or Pink Dungeon Lamp), one found in Underworld houses (Obsidian Lamp), and one that can be dropped during a Pirate Invasion (Golden Lamp). Most lamps are dislodged by liquids, but Obsidian Lamp and Ash Wood Lamp are not dislodged by Lava. The Tiki Torch shares its Tile ID with the rest of these Lamps. Also see Lamp Post ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions) which does not count as valid House lighting.)

Solar Lantern.name: Solar Lantern
Solar Lantern.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Solar Piano.name: Solar Piano
Solar Piano.tooltip: Pianos are a type of furniture which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 15 /  10 craftable Pianos, and 5 non-craftable Pianos that can be found in the Dungeon, Ruined Houses, and Pirate Invasion event. Some Pianos can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin that they are found in.

Solar Platform.name: Solar Platform
Solar Platform.tooltip: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Solar Sink.name: Solar Sink
Solar Sink.tooltip: The Sink is a type of furniture item and crafting station. Like Fountains, it can be used to craft items that require water as a crafting station. There is a total of 66 Sink types, all being functionally identical.

Solar Sofa.name: Solar Sofa
Solar Sofa.tooltip: Sofas are furniture items which fulfill a house's chair requirement. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Players can sit in sofas by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Players can choose to sit on the left, middle, or right positions, and thus up to 3 players can sit on a sofa at a time. Sitting on sofas gives a boost to health regeneration, similar to chairs and beds. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Sofa will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 21 craftable sofas and 5 noncraftable sofas. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Solar Table.name: Solar Table
Solar Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Solar Work Bench.name: Solar Work Bench
Solar Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Trapped Solar Chest.name: Trapped Solar Chest
Trapped Solar Chest.tooltip: A Trapped Chest is a mechanical item that has the appearance of a normal chest. It cannot be used for storage, as it does not have any storage slots. When it is opened, it emits a signal and can be connected with wire. Any chest can be crafted into a Trapped Chest at the Heavy Assembler with the desired chest and 10 wire. The Trapped Chest can be sold for 1 Silver.

Vortex Lamp.name: Vortex Lamp
Vortex Lamp.tooltip: Lamps are a type of furniture and light source. They also count as valid house lighting and can be toggled on and off by mechanisms. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 59 types of craftable Lamps, three types that are found in the Dungeon (Green, Blue, or Pink Dungeon Lamp), one found in Underworld houses (Obsidian Lamp), and one that can be dropped during a Pirate Invasion (Golden Lamp). Most lamps are dislodged by liquids, but Obsidian Lamp and Ash Wood Lamp are not dislodged by Lava. The Tiki Torch shares its Tile ID with the rest of these Lamps. Also see Lamp Post ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions) which does not count as valid House lighting.)

Vortex Lantern.name: Vortex Lantern
Vortex Lantern.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Vortex Piano.name: Vortex Piano
Vortex Piano.tooltip: Pianos are a type of furniture which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 15 /  10 craftable Pianos, and 5 non-craftable Pianos that can be found in the Dungeon, Ruined Houses, and Pirate Invasion event. Some Pianos can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin that they are found in.

Vortex Platform.name: Vortex Platform
Vortex Platform.tooltip: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Vortex Sink.name: Vortex Sink
Vortex Sink.tooltip: The Sink is a type of furniture item and crafting station. Like Fountains, it can be used to craft items that require water as a crafting station. There is a total of 66 Sink types, all being functionally identical.

Vortex Sofa.name: Vortex Sofa
Vortex Sofa.tooltip: Sofas are furniture items which fulfill a house's chair requirement. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Players can sit in sofas by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Players can choose to sit on the left, middle, or right positions, and thus up to 3 players can sit on a sofa at a time. Sitting on sofas gives a boost to health regeneration, similar to chairs and beds. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Sofa will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 21 craftable sofas and 5 noncraftable sofas. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Vortex Table.name: Vortex Table
Vortex Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Vortex Work Bench.name: Vortex Work Bench
Vortex Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Trapped Vortex Chest.name: Trapped Vortex Chest
Trapped Vortex Chest.tooltip: A Trapped Chest is a mechanical item that has the appearance of a normal chest. It cannot be used for storage, as it does not have any storage slots. When it is opened, it emits a signal and can be connected with wire. Any chest can be crafted into a Trapped Chest at the Heavy Assembler with the desired chest and 10 wire. The Trapped Chest can be sold for 1 Silver.

Vortex Toilet.name: Vortex Toilet
Vortex Toilet.tooltip: Toilets are furniture items which can be placed on the ground. They are functionally similar to chairs, and fulfill a house's chair requirement. Similarly to chairs, Toilets can be sat on by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Having any tier of Well Fed active while sitting on a Toilet allows the production of Poo. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Toilet will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Toilets act as mechanisms that can be activated via wire, which makes them appear to explosively eject sewage. This effect is purely a novelty visual. Ejected sewage on the ground fades after a few seconds. There are 67 Toilets.

Nebula Bathtub.name: Nebula Bathtub
Nebula Bathtub.tooltip: Bathtubs are furniture items which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 65 / (Old-gen console version) 16 / (3DS version) 11 Bathtub types, all being functionally identical but presenting different appearances.

Nebula Bed.name: Nebula Bed
Nebula Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration. Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 craftable Beds and 5 that can be acquired from the environment. All Beds are functionally identical and differ only in appearance.

Nebula Bookcase.name: Nebula Bookcase
Nebula Bookcase.tooltip: Bookcases are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station used for the crafting of three Hardmode magic weapons (the Crystal Storm, Cursed Flames, and Golden Shower) as well as the Librarian furniture out of Librarian Blocks. Bookcases also fulfill a house's table requirement. There is a total of 65 types of Bookcases: 60 craftable Bookcases, and 5 looted from the environment: one from the Underworld, three from the Dungeon, and one from the Pirate Invasion. Some bookcases can also be found in Underground Cabins; their style follows the theme of the cabin where they are found.

Nebula Dresser.name: Nebula Dresser
Nebula Dresser.tooltip: Dressers are a type of flat-surface furniture (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and storage item. They also fulfill house's table requirement. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 19 / (3DS version) 5 craftable versions, and (Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) 5 noncraftable versions which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Nebula Candelabra.name: Nebula Candelabra
Nebula Candelabra.tooltip: Candelabras are a type of furniture and light source that emits light when placed on a flat surface such as blocks, platforms, and flat furniture items. It is not destroyed by water. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 23 /  12 craftable and 5 looted variations of the Candelabra.

Nebula Candle.name: Nebula Candle
Nebula Candle.tooltip: Candles are a type of furniture and light source. Candles can only be placed on flat-surface items. Candles will produce light underwater if placed and can be toggled on and off with ⚷ Open / Activate and by mechanisms. Certain types of candles provide buffs or debuffs. The Water Candle is a special type of candle found in Dungeons which increases enemy spawn rates by 33% and the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50% when placed or held. The Peace Candle reduces spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%, in contrast to the Water Candle. The Shadow Candle(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns in the area. For Water Candles and Peace Candles, multiple candles cannot stack, even if one is placed and the other is held.

Nebula Chair.name: Nebula Chair
Nebula Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Nebula Chandelier.name: Nebula Chandelier
Nebula Chandelier.tooltip: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers come in many varieties which differ only in appearance and sell value. All chandeliers can be picked up using a pickaxe, drill, or explosives. Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.

Nebula Chest.name: Nebula Chest
Nebula Chest.tooltip: Chests are a type of furniture functioning as storage items. They are accessed using ⚷ Open / Activate and can store up to 40 item stacks in rows of  10×4 /   8×5. In addition to many being craftable, a number of Chests are placed in random locations during world generation. The loot contained in these Chests is determined during world generation, and will not change if the world enters Hardmode. Chests cannot be broken with items inside (the blocks a filled Chest is placed on would also have this trait). However, the Block Swap feature allows the player to change the type of a Chest without having to destroy it. Some types of Chests can be locked by the player using a Chest Lock. When doing so, they will require a key to open again. There are 23 varieties of naturally-occurring Chests (12 of which cannot be crafted), 53 that can only be crafted, and 1 purchasable Chest, for a total of 77 Chest types.

Nebula Clock.name: Nebula Clock
Nebula Clock.tooltip: Grandfather Clocks are furniture items which provide information about the in-game time. If a player is nearby a Grandfather Clock (about 80 tiles horizontally and 50 tiles vertically), the time is displayed on the right side of the screen, underneath the minimap. The time is rounded to the last hour, similar to Tin and Copper Watches, but pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it will show precise time in minutes as a status message on the bottom left corner. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 21 /  5 craftable versions and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 5 / (Old-gen console version) 2 noncraftable (but still lootable) versions. The regular Grandfather Clock can rarely be found in Underground Cabins. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Nebula Door.name: Nebula Door
Nebula Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Nebula Lamp.tooltip: Lamps are a type of furniture and light source. They also count as valid house lighting and can be toggled on and off by mechanisms. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Trapped Stardust Chest.name: Trapped Stardust Chest
Trapped Stardust Chest.tooltip: A Trapped Chest is a mechanical item that has the appearance of a normal chest. It cannot be used for storage, as it does not have any storage slots. When it is opened, it emits a signal and can be connected with wire. Any chest can be crafted into a Trapped Chest at the Heavy Assembler with the desired chest and 10 wire. The Trapped Chest can be sold for 1 Silver.

Stardust Toilet.name: Stardust Toilet
Stardust Toilet.tooltip: Toilets are furniture items which can be placed on the ground. They are functionally similar to chairs, and fulfill a house's chair requirement. Similarly to chairs, Toilets can be sat on by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Having any tier of Well Fed active while sitting on a Toilet allows the production of Poo. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Toilet will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Toilets act as mechanisms that can be activated via wire, which makes them appear to explosively eject sewage. This effect is purely a novelty visual. Ejected sewage on the ground fades after a few seconds. There are 67 Toilets.

Solar Brick.name: Solar Brick
Solar Brick.tooltip: The Solar Brick is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist brick that is crafted from Solar Fragments. It is one of the four Fragment Bricks, bricks which are crafted with Lunar Fragments. It glows when placed and can be used to craft Solar furniture.

Vortex Brick.name: Vortex Brick
Vortex Brick.tooltip: The Vortex Brick is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist brick that is crafted from Vortex Fragments. It is one of the four Fragment Bricks, bricks which are crafted with Lunar Fragments. It glows when placed and can be used to craft Vortex furniture.

Nebula Brick.name: Nebula Brick
Nebula Brick.tooltip: The Nebula Brick is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist brick that is crafted from Nebula Fragments. It is one of the four Fragment Bricks, bricks which are crafted with Lunar Fragments. It glows when placed and can be used to craft Nebula furniture.

Stardust Brick.name: Stardust Brick
Stardust Brick.tooltip: The Stardust Brick is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist brick that is crafted from Stardust Fragments. It is one of the four Fragment Bricks, bricks which are crafted with Lunar Fragments. It glows when placed and can be used to craft Stardust furniture.

Solar Brick Wall.name: Solar Brick Wall
Solar Brick Wall.tooltip: Solar Brick Wall is a background wall made from Solar Bricks.

Vortex Brick Wall.name: Vortex Brick Wall
Vortex Brick Wall.tooltip: Vortex Brick Wall is a background wall made from Vortex Bricks.

Nebula Brick Wall.name: Nebula Brick Wall
Nebula Brick Wall.tooltip: Nebula Brick Wall is a background wall made from Nebula Bricks.

Stardust Brick Wall.name: Stardust Brick Wall
Stardust Brick Wall.tooltip: Stardust Brick Wall is a background wall made from Stardust Bricks.

Music Box (Day Remix).name: Music Box (Day Remix)
Music Box (Day Remix).tooltip: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End), which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 Gold after defeating the Moon Lord. A recorded Music Box can be played back in one of two ways: Equipping it as an accessory. Placing it as furniture and activating it, either by the ⚷ Open / Activate button or with wires. Recorded Music Boxes can be reverted into blank ones through Shimmer transmutation. There are 101 different Music Boxes available.

Cracked Blue Brick.name: Cracked Blue Brick
Cracked Blue Brick.tooltip: Cracked Dungeon Bricks are bricks which can be found in the Dungeon and appear very similar to ordinary Dungeon Bricks. If jumped on, walked across, grappled to, mined with any pickaxe or drill, or hit by projectiles, several Cracked Dungeon Bricks nearby the targeted block, including the block itself, may fall and be destroyed upon hitting solid ground, dropping no item. Cracked Dungeon Bricks can conceal important pathways to significant portions of the Dungeon, potentially making it seem much smaller than it actually is. Additionally, naturally-generated Cracked Dungeon Bricks often conceal rectangular pits lined with Spikes, which may sometimes be filled with water to make escape more difficult.  Cracked Dungeon Bricks can be crafted with regular Dungeon Bricks at a Heavy Assembler. Crafted Cracked Dungeon Bricks behave the same as naturally generated Cracked Dungeon Bricks, and do not drop an item upon destruction.

Cracked Green Brick.tooltip: Cracked Dungeon Bricks are bricks which can be found in the Dungeon and appear very similar to ordinary Dungeon Bricks. Wild Flower Seeds.name: Wild Flower Seeds
Wild Flower Seeds.tooltip: Flower Seeds are seeds used to plant a random flower. They can all be purchased from the Dryad for 5 Silver each. Flower Seeds can only be planted on pure grass and mowed grass blocks (not on any other type of grass), in Clay Pots, in Planter Boxes, and in Rock Golem Heads. When used on a grass or mowed grass block, Flower Seeds cannot be planted if there is a background wall behind the block or on the tile above the block (with a few exceptions). However, it is possible to plant the seed and then place a wall behind it without breaking the plant.

Black Golf Ball.name: Black Golf Ball
Black Golf Ball.tooltip: Golf Balls are accessories that are used in golf and come in a variety of colors. The plain, white Golf Ball can be purchased from the Golfer for 1 Gold and can be used for crafting the colored variants. The Golf Ball items are not required to play golf, as pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on an empty Golf Tee will always create a Golf Ball projectile. Their main purposes are: Changing the color of this projectile, which is a purely visual effect. The Golf Ball item does not need to be equipped for this, having it in the inventory is sufficient. Manually placing Golf Ball projectiles anywhere in the world, even outside of Golf Tees. This is done by pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button while the Golf Ball item is selected. The item will not be consumed, it can be reused to place an unlimited number of Golf Ball projectiles. Golf Ball projectiles can be hit with a Golf Club and despawn when entering a Golf Cup.

Amber Robe.name: Amber Robe
Amber Robe.tooltip: The Amber Robe is an armor item that can be worn in the shirt slot. It is a gem robe and part of the Wizard set. The Amber Robe enchants gem staff projectiles to pierce an additional 2 enemies, and bounce up to 2 times on blocks, at the cost of dealing 80% damage. The Amber Staff instead receives a flat damage buff of 4, applied after the 80% damage multiplier. Wearing the Wizard Hat alongside the Amber Robe provides a set bonus of +10% magic critical strike chance, whereas wearing a Magic Hat alongside it provides a set bonus of +60 mana. Any leg-slot equipment can be worn with these set bonuses remaining intact.

Amber Hook.name: Amber Hook
Amber Hook.tooltip: Hooks are a class of tools which aid the player in traversing terrain. When used, hooks fire a chain that latches to a surface or platform and pulls the player towards it. A hook is an essential tool which offers significant freedom from terrain height restrictions as well as being a fast movement option, and will often be the first major mobility tool a player acquires. A variety of hooks are available at all stages of the game (see table below). The Grapple hotkey activates the equipped hook in the player's equipment slot, or the first hook from the inventory (from left to right, top to bottom) without requiring it to be in the player's hotbar.Verify Several higher-tier hooks, such as the Ivy Whip, allow the player to grapple multiple surfaces simultaneously. If the character grapples one surface, then fires the hook a second time, another chain extends from the player without dislodging the first. Upon grappling a second surface, the player will be suspended in midair at a point midway between the two surfaces. This allows players more freedom during construction, or for navigating hazardous areas, such as above lava or Meteorite. All Journey Mode characters will spawn with the basic Grappling Hook already in their inventory.

Orange Phaseblade.name: Orange Phaseblade
Orange Phaseblade.tooltip: Phaseblades are a group of pre-Hardmode broadswords. There are nine different color variations with identical statistics. Letting go of ⚒ Use / Attack while swinging will throw the weapons, causing them to sharply drop down after traveling for 0.5 seconds or upon contact with blocks, then embed themselves in the ground and continuously damage any enemy that touches them. They can be recalled by pressing ⚒ Use / Attack again, which will damage enemies along the way. They can also be recalled mid-throw. All phaseblades emit a small amount of light corresponding to their color when swung, thrown, or embedded in the ground. Phasesabers are the Hardmode upgrades of the phaseblades. Their best modifier is Legendary.

Orange Phasesaber.name: Orange Phasesaber
Orange Phasesaber.tooltip: Phasesabers are a group of Hardmode broadswords, direct upgrades to the phaseblades with much more damage and slightly faster use time. There are nine different color variations with identical statistics. Letting go of ⚒ Use / Attack while swinging will throw the weapons, causing them to sharply drop down after traveling for 0.5 seconds or upon contact with blocks, then embed themselves in the ground and continuously damage any enemy that touches them. They can be recalled by pressing ⚒ Use / Attack again, which will damage enemies along the way. They can also be recalled mid-throw. All phasesabers emit a small amount of light corresponding to their color when swung, thrown, or embedded in the ground. Their best modifier is Legendary.

Orange Stained Glass.name: Orange Stained Glass
Orange Stained Glass.tooltip: Stained Glass are a group of walls made from combining gems with Glass Walls. They work like the normal Glass Wall besides changing the color of the sunlight to match that of the stained glass. Multicolored Stained Glass causes sunlight to shift through the color spectrum in a similar manner to Rainbow Brick, although dimmer.

Orange Pressure Plate.name: Orange Pressure Plate
Orange Pressure Plate.tooltip: Pressure Plates are activation mechanisms that trigger wired mechanisms when stepped on. A pressure plate's color determines which characters can trigger it. Red, Brown, Gray, Orange, and Lihzahrd Pressure Plates are randomly generated on the map during world creation as the trigger for traps. They only take up a very small space on top of blocks, so they may be difficult to spot. The color of naturally spawned pressure plates is dependent on the color of the block they are generated on top of. Except for Lihzahrd Pressure Plates, they can also be purchased from the Mechanic. Weighted Pressure Plates activate once on being depressed, and again on being released. All Weighted Pressure Plates of the same color share a single state. As long as one Weighted Pressure Plate of a given color is already pressed down within a circuit, stepping on another identical plate will not send a new signal. They can be crafted from regular pressure plates. The Teal Pressure Pad is a special kind of pressure plate that responds to projectiles impacting it, which includes pets that touch it. Unlike regular pressure plates, the Teal Pressure Pad can be placed on all four sides of a block, e.g. on the ceiling or sidewall. It can be purchased from the Mechanic.

Snake Charmer's Flute.name: Snake Charmer's Flute
Snake Charmer's Flute.tooltip: The Snake Charmer's Flute is a pre-Hardmode tool that places a pot from which a snake rises. Once the snake reaches its full height of 100 tiles or touches a block, it stops rising and becomes climbable like a rope. Blocks can also be placed next to the snake once it has fully extended. The snake and the pot disappear after 30 seconds, and also produce a small amount of light. The Snake Charmer's Flute can be found in Sandstone Chests in the top 4/7ths of the Underground Desert and in Oasis Crates and Mirage Crates obtained from fishing in the Oasis.
Snake Charmer's Flute.drops_summary: Mirage Crate (12.5%), Oasis Crate (12.5%), Sandstone Chest (25%)

Magic Conch.name: Magic Conch
Magic Conch.tooltip: The Magic Conch is a tool that teleports the player to the Ocean that is furthest away from them, 0.75 seconds (45 ticks) after being used. Like the Magic Mirror and Demon Conch, it can be used an unlimited amount of times. The Magic Conch can be found in Sandstone Chests in the top 4/7ths of the Underground Desert and Oasis Crates and Mirage Crates obtained from fishing in the Oasis.
Magic Conch.drops_summary: Mirage Crate (12.5%), Oasis Crate (12.5%), Sandstone Chest (25%)

Golf Cart Keys.name: Golf Cart Keys
Golf Cart Keys.tooltip: The Golf Cart Keys are a post-Skeletron mount-summoning item that places the player in a rideable Golf Cart. The Golf Cart emits light from its front that reaches about 40 tiles, with the brightest point being at about 15 tiles. The Golf Cart Keys can be purchased from the Golfer for 50 Gold after Skeletron has been defeated, and a golf score greater than 2000 is earned by the player.

Golf Chest.name: Golf Chest
Golf Chest.tooltip: Chests are a type of furniture functioning as storage items. They are accessed using ⚷ Open / Activate and can store up to 40 item stacks in rows of  10×4 /   8×5. In addition to many being craftable, a number of Chests are placed in random locations during world generation. The loot contained in these Chests is determined during world generation, and will not change if the world enters Hardmode. Chests cannot be broken with items inside (the blocks a filled Chest is placed on would also have this trait). However, the Block Swap feature allows the player to change the type of a Chest without having to destroy it. Some types of Chests can be locked by the player using a Chest Lock. When doing so, they will require a key to open again. There are 23 varieties of naturally-occurring Chests (12 of which cannot be crafted), 53 that can only be crafted, and 1 purchasable Chest, for a total of 77 Chest types.

Trapped Golf Chest.name: Trapped Golf Chest
Trapped Golf Chest.tooltip: A Trapped Chest is a mechanical item that has the appearance of a normal chest. It cannot be used for storage, as it does not have any storage slots. When it is opened, it emits a signal and can be connected with wire. Any chest can be crafted into a Trapped Chest at the Heavy Assembler with the desired chest and 10 wire. The Trapped Chest can be sold for 1 Silver.

Sandstone Chest.name: Sandstone Chest
Sandstone Chest.tooltip: The Sandstone Chest is a storage item found in the Underground Desert. They are usually found in Underground Cabins but may also uncommonly generate by themselves. Sandstone Chests can also be crafted.

Trapped Sandstone Chest.name: Trapped Sandstone Chest
Trapped Sandstone Chest.tooltip: A Trapped Chest is a mechanical item that has the appearance of a normal chest. It cannot be used for storage, as it does not have any storage slots. When it is opened, it emits a signal and can be connected with wire. Any chest can be crafted into a Trapped Chest at the Heavy Assembler with the desired chest and 10 wire. The Trapped Chest can be sold for 1 Silver.

Sanguine Staff.name: Sanguine Staff
Sanguine Staff.tooltip: The Sanguine Staff is a Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Sanguine Bat minion. It flies in an elliptical loop between the player and the target enemy. Sanguine Bats arrange themselves along a semicircle around the player's head, and immediately return to the player if no enemies are nearby. The Sanguine Staff has a 1/2 (50%) / 1/1 (100%) chance of being dropped by Dreadnautiluses. Its best modifier is Fabled.

Blood Thorn.name: Blood Thorn
Blood Thorn.tooltip: The Blood Thorn is a Hardmode magic weapon that summons three penetrating Blood Thorn projectiles upon use, which erupt from solid blocks and platforms to damage enemies near the player's cursor. It has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Hemogoblin Sharks. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Bloody Tear.name: Bloody Tear
Bloody Tear.tooltip: The Bloody Tear is an event-summoning item used to summon a Blood Moon. It can only be used at night, and attempting to use it during the day or while a Blood Moon is already active will not summon a Blood Moon, affect the ongoing Blood Moon, or consume the item. The Bloody Tear has a 1/100 (1%) chance to be dropped from Blood Zombies and Dripplers, a 1/25 (4%) chance from Blood Eels, Hemogoblin Sharks, Wandering Eye Fish, and Zombie Mermen, a 1/10 (10%) chance from Clowns, and a 1/5 (20%) chance from The Bride and The Groom. The Bloody Tear can only be dropped during a Blood Moon, i.e. enemies killed after the Blood Moon has ended do not drop it. The exception to this are The Groom and The Bride, who can drop it at any time. Statue-spawned Blood Zombies and Dripplers can never drop a Bloody Tear. Additionally, Dreadnautiluses have a 1/2 (50%) / 1/1 (100%) chance of dropping it at any time.
Bloody Tear.drops_summary: Blood Eel (4%), Blood Zombie (1%), Clown (10%), +7 more

Drippler Crippler.name: Drippler Crippler
Drippler Crippler.tooltip: The Drippler Crippler is a Hardmode flail that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Blood Eels. When thrown, it fires a thorny ball from the flail's head, which deals 50% of the weapon's damage (55 base damage). Thorny balls are affected by gravity, can bounce off blocks twice, and pierce two enemies; dissipating upon hitting a block or enemy a third time, or when it stops rolling. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Vampire Frog Staff.name: Vampire Frog Staff
Vampire Frog Staff.tooltip: The Vampire Frog Staff is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Vampire Frog minion. It hops towards enemies to deal contact damage. The Vampire Frog Staff has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Wandering Eye Fish and Zombie Mermen. Its best modifier is Fabled.

Gold Goldfish.name: Gold Goldfish
Gold Goldfish.tooltip: The Gold Goldfish is a harmless critter. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Goldfish, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version. The Gold Goldfish has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Gold Goldfish can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gold Fish Bowl). Once crafted, the Gold Goldfish cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Gold Goldfish itself or the crafted furniture can be sold for 10 Gold. It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.

Gold Fish Bowl.name: Gold Fish Bowl
Gold Fish Bowl.tooltip: The Fish Bowl, Gold Fish Bowl (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Pupfish Bowl (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Lava Serpent Bowl (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are decorative furniture items. The Fish Bowl and Gold Fish Bowl also double as wearable items that can be equipped in the player's helmet slot. Fish Bowls cause only visual effects when placed in the helmet vanity slot. When instead placed in the functional head armor slot, the breath meter appears as if the player were underwater, and if worn long enough the player will drown and die. Breathing aids like the Breathing Reed or Gills Potion will allow for normal breathing when wearing the bowl. The Fish, Gold Fish and Pupfish Bowls are crafted, while the Lava Serpent Bowl has a 39/200 (19.5%) chance of being found inside Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates. Crafted Fish Bowls can be converted back into their ingredients by throwing them into Shimmer, gaining back the fish as an item.

Bast Statue.name: Bast Statue
Bast Statue.tooltip: The Bast Statue is a furniture item that grants The Bast Defense buff to players in its vicinity, increasing their defense by 5. The buff effect can be toggled via wire. The Bast Statue can be found in Sandstone Chests in the lower 3/7ths of the Underground Desert and in Oasis Crates and Mirage Crates obtained from fishing in the Oasis. It can also be found as a furniture in Underground Desert Cabins. The buff is applied to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the Bast Statue, similar to Heart Lanterns and Campfires.
Bast Statue.drops_summary: Mirage Crate (12.5%), Oasis Crate (12.5%), Sandstone Chest (33.33%)

Gold Starry Block.name: Gold Starry Block
Gold Starry Block.tooltip: The Gold Starry Block is an animated decorative block. When placed it shows twinkling, gold stars on a black background. It is the gold-themed variant of the Blue Starry Block.

Blue Starry Block.name: Blue Starry Block
Blue Starry Block.tooltip: The Blue Starry Block is an animated decorative block that depicts twinkling blue stars on a black background. It is the blue-themed variant of the Gold Starry Block.

Gold Starry Wall.name: Gold Starry Wall
Gold Starry Wall.tooltip: Gold Starry Wall is a background wall made from Gold Starry Blocks. It is one of only a few animated background walls.

Blue Starry Wall.name: Blue Starry Wall
Blue Starry Wall.tooltip: Blue Starry Wall is a decorative wall crafted from Blue Starry Blocks. It is one of only a few animated background walls.

Finch Staff.name: Finch Staff
Finch Staff.tooltip: The Finch Staff is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Baby Finch minion. It flies towards enemies to deal contact damage. The Finch Staff has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being found in Living Wood Chests within Living Trees. Newly created Journey Mode characters spawn with a Finch Staff. Its best modifier is Fabled.

Apricot.name: Apricot
Apricot.tooltip: The Apricot is a food and fruit item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). It has a small chance of dropping when shaking a Forest tree.

It has a small chance of dropping when shaking a regular, Corrupt, Crimson, or Hallowed Palm tree in the Ocean biome.
