Sandstone Bathtub.name: Sandstone Bathtub
Sandstone Bathtub.tooltip: Bathtubs are furniture items which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 65 / (Old-gen console version) 16 / (3DS version) 11 Bathtub types, all being functionally identical but presenting different appearances.

Sandstone Bed.name: Sandstone Bed
Sandstone Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration. Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 craftable Beds and 5 that can be acquired from the environment. All Beds are functionally identical and differ only in appearance.

Sandstone Bookcase.name: Sandstone Bookcase
Sandstone Bookcase.tooltip: Bookcases are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station used for the crafting of three Hardmode magic weapons (the Crystal Storm, Cursed Flames, and Golden Shower) as well as the Librarian furniture out of Librarian Blocks. Bookcases also fulfill a house's table requirement. There is a total of 65 types of Bookcases: 60 craftable Bookcases, and 5 looted from the environment: one from the Underworld, three from the Dungeon, and one from the Pirate Invasion. Some bookcases can also be found in Underground Cabins; their style follows the theme of the cabin where they are found.

Sandstone Dresser.name: Sandstone Dresser
Sandstone Dresser.tooltip: Dressers are a type of flat-surface furniture (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and storage item. They also fulfill house's table requirement. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 19 / (3DS version) 5 craftable versions, and (Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) 5 noncraftable versions which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Sandstone Candelabra.name: Sandstone Candelabra
Sandstone Candelabra.tooltip: Candelabras are a type of furniture and light source that emits light when placed on a flat surface such as blocks, platforms, and flat furniture items. It is not destroyed by water. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 23 /  12 craftable and 5 looted variations of the Candelabra.

Sandstone Candle.name: Sandstone Candle
Sandstone Candle.tooltip: Candles are a type of furniture and light source. Candles can only be placed on flat-surface items. Candles will produce light underwater if placed and can be toggled on and off with ⚷ Open / Activate and by mechanisms. Certain types of candles provide buffs or debuffs. The Water Candle is a special type of candle found in Dungeons which increases enemy spawn rates by 33% and the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50% when placed or held. The Peace Candle reduces spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%, in contrast to the Water Candle. The Shadow Candle(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns in the area. For Water Candles and Peace Candles, multiple candles cannot stack, even if one is placed and the other is held.

Sandstone Chair.name: Sandstone Chair
Sandstone Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Sandstone Chandelier.name: Sandstone Chandelier
Sandstone Chandelier.tooltip: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers come in many varieties which differ only in appearance and sell value. All chandeliers can be picked up using a pickaxe, drill, or explosives. Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.

Sandstone Clock.name: Sandstone Clock
Sandstone Clock.tooltip: Grandfather Clocks are furniture items which provide information about the in-game time. If a player is nearby a Grandfather Clock (about 80 tiles horizontally and 50 tiles vertically), the time is displayed on the right side of the screen, underneath the minimap. The time is rounded to the last hour, similar to Tin and Copper Watches, but pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it will show precise time in minutes as a status message on the bottom left corner. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 21 /  5 craftable versions and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 5 / (Old-gen console version) 2 noncraftable (but still lootable) versions. The regular Grandfather Clock can rarely be found in Underground Cabins. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Sandstone Door.name: Sandstone Door
Sandstone Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Sandstone Lamp.name: Sandstone Lamp
Sandstone Lamp.tooltip: Lamps are a type of furniture and light source. They also count as valid house lighting and can be toggled on and off by mechanisms. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 59 types of craftable Lamps, three types that are found in the Dungeon (Green, Blue, or Pink Dungeon Lamp), one found in Underworld houses (Obsidian Lamp), and one that can be dropped during a Pirate Invasion (Golden Lamp). Most lamps are dislodged by liquids, but Obsidian Lamp and Ash Wood Lamp are not dislodged by Lava. The Tiki Torch shares its Tile ID with the rest of these Lamps. Also see Lamp Post ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions) which does not count as valid House lighting.)

Sandstone Lantern.name: Sandstone Lantern
Sandstone Lantern.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Sandstone Piano.name: Sandstone Piano
Sandstone Piano.tooltip: Pianos are a type of furniture which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 15 /  10 craftable Pianos, and 5 non-craftable Pianos that can be found in the Dungeon, Ruined Houses, and Pirate Invasion event. Some Pianos can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin that they are found in.

Sandstone Platform.name: Sandstone Platform
Sandstone Platform.tooltip: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Sandstone Sink.name: Sandstone Sink
Sandstone Sink.tooltip: The Sink is a type of furniture item and crafting station. Like Fountains, it can be used to craft items that require water as a crafting station. There is a total of 66 Sink types, all being functionally identical.

Sandstone Sofa.name: Sandstone Sofa
Sandstone Sofa.tooltip: Sofas are furniture items which fulfill a house's chair requirement. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Players can sit in sofas by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Players can choose to sit on the left, middle, or right positions, and thus up to 3 players can sit on a sofa at a time. Sitting on sofas gives a boost to health regeneration, similar to chairs and beds. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Sofa will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 21 craftable sofas and 5 noncraftable sofas. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Sandstone Table.name: Sandstone Table
Sandstone Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Sandstone Work Bench.name: Sandstone Work Bench
Sandstone Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Sandstone Toilet.name: Sandstone Toilet
Sandstone Toilet.tooltip: Toilets are furniture items which can be placed on the ground. They are functionally similar to chairs, and fulfill a house's chair requirement. Similarly to chairs, Toilets can be sat on by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Having any tier of Well Fed active while sitting on a Toilet allows the production of Poo. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Toilet will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Toilets act as mechanisms that can be activated via wire, which makes them appear to explosively eject sewage. This effect is purely a novelty visual. Ejected sewage on the ground fades after a few seconds. There are 67 Toilets.

Haemorrhaxe.name: Haemorrhaxe
Haemorrhaxe.tooltip: The Haemorrhaxe is a Hardmode hamaxe that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Hemogoblin Sharks and Blood Eels. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Void Monolith.name: Void Monolith
Void Monolith.tooltip: Monoliths are furniture items that activate backgrounds and other screen effects normally seen during events or under other special circumstances. When placed, they can be toggled with the ⚷ Open / Activate button or via wire, like other mechanisms, providing their effects in a small area around them. Monoliths only cause modified visuals; they do not spawn any event enemies or bosses, and they do not change the music. They can also be equipped as vanity accessories, which enables their effect globally for the player. There are 11 different monoliths: the Vortex, Nebula, Stardust, Solar, and Void Monoliths can be crafted at an Ancient Manipulator, the Blood Moon Monolith has a 1/10 (10%) chance of being dropped by Dreadnautiluses, the Radio Thing has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to be dropped by Deerclops, the Aether Monolith can be obtained via dropping an Angel Statue into Shimmer, the CRT and Retro Monoliths are sold by the Cyborg for 25 Gold, and the Film Projector can be obtained as part of Heroicis' set by dropping a Platinum Coin into the Water of an Oasis. The Nebula, Solar, Stardust, and Vortex Monoliths mimic effects that normally surround the corresponding Celestial Pillar during the Lunar Events. The Blood Moon Monolith mimics the effects seen during a Blood Moon. The Void Monolith mimics the screen effects of the Moon Lord boss fight. The Radio Thing activates the same sepia filter of The Constant world seed. In The Constant seed, however, it instead deactivates the filter. The Aether Monolith mimics the screen effects of the Aether mini-biome. Unlike the other monoliths, the Aether Monolith has three states: One off state (which disables the Aether effect entirely in its area, even if it would normally be present due to Shimmer) and two on states – low, which acts as if the monolith were not present (allowing the Aether effect if enough Shimmer is nearby but not forcing it on), and high, which forces the Aether effect on. The CRT Monolith mimics the effect of an old-fashioned CRT TV. The Retro Monolith mimics the effect of an old two-color green and black monitor, like the original Gameboy. The Film Projector adds a black-and-white effect to the screen.

Arrow Sign.name: Arrow Sign
Arrow Sign.tooltip: Arrow Signs are furniture items used in Golfing. They are purely decorative and come in a regular and a painted variety. They are both purchased from the Golfer for 20 Silver each. It is possible to turn the orientation of arrows with a right-click (⚷ Open / Activate) into 8 different directions.

Painted Arrow Sign.name: Painted Arrow Sign
Painted Arrow Sign.tooltip: Arrow Signs are furniture items used in Golfing. They are purely decorative and come in a regular and a painted variety. They are both purchased from the Golfer for 20 Silver each. It is possible to turn the orientation of arrows with a right-click (⚷ Open / Activate) into 8 different directions.

Master Gamer's Jacket.name: Master Gamer's Jacket
Master Gamer's Jacket.tooltip: The Master Gamer's set is a vanity set consisting of the Master Gamer's Jacket and the Master Gamer's Pants. They are purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 10 Gold (set).

Master Gamer's Pants.name: Master Gamer's Pants
Master Gamer's Pants.tooltip: The Master Gamer's set is a vanity set consisting of the Master Gamer's Jacket and the Master Gamer's Pants. They are purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 10 Gold (set).

Star Princess Crown.name: Star Princess Crown
Star Princess Crown.tooltip: The Star Princess set is a vanity set consisting of the Star Princess Crown and Star Princess Dress. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. They are purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 1 Platinum (set), and is always sold along with the Celestial Wand.

Star Princess Dress.name: Star Princess Dress
Star Princess Dress.tooltip: The Star Princess set is a vanity set consisting of the Star Princess Crown and Star Princess Dress. Chum Caster.name: Chum Caster
Chum Caster.tooltip: Fishing poles are tools used with bait for fishing.

Plate.name: Plate
Plate.tooltip: The Plate is a decorative furniture item that can be placed. Once placed, food can be placed onto or removed from the Plate by pressing ⚷ Open / Activate.

Black Dragonfly Jar.name: Black Dragonfly Jar
Black Dragonfly Jar.tooltip: A dragonfly jar is a piece of decorative furniture created by combining a dragonfly , captured with any Bug Net , with a Bottle . By throwing a dragonfly jar into shimmer , it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the dragonfly as an item.

Blue Dragonfly Jar.name: Blue Dragonfly Jar
Blue Dragonfly Jar.tooltip: A dragonfly jar is a piece of decorative furniture created by combining a dragonfly , captured with any Bug Net , with a Bottle . By throwing a dragonfly jar into shimmer , it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the dragonfly as an item.

Green Dragonfly Jar.tooltip: A dragonfly jar is a piece of decorative furniture created by combining a dragonfly , captured with any Bug Net , with a Bottle . By throwing a dragonfly jar into shimmer , it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the dragonfly as an item.

Yellow Dragonfly Jar.tooltip: A dragonfly jar is a piece of decorative furniture created by combining a dragonfly , captured with any Bug Net , with a Bottle . By throwing a dragonfly jar into shimmer , it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the dragonfly as an item.

Gold Dragonfly Jar.name: Gold Dragonfly Jar
Gold Dragonfly Jar.tooltip: A dragonfly jar is a piece of decorative furniture created by combining a dragonfly , captured with any Bug Net , with a Bottle . By throwing a dragonfly jar into shimmer , it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the dragonfly as an item.

Black Dragonfly.name: Black Dragonfly
Black Dragonfly.tooltip: Dragonflies are small, rare critters which can be found on surface. When approached, they will fly a short distance up and away from the player. Dragonflies can only spawn during the day when the wind speed is lower than 20 mph, with their weather requirements depending on the number of nearby Town NPCs: No Town NPCs: They can only spawn when it is not raining. 1 or 2 Town NPCs: They can spawn during both clear weather and rain, though it becomes less likely for them to spawn during clear weather the more NPCs there are. 3 or more Town NPCs (Town): In Classic Mode or below, they can only spawn during rain. In Expert Mode or above, they primarily spawn during rain, but have a small chance (1/30 (3.33%) of spawn attempts) to spawn in clear weather. Furthermore, there must be at least one cattail within a 61×41-tile rectangle area centered on the spawning tile. The dragonfly will spawn on the cattail instead of the original spawning tile. As a result, they are capable of spawning on screen. Black, Orange and Yellow variants can spawn at cattails near Sand Blocks (usually in Desert), whereas Blue, Green and Red variants can spawn at cattails near pure Grass or Mowed grass (usually in Forest). Note that this is determined by the original spawning tile, not the tile the cattail grows, e.g. a Red Dragonfly can spawn on a cattail growing on a Sand Block as long as there is a Grass tile nearby. Dragonflies have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. Dragonflies can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (dragonfly jars). Once crafted, the Dragonflies cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. Dragonflies can be spawned by the Dragonfly Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so. There is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Dragonfly to spawn in place of an ordinary one.

Gold Dragonfly.name: Gold Dragonfly
Gold Dragonfly.tooltip: The Gold Dragonfly is a harmless critter. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Dragonfly, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version. The Gold Dragonfly has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Gold Dragonfly can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gold Dragonfly Jar). Once crafted, the Gold Dragonfly cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Gold Dragonfly itself or the crafted furniture can be sold for 10 Gold. The Gold Dragonfly can be used as bait for fishing, with 50% bait power. It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.

Step Stool.name: Step Stool
Step Stool.tooltip: The Step Stool is a pre-Hardmode accessory. While equipped, holding ▲ Up while stationary extends the Step Stool, granting the following effects: +2 upwards placement range (does not affect downwards range at all) Increased jump speed Increased hitbox, meaning anything that deals damage that touches the Step Stool will damage the player. The Step Stool has a 1/11 (9.09%) chance of being found inside surface Chests, or a 1/120 (0.83%) chance in Wooden Crates and Pearlwood Crates obtained from fishing. It can also be purchased for 2 Gold 50 Silver from the Skeleton Merchant during a Waning Crescent.

Dragonfly Statue.name: Dragonfly Statue
Dragonfly Statue.tooltip: Statues are furniture items. While some are purely decorative, others have a functional effect when activated via Wire—depending on the statue, it may spawn enemies, drop items, or teleport an NPC to the statue's location. Most statues can be found already placed in any area underground (most frequently in the Dungeon, Underground Cabins, and Cavern level), though Angel Statues also appear in Chests. Like all furniture, a pickaxe, a drill, or explosives are used to collect them. There are a total of 117 different statues: 25 decoration statues, 36 text and numerical statues, and 56 functional mechanisms.

Paper Airplane.name: Paper Airplane
Paper Airplane.tooltip: The Paper Airplane and White Paper Airplane are consumable ranged weapons. When thrown, they will travel in a different path each time, as they are affected by wind speed and direction, which is especially apparent on a Windy Day. The two variants are functionally identical. They are sometimes dropped by slimes that are carried by Windy Balloons, which can spawn during a Windy Day. Unlike other consumable ranged weapons, Paper Airplanes always drop as an item after flying for too long, hitting a block, or hitting an enemy.

White Paper Airplane.name: White Paper Airplane
White Paper Airplane.tooltip: The Paper Airplane and White Paper Airplane are consumable ranged weapons. When thrown, they will travel in a different path each time, as they are affected by wind speed and direction, which is especially apparent on a Windy Day. The two variants are functionally identical. They are sometimes dropped by slimes that are carried by Windy Balloons, which can spawn during a Windy Day. Unlike other consumable ranged weapons, Paper Airplanes always drop as an item after flying for too long, hitting a block, or hitting an enemy.

Can Of Worms.name: Can Of Worms
Can Of Worms.tooltip: The Can Of Worms is a consumable grab bag item, which when opened with ⚷ Open / Activate from within the player's inventory, contains 5–11 different worms. Cans Of Worms can be found in Chests on the surface.

Encumbering Stone.name: Encumbering Stone
Encumbering Stone.tooltip: The Encumbering Stone is a pre-Hardmode tool that prevents item pickup while inside the player's inventory. While in the inventory, the Encumbering Stone will prevent the pickup of any items, even if the player already has a stackable item in their inventory. The Encumbering Stone will also prevent items from being added to the Void Bag. Items reeled in from fishing are still placed in the player's inventory. Hearts and Stars will also be picked up even with the Encumbering Stone in the inventory. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Encumbering Stone in the player's inventory or hotbar will toggle it between the Encumbering Stone and Uncumbering Stone. Toggling it to the Uncumbering Stone disables its functions, allowing the player to pick up items again. The Encumbering Stone has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being found in Sandstone Chests in the Underground Desert.

Gray Zapinator.name: Gray Zapinator
Gray Zapinator.tooltip: The Gray Zapinator is a pre-Hardmode-exclusive magic gun that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 17 Gold. It is only available once King Slime, the Eye of Cthulhu, Eater of Worlds, Brain of Cthulhu, Queen Bee, Deerclops, or Skeletron has been defeated. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Orange Zapinator. The weapon fires a blue laser beam that behaves very erratically. Upon striking an enemy, the projectile slows down by 40%, decreases its current damage and knockback by 10%, and can choose from an assortment of special effects as described below. The laser beam will disappear after hitting eight enemies or after 60 seconds. While a full set of Meteor armor is equipped, it costs no mana to use. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Orange Zapinator.name: Orange Zapinator
Orange Zapinator.tooltip: The Orange Zapinator is a Hardmode magic gun that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 50 Gold. This content is transcluded from Gray Zapinator.The weapon fires a blue laser beam that behaves very erratically. Upon striking an enemy, the projectile slows down by 40%, decreases its current damage and knockback by 10%, and can choose from an assortment of special effects as described below. The laser beam will disappear after hitting eight enemies or after 60 seconds. While a full set of Meteor armor is equipped, it costs no mana to use. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Green Moss.name: Green Moss
Green Moss.tooltip: Moss is a grass-like plant that grows on Stone Blocks. It comes in 11 different variants. Mossy stone requires one more hit to break than clean stone. Moss will be destroyed if the Stone Block it is on converts to Ebonstone, Crimstone, or Pearlstone. Moss sprouts fuzz that can be cut like wild grass plants. Using a Paint Scraper or Spectre Paint Scraper to harvest moss fuzz has a 1/9 (11.11%) chance of dropping moss as a plantable item. Collected moss can be placed on Stone Blocks and Gray Bricks, or used to craft Mossy Walls. There are 5 types of regular moss: Green Moss, Brown Moss, Red Moss, Blue Moss, and Purple Moss. One of each regular moss can be found throughout each third of a given map (three variants per world). They can be found either randomly on cave surfaces or in moss chambers with a matching Mossy Wall. Glowing mosses are special variants of moss that glow in vibrant colors. These include the Lava Moss, Krypton Moss, Xenon Moss, Argon Moss, Neon Moss, and Helium Moss. Lava Moss can be found in patches around the lava layer of the Caverns. Krypton, Xenon, Argon, and Neon Moss grow in glowing moss biomes and in much larger areas than other mosses, and only one type among these can be found in each world. Up to two (small world) / three (medium world) / four (large world) glowing moss biomes will be generated in the Cavern layer, mostly above the lava layers, but not near the horizontal center of the world. Helium Moss does not spawn naturally and can instead be obtained by throwing any other glowing moss into Shimmer. Mosses that did not naturally spawn in a world can be obtained by putting any glowing moss in an Extractinator, which produces regular mosses, or a Chlorophyte Extractinator, which produces all variants of mosses. Moss Zombies spawned in surface Graveyards can also drop all variants of mosses.

Music Box (Journey's Beginning).name: Music Box (Journey's Beginning)
Music Box (Journey's Beginning).tooltip: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End), which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 Gold after defeating the Moon Lord. A recorded Music Box can be played back in one of two ways: Equipping it as an accessory. Placing it as furniture and activating it, either by the ⚷ Open / Activate button or with wires. Recorded Music Boxes can be reverted into blank ones through Shimmer transmutation. There are 101 different Music Boxes available.

When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End), which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 Gold after defeating the Moon Lord. A recorded Music Box can be played back in one of two ways: Equipping it as an accessory. Placing it as furniture and activating it, either by the ⚷ Open / Activate button or with wires. Recorded Music Boxes can be reverted into blank ones through Shimmer transmutation. There are 101 different Music Boxes available.

Music Box (Graveyard).name: Music Box (Graveyard)
Music Box (Graveyard).tooltip: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End), which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 Gold after defeating the Moon Lord. A recorded Music Box can be played back in one of two ways: Equipping it as an accessory. Placing it as furniture and activating it, either by the ⚷ Open / Activate button or with wires. Recorded Music Boxes can be reverted into blank ones through Shimmer transmutation. There are 101 different Music Boxes available.

Seagull.name: Seagull
Seagull.tooltip: The Seagull is a critter that spawns in the Ocean. It also has a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Palm tree or its Corrupt, Crimson, or Hallowed variant in the Ocean biome. Unlike Birds, it will not fly away when a player approaches. It will occasionally make typical seagull sounds, walk passively on land, and swim on the water's surface until they fall a certain distance or are approached while swimming, at which point they will switch to their alternative flying form. In their flying form, they will fly in a given direction for a certain amount of time before landing and switching back to their passive form. Despite their spawn conditions, they do not prioritize water whenever landing. The Seagull may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details. The Seagull has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Seagull can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Seagull Cage). Once crafted, the Seagull cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Seagull can be spawned by the Seagull Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.

Seagull Statue.name: Seagull Statue
Seagull Statue.tooltip: Statues are furniture items. While some are purely decorative, others have a functional effect when activated via Wire—depending on the statue, it may spawn enemies, drop items, or teleport an NPC to the statue's location. Most statues can be found already placed in any area underground (most frequently in the Dungeon, Underground Cabins, and Cavern level), though Angel Statues also appear in Chests. Like all furniture, a pickaxe, a drill, or explosives are used to collect them. There are a total of 117 different statues: 25 decoration statues, 36 text and numerical statues, and 56 functional mechanisms.

Ladybug.name: Ladybug
Ladybug.tooltip: The Ladybug is a small uncommon critter that can be found in Forests at daytime if the wind speed is greater than or equal to 20 mph. Ladybugs spawn much more frequently if the player is also in a town. The Ladybug has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Ladybug can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Ladybug Cage). Once crafted, the Ladybug cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Ladybug can be used as bait for fishing, with 17% bait power. There is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Ladybug to spawn in place of an ordinary one. Touching naturally spawned Ladybugs will temporarily increase the player's luck, while killing natural or player-released Ladybugs or consuming them as bait will temporarily decrease the player's luck and boost the chance of rain. However, using them for crafting does not affect luck, allowing the following recipes to be made consequence-free. See Ladybug luck for more details.

Gold Ladybug.name: Gold Ladybug
Gold Ladybug.tooltip: The Gold Ladybug is a harmless critter. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Ladybug, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version. The Gold Ladybug has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Gold Ladybug can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gold Ladybug Cage). Once crafted, the Gold Ladybug cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Gold Ladybug itself or the crafted furniture can be sold for 10 Gold. The Gold Ladybug can be used as bait for fishing, with 50% bait power. Touching naturally spawned Gold Ladybugs will temporarily increase the player's luck, while killing natural or player-released Gold Ladybugs or consuming them as bait will temporarily decrease the player's luck and boost the chance of rain. However, using them for crafting does not affect luck, allowing the following recipes to be made consequence-free. It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.

Maggot.name: Maggot
Maggot.tooltip: The Maggot is a critter that replaces Worms in the Graveyard biome, and can also be spawned from Maggot Zombies when they are killed. The Maggot has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Maggot can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Maggot Cage). Once crafted, the Maggot cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Maggot can be used as bait for fishing, with 22% bait power.

Maggot Cage.name: Maggot Cage
Maggot Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters. A critter caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item. Gold cages are regular cages containing gold critters. Aside from their higher sell value and rarity, they are the same as regular cages. Placed cages are partially transparent. They can be stacked on top of each other, but no other types of furniture can be placed on a cage. Players can stand on top of cages like platforms, even though they are otherwise background furniture.

Celestial Wand.name: Celestial Wand
Celestial Wand.tooltip: The Celestial Wand is a pet-summoning item that spawns Estee to follow the player. When the player is far enough away, Estee will emit a bright yellow beam trail while flying at high speed in order to catch up to them, which resembles that of a Fallen Star. The Celestial Wand can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 1 Platinum, and is always sold alongside the Star Princess set.

Eucalyptus Sap.name: Eucalyptus Sap
Eucalyptus Sap.tooltip: The Eucalyptus Sap is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Sugar Glider that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Sugar Glider flies while extending its gliding membranes to catch up to them. The Eucalyptus Sap has a small chance of dropping when the player shakes a Forest tree.

Blue Kite.name: Blue Kite
Blue Kite.tooltip: Kites are miscellaneous items that can be held by the player. A kite can be flown during Windy Days or if the player runs fast enough while holding it. It can be raised higher with ⚒ Use / Attack and lowered with ⚷ Open / Activate. Lowering a kite back to the player will make them put it away. As long as the kite is above the player's head, the player will get the High Spirits buff which will increase in duration until it maxes out at 12 minutes and 1 second. The buff has the following effects: +15% movement speed +10% mining speed +15% placement speed when placing blocks and walls Up to +0.1 luck, depending on the remaining buff duration: +0.1 with at least 9 minutes remaining +0.067 with less than 9 minutes but at least 6 minutes remaining +0.033 with less than 6 minutes but at least 3 minutes remaining 0 with less than 3 minutes remaining A kite can be placed on the ground from the hotbar with ⚷ Open / Activate if the player is not currently flying the kite. The kite initially has some upwards momentum that carries it several blocks above the stake into the air, even on a calm day.

Ivy.name: Ivy
Ivy.tooltip: The Ivy is a novelty instrument. It will always drop from the Steampunker, but only when her name is Whitney. When used, the player strums a chord depending on how far the cursor is from the player.

Pupfish.name: Pupfish
Pupfish.tooltip: The Pupfish is a critter that spawns infrequently in bodies of water in the Desert biome that are directly above Sand Blocks. Unlike many critters, Pupfish are capable of spawning on-screen. The Pupfish has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Pupfish can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Pupfish Bowl). Once crafted, the Pupfish cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.

Grebe.name: Grebe
Grebe.tooltip: The Grebe is a critter that spawns in bodies of water in the Desert biome that are directly above Sand Blocks. It may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details. The Grebe has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Grebe can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Grebe Cage). Once crafted, the Grebe cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.

Rat.name: Rat
Rat.tooltip: The Rat is a harmless critter that spawns in the Graveyard biome. The Rat has only 5 health and no defense, and can only be damaged by players. The Rat can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Rat Cage). Once crafted, the Rat cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.

Rat Cage.name: Rat Cage
Rat Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters. A critter caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item. Gold cages are regular cages containing gold critters. They can be stacked on top of each other, but no other types of furniture can be placed on a cage. Players can stand on top of cages like platforms, even though they are otherwise background furniture.

Krypton Moss.name: Krypton Moss
Krypton Moss.tooltip: Moss is a grass-like plant that grows on Stone Blocks. It comes in 11 different variants. Mossy stone requires one more hit to break than clean stone. Moss will be destroyed if the Stone Block it is on converts to Ebonstone, Crimstone, or Pearlstone. Moss sprouts fuzz that can be cut like wild grass plants. Using a Paint Scraper or Spectre Paint Scraper to harvest moss fuzz has a 1/9 (11.11%) chance of dropping moss as a plantable item. Collected moss can be placed on Stone Blocks and Gray Bricks, or used to craft Mossy Walls. There are 5 types of regular moss: Green Moss, Brown Moss, Red Moss, Blue Moss, and Purple Moss. One of each regular moss can be found throughout each third of a given map (three variants per world). They can be found either randomly on cave surfaces or in moss chambers with a matching Mossy Wall. Glowing mosses are special variants of moss that glow in vibrant colors. These include the Lava Moss, Krypton Moss, Xenon Moss, Argon Moss, Neon Moss, and Helium Moss. Lava Moss can be found in patches around the lava layer of the Caverns. Krypton, Xenon, Argon, and Neon Moss grow in glowing moss biomes and in much larger areas than other mosses, and only one type among these can be found in each world. Up to two (small world) / three (medium world) / four (large world) glowing moss biomes will be generated in the Cavern layer, mostly above the lava layers, but not near the horizontal center of the world. Helium Moss does not spawn naturally and can instead be obtained by throwing any other glowing moss into Shimmer. Mosses that did not naturally spawn in a world can be obtained by putting any glowing moss in an Extractinator, which produces regular mosses, or a Chlorophyte Extractinator, which produces all variants of mosses. Moss Zombies spawned in surface Graveyards can also drop all variants of mosses.

Blood Rain Bow.name: Blood Rain Bow
Blood Rain Bow.tooltip: The Blood Rain Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by Wandering Eye Fish and Zombie Mermen. When used, it converts any type of arrow into a spread of 1–3 streams of blood (average of 1.83 streams) to rain from the sky, directed towards the cursor. Each use only consumes one arrow. The streams dissipate upon contact with an enemy or a block. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Advanced Combat Techniques.name: Advanced Combat Techniques
Advanced Combat Techniques.tooltip: Advanced Combat Techniques is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the defense of Town NPCs by 8, their attack damage by 25%, their attack speed by 20%, and their health by 250. Advanced Combat Techniques can only be obtained by fishing during a Blood Moon. It can only be used once per world, and others cannot be fished up once one has already been used. However, multiple copies can be obtained until the first is used. The chance of fishing it up when conditions are met is 1/360 (0.28%) with 50 Fishing Power and 1/180 (0.56%) with 100 Fishing Power (assuming neither Crate Potion nor Chum Caster is used and that the body of water is not too small). When used, the status message “The book's knowledge empowers your villagers!” is displayed.

Desert Torch.name: Desert Torch
Desert Torch.tooltip: Torches are furniture items that function as light sources when placed, held, or dropped (via the Throw button). Regular Torches can be found randomly in Chests and Pots, as a bonus drop from slimes, Torch Zombies, or purchased from the Merchant or Skeleton Merchant for 50 Copper each. Placing at least 101 Torches in close proximity below the surface layer in any biome will start the Torch God mini-event. Completing the event will grant the Torch God's Favor, which allows the player to automatically convert ordinary Torches to one of the biome types.

Rolling Cactus.name: Rolling Cactus
Rolling Cactus.tooltip: The Rolling Cactus is a placeable object that behaves similarly to the Boulder. Rolling Cacti are naturally generated all throughout the Underground Desert but do not respawn once they have been activated. It is stationary when placed, and begins to move when hit by projectiles, pickaxes, or drills, or when the blocks under it are mined or hammered. Its roll direction is determined by whether its horizontal position in the world is an odd or even number, regardless of the slope of the surface it is on (unless it is blocked on one side by blocks, in which case it rolls in the other direction). When both blocks under a Rolling Cactus are removed or hammered into a half-block, it will drop vertically until it hits a surface, then bounce and roll. A Rolling Cactus projectile pierces an unlimited number of entities. When a Rolling Cactus that has already started rolling falls onto a lower surface, it maintains its forward momentum while bouncing back up, releasing 3–5 Rolling Cactus Spikes that travel in random directions. Hitting a vertical obstacle also releases Spikes, but destroys the Rolling Cactus. A Rolling Cactus' movement is affected by liquids, and it can roll uphill. A stationary Rolling Cactus deals 25 damage when a player touches it. A Rolling Cactus projectile deals 70 / 140 / 210 damage to players (35 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters) and inflicts a knockback value of 10 (Extremely strong) upon contact. Rolling Cactus Spikes deal 60 / 120 / 180 damage to players (30 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters), inflict a knockback value of 2 (Very weak), pierce entities, and break upon contact with solid tiles.

Thin Ice.name: Thin Ice
Thin Ice.tooltip: Thin Ice is a type of block found in the Snow and Ice biomes. It is found naturally in two configurations: either as a single layer over a pool of water, or in large packed regions underground. Similar to Ice Blocks, Thin Ice has reduced friction, and players will slide across it. Thin Ice will break if a player falls on it at a certain speed, usually achieved by falling normally onto it. Landing on Thin Ice will not cause fall damage itself, but it will not slow the player's fall on contact, and fall damage will continue to accumulate until the player lands on another block type (unlike Cobwebs, for instance, which reset fall damage). Ice Skates or their upgrades can be equipped to land on Thin Ice without breaking it, though this does not prevent fall damage. Thin Ice is destroyed permanently when broken, dropping nothing. On the  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version, Thin Ice cannot be picked up, crafted, or moved in any way.

Echo Block.name: Echo Block
Echo Block.tooltip: The Echo Block is a type of block which turns completely invisible once placed. It is sold by the Cyborg NPC for 10 Silver when he is spoken to in a Graveyard. Once placed, the Echo Block cannot be seen by the player unless they have the Spectre Goggles equipped or are near an Echo Chamber. Despite their invisibility, Echo Blocks retain the properties of normal blocks and can thus be hammered, actuated with an Actuator, stood and grappled on, used to hoik, and mined with any pickaxe or drill.

Scarab Fish.name: Scarab Fish
Scarab Fish.tooltip: This is the main page whose information applies to the Desktop , Console , and Mobile versions of Terraria.

Scorpio Fish.name: Scorpio Fish
Scorpio Fish.tooltip: This is the main page whose information applies to the Desktop , Console , and Mobile versions of Terraria.

Owl.name: Owl
Owl.tooltip: The Owl is a critter that spawns near Towns on the surface Forest and Hallow during the night, when it is not raining. It also has a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Forest tree at night. The Owl has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Owl can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Owl Cage). Once crafted, the Owl cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Owl can be spawned by the Owl Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.

Owl Cage.name: Owl Cage
Owl Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters. A critter caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item. Gold cages are regular cages containing gold critters. Aside from their higher sell value and rarity, they are the same as regular cages. Placed cages are partially transparent. They can be stacked on top of each other, but no other types of furniture can be placed on a cage. Players can stand on top of cages like platforms, even though they are otherwise background furniture.

Owl Statue.name: Owl Statue
Owl Statue.tooltip: Statues are furniture items. While some are purely decorative, others have a functional effect when activated via Wire—depending on the statue, it may spawn enemies, drop items, or teleport an NPC to the statue's location. Most statues can be found already placed in any area underground (most frequently in the Dungeon, Underground Cabins, and Cavern level), though Angel Statues also appear in Chests. Like all furniture, a pickaxe, a drill, or explosives are used to collect them. There are a total of 117 different statues: 25 decoration statues, 36 text and numerical statues, and 56 functional mechanisms.

Pupfish Bowl.name: Pupfish Bowl
Pupfish Bowl.tooltip: The Fish Bowl, Gold Fish Bowl (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Pupfish Bowl (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Lava Serpent Bowl (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are decorative furniture items. The Fish Bowl and Gold Fish Bowl also double as wearable items that can be equipped in the player's helmet slot. Fish Bowls cause only visual effects when placed in the helmet vanity slot. When instead placed in the functional head armor slot, the breath meter appears as if the player were underwater, and if worn long enough the player will drown and die. Breathing aids like the Breathing Reed or Gills Potion will allow for normal breathing when wearing the bowl. The Fish, Gold Fish and Pupfish Bowls are crafted, while the Lava Serpent Bowl has a 39/200 (19.5%) chance of being found inside Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates. Crafted Fish Bowls can be converted back into their ingredients by throwing them into Shimmer, gaining back the fish as an item.

Gold Ladybug Cage.name: Gold Ladybug Cage
Gold Ladybug Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters. A critter caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item. Gold cages are regular cages containing gold critters. Aside from their higher sell value and rarity, they are the same as regular cages. Placed cages are partially transparent. They can be stacked on top of each other, but no other types of furniture can be placed on a cage. Players can stand on top of cages like platforms, even though they are otherwise background furniture.

Geode.name: Geode
Geode.tooltip: The Geode is a consumable that has a 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped by Granite Elementals and Granite Golems. When used, it is thrown and drops gems upon impact with blocks. Each Geode drops 2 types of gems with 3–6 gems of each type.

Flounder.name: Flounder
Flounder.tooltip: Flounders are a type of fish which are found plentifully by fishing in the Desert biome.

Rock Lobster.name: Rock Lobster
Rock Lobster.tooltip: Rock Lobsters are a type of fishing catch which are found plentifully by fishing in the Desert biome.

Lobster Tail.name: Lobster Tail
Lobster Tail.tooltip: The Lobster Tail is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().

Inner Tube.name: Inner Tube
Inner Tube.tooltip: The Inner Tube is an accessory that has a 9/40 (22.5%) chance of being found in Water Chests, Ocean Crates, and Seaside Crates. When equipped, it causes the player to float on the surface of liquids instead of sinking to the bottom and gives +5 Fishing Power. This effect can be temporarily negated by holding ▼ Down. Additionally, when the player is in any liquid, the Inner Tube also grants the player the Flipper's effect (press ↷ Jump to swim upwards).
Inner Tube.drops_summary: Ocean Crate (22.5%), Seaside Crate (22.5%), Water Chest (22.5%)

Frozen Crate.name: Frozen Crate
Frozen Crate.tooltip: The Frozen Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can only be fished in the Snow and Ice biome. Frozen Crates contain items found in standard crates, and always contain one item normally found in Frozen Chests. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Boreal Crate.

Boreal Crate.name: Boreal Crate
Boreal Crate.tooltip: The Boreal Crate is a Hardmode crate that can only be fished in the Snow and Ice biome. Boreal Crates contain items found in standard crates, and always contain one item normally found in Frozen Chests. Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Frozen Crate.

Oasis Crate.name: Oasis Crate
Oasis Crate.tooltip: The Oasis Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can only be fished in the Desert biome. Oasis Crates contain items found in standard crates, and always contain one item normally found in a Sandstone Chest in the Underground Desert. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Mirage Crate.

Mirage Crate.name: Mirage Crate
Mirage Crate.tooltip: The Mirage Crate is a Hardmode crate that can only be fished in the Desert biome. Mirage Crates contain items found in standard crates, and always contain one item normally found in a Sandstone Chest in the Underground Desert. Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Oasis Crate.

Spectre Goggles.name: Spectre Goggles
Spectre Goggles.tooltip: The Spectre Goggles are a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron accessory which allows the player to see Echo Blocks, Echo Platforms, Echo Walls, Ghostly Stinkbug Blockers, and tiles painted with Echo Coating while equipped. They are sold by the Cyborg and Mechanic for 10 Gold when they are spoken to in a Graveyard. On the Invisible plane secret world seed, Spectre Goggles have a 1/25 (4%) of being obtained from any Chest.

Oyster.name: Oyster
Oyster.tooltip: The Oyster is a consumable grab bag item, which when opened with ⚷ Open / Activate from within the player's inventory, contains a Shucked Oyster, and has a 1/4 (25%) chance to drop (in order of increasing rarity) a White, Black, or Pink Pearl. Oysters can be acquired by fishing in the Desert biome.

Shucked Oyster.name: Shucked Oyster
Shucked Oyster.tooltip: The Shucked Oyster is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). It is guaranteed to be obtained when opening an Oyster.

White Pearl.name: White Pearl
White Pearl.tooltip: Pearls are crafting materials obtained from opening Oysters, and are used to craft Luck Potions. Each of the three pearls have different rarities, with the rarer ones being crafted into stronger potions. Additionally, when the Pink Pearl is thrown into Shimmer, it turns into a Galaxy Pearl. The player can only receive one pearl from each Oyster, with a 1/4 (25%) chance in total.

Black Pearl.name: Black Pearl
Black Pearl.tooltip: Pearls are crafting materials obtained from opening Oysters, and are used to craft Luck Potions. Each of the three pearls have different rarities, with the rarer ones being crafted into stronger potions. Additionally, when the Pink Pearl is thrown into Shimmer, it turns into a Galaxy Pearl. The player can only receive one pearl from each Oyster, with a 1/4 (25%) chance in total.

Pink Pearl.name: Pink Pearl
Pink Pearl.tooltip: Pearls are crafting materials obtained from opening Oysters, and are used to craft Luck Potions. Each of the three pearls have different rarities, with the rarer ones being crafted into stronger potions. Additionally, when the Pink Pearl is thrown into Shimmer, it turns into a Galaxy Pearl. The player can only receive one pearl from each Oyster, with a 1/4 (25%) chance in total.

Stone Door.name: Stone Door
Stone Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Stone Platform.name: Stone Platform
Stone Platform.tooltip: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Oasis Water Fountain.name: Oasis Water Fountain
Oasis Water Fountain.tooltip: Water fountains are mechanisms and crafting stations that change the color of all nearby water. They can be activated via ⚷ Open / Activate or wire. Like Sinks, they can be used to craft items that require water as a crafting station. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) The range of a fountain's effects is a radius 60 tiles horizontally and 53 tiles vertically, measured from the edges of its sprite. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 10 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 8 different obtainable fountains, all of which are purchased from the Witch Doctor for 4 Gold each at any time.  Additionally, some special world seeds contain naturally generated Water Fountains on their Floating Islands: Drunk worlds have Icy and Desert Water Fountains. Celebration Mk 10 worlds have Hallowed Water Fountains. Remix worlds have Corrupt or Crimson Water Fountains depending on the world evil. On the  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS versions, they can be purchased for free, but are only available after Plantera has been defeated.

Water Strider.name: Water Strider
Water Strider.tooltip: The Water Strider is a harmless critter that spawns on bodies of water on the Surface during the day. It only spawns near Sand or Jungle grass blocks, but not in the Ocean biome. It will not spawn if the wind speed is greater than 22.5 mph, or if it is raining. The Water Strider moves by gliding on water and hopping around on land. The Water Strider has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Water Strider can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Water Strider Cage). Once crafted, the Water Strider cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Water Strider can be used as bait for fishing, with 17% bait power. There is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Water Strider to spawn in place of an ordinary one.

Gold Water Strider.name: Gold Water Strider
Gold Water Strider.tooltip: The Gold Water Strider is a harmless critter. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Water Strider, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version. The Gold Water Strider has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Gold Water Strider can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gold Water Strider Cage). Once crafted, the Gold Water Strider cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Gold Water Strider itself or the crafted furniture can be sold for 10 Gold. The Gold Water Strider can be used as bait for fishing, with 50% bait power. It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.

Lawn Flamingo.name: Lawn Flamingo
Lawn Flamingo.tooltip: The Lawn Flamingo is a decorative furniture item that can be placed and serves no purpose other than as decoration. It can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 5 Gold.

Music Box (Underground Jungle).name: Music Box (Underground Jungle)
Music Box (Underground Jungle).tooltip: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End), which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 Gold after defeating the Moon Lord. A recorded Music Box can be played back in one of two ways: Equipping it as an accessory. Placing it as furniture and activating it, either by the ⚷ Open / Activate button or with wires. Recorded Music Boxes can be reverted into blank ones through Shimmer transmutation. There are 101 different Music Boxes available.

Grate.name: Grate
Grate.tooltip: The Grate is a foreground block which allows liquids to fall through while remaining solid for everything else, acting like a drainage system. Grates can be toggled open and closed when triggered via wire. An open Grate is transparent, allowing light and liquid through, while a closed Grate is opaque and acts as a solid block. If a Grate is triggered while liquid is passing through it, the Grate holds the liquid until it is opened again or the liquid is removed by a player, e.g. via the use of an Empty Bucket, Super Absorbant Sponge, or Dry Bomb. Bubbles function as the opposite of Grates, acting as background objects which prevent the flow of liquids through them but allow through other things like players. Grates are not destroyed when dropped in lava, despite having a rarity of .

Scarab Bomb.name: Scarab Bomb
Scarab Bomb.tooltip: The Scarab Bomb is an explosive that functions like the Sticky Bomb, but instead creates a 21-tile long and 3-tile wide shaft. The explosion will always aim away from the player's position, even after being thrown. It can be crafted, found in Oasis Crates, Mirage Crates, Sandstone Chests, or Pots in the Underground Desert.

Wrought Iron Fence.name: Wrought Iron Fence
Wrought Iron Fence.tooltip: Fences are a type of safe wall that are visually thin with most of them having transparency to allow view of the background. The only fences that have no transparency to them are Palm Fence, Rich Mahogany Fence, and Shadewood Fence. Unlike most other safe walls, they allow for wild plants and trees to grow. The safe Grass Wall, Flower Wall, and Jungle Wall are functionally identical to fences. All fences are obtained by crafting, and the Wrought Iron Fence can also be found on certain designs of the Dungeon.

Shark Bait.name: Shark Bait
Shark Bait.tooltip: The Shark Bait is a pet-summoning item that summons a pet Shark Pup. When underwater, the Shark Pup swims around freely. When out of water, it is encased in a bubble. When the player is too far away, the Shark Pup will move swiftly toward them. The Shark Bait has a 1/2 (50%) chance of being found in Water Chests and a 1/10 (10%) chance of being found in Ocean and Seaside Crates.
Shark Bait.drops_summary: Ocean Crate (10%), Seaside Crate (10%), Water Chest (50%)

Bee Minecart.name: Bee Minecart
Bee Minecart.tooltip: Minecarts are mounts that allow players to ride on Minecart Tracks. When the player is near a Minecart Track, pressing the Quick Mount hotkey or pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on a point on the track causes a Minecart to spawn, which the player is automatically placed in. Once inside, the ▶ Right and ◀ Left direction keys either accelerate, decelerate, or reverse the cart's movement. The cart will maintain its current speed and direction if no keys are pressed and no obstacles are reached. The cart can also "jump" with the ↷ Jump key. Weapons and tools, as well as most other items except hooks, can be used while riding a Minecart. The Minecart will deal damage to enemies it collides with and knock them back, with higher potency at higher speeds (see below for details). To exit the Minecart (which causes the Minecart to despawn), the player can use a hook, press the Quick Mount hotkey, or cancel the buff  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Minecart will also despawn if the player jumps off the tracks, lands on blocks, and attempts to move sideways. By default, a Wooden Minecart is spawned for the player. This can be overridden by equipping other Minecart items in the Minecart equipment slot of the player's inventory. The corresponding dye slot allows dyeing the Minecart. Using a Minecart Upgrade Kit will significantly boost the speed of all Minecarts, equip them with a laser that fires at nearby enemies, and increase the player's defense while moving. The boost effect is permanently available after using the item, though it can be toggled on and off through a probe icon next to the Minecart slot.

Scarab Fishing Rod.tooltip: Fishing poles are tools used with bait for fishing.

Witch's Broom.name: Witch's Broom
Witch's Broom.tooltip: The Witch's Broom is a Hardmode, post-Plantera mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Witch's Broom, allowing the player to fly and hover indefinitely in any direction. It is dropped by the Mourning Wood during the Pumpkin Moon event in Expert Mode with a 5–20% chance depending on the current wave.

Cluster Rocket I.name: Cluster Rocket I
Cluster Rocket I.tooltip: The Cluster Rocket I is a type of rocket ammunition. Unlike the Cluster Rocket II, it does not destroy tiles. Upon exploding, cluster rockets shoot out 6 shrapnels that create secondary explosions upon hitting enemies or after a short time, each of which deals 50% of the rocket's damage. It can be purchased from the Cyborg for 7 Silver 50 Copper each after completing the Martian Madness event.

Cluster Rocket II.name: Cluster Rocket II
Cluster Rocket II.tooltip: The Cluster Rocket II is a type of rocket ammunition. Unlike the Cluster Rocket I, it destroys tiles. Unique from other rockets, cluster rockets shoot out shrapnel that create several secondary explosions which deal half of the base damage. These secondary explosions will destroy additional tiles. Cluster Rocket IIs can be purchased from the Cyborg for 15 Silver each during a Blood Moon or Solar Eclipse after the Martian Madness event has been defeated.

Wet Rocket.name: Wet Rocket
Wet Rocket.tooltip: Liquid rockets are rocket ammunition items which place or remove liquids in addition to dealing damage. There are four different types of liquid rockets: Dry Rocket, Wet Rocket, Lava Rocket, and Honey Rocket. When a liquid rocket is fired, it will explode upon contact with enemies or blocks similarly to normal rockets, and additionally apply its special effect (see below). If, however, the rocket touches any liquid while in flight, it will immediately explode and apply its effects. All liquid rockets deal damage to nearby players, enemies, and critters. Dry Rockets are purchasable from the Cyborg for 50 Silver each at any time. They can be used to craft the other three rockets, and those can be crafted back into Dry Rockets (see below).

Lava Rocket.name: Lava Rocket
Lava Rocket.tooltip: Liquid rockets are rocket ammunition items which place or remove liquids in addition to dealing damage. There are four different types of liquid rockets: Dry Rocket, Wet Rocket, Lava Rocket, and Honey Rocket. When a liquid rocket is fired, it will explode upon contact with enemies or blocks similarly to normal rockets, and additionally apply its special effect (see below). If, however, the rocket touches any liquid while in flight, it will immediately explode and apply its effects. All liquid rockets deal damage to nearby players, enemies, and critters. Dry Rockets are purchasable from the Cyborg for 50 Silver each at any time. They can be used to craft the other three rockets, and those can be crafted back into Dry Rockets (see below).

Honey Rocket.name: Honey Rocket
Honey Rocket.tooltip: Liquid rockets are rocket ammunition items which place or remove liquids in addition to dealing damage. There are four different types of liquid rockets: Dry Rocket, Wet Rocket, Lava Rocket, and Honey Rocket. When a liquid rocket is fired, it will explode upon contact with enemies or blocks similarly to normal rockets, and additionally apply its special effect (see below). If, however, the rocket touches any liquid while in flight, it will immediately explode and apply its effects. All liquid rockets deal damage to nearby players, enemies, and critters. Dry Rockets are purchasable from the Cyborg for 50 Silver each at any time. They can be used to craft the other three rockets, and those can be crafted back into Dry Rockets (see below).

Shroom Minecart.name: Shroom Minecart
Shroom Minecart.tooltip: Minecarts are mounts that allow players to ride on Minecart Tracks. When the player is near a Minecart Track, pressing the Quick Mount hotkey or pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on a point on the track causes a Minecart to spawn, which the player is automatically placed in. Once inside, the ▶ Right and ◀ Left direction keys either accelerate, decelerate, or reverse the cart's movement. The cart will maintain its current speed and direction if no keys are pressed and no obstacles are reached. The cart can also "jump" with the ↷ Jump key. Weapons and tools, as well as most other items except hooks, can be used while riding a Minecart. The Minecart will deal damage to enemies it collides with and knock them back, with higher potency at higher speeds (see below for details). To exit the Minecart (which causes the Minecart to despawn), the player can use a hook, press the Quick Mount hotkey, or cancel the buff  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Minecart will also despawn if the player jumps off the tracks, lands on blocks, and attempts to move sideways. By default, a Wooden Minecart is spawned for the player. This can be overridden by equipping other Minecart items in the Minecart equipment slot of the player's inventory. The corresponding dye slot allows dyeing the Minecart. Using a Minecart Upgrade Kit will significantly boost the speed of all Minecarts, equip them with a laser that fires at nearby enemies, and increase the player's defense while moving. The boost effect is permanently available after using the item, though it can be toggled on and off through a probe icon next to the Minecart slot.

Sandcastle Bucket.name: Sandcastle Bucket
Sandcastle Bucket.tooltip: The Sandcastle Bucket is a tool that places a decorative sandcastle and consumes one Sand Block upon use. It can be used on all variants of Sand Blocks and platforms, in any biome. Sandcastles are background furniture objects, but they cannot be picked up; using a pickaxe or drill on them destroys them immediately. The Sandcastle Bucket can be found randomly in Water Chests, Ocean Crates, and Seaside Crates. When the cursor is moved over a valid block, one out of four sandcastle styles will be selected randomly, they can also be cycled through using the ▲ Up and ▼ Down buttons. Moving the cursor over a different block will produce a different sandcastle preview.
Sandcastle Bucket.drops_summary: Ocean Crate (10%), Seaside Crate (10%), Water Chest (50%)

Turtle Cage.name: Turtle Cage
Turtle Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters. A critter caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item. Gold cages are regular cages containing gold critters. Aside from their higher sell value and rarity, they are the same as regular cages. Placed cages are partially transparent. They can be stacked on top of each other, but no other types of furniture can be placed on a cage. Players can stand on top of cages like platforms, even though they are otherwise background furniture.

Gladius.name: Gladius
Gladius.tooltip: The Gladius is a pre-Hardmode shortsword that is dropped by Hoplites with a 1/20 (5%) chance. It attacks three times in quick succession per use, with slightly varying angles with each stab. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Turtle.name: Turtle
Turtle.tooltip: The Turtle is a critter which can spawn in bodies of water in the Forest during the day. They move slowly on land and swim at the surface of water. The Turtle has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Turtle can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Turtle Cage). Once crafted, the Turtle cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Turtle can be spawned by the Turtle Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.

Jungle Turtle.name: Jungle Turtle
Jungle Turtle.tooltip: The Jungle Turtle is a harmless critter that spawns in or near a body of water on the surface Jungle at any time. Like its Forest counterpart, it moves slowly on land and swims at the surface of water. The Jungle Turtle has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Jungle Turtle can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Jungle Turtle Cage). Once crafted, the Jungle Turtle cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Jungle Turtle can be spawned by the Turtle Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.

Turtle Statue.name: Turtle Statue
Turtle Statue.tooltip: Statues are furniture items. While some are purely decorative, others have a functional effect when activated via Wire—depending on the statue, it may spawn enemies, drop items, or teleport an NPC to the statue's location. Most statues can be found already placed in any area underground (most frequently in the Dungeon, Underground Cabins, and Cavern level), though Angel Statues also appear in Chests. Like all furniture, a pickaxe, a drill, or explosives are used to collect them. There are a total of 117 different statues: 25 decoration statues, 36 text and numerical statues, and 56 functional mechanisms.
