Lesser Luck Potion.name: Lesser Luck Potion
Lesser Luck Potion.tooltip: The Luck Potions are three types of buff potions which grant the Lucky buff, increasing the player's luck. This lasts for 5–15 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().  Consuming a Lesser, regular, or Greater Luck Potion grants 5, 10, or 15 minutes of the Lucky buff, respectively. The buff is unique in that its effectiveness depends on the remaining duration, which is shown below: The values do not stack, and the only difference between the Luck Potions is the duration of the effect:  Consuming a Lesser Luck Potion (5 minutes of Lucky) gives +0.1 luck for 5 minutes. Consuming a regular Luck Potion (10 minutes of Lucky) gives +0.2 luck for 5 minutes, then +0.1 luck for 5 minutes. Consuming a Greater Luck Potion (15 minutes of Lucky) gives +0.3 luck for 5 minutes, then +0.2 luck for 5 minutes, and then +0.1 luck for 5 minutes.

Seahorse.name: Seahorse
Seahorse.tooltip: The Seahorse is a critter that spawns in the Ocean. They occasionally move in water by swimming in bursts at random directions. The Seahorse has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Seahorse can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Seahorse Cage). Once crafted, the Seahorse cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. There is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance for a Gold Seahorse to spawn in place of an ordinary one.

A critter caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item. Gold cages are regular cages containing gold critters. Gold Seahorse.name: Gold Seahorse
Gold Seahorse.tooltip: The Gold Seahorse is a harmless critter. It is a golden recolor of the ordinary Seahorse, with a 1/400 (0.25%) chance of spawning in place of the ordinary version. The Gold Seahorse has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.

1/2 Second Timer.name: 1/2 Second Timer
1/2 Second Timer.tooltip: Timers are triggering mechanisms that periodically send an activation signal to other mechanisms. There are five different types of timers, which differ in the interval at which the signal is sent: 5 Second Timer, 3 Second Timer, 1 Second Timer, 1/2 Second Timer, and 1/4 Second Timer. Timers need to be placed in order to function; they can be placed freely in the air, allowing platforms and walls to be built off of them. They are toggled on and off by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Timers can also be activated and deactivated using other mechanism activation items. For example, a Switch on the same path of Wire will toggle a timer on and off. Multiple timers on the same circuit will also repeatedly toggle each other on and off. All timers can be purchased from the Mechanic, while some can also be crafted.

Cinder Wall.tooltip: The Obsidian Wall, Ember Wall, Cinder Wall, Magma Wall, and Smouldering Stone Wall are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the lower Cavern layer, considered unsafe. They do not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained on the  Desktop,  Console, and  Mobile, via crafting. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player. The Ember, Cinder, Magma, and Smouldering Stone Walls are unavailable on the  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS version.

The Bride Banner.name: The Bride Banner
The Bride Banner.tooltip: Enemy banners are functional furniture items that can be placed on the underside of blocks and platforms. They are obtained by killing most enemies and a few critters. When placed, enemy banners provide a Banner buff to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the banner. The buff grants players +50%/+100% damage inflicted with all damage to the corresponding enemy and −25%/−50% damage taken from attacks by the enemy. The banners of Old One's Army enemies will apply a weaker banner buff to the respective enemy, granting the players +10%/+20% damage inflicted and −8.33% / −16.67% damage taken. Multiple banners of the same type will not grant stacked buffs. Multiple different banner types in the vicinity will, however, all take effect and consolidate into a single buff icon. There are a total of 286 obtainable enemy banners: 115 in pre-Hardmode, 171 in Hardmode. Out of these, 118 belong to event enemies (28 in pre-Hardmode and 90 in Hardmode). In addition, there are 6 unobtainable enemy banners.

Large Bamboo.name: Large Bamboo
Large Bamboo.tooltip: Large Bamboo is a block created from Bamboo that visually appears to be one large stalk as opposed to several bundled together.

Large Bamboo Wall.name: Large Bamboo Wall
Large Bamboo Wall.tooltip: Large Bamboo Wall is a wall created from Large Bamboo that visually appears to be made of larger stalks than Bamboo Wall.

Demon Horns.name: Demon Horns
Demon Horns.tooltip: The Demon Horns are a vanity item purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 Gold 50 Silver.

Bamboo Leaf.name: Bamboo Leaf
Bamboo Leaf.tooltip: The Bamboo Leaf is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Red Panda to follow the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Baby Red Panda will fly towards them while surfing on a bamboo leaf to catch up to them. The Bamboo Leaf can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 75 Gold.

Slice of Hell Cake.name: Slice of Hell Cake
Slice of Hell Cake.tooltip: The Slice of Hell Cake is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Imp to follow the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Baby Imp will spread its arms and fly to catch up to them. The Slice of Hell Cake has a 1/10 (10%) chance of being found in Shadow Chests and a 1/20 (5%) chance of being found in Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates.
Slice of Hell Cake.drops_summary: Hellstone Crate (5%), Obsidian Crate (5%), Shadow Chest (10%)

Fog Machine.name: Fog Machine
Fog Machine.tooltip: The Fog Machine is a placed novelty mechanism that is purchased from the Party Girl for 4 Gold at night. When placed, it produces fog cloud effects around itself. It can be toggled on and off via Wire. The fog is purely visual, has no functional effect, and can be produced infinitely at no cost.

Plasma Lamp.name: Plasma Lamp
Plasma Lamp.tooltip: The Plasma Lamp is a mechanism item that emits a faint blue light and has an animated texture. It is not considered a suitable light source for an NPC house. It is used purely as a decorative light source. The Plasma Lamp can be purchased from the Party Girl for 2 Gold.

Marble Column.name: Marble Column
Marble Column.tooltip: Beams or columns are background furniture items that provide support for Torches and can be used as decoration. They form continuous vertical pillars when stacked. They are found naturally in Underground Cabins, and can be crafted. Beams and columns can be stacked from the ground, and exist in the background, providing support for suspended Torches that will not inhibit character movement. In this way, beams and columns provide a function similar to trees (which also exist in the background and allow the player to suspend high Torches), but which the player can construct where they like. Where background walls exist, beams and columns can also be placed in "midair", without support from below. Despite their appearance as background walls, beams and columns instead share a layer with other furniture items (like tables, Torches, statues, Switches, timers, etc.), thus the two cannot share the same tile space. They can also prevent a door from opening.

Chef Hat.name: Chef Hat
Chef Hat.tooltip: The Chef set is a set of Vanity items made up of the Chef Hat, the Chef Uniform, and the Chef Pants. It is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 7 Gold 50 Silver (set).

Chef Uniform.name: Chef Uniform
Chef Uniform.tooltip: The Chef set is a set of Vanity items made up of the Chef Hat, the Chef Uniform, and the Chef Pants. It is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 7 Gold 50 Silver (set).

Chef Pants.name: Chef Pants
Chef Pants.tooltip: The Chef set is a set of Vanity items made up of the Chef Hat, the Chef Uniform, and the Chef Pants. It is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 7 Gold 50 Silver (set).

Star Hairpin.name: Star Hairpin
Star Hairpin.tooltip: The Star Hairpin is a vanity item that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 Gold. It is worn in the helmet slot.

Heart Hairpin.name: Heart Hairpin
Heart Hairpin.tooltip: The Heart Hairpin is a vanity item that is sold by the Traveling Merchant for 2 Gold. It is worn in the helmet slot.

Bunny Ears.name: Bunny Ears
Bunny Ears.tooltip: The Bunny set is a vanity set composed of the Bunny Tail and Bunny Ears. It can be purchased from the Zoologist during a First Quarter or a Waxing Gibbous for 6 Gold (set).

Devil Horns.name: Devil Horns
Devil Horns.tooltip: The Devil Horns are a vanity item that can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 Gold 50 Silver. Unlike Demon Horns, they do not hide the player's hair.

Fedora.name: Fedora
Fedora.tooltip: The Fedora is a vanity item purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 Gold 50 Silver.

Fake Unicorn Horn.name: Fake Unicorn Horn
Fake Unicorn Horn.tooltip: The Fake Unicorn Horn is a vanity accessory purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 Gold 50 Silver.

Bamboo.name: Bamboo
Bamboo.tooltip: Bamboo is a placeable block obtained by harvesting Bamboo stalks, which generate naturally in the Jungle biome, with any pickaxe or drill.

Bamboo Wall.name: Bamboo Wall
Bamboo Wall.tooltip: Bamboo Wall is a type of wall. As with most crafted walls, Bamboo Walls are compatible with NPC housing and will stop enemies from spawning.

Bamboo Bathtub.name: Bamboo Bathtub
Bamboo Bathtub.tooltip: Bathtubs are furniture items which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 65 / (Old-gen console version) 16 / (3DS version) 11 Bathtub types, all being functionally identical but presenting different appearances.

Bamboo Bed.name: Bamboo Bed
Bamboo Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration. Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 craftable Beds and 5 that can be acquired from the environment. All Beds are functionally identical and differ only in appearance.

Bamboo Bookcase.name: Bamboo Bookcase
Bamboo Bookcase.tooltip: Bookcases are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station used for the crafting of three Hardmode magic weapons (the Crystal Storm, Cursed Flames, and Golden Shower) as well as the Librarian furniture out of Librarian Blocks. Bookcases also fulfill a house's table requirement. There is a total of 65 types of Bookcases: 60 craftable Bookcases, and 5 looted from the environment: one from the Underworld, three from the Dungeon, and one from the Pirate Invasion. Some bookcases can also be found in Underground Cabins; their style follows the theme of the cabin where they are found.

Bamboo Dresser.name: Bamboo Dresser
Bamboo Dresser.tooltip: Dressers are a type of flat-surface furniture (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and storage item. They also fulfill house's table requirement. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 19 / (3DS version) 5 craftable versions, and (Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) 5 noncraftable versions which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Bamboo Candelabra.name: Bamboo Candelabra
Bamboo Candelabra.tooltip: Candelabras are a type of furniture and light source that emits light when placed on a flat surface such as blocks, platforms, and flat furniture items. It is not destroyed by water. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 23 /  12 craftable and 5 looted variations of the Candelabra.

Bamboo Candle.name: Bamboo Candle
Bamboo Candle.tooltip: Candles are a type of furniture and light source. Candles can only be placed on flat-surface items. Candles will produce light underwater if placed and can be toggled on and off with ⚷ Open / Activate and by mechanisms. Certain types of candles provide buffs or debuffs. The Water Candle is a special type of candle found in Dungeons which increases enemy spawn rates by 33% and the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50% when placed or held. The Peace Candle reduces spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%, in contrast to the Water Candle. The Shadow Candle(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns in the area. For Water Candles and Peace Candles, multiple candles cannot stack, even if one is placed and the other is held.

Bamboo Chair.name: Bamboo Chair
Bamboo Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Bamboo Chandelier.name: Bamboo Chandelier
Bamboo Chandelier.tooltip: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers come in many varieties which differ only in appearance and sell value. All chandeliers can be picked up using a pickaxe, drill, or explosives. Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.

Bamboo Chest.name: Bamboo Chest
Bamboo Chest.tooltip: Chests are a type of furniture functioning as storage items. They are accessed using ⚷ Open / Activate and can store up to 40 item stacks in rows of  10×4 /   8×5. In addition to many being craftable, a number of Chests are placed in random locations during world generation. The loot contained in these Chests is determined during world generation, and will not change if the world enters Hardmode. Chests cannot be broken with items inside (the blocks a filled Chest is placed on would also have this trait). However, the Block Swap feature allows the player to change the type of a Chest without having to destroy it. Some types of Chests can be locked by the player using a Chest Lock. When doing so, they will require a key to open again. There are 23 varieties of naturally-occurring Chests (12 of which cannot be crafted), 53 that can only be crafted, and 1 purchasable Chest, for a total of 77 Chest types.

Bamboo Clock.name: Bamboo Clock
Bamboo Clock.tooltip: Grandfather Clocks are furniture items which provide information about the in-game time. If a player is nearby a Grandfather Clock (about 80 tiles horizontally and 50 tiles vertically), the time is displayed on the right side of the screen, underneath the minimap. The time is rounded to the last hour, similar to Tin and Copper Watches, but pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it will show precise time in minutes as a status message on the bottom left corner. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 21 /  5 craftable versions and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 5 / (Old-gen console version) 2 noncraftable (but still lootable) versions. The regular Grandfather Clock can rarely be found in Underground Cabins. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Bamboo Door.name: Bamboo Door
Bamboo Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Bamboo Lamp.name: Bamboo Lamp
Bamboo Lamp.tooltip: Lamps are a type of furniture and light source. They also count as valid house lighting and can be toggled on and off by mechanisms. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 59 types of craftable Lamps, three types that are found in the Dungeon (Green, Blue, or Pink Dungeon Lamp), one found in Underworld houses (Obsidian Lamp), and one that can be dropped during a Pirate Invasion (Golden Lamp). Most lamps are dislodged by liquids, but Obsidian Lamp and Ash Wood Lamp are not dislodged by Lava. The Tiki Torch shares its Tile ID with the rest of these Lamps. Also see Lamp Post ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions) which does not count as valid House lighting.)

Bamboo Lantern.name: Bamboo Lantern
Bamboo Lantern.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Bamboo Piano.name: Bamboo Piano
Bamboo Piano.tooltip: Pianos are a type of furniture which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 15 /  10 craftable Pianos, and 5 non-craftable Pianos that can be found in the Dungeon, Ruined Houses, and Pirate Invasion event. Some Pianos can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin that they are found in.

Bamboo Platform.name: Bamboo Platform
Bamboo Platform.tooltip: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Bamboo Sink.name: Bamboo Sink
Bamboo Sink.tooltip: The Sink is a type of furniture item and crafting station. Like Fountains, it can be used to craft items that require water as a crafting station. There is a total of 66 Sink types, all being functionally identical.

Bamboo Sofa.name: Bamboo Sofa
Bamboo Sofa.tooltip: Sofas are furniture items which fulfill a house's chair requirement. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Players can sit in sofas by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Players can choose to sit on the left, middle, or right positions, and thus up to 3 players can sit on a sofa at a time. Sitting on sofas gives a boost to health regeneration, similar to chairs and beds. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Sofa will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 21 craftable sofas and 5 noncraftable sofas. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Bamboo Table.name: Bamboo Table
Bamboo Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Bamboo Work Bench.name: Bamboo Work Bench
Bamboo Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Trapped Bamboo Chest.name: Trapped Bamboo Chest
Trapped Bamboo Chest.tooltip: A Trapped Chest is a mechanical item that has the appearance of a normal chest. It cannot be used for storage, as it does not have any storage slots. When it is opened, it emits a signal and can be connected with wire. Any chest can be crafted into a Trapped Chest at the Heavy Assembler with the desired chest and 10 wire. The Trapped Chest can be sold for 1 Silver.

Bamboo Toilet.name: Bamboo Toilet
Bamboo Toilet.tooltip: Toilets are furniture items which can be placed on the ground. They are functionally similar to chairs, and fulfill a house's chair requirement. Similarly to chairs, Toilets can be sat on by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Having any tier of Well Fed active while sitting on a Toilet allows the production of Poo. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Toilet will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Toilets act as mechanisms that can be activated via wire, which makes them appear to explosively eject sewage. This effect is purely a novelty visual. Ejected sewage on the ground fades after a few seconds. There are 67 Toilets.

Worn Golf Club (Iron).name: Worn Golf Club (Iron)
Worn Golf Club (Iron).tooltip: Golf Clubs are tools used in the golf minigame. There are four types of Golf Clubs, the Driver, Iron, Wedge, and Putter, which are each used to hit the Golf Ball a different horizontal and vertical distance. Special variants of Golf Clubs can be unlocked by achieving different golf scores. All upgrades are purely aesthetic, despite being more expensive as the tier increases. They do not harm enemies or critters.

Worn Golf Club (Putter).name: Worn Golf Club (Putter)
Worn Golf Club (Putter).tooltip: Golf Clubs are tools used in the golf minigame. There are four types of Golf Clubs, the Driver, Iron, Wedge, and Putter, which are each used to hit the Golf Ball a different horizontal and vertical distance. Special variants of Golf Clubs can be unlocked by achieving different golf scores. All upgrades are purely aesthetic, despite being more expensive as the tier increases. They do not harm enemies or critters.

Worn Golf Club (Wedge).name: Worn Golf Club (Wedge)
Worn Golf Club (Wedge).tooltip: Golf Clubs are tools used in the golf minigame. There are four types of Golf Clubs, the Driver, Iron, Wedge, and Putter, which are each used to hit the Golf Ball a different horizontal and vertical distance. Special variants of Golf Clubs can be unlocked by achieving different golf scores. All upgrades are purely aesthetic, despite being more expensive as the tier increases. They do not harm enemies or critters.

Worn Golf Club (Driver).name: Worn Golf Club (Driver)
Worn Golf Club (Driver).tooltip: Golf Clubs are tools used in the golf minigame. There are four types of Golf Clubs, the Driver, Iron, Wedge, and Putter, which are each used to hit the Golf Ball a different horizontal and vertical distance. Special variants of Golf Clubs can be unlocked by achieving different golf scores. All upgrades are purely aesthetic, despite being more expensive as the tier increases. They do not harm enemies or critters.

Dreadnautilus Banner.name: Dreadnautilus Banner
Dreadnautilus Banner.tooltip: Enemy banners are functional furniture items that can be placed on the underside of blocks and platforms. They are obtained by killing most enemies and a few critters. When placed, enemy banners provide a Banner buff to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the banner. The buff grants players +50%/+100% damage inflicted with all damage to the corresponding enemy and −25%/−50% damage taken from attacks by the enemy. The banners of Old One's Army enemies will apply a weaker banner buff to the respective enemy, granting the players +10%/+20% damage inflicted and −8.33% / −16.67% damage taken. Multiple banners of the same type will not grant stacked buffs. Multiple different banner types in the vicinity will, however, all take effect and consolidate into a single buff icon. There are a total of 286 obtainable enemy banners: 115 in pre-Hardmode, 171 in Hardmode. Out of these, 118 belong to event enemies (28 in pre-Hardmode and 90 in Hardmode). In addition, there are 6 unobtainable enemy banners.

Birdie Rattle.name: Birdie Rattle
Birdie Rattle.tooltip: The Birdie Rattle is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Lil' Harpy that follows the player. The Lil' Harpy, when summoned, will fly above and behind the player, and will behave similar to the Zephyr Fish, continually flying around and looking side to side. It will never land and can fly through blocks. The Birdie Rattle can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 50 Gold.

Exotic Chew Toy.name: Exotic Chew Toy
Exotic Chew Toy.tooltip: The Exotic Chew Toy is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Fennec Fox that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Fennec Fox pet will fly by flapping its ears like wings to catch up to them. The Exotic Chew Toy can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 1 Platinum.

Bedazzled Nectar.name: Bedazzled Nectar
Bedazzled Nectar.tooltip: The Bedazzled Nectar is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Glittery Butterfly that follows the player. The Bedazzled Nectar has a chance of being sold by the Traveling Merchant for 1 Platinum.

Music Box (Jungle Night).name: Music Box (Jungle Night)
Music Box (Jungle Night).tooltip: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End), which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 Gold after defeating the Moon Lord. A recorded Music Box can be played back in one of two ways: Equipping it as an accessory. Placing it as furniture and activating it, either by the ⚷ Open / Activate button or with wires. Recorded Music Boxes can be reverted into blank ones through Shimmer transmutation. There are 101 different Music Boxes available.

Desert Tiger Staff.name: Desert Tiger Staff
Desert Tiger Staff.tooltip: The Desert Tiger Staff is a Hardmode, post-Plantera summon weapon that summons a Desert Tiger minion. It runs towards enemies to deal contact damage. Every six seconds, the tiger can perform a pounce attack at nearby enemies, dealing 50% extra damage (+20 base damage) and passing through blocks to reach them. When the Desert Tiger Staff is used more than once, multiple Desert Tigers do not spawn; instead, the existing Desert Tiger becomes stronger (+16/+17 damage; 40% of the weapon's listed damage, which is additive to pounce's 50%) and faster for each additional summon. The Desert Tiger appears as a cub if summoned 1 to 3 times, an adult if summoned 4 to 6 times, and an armored adult if summoned 7 or more times. The Desert Tiger Staff is always found in the Dungeon's Desert Chest, which can only be unlocked with a Desert Key after Plantera has been defeated. Its best modifier is Fabled. However, if the player's summon damage bonuses reach a certain threshold (including whip bonuses), the best modifier becomes Ruthless. The exact threshold varies depending on the number of summons, which is listed in Notes below.

Chum Bucket.name: Chum Bucket
Chum Bucket.tooltip: The Chum Bucket is a consumable item that increases Fishing Power when thrown into a liquid. Chum Buckets have a 1/2 (50%) chance of being dropped from Blood Moon enemies: Wandering Eye Fish and Zombie Mermen drop it in stacks of 4–6, and Hemogoblin Sharks, Blood Eels, and Dreadnautiluses in stacks of 7–10. All of these enemies have a chance to spawn while fishing during a Blood Moon. The Fishing Power bonus depends on how many Chum Buckets are present on the liquid's surface. A single bucket used will increase Fishing Power by 11, two for a total of 17, and finally three for a total of 20. This bonus is added after all other fishing factors; therefore, unlike other fishing gear, it is not influenced by time factors. See the relevant section on Fishing for details. Each bucket present in the pool lasts up to 10 times reeling in the line, even if nothing is on the line or if the line breaks. Reeling in the line reduces the lifetime of all Chum Buckets in the same body of liquid, rather than just one Chum Bucket. Having any Chum Buckets present on the water's surface will multiply Shark spawn rates by 5× and Orca spawn rates by 2.78×.

Garden Gnome.name: Garden Gnome
Garden Gnome.tooltip: The Garden Gnome is a small furniture item formed when a Gnome touches sunlight. A placed Garden Gnome positively influences the player's Luck stat by 0.2. The buff is applied to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the Garden Gnome, similar to the Heart Lantern. Additional Garden Gnomes do not increase luck further. Garden Gnomes have five different sprites when placed (which are functionally identical): Facing a direction with their arms akimbo. Facing a direction while slouching. Facing a direction with their arms on their side. Mooning their bottom toward the screen. Facing the screen. The ▲ Up and ▼ Down buttons cycle which sprite will be placed.

Bone Serpent Kite.name: Bone Serpent Kite
Bone Serpent Kite.tooltip: Kites are miscellaneous items that can be held by the player. A kite can be flown during Windy Days or if the player runs fast enough while holding it. It can be raised higher with ⚒ Use / Attack and lowered with ⚷ Open / Activate. Lowering a kite back to the player will make them put it away. As long as the kite is above the player's head, the player will get the High Spirits buff which will increase in duration until it maxes out at 12 minutes and 1 second. The buff has the following effects: +15% movement speed +10% mining speed +15% placement speed when placing blocks and walls Up to +0.1 luck, depending on the remaining buff duration: +0.1 with at least 9 minutes remaining +0.067 with less than 9 minutes but at least 6 minutes remaining +0.033 with less than 6 minutes but at least 3 minutes remaining 0 with less than 3 minutes remaining A kite can be placed on the ground from the hotbar with ⚷ Open / Activate if the player is not currently flying the kite. The kite initially has some upwards momentum that carries it several blocks above the stake into the air, even on a calm day.

Andrew Sphinx.name: Andrew Sphinx
Andrew Sphinx.tooltip: Paintings are decorative furniture items that can be placed on background walls. Each one is a framed image that depicts a particular scene, usually Terraria-related. Their tooltips generally contain a person's name, intended to credit each painting's artist; although the names appear to be fictional, most of them correspond to known Terraria developers, artists, testing staff, and community members (see Trivia below). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions, the Magic Lantern, Spelunker Glowsticks, and Spelunker Flares. There are a total of 193 paintings, 25 of which are sold by the Painter, 7 by the Princess, 4 by the Golfer, 2 by the Zoologist, 2 by the Clothier, 1 by the Truffle, and 27 are randomly sold by the Traveling Merchant. 35 paintings can be found in Underground Cabins, another 14 in the Underground Desert Cabins, 26 in the Dungeon, 12 in The Underworld, 6 from Floating Islands, 5 obtained by fishing, 1 from the Jungle Temple, 5 randomly acquired from Goodie Bags, 8 dropped by Solar Eclipse enemies, 8 awarded randomly by the Angler for completing fishing quests, 1 from the Living Tree, and 4 dropped by enemies.

Oasis.name: Oasis
Oasis.tooltip: The Oasis is a naturally spawning mini-biome that can be found on the Surface layer of the Desert biome. It consists of a sizable body of water surrounded by multiple palm trees and shrubbery such as mini cacti, ferns, and flowers. Cattail plants grow in the lake and there are often multiple Dragonflies flying around and above the surface of the water. The water of the Oasis is a turquoise color, just like that of regular surface Desert water. An Oasis Water Fountain can be purchased in order to replicate this water color at a location of choice. As a mini-biome, the Oasis is not considered to be a separate biome from the Desert: the Oasis counts as a Desert in terms of an NPC's preferred biome, the Oasis will spawn Desert-exclusive critters and enemies, and fishing in an Oasis will yield the same results as fishing in a Desert. Thus, it is possible to create an artificial Oasis by placing water in the surface layer of a Desert biome.

Amber Stone Wall.name: Amber Stone Wall
Amber Stone Wall.tooltip: The Gemstone Walls are types of background walls. Except for the Amber Stone Wall, they can be found naturally generated in Gemstone Caves, considered unsafe. They do not drop as an item when destroyed, and can only be obtained on the  Desktop,  Console, and  Mobile, via crafting. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player.

Man Eater Kite.name: Man Eater Kite
Man Eater Kite.tooltip: Kites are miscellaneous items that can be held by the player. A kite can be flown during Windy Days or if the player runs fast enough while holding it. It can be raised higher with ⚒ Use / Attack and lowered with ⚷ Open / Activate. Lowering a kite back to the player will make them put it away. As long as the kite is above the player's head, the player will get the High Spirits buff which will increase in duration until it maxes out at 12 minutes and 1 second. The buff has the following effects: +15% movement speed +10% mining speed +15% placement speed when placing blocks and walls Up to +0.1 luck, depending on the remaining buff duration: +0.1 with at least 9 minutes remaining +0.067 with less than 9 minutes but at least 6 minutes remaining +0.033 with less than 6 minutes but at least 3 minutes remaining 0 with less than 3 minutes remaining A kite can be placed on the ground from the hotbar with ⚷ Open / Activate if the player is not currently flying the kite. The kite initially has some upwards momentum that carries it several blocks above the stake into the air, even on a calm day.

Pink Fairy Jar.name: Pink Fairy Jar
Pink Fairy Jar.tooltip: Fairy jars are animated decorative furniture items, crafted using a Bottle and their respective fairy. By throwing a fairy jar into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the fairy as an item.  Fairy jars can be placed on top of solid blocks and platforms, and give off a faint light. They function as light sources (but will not function as a valid one for housing) and illuminate underwater, but are not controllable mechanisms like some other light sources.

Fogbound Dye.name: Fogbound Dye
Fogbound Dye.tooltip: Fogbound Dye is a dye purchased from the Dye Trader while in a Graveyard for 7 Gold 50 Silver. When equipped, it reduces the color saturation of the item and gives it a grayer tone, with a fog-like effect overlaying on top of the item.

Bloodbath Dye.name: Bloodbath Dye
Bloodbath Dye.tooltip: Bloodbath Dye is a dye purchased from the Dye Trader during a Blood Moon for 7 Gold 50 Silver. When applied, it gives the item an appearance similar to dripping blood.

Pretty Pink Dress.name: Pretty Pink Dress
Pretty Pink Dress.tooltip: The Pretty Pink set is a vanity set consisting of the Pretty Pink Ribbon, Pretty Pink Dress, and Pretty Pink Stockings. The set is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 55 Gold (set). These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Bamboo Fence.name: Bamboo Fence
Bamboo Fence.tooltip: Fences are a type of safe wall that are visually thin with most of them having transparency to allow view of the background. The only fences that have no transparency to them are Palm Fence, Rich Mahogany Fence, and Shadewood Fence. Unlike most other safe walls, they allow for wild plants and trees to grow. The safe Grass Wall, Flower Wall, and Jungle Wall are functionally identical to fences. All fences are obtained by crafting, and the Wrought Iron Fence can also be found on certain designs of the Dungeon.

Illuminant Coating.name: Illuminant Coating
Illuminant Coating.tooltip: Paint is used to modify the color of objects. Nearly anything can be painted, including blocks, background walls, and furniture, along with non-collectable environment objects like trees, tall grass, flowers, and other ambient growth. Basic paint is purchased from the Painter NPC. Two of the same color can be combined at a Dye Vat to create "deep" color versions, which apply their color more vividly and are required in order to paint certain objects. Coating(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is used to apply a special effect over a block and can be applied in tandem with paint and other coatings. It is purchased from the Painter NPC. Paint and coatings are applied to blocks and furniture with the Paintbrush, and to walls with the Paint Roller, with each tile consuming one item of paint/coating. The Paint Sprayer will automatically paint items when placing them. Paint and coatings can be removed with the Paint Scraper, although they will never be retrieved upon doing so. Destroying a painted block will not drop the paint item either. Paint can be placed in ammo slots. If more than one type of paint or coating is present in the player's inventory, the paint or coating in the earliest inventory slot is used first (starting from the top-left slot).

Leather Whip.name: Leather Whip
Leather Whip.tooltip: The Leather Whip is a pre-Hardmode whip that is virtually always available to be purchased from the Zoologist for 5 Gold (save for certain scenarios). It has a 50% multihit penalty, and inflicts 4 tag damage on enemies. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Drumstick.name: Drumstick
Drumstick.tooltip: The Drum Set is a novelty furniture item used in conjunction with the Drumstick to produce drum sounds. The Drum Set and Drumstick can be purchased from the Merchant for 10 Gold and 50 Silver respectively after either the Eater of Worlds, the Brain of Cthulhu, Skeletron, or the Wall of Flesh has been defeated. To play drum sounds, the player holding the Drumstick must be standing directly over the Drum Set and press ⚒ Use / Attack. The particular drum sound played is determined by the distance from the character to the cursor. From closest to farthest, by distance from the player (approximate percentage of the screen away from the character): 0-2.5%: Kick Drum 2.5-5%: Low Tom 5-7.5%: Mid Tom 7.5-11%: Hi Tom 11-13.3%: Snare Drum 13.3-16.6%: Floor Tom 16.6-19%: Hi-Hat (closed) 19-22.5%: Hi-Hat (open) 22.5-25%: Cymbal 1 25%+: Cymbal 2

Durendal.tooltip: The Durendal is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss whip. It has a 20% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit: 9 tag damage Marks enemies with enchanted energy. When a minion or sentry strikes an enemy marked by the Durendal, the hit deals 30 extra damage and a visual bright flash appears. The mark expires after its effect is triggered once, meaning the enemy must be tagged again to reapply it, but the tag damage will still last for its usual duration. Grants the Durendal's Blessing buff, increasing whip speed by 25% for 3 seconds. This duration can be refreshed with further hits. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Morning Star.name: Morning Star
Morning Star.tooltip: The Morning Star is a Hardmode, post-Plantera whip that has a 1/200 (0.5%) / 399/40,000 (0.9975%) chance of being dropped by Blue Armored Bones, Rusty Armored Bones, and Hell Armored Bones in the Hardmode Dungeon. It has a 5% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit: 8 tag damage 10% tag critical strike chance Its best modifier is Legendary.
Morning Star.drops_summary: Blue Armored Bones (0.5%), Hell Armored Bones (0.5%), Rusty Armored Bones (0.5%)

Dark Harvest.name: Dark Harvest
Dark Harvest.tooltip: The Dark Harvest is a Hardmode, post-Plantera whip that is dropped by Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event with a 2.5–12.5% (6.25–12.5%) chance depending on the current wave. It has a 10% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit: 15 tag damage Marks enemies with dark energy. When a minion or sentry damages an enemy marked by the Dark Harvest, it triggers a Reaping effect, causing up to 3 nearby targets to take 15 damage. Reaping is not affected by any damage bonuses and has 50 armor penetration. The dark energy is not consumed upon activating its effect and its duration can be refreshed. Grants the Harvest Time buff, increasing whip speed by 35% for 3 seconds. This duration can be refreshed with further hits. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Spectrum Kite.name: Spectrum Kite
Spectrum Kite.tooltip: Kites are miscellaneous items that can be held by the player. A kite can be flown during Windy Days or if the player runs fast enough while holding it. It can be raised higher with ⚒ Use / Attack and lowered with ⚷ Open / Activate. Lowering a kite back to the player will make them put it away. As long as the kite is above the player's head, the player will get the High Spirits buff which will increase in duration until it maxes out at 12 minutes and 1 second. The buff has the following effects: +15% movement speed +10% mining speed +15% placement speed when placing blocks and walls Up to +0.1 luck, depending on the remaining buff duration: +0.1 with at least 9 minutes remaining +0.067 with less than 9 minutes but at least 6 minutes remaining +0.033 with less than 6 minutes but at least 3 minutes remaining 0 with less than 3 minutes remaining A kite can be placed on the ground from the hotbar with ⚷ Open / Activate if the player is not currently flying the kite. The kite initially has some upwards momentum that carries it several blocks above the stake into the air, even on a calm day.

Release Doves.name: Release Doves

Angry Dandelion Banner.name: Angry Dandelion Banner
Angry Dandelion Banner.tooltip: Enemy banners are functional furniture items that can be placed on the underside of blocks and platforms. They are obtained by killing most enemies and a few critters. When placed, enemy banners provide a Banner buff to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the banner. The buff grants players +50%/+100% damage inflicted with all damage to the corresponding enemy and −25%/−50% damage taken from attacks by the enemy. The banners of Old One's Army enemies will apply a weaker banner buff to the respective enemy, granting the players +10%/+20% damage inflicted and −8.33% / −16.67% damage taken. Multiple banners of the same type will not grant stacked buffs. Multiple different banner types in the vicinity will, however, all take effect and consolidate into a single buff icon. There are a total of 286 obtainable enemy banners: 115 in pre-Hardmode, 171 in Hardmode. Out of these, 118 belong to event enemies (28 in pre-Hardmode and 90 in Hardmode). In addition, there are 6 unobtainable enemy banners.

Desert Campfire.name: Desert Campfire
Desert Campfire.tooltip: Campfires are a type of furniture and crafting station that emit light and grant the Cozy Fire buff to players in their vicinity, which provides 10% increased innate health regeneration and additionally grants 0.5 HP/s constant regeneration. The buff is applied to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the campfire, similar to Heart Lanterns and Sunflowers. Campfires are also minor crafting stations, and uniquely, campfires are used to cook Marshmallow on a Stick (see their page for details). Campfires can be toggled off and on with ⚷ Open / Activate, which extinguishes the flame, light, and disables the Cozy Fire buff. They can also be extinguished and lit with the Water Gun and Slime Gun respectively, and as mechanisms, they can be toggled with wire. Campfires are extinguished by rain in The Constant special world seed.

Soul of Light in a Bottle.name: Soul of Light in a Bottle
Soul of Light in a Bottle.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Mud Bud.name: Mud Bud
Mud Bud.tooltip: The Mud Bud is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pet-summoning item that spawns Plantero, a miniature version of Plantera, that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, Plantero flies towards them in a manner similar to Plantera's second form while emitting a trail of falling leaves that are affected by wind. The Mud Bud can be purchased from the Zoologist for 50 Gold after defeating Plantera.

Release Lantern.name: Release Lantern
Release Lantern.tooltip: The Release Lantern is a consumable light source sold by the Party Girl for 1 Silver each during a Lantern Night. When used, it releases a lantern that will float up into the air before disappearing after 16 seconds. It closely resembles the lanterns seen in the background of Lantern Nights and also travels in the direction of the wind.

Quad-Barrel Shotgun.name: Quad-Barrel Shotgun
Quad-Barrel Shotgun.tooltip: The Quad-Barrel Shotgun is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron gun that can be purchased for 35 Gold from the Arms Dealer when he is spoken to in a Graveyard. When used, it fires eight bullets at a 45° spread, consuming one piece of ammunition. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Funeral Hat.name: Funeral Hat
Funeral Hat.tooltip: The Funeral set is a vanity set consisting of the Funeral Hat, Funeral Coat, and Funeral Pants. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. They are purchased from the Clothier for 30 Gold (set) when he is spoken to in the Graveyard biome.

Funeral Coat.name: Funeral Coat
Funeral Coat.tooltip: The Funeral set is a vanity set consisting of the Funeral Hat, Funeral Coat, and Funeral Pants. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. They are purchased from the Clothier for 30 Gold (set) when he is spoken to in the Graveyard biome.

Funeral Pants.name: Funeral Pants
Funeral Pants.tooltip: The Funeral set is a vanity set consisting of the Funeral Hat, Funeral Coat, and Funeral Pants. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. They are purchased from the Clothier for 30 Gold (set) when he is spoken to in the Graveyard biome.

Tragic Umbrella.name: Tragic Umbrella
Tragic Umbrella.tooltip: The Tragic Umbrella is a pre-Hardmode melee weapon and held item that can be purchased from the Clothier for 10 Gold while in a Graveyard. It functions identical to the standard Umbrella, aside from dealing higher damage. While held, the Tragic Umbrella appears above the character, allowing them to fall at a slower rate than normal and preventing fall damage. The player can hold ▼ Down to increase the fall speed. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Victorian Goth Hat.name: Victorian Goth Hat
Victorian Goth Hat.tooltip: The Victorian Goth set is a vanity set consisting of the Victorian Goth Hat and Victorian Goth Dress. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. They are purchased from the Clothier for 20 Gold (set) when he is spoken to in the Graveyard biome.

Victorian Goth Dress.name: Victorian Goth Dress
Victorian Goth Dress.tooltip: The Victorian Goth set is a vanity set consisting of the Victorian Goth Hat and Victorian Goth Dress. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. They are purchased from the Clothier for 20 Gold (set) when he is spoken to in the Graveyard biome.

Tattered Wood Sign.name: Tattered Wood Sign
Tattered Wood Sign.tooltip: The Tattered Wood Sign is a placeable item that functions like the regular Sign. It can be crafted from wood when the player is near a Work Bench in the Graveyard mini-biome.

Gravedigger's Shovel.name: Gravedigger's Shovel
Gravedigger's Shovel.tooltip: The Gravedigger's Shovel is a tool that can be used to dig up "soft" blocks (see below) more efficiently than a pickaxe or drill, in a 3×3-tile rectangle centered on the cursor. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Desert Chest.name: Desert Chest
Desert Chest.tooltip: Biome Chests are Hardmode Chests found within the Dungeon. Each contains one specific rare, powerful weapon, in addition to other miscellaneous items. While Biome Chests are placed during world creation, they are initially locked and can only be opened with an appropriate Biome Key, which will only become available in Hardmode. While Biome Keys can be obtained at any point in Hardmode, Plantera must be defeated in the current world for Biome Keys to be usable; if Plantera has not been defeated, Biome Keys will display the tooltip "It has been cursed by a powerful Jungle creature" and cannot be used. Only five Biome Chests (one of each type) will spawn in a particular world. Each represents a biome found in the current world. There are six types of Biome Chests in total, though a world will only contain one evil biome chest, a Crimson or Corruption variant, depending on which of those biomes the world contains.

Trapped Desert Chest.name: Trapped Desert Chest
Trapped Desert Chest.tooltip: A Trapped Chest is a mechanical item that has the appearance of a normal chest. It cannot be used for storage, as it does not have any storage slots. When it is opened, it emits a signal and can be connected with wire. Any chest can be crafted into a Trapped Chest at the Heavy Assembler with the desired chest and 10 wire. The Trapped Chest can be sold for 1 Silver.

Desert Key.name: Desert Key
Desert Key.tooltip: Biome Keys are Hardmode items used to open the Biome Chests in the Dungeon. Opening a Chest consumes the key. Though unusable until Plantera is defeated, they can be dropped at any time during Hardmode. Each key has a 1/2500 (0.04%) chance of dropping from an enemy in the key's respective biome. Any enemy in the biome that drops coins, except Meteor Heads, when killed has a chance of dropping a key, not just biome-exclusive enemies. Additionally, enemies in hybrid biomes have a chance to drop any key from their composite biomes. The type of key is determined by which biome the player currently is in, not the enemy killed. Any Biome Key dropped prior to defeating Plantera will display the tooltip “It has been cursed by a powerful Jungle creature” and will be unable to open its respective chest until Plantera is defeated, although they are usable in other worlds that have Plantera defeated already.

Stellar Tune.name: Stellar Tune
Stellar Tune.tooltip: The Stellar Tune is a Hardmode, post-Plantera magic weapon that fires pairs of star-shaped projectiles that travel in a wave-like pattern toward the cursor and home in on enemies, travel through solid blocks, and explode in a small radius upon impact. Star projectiles will have their damage reduced by 25% (down to 63 base damage) when the line of sight between the player and the projectiles' point of impact is obstructed. It also plays an acoustic guitar chord when fired based on the distance between the player and the cursor (in a similar fashion to the Magical Harp). There are a total of six chords, and each one spans about a four-block distance from the player, except for the last one, which is played at a distance of 21 blocks or more.  The distance from the player to the cursor also controls the speed at which projectiles are fired. However, if the star projectiles are seeking an enemy, they will instead determine their speed based on the distance between them and their target. The Stellar Tune also has a base 24% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. The Stellar Tune has a 1/50 (2%) / 1/20 (5%) chance of being dropped by the Empress of Light. Its best modifier is Mythical.
Stellar Tune.drops_summary: Empress of Light (2%), Treasure Bag (Empress of Light) (5%)

Mollusk Whistle.name: Mollusk Whistle
Mollusk Whistle.tooltip: The Mollusk Whistle is a mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Flamingo. The Flamingo mount allows players to float in all liquids, similar to using an Inner Tube, and dive by holding ▼ Down. The mount bobs to the surface when the ▼ Down key is released, and if deep enough, the player will launch out of the water into the air. The Mollusk Whistle can be purchased from the Zoologist for 20 Gold after filling out 25% (137 entries) of the Bestiary.

Boreal Beam.name: Boreal Beam
Boreal Beam.tooltip: Beams or columns are background furniture items that provide support for Torches and can be used as decoration. They form continuous vertical pillars when stacked. They are found naturally in Underground Cabins, and can be crafted. Beams and columns can be stacked from the ground, and exist in the background, providing support for suspended Torches that will not inhibit character movement. In this way, beams and columns provide a function similar to trees (which also exist in the background and allow the player to suspend high Torches), but which the player can construct where they like. Where background walls exist, beams and columns can also be placed in "midair", without support from below. Despite their appearance as background walls, beams and columns instead share a layer with other furniture items (like tables, Torches, statues, Switches, timers, etc.), thus the two cannot share the same tile space. They can also prevent a door from opening.

They can also prevent a door from opening.

Nevermore.name: Nevermore
Nevermore.tooltip: Paintings are decorative furniture items that can be placed on background walls. Each one is a framed image that depicts a particular scene, usually Terraria-related. Their tooltips generally contain a person's name, intended to credit each painting's artist; although the names appear to be fictional, most of them correspond to known Terraria developers, artists, testing staff, and community members (see Trivia below). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions, the Magic Lantern, Spelunker Glowsticks, and Spelunker Flares. There are a total of 193 paintings, 25 of which are sold by the Painter, 7 by the Princess, 4 by the Golfer, 2 by the Zoologist, 2 by the Clothier, 1 by the Truffle, and 27 are randomly sold by the Traveling Merchant. 35 paintings can be found in Underground Cabins, another 14 in the Underground Desert Cabins, 26 in the Dungeon, 12 in The Underworld, 6 from Floating Islands, 5 obtained by fishing, 1 from the Jungle Temple, 5 randomly acquired from Goodie Bags, 8 dropped by Solar Eclipse enemies, 8 awarded randomly by the Angler for completing fishing quests, 1 from the Living Tree, and 4 dropped by enemies.

Graveyard.name: Graveyard
Graveyard.tooltip: The Graveyard is a mini-biome that starts to appear when at least five Tombstones are near the player and completes when at least seven Tombstones are near the player. Some special visual effects can be seen in the Graveyard, and these effects grow stronger as more Tombstones are added, capped at nine Tombstones: colors desaturate, lightning randomly strikes in the background, and Ecto Mist accumulates on the ground. When at least seven Tombstones are nearby, the Graveyard biome will gain additional functional effects: unique Graveyard enemies spawn here day and night, as well as the usual creatures originally spawning at night. The spawn rate is not increased, but the enemy spawn reduction of towns is weakened. NPC vendors have unique trades here, and the Ecto Mist on the ground enables unique crafting recipes for the player. Sunflowers can prevent the forming of Graveyards: each Sunflower nearby negates the presence of one Tombstone.

Ghostar's Infinity Eight.name: Ghostar's Infinity Eight
Ghostar's Infinity Eight.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Terra Toilet.name: Terra Toilet
Terra Toilet.tooltip: Toilets are furniture items which can be placed on the ground. They are functionally similar to chairs, and fulfill a house's chair requirement. Similarly to chairs, Toilets can be sat on by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Having any tier of Well Fed active while sitting on a Toilet allows the production of Poo. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Toilet will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Toilets act as mechanisms that can be activated via wire, which makes them appear to explosively eject sewage. This effect is purely a novelty visual. Ejected sewage on the ground fades after a few seconds. There are 67 Toilets.

Ghostar's Soul Jar.name: Ghostar's Soul Jar
Ghostar's Soul Jar.tooltip: Ghostar's set are vanity developer items that can be obtained rarely (6.25% chance) from Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses (except Queen Slime's). It is the vanity set made for Ghostar, a former production assistant at Re-Logic. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. Ghostar's equipment also includes a non-vanity item, which will drop in addition to her clothing set: Ghostar's Infinity Eight

Ball O' Fuse Wire.name: Ball O' Fuse Wire
Ball O' Fuse Wire.tooltip: The Ball O' Fuse Wire is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Dynamite Kitten, which resembles the Orange Tabby variant of the Town Cat, that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Kitten will ride towards them on a stick of Dynamite and immediately dismount when it is on solid ground. The Ball O' Fuse Wire can be purchased from the Zoologist for 50 Gold after completing 70% (383 entries) of the Bestiary.

Full Moon Squeaky Toy.name: Full Moon Squeaky Toy
Full Moon Squeaky Toy.tooltip: The Full Moon Squeaky Toy is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Werewolf that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Baby Werewolf flies after them by flapping its arms, mimicking a bird-like creature. The Full Moon Squeaky Toy can be purchased from the Zoologist during a Hardmode Blood Moon for 30 Gold.

Ornate Shadow Key.name: Ornate Shadow Key
Ornate Shadow Key.tooltip: The Ornate Shadow Key is a pet-summoning item that spawns a pet Shadow Mimic to follow the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Shadow Mimic propels itself by spinning towards them while emitting a trail of purple flames. It will also occasionally spit out non-collectible cosmetic coins. The Ornate Shadow Key has a 1/10 (10%) chance of being obtained from Shadow Chests and a 1/20 (5%) chance of being obtained from Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates.
Ornate Shadow Key.drops_summary: Hellstone Crate (5%), Obsidian Crate (5%), Shadow Chest (10%)

Dr. Man Fly Mask.name: Dr. Man Fly Mask
Dr. Man Fly Mask.tooltip: The Dr. Man Fly set is a Hardmode, post-Plantera vanity set consisting of the Dr. Man Fly Mask and the Dr. Man Fly's Lab Coat. Each piece has a 1/50 (2%) chance of being dropped by Dr. Man Flies during the Solar Eclipse event. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Football.name: Football
Football.tooltip: The Football is a novelty item that players can throw to each other, or to themselves. It is sold by the Party Girl for 20 Copper, after the player has accumulated a golf score of at least 501. Holding the Football and pressing ⚒ Use / Attack throws the Football. It can then be "caught" and picked up again, even while in flight, by another player, or by the same player. A player who takes any damage while a Football is anywhere in their inventory will automatically fumble (drop) the Football, and it can again be picked up by another player, or by the same player. If multiple Footballs are in the player's inventory at the time, they all drop.

Hunter Cloak.name: Hunter Cloak
Hunter Cloak.tooltip: The Hunter Cloak is a vanity item sold by the Clothier for 15 Gold when the player has an accumulated golf score of 2000 or more. It is also occasionally sold by the Traveling Merchant, regardless of golf scores. The Hunter Cloak cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Coffin Minecart.name: Coffin Minecart
Coffin Minecart.tooltip: Minecarts are mounts that allow players to ride on Minecart Tracks. When the player is near a Minecart Track, pressing the Quick Mount hotkey or pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on a point on the track causes a Minecart to spawn, which the player is automatically placed in. Once inside, the ▶ Right and ◀ Left direction keys either accelerate, decelerate, or reverse the cart's movement. The cart will maintain its current speed and direction if no keys are pressed and no obstacles are reached. The cart can also "jump" with the ↷ Jump key. Weapons and tools, as well as most other items except hooks, can be used while riding a Minecart. The Minecart will deal damage to enemies it collides with and knock them back, with higher potency at higher speeds (see below for details). To exit the Minecart (which causes the Minecart to despawn), the player can use a hook, press the Quick Mount hotkey, or cancel the buff  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Minecart will also despawn if the player jumps off the tracks, lands on blocks, and attempts to move sideways. By default, a Wooden Minecart is spawned for the player. This can be overridden by equipping other Minecart items in the Minecart equipment slot of the player's inventory. The corresponding dye slot allows dyeing the Minecart. Using a Minecart Upgrade Kit will significantly boost the speed of all Minecarts, equip them with a laser that fires at nearby enemies, and increase the player's defense while moving. The boost effect is permanently available after using the item, though it can be toggled on and off through a probe icon next to the Minecart slot.
