Blade Staff.name: Blade Staff
Blade Staff.tooltip: The Blade Staff is a Hardmode summon weapon that summons an Enchanted Dagger minion. It flies towards enemies and slashes through them repeatedly at a fast pace. It also has 25 armor penetration. Enchanted Daggers arrange themselves along a carousel above the player's head, and immediately return to the player if no enemies are nearby. The Blade Staff has a 1/4 (25%) / 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by Queen Slime. Its best modifier is generally Focused, Ballistic, or Worthy (see below for details), as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it. Although the Eager modifier is recognized in-game as its best modifier, the majority of enemies do not have enough defense for the extra armor penetration to provide a greater benefit, with the exception of high-defense bosses like Duke Fishron or the Empress of Light.

Squirrel Hook.name: Squirrel Hook
Squirrel Hook.tooltip: The Squirrel Hook is a pre-Hardmode grappling hook that fires a single hook that reaches 19 tiles, and functions similarly to other hooks with the unique ability to grapple and attach to the trunks of trees and Giant Glowing Mushrooms. The Squirrel Hook can be purchased from the Zoologist for 2 Gold after filling out at least 10% (55 entries) of the Bestiary. Therefore, it is normally always available for purchase, since the Zoologist does not appear before the Bestiary has been filled to at least 10%. The only exception is the secret world seed Vampirism, where she is the starting NPC.

Sergeant United Shield.name: Sergeant United Shield
Sergeant United Shield.tooltip: The Sergeant United Shield is a Hardmode boomerang that is rarely sold by the Traveling Merchant for 35 Gold. When thrown, it homes in on enemies within 50 tiles and will attempt to hit up to five enemies before returning to the player, but loses 20% of its damage for each enemy struck. While holding this weapon and equipping a shield (including the Sergeant United Shield itself, while it is not being thrown), the player is granted the ability to parry incoming damage. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate will cause the player to raise the shield and brace for the next attack. When timed correctly, up to 0.33 seconds before taking a hit, the enemy's attack will be parried, which negates the contact damage being dealt to the player, deals 200% of the contact damage of the attacking enemy, inflicts a knockback value of 5 (Average), and grants the player 30 invincibility frames (60 with the Cross Necklace equipped). Successfully parrying an attack also grants the Striking Moment buff, causing the next melee attack to deal 500% or five times its usual base damage for the next five seconds. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Rock Golem Head.name: Rock Golem Head
Rock Golem Head.tooltip: The Rock Golem Head is a dual-purpose vanity and furniture item dropped by Rock Golems at a 1/3 (33.33%) chance. It can be worn or placed. Flower Seeds can be planted in a placed Rock Golem Head. If left empty, wild grass plants will randomly grow out of it, provided the item is placed on the surface or in Space. The plant in a Rock Golem Head cannot be cut in the regular manner, e.g. via nearby swinging tools. Instead, it needs to be removed with a pickaxe or drill, or the Staff of Regrowth or Axe of Regrowth.

Critter Shampoo.name: Critter Shampoo
Critter Shampoo.tooltip: Critter Shampoo is a vanity accessory equipped in a social accessory slot that changes the color of summoned minions when paired with a dye in the corresponding dye slot. It is purchased from the Zoologist for 10 Gold after completing at least 30% (164 entries) of the Bestiary. The Critter Shampoo cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Digging Molecart.name: Digging Molecart
Digging Molecart.tooltip: The Digging Molecart is a minecart that automatically digs a tunnel and lays down regular Minecart Tracks. It is sold by the Zoologist for 50 Gold once the Bestiary is 25% completed (137 entries). Once mounted on existing tracks, the Digging Molecart moves forward with a maximum speed of 31 mph, digging out a tunnel five tiles high and laying track as it goes. The Digging Molecart will only move and place tracks horizontally, even if it is started on a diagonal slope.

Shroomerang.name: Shroomerang
Shroomerang.tooltip: The Shroomerang is a pre-Hardmode boomerang that is dropped by Spore Bats with a 1/40 (2.5%) chance. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Tree Globe.name: Tree Globe
Tree Globe.tooltip: The Tree Globe is a thrown consumable item sold by the Zoologist for 3 Gold after 50% of the Bestiary (273 entries) has been filled out. When a Tree Globe is thrown and shatters on a surface, all of the trees in the current biome will switch to another random style.

World Globe.name: World Globe
World Globe.tooltip: The World Globe is a thrown consumable item sold by the Zoologist after the Bestiary is 50% complete (273 entries). Once a World Globe is thrown and shatters on a surface, the background for the current biome changes permanently for the current world, to a random one of the backgrounds available for that biome. This lasts until another World Globe is thrown. The World Globe can be used in any biome.

Guide to Critter Companionship.name: Guide to Critter Companionship
Guide to Critter Companionship.tooltip: The Guide to Critter Companionship is a pre-Hardmode tool that prevents the player's attacks from harming critters while inside their inventory or opened Void Bag. It can be purchased from the Zoologist for 5 Gold. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Guide to Critter Companionship in the player's inventory or hotbar will toggle it between the Guide to Critter Companionship and the Guide to Critter Companionship (Inactive), disabling its functions.

Dog Ears.name: Dog Ears
Dog Ears.tooltip: The Dog set is a vanity set composed of the Dog Tail and Dog Ears. It can be purchased from the Zoologist during a Full Moon or a Waning Gibbous for 6 Gold (set).

Dog Tail.name: Dog Tail
Dog Tail.tooltip: The Dog set is a vanity set composed of the Dog Tail and Dog Ears. It can be purchased from the Zoologist during a Full Moon or a Waning Gibbous for 6 Gold (set).

Fox Ears.name: Fox Ears
Fox Ears.tooltip: The Fox set is a vanity set composed of the Fox Tail and Fox Ears. It can be purchased from the Zoologist during a Third Quarter or a Waning Crescent for 6 Gold (set).

Fox Tail.name: Fox Tail
Fox Tail.tooltip: The Fox set is a vanity set composed of the Fox Tail and Fox Ears. It can be purchased from the Zoologist during a Third Quarter or a Waning Crescent for 6 Gold (set).

Lizard Ears.name: Lizard Ears
Lizard Ears.tooltip: The Lizard set is a vanity set composed of the Lizard Tail and the Lizard Ears. It can be purchased from the Zoologist during a New Moon or a Waxing Crescent for 6 Gold (set).

Lizard Tail.name: Lizard Tail
Lizard Tail.tooltip: The Lizard set is a vanity set composed of the Lizard Tail and the Lizard Ears. It can be purchased from the Zoologist during a New Moon or a Waxing Crescent for 6 Gold (set).

Panda Ears.name: Panda Ears
Panda Ears.tooltip: Panda Ears are a vanity item purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 Gold 50 Silver.

Bunny Tail.name: Bunny Tail
Bunny Tail.tooltip: The Bunny set is a vanity set composed of the Bunny Tail and Bunny Ears. It can be purchased from the Zoologist during a First Quarter or a Waxing Gibbous for 6 Gold (set).

Fairy Glowstick.name: Fairy Glowstick
Fairy Glowstick.tooltip: The Fairy Glowstick is a consumable light source sold by the Zoologist for 75 Copper when all three fairies have been recorded in the Bestiary. The Fairy Glowstick functions like a regular Glowstick when thrown. However, upon colliding with solid blocks, it will hover to a maximum of approximately 7 tiles above where it had landed. The Fairy Glowstick provides more illumination compared to a regular Glowstick while in liquids.

Lightning Carrot.name: Lightning Carrot
Lightning Carrot.tooltip: The Lightning Carrot is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Volt Bunny that follows the player. While flying to keep pace with the player, the Volt Bunny dashes and releases a series of spherical blue sparks, which emit a decent amount of light while moving erratically and can spread light over an area. If there are no available tiles for the pet to "sit" on, like when climbing walls or flying, the Volt Bunny will constantly jump around. The Lightning Carrot can be purchased from the Zoologist for 50 Gold after completing 50% (273 entries) of the Bestiary.

Prismatic Dye.name: Prismatic Dye
Prismatic Dye.tooltip: Prismatic Dye is a Hardmode, post-Plantera dye dropped by the Empress of Light with a 1/4 (25%) chance. The dye creates a prism-esque effect, making the equipped item seem transparent and glow in a cycling rainbow.
Prismatic Dye.drops_summary: Empress of Light (25%), Treasure Bag (Empress of Light) (25%)

Mushroom Hat.name: Mushroom Hat
Mushroom Hat.tooltip: The Mushroom set is a vanity set consisting of the Mushroom Hat, Mushroom Vest, and Mushroom Pants. All three pieces have a 1/2 (50%) chance of being found in Mushroom Chests in underground Glowing Mushroom biomes. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Mushroom Vest.name: Mushroom Vest
Mushroom Vest.tooltip: The Mushroom set is a vanity set consisting of the Mushroom Hat, Mushroom Vest, and Mushroom Pants. All three pieces have a 1/2 (50%) chance of being found in Mushroom Chests in underground Glowing Mushroom biomes. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Mushroom Pants.name: Mushroom Pants
Mushroom Pants.tooltip: The Mushroom set is a vanity set consisting of the Mushroom Hat, Mushroom Vest, and Mushroom Pants. All three pieces have a 1/2 (50%) chance of being found in Mushroom Chests in underground Glowing Mushroom biomes. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Treasure Bag (Empress of Light).name: Treasure Bag (Empress of Light)
Treasure Bag (Empress of Light).tooltip: Treasure Bags are consumable grab bag-like items obtained in Expert Mode and Master Mode as a reward for defeating bosses. The contents and appearance of Treasure Bags depend on the boss it comes from, and are opened by using either ⚷ Open / Activate while inside the inventory, or ⚒ Use / Attack when selected in the hotbar. They emit light and have a special effect around them when dropped, making them easier to spot. In multiplayer, each player that deals damage to the boss receives one Treasure Bag upon defeating it. Treasure Bags are client-side and will despawn upon exiting the world. See Notes for details. Each Treasure Bag contains the boss's usual drops from Classic Mode, along with one Expert Mode-exclusive item (highlighted items below) – with the exception of the Lunatic Cultist, Dark Mage, Ogre, and Betsy, who do not provide an Expert Mode-exclusive item. Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses additionally have a 1/16 (6.25%) chance to contain one random set of developer items (with the exception of Queen Slime). Expert Mode-exclusive items all have the  rarity, with the exception of developer items, which have the  rarity.

Empress of Light Trophy.name: Empress of Light Trophy
Empress of Light Trophy.tooltip: Trophies are decorative furniture items which usually have a 1/10 (10%) chance to be dropped from most bosses. While they can be considered the "boss version of banners", they are purely cosmetic and do not provide any bonuses. Some trophies can only be rewarded by the Angler for completing fishing quests. In total, there are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 33 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 24 trophies.

Empress of Light Mask.name: Empress of Light Mask
Empress of Light Mask.tooltip: Masks are vanity items dropped by all non-event bosses, as well as those from the Old One's Army(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). They are worn in the social head slot. Each boss has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance to drop its own mask in all difficulties, with the following exceptions: The Skeletron Mask has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to drop from Skeletron's Treasure Bag. The Dark Mage Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 1) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Dark Mage. The Ogre Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 2) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Ogre.

Dusty Rawhide Saddle.name: Dusty Rawhide Saddle
Dusty Rawhide Saddle.tooltip: The Dusty Rawhide Saddle, Royal Gilded Saddle, and Black Studded Saddle are mount-summoning items that summon the rideable Painted Horse Mount, Majestic Horse Mount, and Dark Horse Mount, respectively. All three horse mounts are functionally identical. Once they reach a high speed, they will deal damage to enemies they come into contact with. Saddles are sold by the Zoologist for 25 Gold each, after completing at least 30% (164 entries) of the Bestiary.

Royal Gilded Saddle.name: Royal Gilded Saddle
Royal Gilded Saddle.tooltip: The Dusty Rawhide Saddle, Royal Gilded Saddle, and Black Studded Saddle are mount-summoning items that summon the rideable Painted Horse Mount, Majestic Horse Mount, and Dark Horse Mount, respectively. All three horse mounts are functionally identical. Once they reach a high speed, they will deal damage to enemies they come into contact with. Saddles are sold by the Zoologist for 25 Gold each, after completing at least 30% (164 entries) of the Bestiary.

Black Studded Saddle.name: Black Studded Saddle
Black Studded Saddle.tooltip: The Dusty Rawhide Saddle, Royal Gilded Saddle, and Black Studded Saddle are mount-summoning items that summon the rideable Painted Horse Mount, Majestic Horse Mount, and Dark Horse Mount, respectively. All three horse mounts are functionally identical. Once they reach a high speed, they will deal damage to enemies they come into contact with. Saddles are sold by the Zoologist for 25 Gold each, after completing at least 30% (164 entries) of the Bestiary.

Jousting Lance.name: Jousting Lance
Jousting Lance.tooltip: The Jousting Lance is a Hardmode melee weapon purchased from the Zoologist for 6 GC after filling out 30% (162 entries) of the Bestiary.

Shadow Jousting Lance.name: Shadow Jousting Lance
Shadow Jousting Lance.tooltip: The Shadow Jousting Lance is a Hardmode, post-Plantera melee weapon. When attacking using ⚒ Use / Attack, the lance will extend, and holding ⚒ Use / Attack will keep it extended at a fixed angle. The damage and knockback will increase depending on the player's movement speed, making mounts, sprinting accessories, or dash abilities (such as those granted by Shield of Cthulhu, Tabi/Master Ninja Gear, or Solar Flare armor) useful for maximizing damage. When the player takes damage, the Shadow Jousting Lance will stop being active. The Shadow Jousting Lance has a 1/25 (4%) / 49/625 (7.84%) chance of being dropped by Giant Cursed Skulls in the post-Plantera Dungeon. It is the upgrade of the Jousting Lance and Hallowed Jousting Lance. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Hallowed Jousting Lance.name: Hallowed Jousting Lance
Hallowed Jousting Lance.tooltip: The Hallowed Jousting Lance is a Hardmode melee weapon. When attacking using ⚒ Use / Attack, the lance will extend, and holding ⚒ Use / Attack will keep it extended at a fixed angle. The damage and knockback will increase depending on the player's movement speed, making mounts, sprinting accessories, or dash abilities (such as those granted by Shield of Cthulhu, Tabi/Master Ninja Gear, or Solar Flare armor) useful for maximizing damage. When the player takes damage, the Hallowed Jousting Lance will stop being active. It is the upgrade of the Jousting Lance and the precursor to the Shadow Jousting Lance. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Pogo Stick.name: Pogo Stick
Pogo Stick.tooltip: The Pogo Stick is a mount-summoning item that summons a Pogo Stick Mount. Jumping again while in the air causes the player to do a front flip. The Pogo Stick Mount doubles the speed at which the player falls, allowing a top falling speed of 102 mph. It also increases the maximum safe falling distance by 20 tiles, reduces fall damage by 75%, has a max horizontal speed of 26 mph, and keeps a certain amount of momentum while airborne, meaning it continues traveling in the last horizontal direction the player inputted while in the air, rather than slowing. The Pogo Stick can be purchased from the Party Girl for 25 Gold.

The Black Spot.name: The Black Spot
The Black Spot.tooltip: The Black Spot is a Hardmode mount-summoning item that spawns a rideable Pirate Ship Mount which can fly infinitely. The Black Spot has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Flying Dutchman in Master Mode. The Pirate Ship Mount has a maximum horizontal flight speed of 36 mph, a diagonal speed of 54 mph, and a vertical speed of 41 mph. It moves slightly slower (30 mph) while in water. Upon achieving a horizontal speed of 27 mph, a ring of gold particles appears around the player and trails behind the mount, indicating that the Pirate Ship Mount begins dealing 100 base summon damage and a knockback of 12 (Insane) upon ramming enemies, which also grants the player 0.1 seconds worth of invincibility frames.

Hexxed Branch.name: Hexxed Branch
Hexxed Branch.tooltip: The Hexxed Branch is a Hardmode, post-Plantera mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Tree Mount, a ground-based mount that is unable to fly. Upon reaching 90% of its full speed, the Tree Mount briefly emits an orange ring and gains a flaming trail, and becomes able to deal 120 base summon damage and knockback of 12 (Insane) to enemies upon contact, which also grants the player 0.1 seconds of Invincibility frames. The Hexxed Branch is dropped by the Mourning Wood during the Pumpkin Moon event in Master Mode with a 6.25–25% chance depending on the current wave.

Toy Tank.name: Toy Tank
Toy Tank.tooltip: The Toy Tank is a Hardmode, post-Plantera mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Santank Mount. The mount is notable for having a double jump as well as two auto-targeting weapons attached; a front-facing machine gun and a homing rocket launcher. The Toy Tank is dropped by Santa-NK1 during the Frost Moon event in Master Mode with a 6.25–25% chance depending on the current wave. The maximum movement speed of the mount is 41 mph, and it takes about 1.5 seconds to reach top speed. The maximum jump height is 12 tiles without a double jump, or 26 tiles with the double jump when timed right. The double jump can be stacked with other double jump accessories. The Santank is 2 tiles wide and 3 tiles tall, meaning that it does not change the player's height and makes it easier to travel through narrower corridors than with larger mounts such as the Unicorn Mount and Pirate Ship Mount. The Santank's two attached weapons only fire if there are enemies in front of the player. The machine gun's bullets deal 100 base damage and are fired in a spread of 22.9°, making the weapon somewhat inaccurate. The homing rockets are initially fired directly upwards, deal 120 base damage, and seek the closest target after being fired, including targets that are outside the mount's initial detection range (e.g. enemies behind the player). The damage of the projectiles does not scale with any damage bonuses the player has, but their critical strike chance is affected by the player's ranged critical strike chance. The machine gun fires a bullet every 0.17 seconds (i.e. 6 shots per second), while the rocket launcher fires a rocket every 0.67 seconds.

Goat Skull.name: Goat Skull
Goat Skull.tooltip: The Goat Skull is a Hardmode mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Goat Mount which allows the mounted player to perform a double jump, similar to the Cloud in a Bottle. The Goat Skull has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Wall of Flesh in Master Mode. Once a high enough speed is reached, the Goat Mount leaves a trail of fire on solid blocks behind itself, similar to Flame Waker Boots, and from that point on, it will be able to damage enemies on contact. The invulnerability is granted for 1/10th of a second when the player and the Goat Mount dash through an enemy, much like the brief invulnerability after taking damage.

Dark Mage's Tome.name: Dark Mage's Tome
Dark Mage's Tome.tooltip: The Dark Mage's Tome is a mount-summoning item that places the player on a Book Mount which grants limited flight. The Dark Mage's Tome has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Dark Mage in Master Mode. The mount allows a player to hover and glide at a fixed height of 8 tiles high in mid-air for 5 seconds following a jump or walking off a ledge. It otherwise glides along the ground, and automatically climbs ledges that are no more than 1-tile-high. Whether on the ground or hovering, its top speed is 41 mph. The Book Mount also cancels fall damage. Extra jump accessories can be used during hover, increasing the max hover height. The height is also adjustable in the down direction by pressing ▼ Down.

Royal Delight.name: Royal Delight
Royal Delight.tooltip: The Royal Delight is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Slime Prince that follows the player. The pet resembles a miniature King Slime with blush, small dotted eyes, and a tiny mouth. The Royal Delight has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by King Slime in Master Mode.

Suspicious Grinning Eye.name: Suspicious Grinning Eye
Suspicious Grinning Eye.tooltip: The Suspicious Grinning Eye is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Suspicious Eye, a miniature version of the Eye of Cthulhu, that follows the player. It normally shows a blue iris and pupil, but when moving faster than 31 mph the pupil slides up and reveals a mouth, similar to the Eye of Cthulhu's second form. The Suspicious Grinning Eye has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Eye of Cthulhu in Master Mode.

Writhing Remains.name: Writhing Remains
Writhing Remains.tooltip: The Writhing Remains is a pet-summoning item that spawns an Eater of Worms that follows the player. The Writhing Remains has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Eater of Worlds in Master Mode.

Brain in a Jar.name: Brain in a Jar
Brain in a Jar.tooltip: The Brain in a Jar is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Spider Brain, a miniature version of the Brain of Cthulhu, that follows the player.

Possessed Skull.name: Possessed Skull
Possessed Skull.tooltip: The Possessed Skull is a pet-summoning item that spawns Skeletron Jr. to follow the player. When the player is too far away or in midair, Skeletron Jr. will start spinning its head in order to catch up to them. The Possessed Skull has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Skeletron in Master Mode.

Sparkling Honey.name: Sparkling Honey
Sparkling Honey.tooltip: The Sparkling Honey is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Honey Bee pet, a large bee which follows the player around. The Sparkling Honey has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Queen Bee in Master Mode.

Deactivated Probe.name: Deactivated Probe
Deactivated Probe.tooltip: The Deactivated Probe is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Destroyer-Lite, a miniature version of The Destroyer that follows the player. The Deactivated Probe has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by The Destroyer in Master Mode.

Pair of Eyeballs.name: Pair of Eyeballs
Pair of Eyeballs.tooltip: The Pair of Eyeballs is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns Rez and Spaz, miniature versions of The Twins in their first form. The Pair of Eyeballs has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by The Twins in Master Mode.

Robotic Skull.name: Robotic Skull
Robotic Skull.tooltip: The Robotic Skull is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns Mini Prime, a miniature version of Skeletron Prime that follows the player.

Plantera Seedling.name: Plantera Seedling
Plantera Seedling.tooltip: The Plantera Seedling is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pet-summoning item that spawns a Plantera Seedling that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Plantera Seedling flies by twirling its petals like a propeller to catch up to them. The Plantera Seedling has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Plantera in Master Mode.

Guardian Golem.name: Guardian Golem
Guardian Golem.tooltip: The Guardian Golem is a Hardmode, post-Golem light pet-summoning item that spawns a Toy Golem light pet upon being used or equipped. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Toy Golem emits a rocket exhaust to catch up to them. The Guardian Golem has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Golem in Master Mode.

Pork of the Sea.name: Pork of the Sea
Pork of the Sea.tooltip: The Pork of the Sea is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Tiny Fishron that follows the player. The Pork of the Sea has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Duke Fishron in Master Mode.

Tablet Fragment.name: Tablet Fragment
Tablet Fragment.tooltip: The Tablet Fragment is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist pet-summoning item that spawns a Phantasmal Dragon that follows the player. The pet resembles the Phantasm Dragon spawned during the Lunatic Cultist's battle, and the only difference between the two is that the pet itself is smaller. The Tablet Fragment has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Lunatic Cultist in Master Mode.

Piece of Moon Squid.name: Piece of Moon Squid
Piece of Moon Squid.tooltip: The Piece of Moon Squid is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord pet-summoning item that spawns a Moonling, which resembles the Moon Lord's head, that follows the player. The Piece of Moon Squid has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Moon Lord in Master Mode.

Jewel of Light.name: Jewel of Light
Jewel of Light.tooltip: The Jewel of Light is a Hardmode, post-Plantera light pet-summoning item that spawns a Fairy Princess that provides pink-colored light. It is fast and will always position itself slightly elevated behind the player. The Jewel of Light has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Empress of Light in Master Mode. While equipped, not only does the pet produce light, but the player as well.

Pumpkin Scented Candle.name: Pumpkin Scented Candle
Pumpkin Scented Candle.tooltip: The Pumpkin Scented Candle is a Hardmode, post-Plantera light pet-summoning item that spawns a miniature Pumpking named Jack 'O Lantern to follow the player around. The Pumpkin Scented Candle is dropped by the Pumpking during the Pumpkin Moon event in Master Mode with a 12.5–25% chance depending on the current wave. While equipped, not only does the pet produce light, but the player as well.

Shrub Star.name: Shrub Star
Shrub Star.tooltip: The Shrub Star is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pet-summoning item that spawns an Everscream Sapling to follow the player around. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Everscream Sapling flies toward them, tucking its legs together and emitting fire from its legs like a rocket. The Shrub Star is dropped by the Everscream during the Frost Moon event in Master Mode with a 5–25% chance depending on the current wave.

Frozen Crown.name: Frozen Crown
Frozen Crown.tooltip: The Frozen Crown is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pet-summoning item that spawns a miniature Ice Queen that follows the player. The Frozen Crown is dropped by the Ice Queen during the Frost Moon event in Master Mode with a 12.5–25% chance depending on the current wave.

Cosmic Skateboard.name: Cosmic Skateboard
Cosmic Skateboard.tooltip: The Cosmic Skateboard is a Hardmode, post-Golem pet-summoning item that spawns an Alien Skater that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Alien Skater turns its skateboard into a rocket-powered hoverboard to catch up to them. The Cosmic Skateboard has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Martian Saucer in Master Mode.

Ogre's Club.name: Ogre's Club
Ogre's Club.tooltip: The Ogre's Club is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Baby Ogre that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Baby Ogre will hold onto an Etherian Wyvern by its tail in order to catch up to them. The Ogre's Club has a 1/4 (25%) chance of dropping from the Ogre in Master Mode.

Betsy's Egg.name: Betsy's Egg
Betsy's Egg.tooltip: Betsy's Egg is a Hardmode, post-Golem pet-summoning item that spawns Itsy Betsy to follow the player. Betsy's Egg has a 1/4 (25%) of being dropped from Betsy in Master Mode.

Combat Wrench.name: Combat Wrench
Combat Wrench.tooltip: The Combat Wrench is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron boomerang that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by the Mechanic. It can pierce multiple targets before returning. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Demon Conch.name: Demon Conch
Demon Conch.tooltip: The Demon Conch is a rare pre-Hardmode tool obtainable by fishing in lava. It teleports the player to the center of the Underworld 0.75 seconds (45 ticks) after being used. Like the Magic Mirror, it can be used infinitely at no cost, making it a viable alternative to using conventional hellevators.

Bottomless Lava Bucket.name: Bottomless Lava Bucket
Bottomless Lava Bucket.tooltip: Bottomless Buckets are tools that are capable of placing an infinite amount of liquids by pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button. There are four different types of Bottomless Buckets, one for each type of liquid: Bottomless Water Bucket, Bottomless Lava Bucket, Bottomless Honey Bucket, and Bottomless Shimmer Bucket. Bottomless Buckets can be used limitlessly and are never depleted. They are also slightly faster at placing liquids when compared to standard buckets (especially when moving the cursor around while placing).

Lavaproof Bug Net.name: Lavaproof Bug Net
Lavaproof Bug Net.tooltip: The Lavaproof Bug Net is an upgraded version of the Bug Net. It allows the player to successfully catch the Lavafly, Magma Snail, and Hell Butterfly that can be used to fish in lava. It swings faster than the Bug Net and can destroy tall grass and vines. Its upgraded version is the Golden Bug Net which is faster and bigger.

Flame Waker Boots.name: Flame Waker Boots
Flame Waker Boots.tooltip: The Flame Waker Boots are a vanity accessory obtained by opening Obsidian Crates or Hellstone Crates, found by fishing in Lava.

Empress Wings.name: Empress Wings
Empress Wings.tooltip: Wings are accessories that allow the player to fly by holding the ↷ Jump button, increase mid-air agility, and provide immunity to fall damage. The player can only equip one set of wings at a time. Flight with wings is much more controlled than with Rocket Boots and the like, and they allow for much greater flight range. Flight will start immediately upon jumping. Extra jump accessories can be used by pressing ↷ Jump again while flying. During flight, the player's flight time gradually depletes until reaching zero. After flight time is exhausted, holding ↷ Jump allows the player to glide. Flight time resets when the player stands, climbs (e.g. using Rope or Shoe Spikes), or hooks onto a tile. Certain wing types also allow the player to hover at fixed heights by holding the ▼ Down button during flight, and/or accelerate their ascent speed by holding the ▲ Up button.

Wet Bomb.name: Wet Bomb
Wet Bomb.tooltip: Liquid bombs are explosive items that function like the Bomb, but their explosion will either place or remove liquids, instead of destroying blocks. There are four different types of liquid bombs: Dry Bomb, Wet Bomb, Lava Bomb, and Honey Bomb. The Dry Bomb deletes all liquids in a small area when it explodes. The Wet Bomb places water in a small area when it explodes. The Lava Bomb places lava in a small area when it explodes. The Honey Bomb places honey in a small area when it explodes. If a liquid bomb touches either of these three liquids, it will immediately explode and apply its effects. However, all liquid bombs will bounce off Shimmer. Shimmer does not restrict their effects in any other way. Wet Bombs are obtainable by opening Obsidian or Hellstone Crates found by fishing in lava. If the player is carrying a Wet Bomb, the Demolitionist will sell Wet Bombs for 25 Silver each. Purchasing more Wet Bombs will allow the player to craft the other variants (see below). The Demolitionist will also sell the three other types of bombs for the same price while the player is carrying them.

Lava Bomb.tooltip: Liquid bombs are explosive items that function like the Bomb, but their explosion will either place or remove liquids, instead of destroying blocks. There are four different types of liquid bombs: Dry Bomb, Wet Bomb, Lava Bomb, and Honey Bomb. The Dry Bomb deletes all liquids in a small area when it explodes. The Wet Bomb places water in a small area when it explodes. The Lava Bomb places lava in a small area when it explodes. The Honey Bomb places honey in a small area when it explodes. If a liquid bomb touches either of these three liquids, it will immediately explode and apply its effects. However, all liquid bombs will bounce off Shimmer. Shimmer does not restrict their effects in any other way. Wet Bombs are obtainable by opening Obsidian or Hellstone Crates found by fishing in lava. If the player is carrying a Wet Bomb, the Demolitionist will sell Wet Bombs for 25 Silver each. Purchasing more Wet Bombs will allow the player to craft the other variants (see below). The Demolitionist will also sell the three other types of bombs for the same price while the player is carrying them.

Honey Bomb.tooltip: Liquid bombs are explosive items that function like the Bomb, but their explosion will either place or remove liquids, instead of destroying blocks. The Demolitionist will also sell the three other types of bombs for the same price while the player is carrying them.

Dry Bomb.name: Dry Bomb
Dry Bomb.tooltip: Liquid bombs are explosive items that function like the Bomb, but their explosion will either place or remove liquids, instead of destroying blocks. There are four different types of liquid bombs: Dry Bomb, Wet Bomb, Lava Bomb, and Honey Bomb. The Dry Bomb deletes all liquids in a small area when it explodes. The Wet Bomb places water in a small area when it explodes. The Lava Bomb places lava in a small area when it explodes. The Honey Bomb places honey in a small area when it explodes. The Demolitionist will also sell the three other types of bombs for the same price while the player is carrying them.

Superheated Blood.name: Superheated Blood
Superheated Blood.tooltip: The Superheated Blood is a mount-summoning item that summons a rideable Lava Shark Mount. The Superheated Blood has a 19/100 (19%) chance of being obtained from Obsidian Crates or Hellstone Crates found by fishing in lava. Riding the mount will allow the player to swim very quickly in lava without taking damage. The player will also be immune to all Burning damage. It can also swim in water and honey, but will not protect the player from drowning. It has a maximum speed of 73 mph in liquids and 11 mph on land. The mount maintains its velocity in the air, allowing for jumps similar to while riding a Minecart. When moving upwards or downwards, it tilts towards that direction. When submerged in lava, this mount enables 'lava vision' which renders all lava more transparent.

Cat License.name: Cat License
Cat License.tooltip: The Cat License is a consumable item that can be purchased from the Zoologist for 5 Gold. Upon use, the status message "The license teleports away to the cat delivery service..." is displayed. Following this status message, a Town Cat will move into an available house the next morning. Using a second Cat License when a Town Cat is already present in the current world displays the status message "Pet Exchange: Successful!" and causes it to be "exchanged": the Town Cat releases a puff of smoke and has its breed and name rerolled immediately.

Dog License.name: Dog License
Dog License.tooltip: The Dog License is a consumable item that can be purchased from the Zoologist for 5 Gold after filling out 25% (137 entries) of the Bestiary. Upon use, the status message "The license teleports away to the dog delivery service..." is displayed. Following this status message, a Town Dog will move into an available house the next morning. Using a Dog License when a Town Dog is already present in the current world displays the status message "Pet Exchange: Successful!" and causes it to be "exchanged": the Town Dog releases a puff of smoke and has its breed and name rerolled immediately.

Amethyst Squirrel.name: Amethyst Squirrel
Amethyst Squirrel.tooltip: Gem Squirrels are harmless critters that can only spawn in the cavern layer near town NPCs, and have a higher spawn chance during rain. Gem Squirrels may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details. Gem Squirrels have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. Gem Squirrels can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Gem Squirrel Cages). Once crafted, the Gem Squirrels cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.

Hell Butterfly.name: Hell Butterfly
Hell Butterfly.tooltip: Butterflies are small critters that can naturally spawn on Surface in Forest and the Hallow, and also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Forest or Pearlwood tree. In both cases, they can only spawn during daytime if wind speed is lower than 20 mph, and if it is not currently raining. There are 8 variants of ordinary Butterflies with different appearences, chosen randomly when they spawn. They can be caught with a Bug Net and carried in the inventory. When an ordinary Butterfly is being spawned, there is a 1/400 (0.25%) chance (affected by luck) for it to be replaced by a Gold Butterfly, which can be caught with a Bug Net and crafted into Golden Delight. The Hell Butterfly(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) can naturally spawn in the Underworld during daytime. It can also spawn from shaking an Ash tree in the Underworld, or from destroying wild Ash grass plants. It can only be caught with the Lavaproof Bug Net(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) or the Golden Bug Net(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Attempting to catch it with a standard Bug Net will not work, and the player will take 1 damage and be inflicted with On Fire! for 5 seconds / 10 seconds / 12.5 seconds. All Butterflies can be crafted into butterfly jars, and can be be used as bait for fishing.

Hell Butterfly Jar.name: Hell Butterfly Jar
Hell Butterfly Jar.tooltip: Butterfly jars are pieces of decorative furniture created by combining a butterfly, captured with a Bug Net, with a Bottle. By throwing a butterfly jar into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the butterfly as an item.  Butterfly jars function the same way as cages for other critters. They have an animated sprite when placed down, and the butterflies will fly around inside the jars.

Lavafly.name: Lavafly
Lavafly.tooltip: The Lavafly is a critter that spawns occasionally in the Underworld at night. It also has a small chance of spawning upon shaking an Ash tree in the Underworld at any time. Also from destroyed wild Ash grass plants at any time and even outside of the Underworld.It gives off a tiny amount of light, similarly to the Firefly. The Lavafly has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Lavafly can only be caught with the Lavaproof Bug Net or the Golden Bug Net. Trying to catch it with a standard Bug Net will only set the player on fire. After being caught, it can be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Lavafly in a Bottle). Once crafted, the Lavafly cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Lavafly can be used as bait for fishing, with 25% bait power. Using it as bait also allows fishing in lava.

Lavafly in a Bottle.name: Lavafly in a Bottle
Lavafly in a Bottle.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Magma Snail.name: Magma Snail
Magma Snail.tooltip: The Magma Snail is a critter that spawns in The Underworld. It also has a small chance of spawning upon shaking an Ash tree in the Underworld. The Magma Snail emits light. The Magma Snail has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Magma Snail can only be caught with the Lavaproof Bug Net or the Golden Bug Net. Trying to catch it with a standard Bug Net will only set the player on fire. After being caught, it can be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Magma Snail Cage). Once crafted, the Magma Snail cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Magma Snail can be used as bait for fishing, with 35% bait power. Using it as bait also allows fishing in lava.

Magma Snail Cage.name: Magma Snail Cage
Magma Snail Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters. A critter caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item. Gold cages are regular cages containing gold critters. Aside from their higher sell value and rarity, they are the same as regular cages. Placed cages are partially transparent. They can be stacked on top of each other, but no other types of furniture can be placed on a cage. Players can stand on top of cages like platforms, even though they are otherwise background furniture.

Topaz Gemcorn.name: Topaz Gemcorn
Topaz Gemcorn.tooltip: Gemcorns are seeds crafted from an Acorn and any gem. When placed, they create saplings that can grow into gem trees. Natural gem trees occasionally generate within the Underground and Cavern layers. Destroying a gem tree generally yields 7–48 Stone Blocks, 0–11 Gemcorns of the tree's type, and 0–24 gems of the tree's type (each tile of the tree has a 1/10 (10%) chance of dropping a gem, otherwise dropping 1–2 Stone Blocks, and every non-barren leaf/branch tile additionally has a 1/2 (50%) chance to drop another Gemcorn. See Growing conditions section for detailed info). Gemcorns cannot be retrieved after being placed. Destroying the sapling will not yield any items.

Hanging Pot.name: Hanging Pot
Hanging Pot.tooltip: The Hanging Pot is a placeable decorative furniture item obtained by opening Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates.

Hanging Daybloom.name: Hanging Daybloom
Hanging Daybloom.tooltip: Hanging herbs are placeable decorative furniture items craftable with one Hanging Pot and one herb. They can only be placed on the ceiling and breaking one of the blocks above a hanging herb will drop the item.

Hanging Moonglow.name: Hanging Moonglow
Hanging Moonglow.tooltip: Hanging herbs are placeable decorative furniture items craftable with one Hanging Pot and one herb. They can only be placed on the ceiling and breaking one of the blocks above a hanging herb will drop the item.

Hanging Crimson Deathweed.name: Hanging Crimson Deathweed
Hanging Crimson Deathweed.tooltip: Hanging herbs are placeable decorative furniture items craftable with one Hanging Pot and one herb. They can only be placed on the ceiling and breaking one of the blocks above a hanging herb will drop the item.

Hanging Fireblossom.name: Hanging Fireblossom
Hanging Fireblossom.tooltip: Hanging herbs are placeable decorative furniture items craftable with one Hanging Pot and one herb. They can only be placed on the ceiling and breaking one of the blocks above a hanging herb will drop the item.

Hanging Brazier.name: Hanging Brazier
Hanging Brazier.tooltip: The Hanging Brazier is a placeable decorative furniture item. It can only be placed on the ceiling, and breaking one of the blocks above it will drop the item. The Hanging Brazier is a valid light source for NPC housing.

Mini Volcano.name: Mini Volcano
Mini Volcano.tooltip: The Mini Volcano is a decorative animated furniture item that emits light when placed. Its animation can be toggled on and off with wires. It has a 19/100 (19%) chance of being dropped when opening Obsidian and Hellstone Crates.

Large Volcano.name: Large Volcano
Large Volcano.tooltip: The Large Volcano is a decorative animated furniture item that emits light when placed. Its animation can be toggled on and off with wires.

Potion of Return.name: Potion of Return
Potion of Return.tooltip: The Potion of Return is a potion that teleports the player back to their spawn point, similar to the Recall Potion, and additionally creates a portal exit at the location where the potion was consumed. A portal entrance will be created at the spawn point, which can be used to teleport back to where the player consumed the potion. The portal can only be used once and will disappear afterwards. In addition to being crafted, the Potion of Return can be found in Pots in the Cavern layer and the Underworld, as well as in Shadow Chests.

Sakura Sapling.name: Sakura Sapling
Sakura Sapling.tooltip: The Sakura Sapling is a type of seed that grows into a Sakura tree, which is a tree that can also spawn naturally in Forest biomes, when planted. Its appearance is purely decorative and it functions identically to regular forest trees. Sakura Saplings can be purchased from the Zoologist for 1 Gold once the Bestiary is 30% completed (164 entries).

Lava Absorbant Sponge.name: Lava Absorbant Sponge
Lava Absorbant Sponge.tooltip: Sponges are tools used to erase liquids by pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button on them. This causes the liquid to disappear from the environment without storing it. There are four different types of sponges: Super Absorbant Sponge for absorbing water and Shimmer Lava Absorbant Sponge for absorbing lava Honey Absorbant Sponge for absorbing honey Ultra Absorbant Sponge for absorbing all kinds of liquid Attempting to use a sponge on a different type of liquid has no effect. Sponges can be used limitlessly and are never depleted. They are also slightly faster at draining liquids when compared to using a standard Empty Bucket (especially when moving the cursor around while draining).

Hallowed Hood.name: Hallowed Hood
Hallowed Hood.tooltip: Hallowed armor is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss armor set consisting of the Hallowed Plate Mail and Hallowed Greaves, as well as four different headpieces: the Hallowed Mask, Hallowed Helmet, Hallowed Headgear, and Hallowed Hood, providing bonuses for melee, ranged, magic, and summon damage type respectively. Crafting a full set with one headpiece requires a total of 54 Hallowed Bars. Crafting all six pieces requires a total of 90 Hallowed Bars. Hallowed armor pieces are interchangeable with Ancient Hallowed armor pieces, still providing the set bonus. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: Upon enemy hits, the player receives the Holy Protection buff, which grants the ability to dodge the next attack dealt by an enemy or other damage source. It has a 30-second cooldown after the dodge has been activated. The player also emits visual pulses and afterimages while moving.

Hellfire Treads.name: Hellfire Treads
Hellfire Treads.tooltip: The Hellfire Treads are a pre-Hardmode accessory that combines the effects of the Spectre and Flame Waker Boots. It grants the player the ability to fly and to gain increased movement speed when running continuously, and causes the player's feet to leave trails of fire while moving on blocks, which is a purely visual effect.

Jungle Pylon.name: Jungle Pylon
Jungle Pylon.tooltip: Pylons are placeable furniture items that appear as a large crystal hovering and rotating above a biome-themed stand. With two or more pylons placed in the world, the player can teleport from one pylon to another one. The system they form is referred to as the Pylon Network. When the player is near a pylon, they can teleport to another pylon by doing any of the following: Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the pylon, which opens the full-screen map, and selecting another pylon on the map. Pressing Toggle Full Map to open the full-screen map, and selecting another pylon on the map.  Selecting another pylon on the overlay-mode or portrait-mode minimap. The following conditions must be met by both the pylon near the player and the target pylon (with the exception of the Universal Pylon): There must be two or more housed NPCs (including the Old Man and town pets) within a rectangular area of 169×124 tiles centered on each of the two pylons. More precisely, the home tile of the NPC (Dungeon point in the case of the Old Man) must be within this rectangle, and the NPC must be less than 100 tiles away from their home tile. The pylons must be placed in their respective biome. Moreover, the following restrictions apply to all pylons (including the Universal Pylon): Only one of each type of pylon may be placed in a world. Pylons can only function when the minimap is enabled in the settings. The player must be within 60 tiles of a pylon to use it.

Forest Pylon.name: Forest Pylon
Forest Pylon.tooltip: Pylons are placeable furniture items that appear as a large crystal hovering and rotating above a biome-themed stand. With two or more pylons placed in the world, the player can teleport from one pylon to another one. The system they form is referred to as the Pylon Network. When the player is near a pylon, they can teleport to another pylon by doing any of the following: Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the pylon, which opens the full-screen map, and selecting another pylon on the map. Pressing Toggle Full Map to open the full-screen map, and selecting another pylon on the map.  Selecting another pylon on the overlay-mode or portrait-mode minimap. The following conditions must be met by both the pylon near the player and the target pylon (with the exception of the Universal Pylon): There must be two or more housed NPCs (including the Old Man and town pets) within a rectangular area of 169×124 tiles centered on each of the two pylons. More precisely, the home tile of the NPC (Dungeon point in the case of the Old Man) must be within this rectangle, and the NPC must be less than 100 tiles away from their home tile. The pylons must be placed in their respective biome. Moreover, the following restrictions apply to all pylons (including the Universal Pylon): Only one of each type of pylon may be placed in a world. Pylons can only function when the minimap is enabled in the settings. The player must be within 60 tiles of a pylon to use it.

Obsidian Crate.name: Obsidian Crate
Obsidian Crate.tooltip: The Obsidian Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can only be fished in lava. Opening Obsidian and Hellstone Crates is the only way to obtain the Obsidian Lock Box, and therefore any Underworld-exclusive items normally found in locked Shadow Chests, once the Underworld has been fully looted. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Hellstone Crate.

Hellstone Crate.name: Hellstone Crate
Hellstone Crate.tooltip: The Hellstone Crate is a Hardmode crate that can only be fished in lava. Opening Hellstone and Obsidian Crates is the only way to obtain the Obsidian Lock Box, and therefore any Underworld-exclusive items normally found in locked Shadow Chests, once the Underworld has been fully looted. Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Obsidian Crate.

Obsidian Lock Box.name: Obsidian Lock Box
Obsidian Lock Box.tooltip: The Obsidian Lock Box is a grab bag item which is always obtained from Obsidian and Hellstone Crates. It always contains one rare item normally found in locked Shadow Chests in the Underworld. It requires a Shadow Key to be in the player's inventory to open the box, which can be found in locked Gold Chests or Golden Lock Boxes in the Dungeon.

Lava Serpent Bowl.name: Lava Serpent Bowl
Lava Serpent Bowl.tooltip: The Fish Bowl, Gold Fish Bowl (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), Pupfish Bowl (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions), and Lava Serpent Bowl (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are decorative furniture items. The Fish Bowl and Gold Fish Bowl also double as wearable items that can be equipped in the player's helmet slot. Fish Bowls cause only visual effects when placed in the helmet vanity slot. When instead placed in the functional head armor slot, the breath meter appears as if the player were underwater, and if worn long enough the player will drown and die. Breathing aids like the Breathing Reed or Gills Potion will allow for normal breathing when wearing the bowl. The Fish, Gold Fish and Pupfish Bowls are crafted, while the Lava Serpent Bowl has a 39/200 (19.5%) chance of being found inside Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates. Crafted Fish Bowls can be converted back into their ingredients by throwing them into Shimmer, gaining back the fish as an item.

Lavaproof Fishing Hook.name: Lavaproof Fishing Hook
Lavaproof Fishing Hook.tooltip: The Lavaproof Fishing Hook is an accessory that allows the player to fish in lava with any bait and any fishing pole. It has a 19/100 (19%) chance of being obtained from Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates, both of which can be obtained from fishing in lava.

Amethyst Bunny Cage.name: Amethyst Bunny Cage
Amethyst Bunny Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters. A critter caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item. Gold cages are regular cages containing gold critters. Aside from their higher sell value and rarity, they are the same as regular cages. Placed cages are partially transparent. They can be stacked on top of each other, but no other types of furniture can be placed on a cage. Players can stand on top of cages like platforms, even though they are otherwise background furniture.

Ancient Hallowed Mask.name: Ancient Hallowed Mask
Ancient Hallowed Mask.tooltip: Ancient Hallowed armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Ancient Hallowed Plate Mail and Ancient Hallowed Greaves, as well as four different headpieces: the Ancient Hallowed Mask, Ancient Hallowed Helmet, Ancient Hallowed Headgear, and Ancient Hallowed Hood. It shares identical stats with Hallowed armor, but differs in appearance and is crafted at an altar instead. Ancient Hallowed armor pieces are interchangeable with Hallowed armor pieces, still providing the set bonus.

Potted Magma Palm.name: Potted Magma Palm
Potted Magma Palm.tooltip: Potted Lava Plants are placeable furniture items. They have a 1/2 (50%) chance of being dropped when opening an Obsidian Crate or Hellstone Crate. They give off a considerable amount of light when placed but do not count as light sources for NPC housing. They cannot be switched on or off using wiring.

Yellow Willow Sapling.name: Yellow Willow Sapling
Yellow Willow Sapling.tooltip: The Yellow Willow Sapling is a type of seed that grows into a Yellow Willow tree, which is a tree that can also spawn naturally in Forest biomes, when planted. Its appearance is purely decorative and it functions identically to regular forest trees. Yellow Willow Saplings can be purchased from the Zoologist for 1 Gold once the Bestiary is 30% completed (164 entries).

Dirt Bomb.name: Dirt Bomb
Dirt Bomb.tooltip: The Dirt Bomb is an explosive that functions like the Bomb, but its explosion will place Dirt Blocks in open spaces, instead of destroying blocks. Existing blocks within the explosion radius will remain unaffected.

Sticky Dirt Bomb.name: Sticky Dirt Bomb
Sticky Dirt Bomb.tooltip: The Sticky Dirt Bomb is an explosive that functions like the Dirt Bomb, but sticks onto any block on contact. If the block it sticks to is removed by some means, it will fall until it hits another.

Bunny License.name: Bunny License
Bunny License.tooltip: The Bunny License is a consumable item that can be purchased from the Zoologist for 5 Gold after filling out 45% (246 entries) of the Bestiary. Upon use, the status message "The license teleports away to the bunny delivery service..." is displayed. Following this status message, a Town Bunny will move into an available house the next morning. Using a second Bunny License when a Town Bunny is already present in the current world displays the status message "Pet Exchange: Successful!" and causes it to be "exchanged": the Town Bunny releases a puff of smoke and has its breed and name rerolled immediately.

Cool Whip.name: Cool Whip
Cool Whip.tooltip: The Cool Whip is a Hardmode whip. It has a 30% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit: 6 tag damage Grants the A Nice Buff buff, creating a homing snowflake projectile that lasts for 3 seconds, which repeatedly deals 15 damage and has 30 armor penetration. The snowflake also applies the Cool Whip's tag damage to enemies it hits, like the whip itself. If a snowflake already exists, Cool Whip hits will refresh its duration instead of creating a new one. Inflicts the Frostbite debuff for 4 seconds. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Firecracker.name: Firecracker
Firecracker.tooltip: The Firecracker is a Hardmode whip that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Wall of Flesh. It has a 34% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit: Marks enemies with blazing energy. When a minion or sentry damages an enemy marked by the Firecracker, a small explosion occurs and multiplies damage of the minion or sentry's attack by 2.75×. The explosion also hits other nearby enemies for 2.75× of the attack's damage. The mark is only applied to one enemy per strike, and the explosion effect only triggers once per mark. Inflicts the Hellfire debuff for 4 seconds to all hit targets. Its best modifier is Legendary. Light is also an option if enemies marked by the Firecracker can be attacked rapidly enough by minions or sentries.
Firecracker.drops_summary: Treasure Bag (Wall of Flesh) (25%), Wall of Flesh (25%)

Snapthorn.name: Snapthorn
Snapthorn.tooltip: The Snapthorn is a pre-Hardmode whip. It has a 40% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit: 6 tag damage Grants the Jungle's Fury buff, increasing whip speed by 12% for 3 seconds. This duration can be refreshed with further hits. Has a 1/5 (20%) chance to inflict the Poisoned debuff. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Kaleidoscope.name: Kaleidoscope
Kaleidoscope.tooltip: The Kaleidoscope is a Hardmode, post-Plantera whip that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Empress of Light. It has a 20% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit: 20 tag damage 10% tag critical strike chance Its best modifier is Legendary.
Kaleidoscope.drops_summary: Empress of Light (25%), Treasure Bag (Empress of Light) (25%)

Tungsten Bullet.name: Tungsten Bullet
Tungsten Bullet.tooltip: The Tungsten Bullet is a pre-Hardmode bullet. It deals 2 more damage and is slightly faster than Musket Balls. When either Musket Balls or Tungsten Bullets are fired with certain guns, they will be converted into a special projectile (e.g. the Uzi converting them into High Velocity Bullets). Some other guns, such as the Pew-matic Horn, can convert any type of bullet. Tungsten Bullets can be bought from the Arms Dealer for 18 Copper each, or 1 Gold 80 Silver for 1000 rounds in worlds with Tungsten. During pre-Hardmode, they are only sold during Blood Moons. Once Hardmode begins, they are always available. Tungsten Bullets can also be found replacing Wooden Arrows in Pots during Hardmode, in Shadow Chests, or crafted using Tungsten Bars. Its alternate ore counterpart is the Silver Bullet.

Hallow Pylon.name: Hallow Pylon
Hallow Pylon.tooltip: Pylons are placeable furniture items that appear as a large crystal hovering and rotating above a biome-themed stand. With two or more pylons placed in the world, the player can teleport from one pylon to another one. The system they form is referred to as the Pylon Network. When the player is near a pylon, they can teleport to another pylon by doing any of the following: Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the pylon, which opens the full-screen map, and selecting another pylon on the map. Pressing Toggle Full Map to open the full-screen map, and selecting another pylon on the map.  Selecting another pylon on the overlay-mode or portrait-mode minimap. The following conditions must be met by both the pylon near the player and the target pylon (with the exception of the Universal Pylon): There must be two or more housed NPCs (including the Old Man and town pets) within a rectangular area of 169×124 tiles centered on each of the two pylons. More precisely, the home tile of the NPC (Dungeon point in the case of the Old Man) must be within this rectangle, and the NPC must be less than 100 tiles away from their home tile. The pylons must be placed in their respective biome. Moreover, the following restrictions apply to all pylons (including the Universal Pylon): Only one of each type of pylon may be placed in a world. Pylons can only function when the minimap is enabled in the settings. The player must be within 60 tiles of a pylon to use it.

Cavern Water Fountain.name: Cavern Water Fountain
Cavern Water Fountain.tooltip: Water fountains are mechanisms and crafting stations that change the color of all nearby water. They can be activated via ⚷ Open / Activate or wire. Like Sinks, they can be used to craft items that require water as a crafting station. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) The range of a fountain's effects is a radius 60 tiles horizontally and 53 tiles vertically, measured from the edges of its sprite. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 10 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 8 different obtainable fountains, all of which are purchased from the Witch Doctor for 4 Gold each at any time.  Additionally, some special world seeds contain naturally generated Water Fountains on their Floating Islands: Drunk worlds have Icy and Desert Water Fountains. Celebration Mk 10 worlds have Hallowed Water Fountains. Remix worlds have Corrupt or Crimson Water Fountains depending on the world evil. On the  Old-gen console version and Nintendo 3DS versions, they can be purchased for free, but are only available after Plantera has been defeated.

Starlight.name: Starlight
Starlight.tooltip: The Starlight is a Hardmode, post-Plantera shortsword that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Empress of Light. When used, it rapidly emits short-range light beams that pierce infinitely. It also has a base 14% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. Its best modifier is Legendary.
Starlight.drops_summary: Empress of Light (25%), Treasure Bag (Empress of Light) (25%)

Eye of Cthulhu Relic.name: Eye of Cthulhu Relic
Eye of Cthulhu Relic.tooltip: Relics are furniture items dropped by bosses and mini-bosses in Master Mode. They are golden depictions of their respective boss that hover above a pedestal, have a golden particle effect, and emit light when placed close to a light source. There are 28 different relics available in Terraria.

Universal Pylon.name: Universal Pylon
Universal Pylon.tooltip: The Universal Pylon is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord pylon obtained by completing 100% of the Bestiary, at which point it will be sold by the Zoologist for 1 Platinum. It can be placed anywhere, and used in any biome. Unlike other pylon variants, it does not require a nearby NPC to function. Only one Universal Pylon can be placed in a world.

Nightglow.name: Nightglow
Nightglow.tooltip: The Nightglow is a Hardmode, post-Plantera magic weapon that fires four rainbow-colored projectiles which emerge from the player and home in on nearby enemies. Each projectile ricochets off solid blocks and can pierce twice before dissipating on the third hit, but loses 20% of its damage for each enemy struck. The Nightglow has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Empress of Light. Its best modifier is Mythical.
Nightglow.drops_summary: Empress of Light (25%), Treasure Bag (Empress of Light) (25%)

Eventide.name: Eventide
Eventide.tooltip: The Eventide is a Hardmode, post-Plantera bow that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by the Empress of Light. When used, it fires a burst of four arrows and one Twilight Lance projectile, with the Twilight Lance dealing 200% of the weapon's damage (110 base damage when using Wooden Arrows). It can also convert Wooden Arrows into Twilight Lances, which only deal 100% of the weapon's damage. The Twilight Lances are unaffected by gravity and can pierce four time, dissipating on the fifth hit. Its best modifier is Unreal.
Eventide.drops_summary: Empress of Light (25%), Treasure Bag (Empress of Light) (25%)

Celestial Starboard.name: Celestial Starboard
Celestial Starboard.tooltip: The Celestial Starboard is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord wing-type accessory. In addition to granting remarkable flight capabilities, it has both hover and upwards boost capability. At its top speed, it travels at 82 mph horizontal, 115 mph vertical, and 51 mph while falling. The Celestial Starboard is always dropped from the Moon Lord's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.

Rabbit Perch.name: Rabbit Perch
Rabbit Perch.tooltip: The Rabbit Perch is a vanity item purchased from the Zoologist for 15 Gold after filling out 40% (219 entries) of the Bestiary. Although the item appears to be a hat with rabbit ears, equipping it will show an animated rabbit on the player's head.

Zenith.name: Zenith
Zenith.tooltip: The Zenith is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord melee weapon. When used, it rapidly fires fast-moving swords towards the cursor in an arc returning to the player. The sword sprites can pass through blocks, pierce enemies infinitely, home in on nearby enemies, and create visual trails while traveling. The swords have varying appearances, which function identically and have the same hitbox size. The Zenith has a base 14% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. The Zenith will transform into the True Copper Shortsword when thrown into Shimmer. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Treasure Bag (Queen Slime).name: Treasure Bag (Queen Slime)
Treasure Bag (Queen Slime).tooltip: Treasure Bags are consumable grab bag-like items obtained in Expert Mode and Master Mode as a reward for defeating bosses. The contents and appearance of Treasure Bags depend on the boss it comes from, and are opened by using either ⚷ Open / Activate while inside the inventory, or ⚒ Use / Attack when selected in the hotbar. They emit light and have a special effect around them when dropped, making them easier to spot. In multiplayer, each player that deals damage to the boss receives one Treasure Bag upon defeating it. Treasure Bags are client-side and will despawn upon exiting the world. See Notes for details. Each Treasure Bag contains the boss's usual drops from Classic Mode, along with one Expert Mode-exclusive item (highlighted items below) – with the exception of the Lunatic Cultist, Dark Mage, Ogre, and Betsy, who do not provide an Expert Mode-exclusive item. Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses additionally have a 1/16 (6.25%) chance to contain one random set of developer items (with the exception of Queen Slime). Expert Mode-exclusive items all have the  rarity, with the exception of developer items, which have the  rarity.

Queen Slime Trophy.name: Queen Slime Trophy
Queen Slime Trophy.tooltip: Trophies are decorative furniture items which usually have a 1/10 (10%) chance to be dropped from most bosses. While they can be considered the "boss version of banners", they are purely cosmetic and do not provide any bonuses. Some trophies can only be rewarded by the Angler for completing fishing quests. In total, there are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 33 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 24 trophies.

Queen Slime Mask.name: Queen Slime Mask
Queen Slime Mask.tooltip: Masks are vanity items dropped by all non-event bosses, as well as those from the Old One's Army(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). They are worn in the social head slot. Each boss has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance to drop its own mask in all difficulties, with the following exceptions: The Skeletron Mask has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to drop from Skeletron's Treasure Bag. The Dark Mage Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 1) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Dark Mage. The Ogre Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 2) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Ogre.

Regal Delicacy.name: Regal Delicacy
Regal Delicacy.tooltip: The Regal Delicacy is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns a Slime Princess that follows the player. The pet resembles a miniature Queen Slime with blush, small dotted eyes, and a tiny mouth. The Regal Delicacy has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Queen Slime in Master Mode.

Prismatic Lacewing.name: Prismatic Lacewing
Prismatic Lacewing.tooltip: The Prismatic Lacewing is a rare Hardmode, post-Plantera flying critter and boss-summoning item that spawns on the surface Hallow after Plantera has been defeated. Prismatic Lacewings disappear almost instantaneously when spawned in any other biome, and only spawn in the Hallow between dusk (7:30 PM) and midnight (12:00 AM). When killed by a player, it summons the Empress of Light; death from non-player sources will generally not result in summoning. Only one Prismatic Lacewing can be naturally spawned at a time. The Prismatic Lacewing can be caught with Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, and Golden Bug Net. Releasing it from the inventory (with ⚒ Use / Attack) and killing it will still summon the Empress of Light. It is one of the few entities that can be detected by the Lifeform Analyzer or its upgrades.

Stone Accent Slab.name: Stone Accent Slab
Stone Accent Slab.tooltip: The Stone Accent Slab is a block which is visually identical to the Stone Slab, except that it does not blend with any blocks other than itself and Smooth Marble Blocks.

Truffle Worm Cage.name: Truffle Worm Cage
Truffle Worm Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters. A critter caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item. Gold cages are regular cages containing gold critters. Aside from their higher sell value and rarity, they are the same as regular cages. Placed cages are partially transparent. They can be stacked on top of each other, but no other types of furniture can be placed on a cage. Players can stand on top of cages like platforms, even though they are otherwise background furniture.

Prismatic Lacewing Jar.name: Prismatic Lacewing Jar
Prismatic Lacewing Jar.tooltip: The Prismatic Lacewing Jar is a placeable furniture item which displays the Prismatic Lacewing, normally a critter which summons the Empress of Light boss if killed. This item is a safe method of displaying captured Prismatic Lacewings. Similarly to the critter it emits light when placed. By throwing a Prismatic Lacewing Jar into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the Prismatic Lacewing as an item.  The item cannot be used to summon the Empress of Light, and is purely decorative. A Prismatic Lacewing must be killed to summon the boss.

Rock Golem Banner.name: Rock Golem Banner
Rock Golem Banner.tooltip: Enemy banners are functional furniture items that can be placed on the underside of blocks and platforms. They are obtained by killing most enemies and a few critters. When placed, enemy banners provide a Banner buff to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the banner. The buff grants players +50%/+100% damage inflicted with all damage to the corresponding enemy and −25%/−50% damage taken from attacks by the enemy. The banners of Old One's Army enemies will apply a weaker banner buff to the respective enemy, granting the players +10%/+20% damage inflicted and −8.33% / −16.67% damage taken. Multiple banners of the same type will not grant stacked buffs. Multiple different banner types in the vicinity will, however, all take effect and consolidate into a single buff icon. There are a total of 286 obtainable enemy banners: 115 in pre-Hardmode, 171 in Hardmode. Out of these, 118 belong to event enemies (28 in pre-Hardmode and 90 in Hardmode). In addition, there are 6 unobtainable enemy banners.

Fledgling Wings.name: Fledgling Wings
Fledgling Wings.tooltip: The Fledgling Wings are the only pre-Hardmode wings. Like all wings, they grant the player the ability to fly and glide when equipped, as well as not take fall damage. At top speed, they allow traveling at 15 mph horizontally and 22 mph vertically. They have a flight time of 0.42 seconds and a vertical speed multiplier of 150%. The Fledgling Wings have a 1/40 (2.5%) chance of being obtained from Skyware Chests, Sky Crates, and Azure Crates. Journey Mode characters always spawn with a pair of Fledgling Wings.
Fledgling Wings.drops_summary: Azure Crate (2.5%), Sky Crate (2.5%), Skyware Chest (2.5%)

Music Box (Queen Slime).name: Music Box (Queen Slime)
Music Box (Queen Slime).tooltip: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End), which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 Gold after defeating the Moon Lord. A recorded Music Box can be played back in one of two ways: Equipping it as an accessory. Placing it as furniture and activating it, either by the ⚷ Open / Activate button or with wires. Recorded Music Boxes can be reverted into blank ones through Shimmer transmutation. There are 101 different Music Boxes available.

Hook of Dissonance.name: Hook of Dissonance
Hook of Dissonance.tooltip: The Hook of Dissonance is a Hardmode grappling hook that fires a single hook that reaches 30 tiles; when the hook attaches to a block, it will instantly teleport the user to the hook's position if the path to the hook is wide enough to fit a player. The Hook of Dissonance has a 1/3 (33.33%) / 1/2 (50%) chance of being dropped by Queen Slime.

Gelatinous Pillion.name: Gelatinous Pillion
Gelatinous Pillion.tooltip: The Gelatinous Pillion is a Hardmode mount-summoning item that summons a friendly Winged Slime Mount. Similar to the pre-Hardmode Slime Mount, the Winged Slime offers increased jump height, provides boosted movement speed, negates fall damage, and allows continuous auto-jump by holding the ↷ Jump key. It also shares the Slime Mount's abilities to deal 40 summon damage to enemies when jumping on them from above, and floating when entering liquids. The Winged Slime Mount grants 2.66 seconds of flight time, similar to low-tier wings, allowing the player to fly up to a height of 73 tiles, as well as gliding while holding the ↷ Jump key after flight time has been exhausted. It can also hover by holding ▼ Down, similar to the Hoverboard. The Gelatinous Pillion has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Queen Slime in Classic Mode, or a 1/2 (50%) chance of being found in Queen Slime's Treasure Bag.

Crystal Assassin Hood.name: Crystal Assassin Hood
Crystal Assassin Hood.tooltip: Crystal Assassin armor is a Hardmode armor set consisting of the Crystal Assassin Hood, Crystal Assassin Shirt, and Crystal Assassin Pants. Queen Slime always drops one piece / two pieces upon defeat. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +36 defense +15% damage +15% critical strike chance +10% melee speed +10% ammo conservation +10% mana cost reduction +20% movement speed The ability to dash by pressing Dash, or by double-tapping ◀ Left or ▶ Right while the "Double Tap Dashing" setting is enabled.

Crystal Assassin Shirt.name: Crystal Assassin Shirt
