Sparkle Slime Balloon.name: Sparkle Slime Balloon
Sparkle Slime Balloon.tooltip: The Sparkle Slime Balloon is a Hardmode novelty consumable item. Upon colliding with solid blocks, it inflicts the Sparkle Slime debuff on players (including the user), enemies, critters, and NPCs within a radius of 9 tiles, causing them to become tinted purple and drip with pink and purple slime for 30 seconds. This debuff is only cosmetic and deals no damage. The Diva Slime spawns and moves in after throwing or discarding a Sparkle Slime Balloon into Shimmer. Queen Slime always drops 25–75 / 25–74 Sparkle Slime Balloons upon her defeat, and they are also dropped by Jungle Mimics, which spawn in Celebration Mk 10 and Zenith worlds.
Sparkle Slime Balloon.drops_summary: Mimics (33%), Queen Slime (100%), Treasure Bag (Queen Slime) (100%)

Volatile Gelatin.name: Volatile Gelatin
Volatile Gelatin.tooltip: The Volatile Gelatin is a Hardmode accessory that periodically fires small, purple slimeballs similar to those of the Queen Slime's Regal Gel projectiles at nearby enemies. The Volatile Gelatin's projectiles are affected by gravity and can pierce up to two entities or ricochet up to two times, dissipating upon the third time. The projectiles deal 65 classless damage while inflicting a knockback value of 7 (Strong); these values are unaffected by any boosts. The Volatile Gelatin is always dropped from Queen Slime's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode. The Volatile Gelatin has a fixed cycle: once every 0.67 seconds (40 ticks), it attempts to release a projectile towards the nearest enemy within 40 tiles that has unobstructed line of sight to the player. If there are no valid targets, no projectile will be fired and the accessory will go on cooldown for the following 40 ticks.

Gelatin Crystal.name: Gelatin Crystal
Gelatin Crystal.tooltip: The Gelatin Crystal is a Hardmode boss-summoning item that summons Queen Slime when used. It can only be used in The Hallow or Underground Hallow, at any time. Crystal Shards have a 1/50 (2%) chance to be replaced by a Gelatin Crystal upon generation. A Shard will drop a Crystal when broken.

Soaring Insignia.name: Soaring Insignia
Soaring Insignia.tooltip: The Soaring Insignia is a Hardmode, post-Plantera accessory that boosts the player's flight and movement abilities. It has the following effects: Increases acceleration by 75%, from 0.3 tiles/second² to 0.525 tiles/second², grants infinite flight time, and increases jump speed by 1.8 Increases movement speed by 7.5% Additionally, it increases flight ascent speed with wings or Rocket Boots. With the Soaring Insignia equipped, the player will reach maximum movement speed much quicker and will be able to stop, change directions, and go from flying upwards to falling or vice versa very quickly. The Soaring Insignia is always dropped from the Empress of Light's Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.

Chippy's Couch.name: Chippy's Couch
Chippy's Couch.tooltip: Chippy's Couch is a furniture item that has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being dropped by Skeletron.

Blue Graduation Cap.name: Blue Graduation Cap
Blue Graduation Cap.tooltip: The Blue Graduation set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Blue Graduation Cap and the Blue Graduation Gown. They are purchased from the Clothier for 20 Gold (set) during a Waning Crescent. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Maroon Graduation Cap.name: Maroon Graduation Cap
Maroon Graduation Cap.tooltip: The Maroon Graduation set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Maroon Graduation Cap and the Maroon Graduation Gown. They are purchased from the Clothier for 20 Gold (set) during a Waxing Crescent. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Terraspark Boots.name: Terraspark Boots
Terraspark Boots.tooltip: The Terraspark Boots are a pre-Hardmode accessory crafted from Frostspark Boots and Lava Waders, and combines their functionality. They grant the following effects while equipped: The ability to sprint, allowing the player to reach maximum running speed faster. The player will leave behind a visual trail of snow clouds as they sprint. Increased maximum movement speed to 35 mph (25.67 tiles/second). The ability to hold ↷ Jump in midair to fly for a total of 1.17 seconds. While flying, the boots emit a visual trail of green sparks. When paired with wings, this flight is disabled to give the wings an additional 0.7 seconds of flight time. Increased acceleration and deceleration on all Ice Blocks, Thin Ice, Frozen Slime Blocks, and Aetherium Blocks. The player will no longer cause Thin Ice to break upon landing. The ability to stand and walk on the surface of all liquids. Prevents fall damage when landing on the surface of any liquid. Immunity to the Burning debuff. Immunity to lava for 7 seconds. After this runs out, it decreases the damage taken from lava from 80 to 35, and reduces the duration of the On Fire! debuff inflicted by it from 7 / 14 / 17.5 seconds to 3.5 / 7 / 8.75 seconds. Equipping the Ash Wood armor at the same time provides immunity to lava damage and the debuff.

Moon Lord Legs.name: Moon Lord Legs
Moon Lord Legs.tooltip: The Moon Lord Legs are an armor item for the legs slot. They are exclusively found in worlds created with the Drunk seed active, where they have a 1/15 (6.67%) chance to generate as secondary loot in all naturally generated Chests. They grant the following effects while equipped: +3 defense Increases the maximum safe falling distance by 10 tiles, jump speed by 1.8, and jump duration by 1 Increases movement speed by 25% The player's legs are replaced with Moon Lord-themed tentacles with a unique walking animation.

Ocean Crate.name: Ocean Crate
Ocean Crate.tooltip: The Ocean Crate is a pre-Hardmode crate that can only be fished in the Ocean. Ocean Crates contain items found in standard crates, and always contain one item normally found in Water Chests. Its Hardmode counterpart is the Seaside Crate.

Seaside Crate.name: Seaside Crate
Seaside Crate.tooltip: The Seaside Crate is a Hardmode crate that can only be fished in the Ocean. Seaside Crates contain items found in standard crates, and always contain one item normally found in Water Chests. Its pre-Hardmode counterpart is the Ocean Crate.

Badger's Hat.name: Badger's Hat
Badger's Hat.tooltip: Badger's Hat is a Hardmode vanity item dropped by the Eye of Cthulhu or the Wall of Flesh when they are both defeated on the same day (from 7:30 PM to 7:30 PM the next day).
Badger's Hat.drops_summary: Eye of Cthulhu (100%), Wall of Flesh (100%)

Terraprisma.name: Terraprisma
Terraprisma.tooltip: The Terraprisma is a Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Terraprisma minion. It flies towards enemies, performing a quick stab before repeatedly attacking with a swinging or stabbing motion. Terraprisma arrange themselves in a wing-like pattern behind the player, and immediately return to the player if no enemies are nearby. The Terraprisma is always dropped from the Empress of Light when all damage dealt to the boss occurs during the day. Its best modifier is Fabled. However, if the player's summon damage bonuses reach 158% (including whip bonuses) or 58% (excluding whip bonuses), the best modifier becomes Ruthless.

Dead Man's Sweater.name: Dead Man's Sweater
Dead Man's Sweater.tooltip: The Dead Man's Sweater is an armor item with a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being found inside Dead Man's Chests. It provides 4 defense, and reduces the duration of the debuffs inflicted by trap projectiles and the damage dealt by them by 50%. If the damage dealt by trap projectiles is greater than 300 after the 50% reduction, it is then set to 300. This is applied before the damage is reduced by the player's defense.

Teapot.name: Teapot
Teapot.tooltip: The Teapot is a crafting station used solely to make Teacups. It can be placed anywhere.

Teacup.name: Teacup
Teacup.tooltip: The Teacup is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().

Treasure Magnet.name: Treasure Magnet
Treasure Magnet.tooltip: The Treasure Magnet is a post-Skeletron accessory which increases the pickup range of items from 2.625 tiles to 12 tiles while equipped. When an item is within its range, before directly flying to the player, it will hover a few blocks off the ground. The Treasure Magnet has a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Shadow Chests in the Underworld, as well as a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Obsidian Lock Boxes obtained from Obsidian Crates and Hellstone Crates.

Mace.name: Mace
Mace.tooltip: The Mace is a pre-Hardmode flail found in Gold Chests located in the underground or cavern layer. Its best modifier is Ruthless. Godly and Demonic modifiers may give higher crit chance, but rounding causes Ruthless to have much higher damage for this weapon.

Flaming Mace.name: Flaming Mace
Flaming Mace.tooltip: The Flaming Mace is a pre-Hardmode flail. It has a 1/6 (16.67%) chance to inflict the On Fire! debuff on hit. While the player is in water or the flail's head is submerged, the fire is extinguished and the weapon effectively becomes a regular Mace. Its best modifier is Ruthless. Godly and Demonic may give higher crit chance, but rounding causes Ruthless to have much higher damage for this weapon.

Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End), which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 Gold after defeating the Moon Lord. A recorded Music Box can be played back in one of two ways: Equipping it as an accessory. Placing it as furniture and activating it, either by the ⚷ Open / Activate button or with wires. Recorded Music Boxes can be reverted into blank ones through Shimmer transmutation. There are 101 different Music Boxes available.

Carton of Milk.name: Carton of Milk
Carton of Milk.tooltip: The Carton of Milk is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 20 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Carton of Milk has a 1/150 (0.67%) chance of being dropped by Skeletons and Spore Skeletons. Statue-spawned Skeletons do not drop it, as it is a food item.

Coffee.name: Coffee
Coffee.tooltip: Coffee is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 10 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). Coffee has a 1/30 (3.33%) chance of being dropped by Snatchers, Man Eaters, and Angry Trappers, and a 1/10 (10%) chance of being dropped by Bone Lees.

Torch God's Favor.name: Torch God's Favor
Torch God's Favor.tooltip: Torch God's Favor is a permanent booster item that permanently grants the player the ability to automatically convert regular Torches and Campfires in the player's hand to the current biome's torch or campfire variant, which increases the player's torch luck in most areas. The Torch God's Favor can only be obtained by surviving The Torch God event if at least 95 Torches were fired during the event. Torch God's Favor is a one-time consumable whose effect cannot stack (similar to the Advanced Combat Techniques or the Demon Heart). When first used, the ability is switched on by default and can then be toggled off and on via a toggle appearing  to the left of the inventory /  in the tools menu below the inventory. Torches and campfires placed with the ability toggled on will permanently remain converted to the biome variant they were placed as, even if freed and picked up.

Plaguebringer's Skull.name: Plaguebringer's Skull
Plaguebringer's Skull.tooltip: The Plaguebringer set is a vanity set consisting of the Plaguebringer's Skull, the Plaguebringer's Cloak, and the Plaguebringer's Treads. It is one of the six sets that were added as part of the Journey's End Vanity Contest; the original concept was submitted by SodaHunter. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. Crafting the set requires materials that can only be found in the Crimson. Its Corruption counterpart is the Timeless Traveler's set. It is possible for the player to create an artificial Crimson biome in a Corrupt world by purchasing Crimson Seeds from the Dryad in a Graveyard during Hardmode to get the materials necessary to make this set.  When the full set is worn, it displays a special set animation of Cursed Flames emitting from it. The color of the flames will change according to the dye applied to the cloak.

Lavaproof Tackle Bag.name: Lavaproof Tackle Bag
Lavaproof Tackle Bag.tooltip: The Lavaproof Tackle Bag is an accessory that combines the functionalities of its components: the Angler Earring's 10% boost to Fishing Power, the Tackle Box's chance not to consume bait, the unbreakable quality of the High Test Fishing Line, and the ability to fish in lava from the Lavaproof Fishing Hook. The Lavaproof Tackle Bag's increase in Fishing Power stacks with that of the Angler Earring and the Angler Tackle Bag, granting a total boost of 30% if all three are equipped. The decreased chance to consume bait does not stack with that of the Tackle Box or the Angler Tackle Bag.

Resonance Scepter.name: Resonance Scepter
Resonance Scepter.tooltip: The Resonance Scepter is a Hardmode, post-Plantera wand that has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being dropped by the Princess. When used, it creates pink circular auras at the cursor's location, which expand and then collapse into sparkles over the course of 1 second. The auras deal rapid damage and knockback. Although the projectile appears to instantly travel to its target, there must be a clear line of sight between the player and the cursor's location; the projectile will be summoned at the location of impact with the first block. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Bee Hive.name: Bee Hive
Bee Hive.tooltip: The Bee Hive is a natural trap which spawns over time under Jungle grass ceilings of the Jungle and Underground Jungle. When a Bee Hive is hit, it falls to the ground and rolls, releasing 2–5 Bees upon breaking. If it falls into any liquid, it will not release any Bees upon breaking, and drop 2–5 Hive blocks instead. It can be crafted and placed manually.

Antlion Eggs.name: Antlion Eggs
Antlion Eggs.tooltip: Antlion Eggs are background objects that are found in naturally-generated clusters in the Underground Desert. They spawn an Antlion Larva when hit with nearly any tool, weapon, or projectile.

Flinx Fur Coat.name: Flinx Fur Coat
Flinx Fur Coat.tooltip: The Flinx Fur Coat is a pre-Hardmode armor piece. When equipped, it gives the player an additional minion slot, and increases summon damage by 5%.

Flinx Staff.name: Flinx Staff
Flinx Staff.tooltip: The Flinx Staff is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons a Flinx minion. It runs towards enemies, bouncing upwards upon contact before attempting to hit its target again. Its rapid attack rate also allows its bouncing to keep it airborne atop slow flying enemies. Its best modifier is Fabled.

Flinx Fur.name: Flinx Fur
Flinx Fur.tooltip: Flinx Fur is a crafting material dropped by Snow Flinx, an enemy found in the Ice biome. They drop 1–2 / 1–3 Flinx Fur.

Royal Tiara.name: Royal Tiara
Royal Tiara.tooltip: The Royal set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Royal Tiara, Royal Blouse, and the Royal Dress. It is purchased from the Princess for 1 Platinum 50 Gold (set).

Royal Blouse.name: Royal Blouse
Royal Blouse.tooltip: The Royal set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Royal Tiara, Royal Blouse, and the Royal Dress. It is purchased from the Princess for 1 Platinum 50 Gold (set).

Royal Dress.name: Royal Dress
Royal Dress.tooltip: The Royal set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Royal Tiara, Royal Blouse, and the Royal Dress. It is purchased from the Princess for 1 Platinum 50 Gold (set).

Spinal Tap.name: Spinal Tap
Spinal Tap.tooltip: The Spinal Tap is a pre-Hardmode, post-Skeletron whip with a tag effect of +7 damage, and it has a 10% multihit penalty.

Rainbow Cursor.name: Rainbow Cursor
Rainbow Cursor.tooltip: The Rainbow Cursor is a Hardmode, post-Plantera vanity accessory that causes the player's cursor to cycle through the colors of the rainbow continuously.
Rainbow Cursor.drops_summary: Empress of Light (5%), Treasure Bag (Empress of Light) (5%)

Royal Scepter.name: Royal Scepter
Royal Scepter.tooltip: The Royal Scepter is a vanity accessory sold by the Princess for 1 Platinum. The Royal Scepter cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Glass Slipper.name: Glass Slipper
Glass Slipper.tooltip: The Glass Slipper is a vanity accessory sold by the Princess for 1 Platinum. It will leave sparkling particles when the player walks around. The Glass Slipper cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Prince Uniform.name: Prince Uniform
Prince Uniform.tooltip: The Prince set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Prince Uniform, Prince Cape, and the Prince Pants. It is purchased from the Princess for 1 Platinum 50 Gold (set). These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Prince Pants.name: Prince Pants
Prince Pants.tooltip: The Prince set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Prince Uniform, Prince Cape, and the Prince Pants. It is purchased from the Princess for 1 Platinum 50 Gold (set). These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Prince Cape.name: Prince Cape
Prince Cape.tooltip: The Prince set is a Hardmode vanity set consisting of the Prince Uniform, Prince Cape, and the Prince Pants. It is purchased from the Princess for 1 Platinum 50 Gold (set). These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Potted Crystal Fern.name: Potted Crystal Fern
Potted Crystal Fern.tooltip: Potted Crystal Plants are placeable furniture items. They are purchased from the Princess for 10 Gold each.

Potted Crystal Spiral.name: Potted Crystal Spiral
Potted Crystal Spiral.tooltip: Potted Crystal Plants are placeable furniture items. They are purchased from the Princess for 10 Gold each.

Potted Crystal Teardrop.name: Potted Crystal Teardrop
Potted Crystal Teardrop.tooltip: Potted Crystal Plants are placeable furniture items. They are purchased from the Princess for 10 Gold each.

Potted Crystal Tree.name: Potted Crystal Tree
Potted Crystal Tree.tooltip: Potted Crystal Plants are placeable furniture items. They are purchased from the Princess for 10 Gold each.

Princess 64.name: Princess 64
Princess 64.tooltip: Paintings are decorative furniture items that can be placed on background walls. Each one is a framed image that depicts a particular scene, usually Terraria-related. Their tooltips generally contain a person's name, intended to credit each painting's artist; although the names appear to be fictional, most of them correspond to known Terraria developers, artists, testing staff, and community members (see Trivia below). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions, the Magic Lantern, Spelunker Glowsticks, and Spelunker Flares. There are a total of 193 paintings, 25 of which are sold by the Painter, 7 by the Princess, 4 by the Golfer, 2 by the Zoologist, 2 by the Clothier, 1 by the Truffle, and 27 are randomly sold by the Traveling Merchant. 35 paintings can be found in Underground Cabins, another 14 in the Underground Desert Cabins, 26 in the Dungeon, 12 in The Underworld, 6 from Floating Islands, 5 obtained by fishing, 1 from the Jungle Temple, 5 randomly acquired from Goodie Bags, 8 dropped by Solar Eclipse enemies, 8 awarded randomly by the Angler for completing fishing quests, 1 from the Living Tree, and 4 dropped by enemies.

Bernie's Button.name: Bernie's Button
Bernie's Button.tooltip: Bernie's Button is a Hardmode, post-Plantera pet-summoning item that spawns  Bernie to follow the player. Bernie's Button can be purchased from the Princess for 25 Gold.

Glommer's Flower.name: Glommer's Flower
Glommer's Flower.tooltip: Glommer's Flower is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that spawns Glommer to follow the player. Glommer's Flower is dropped from Derplings with a 1/100 (1%) chance and increased to 1/40 (2.5%) in The Constant secret seed.

Deerclops Eyeball.name: Deerclops Eyeball
Deerclops Eyeball.tooltip: The Deerclops Eyeball is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Tiny Deerclops that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, Tiny Deerclops flies while holding onto a bird to catch up with them. The Deerclops Eyeball has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Deerclops in Master Mode.

Monster Meat.name: Monster Meat
Monster Meat.tooltip: The Monster Meat is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Pig Man that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Pig Man flies while carrying an Umbrella from Don't Starve in order to catch up. The Monster Meat can be dropped from most Corruption or Crimson enemies with a 1/1500 (0.07%) chance. On The Constant seed, the drop rate is increased to a 1/500 (0.2%) chance.

Monster Lasagna.name: Monster Lasagna
Monster Lasagna.tooltip: The Monster Lasagna is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 8 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().

Froggle Bunwich.name: Froggle Bunwich
Froggle Bunwich.tooltip: The Froggle Bunwich is a food item that grants the Plenty Satisfied buff when consumed. This lasts for 6 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().

Tentacle Spike.name: Tentacle Spike
Tentacle Spike.tooltip: The Tentacle Spike is a pre-Hardmode broadsword dropped by Eaters of Souls, Devourers, Crimeras, Face Monsters, and Blood Crawlers with a 1/525 (0.19%) chance. When swung, it sticks tentacle spikes into enemies on hit, which linger on the enemy and deal 3 damage per second for 9 seconds. The spikes can stack up to 5 times on each target. On The Constant seed, the drop chance is increased to a 1/100 (1%) chance. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Lucy the Axe.name: Lucy the Axe
Lucy the Axe.tooltip: Lucy the Axe is a pre-Hardmode axe that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Deerclops. She occasionally displays a line of dialogue depending on certain player actions. Lucy the Axe also has a base 14% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. Her best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Ham Bat.name: Ham Bat
Ham Bat.tooltip: The Ham Bat is a Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/25 (4%) chance of being dropped by Pigrons. It gains slightly increased damage if a food buff is active. Killing an enemy with the Ham Bat grants the Hearty Meal buff, which increases the player's health regeneration by 3 per second. This lasts for 7 seconds, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The buff will not stack upon killing another enemy; the duration instead resets. In a The Constant world, the drop chance is increased to 1/10 (10%). Its best modifier is Legendary.

Bat Bat.name: Bat Bat
Bat Bat.tooltip: The Bat Bat is a pre-Hardmode broadsword that has a 1/300 (0.33%) chance of being dropped by any type of bat. When swung, it restores 1 health to the user upon hitting an enemy. On The Constant seed, the drop chance is increased to a 1/100 (1%) chance. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Eye Bone.name: Eye Bone
Eye Bone.tooltip: The Eye Bone is a pet-summoning item that spawns Chester, a mobile Piggy Bank, to follow the player. Chester, being a pet, is essentially an upgrade to the Money Trough as it follows the player and does not require repeated summons. The Eye Bone has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by Deerclops.

Garland.name: Garland
Garland.tooltip: The Garland is a vanity item for the Social Helmet slot.

Bone Helm.name: Bone Helm
Bone Helm.tooltip: The Bone Helm is a pre-Hardmode accessory that summons Shadow Hand projectiles to damage enemies. These Shadow Hands spawn a distance from enemies before flying at them, piercing anything in their path including through blocks. Their flight behavior mirrors the Shadow Hands found in the Deerclops fight, either flying straight or swerving harshly in flight. The Bone Helm is always dropped from Deerclops' Treasure Bag in Expert Mode.

Eyebrella.name: Eyebrella
Eyebrella.tooltip: The Eyebrella is a vanity item that has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of being dropped by Deerclops. When equipped, it summons a raincloud that constantly produces raindrops above the player's head. This effect is purely visual; it does not deal any damage.

Gentleman's Vest.name: Gentleman's Vest
Gentleman's Vest.tooltip: The Gentleman's set is a vanity set consisting of the Gentleman's Beard, the Gentleman's Long Beard, the Gentleman's Magnificent Beard, the Gentleman's Vest, and the Gentleman's Trousers. The Vest and Trousers can be crafted, while the Gentleman's Beard can be bought from the Stylist for 5 Gold. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. When equipped in an accessory slot, the Gentleman's Beard will grow longer over time. After 12 minutes of being equipped, the beard has a 1/9 (11.11%) chance every second to grow to the next stage. This growth is not affected by speeding up time, and will not occur when the beard is equipped in a vanity slot. The beard also changes colors based on the player's hair color. The longer versions of the beard can be crafted back into the shorter versions.

Gentleman's Trousers.name: Gentleman's Trousers
Gentleman's Trousers.tooltip: The Gentleman's set is a vanity set consisting of the Gentleman's Beard, the Gentleman's Long Beard, the Gentleman's Magnificent Beard, the Gentleman's Vest, and the Gentleman's Trousers. The Vest and Trousers can be crafted, while the Gentleman's Beard can be bought from the Stylist for 5 Gold. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance. When equipped in an accessory slot, the Gentleman's Beard will grow longer over time. After 12 minutes of being equipped, the beard has a 1/9 (11.11%) chance every second to grow to the next stage. This growth is not affected by speeding up time, and will not occur when the beard is equipped in a vanity slot. The beard also changes colors based on the player's hair color. The longer versions of the beard can be crafted back into the shorter versions.

Magiluminescence.name: Magiluminescence
Magiluminescence.tooltip: The Magiluminescence is a pre-Hardmode accessory that increases the player's maximum movement speed by 15% and their acceleration and deceleration by 75%. This increase stacks with the bonus of the Hermes Boots and their variants. It also creates an aura of light around the player, which can be useful when exploring underground. The Magiluminescence's movement speed buffs are disabled when the player is not grounded.

Deerclops Trophy.name: Deerclops Trophy
Deerclops Trophy.tooltip: Trophies are decorative furniture items which usually have a 1/10 (10%) chance to be dropped from most bosses. While they can be considered the "boss version of banners", they are purely cosmetic and do not provide any bonuses. Some trophies can only be rewarded by the Angler for completing fishing quests. In total, there are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 33 / (Old-gen console and 3DS versions) 24 trophies.

Deerclops Mask.name: Deerclops Mask
Deerclops Mask.tooltip: Masks are vanity items dropped by all non-event bosses, as well as those from the Old One's Army(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). They are worn in the social head slot. Each boss has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance to drop its own mask in all difficulties, with the following exceptions: The Skeletron Mask has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to drop from Skeletron's Treasure Bag. The Dark Mage Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 1) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Dark Mage. The Ogre Mask has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance (tier 2) or 1/14 (7.14%) chance (tier 3) to drop from the Ogre.

Deerclops Relic.name: Deerclops Relic
Deerclops Relic.tooltip: Relics are furniture items dropped by bosses and mini-bosses in Master Mode. They are golden depictions of their respective boss that hover above a pedestal, have a golden particle effect, and emit light when placed close to a light source. There are 28 different relics available in Terraria.

Treasure Bag (Deerclops).name: Treasure Bag (Deerclops)
Treasure Bag (Deerclops).tooltip: Treasure Bags are consumable grab bag-like items obtained in Expert Mode and Master Mode as a reward for defeating bosses. The contents and appearance of Treasure Bags depend on the boss it comes from, and are opened by using either ⚷ Open / Activate while inside the inventory, or ⚒ Use / Attack when selected in the hotbar. They emit light and have a special effect around them when dropped, making them easier to spot. In multiplayer, each player that deals damage to the boss receives one Treasure Bag upon defeating it. Treasure Bags are client-side and will despawn upon exiting the world. See Notes for details. Each Treasure Bag contains the boss's usual drops from Classic Mode, along with one Expert Mode-exclusive item (highlighted items below) – with the exception of the Lunatic Cultist, Dark Mage, Ogre, and Betsy, who do not provide an Expert Mode-exclusive item. Treasure Bags dropped from Hardmode bosses additionally have a 1/16 (6.25%) chance to contain one random set of developer items (with the exception of Queen Slime). Expert Mode-exclusive items all have the  rarity, with the exception of developer items, which have the  rarity.

Music Box (Deerclops).name: Music Box (Deerclops)
Music Box (Deerclops).tooltip: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End), which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 Gold after defeating the Moon Lord. A recorded Music Box can be played back in one of two ways: Equipping it as an accessory. Placing it as furniture and activating it, either by the ⚷ Open / Activate button or with wires. Recorded Music Boxes can be reverted into blank ones through Shimmer transmutation. There are 101 different Music Boxes available.

Radio Thing.name: Radio Thing
Radio Thing.tooltip: Monoliths are furniture items that activate backgrounds and other screen effects normally seen during events or under other special circumstances. When placed, they can be toggled with the ⚷ Open / Activate button or via wire, like other mechanisms, providing their effects in a small area around them. Monoliths only cause modified visuals; they do not spawn any event enemies or bosses, and they do not change the music. They can also be equipped as vanity accessories, which enables their effect globally for the player. There are 11 different monoliths: the Vortex, Nebula, Stardust, Solar, and Void Monoliths can be crafted at an Ancient Manipulator, the Blood Moon Monolith has a 1/10 (10%) chance of being dropped by Dreadnautiluses, the Radio Thing has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to be dropped by Deerclops, the Aether Monolith can be obtained via dropping an Angel Statue into Shimmer, the CRT and Retro Monoliths are sold by the Cyborg for 25 Gold, and the Film Projector can be obtained as part of Heroicis' set by dropping a Platinum Coin into the Water of an Oasis. The Nebula, Solar, Stardust, and Vortex Monoliths mimic effects that normally surround the corresponding Celestial Pillar during the Lunar Events. The Blood Moon Monolith mimics the effects seen during a Blood Moon. The Void Monolith mimics the screen effects of the Moon Lord boss fight. The Radio Thing activates the same sepia filter of The Constant world seed. In The Constant seed, however, it instead deactivates the filter. The Aether Monolith mimics the screen effects of the Aether mini-biome. Unlike the other monoliths, the Aether Monolith has three states: One off state (which disables the Aether effect entirely in its area, even if it would normally be present due to Shimmer) and two on states – low, which acts as if the monolith were not present (allowing the Aether effect if enough Shimmer is nearby but not forcing it on), and high, which forces the Aether effect on. The CRT Monolith mimics the effect of an old-fashioned CRT TV. The Retro Monolith mimics the effect of an old two-color green and black monitor, like the original Gameboy. The Film Projector adds a black-and-white effect to the screen.

Abigail's Flower.name: Abigail's Flower
Abigail's Flower.tooltip: Abigail's Flower is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons the Abigail minion. She floats towards enemies and inflicts continuous contact damage, as well as pausing to emit damaging flashes of light. When Abigail's Flower is used more than once, multiple Abigails do not spawn; instead, the existing Abigail becomes stronger and faster for each additional summon. Abigail has a visual indicator for the number of times she is summoned, with the flower on her head changing shape and hue for each stage. In Hardmode, the boost from multiple summons is much greater. Abigail's Flower can be uncommonly found as a plant growing on grass near a placed Tombstone, regardless of world progression. It spawns more frequently in The Constant and Zenith worlds. Its best modifier is Fabled.

Firestarter's Sweater.name: Firestarter's Sweater
Firestarter's Sweater.tooltip: The Firestarter's set is a vanity set consisting of the Firestarter's Sweater and the Firestarter's Skirt. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Firestarter's Skirt.name: Firestarter's Skirt
Firestarter's Skirt.tooltip: The Firestarter's set is a vanity set consisting of the Firestarter's Sweater and the Firestarter's Skirt. These items are to be equipped in the Social Slots as they only provide a visual appearance.

Pew-matic Horn.name: Pew-matic Horn
Pew-matic Horn.tooltip: The Pew-matic Horn is a pre-Hardmode gun that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Deerclops. When used, it converts any bullet into a randomized item fired as a projectile. The projectiles travel in an arc and dissipate upon contact with an enemy or block. The projectile's damage varies depending on its appearance. Its best modifier is Unreal.

Weather Pain.name: Weather Pain
Weather Pain.tooltip: The Weather Pain is a pre-Hardmode wand that has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Deerclops. When used, it fires a Hurtnado that dissipates after 9.5 seconds or after hitting 15 enemies. The Hurtnado has 10 armor penetration, bounces off blocks, and homes in on nearby enemies, attempting to hover in front of them to deal continuous damage. Only one Hurtnado can exist at a time. If the Weather Pain is used again while another Hurtnado is already active, the existing Hurtnado dissipates 0.25 seconds after the new one is summoned. Its best modifier is Mythical.

Houndius Shootius.name: Houndius Shootius
Houndius Shootius.tooltip: The Houndius Shootius is a pre-Hardmode summon weapon that summons the Houndius Shootius sentry. It shoots fireballs towards enemies, which dissipate upon contact with enemies or blocks. The Houndius Shootius has a 1/4 (25%) chance of being dropped by Deerclops. Its best modifier is Fabled.

Deer Thing.name: Deer Thing
Deer Thing.tooltip: The Deer Thing is a boss-summoning item that summons Deerclops when used. It can only be used in the Snow or Ice biome, at any time. In addition to being crafted, Deer Things also have a 1/5 (20%) chance of being found in Frozen Chests found in the Ice biome (but not Snow).

The Strongman.name: The Strongman
The Strongman.tooltip: Paintings are decorative furniture items that can be placed on background walls. Each one is a framed image that depicts a particular scene, usually Terraria-related. Their tooltips generally contain a person's name, intended to credit each painting's artist; although the names appear to be fictional, most of them correspond to known Terraria developers, artists, testing staff, and community members (see Trivia below). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions, the Magic Lantern, Spelunker Glowsticks, and Spelunker Flares. There are a total of 193 paintings, 25 of which are sold by the Painter, 7 by the Princess, 4 by the Golfer, 2 by the Zoologist, 2 by the Clothier, 1 by the Truffle, and 27 are randomly sold by the Traveling Merchant. 35 paintings can be found in Underground Cabins, another 14 in the Underground Desert Cabins, 26 in the Dungeon, 12 in The Underworld, 6 from Floating Islands, 5 obtained by fishing, 1 from the Jungle Temple, 5 randomly acquired from Goodie Bags, 8 dropped by Solar Eclipse enemies, 8 awarded randomly by the Angler for completing fishing quests, 1 from the Living Tree, and 4 dropped by enemies.

Fart Kart.name: Fart Kart
Fart Kart.tooltip: Minecarts are mounts that allow players to ride on Minecart Tracks. When the player is near a Minecart Track, pressing the Quick Mount hotkey or pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on a point on the track causes a Minecart to spawn, which the player is automatically placed in. Once inside, the ▶ Right and ◀ Left direction keys either accelerate, decelerate, or reverse the cart's movement. The cart will maintain its current speed and direction if no keys are pressed and no obstacles are reached. The cart can also "jump" with the ↷ Jump key. Weapons and tools, as well as most other items except hooks, can be used while riding a Minecart. The Minecart will deal damage to enemies it collides with and knock them back, with higher potency at higher speeds (see below for details). To exit the Minecart (which causes the Minecart to despawn), the player can use a hook, press the Quick Mount hotkey, or cancel the buff  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Minecart will also despawn if the player jumps off the tracks, lands on blocks, and attempts to move sideways. By default, a Wooden Minecart is spawned for the player. This can be overridden by equipping other Minecart items in the Minecart equipment slot of the player's inventory. The corresponding dye slot allows dyeing the Minecart. Using a Minecart Upgrade Kit will significantly boost the speed of all Minecarts, equip them with a laser that fires at nearby enemies, and increase the player's defense while moving. The boost effect is permanently available after using the item, though it can be toggled on and off through a probe icon next to the Minecart slot.

Hand Of Creation.name: Hand Of Creation
Hand Of Creation.tooltip: The Hand Of Creation is a post-Skeletron construction accessory. It grants the following effects while equipped: +50% placement speed when placing blocks and walls Increased placement range and tool range by 2 tiles vertically and 3 tiles horizontally Automatically applies paint or coating to placed objects +25% mining speed Increased pickup range of items from 2.625 tiles to 12 tiles All Step Stool effects

Neon Moss.name: Neon Moss
Neon Moss.tooltip: Moss is a grass-like plant that grows on Stone Blocks. It comes in 11 different variants. Mossy stone requires one more hit to break than clean stone. Moss will be destroyed if the Stone Block it is on converts to Ebonstone, Crimstone, or Pearlstone. Moss sprouts fuzz that can be cut like wild grass plants. Using a Paint Scraper or Spectre Paint Scraper to harvest moss fuzz has a 1/9 (11.11%) chance of dropping moss as a plantable item. Collected moss can be placed on Stone Blocks and Gray Bricks, or used to craft Mossy Walls. There are 5 types of regular moss: Green Moss, Brown Moss, Red Moss, Blue Moss, and Purple Moss. One of each regular moss can be found throughout each third of a given map (three variants per world). They can be found either randomly on cave surfaces or in moss chambers with a matching Mossy Wall. Glowing mosses are special variants of moss that glow in vibrant colors. These include the Lava Moss, Krypton Moss, Xenon Moss, Argon Moss, Neon Moss, and Helium Moss. Lava Moss can be found in patches around the lava layer of the Caverns. Krypton, Xenon, Argon, and Neon Moss grow in glowing moss biomes and in much larger areas than other mosses, and only one type among these can be found in each world. Up to two (small world) / three (medium world) / four (large world) glowing moss biomes will be generated in the Cavern layer, mostly above the lava layers, but not near the horizontal center of the world. Helium Moss does not spawn naturally and can instead be obtained by throwing any other glowing moss into Shimmer. Mosses that did not naturally spawn in a world can be obtained by putting any glowing moss in an Extractinator, which produces regular mosses, or a Chlorophyte Extractinator, which produces all variants of mosses. Moss Zombies spawned in surface Graveyards can also drop all variants of mosses.

Flymeal.name: Flymeal
Flymeal.tooltip: The Flymeal is a pre-Hardmode broadsword. Like the Classy Cane, it has the special ability to attack town NPCs. Flymeal completely ignores the defense of NPCs, and does 2× damage to them (30 base damage; 4× damage or 60 base damage to the Nurse instead). It also inflicts the Stinky debuff for 5 seconds. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Lilith's Necklace.name: Lilith's Necklace
Lilith's Necklace.tooltip: Lilith's Necklace is a Hardmode transformation mount item that turns the player into a Wolf. Some vanity items are visible when transformed, but certain accessories cannot be used, such as wings. The player can still swing weapons, drink potions, and use items as normal, with unique visual animations for each action. The player's hurt sound is also replaced with a wolf's bark. Lilith's Necklace has a 1/30 (3.33%) / 1/25 (4%) chance of being dropped by Wolves. Newly created Journey Mode characters named Wolfpet or Wolf Pet (case-insensitive) will have Lilith's Necklace equipped in the mount slot.

Resplendent Dessert.name: Resplendent Dessert
Resplendent Dessert.tooltip: The Resplendent Dessert is a Hardmode pet-summoning item that is a combination of the Royal Delight from King Slime and the Regal Delicacy from Queen Slime, allowing the player to summon both the Slime Prince and Slime Princess at the same time.

Stinkbug.name: Stinkbug
Stinkbug.tooltip: The Stinkbug is a harmless critter which spawns on the surface. The Stinkbug has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Stinkbug can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Stinkbug Cage). Once crafted, the Stinkbug cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. The Stinkbug can be used as bait for fishing, with 10% bait power. Stinkbugs can also be used to craft the Flymeal and Stinkbug Blockers.

Stinkbug Cage.name: Stinkbug Cage
Stinkbug Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters. A critter caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item. Gold cages are regular cages containing gold critters. Aside from their higher sell value and rarity, they are the same as regular cages. Placed cages are partially transparent. They can be stacked on top of each other, but no other types of furniture can be placed on a cage. Players can stand on top of cages like platforms, even though they are otherwise background furniture.

Terraformer.name: Terraformer
Terraformer.tooltip: The Terraformer is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord tool. It has the same effects as a Clentaminator but reaches 95 tiles and has a width of 7 tiles and has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance not to consume ammunition, compared to the Clentaminator which reaches 60 tiles and has a width of 5 tiles. The Terraformer can only be obtained by throwing a Clentaminator into Shimmer after the Moon Lord has been defeated. The Terraformer cannot be reforged, and therefore cannot have modifiers.

Venom Dart Trap.name: Venom Dart Trap
Venom Dart Trap.tooltip: The Venom Dart Trap is a Hardmode trap that fires a venomous dart when triggered via wire. It is a direct upgrade to the Dart Trap. It has a cooldown period of 3 1/3 seconds between firings. The darts deal 60 / 120 / 180 damage to players and 30 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters, as well as inflicting Acid Venom for 5 / 10 / 12.5 seconds to players (75/150/187.5 damage) and 5 seconds of Acid Venom to NPCs, enemies, and critters (150 damage). Venom Dart Traps can be rotated 90° with a hammer. Venom Dart Traps do not generate naturally, and can only be obtained via crafting.

Vulkelf Ears.name: Vulkelf Ears
Vulkelf Ears.tooltip: Vulkelf Ears are a vanity item purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 Gold 50 Silver.

Stinkbug Blocker.name: Stinkbug Blocker
Stinkbug Blocker.tooltip: The Stinkbug Blocker and Ghostly Stinkbug Blocker are furniture items. When placed in a valid house, they will prevent NPCs from moving in. The Ghostly Stinkbug Blocker is completely invisible when placed and can only been seen if the player has the Spectre Goggles equipped or if they are near an activated Echo Chamber, similar to Echo Blocks.

Ghostly Stinkbug Blocker.name: Ghostly Stinkbug Blocker
Ghostly Stinkbug Blocker.tooltip: The Stinkbug Blocker and Ghostly Stinkbug Blocker are furniture items. When placed in a valid house, they will prevent NPCs from moving in. The Ghostly Stinkbug Blocker is completely invisible when placed and can only been seen if the player has the Spectre Goggles equipped or if they are near an activated Echo Chamber, similar to Echo Blocks.

Fishing Bobber.name: Fishing Bobber
Fishing Bobber.tooltip: Fishing Bobbers are accessories that change the appearance of a fishing pole's bobber and increase the player's Fishing Power by 10. The Fishing Bobber is acquired as a 1/34 (2.94%) chance reward for completing a fishing quest for the Angler NPC, depending on the number of completed quests and other factors (see Angler § Quest rewards for details), while the rest are crafted. The Angler will not give the player a Fishing Bobber as a reward if they already have one in their inventory, in any of their portable storage items or loadouts. However, if the player has all of Angler's fishing and informational accessories (or their upgrades like the Angler Tackle Bag and Fish Finder) in their inventories, this rule will be ignored.

Glowing Fishing Bobber.name: Glowing Fishing Bobber
Glowing Fishing Bobber.tooltip: Fishing Bobbers are accessories that change the appearance of a fishing pole's bobber and increase the player's Fishing Power by 10. The Fishing Bobber is acquired as a 1/34 (2.94%) chance reward for completing a fishing quest for the Angler NPC, depending on the number of completed quests and other factors (see Angler § Quest rewards for details), while the rest are crafted. The Angler will not give the player a Fishing Bobber as a reward if they already have one in their inventory, in any of their portable storage items or loadouts. However, if the player has all of Angler's fishing and informational accessories (or their upgrades like the Angler Tackle Bag and Fish Finder) in their inventories, this rule will be ignored.

Wand of Frosting.name: Wand of Frosting
Wand of Frosting.tooltip: The Wand of Frosting is a pre-Hardmode wand and the direct upgrade to the Wand of Sparking. When used, it fires a blue spark that travels in a slight curve for about 23 tiles before dissipating. The spark can pierce one enemy and has a 1/2 (50%) chance to inflict the Frostburn debuff for 2 seconds (2/3 (66.67%) chance) or 3 seconds (1/3 (33.33%) chance). The Wand of Frosting also has a base 14% critical strike chance as opposed to the usual 4%. Its best modifier is Demonic or Deadly, with the former granting improved critical strike chance and the latter granting improved speed. It cannot get modifiers that affect knockback or mana cost.

Reef Bathtub.name: Reef Bathtub
Reef Bathtub.tooltip: Bathtubs are furniture items which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 65 / (Old-gen console version) 16 / (3DS version) 11 Bathtub types, all being functionally identical but presenting different appearances.

Reef Bed.name: Reef Bed
Reef Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration. Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 craftable Beds and 5 that can be acquired from the environment. All Beds are functionally identical and differ only in appearance.

Reef Bookcase.name: Reef Bookcase
Reef Bookcase.tooltip: Bookcases are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station used for the crafting of three Hardmode magic weapons (the Crystal Storm, Cursed Flames, and Golden Shower) as well as the Librarian furniture out of Librarian Blocks. Bookcases also fulfill a house's table requirement. There is a total of 65 types of Bookcases: 60 craftable Bookcases, and 5 looted from the environment: one from the Underworld, three from the Dungeon, and one from the Pirate Invasion. Some bookcases can also be found in Underground Cabins; their style follows the theme of the cabin where they are found.

Reef Dresser.name: Reef Dresser
Reef Dresser.tooltip: Dressers are a type of flat-surface furniture (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and storage item. They also fulfill house's table requirement. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 19 / (3DS version) 5 craftable versions, and (Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) 5 noncraftable versions which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Reef Candelabra.name: Reef Candelabra
Reef Candelabra.tooltip: Candelabras are a type of furniture and light source that emits light when placed on a flat surface such as blocks, platforms, and flat furniture items. It is not destroyed by water. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 23 /  12 craftable and 5 looted variations of the Candelabra.

Reef Candle.name: Reef Candle
Reef Candle.tooltip: Candles are a type of furniture and light source. Candles can only be placed on flat-surface items. Candles will produce light underwater if placed and can be toggled on and off with ⚷ Open / Activate and by mechanisms. Certain types of candles provide buffs or debuffs. The Water Candle is a special type of candle found in Dungeons which increases enemy spawn rates by 33% and the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50% when placed or held. The Peace Candle reduces spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%, in contrast to the Water Candle. The Shadow Candle(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns in the area. For Water Candles and Peace Candles, multiple candles cannot stack, even if one is placed and the other is held.

Reef Chair.name: Reef Chair
Reef Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Reef Chandelier.name: Reef Chandelier
Reef Chandelier.tooltip: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers come in many varieties which differ only in appearance and sell value. All chandeliers can be picked up using a pickaxe, drill, or explosives. Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.

Reef Chest.name: Reef Chest
Reef Chest.tooltip: Chests are a type of furniture functioning as storage items. They are accessed using ⚷ Open / Activate and can store up to 40 item stacks in rows of  10×4 /   8×5. In addition to many being craftable, a number of Chests are placed in random locations during world generation. The loot contained in these Chests is determined during world generation, and will not change if the world enters Hardmode. Chests cannot be broken with items inside (the blocks a filled Chest is placed on would also have this trait). However, the Block Swap feature allows the player to change the type of a Chest without having to destroy it. Some types of Chests can be locked by the player using a Chest Lock. When doing so, they will require a key to open again. There are 23 varieties of naturally-occurring Chests (12 of which cannot be crafted), 53 that can only be crafted, and 1 purchasable Chest, for a total of 77 Chest types.

Reef Clock.name: Reef Clock
Reef Clock.tooltip: Grandfather Clocks are furniture items which provide information about the in-game time. If a player is nearby a Grandfather Clock (about 80 tiles horizontally and 50 tiles vertically), the time is displayed on the right side of the screen, underneath the minimap. The time is rounded to the last hour, similar to Tin and Copper Watches, but pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it will show precise time in minutes as a status message on the bottom left corner. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 21 /  5 craftable versions and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 5 / (Old-gen console version) 2 noncraftable (but still lootable) versions. The regular Grandfather Clock can rarely be found in Underground Cabins. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Reef Door.name: Reef Door
Reef Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Reef Lamp.name: Reef Lamp
Reef Lamp.tooltip: Lamps are a type of furniture and light source. They also count as valid house lighting and can be toggled on and off by mechanisms. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 59 types of craftable Lamps, three types that are found in the Dungeon (Green, Blue, or Pink Dungeon Lamp), one found in Underworld houses (Obsidian Lamp), and one that can be dropped during a Pirate Invasion (Golden Lamp). Most lamps are dislodged by liquids, but Obsidian Lamp and Ash Wood Lamp are not dislodged by Lava. The Tiki Torch shares its Tile ID with the rest of these Lamps. Also see Lamp Post ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions) which does not count as valid House lighting.)

Reef Lantern.name: Reef Lantern
Reef Lantern.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Reef Piano.name: Reef Piano
Reef Piano.tooltip: Pianos are a type of furniture which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 15 /  10 craftable Pianos, and 5 non-craftable Pianos that can be found in the Dungeon, Ruined Houses, and Pirate Invasion event. Some Pianos can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin that they are found in.

Reef Platform.name: Reef Platform
Reef Platform.tooltip: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Reef Sink.name: Reef Sink
Reef Sink.tooltip: The Sink is a type of furniture item and crafting station. Like Fountains, it can be used to craft items that require water as a crafting station. There is a total of 66 Sink types, all being functionally identical.

Reef Sofa.name: Reef Sofa
Reef Sofa.tooltip: Sofas are furniture items which fulfill a house's chair requirement. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Players can sit in sofas by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Players can choose to sit on the left, middle, or right positions, and thus up to 3 players can sit on a sofa at a time. Sitting on sofas gives a boost to health regeneration, similar to chairs and beds. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Sofa will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 21 craftable sofas and 5 noncraftable sofas. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Reef Table.name: Reef Table
Reef Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.

Reef Work Bench.name: Reef Work Bench
Reef Work Bench.tooltip: Work Benches are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station required to craft many essential early-game items. They fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 60 types of Work Benches which can be crafted, and 5 types which must be picked up from areas such as the Dungeon. Some Work Benches can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are found in. All types of Work Benches have exactly the same function and only differ in visual appearance.

Trapped Reef Chest.name: Trapped Reef Chest
Trapped Reef Chest.tooltip: A Trapped Chest is a mechanical item that has the appearance of a normal chest. It cannot be used for storage, as it does not have any storage slots. When it is opened, it emits a signal and can be connected with wire. Any chest can be crafted into a Trapped Chest at the Heavy Assembler with the desired chest and 10 wire. The Trapped Chest can be sold for 1 Silver.

Reef Toilet.name: Reef Toilet
Reef Toilet.tooltip: Toilets are furniture items which can be placed on the ground. They are functionally similar to chairs, and fulfill a house's chair requirement. Similarly to chairs, Toilets can be sat on by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Having any tier of Well Fed active while sitting on a Toilet allows the production of Poo. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Toilet will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Toilets act as mechanisms that can be activated via wire, which makes them appear to explosively eject sewage. This effect is purely a novelty visual. Ejected sewage on the ground fades after a few seconds. There are 67 Toilets.

Balloon Bathtub.name: Balloon Bathtub
Balloon Bathtub.tooltip: Bathtubs are furniture items which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 65 / (Old-gen console version) 16 / (3DS version) 11 Bathtub types, all being functionally identical but presenting different appearances.

Balloon Bed.name: Balloon Bed
Balloon Bed.tooltip: Beds are furniture items which allow the player to set a new spawn point by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the foot half of the Bed, if the Bed is placed in a valid bedroom (see details below). On the  Desktop version,  Console version, and  Mobile version, Beds also allow the player to sleep in them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on the head half of the Bed. This makes time pass five times faster and, similar to Chairs and Sofas, gives a boost to health regeneration. Beds fulfill a house's chair requirement. Like most other furniture, the direction a Bed is placed in depends on the direction the player is facing when placing it. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 craftable Beds and 5 that can be acquired from the environment. All Beds are functionally identical and differ only in appearance.

Balloon Bookcase.name: Balloon Bookcase
Balloon Bookcase.tooltip: Bookcases are a type of flat-surface furniture and crafting station used for the crafting of three Hardmode magic weapons (the Crystal Storm, Cursed Flames, and Golden Shower) as well as the Librarian furniture out of Librarian Blocks. Bookcases also fulfill a house's table requirement. There is a total of 65 types of Bookcases: 60 craftable Bookcases, and 5 looted from the environment: one from the Underworld, three from the Dungeon, and one from the Pirate Invasion. Some bookcases can also be found in Underground Cabins; their style follows the theme of the cabin where they are found.

Balloon Dresser.name: Balloon Dresser
Balloon Dresser.tooltip: Dressers are a type of flat-surface furniture (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) and storage item. They also fulfill house's table requirement. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 19 / (3DS version) 5 craftable versions, and (Desktop, Console, Old-gen console and Mobile versions) 5 noncraftable versions which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Balloon Candelabra.name: Balloon Candelabra
Balloon Candelabra.tooltip: Candelabras are a type of furniture and light source that emits light when placed on a flat surface such as blocks, platforms, and flat furniture items. It is not destroyed by water. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 23 /  12 craftable and 5 looted variations of the Candelabra.

Balloon Candle.name: Balloon Candle
Balloon Candle.tooltip: Candles are a type of furniture and light source. Candles can only be placed on flat-surface items. Candles will produce light underwater if placed and can be toggled on and off with ⚷ Open / Activate and by mechanisms. Certain types of candles provide buffs or debuffs. The Water Candle is a special type of candle found in Dungeons which increases enemy spawn rates by 33% and the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 50% when placed or held. The Peace Candle reduces spawn rates by 23% in the area and decreases the maximum number of simultaneous on-screen enemies by 30%, in contrast to the Water Candle. The Shadow Candle(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns in the area. For Water Candles and Peace Candles, multiple candles cannot stack, even if one is placed and the other is held.

Balloon Chair.name: Balloon Chair
Balloon Chair.tooltip: The chair is a type of furniture item that can be placed on top of a solid block or platform. They fulfill a house's chair requirement. Players can sit in chairs by using ⚷ Open / Activate on them and get a boost on health regeneration, similar to beds and sofas. NPCs can sit on chairs too. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any chair will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. Also see Throne, which also fulfills a house's chair requirement. Including the Throne and Bar Stool, there are 67 varieties of chairs.

Balloon Chandelier.name: Balloon Chandelier
Balloon Chandelier.tooltip: Chandeliers are a type of furniture and light source suitable for house lighting requirements that hang from the ceiling. Chandeliers come in many varieties which differ only in appearance and sell value. All chandeliers can be picked up using a pickaxe, drill, or explosives. Chandeliers take up a 3×3 area of tile space and can be turned on and off using mechanisms. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier because of its dimensions.

Balloon Chest.name: Balloon Chest
Balloon Chest.tooltip: Chests are a type of furniture functioning as storage items. They are accessed using ⚷ Open / Activate and can store up to 40 item stacks in rows of  10×4 /   8×5. In addition to many being craftable, a number of Chests are placed in random locations during world generation. The loot contained in these Chests is determined during world generation, and will not change if the world enters Hardmode. Chests cannot be broken with items inside (the blocks a filled Chest is placed on would also have this trait). However, the Block Swap feature allows the player to change the type of a Chest without having to destroy it. Some types of Chests can be locked by the player using a Chest Lock. When doing so, they will require a key to open again. There are 23 varieties of naturally-occurring Chests (12 of which cannot be crafted), 53 that can only be crafted, and 1 purchasable Chest, for a total of 77 Chest types.

Balloon Clock.name: Balloon Clock
Balloon Clock.tooltip: Grandfather Clocks are furniture items which provide information about the in-game time. If a player is nearby a Grandfather Clock (about 80 tiles horizontally and 50 tiles vertically), the time is displayed on the right side of the screen, underneath the minimap. The time is rounded to the last hour, similar to Tin and Copper Watches, but pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on it will show precise time in minutes as a status message on the bottom left corner. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 61 / (Old-gen console version) 21 /  5 craftable versions and (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 5 / (Old-gen console version) 2 noncraftable (but still lootable) versions. The regular Grandfather Clock can rarely be found in Underground Cabins. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Balloon Door.name: Balloon Door
Balloon Door.tooltip: Doors are furniture items that fulfill a house's door requirement. Players can open them by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate on them. Doors can be placed in any space so long as it is exactly three blocks high, with ceiling and floor blocks. Friendly NPCs will also open and close doors during the day as they wander about. Some enemies that follow the Fighter AI can open doors, and Goblin Peons can remove them entirely. See Fighter AI § Opening doors and Tall Gates for details. Doors can also be opened and closed via Wires. If wires are placed on the door's hinge, then the wiring will toggle the door's closed/open state upon activation, but if wires are placed on the side tiles, where the door opens, then the wiring will only close the door. The Lihzahrd Door occurs naturally at the entrance to the Jungle Temple and initially requires a Temple Key to open. Once unlocked, it can be freed with a pickaxe or drill, and placed again by the player like any other door. Lihzahrd Doors can also be crafted, but their crafting station can only be obtained after opening the initial door, and the ingredients require the Picksaw (or better) to mine, which is dropped by Golem. A locked Lihzahrd Door automatically completely prevents itself and the 2 blocks above and below it from breaking by any method. Apart from the standard doors listed here, there also exist Trap Doors and Tall Gates, which behave similarly. Every block in the game can also be used like a (Switch-toggled) door via Actuators. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 62 / (Old-gen console version) 22 /  19 craftable and 6 noncraftable types of doors which must be looted from various locations in the world.

Balloon Lamp.name: Balloon Lamp
Balloon Lamp.tooltip: Lamps are a type of furniture and light source. They also count as valid house lighting and can be toggled on and off by mechanisms. There are (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 59 types of craftable Lamps, three types that are found in the Dungeon (Green, Blue, or Pink Dungeon Lamp), one found in Underworld houses (Obsidian Lamp), and one that can be dropped during a Pirate Invasion (Golden Lamp). Most lamps are dislodged by liquids, but Obsidian Lamp and Ash Wood Lamp are not dislodged by Lava. The Tiki Torch shares its Tile ID with the rest of these Lamps. Also see Lamp Post ((Old-gen console and 3DS versions) which does not count as valid House lighting.)

Balloon Lantern.name: Balloon Lantern
Balloon Lantern.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Balloon Piano.name: Balloon Piano
Balloon Piano.tooltip: Pianos are a type of furniture which fulfills a house's table requirement. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 15 /  10 craftable Pianos, and 5 non-craftable Pianos that can be found in the Dungeon, Ruined Houses, and Pirate Invasion event. Some Pianos can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin that they are found in.

Balloon Platform.name: Balloon Platform
Balloon Platform.tooltip: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Balloon Sink.name: Balloon Sink
Balloon Sink.tooltip: The Sink is a type of furniture item and crafting station. Like Fountains, it can be used to craft items that require water as a crafting station. There is a total of 66 Sink types, all being functionally identical.

Balloon Sofa.name: Balloon Sofa
Balloon Sofa.tooltip: Sofas are furniture items which fulfill a house's chair requirement. (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Players can sit in sofas by pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button on them. Players can choose to sit on the left, middle, or right positions, and thus up to 3 players can sit on a sofa at a time. Sitting on sofas gives a boost to health regeneration, similar to chairs and beds. As with all furniture that can be sat on, sitting on any Sofa will increase the player's Fishing Power by 5. There is a total of (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) 60 / (Old-gen console version) 21 craftable sofas and 5 noncraftable sofas. All are functionally identical, and differ only in their appearance.

Balloon Table.name: Balloon Table
Balloon Table.tooltip: Tables are a type of furniture which can be placed on the ground, commonly used in conjunction with chairs. All variants fulfill a house's table requirement. There are 64 craftable tables and 5 noncraftable tables. Some tables can also be found in Underground Cabins, in which they follow the theme of the cabin they are in.
