Biome Sight Potion.name: Biome Sight Potion
Biome Sight Potion.tooltip: The Biome Sight Potion is a buff potion which grants the Biome Sight buff when consumed. The buff highlights all tiles that are infected with The Corruption, The Crimson, or The Hallow in purple, red, and pink respectively, while in the dark. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon ().

Scarlet Macaw.name: Scarlet Macaw
Scarlet Macaw.tooltip: The Scarlet Macaw and Blue Macaw are critters that spawn in the Jungle during the daytime. They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Mahogany tree during the day. They may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details. Macaws have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. Macaws can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Scarlet / Blue Macaw Cage). Once crafted, the Macaws cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. Macaws can be spawned by the Macaw Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.

Scarlet Macaw Cage.name: Scarlet Macaw Cage
Scarlet Macaw Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters. A critter caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item. Gold cages are regular cages containing gold critters. Aside from their higher sell value and rarity, they are the same as regular cages. Placed cages are partially transparent. They can be stacked on top of each other, but no other types of furniture can be placed on a cage. Players can stand on top of cages like platforms, even though they are otherwise background furniture.

Ash Grass Seeds.name: Ash Grass Seeds
Ash Grass Seeds.tooltip: Ash Grass Seeds are seeds used to plant Ash grass. They are purchased from the Dryad for 1 Silver 50 Copper each, when she is talked to in The Underworld. They can also be gathered by clearing Ash grass foliage in the Underworld. Ash trees can grow on planted Ash grass. Ash grass, Ash trees, and the plants that grow on the grass, emit faint light.

Ash Wood.name: Ash Wood
Ash Wood.tooltip: Ash Wood is a type of wood harvested from Ash trees found naturally growing in Ash forests. Ash trees can be cultivated by placing Acorns on top of Ash grass at any height.

Ash Wood Wall.name: Ash Wood Wall
Ash Wood Wall.tooltip: Ash Wood Wall is a type of background wall crafted using Ash Wood.

Ash Wood Fence.name: Ash Wood Fence
Ash Wood Fence.tooltip: Fences are a type of safe wall that are visually thin with most of them having transparency to allow view of the background. The only fences that have no transparency to them are Palm Fence, Rich Mahogany Fence, and Shadewood Fence. Unlike most other safe walls, they allow for wild plants and trees to grow. The safe Grass Wall, Flower Wall, and Jungle Wall are functionally identical to fences. All fences are obtained by crafting, and the Wrought Iron Fence can also be found on certain designs of the Dungeon.

Outcast.name: Outcast
Outcast.tooltip: Paintings are decorative furniture items that can be placed on background walls. Each one is a framed image that depicts a particular scene, usually Terraria-related. Their tooltips generally contain a person's name, intended to credit each painting's artist; although the names appear to be fictional, most of them correspond to known Terraria developers, artists, testing staff, and community members (see Trivia below). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions, the Magic Lantern, Spelunker Glowsticks, and Spelunker Flares. There are a total of 193 paintings, 25 of which are sold by the Painter, 7 by the Princess, 4 by the Golfer, 2 by the Zoologist, 2 by the Clothier, 1 by the Truffle, and 27 are randomly sold by the Traveling Merchant. 35 paintings can be found in Underground Cabins, another 14 in the Underground Desert Cabins, 26 in the Dungeon, 12 in The Underworld, 6 from Floating Islands, 5 obtained by fishing, 1 from the Jungle Temple, 5 randomly acquired from Goodie Bags, 8 dropped by Solar Eclipse enemies, 8 awarded randomly by the Angler for completing fishing quests, 1 from the Living Tree, and 4 dropped by enemies.

Constellation.name: Constellation
Constellation.tooltip: The Constellation is a Hardmode, post-Lunatic Cultist whip. It has a 10% multihit penalty and performs the following effects on hit: 15 tag damage 15% tag critical strike chance Marks enemies with cosmic energy. When a minion or sentry strikes an enemy marked by the Constellation, the cosmic energy fully grows. The next time Constellation hits an enemy marked with grown cosmic energy, it releases 6 non-piercing Shooting Stars that home in on enemies after a short delay, each dealing 39.6% of the whip's damage (51 base damage) and 100% of its knockback, and the cosmic energy is reset to its non-grown state. The Shooting Stars also apply the Constellation's cosmic energy, tag damage, tag critical strike chance to enemies they hit like the whip itself, but cannot trigger the effect of grown cosmic energy and cause more Shooting Stars to spawn. All enemies hit by a swing will be marked by cosmic energy, but effect of cosmic energy can be triggered only once per swing. Uniquely among whips, the Constellation's tag effect lasts for 8 seconds instead of the usual 4 seconds. Its best modifier is Legendary.

(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions, the Magic Lantern, Spelunker Glowsticks, and Spelunker Flares. There are a total of 193 paintings, 25 of which are sold by the Painter, 7 by the Princess, 4 by the Golfer, 2 by the Zoologist, 2 by the Clothier, 1 by the Truffle, and 27 are randomly sold by the Traveling Merchant. 35 paintings can be found in Underground Cabins, another 14 in the Underground Desert Cabins, 26 in the Dungeon, 12 in The Underworld, 6 from Floating Islands, 5 obtained by fishing, 1 from the Jungle Temple, 5 randomly acquired from Goodie Bags, 8 dropped by Solar Eclipse enemies, 8 awarded randomly by the Angler for completing fishing quests, 1 from the Living Tree, and 4 dropped by enemies.

Joja Cola.name: Joja Cola
Joja Cola.tooltip: The Joja Cola is a food item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 2 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). It has a 1/8 (12.5%) chance of being fished up instead of a junk item when fishing. When talking to the Dryad and holding a Joja Cola, the Dryad's “Status” option will be replaced by “Purify”. Upon selecting this option, the Dryad will summon a star-shaped portal with a Junimo pet jumping out of it after a brief delay. The pet will pull a Stardrop from the ground and then vanish, dropping the item for the player to collect. This process can be repeated an unlimited number of times.

Stardrop.name: Stardrop
Stardrop.tooltip: The Stardrop is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Junimo that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, the Junimo twirls the leaf on its head like a propeller to fly after them. The Stardrop can be obtained by holding a Joja Cola, talking to the Dryad, and selecting her “Purify” option. After a short animation sequence, the Stardrop is dropped on the ground.

Spicy Pepper.name: Spicy Pepper
Spicy Pepper.tooltip: The Spicy Pepper is a food and fruit item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). It has a small chance of dropping when shaking an Ash tree.

Pomegranate.name: Pomegranate
Pomegranate.tooltip: The Pomegranate is a food and fruit item that grants the Well Fed buff when consumed. This lasts for 5 minutes, but can be canceled at any time  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). It has a small chance of dropping when shaking an Ash tree.

Ash Wood Helmet.name: Ash Wood Helmet
Ash Wood Helmet.tooltip: Ash Wood armor is a pre-Hardmode armor set consisting of the Ash Wood Helmet, Ash Wood Breastplate, and Ash Wood Greaves. Crafting the full set requires a total of 75 Ash Wood. The full set grants the following effects while equipped: +7 defense Reduces the contact damage of lava from 80 to 40. Halves the duration of the On Fire! debuff from contact with lava from 7 / 14 / 17.5 seconds to 3.5 / 7 / 8.75 seconds. Additionally, equipping both Ash Wood armor and the Obsidian Rose (or its upgrades) provides immunity to lava damage and the debuff.

Ash Wood Bow.name: Ash Wood Bow
Ash Wood Bow.tooltip: The Ash Wood Bow is a pre-Hardmode bow and a variation of the Wooden Bow. Its best modifier is Demonic, as it does not have any knockback and thus cannot get modifiers that affect it.

Ash Wood Hammer.name: Ash Wood Hammer
Ash Wood Hammer.tooltip: The Ash Wood Hammer is a pre-Hardmode hammer. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Ash Wood Sword.name: Ash Wood Sword
Ash Wood Sword.tooltip: The Ash Wood Sword is a pre-Hardmode broadsword and a variation of the Wooden Sword. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Moon Globe.name: Moon Globe
Moon Globe.tooltip: The Moon Globe is a thrown consumable item purchased from the Zoologist for 3 Gold after the Bestiary is 50% complete (273 entries). When a Moon Globe is thrown and shatters on a surface, the world's moon style will be randomized to one of 9 options.

Repaired Life Crystal.name: Repaired Life Crystal
Repaired Life Crystal.tooltip: The Repaired Life Crystal is a furniture item that places down a decorative Life Crystal. It drops a Life Crystal when destroyed.

Repaired Mana Crystal.name: Repaired Mana Crystal
Repaired Mana Crystal.tooltip: The Repaired Mana Crystal is a furniture item that places down a decorative Mana Crystal. It drops a Mana Crystal when destroyed.

Terra Fart Kart.name: Terra Fart Kart
Terra Fart Kart.tooltip: Minecarts are mounts that allow players to ride on Minecart Tracks. When the player is near a Minecart Track, pressing the Quick Mount hotkey or pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate key on a point on the track causes a Minecart to spawn, which the player is automatically placed in. Once inside, the ▶ Right and ◀ Left direction keys either accelerate, decelerate, or reverse the cart's movement. The cart will maintain its current speed and direction if no keys are pressed and no obstacles are reached. The cart can also "jump" with the ↷ Jump key. Weapons and tools, as well as most other items except hooks, can be used while riding a Minecart. The Minecart will deal damage to enemies it collides with and knock them back, with higher potency at higher speeds (see below for details). To exit the Minecart (which causes the Minecart to despawn), the player can use a hook, press the Quick Mount hotkey, or cancel the buff  by right-clicking the icon (),  by selecting the icon using Cycle Next/Previous Buff and then pressing Remove Buff (), or  by double-tapping the buff icon (). The Minecart will also despawn if the player jumps off the tracks, lands on blocks, and attempts to move sideways. By default, a Wooden Minecart is spawned for the player. This can be overridden by equipping other Minecart items in the Minecart equipment slot of the player's inventory. The corresponding dye slot allows dyeing the Minecart. Using a Minecart Upgrade Kit will significantly boost the speed of all Minecarts, equip them with a laser that fires at nearby enemies, and increase the player's defense while moving. The boost effect is permanently available after using the item, though it can be toggled on and off through a probe icon next to the Minecart slot.

Minecart Upgrade Kit.name: Minecart Upgrade Kit
Minecart Upgrade Kit.tooltip: The Minecart Upgrade Kit is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses permanent booster item that permanently unlocks a boost for all Minecarts, including a speed increase, extra defense when moving, and a laser attack. It also drops a Mechanical Cart when used. The Minecart Upgrade Kit can only be obtained by combining the Mechanical Wheel Piece, Wagon Piece, and Battery Piece, which are dropped from the Treasure Bags of the mechanical bosses in Expert Mode. The Minecart boost can be toggled via a toggle on the Minecart slot in the equipment menu.

Jim's Cap.name: Jim's Cap
Jim's Cap.tooltip: Jim's Cap is an vanity item. It will always drop from the Painter, but only when his name is Jim.

Echo Wall.name: Echo Wall
Echo Wall.tooltip: The Echo Wall is a type of background wall made from Echo Blocks. It appears completely invisible once placed and cannot be seen by the player unless they have the Spectre Goggles equipped or are near an Echo Chamber. Like other walls, it stops enemies from spawning when it is placed and can be used for houses.

Echo Platform.name: Echo Platform
Echo Platform.tooltip: Platforms are special types of blocks that allow movement through the space they occupy. The player normally stands and walks on platforms as if they were ordinary blocks, and they can move down through a platform by pressing the ▼ Down key while standing on one. Players can also walk or jump horizontally through the space occupied by platforms, only treating the platform as "solid" when landing on them from above. Platforms fulfill a house's door requirement.

Mushroom Torch.name: Mushroom Torch
Mushroom Torch.tooltip: Torches are furniture items that function as light sources when placed, held, or dropped (via the Throw button). Regular Torches can be found randomly in Chests and Pots, as a bonus drop from slimes, Torch Zombies, or purchased from the Merchant or Skeleton Merchant for 50 Copper each. Placing at least 101 Torches in close proximity below the surface layer in any biome will start the Torch God mini-event. Completing the event will grant the Torch God's Favor, which allows the player to automatically convert ordinary Torches to one of the biome types.

Hive-Five.name: Hive-Five
Hive-Five.tooltip: The Hive-Five is a pre-Hardmode yoyo. Upon enemy hits, it has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance of summoning a homing Bee projectile. The Bee projectile deals 50% of the weapon's damage (12 base damage), has a 1/2 (50%) chance to deal 1 extra damage, can pierce enemies or bounce off blocks up to 3 times, and lasts for 10 seconds.  Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Axe of Regrowth.name: Axe of Regrowth
Axe of Regrowth.tooltip: The Axe of Regrowth is a pre-Hardmode axe crafted from the Staff of Regrowth. It retains the same functions and additionally replants felled trees that can grow from Acorns without requiring or consuming Acorns from the player's inventory. Its best modifier is Light for harvesting purposes and Legendary for combat purposes.

Chlorophyte Extractinator.name: Chlorophyte Extractinator
Chlorophyte Extractinator.tooltip: The Chlorophyte Extractinator is a Hardmode, post-mechanical bosses crafting station and the upgrade to the Extractinator. It has the following upgraded functions: It converts items 3.33× as fast (every 3 ticks). In Hardmode, it converts Silt, Slush, and Desert Fossils into early Hardmode ores (those that can generate from destroying altars). Existing conversions and rates are unchanged. If it is obtained in pre-Hardmode (whether via bringing it from a different world or on I am error worlds), it will not return Hardmode ores. It converts Glowing Mosses into any kind of moss (except Helium Moss), instead of only regular ones. It converts the Corruption, Crimson, and Hallow variants of most blocks into their normal variants. It converts ores and bars into their alternate ore types (such as Copper into Tin). It converts Dungeon Bricks into their variants. In worlds with the I am error secret world seed enabled, it can also be found naturally in Underground Desert Cabins.

Blue Chicken Egg.name: Blue Chicken Egg
Blue Chicken Egg.tooltip: The Blue Chicken Egg is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Blue Chicken that follows the player. The Blue Chicken Egg can be purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 25 Gold.

Trimarang.name: Trimarang
Trimarang.tooltip: The Trimarang is a pre-Hardmode boomerang crafted using three different boomerangs. Unlike most boomerangs, it does not have to return to the player before being fired, with a maximum of three Trimarangs that can be thrown out at one time. Its best modifier is Godly or Demonic. Both modifiers increase the average damage output by the same amount.

Mushroom Campfire.name: Mushroom Campfire
Mushroom Campfire.tooltip: Campfires are a type of furniture and crafting station that emit light and grant the Cozy Fire buff to players in their vicinity, which provides 10% increased innate health regeneration and additionally grants 0.5 HP/s constant regeneration. The buff is applied to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the campfire, similar to Heart Lanterns and Sunflowers. Campfires are also minor crafting stations, and uniquely, campfires are used to cook Marshmallow on a Stick (see their page for details). Campfires can be toggled off and on with ⚷ Open / Activate, which extinguishes the flame, light, and disables the Cozy Fire buff. They can also be extinguished and lit with the Water Gun and Slime Gun respectively, and as mechanisms, they can be toggled with wire. Campfires are extinguished by rain in The Constant special world seed.

Blue Macaw.name: Blue Macaw
Blue Macaw.tooltip: The Scarlet Macaw and Blue Macaw are critters that spawn in the Jungle during the daytime. They also have a small chance of spawning upon shaking a Mahogany tree during the day. They may turn hostile to players with negative luck; see hostile critter for details. Macaws have only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. Macaws can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Scarlet / Blue Macaw Cage). Once crafted, the Macaws cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer. Macaws can be spawned by the Macaw Statue, however statue-spawned critters cannot be caught with any Bug Net, and will disappear in a puff of smoke when the player attempts to do so.

Blue Macaw Cage.name: Blue Macaw Cage
Blue Macaw Cage.tooltip: Cages are placeable decorative furniture items that display animated critters. A critter caught with the Bug Net, Lavaproof Bug Net, or Golden Bug Net is combined with a Terrarium to craft a cage. By throwing a cage into Shimmer, it can be converted back into its ingredients, gaining back the caged critter as an item. Gold cages are regular cages containing gold critters. Aside from their higher sell value and rarity, they are the same as regular cages. Placed cages are partially transparent. They can be stacked on top of each other, but no other types of furniture can be placed on a cage. Players can stand on top of cages like platforms, even though they are otherwise background furniture.

Bottomless Honey Bucket.name: Bottomless Honey Bucket
Bottomless Honey Bucket.tooltip: Bottomless Buckets are tools that are capable of placing an infinite amount of liquids by pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button. There are four different types of Bottomless Buckets, one for each type of liquid: Bottomless Water Bucket, Bottomless Lava Bucket, Bottomless Honey Bucket, and Bottomless Shimmer Bucket. Bottomless Buckets can be used limitlessly and are never depleted. They are also slightly faster at placing liquids when compared to standard buckets (especially when moving the cursor around while placing).

Honey Absorbant Sponge.name: Honey Absorbant Sponge
Honey Absorbant Sponge.tooltip: Sponges are tools used to erase liquids by pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button on them. This causes the liquid to disappear from the environment without storing it. There are four different types of sponges: Super Absorbant Sponge for absorbing water and Shimmer Lava Absorbant Sponge for absorbing lava Honey Absorbant Sponge for absorbing honey Ultra Absorbant Sponge for absorbing all kinds of liquid Attempting to use a sponge on a different type of liquid has no effect. Sponges can be used limitlessly and are never depleted. They are also slightly faster at draining liquids when compared to using a standard Empty Bucket (especially when moving the cursor around while draining).

Ultra Absorbant Sponge.name: Ultra Absorbant Sponge
Ultra Absorbant Sponge.tooltip: Sponges are tools used to erase liquids by pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button on them. This causes the liquid to disappear from the environment without storing it. Goblorc Ears.name: Goblorc Ears
Goblorc Ears.tooltip: The Goblorc Ears are a vanity item purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 2 Gold 50 Silver.

Reef Block.name: Reef Block
Reef Block.tooltip: Reef Blocks are a type of decorative block. They can be used to craft Reef furniture.

Reef Wall.name: Reef Wall
Reef Wall.tooltip: Reef Walls are a type of background wall. They are crafted with Reef Blocks at a Work Bench.

Guide to Environmental Preservation.tooltip: The Guide to Environmental Preservation is a pre-Hardmode tool that prevents the player's attacks from breaking plants while inside their inventory or opened Void Bag. It can be purchased from the Dryad for 5 Gold. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Guide to Environmental Preservation in the player's inventory or hotbar will toggle it between the Guide to Environmental Preservation and the Guide to Environmental Preservation (Inactive), disabling its functions.

Macaw Statue.name: Macaw Statue
Macaw Statue.tooltip: Statues are furniture items. While some are purely decorative, others have a functional effect when activated via Wire—depending on the statue, it may spawn enemies, drop items, or teleport an NPC to the statue's location. Most statues can be found already placed in any area underground (most frequently in the Dungeon, Underground Cabins, and Cavern level), though Angel Statues also appear in Chests. Like all furniture, a pickaxe, a drill, or explosives are used to collect them. There are a total of 117 different statues: 25 decoration statues, 36 text and numerical statues, and 56 functional mechanisms.

While some are purely decorative, others have a functional effect when activated via Wire—depending on the statue, it may spawn enemies, drop items, or teleport an NPC to the statue's location. Most statues can be found already placed in any area underground (most frequently in the Dungeon, Underground Cabins, and Cavern level), though Angel Statues also appear in Chests. Like all furniture, a pickaxe, a drill, or explosives are used to collect them. There are a total of 117 different statues: 25 decoration statues, 36 text and numerical statues, and 56 functional mechanisms.

Decorative Healing Potion.name: Decorative Healing Potion
Decorative Healing Potion.tooltip: The Decorative Healing Potion is a furniture item and crafting station that can only be placed on flat-surface items. It generates naturally on Dungeon shelves, and drops a Lesser Healing Potion when mined. It shares recipes with Placed Bottles. Its thematic counterpart is the Decorative Mana Potion.

Decorative Mana Potion.name: Decorative Mana Potion
Decorative Mana Potion.tooltip: The Decorative Mana Potion is a furniture item and crafting station that can only be placed on flat-surface items. It generates naturally on Dungeon shelves, and drops a Lesser Mana Potion when mined. It shares recipes with Placed Bottles. Its thematic counterpart is the Decorative Healing Potion.

Shadow Candle.name: Shadow Candle
Shadow Candle.tooltip: The Shadow Candle is a  furniture item that emits a low amount of light, and can be placed only on flat-surface items. While placed nearby or while held, it grants Shadow Candle debuff to the player. The Shadow Candle debuff nullifies the enemy spawn reduction benefits of towns. The debuff is applied to any players holding or standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on a Shadow Candle. In order to be considered "holding" the candle, it must be in the player's hotbar and currently selected; merely being in a player's inventory will not suffice. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on a placed Shadow Candle will turn it off. Shadow Candles that are turned off will not activate the Shadow Candle debuff.

Guide to Peaceful Coexistence.name: Guide to Peaceful Coexistence
Guide to Peaceful Coexistence.tooltip: The Guide to Peaceful Coexistence is a pre-Hardmode tool that combines the effects of the Guide to Critter Companionship and the Guide to Environmental Preservation, preventing player attacks from harming critters and breaking plants when placed within the player's inventory or opened Void Bag. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Guide to Peaceful Coexistence in the player's inventory or hotbar will toggle it between the Guide to Peaceful Coexistence and the Guide to Peaceful Coexistence (Inactive), disabling its functions.

Rubblemaker (Small).name: Rubblemaker (Small)
Rubblemaker (Small).tooltip: The Rubblemaker is a tool used to place ambient objects ("rubble") using items from the player's inventory. It is sold by the Goblin Tinkerer for 25 Gold.  The Rubblemaker can use various blocks to place down decorative backgrounds from different biomes. These background objects drop the block used to place them when destroyed. By pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button, the Rubblemaker can toggle between three placement sizes: Small, Medium, and Large. The Small setting corresponds to one tile-wide rubble, the Medium setting to two tile-wide rubble, and the Large setting to three tile-wide rubble. Rubble within each setting can be cycled through using the ▲ Up and ▼ Down buttons. The material which is highest and furthest to the left in the player's inventory will be prioritized, and only that material's rubble will be placeable until another supersedes it.

Closed Void Bag.name: Closed Void Bag
Closed Void Bag.tooltip: The Void Bag is a portable storage item that grants the player access to the Void Vault anywhere. When used, it will summon a temporary portal which lasts for 3 minutes, and pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the portal opens the player's Void Vault inventory. The Void Bag is never consumed and can be used limitlessly. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Void Bag item in the inventory turns it into the Closed Void Bag. Pressing the button again opens the Void Bag again. When opened, the Void Vault storage will effectively act as the player's secondary inventory, which automatically stores items collected after the player's main inventory is full, indicated by a purple mask on the pickup text. Additionally, it also allows the player to interact with the items inside it as if they were in the main inventory without opening the Void Vault storage interface. When closed, the Void Bag functions similarly to the Money Trough / Eye Bone, only acting as a regular portable storage item. This will prevent it from picking up items when the player has a full inventory, and it loses the function of the secondary inventory.

Artisan Loaf.name: Artisan Loaf
Artisan Loaf.tooltip: The Artisan Loaf is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the range that the player can access crafting stations by 4 tiles in all directions. The Artisan Loaf can be purchased from the Skeleton Merchant for 10 Gold during a Waning Crescent, New Moon, or Waxing Crescent. It can also only be used once per player, and the Skeleton Merchant will cease to sell it once the player has consumed an Artisan Loaf.

TNT Barrel.name: TNT Barrel
TNT Barrel.tooltip: The TNT Barrel is a trap which explodes immediately when destroyed, or hit by virtually any weapon or tool. The explosion does not destroy any tiles, deals 400 base damage to players (200 base damage to non-player entities), and inflicts a knockback of 10 (Extremely strong) to all entities within a 16.25×16.25-tile area. The TNT Barrel is not a mechanism and cannot be triggered directly by Wire. TNT Barrels can naturally generate (and generate in particularly large numbers in the Jungle Temple) when the No Traps special seed is active.

Chest Lock.name: Chest Lock
Chest Lock.tooltip: The Chest Lock is a consumable item. Pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button on certain types of Chests when holding it will turn the Chest into a locked Chest and consume the Chest Lock. The content of the Chest will not be affected by the conversion. Chests locked by this way work the same as the naturally generated locked Chests, requiring another respective key to unlock.

Rubblemaker (Medium).name: Rubblemaker (Medium)
Rubblemaker (Medium).tooltip: The Rubblemaker is a tool used to place ambient objects ("rubble") using items from the player's inventory. It is sold by the Goblin Tinkerer for 25 Gold.  The Rubblemaker can use various blocks to place down decorative backgrounds from different biomes. These background objects drop the block used to place them when destroyed. By pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button, the Rubblemaker can toggle between three placement sizes: Small, Medium, and Large. The Small setting corresponds to one tile-wide rubble, the Medium setting to two tile-wide rubble, and the Large setting to three tile-wide rubble. Rubble within each setting can be cycled through using the ▲ Up and ▼ Down buttons. The material which is highest and furthest to the left in the player's inventory will be prioritized, and only that material's rubble will be placeable until another supersedes it.

Rubblemaker (Large).name: Rubblemaker (Large)
Rubblemaker (Large).tooltip: The Rubblemaker is a tool used to place ambient objects ("rubble") using items from the player's inventory. It is sold by the Goblin Tinkerer for 25 Gold.  The Rubblemaker can use various blocks to place down decorative backgrounds from different biomes. These background objects drop the block used to place them when destroyed. By pressing the ⚷ Open / Activate button, the Rubblemaker can toggle between three placement sizes: Small, Medium, and Large. The Small setting corresponds to one tile-wide rubble, the Medium setting to two tile-wide rubble, and the Large setting to three tile-wide rubble. Rubble within each setting can be cycled through using the ▲ Up and ▼ Down buttons. The material which is highest and furthest to the left in the player's inventory will be prioritized, and only that material's rubble will be placeable until another supersedes it.

Bundle of Horseshoe Balloons.name: Bundle of Horseshoe Balloons
Bundle of Horseshoe Balloons.tooltip: The Bundle of Horseshoe Balloons is an accessory which combines the functionalities of the Bundle of Balloons and the Lucky Horseshoe. When equipped, it allows the wearer to perform a quadruple jump, as well as increasing the player's jump duration by 33%, jump speed by 30%, and luck by 0.05. Each of the jumps has an effect from the different combined items: sandstorm jump, then blizzard jump, then cloud jump. Having it equipped also prevents the player from taking fall damage.

Spiffo Plush.name: Spiffo Plush
Spiffo Plush.tooltip: The Spiffo Plush is a pet-summoning item that spawns Spiffo to follow the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, Spiffo twirls its tail like a propeller to fly towards them. The Spiffo Plush has a 1/1500 (0.07%) chance of being dropped by Zombies, Frozen Zombies, and Raincoat Zombies.

Glow Tulip.name: Glow Tulip
Glow Tulip.tooltip: The Glow Tulip is a pet-summoning item that spawns a Caveling Gardener that follows the player. When the player is far enough away or in midair, it flies through solid tiles while holding onto a Snare Plant in order to catch up to them. The Glow Tulip can be found rarely near the left and right edges of the world below the Surface as a plant. Depending on world size, a set amount of Glow Tulips will spawn during world generation: 2 in small worlds, 4 in medium worlds, and 6 in large worlds. Half of them are usually generated on the left side and the other half on the right side of the world. It can also be detected by the Metal Detector.

Ocram's Razor.name: Ocram's Razor
Ocram's Razor.tooltip: Ocram's Razor is a Hardmode boss-summoning item that summons Mechdusa when used. It can only be used in worlds that combine the For the Worthy and Remix seeds. It is crafted with the Mechanical Eye, Mechanical Worm, and Mechanical Skull and can be used in any biome, at any time. This item has no function when brought to other worlds, and its tooltip will display 'It has no effect in this world' instead.

Rod of Harmony.name: Rod of Harmony
Rod of Harmony.tooltip: The Rod of Harmony is a Hardmode, post-Moon Lord tool. It is the direct upgrade to the Rod of Discord, instantly teleporting the player to the location of the cursor when used, but without inflicting the Chaos State debuff. It is obtained by throwing the Rod of Discord into Shimmer after the Moon Lord has been defeated.

Advanced Combat Techniques: Volume Two.name: Advanced Combat Techniques: Volume Two
Advanced Combat Techniques: Volume Two.tooltip: Advanced Combat Techniques: Volume Two is a Hardmode permanent booster item that permanently increases the defense of Town NPCs by 8, their attack damage by 25%, their attack speed by 20%, and their health by 250, similar to the increases after each type of boss is defeated. It can only be consumed once per world and is obtained by throwing a Spell Tome into Shimmer. When used, the status message "The book's knowledge empowers your villagers!" is displayed.

Vital Crystal.name: Vital Crystal
Vital Crystal.tooltip: The Vital Crystal is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the player's health regeneration. It can only be used once per player and is obtained by throwing a Life Crystal into Shimmer.

Aegis Fruit.name: Aegis Fruit
Aegis Fruit.tooltip: The Aegis Fruit is a Hardmode, post-one mechanical boss permanent booster item that permanently increases the player's defense by 4. It can only be used once per player and is obtained by throwing a Life Fruit into Shimmer.

Arcane Crystal.name: Arcane Crystal
Arcane Crystal.tooltip: The Arcane Crystal is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the player's mana regeneration by 1/50 (2%) of their maximum mana. It can only be used once per player and is obtained by throwing a Mana Crystal into Shimmer. See Mana § Restoring mana for details about mana regeneration.

Galaxy Pearl.name: Galaxy Pearl
Galaxy Pearl.tooltip: The Galaxy Pearl is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the player's luck by 0.03. It can only be used once per player and is obtained by throwing a Pink Pearl into Shimmer.

Gummy Worm.name: Gummy Worm
Gummy Worm.tooltip: The Gummy Worm is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the player's Fishing Power by 3. It can only be used once per player and is obtained when a Gold Worm comes into contact with Shimmer, either as a critter or in dropped item form.

Ambrosia.name: Ambrosia
Ambrosia.tooltip: Ambrosia is a permanent booster item that permanently grants the following effects: +5% mining speed +5% placement speed when placing blocks and walls It can only be used once per player and is obtained by throwing any type of fruit into Shimmer.

Peddler's Satchel.name: Peddler's Satchel
Peddler's Satchel.tooltip: The Peddler's Satchel is a permanent booster item that permanently increases the number of items sold by the Traveling Merchant by 1. It can only be used once in the world and is obtained by throwing a Peddler's Hat into Shimmer. Consuming the item displays the status message "The Traveling Merchant's satchel deepens!".

Echo Coating.name: Echo Coating
Echo Coating.tooltip: Paint is used to modify the color of objects. Nearly anything can be painted, including blocks, background walls, and furniture, along with non-collectable environment objects like trees, tall grass, flowers, and other ambient growth. Basic paint is purchased from the Painter NPC. Two of the same color can be combined at a Dye Vat to create "deep" color versions, which apply their color more vividly and are required in order to paint certain objects. Coating(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is used to apply a special effect over a block and can be applied in tandem with paint and other coatings. It is purchased from the Painter NPC. Paint and coatings are applied to blocks and furniture with the Paintbrush, and to walls with the Paint Roller, with each tile consuming one item of paint/coating. The Paint Sprayer will automatically paint items when placing them. Paint and coatings can be removed with the Paint Scraper, although they will never be retrieved upon doing so. Destroying a painted block will not drop the paint item either. Paint can be placed in ammo slots. If more than one type of paint or coating is present in the player's inventory, the paint or coating in the earliest inventory slot is used first (starting from the top-left slot).

Echo Chamber.name: Echo Chamber
Echo Chamber.tooltip: The Echo Chamber is a furniture item. It can be activated and deactivated similarly to a monolith. When active, it grants the ability to see Echo Blocks, Echo Platforms, Echo Walls, Ghostly Stinkbug Blockers, and tiles painted with Echo Coating. It can also be equipped as a vanity accessory, which enables its effect globally for the player, similar to the Radio Thing.

Gas Trap.name: Gas Trap
Gas Trap.tooltip: The Gas Trap is a trap item obtained by throwing a Whoopie Cushion into Shimmer. It also has a 1/15 (6.67%) chance to appear in any chest when the No Traps special seed is active. After being placed in a stationary storage item, the Gas Trap will activate the next time that storage item is opened, inflicting the Poisoned debuff to all entities within a small radius, with a duration of 49 seconds / 1 minute 38 seconds / 2 minutes 3 seconds for players and 49 seconds for NPCs, enemies and critters. The Gas Trap then becomes a Used Gas Trap and can only be "refilled" by throwing it into Shimmer, producing a new Gas Trap. Only one Gas Trap will be used at a time whenever a player opens a storage item if multiple are inside. A Gas Trap will not activate if the storage item it was placed in is opened in a singleplayer world while autopause is enabled.

Aether Monolith.name: Aether Monolith
Aether Monolith.tooltip: Monoliths are furniture items that activate backgrounds and other screen effects normally seen during events or under other special circumstances. When placed, they can be toggled with the ⚷ Open / Activate button or via wire, like other mechanisms, providing their effects in a small area around them. Monoliths only cause modified visuals; they do not spawn any event enemies or bosses, and they do not change the music. They can also be equipped as vanity accessories, which enables their effect globally for the player. There are 11 different monoliths: the Vortex, Nebula, Stardust, Solar, and Void Monoliths can be crafted at an Ancient Manipulator, the Blood Moon Monolith has a 1/10 (10%) chance of being dropped by Dreadnautiluses, the Radio Thing has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to be dropped by Deerclops, the Aether Monolith can be obtained via dropping an Angel Statue into Shimmer, the CRT and Retro Monoliths are sold by the Cyborg for 25 Gold, and the Film Projector can be obtained as part of Heroicis' set by dropping a Platinum Coin into the Water of an Oasis. The Nebula, Solar, Stardust, and Vortex Monoliths mimic effects that normally surround the corresponding Celestial Pillar during the Lunar Events. The Blood Moon Monolith mimics the effects seen during a Blood Moon. The Void Monolith mimics the screen effects of the Moon Lord boss fight. The Radio Thing activates the same sepia filter of The Constant world seed. In The Constant seed, however, it instead deactivates the filter. The Aether Monolith mimics the screen effects of the Aether mini-biome. Unlike the other monoliths, the Aether Monolith has three states: One off state (which disables the Aether effect entirely in its area, even if it would normally be present due to Shimmer) and two on states – low, which acts as if the monolith were not present (allowing the Aether effect if enough Shimmer is nearby but not forcing it on), and high, which forces the Aether effect on. The CRT Monolith mimics the effect of an old-fashioned CRT TV. The Retro Monolith mimics the effect of an old two-color green and black monitor, like the original Gameboy. The Film Projector adds a black-and-white effect to the screen.

Shimmer Arrow.name: Shimmer Arrow
Shimmer Arrow.tooltip: The Shimmer Arrow is a pre-Hardmode arrow that is obtained by throwing a Wooden or Hellfire Arrow into Shimmer. It experiences reversed gravity when fired. Upon contact with enemies or blocks, it creates a visual rainbow explosion.

Aetherium Block.name: Aetherium Block
Aetherium Block.tooltip: Aetherium Blocks are blocks formed when Shimmer comes into contact with any other liquid besides itself. Similarly to Ice Blocks, Aetherium Blocks have low friction, causing a player walking over them to slide when stopping or changing directions. This effect can be mitigated by equipping Ice Skates or other accessories crafted from them. Aetherium Blocks emit light when placed.

Faeling.name: Faeling
Faeling.tooltip: The Faeling is a flying critter that emits light, which naturally spawns in the Aether. Most critters that come into contact with Shimmer will also transform into Faelings. Faelings can pass through blocks and try to fly away from the player if they get too close. The Faeling has only 5 health and no defense, and can be damaged by other enemies and players. The Faeling can be caught with any Bug Net to be carried around in the inventory and released later, or crafted into animated decorative furniture (Faeling in a Bottle). Once crafted, the Faeling cannot be released again, unless the furniture item is de-crafted via Shimmer.

Faeling in a Bottle.name: Faeling in a Bottle
Faeling in a Bottle.tooltip: Lanterns are small light sources that hang from ceilings (the underside of blocks). They occupy less room than a chandelier, making them ideal for smaller spaces. Most lanterns can be toggled on and off via wire. There are two lanterns that provide regeneration buffs, the Heart Lantern and the Star in a Bottle, which grant health and mana regeneration, respectively. Toggling these lanterns off will only deactivate the light source, but not the buff. The Skull Lantern and Jack 'O Lantern, while having lantern in their name, are not like the rest of the lanterns in that they need to be placed on a flat surface. The Large Dynasty Lantern is considered a chandelier due to its dimensions. The Magic Lantern light pet is not considered a lantern, as it is not a furniture item and cannot be placed.

Shimmer Slime Banner.name: Shimmer Slime Banner
Shimmer Slime Banner.tooltip: Enemy banners are functional furniture items that can be placed on the underside of blocks and platforms. They are obtained by killing most enemies and a few critters. When placed, enemy banners provide a Banner buff to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the banner. The buff grants players +50%/+100% damage inflicted with all damage to the corresponding enemy and −25%/−50% damage taken from attacks by the enemy. The banners of Old One's Army enemies will apply a weaker banner buff to the respective enemy, granting the players +10%/+20% damage inflicted and −8.33% / −16.67% damage taken. Multiple banners of the same type will not grant stacked buffs. Multiple different banner types in the vicinity will, however, all take effect and consolidate into a single buff icon. There are a total of 286 obtainable enemy banners: 115 in pre-Hardmode, 171 in Hardmode. Out of these, 118 belong to event enemies (28 in pre-Hardmode and 90 in Hardmode). In addition, there are 6 unobtainable enemy banners.

Aether Torch.name: Aether Torch
Aether Torch.tooltip: Torches are furniture items that function as light sources when placed, held, or dropped (via the Throw button). Regular Torches can be found randomly in Chests and Pots, as a bonus drop from slimes, Torch Zombies, or purchased from the Merchant or Skeleton Merchant for 50 Copper each. Placing at least 101 Torches in close proximity below the surface layer in any biome will start the Torch God mini-event. Completing the event will grant the Torch God's Favor, which allows the player to automatically convert ordinary Torches to one of the biome types.

Reflective Shades.name: Reflective Shades
Reflective Shades.tooltip: The Reflective Shades are a Hardmode immunity accessory that grants the player immunity to the Darkness and Stoned debuffs.

Chromatic Cloak.name: Chromatic Cloak
Chromatic Cloak.tooltip: The Chromatic Cloak is a Hardmode accessory. When equipped, touching Shimmer does not immediately inflict the Shimmering debuff, and the player can instead start Shimmering at any time by holding the ▼ Down key. However, after Shimmering starts, it cannot be interrupted, not even if the Chromatic Cloak is removed and equipped again. While the Chromatic Cloak is equipped, being submerged in Shimmer is comparable to being submerged in water: the player's horizontal and vertical movement speed are slowed by the same amount, the Shimmer can be swam in using accessories such as Flippers, and the player will transform into Merfolk if wearing the Neptune's Shell or its upgrades. However, the player cannot drown in the Shimmer; the breath meter does not appear.

Used Gas Trap.name: Used Gas Trap
Used Gas Trap.tooltip: The Gas Trap is a trap item obtained by throwing a Whoopie Cushion into Shimmer. It also has a 1/15 (6.67%) chance to appear in any chest when the No Traps special seed is active. After being placed in a stationary storage item, the Gas Trap will activate the next time that storage item is opened, inflicting the Poisoned debuff to all entities within a small radius, with a duration of 49 seconds / 1 minute 38 seconds / 2 minutes 3 seconds for players and 49 seconds for NPCs, enemies and critters. The Gas Trap then becomes a Used Gas Trap and can only be "refilled" by throwing it into Shimmer, producing a new Gas Trap. Only one Gas Trap will be used at a time whenever a player opens a storage item if multiple are inside. A Gas Trap will not activate if the storage item it was placed in is opened in a singleplayer world while autopause is enabled.

Aether Campfire.name: Aether Campfire
Aether Campfire.tooltip: Campfires are a type of furniture and crafting station that emit light and grant the Cozy Fire buff to players in their vicinity, which provides 10% increased innate health regeneration and additionally grants 0.5 HP/s constant regeneration. The buff is applied to any players standing within a rectangular area of 170×125 tiles centered on the campfire, similar to Heart Lanterns and Sunflowers. Campfires are also minor crafting stations, and uniquely, campfires are used to cook Marshmallow on a Stick (see their page for details). Campfires can be toggled off and on with ⚷ Open / Activate, which extinguishes the flame, light, and disables the Cozy Fire buff. They can also be extinguished and lit with the Water Gun and Slime Gun respectively, and as mechanisms, they can be toggled with wire. Campfires are extinguished by rain in The Constant special world seed.

Shellphone (Home).name: Shellphone (Home)
Shellphone (Home).tooltip: The Shellphone is a post-Skeletron informational item and tool that combines the functions of the Cell Phone, Magic Conch, and Demon Conch. The player can press ⚷ Open / Activate to cycle through four teleport locations: the world's spawn point, the Ocean, the Underworld, and the player's spawn point set via a Bed.

Shellphone (Spawn).name: Shellphone (Spawn)
Shellphone (Spawn).tooltip: The Shellphone is a post-Skeletron informational item and tool that combines the functions of the Cell Phone, Magic Conch, and Demon Conch. The player can press ⚷ Open / Activate to cycle through four teleport locations: the world's spawn point, the Ocean, the Underworld, and the player's spawn point set via a Bed.

Shellphone (Ocean).name: Shellphone (Ocean)
Shellphone (Ocean).tooltip: The Shellphone is a post-Skeletron informational item and tool that combines the functions of the Cell Phone, Magic Conch, and Demon Conch. The player can press ⚷ Open / Activate to cycle through four teleport locations: the world's spawn point, the Ocean, the Underworld, and the player's spawn point set via a Bed.

Shellphone (Underworld).name: Shellphone (Underworld)
Shellphone (Underworld).tooltip: The Shellphone is a post-Skeletron informational item and tool that combines the functions of the Cell Phone, Magic Conch, and Demon Conch. The player can press ⚷ Open / Activate to cycle through four teleport locations: the world's spawn point, the Ocean, the Underworld, and the player's spawn point set via a Bed.

Music Box (Aether).name: Music Box (Aether)
Music Box (Aether).tooltip: The Music Box is a Hardmode accessory and furniture item that can be purchased from the Wizard for 10 Gold. When the Music Box is equipped in an accessory slot, it will record the currently playing in-game music after a randomized delay. This includes tracks being played by other Music Boxes. Once recorded, it will change into one of the Music Boxes listed below. A record sound alerts the player about a completed recording. Most Music Box variants can only be obtained by recording in-game music with the exception of Music Box (Journey's End), which can be bought directly from the Princess for 10 Gold after defeating the Moon Lord. A recorded Music Box can be played back in one of two ways: Equipping it as an accessory. Placing it as furniture and activating it, either by the ⚷ Open / Activate button or with wires. Recorded Music Boxes can be reverted into blank ones through Shimmer transmutation. There are 101 different Music Boxes available.

Infested Spider Wall.name: Infested Spider Wall
Infested Spider Wall.tooltip: The Spider Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in Spider Nests, considered unsafe. It does not drop as an item when destroyed and can only be obtained on  Desktop,  Console, and  Mobile, via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player. The Infested Spider Wall(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) is an item that places an unsafe Spider Wall. It is visually identical and is obtained by throwing a Spider Wall into Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions). Unsafe Spider Walls will create Cobwebs in front of them over time, serving as a renewable source for the item. These Cobwebs only have a 1/4 (25%) chance to yield a Cobweb item when destroyed.

Bottomless Shimmer Bucket.name: Bottomless Shimmer Bucket
Bottomless Shimmer Bucket.tooltip: Bottomless Buckets are tools that are capable of placing an infinite amount of liquids by pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button. There are four different types of Bottomless Buckets, one for each type of liquid: Bottomless Water Bucket, Bottomless Lava Bucket, Bottomless Honey Bucket, and Bottomless Shimmer Bucket. Bottomless Buckets can be used limitlessly and are never depleted. They are also slightly faster at placing liquids when compared to standard buckets (especially when moving the cursor around while placing).

Cursed Blue Brick Wall.name: Cursed Blue Brick Wall
Cursed Blue Brick Wall.tooltip: Dungeon Brick Walls are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Dungeon, considered unsafe. They drop as items when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting on  Desktop,  Console, and  Mobile. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player. There are a total of nine different variants (three variants in three colors), but each Dungeon can include only the three wall types matching that Dungeon's color. A single Dungeon will usually contain all three types in different areas; in each area, the faction flags found will correspond to the wall variant. Cursed Dungeon Brick Walls(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are items that place unsafe Dungeon Brick Walls. They are visually identical to their counterparts and are obtained via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

Cursed Blue Slab Wall.name: Cursed Blue Slab Wall
Cursed Blue Slab Wall.tooltip: Dungeon Brick Walls are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Dungeon, considered unsafe. They drop as items when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting on  Desktop,  Console, and  Mobile. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player. There are a total of nine different variants (three variants in three colors), but each Dungeon can include only the three wall types matching that Dungeon's color. A single Dungeon will usually contain all three types in different areas; in each area, the faction flags found will correspond to the wall variant. Cursed Dungeon Brick Walls(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are items that place unsafe Dungeon Brick Walls. They are visually identical to their counterparts and are obtained via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

Cursed Blue Tiled Wall.tooltip: Dungeon Brick Walls are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Dungeon, considered unsafe. Cursed Pink Slab Wall.tooltip: Dungeon Brick Walls are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Dungeon, considered unsafe. They drop as items when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting on  Desktop,  Console, and  Mobile. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player. There are a total of nine different variants (three variants in three colors), but each Dungeon can include only the three wall types matching that Dungeon's color. A single Dungeon will usually contain all three types in different areas; in each area, the faction flags found will correspond to the wall variant. Cursed Dungeon Brick Walls(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) are items that place unsafe Dungeon Brick Walls. They are visually identical to their counterparts and are obtained via Shimmer(Desktop, Console and Mobile versions).

Treacherous Sandstone Wall.name: Treacherous Sandstone Wall
Treacherous Sandstone Wall.tooltip: The Sandstone Wall, Ebonsandstone Wall, Crimsandstone Wall, and Pearlsandstone Wall are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Underground Desert, considered unsafe. Underground Deserts generate by default the normal Sandstone Sand Wall which may be converted into the respective variant if exposed to the Corruption, Crimson, or Hallow. Converted Sandstone Walls may further spread conversion to other walls; see Biome spread for more information. Unsafe Sandstone Walls do not drop as items when destroyed, and can only be obtained via crafting. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player. The Treacherous Sandstone Wall is an item that places an unsafe Sandstone Wall. It is visually identical and is obtained by throwing a Sandstone Wall into Shimmer.

Treacherous Hardened Sand Wall.name: Treacherous Hardened Sand Wall
Treacherous Hardened Sand Wall.tooltip: The Hardened Sand Wall, Hardened Ebonsand Wall, Hardened Crimsand Wall, and Hardened Pearlsand Wall are types of background walls which can be found naturally generated in the Underground Desert, considered unsafe. Underground Deserts generate by default the normal Hardened Sand Wall which may be converted into the respective variant if exposed to the Corruption, Crimson, or Hallow. Converted Hardened Sand Walls may further spread conversion; see Biome spread for more information. Unsafe Hardened Sand Walls do not drop as items when destroyed, and can only be obtained via crafting. They are considered safe walls when placed by the player. The Treacherous Hardened Sand Wall is an item that places an unsafe Hardened Sand Wall. It is visually identical and is obtained by throwing a Hardened Sand Wall into Shimmer.

Forbidden Lihzahrd Brick Wall.name: Forbidden Lihzahrd Brick Wall
Forbidden Lihzahrd Brick Wall.tooltip: The Lihzahrd Brick Wall is a type of background wall which can be found naturally generated in the Jungle Temple, considered unsafe. It drops as an item when destroyed, and can also be obtained via crafting. It is considered a safe wall when placed by the player. The Forbidden Lihzahrd Brick Wall is an item that places an unsafe Lihzahrd Brick Wall. It is visually identical and is obtained by throwing a Lihzahrd Brick Wall into Shimmer after Golem has been defeated.

Spelunker Flare.name: Spelunker Flare
Spelunker Flare.tooltip: Flares are a type of ammunition used solely by the Flare Gun. When fired, they travel in a slight arc and stick to blocks, similar to Sticky Glowsticks, but have greater velocity and range. They emit low-level tinted light that lasts for 10 minutes. Flares work in liquids, although they bounce off Shimmer. Flares cannot be recovered once they burn out. All types of Flares (except the Cursed Flare) inflict the On Fire! debuff. There is a 2/3 (66.67%) chance that the debuff will last 5 seconds, and a 1/3 (33.33%) chance that it will last 10 seconds.

Enchanted Moondial.name: Enchanted Moondial
Enchanted Moondial.tooltip: The Enchanted Moondial is a Hardmode furniture item. It can be triggered by the ⚷ Open / Activate key or wires, doing so will advance time to dusk (7:30 PM) on the current or following day (depending on whether it is activated during day or night). It has a 7-day cooldown period, so once used, it will not be usable again until 7 in-game days have passed (see Notes for details). When the Enchanted Moondial is ready to be used, the dial at the top of its sprite and the moon in the middle will both glow bright blue, and the shape of the glowing moon in the middle corresponds to the current moon phase. The Enchanted Moondial is obtained by throwing an Enchanted Sundial into Shimmer. The Enchanted Moondial does not turn the time to dusk immediately. It instead "fast-forwards" time, causing it to pass 60 times faster than usual (1 hour of in-game time, which would usually take 1 minute of real-life time, takes only 1 second while the Enchanted Moondial is active). When the Enchanted Moondial is taking effect, the effect of other time-accelerating methods (beds and the Journey Mode Time Menu) will be ignored. However, unlike these methods, the Enchanted Moondial does not increase the tile update rate in the world, meaning that things like plant growth and biome spread are unaffected when it is active.

Waffle's Iron.name: Waffle's Iron
Waffle's Iron.tooltip: Waffle's Iron is a Hardmode broadsword that is always dropped by Mechdusa, a boss exclusive to worlds with both Remix and For the Worthy enabled. When swung, it fires a waffle projectile once per swing, which is significantly affected by gravity. The weapon itself also has a 1/3 (33.33%) chance to inflict the Hellfire debuff upon contact for 5 seconds. Its best modifier is Legendary.

Bouncy Boulder.name: Bouncy Boulder
Bouncy Boulder.tooltip: The Bouncy Boulder is a placeable object that begins to roll and bounce when it becomes unsupported. Once it is in motion, it will bounce several times before coming to a stop. Its motion is similar to a Bouncy Bomb but faster, and it does damage like a Boulder. It rarely spawns naturally in most worlds, but is more common in Celebration Mk 10, No Traps, and Zenith worlds.

Life Crystal Boulder.name: Life Crystal Boulder
Life Crystal Boulder.tooltip: The Life Crystal Boulder is a furniture item. It spawns naturally in the Celebration Mk 10, No Traps, and the Zenith special world seeds. It appears to be an ordinary Life Crystal and is generated in a similar manner upon world creation, but acts identically to a Boulder if hit with a pickaxe or drill, or otherwise unsupported by solid blocks. The Life Crystal Boulder falls directly downwards until it collides with a solid block, at which point it begins rolling, accelerating and dealing damage to the player, enemies, critters, and NPCs. Life Crystal Boulders pierce through an unlimited number of entities and accelerate to a top speed of 36 mph over the course of 2.17 seconds. Life Crystal Boulders roll across flat surfaces and down slopes but break and disappear upon colliding with an obstacle, such as a wall of solid tiles. They deal 140 / 280 / 420 to players (70 damage to NPCs, enemies, and critters) and inflict a knockback value of 10 (Extremely strong) on contact. However, when the Life Crystal Boulder breaks after colliding with solid blocks or after rolling for one minute (like all other projectiles), it drops a Life Crystal item.

Dizzy's Rare Gecko Chester.name: Dizzy's Rare Gecko Chester
Dizzy's Rare Gecko Chester.tooltip: Dizzy's Rare Gecko Chester is a vanity item that has a 1/14 (7.14%) chance of being dropped by Deerclops.

Raynebro's Hoodie.name: Raynebro's Hoodie
Raynebro's Hoodie.tooltip: Raynebro's set is a vanity set consisting of Raynebro's Hood , Raynebro's Hoodie , and Raynebro's Pants . It is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 3 GC (set) .

Raynebro's Pants.name: Raynebro's Pants
Raynebro's Pants.tooltip: Raynebro's set is a vanity set consisting of Raynebro's Hood , Raynebro's Hoodie , and Raynebro's Pants . It is purchased from the Traveling Merchant for 3 GC (set) .

Eye of the Sun.name: Eye of the Sun
Eye of the Sun.tooltip: Paintings are decorative furniture items that can be placed on background walls. Each one is a framed image that depicts a particular scene, usually Terraria-related. Their tooltips generally contain a person's name, intended to credit each painting's artist; although the names appear to be fictional, most of them correspond to known Terraria developers, artists, testing staff, and community members (see Trivia below). (Desktop, Console and Mobile versions) Paintings are highlighted by Spelunker Potions, the Magic Lantern, Spelunker Glowsticks, and Spelunker Flares. There are a total of 193 paintings, 25 of which are sold by the Painter, 7 by the Princess, 4 by the Golfer, 2 by the Zoologist, 2 by the Clothier, 1 by the Truffle, and 27 are randomly sold by the Traveling Merchant. 35 paintings can be found in Underground Cabins, another 14 in the Underground Desert Cabins, 26 in the Dungeon, 12 in The Underworld, 6 from Floating Islands, 5 obtained by fishing, 1 from the Jungle Temple, 5 randomly acquired from Goodie Bags, 8 dropped by Solar Eclipse enemies, 8 awarded randomly by the Angler for completing fishing quests, 1 from the Living Tree, and 4 dropped by enemies.

Uncumbering Stone.name: Uncumbering Stone
Uncumbering Stone.tooltip: The Encumbering Stone is a pre-Hardmode tool that prevents item pickup while inside the player's inventory. While in the inventory, the Encumbering Stone will prevent the pickup of any items, even if the player already has a stackable item in their inventory. The Encumbering Stone will also prevent items from being added to the Void Bag. Items reeled in from fishing are still placed in the player's inventory. Hearts and Stars will also be picked up even with the Encumbering Stone in the inventory. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Encumbering Stone in the player's inventory or hotbar will toggle it between the Encumbering Stone and Uncumbering Stone. Toggling it to the Uncumbering Stone disables its functions, allowing the player to pick up items again. The Encumbering Stone has a 1/7 (14.29%) chance of being found in Sandstone Chests in the Underground Desert.

Yellow Solution.name: Yellow Solution
Yellow Solution.tooltip: Solutions are a type of ammunition used solely by the Clentaminator and Terraformer. Each solution will convert certain blocks and walls to other blocks and walls, creating and/or destroying different biomes in the process. There are 8 different solutions. 7 of them are sold by the Steampunker, who sells different solutions based on certain conditions, and one is sold by the Truffle, who always sells it. Solutions cannot be purchased in worlds with the Remix special world seed active.

Poo.name: Poo
Poo.tooltip: Poo is a type of decorative block obtained by sitting on a toilet while any tier of the Well Fed buff is active. The time until Poo is produced is random, though it averages to 10 seconds. Having the Tipsy debuff will reduce this time by 66.67%. Producing Poo will remove the food buff, and the number of blocks dropped increases with the type of the buff and its remaining duration. The maximum number of Poo blocks acquirable at once is 169, from a Golden Delight with 47 minutes of buff time remaining while the player has negative luck. When Poo is placed down, small flies will continuously fade in and out around it as a visual effect. The quantity of flies scales with the amount of Poo blocks placed in one area. Additionally, Poo blocks apply 3 seconds of the Stinky debuff to all players standing on them. Poo blocks create a squelchy sound when stepped on, and landing on top of them will also not inflict fall damage. Poo can also generate naturally in Truck stop worlds or drop from the Jungle Mimic in Celebration Mk 10 worlds. Poo can be used on an Extractinator or Chlorophyte Extractinator to obtain Dirt, Grass Seeds, Jungle Grass Seeds, and Mushroom Grass Seeds.

Shellphone.name: Shellphone
Shellphone.tooltip: The Shellphone is a post-Skeletron informational item and tool that combines the functions of the Cell Phone, Magic Conch, and Demon Conch. The player can press ⚷ Open / Activate to cycle through four teleport locations: the world's spawn point, the Ocean, the Underworld, and the player's spawn point set via a Bed.

Fertilizer.name: Fertilizer
Fertilizer.tooltip: The Fertilizer is a consumable item which immediately grows a sapling or gemcorn into the corresponding tree. Each use causes the player character to throw out Fertilizer in a small area in front of them. If a sapling meeting the required growing conditions is present in the area of effect, it will immediately sprout into a tree of the corresponding biome, but saplings that do not meet the conditions will not sprout into trees. The Fertilizer allows saplings to grow in front of any background walls and removes the restrictions related to them, but the other growing conditions still remain. The Fertilizer will be consumed on use regardless of whether saplings grow or not.

Kwad Racer Drone.name: Kwad Racer Drone
Kwad Racer Drone.tooltip: The Kwad Racer Drone is a Hardmode, post-Plantera novelty item purchased from the Cyborg for 10 Gold. Pressing the ⚒ Use / Attack button while selected in the hotbar summons a harmless drone that can be controlled by the ▲ Up, ◀ Left, and ▶ Right buttons. Pressing ⚒ Use / Attack again or switching to another item instantly destroys the drone. The player appears to wield a remote control when the drone is in use. The player is locked in place while the drone is active. Equipping the FPV Goggles will center the camera on the drone.

FPV Goggles.name: FPV Goggles
FPV Goggles.tooltip: The FPV Goggles are a Hardmode, post-Plantera accessory purchased from the Cyborg for 10 Gold. It centers the screen on the Kwad Racer Drone or Wall Racer Car while one is active, allowing the player to fly the drone or drive the car without having to keep it within the screen, or to use it to scout out areas that are difficult to reach.

Guide to Critter Companionship (Inactive.name: Guide to Critter Companionship (Inactive)
Guide to Critter Companionship (Inactive.tooltip: The Guide to Critter Companionship is a pre-Hardmode tool that prevents the player's attacks from harming critters while inside their inventory or opened Void Bag. It can be purchased from the Zoologist for 5 Gold. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Guide to Critter Companionship in the player's inventory or hotbar will toggle it between the Guide to Critter Companionship and the Guide to Critter Companionship (Inactive), disabling its functions.

Guide to Environmental Preservation (Ina.name: Guide to Environmental Preservation (Inactive)
Guide to Environmental Preservation (Ina.tooltip: The Guide to Environmental Preservation is a pre-Hardmode tool that prevents the player's attacks from breaking plants while inside their inventory or opened Void Bag. It can be purchased from the Dryad for 5 Gold. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Guide to Environmental Preservation in the player's inventory or hotbar will toggle it between the Guide to Environmental Preservation and the Guide to Environmental Preservation (Inactive), disabling its functions.

Guide to Peaceful Coexistence (Inactive).name: Guide to Peaceful Coexistence (Inactive)
Guide to Peaceful Coexistence (Inactive).tooltip: The Guide to Peaceful Coexistence is a pre-Hardmode tool that combines the effects of the Guide to Critter Companionship and the Guide to Environmental Preservation, preventing player attacks from harming critters and breaking plants when placed within the player's inventory or opened Void Bag. Pressing ⚷ Open / Activate on the Guide to Peaceful Coexistence in the player's inventory or hotbar will toggle it between the Guide to Peaceful Coexistence and the Guide to Peaceful Coexistence (Inactive), disabling its functions.
